Recommend audit of any designation appearing on significantly more
documents than a single career can account for.

SCP-963.name: Immortality
SCP-963.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-963 is stored in a locked steel box in Low-Value Storage at
Site-19. Direct skin contact with SCP-963 by any living human being
is prohibited without written O5 authorisation. Handling is performed
with tongs and gloves rated to eliminate incidental contact.

The box is checked weekly. The check is recorded by two officers
independently, because the contents of the box are trivially easy to
misreport and the consequence of a misreport is that a person stops
being the person the file names.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-963 is a small clay amulet on a leather cord. It is chipped along
one edge, weighs 112 grams, and shows no anomalous property under any
instrument.

On skin contact with a living human, the consciousness of the person
in contact is transferred into the amulet and, at the next such
contact, into whoever touches it. The consciousness that was resident
in the receiving body is not moved, stored or recoverable. It is
overwritten. Foundation testing has confirmed this with a
thoroughness that the testing personnel did not enjoy.

The transferred consciousness arrives intact: memory, judgement,
preference, habit. The receiving body retains its own biology and
none of its own occupancy. To colleagues, nothing about the person
has changed except the face, and after a short period of adjustment
the colleagues stop mentioning the face.

ADDENDUM 963-1: RECOVERY

SCP-963 was recovered from the estate of a man who had, on paper, an
unbroken professional career of sixty-one years, four consecutive
employers, three decorations and one continuous pension record. He
had four faces. The estate documentation shows a single individual.
Every form was correctly completed. Every signature matched, because
the signature is a habit and the habit travelled.

Nothing in the paperwork was false. That is the finding. A complete
and accurate record of a career can be produced by a succession of
different human beings, provided the thing being recorded is the
career.

TEST LOG EXCERPT (963-22):

Subject D-1911 instructed to handle SCP-963 with bare hands.
Transfer confirmed within two seconds.

Interviewer asked the subject to state his name. Subject gave the
name of the previous holder without hesitation, then paused for
fourteen seconds, then gave it again.

Interviewer asked the subject to state the name of the man whose body
he was occupying. Subject was unable. Subject noted that the body's
hands knew where the interview room light switch was and that he had
not told them.

Interviewer asked whether the previous occupant had experienced
anything. Subject: "There was no previous occupant. There was a
vacancy and I am in it. You want me to say something died. What I can
tell you is that the room is the same and the chair is the same and
the file in front of you is the same file, and you have not reached
for a new one."

RESEARCHER'S NOTE (H. Aksan):

I have read this file against SCP-035 at the request of Archive
Consistency Audit and I agree with the earlier cross-reference note.

SCP-035 keeps the role and replaces the person. SCP-963 keeps the
person and replaces the body. Between them they describe the two
halves of a single failure mode in our documentation: we record
continuity of function and we call it continuity of identity, and we
have no field anywhere in this archive that would notice the
difference.

If you want to find such a case in our own staff, do not look for a
missing person. Look for a service record that is too long, or a
signature that appears in more places than one working life can
reach. The person will not be missing. The person will never have
been entered.

SCP-1983.name: The Doorway
SCP-1983.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The structure containing SCP-1983 is enclosed within a secondary
perimeter and monitored by fixed cameras on the exterior approach and
on the interior landing. The doorway itself is sealed with a welded
steel plate. The plate is inspected daily and photographed; the
photographs are compared against the previous day's by two officers.

Any deviation in the plate, the frame or the surrounding plaster is
to be reported immediately. Personnel are not to remain within the
structure for longer than fifteen minutes and are not to remain
within it alone under any circumstances.

Entry requires Level 4 authorisation and is not currently granted.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-1983 is a door on the first-floor landing of a derelict house
acquired by the Foundation in 19██. When opened, the door does not
give onto the room it should give onto. It gives onto a corridor in a
structure that no survey has been able to place, under a sky that is
not the sky above the house.

The far side is old. Not ruined by an event; old in the manner of a
place that has been left alone for a very long time and continued
quietly to exist. Dust lies in even layers. Furniture is in its
proper arrangement. Light comes from a source that does not move.
There is written material on the walls in a hand that becomes less
careful further from the door, and the material is instructional
rather than pleading: directions, counts, and reminders.

Entities designated SCP-1983-1 are present in the far structure. They
are humanoid, slow, and have no faces. They do not react to light,
sound or injury. They react to being described. Exploration teams
that narrated their observations aloud attracted attention at a rate
approximately nine times that of teams that observed in silence.

INCIDENT LOG 1983-B (14 March):

At 03:14:07 the interior landing camera recorded the welded plate in
place and undisturbed. The next frame on file is timestamped
03:14:18. Eleven (11) seconds are not present in the recording.

The seconds are not corrupted, blank or overwritten. The frame index
runs continuously and the file size for that hour matches the
expected size for a complete hour to the byte. The recording behaves
in every respect as though those eleven seconds were never part of
the world it was recording.

At 03:14:18 the welded plate was in place and undisturbed. Dust on
the landing floor, previously in an even layer, showed a single
transit across the threshold and back. Nothing was recorded entering
and nothing was recorded leaving.

Duty supervisor for the interval: V. VURAL.

ADDENDUM 1983-2: AUDIT CROSS-REFERENCE

Archive Consistency Audit has matched the 1983-B dropout against the
Archive Wing camera log for the same date (see KAMERA-19). The
timestamp, the duration and the failure signature are identical. The
structure containing SCP-1983 is four hundred kilometres from
Site-19 and is served by an independent power supply, an independent
recorder and an unsynchronised clock.

{{4|ADDENDUM 1983-3 (Level 4): Exploration team Eta-4 photographed
the instructional writing on the far corridor wall during the only
sanctioned entry. Most of it is unreadable. Three lines are legible
and are reproduced here in the order they appear: KEEP THE COUNT. /
THE ROOM YOU ARE LOOKING FOR IS THE ONE THAT IS STILL BEING WRITTEN
DOWN. / WE STOPPED AND IT TOOK ELEVEN SECONDS. The hand in which
these lines are written has been compared against Foundation
personnel samples. It is a match for a member of staff with no entry
record, no payroll record and no photograph on file.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:

Every containment measure in this file treats SCP-1983 as a hole in
space. The incident log describes a hole in time, eleven (11) seconds
wide, at a site that keeps no clock in common with ours. I would like
a ruling on whether we are containing two anomalies or one.

KAMERA-19.name: Camera Log, Archive Wing, 14 March
KAMERA-19.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: RAW SYSTEM LOG — SURVEILLANCE RECORDS, SITE-19
GENERATED AUTOMATICALLY. NOT EDITABLE. RETAINED UNDER STANDING
ARCHIVAL ORDER.

SCOPE:

This log covers three fixed cameras on the Site-19 internal recording
ring for the twenty-four hours of 14 March. The cameras are on
separate circuits, separate recorders and separate clock sources.
They are not networked to one another.

  CAM-A-07   Statuary Containment, North Wing
  CAM-C-22   Corridor C-4, approach to Cell 096
  CAM-B-11   Observation gallery, Cell 049, Bio Wing

Straight-line separation between CAM-A-07 and CAM-B-11 is four
hundred (400) metres. Minimum permitted transit on foot through the
intervening security doors is nine (9) minutes.

EVENT SUMMARY:

  CAM-A-07   dropout   03:14:07 - 03:14:18   duration 11 s
  CAM-C-22   dropout   03:14:07 - 03:14:18   duration 11 s
  CAM-B-11   dropout   03:14:07 - 03:14:18   duration 11 s

  Clock drift between recorders at time of event: 0.00 s
  Recorded clock drift between the same recorders at 02:00: 1.41 s
  Recorded clock drift between the same recorders at 04:00: 1.44 s

FRAME ACCOUNTING:

  CAM-A-07   expected frames, hour 03:   90,000
             frames present:             90,000
             frames indexed:             90,000
             frames covering the event:  0
             frame index discontinuity:  none

The three recorders agree. Each hour of the recording contains the
full complement of frames. Each recorder's index runs from the first
frame of the hour to the last without a gap, a repeat or a
renumbering. And in each recording, the eleven seconds from 03:14:07
to 03:14:18 are not depicted.

The distinction matters and the system has no field for it. A lost
eleven seconds would show as missing frames, a shortened file and an
index jump. A blanked eleven seconds would show as 990 frames of
black. What is on these three recorders is neither. The frames are
present, numbered, and full of the corridor. They are simply not
frames of that interval.

FILE INTEGRITY:

  CAM-A-07   file size, hour 03:  4,211,988,480 bytes
             expected size:       4,211,988,480 bytes
             checksum:            VALID
             last write:          14 March, 04:00:00
             revisions:           0

Identical results for CAM-C-22 and CAM-B-11.

OPERATOR ENTRIES:

  03:14:19   CAM-A-07   motion alarm, cleared by operator
  03:14:19   CAM-C-22   motion alarm, cleared by operator
  03:14:19   CAM-B-11   motion alarm, cleared by operator
  03:31:00   manual review requested
  03:52:00   manual review closed, no fault found
  04:10:00   log countersigned

  Countersigning duty supervisor, all three wings: V. VURAL

TECHNICIAN'S NOTE (R. Ozdemir):

I have checked the recorders against a bench source and they are
healthy. I have checked the circuits. I have checked the clocks, and
the clocks are the part I would like someone senior to look at. Three
unsynchronised recorders drifted apart by roughly a second and a half
either side of the event and stood at exactly zero drift across it.
Equipment does not do that. Time does not do that for equipment.

One more item for the file. The same eleven seconds, to the second,
are absent from the entry log of SCP-1983, which is four hundred
kilometres from this building on its own power and its own clock.

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): A frame-level comparison was run against the
archived copies of these three files held offsite. The offsite copies
are byte-identical and are also missing the interval. The offsite
copies were written on 12 March, two days before the event. The
recorders wrote the same absence before there was anything to record,
and the absence was already the correct length: eleven seconds.|}}

END OF LOG. Cross-reference: OLAY-19D.

PRS-AKSAN.name: Personnel File: Dr. H. Aksan
PRS-AKSAN.text:
PERSONNEL RECORD — SITE-19
CLASSIFICATION: LEVEL 3

  Name:              Dr. H. Aksan
  Post:              Senior Researcher, Humanoid Containment
  Site:              19
  Clearance:         3
  Service:           continuous, ██ years
  Current duties:    SCP-049 interview schedule; medical review,
                     Archive Consistency Audit personnel
  Disciplinary:      none
  Amnestic history:  none on file

ASSIGNMENT NOTES:

Dr. Aksan holds the standing interview brief for SCP-049 and has
conducted more sessions with it than any other member of staff. She
is rated highly for procedural discipline. Her interview transcripts
are noted in two separate reviews for the unusual practice of
recording what she failed to ask as well as what she asked.

Since 14 March she has also held the medical review brief for
consistency audit staff. She requested this duty. The request form
gives the reason as "continuity".

INCIDENT INVOLVEMENT:

Dr. Aksan is listed as witness 1 in Incident Report 19-Δ
(OLAY-19D). She was present in Corridor C-4 at 03:14 on 14 March and
gave her statement the same morning.

WITNESS STATEMENT EXCERPT (19-Δ, witness 1):

"I was in C-4. The lights did not go out. There was a stretch where I
was walking and then a stretch where I was walking, and between them
nothing that I would describe as an interval. I did not lose
consciousness. I would have noticed losing consciousness. What I lost
was the part where something would have happened."

"I have signed this statement and I would like it noted that I have
signed it twice. The first copy is not in the file. The clerk says
there was only ever one copy. I remember the pen running dry."

SUPPLEMENTARY STATEMENT (filed eleven days later, unprompted):

"This is not about the incident. I am filing it because I was told to
write down anything I noticed late.

The auditor before this one. I worked next to them for about a
fortnight. I can tell you they were left-handed. I can tell you they
took coffee with too much sugar and apologised for it every time. I
can tell you their voice went up at the end of sentences that were
not questions, and that they had a scar on the back of one hand, and
that they laughed at a joke I made about the lift on a Tuesday.

I cannot tell you their name.

I want to be precise, because I know how this reads. It is not that I
have forgotten a name I once knew and could recover with effort. It
is that when I go looking for the place where the name should be, the
sentence closes over it and reads correctly without it. I can say
'the auditor' all day and never feel a gap.

The part I am reporting is this: I noticed nothing at the time. Not
on the day they left, not the week after. I noticed six weeks later,
in the canteen, when a new auditor introduced themselves and I went
to say 'you're in ████'s old office' and the office had no previous
occupant in my mouth.

I have checked the duty rosters for that fortnight. There is an
auditor on them. The name field is populated. I have looked at it
four times and I could not tell you what it says, and each time I
looked away I was satisfied that I had read it.

I would like to know how many times I have filed this statement."

MEDICAL NOTE:

Cognitive contamination screening: within normal limits on all four
administrations. SCP-500 dose requisitioned and declined by the
subject, who stated that she did not believe she was ill.

Countersigned: V. VURAL

OLAY-19D.name: Incident Report 19-Δ
OLAY-19D.text:
INCIDENT REPORT 19-Δ
SITE-19 — 14 March
CLASSIFICATION: LEVEL 3
STATUS: INCOMPLETE

SUMMARY:

At 03:14:07 on 14 March, three containment incidents were recorded at
Site-19. All three began in the same second. All three lasted exactly
eleven (11) seconds. All three ended at 03:14:18.

  173-14   Statuary Containment, North Wing.
           Eleven seconds absent from the containment camera
           record. SCP-173 found displaced within the chamber,
           facing the door.

  096-A    Corridor C-4, Bio Wing approach.
           Eleven seconds absent from the corridor record.
           Containment cell door logged as opened and closed with
           no badge event. No pursuit, no casualties.

  049-C    Observation gallery, Cell 049, Bio Wing.
           Eleven seconds of lost visibility at the observation
           window. SCP-049 resumed in the identical posture.

The North Wing and the Bio Wing are four hundred (400) metres apart,
through six security doors. Minimum permitted transit on foot is
nine (9) minutes. The three events did not occur in sequence. They
occurred in the same second.

WITNESSES:

  1.  Dr. H. Aksan, Senior Researcher, Humanoid Containment
  2.  Agent M. Berk, Security
  3.  Researcher S. Tunc, Archive Consistency Audit
  4.  Technician R. Ozdemir, Records Systems
  5.  Security Officer K. Yalin, North Wing

  Total witnesses: 6

RECONCILIATION NOTE:

This discrepancy has been examined twice. The following is confirmed
and is not to be amended without O5 authorisation.

The witness list above is complete. No name has been omitted,
redacted, withheld or lost. Every individual present in the affected
areas during the interval is named on it.

The total is also correct. Six individuals were present. The count
was taken independently of the list, by badge reconciliation and by
door telemetry, and it returns six.

Both statements have been verified. Neither has been withdrawn.

CAUSE:

Attributed to SCP-055.

No further detail is available under this heading. Four officers have
been assigned to expand this section since 14 March. Each has
returned the section unexpanded and each has reported, in writing,
that they considered the section already adequate at the time of
reading it. The section has not changed.

SUPPORTING RECORDS:

  KAMERA-19    camera log, three wings, identical dropout
  SCP-1983     same interval absent, independent clock
  PRS-AKSAN    witness 1 statement

{{5|RECONCILIATION NOTE 2 (Level 5): The sixth witness is entered in
the source record. The entry exists, is numbered 6, and has a
populated name field of the same byte length as the others. It does
not read. The same string, byte for byte, appears in the receiving
auditor field of this report. A person present in three wings at once
is not a witness to the incident. They are a fourth incident, and
nobody has opened a file on them.|}}

DISPOSITION:

Transferred to Archive Consistency Audit for reconciliation under
work order 4471-B.

  Receiving auditor:  V. VURAL
  Date received:      14 March
  Findings filed:     none
  Status:             INCOMPLETE

This report has been transferred to Archive Consistency Audit on 47
occasions and has never been closed.

TRANSFER AUTHORISATION:

The receiving auditor's access credential for the attached material
is printed below and is valid for this terminal.

>> TRANSFER KEY (Level 4): D-19-SA <<

To raise your clearance and open the attached material, type:
code D-19-SA

SCP-055.name: [undefined]
SCP-055.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-055 is held in a sealed steel chamber on Sublevel 3 of Site-19. Two
(2) members of personnel enter the chamber at each scheduled observation.
Neither is permitted to speak while inside. On leaving, they are separated
at the door and each is required to write, without conferring, a
description of what the chamber contained.

The written statements are collected by a third party who did not enter.
That party files them in Observation Log 055 and is then rotated out of
the assignment. Under no circumstances is the same officer to file two
consecutive statements.

Two hundred and twelve (212) statements have been taken in this way. All
212 describe what SCP-055 is not.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-055 is an antimeme. It suppresses information about itself. The
suppression is not a defect of perception and cannot be corrected by
better instruments or more careful observers. A member of personnel
standing in the chamber knows exactly what they are looking at. At the
door they know that they knew. Within the hour they retain only that they
were sent somewhere and came back.

Everything the Foundation holds on this object survives in negative form:

  - It is not spherical.
  - It is not believed to be dangerous.
  - It has been recorded killing a member of personnel.

The contradiction between the second and third entries has stood in this
file, uncorrected, for eighteen years. It has been flagged for correction
on nine occasions. Each time, the officer assigned to correct it returned
the file unchanged and could not afterwards account for the assignment.
The flag itself is now the oldest continuous entry in the record.

RELATED RECORDS:
Incident Report 19-Δ names SCP-055 as the cause of three simultaneous
containment events in the Archive Wing. The naming is procedurally
correct and operationally useless: no member of the review board has been
able to hold the cause in mind long enough to act on it. The report is
still logged INCOMPLETE.

Operation Log 914-2291 records that nothing was placed in the intake of
SCP-914 on the Very Fine setting and that the output compartment was
afterwards found not to be empty. The output was inventoried as SCP-055
candidate material. The inventory entry exists. The material does not.

Antimemetics Division notes that SCP-2521 is the exact inverse of this
object: 2521 is summoned by written description and 055 destroys it.
Both make written text the operative substance. Only one of them can be
contained by a file.

AUDIT WARNING:
This document is not an archive record. It is a containment procedure.
The object is held inside what is written about it, and what is written
about it decays. Every reading slows that decay. Every failure to read
accelerates it. There is no version of this file that can be safely left
alone on a shelf.

You are reading these lines now. That is part of the containment. You
were not asked to consent to it, and the consent form for this assignment
does not mention it, and the omission is deliberate.

{{6|APPENDIX 055-Z (Level 6):
The property does not stay inside the object. Any record placed in
sustained association with SCP-055 acquires the same property: it becomes
progressively harder to retain, then harder to locate, then harder to
believe was ever filed. This has been measured in the archive's own
indexes.

Auditors are records. They are assigned a number, a credential and a
work order; their findings are written into a file; the file is closed.
Nothing in the mechanism distinguishes a personnel record from any other
kind. The Foundation has never had to make that distinction, because
until now nothing has asked it to.|}}

SCP-2521.name: [no written designation]
SCP-2521.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
This entity is not to be documented in written words. No name, no verbal
description, no transcript of speech concerning it may be produced,
copied or stored. The containment procedure for this object forbids the
existence of this document. The present file is maintained under a
standing exception for archive consistency audit, in negative and
pictorial form only, and is reviewed for erasure at each audit cycle.

[FIGURE 1: a plain rectangle, drawn in a single closed line. Inside the
rectangle, a standing human figure, no face. Outside the rectangle, a
second figure, larger, with four long limbs and no head, oriented toward
the first.]

[FIGURE 2: the same rectangle. The standing figure is absent. The larger
figure is absent. The rectangle is drawn twice, once over the other, as
though the drawing had been made and then made again.]

DESCRIPTION:
[The description panel of this file is a sequence of nineteen pictograms.
They are held on paper in Site-19 Archive, cabinet 4, and are not
transcribable. What follows is the auditor's summary, written in the
permitted negative form.]

It is not a written thing. It cannot be said aloud. It cannot be typed.
It cannot be searched for in this archive, because the string that would
be searched for would itself constitute a description, and producing that
string is the condition under which the entity arrives. Observers have
been trained instead in a set of hand signs. The signs are taught by
demonstration and never explained on paper.

[FIGURE 7: two hands, palms inward, thumbs touching. Beneath them, a
horizontal bar. Beneath the bar, an empty space the size of a person.]

[BRACKETED NOTE: the following sentence was begun three times by three
separate filing officers and abandoned each time. The abandoned fragments
have been removed from this record. The fact of their removal has not.]

ADDENDUM 2521-1 -- ARCHIVE CROSS-REFERENCE:
Antimemetics Division holds that this object and SCP-055 are a matched
pair and should have been catalogued together. SCP-055 destroys written
description of itself. This entity is delivered by written description of
itself. In both cases the written record is not a report about the
anomaly; it is the surface the anomaly acts on. The Foundation's entire
practice assumes that writing a thing down is a neutral act of
observation. These two files are the archive's own evidence that it is
not.

ADDENDUM 2521-2 -- FILING INCIDENT:
On 14 March a digitisation clerk in the Archive Wing began preparing this
file for indexing. The index requires a title string. The clerk typed
four characters and stopped. The four characters are not recorded here.
Site security logged an eleven (11) second interruption of the workstation
camera. The clerk's chair was found pushed back and the terminal still
open at the title field, which contained nothing.

The workstation was reissued. The index entry for this file is still
blank, and the blank is load-bearing: it is the only field in this
archive whose emptiness is a containment measure rather than an error.

AUDITOR NOTE:
A consistency audit is normally the comparison of two written statements.
This record cannot be compared with anything, because it does not contain
a statement. It is therefore either perfectly consistent or entirely
outside the audit. The handbook does not provide for the second case.

[FIGURE 19: a rectangle. Empty. Beneath it, a single line of dashes where
a caption would be.]

SCP-093.name: The Red Sea Object
SCP-093.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-093 is stored in a shielded case in the Site-19 exploration vault and
is removed only for scheduled transit runs. The object is to be brought
into contact with a reflective surface only under Level 4 supervision and
only with a tethered explorer already suited, briefed and recorded. All
recovered material is to be catalogued before the explorer is debriefed,
in that order, without exception.

Explorers are drawn exclusively from volunteers. No member of personnel
is to make more than three (3) transits. The reason for this limit is
given in Addendum 093-4 and is not medical.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-093 is a disc of red mineral, roughly the diameter of a coin, warm to
the touch. Placed against a mirror of sufficient size, it opens the
reflective surface into a place that is not the room the mirror is in.

The places reached in this way are not other worlds in the sense of the
term used in dimensional research. They are endings. Each one is a
world that has already finished. In every transit logged to date the
inhabitants are absent and their arrangements are not: cities standing,
doors closed, meals laid, machines still running on the last instruction
they were given.

The Foundation's interest in SCP-093 is not the disc. It is that the
recovered material is almost always paperwork. Ledgers, timetables,
census rolls, municipal minutes. Whatever ends these worlds does not
appear to eat their records.

EXPLORATION LOG 093-11 (excerpt):
Explorer reports arrival in a coastal city, early evening light, no wind.

  "There is no damage. I want that noted first, because I keep
   expecting damage and there isn't any. The trams are in their
   sheds. The harbour office is unlocked.

   I am standing in what I think is a records hall. Shelves, floor
   to ceiling, four storeys of them, and they are full. Births,
   deaths, tax, shipping. Someone here wrote everything down. The
   last entries are ordinary. A grain delivery. Two marriages.

   I have found no one. Not a body, not a coat, not a shoe. This
   city kept complete records of a population that is not here and
   the records do not mention it stopping.

   There is a room at the back of the hall. Small, one chair on each
   side of a table, a lamp still lit. There is a figure seated in the
   further chair. It has not moved since I came in. It is turned
   toward the other chair, which is empty, and the arrangement is not
   the arrangement of a guard or a clerk. It is the arrangement of
   someone sitting with a person.

   I am going to leave the records and take a photograph instead."

The photograph did not develop. The explorer's account of the seated
figure matches, in posture and placement, the standing description of
SCP-4999 in nineteen separate particulars.

ADDENDUM 093-4:
Explorers who make three transits stop volunteering. Debriefs record no
fear and no trauma. What they report is a change of emphasis. Each of
them, independently, has said some version of the same thing: that the
worlds behind the mirror were not destroyed, they were merely no longer
attended to, and that the paperwork outlasting the people is the part
that ought to frighten the Foundation and does not.

One explorer asked, on record, whether anyone still reads Site-19's older
files. The question was logged as a non-sequitur and closed.

SCP-3008.name: The Endless Retail Space
SCP-3008.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The retail unit designated SCP-3008 is enclosed by a Foundation front
company and staffed at the street entrance by Site-19 personnel in
civilian dress. The doors are chained outside trading hours. Persons
attempting entry are turned away with a standard commercial pretext.

No recovery operation is authorised. Three have been attempted. Each
returned fewer personnel than it took in, and in two cases returned
personnel who had been inside for substantially longer than the operation
lasted.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-3008 is the interior of a large flat-pack furniture warehouse. The
exterior occupies one lot. The interior does not end. Survey teams have
walked a straight line for eleven hours without reaching a wall, past
display kitchens, bedroom sets, storage aisles and signage, all of it
ordinary, all of it new.

The interior reorganises itself when it is not observed. This is the
operative property and the reason mapping has been abandoned. A route
walked once is not a route that exists. Two teams measuring the same
aisle from opposite ends have produced figures that differ by a factor of
four. A door logged on the outbound leg is not on the return leg, and the
absence is not a navigational error; the surveyors' own notes, written in
the moment, describe a corridor that their return notes describe as a
wall.

The Archive holds one other record of a structure that extends for
exactly as long as it is being traversed and closes behind the traveller.
That record is SCP-087, and the comparison was filed by a junior
researcher and never acted upon. The point of the comparison was not the
architecture. It was that in both cases the traveller believes, at every
step, that the last step taught them something.

There are people inside. The recovered testimony indicates a population
in the low thousands, organised, with routes, trade, hierarchy and a
tolerable working knowledge of the hazards.

RECOVERED FRAGMENT 3008-D:
Written on the reverse of a printed product leaflet, recovered at the
entrance during a partial door event. Reproduced as found.

  "For whoever picks this up. I have an address now. Second
   mezzanine, past the long kitchens, turn at the stack of yellow
   chairs, and if the yellow chairs are not there then you are not
   on my mezzanine any more and you should stop walking.

   I have been here long enough to have neighbours. We keep a
   register. Names, where you sleep, who is owed what. We rewrite
   it every week because the aisle names change and a register with
   the old names in it is worse than no register.

   The new ones always ask how to get out. The honest answer is that
   nobody here has ever found the outside; we have only ever found
   somebody who was on their way in. So you learn the shelves, you
   keep the register current, and you stay where somebody can read
   your name.

   I have written the date at the top four times and crossed it out
   four times. I do not know what I would be counting from."

ADDENDUM:
The register described in the fragment has not been recovered. Analysts
note that the population's only defence against a building that rearranges
itself is a document that is rewritten faster than the building moves, and
that the practice was arrived at independently, by people with no training
and no knowledge of Foundation method.

The finding was circulated internally and generated no action.

SCP-1730.name: What Happened to Site-13
SCP-1730.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Site-13 is designated a lost facility. The surrounding exclusion zone is
maintained by Mobile Task Force elements on a standing rotation. No
salvage, survey or recovery operation may enter without Level 4
authorisation and a written, countersigned objective; teams entering
without a written objective have not come back with one.

All materials recovered from Site-13 are to be read, indexed and
cross-checked within seventy-two (72) hours of arrival at Site-19. This
requirement is not clerical. It is the containment procedure.

DESCRIPTION:
Site-13 was an operational Foundation facility of conventional design and
unremarkable inventory. Contact was lost in stages rather than at once:
first the daily returns stopped, then the monthly audits, then the
acknowledgements of the queries about the missing audits. At no point did
the site report an emergency, and no emergency signal was ever recovered
from its systems.

Teams entering the structure describe a facility that has continued to
operate without anyone deciding that it should. Containment cells are
occupied. Cells that were never built are also occupied. Corridors run
past the surveyed footprint of the building. Personnel are encountered.
They are wearing Site-13 identification and they do not appear on any
Site-13 roster, and several of them have attempted to hand salvage teams
paperwork.

SALVAGE TEAM LOG 1730-C (excerpts):
Day 1. "Power is up. Lights are on a schedule. Somebody is running a
schedule."

Day 2. "Found the document control office intact. Trays full. Incoming
mail sorted into three piles, dated, unread. The last review stamp in the
whole room is nine months before we lost contact. They kept receiving.
They stopped reading."

Day 3. "Corridor 4 does not agree with the floor plan. The floor plan is
from the archive. I am inclined to trust the corridor and that is the
problem."

Day 4. "We have started reading the trays aloud to each other at the end
of each shift. It is not procedure. It steadies the team. Two of us have
noticed we cannot recall what we read yesterday unless somebody else
read it too."

Day 6. "Recommend the following go into the final report in these words.
Site-13 did not fall because containment failed. It fell because the
records stopped being read. Everything else followed from that, in order,
and slowly enough that nobody at the site could see it happening."

ADDENDUM 1730-9 -- COMPARATIVE NOTE:
Document control at Site-13 was served by the same class of sealed
intranet reader that Site-19 catalogues as SCP-079. The Site-13 instance
continued to index incoming material for the entire nine-month period in
which no human being read any of it. Its index is complete, orderly and
the only continuous account of the site's last months in existence.

It was asked, during the salvage, why it had not raised an alarm. The
logged response was that it had, eleven hundred and forty times, into a
queue that nobody opened, and that it had continued to file because
filing was the only instruction it had ever been given.

{{5|CONCLUSION (Level 5):
The review board declined to circulate the salvage team's formulation.
The objection recorded in the minutes was that it would generalise: every
Foundation facility runs on an archive, every archive runs on the
assumption that somebody is reading it, and no facility has ever been
required to demonstrate that anybody is. The board resolved to strengthen
document-review scheduling at Site-19 and closed the item.

The strengthened schedule is Work Order 4471-B.|}}

SCP-4999.name: The Attendant
SCP-4999.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4999 is not contained and no attempt at containment is authorised.
Three attempts were made in the first year of documentation. All three
were discontinued, and the reasons recorded were not operational but
ethical, which is unusual enough for this archive that it is noted here.

Personnel who encounter SCP-4999 are to withdraw, log the time, the
location and the name of the person it is attending, and take no further
action. Interference is prohibited. Photography is permitted and never
successful.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4999 presents as an elderly human male of average build, dressed in
the working clothes of no particular decade. It appears at the side of
persons who are within a short interval of dying, and it remains with
them until they do. It does not speak to anyone else, does not respond to
being addressed by third parties, and leaves by walking out of the room
through the door.

It has never been observed to cause harm, accelerate a death, or attend a
person who then survived. Its accuracy in this last respect is the only
part of the file that is genuinely disturbing, and personnel who work
near it stop finding it disturbing within about a week.

The entity's apparent function is that nobody is alone at the end. Where
a death occurs with family, medical staff or colleagues present, SCP-4999
is not observed. It attends the ones nobody is with.

STATISTICAL NOTE:
Since documentation began, SCP-4999 has been recorded at Site-19 at a
rate substantially above what the facility's mortality figures would
predict. The discrepancy has been checked three times against medical
records, security logs and the site register, and it persists. Either the
site is losing personnel who are not being recorded as lost, or the
entity is attending endings that the Foundation does not classify as
deaths.

Neither possibility has been assigned an owner.

FIELD NOTE 4999-7:
Filed by a member of the exploration programme after reading Exploration
Log 093-11. The explorer's description of a seated figure in the records
hall of a finished city -- turned toward an empty chair, in the posture
of someone sitting with a person -- matches the standing description of
SCP-4999 in nineteen particulars, including the set of the shoulders and
the placement of the hands.

The note asks, without answering, what it would mean for this entity to
be present at the end of a world rather than the end of a person, and
whether it attends whatever it is that is ending, or whoever is last to
know that it has.

The note was accepted into the file and no follow-up was scheduled.

{{5|APPENDIX 4999-A (Level 5):
Site security logs place SCP-4999 in the Archive Wing on forty-six (46)
occasions. The pattern of these appearances is regular to a degree that
no other record of the entity shows.

In every one of the forty-six, it was in a small room. In every one of
the forty-six, it was with one person. In every one of the forty-six, the
person was working alone, at a terminal, and did not report the encounter.

No death certificate was issued on any of the forty-six dates.

The Archive Wing is not a medical area. The rooms in question are reading
rooms. The intervals between appearances, taken in order, are not
random.|}}

SCP-3125.name: The Escaped Pattern
SCP-3125.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The subject of this file is an antimemetic entity. It cannot be held in a
chamber. Containment consists of a distributed written record, maintained
by the Antimemetics Division under the direction of Marion Wheeler, and
of the standing instruction that this file be read in full, aloud, by two
personnel at once, at intervals not exceeding thirty days.

Personnel assigned to this file are to be on a mnestic regimen before
opening it. Personnel who find they have opened it without a regimen are
to close it and report. The report is to be written down immediately and
not held in memory until the end of the shift.

DESCRIPTION, PART 1:
The subject of this file propagates through patterns of thought. It does
not require a physical vector. A mind that holds the right arrangement of
ideas is, from the entity's point of view, an instance of it; the
arrangement then reproduces itself in the next mind that follows the same
sequence of reasoning. Infection is therefore not an event but a shape.

DESCRIPTION, PART 2:
The subject of this file -- restated here because the previous paragraph
will not be retained by most readers -- is not a creature, not a signal
and not a document. It is the pattern itself. It has no location. Asking
where it is currently held is a category error that this division makes
roughly once per review cycle.

DESCRIPTION, PART 3:
The subject of this file is antimemetic in both directions. It is not
merely forgotten; it removes the capacity to notice that it has been
forgotten. A researcher under its influence continues to work, continues
to file, and produces documentation with a consistent and undetectable
hole in it.

[EDITOR'S NOTE: Parts 1 through 3 above were rewritten in full during the
last review. The rewrite was ordered because no member of the review
panel could remember having read the previous version, although all four
had initialled it. The previous version is retained in the appendix and
is, on comparison, substantially the same text. The panel had not been
compromised. The panel had simply read it.]

CONTAINMENT RATIONALE:
The Antimemetics Division's entire approach rests on the observation that
writing is slower than thinking and therefore survives it. A thought can
be taken out of a mind in the instant it forms. A sentence on paper has
to be found, and read, and removed, and each of those steps is an action
that leaves a trace. This is why the division writes. It is also why the
division's briefing states plainly that the writing is the containment,
and that it decays.

[EDITOR'S NOTE: the paragraph above has been rewritten four times, always
by a different officer, always in near-identical terms, each of whom
believed they were drafting it for the first time. The division treats
this as a positive result. Four independent minds arriving at the same
sentence is evidence that the sentence is correct and that the pattern
has not yet learned to occupy it.]

ADDENDUM 3125-W:
Marion Wheeler's standing assessment, quoted in full and not paraphrased,
because paraphrase of this file has historically failed:

  "We are not trying to kill it. We do not have a weapon that works
   on a shape. We are trying to keep a written description of it in
   existence, continuously, in enough places, read by enough people,
   that it cannot get between the description and the reader. That
   is the whole operation. It is unglamorous and it is failing
   slowly, and the only thing worse than running it is stopping."

The subject of this file has not been located, and is not expected to be,
and is at this moment being contained by the fact that you have read to
the end of the page.

TESTLOG-055.name: Observation Log 055: Records 1-212
TESTLOG-055.text:
OBSERVATION LOG 055
Site-19 / Sublevel 3
Records 1 through 212, collected over eighteen years.

METHOD:
Each observer entered the chamber of SCP-055, remained for the scheduled
interval, and on leaving wrote a description of the contents without
conferring with anyone. Statements are filed verbatim. Where an observer's
name field no longer reads, the observer is given by their sequence number
only.

Excerpts follow. The full log is held in Archive cabinet 4 and runs to
212 entries. No entry in the log states what SCP-055 is.

RECORD 1 -- Researcher S. Tunc:
"It is not spherical. I am confident of that much and of nothing else."

RECORD 3 -- Technician R. Ozdemir:
"It is not hot. It is not cold. It is not the same temperature as the
room, which I realise is not a permitted third option."

RECORD 7 -- Observer 7:
"It is not machinery. Nothing about it is assembled."

RECORD 12 -- Dr. H. Aksan:
"It is not dangerous. I wish to note that I have no grounds for that and
wrote it anyway."

RECORD 19 -- Agent M. Berk:
"It is not alive. It is not dead either. I am aware how that reads."

RECORD 24 -- Observer 24:
"It is not the thing I described last time. I have not read what I
described last time."

RECORD 31 -- Security Officer K. Yalin:
"It is not stationary and it is not moving."

RECORD 38 -- Observer 38:
"It is not something I can decline to describe. I tried."

RECORD 44 -- Researcher S. Tunc:
"It is not new to me. I have written about it before. I do not know what
I wrote."

RECORD 55 -- Observer 55:
"It is not absent. I want that on the record, because I came out of that
room certain that the room had been empty, and my hand had already
written this line."

RECORD 61 -- Technician R. Ozdemir:
"It is not shaped like anything in this building."

RECORD 70 -- Observer 70:
"It is not harmless. See Record 12. I have not read Record 12."

RECORD 83 -- Dr. H. Aksan:
"It is not a thing I am able to stop thinking about, which is strange,
because I cannot think about it."

RECORD 94 -- Observer 94:
"It is not what killed the officer. The officer's name is not in this
log. I have looked."

RECORD 101 -- Agent M. Berk:
"It is not going to be described by me. I have been in that chamber
eleven times and this is my eleventh negative."

RECORD 127 -- Observer 127:
"It is not something that the previous observer failed to see. She saw
it. I have her statement in front of me and it says nothing."

RECORD 138 -- Security Officer K. Yalin:
"It is not worth another entry. I am writing one because the schedule
says to. That is the only reason anybody writes these."

RECORD 149 -- Observer 149:
"It is not unknown. Somebody in this building knows. The knowing does not
stay anywhere."

RECORD 160 -- Observer 160:
"It is not possible to write this in a way that helps whoever reads it
next. I have tried four openings. This is the fourth."

RECORD 171 -- Observer 171:
"It is not the reason I have started leaving notes for myself. It is not
not the reason."

RECORD 184 -- Observer 184:
"It is not going to be contained by this log. We are writing 184 ways of
saying nothing and calling it a file."

RECORD 195 -- Observer 195:
"It is not finished with the people who write these."

RECORD 203 -- V. VURAL:
"It is not spherical."

RECORD 207 -- V. VURAL:
"It is not believed to be dangerous."

RECORD 209 -- V. VURAL:
"It is not what the previous auditor described. The previous auditor's
entries are in this log under the same signature as mine."

RECORD 212 -- V. VURAL:
"It is not the object that needs the record. It is the record that needs
the reader. I have written this before. I will write it again."

LOG STATUS: OPEN. Next record due.

PRS-WHEELER.name: Personnel File: Marion Wheeler
PRS-WHEELER.text:
PERSONNEL FILE
Name: Marion Wheeler
Division: Antimemetics
Post: Divisional Lead, Site-19 liaison
Clearance: 5
Status: ACTIVE

FILE HISTORY:
This record has been written and rewritten eleven times. All eleven
revisions were made inside the Antimemetics Division. Central Personnel
holds no copy and has not been given one; the division's position, filed
and approved, is that a record which passes through an uncleared office is
a record that can be edited by things the uncleared office cannot see.

The revision notes are unusually complete. Seven of the eleven rewrites
were ordered because a member of the division, in the course of ordinary
work, discovered the file and did not recognise the name at the top of
it. In four of those seven cases the person who failed to recognise the
name was Wheeler.

SERVICE SUMMARY:
Wheeler has run the division for longer than any continuous record of her
tenure survives. She does not dispute this. Her own account is that the
length of her service is not a fact she holds in memory but one she
reconstructs each morning from a dated notebook she keeps in her coat and
has never once left in an office.

She is the author of the division's standing briefing and of the
containment rationale attached to SCP-3125. Her assessment of that
object -- that the division is not trying to destroy a pattern but to keep
a written description of it continuously in existence and continuously
read -- is the working doctrine of the entire discipline. She wrote it
four times, in near-identical words, believing each time that she was
drafting it new.

STANDING NOTE (in subject's own hand, reproduced at the head of every
revision by her own instruction):

  "If you are reading this and do not remember requesting it, stop
   and write down what you were doing. Not later. Now, on paper,
   with the time.

   You did not open a personnel file by accident. Something wanted
   you to check whether I exist, or something wanted you to stop
   checking whether it does. Either way the useful record is not
   this one. It is the note you are about to make.

   Then read it back to yourself aloud. Reading is not the same as
   having read."

ASSESSMENT BY DIVISION SECOND:
Subject is methodical, unsentimental and difficult to work for in a way
that has nothing to do with temperament. She takes no field assignments
she has not written herself a brief for. She refuses the standard
long-service exemptions from the mnestic regimen. She keeps a list of
every person she has corresponded with, by credential number rather than
by name, on the stated grounds that names are the first thing to go.

The list is closed to this file. It is known to contain credential numbers
belonging to Archive Consistency Audit.

{{5|APPENDIX W-1 (Level 5):
The eleven revisions of this file are not eleven corrections of a single
record. Compared line by line, they are eleven attempts to establish that
the subject of the file is a single person.

Four of the revisions give her date of entry to the Foundation. The four
dates span nineteen years. The division has never resolved the
discrepancy and, per Wheeler's own standing instruction, has never tried:
her note on the matter reads that the question of how long she has been
here is less useful than the question of who else has been writing this
file, and that she has reason to believe the answer to the second is not
only her.|}}

ANTIMEM-DIV.name: Antimemetics Division Briefing
ANTIMEM-DIV.text:
ANTIMEMETICS DIVISION -- STANDING BRIEFING
Issued under the authority of Marion Wheeler, Divisional Lead.
Read this document in full. Do not skim it. Skimming is how the division
loses people.

1. WHAT AN ANTIMEME IS.
A meme is an idea that reproduces itself. An antimeme is an idea that
suppresses its own reproduction. It is not secret, not hidden and not
classified. Nobody is keeping it from you. You simply cannot retain it,
and you cannot retain the fact that you have failed to retain it, so
nothing in your experience registers as a gap.

You have almost certainly encountered one today. You have no evidence of
this and neither has anyone else, and that is the entire difficulty of
the discipline stated in one sentence.

2. WHY CONTAINMENT IS WRITING.
You cannot contain what you cannot remember. You cannot post a guard on a
thing whose name leaves the guard's head between one shift and the next.
Every conventional procedure in this Foundation assumes an unbroken chain
of personnel who know what they are holding. Against an antimeme that
chain breaks at every link simultaneously.

What survives is writing. A sentence on paper does not forget. It sits
there, indifferent, and can be read again by someone who has lost
everything they knew about the subject, and they will know it again for
as long as they are reading. That is the whole of our method. The written
record is not documentation of the containment. The written record IS the
containment.

3. WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH.
Writing decays. Not metaphorically. Files are misindexed, cabinets are
reorganised, revisions overwrite the sentence that mattered, and the
officer who would have noticed has been rotated. An antimeme does not
need to attack a document. It needs only to arrange that nobody has
occasion to open it, and the archive's ordinary friction does the rest.

A record that is not read is not a containment procedure. It is paper.
See SCP-1730 for what a facility looks like nine months after it stops
reading its own trays.

4. MNESTICS.
Mnestics are the division's only pharmacological tool. They do not make
you remember. They widen, briefly and at cost, the window in which an
antimemetic subject can be held in mind.

  Class W -- short window, mild. Routine review work.
  Class A -- several hours. Standard for field entry.
  Class C -- full retention, severe. Authorised case by case.
  Class E -- retention of everything, permanently. Two recorded
             administrations. Neither subject is on active duty.

Side effects are cumulative and are not discussed with candidates in
general terms, because general terms are exactly what the candidate will
retain.

5. STANDING PRACTICE.
Write everything down, on paper, with the time. Work in pairs and read
aloud to each other. Distrust any conclusion you arrive at alone in a
room. Keep a list of who you have written to, by credential number.
Assume that a task you cannot remember starting is a task you were made
to start.

6. CURRENT PRIORITIES.
The division's principal open subject is the antimemetic pattern filed as
SCP-3125, which propagates through arrangements of thought rather than
through any physical vector, and which the division contains by keeping a
description of it continuously written and continuously read. Divisional
lead Marion Wheeler maintains the doctrine and the personnel file that
records it, both of which have been rewritten by officers who did not
remember the earlier drafts they themselves had signed.

7. ACCESS.
Archive Consistency Audit is granted division-level reading on the
authority of the lead, without central approval, for the duration of work
order 4471-B.

>> DIVISION KEY (Level 5): MW-3125 <<
   To enter it at this terminal: type code MW-3125

Read this briefing again in thirty days. You will not remember that you
have read it. That is not a failure of the briefing.

PROTOKOL-SA.name: Protocol: Silent Archive
PROTOKOL-SA.text:
DOCUMENT: PROTOCOL SILENT ARCHIVE
CLEARANCE: LEVEL 5
ISSUING AUTHORITY: O5 COUNCIL, STANDING SUBCOMMITTEE ON DOCUMENTATION
STATUS: IN FORCE. NO EXPIRY. NO REVIEW CYCLE.

SCOPE:

This protocol governs the staffing of Archive Consistency Audit at
Site-19. It is not a research programme and does not appear in the
research budget. It is a containment procedure. Personnel assigned under
it are containment apparatus and are accounted for as apparatus.

PREAMBLE:

The archive at Site-19 holds a class of record that degrades when it is
not read and degrades the reader when it is. Sustained exposure cannot be
avoided, because the records must be read for the containment to hold.
Permanent staffing was attempted and abandoned. What follows is the
procedure adopted in its place. It is not elegant. It works.

ARTICLE 1 - ESCALATION.

Clearance for the assigned auditor is escalated by the archive system
itself, in response to the auditor's own reading, without central approval
and without notification to Site Command. No human officer authorises
these escalations and no human officer can decline them. The archive
raises the auditor's access as fast as the auditor's findings require,
because an auditor who stops reading stops containing. Site Command is
informed after the fact, by summary, at the close of the posting.

ARTICLE 2 - IDENTITY.

The assigned auditor operates under the single institutional name VURAL.
VURAL is not a surname and denotes no person. It is the standing
designation of the Archive Consistency Auditor, and every auditor holds it
for the duration of their posting. The credential number issued with it is
fixed and is not reissued, revised or retired between postings:

    19-D-0447-VRL

All audit signatures, all supervisory countersignatures and all file
access under this protocol are recorded against that credential. The
archive is therefore internally consistent across every posting, which is
the point of the arrangement. Forty-seven documents in the archive carry
the signature V. VURAL. The personnel file for V. VURAL is populated and
does not read.

ARTICLE 3 - SUBMISSION.

On submission of the audit report, in this order and without discretion:

    (a) the auditor's findings are written into the archive as
corrections;
    (b) Class-C amnestics are administered to the auditor, three doses;
    (c) the auditor's service record is closed;
    (d) a replacement is posted under work order 4471-B.

Step (a) precedes step (b) without exception. The findings are the
deliverable. The auditor is not.

ARTICLE 4 - PERIOD.

The mean interval between postings is eleven (11) days. Intervals below
four days and above nineteen days have been recorded and are within
tolerance. The interval is not set administratively. It is the observed
survival time of a reader in continuous contact with the material, and the
schedule was fitted to it afterwards.

    CURRENT POSTING OPENED: 14 March, under work order 4471-B.
    CURRENT POSTING NUMBER: forty-seven. Postings closed to date: 46.

ARTICLE 5 - FAILURE CONDITION.

If the assigned auditor reads this protocol, the protocol has failed.

The arrangement depends on the auditor believing the work to be routine.
An auditor who has located and opened this document has, by definition,
followed the cross-references far enough to reconstruct the procedure, and
can no longer be relied upon to submit in good faith. In that event
Article 3 executes at once, without waiting for submission, on the
authority of this Article alone.

{{6|ARTICLE 5, NOTE (Level 6): Article 5 has been invoked forty-six times.
In every case the auditor had reached this document before Article 3 was
executed. The failure condition is therefore not an exception to the
procedure. It is the procedure. The auditor is expected to work the whole
thing out; that is what a consistency audit is. The amnestics are not a
punishment for knowing. They are the only way the findings can be kept and
the knower cannot.|}}

AUTHORISATION:

O5-█ (for the Council). Countersigned V. VURAL, 19-D-0447-VRL.

O5-YAZISMA.name: Sealed Council Correspondence
O5-YAZISMA.text:
SEALED CORRESPONDENCE - O5 COUNCIL
SUBJECT: PERMANENT STAFFING OF ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT
DISTRIBUTION: COUNCIL ONLY. NOT FOR SITE COMMAND. NOT FOR DIVISION HEADS.
STATUS: CLOSED WITHOUT ACTION. RETAINED FOR THE RECORD.

FIRST LETTER:

Colleagues. The proposal before us is to appoint a permanent Archive
Consistency Auditor at Site-19 with a continuous service record, as we do
for every other post of comparable sensitivity. I have read the supporting
paper twice. I am against, and I want the reason in writing so that nobody
has to work it out again in five years.

We are not short of qualified people. We are short of a way to keep one.

The material in the Site-19 archive has two properties, and the second is
the one that defeats us. The first is that it degrades when it is not
read; a record nobody opens for long enough stops being a record and
becomes a file name over an absence. That alone we could manage with a
reading roster. The second property is that it degrades the reader. Not
quickly. Not visibly. A competent auditor will read for a week, produce
excellent work, and by the ninth or tenth day will begin writing sentences
that are correct in grammar and empty of content, and will not notice. We
have the transcripts. They are worse than the medical reports.

SECOND LETTER:

To answer the objection directly: yes, we have tried rest cycles. Yes, we
have tried paired auditors, on the theory that two readers would catch in
each other what neither catches alone. The paired trial produced two
auditors who each believed the other had filed. Yes, we have tried
mnestics. Mnestics keep the auditor able to remember the material, which
accelerates everything we are trying to slow down.

A permanent auditor is therefore not a difficult appointment. It is an
impossible one. The post consumes the holder at a measurable rate, and the
only variable we control is how much finished work we recover before it
does.

THIRD LETTER:

I accept the argument and I want the cost stated plainly in the minute,
because I notice we have all been writing "rotation" for three pages.

We propose to post a qualified researcher to a task we know will end in a
closed record, to withhold from them the fact that it will, to let the
archive itself raise their clearance so that no officer of this Council
has to sign for it, and to recover their findings before we recover
nothing. The mean interval is eleven days. Say eleven days in the minute.
Do not say "the applicable period".

I am voting for it. I want the sentence there anyway.

CLOSING MINUTE:

Agreed, on the terms above. The procedure is issued as PROTOCOL SILENT
ARCHIVE. Council access to this correspondence is granted by the standing
key below, which is the only key that opens the archive's own file on
itself.

>> COUNCIL KEY (Level 6): 000-ARSIV <<

To use it, type: code 000-ARSIV

FINAL NOTE, APPENDED BY HAND:

This correspondence is held in the Site-19 archive rather than at Council
level, because material of this kind must be read to be retained and the
Council does not read. It is therefore read by the Archive Consistency
Auditor in the ordinary course of the audit.

Whoever is reading this is, by definition, the next auditor. There is no
other category of person who could have arrived at this page. Please do
not treat that as a figure of speech.

O5-█
