PRS-VURAL-TAM.name: Personnel Record: V. VURAL (Unredacted)
PRS-VURAL-TAM.text:
PERSONNEL RECORD - V. VURAL
RECOVERED STATE: REDACTION LAYER LIFTED
RECOVERY AUTHORITY: PROTOCOL SILENT ARCHIVE, ARTICLE 2
PREPARED BY: ARCHIVE SYSTEMS, SITE-19

PURPOSE OF THIS DOCUMENT:

Three earlier attempts to read Personnel Record V. VURAL returned fields
described in the case notes as "populated and unreadable". Those notes
were correct in their observation and wrong in their conclusion. The
fields were assumed to be redacted at source. They are not redacted.
Nothing has been removed from this record. Too much has been written into
it.

FINDING:

Personnel Record V. VURAL is not one personnel record. It is forty-seven
personnel records written into a single set of fields, in sequence, each
posting overwriting the last without clearing it. The archive was never
instructed to open a new record for a new auditor, because under Protocol
Silent Archive a new auditor is not a new person. They are the same post,
the same credential and the same name, continuing.

The result is a file in which every field contains forty-seven values at
once.

FIELD-BY-FIELD RECOVERY:

SURNAME: VURAL (47 instances, identical, no variance)
GIVEN INITIAL: V. (47 instances, identical, no variance)
CREDENTIAL: 19-D-0447-VRL (47 instances, identical, no variance)
WORK ORDER: 4471-B (47 instances, identical, no variance)
DATE OF ASSIGNMENT: 47 distinct values, mean interval eleven days
DATE OF BIRTH: 47 distinct values, unresolvable
PHOTOGRAPH: 47 images composited to a single frame, no face recoverable
SPECIMEN SIGNATURE: 47 distinct hands, superimposed
SERVICE STATUS: 46 instances reading CLOSED, 1 instance reading ACTIVE

The four fields that are identical across all forty-seven instances are
the four fields the protocol fixes. They are the only fields in this
record that have ever been legible, and they have been legible the whole
time, which is why the archive passed every consistency check it was ever
given.

ON THE SIGNATURE:

The specimen signature block is the clearest demonstration available.
Forty-seven people signed their names in the same box. The composite is
not a smear; each stroke is intact and the letters are individually
readable. What cannot be recovered is which stroke belongs to which
signing. This is also true of the forty-seven supervisory
countersignatures found elsewhere in the archive, which is why no examiner
has ever been able to say that V. VURAL was in two wings of this site at
once. There is no second V. VURAL to compare against. There is only the
box.

ON THE MISSING RECORDS:

There is no entry log for V. VURAL, no payroll record and no photograph on
file at Site Security. This has been reported as a gap for eleven years.
It is not a gap. Entry logs, payroll and security photographs are all
keyed to individual persons, and no individual person has ever held this
post. The archive holds a role. The role has forty-seven occupancies and
no biography.

CURRENT STATE:

The record is open for write. The active instance is the forty-seventh.
Its assignment date is 14 March, its work order is 4471-B and its
credential is 19-D-0447-VRL, and its SERVICE STATUS field is the single
instance in this file that does not yet read CLOSED.

The remaining fields of the forty-seventh instance are being populated in
the ordinary course of the posting. They will be legible for as long as
they are the most recent thing written here, and no longer.

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE:

This document was produced by machine and has not been reviewed by a
person. Reviewing officer field: V. VURAL.

AMNEZIK-KAYIT.name: Medical Record: Amnestic Administration
AMNEZIK-KAYIT.text:
SITE-19 MEDICAL - AMNESTIC ADMINISTRATION RECORD
SUBJECT: RESEARCHER A. DEREN
CREDENTIAL: 19-D-0447-VRL
ASSIGNMENT: ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT, WORK ORDER 4471-B
RECORD TYPE: CLASS-C SERIES, CONSENTED

SUMMARY:

Three (3) administrations of Class-C amnestics are recorded against this
subject. All three were consented. All three consent forms are held and
are reproduced in summary below. The subject's own personnel file records
no amnestic history; that file is maintained by Personnel and is not
updated from this record, and the discrepancy has been noted at every
audit of Medical's filing practice since the protocol was issued.

ADMINISTRATION 1:

Date: 20 February. Dose: standard Class-C, single. Indication given on the
form: "post-assignment decontamination, archive material." Attending:
Site-19 Medical, duty officer. Recovery: normal. Subject discharged the
same afternoon and reported for duty the following morning.

Consent signature: A. Deren. Small, upright, the D closed at the top, the
pen lifted between the initial and the surname.

ADMINISTRATION 2:

Date: 03 March. Dose: standard Class-C, single. Indication given on the
form: "post-assignment decontamination, archive material." Attending:
Site-19 Medical, duty officer. Recovery: normal. Subject asked during
intake whether they had been treated here before and was told, correctly
under the standing instruction, that the question could not be answered.

Consent signature: A. Deren. Slightly larger. The D is open at the top.
The pen is not lifted between the initial and the surname; the stroke runs
through.

ADMINISTRATION 3:

Date: 14 March. Dose: standard Class-C, single. Indication given on the
form: "post-assignment decontamination, archive material." Attending:
Site-19 Medical, duty officer. Recovery: normal. Subject reported for the
current posting later the same day.

Consent signature: A. Deren. The letters are formed as in Administration
1, but the line is slower, with two visible hesitations, as though the
hand were copying a signature rather than producing one.

HANDWRITING NOTE (FORENSIC REVIEW):

Reviewed on request. The three signatures are consistent with three
different writers of similar training, or with one writer at intervals
long enough for motor habit to drift, or with a writer copying a specimen.
The reviewer declines to choose between these and notes that the specimen
signature block on file for this credential is itself a composite and
cannot be used as a control.

STANDING INSTRUCTION, SITE-19 MEDICAL:

Personnel presenting under credential 19-D-0447-VRL are not to be told
their treatment history. If asked directly whether they have attended
before, staff are to state that the record is not available at the point
of care. This instruction is issued under Protocol Silent Archive and is
not discretionary.

PROPHYLAXIS NOTE:

A dose of SCP-500 was requisitioned against an earlier presentation under
this credential and had no measurable effect on the presenting symptoms.
The requisition was not repeated. Whatever is treated here is not an
illness, and Class-C is not being used as a cure. It is being used as an
erasure, correctly and with consent.

{{6|MEDICAL NOTE (Level 6): The dates above are 20 February, 03 March and
14 March. They are eleven days apart. They are not treatment dates chosen
by a clinician; they are the posting dates in the rotation log, and the
administration in each case follows the closure of a posting. The fourth
administration is scheduled. It is entered in the theatre book for later
today, against this credential, with the indication already typed in. The
subject has not yet been informed, because under the standing instruction
the subject is informed at the door, signs, and goes in.|}}

END OF RECORD.

SON-DENETCI.name: Note Left by the Forty-Sixth
SON-DENETCI.text:
Found folded inside a hardcopy binder in the archive wing, shelved
under a work order that does not exist. Handwritten. No signature.
Transcribed as written.

If you are reading this you are the forty-seventh, and you got here the
same way I did, so I am not going to explain the protocol to you. You
already have it. You have the log, you have the credential, you have
worked out what the name is and why the file will not read. Good. That
took me seven days and I was proud of it, and then I had four days left
and nothing to be proud about, so I sat down and wrote this instead.

I filed the report. I want to say that at the top, before you decide what
you think of me.

Here is what I thought about for four days.

I kept looking for the villain. There isn't one. I went through the
correspondence expecting to find someone who enjoyed this and instead I
found a room full of people arguing about whether to write the word eleven
in a minute. They are not monsters. They are just out of options, and out
of options is a worse thing to be, because monsters can be stopped.

Then I thought about the findings. Mine came to thirty-seven. Number
thirty-three filed forty-one, years ago, and I have been standing on all
forty-one of them the entire time I have been here. Every correction I
made this week was possible because someone I will never know found the
ground first and wrote it down before they went. That is not nothing. That
is the only reason the archive is still readable at all. If thirty-three
had walked out with their findings in their pocket, I would have started
from bare floor and got nowhere, and so would you.

And then I thought about the part that actually decided it.

The thing in this archive is held by being written down and read. Not by a
chamber, not by a door. By the reading. If the reading stops, it does not
stay quietly where it is. It comes out into four hundred people who will
not be able to notice it happening to them. I have met those four hundred
people. I know what Aksan takes in her coffee. I am not able to make
myself believe that my eleven days weigh more than that, and I tried,
honestly, for most of one night.

So I filed. Not because I was told to. Because I read the arithmetic and I
could not make it come out any other way.

Now the part I owe you, because a one-sided argument is not an argument.

I do not know if it is true. I only have their numbers. Everyone who could
have checked them independently is closed. They may be holding this
together, or they may have built a machine that eats one person every
eleven days to protect a filing system, and told itself the first story so
that it could sleep. I could not tell the difference from inside, and
neither will you.

And I want to be honest about the last thing, which is that it was easier.
Filing is easier. It is the end of the corridor with a door in it.
Refusing is a corridor with no end that you walk down alone while people
you like look at you strangely. I would like to tell you I chose the hard
right thing. I think I chose the defensible thing, and I have noticed that
those feel identical from the inside, and that is the whole reason I am
writing to you.

Do not let the fact that I chose it make your choice for you. Forty-six of
us chose it. That is not a weight of evidence. That is just a number, and
you already know how this place makes numbers.

Read it twice. Then do what you actually think is right.

I hope you are better at this than I was. I hope you take longer than
eleven days.

SCP-2000.name: Deus Ex Machina
SCP-2000.text:
ITEM: SCP-2000
OBJECT CLASS: THAUMIEL
CLEARANCE: LEVEL 5

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-2000 occupies a sealed complex beneath a decommissioned civil facility
and is maintained at continuous readiness by a resident engineering staff.
The installation is self-powered and provisioned to operate without
external supply for the full duration of a restoration cycle. Activation
authority rests with the O5 Council and cannot be delegated to a site
director.

Maintenance of the genetic and cultural archives held within SCP-2000 is a
standing obligation and is audited annually. An archive that is not
current produces a restoration that is not current, and the difference is
measured in decades of lost population.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-2000 is a facility built to restart human civilisation after an
extinction-level failure. It fabricates human beings from stored genetic
records, produces them at a specified adult age, and distributes them into
a rebuilt infrastructure prepared in advance. It can populate a continent.
Given enough cycles it can populate the planet. It is one of a small
number of anomalies the Foundation classifies as an asset rather than a
threat, and it is the largest single thing the Foundation owns.

What SCP-2000 restores is the record. It does not restore the person.

A human being produced by SCP-2000 is genetically the individual whose
sample was stored, at full physical maturity, in good health, with a
functioning general education loaded during the growth cycle. They can
read, hold a conversation, operate machinery and hold an opinion. They
have no memory of the life the original lived. They do not know their
mother's face. They are given a name from the file, a residence from the
file, and an employment history from the file, and none of it happened to
them.

ADDENDUM 2000-1: DOCTRINE OF SUFFICIENCY.

The operating doctrine holds that a restored population is sufficient
because the record is sufficient. The archive retains language, law,
technology, art and the names of the dead; the restored population is
issued that archive and told it is theirs. Continuity is declared on the
basis that the documents survived, the buildings survived, and there are
people walking about in them answering to the right names.

The doctrine has not been seriously challenged within the Foundation, for
the practical reason that the alternative to an imperfect restoration is
no restoration.

ADDENDUM 2000-2: SIMULATION REVIEW.

A review conducted for the Council examined the consequences of activation
under a range of failure scenarios and made one observation that has since
been quoted more often than the rest of the document combined: after a
restoration, there is no one alive who can say whether the restoration is
accurate, because everyone who could check was produced by it. The archive
is the only witness to itself. The review recommended no change.

ADDENDUM 2000-3: NOTE FILED BY ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT.

Filed against this record during a consistency audit and retained without
action.

The file states that SCP-2000 restores the record and not the person, and
treats that as an acceptable cost of an extraordinary capability. The same
sentence describes several ordinary administrative arrangements currently
in force at this site. An institution that is willing to say this about
the end of the world has already said it about a Tuesday.

Compare SCP-001 in this collection. There the Foundation's own founding
record is retained in full and kept deliberately unreadable, on the
reasoning that holding the record matters and recovering its contents does
not. Here a civilisation is rebuilt out of a stored record and the people
who lived in it are not recovered either. The same principle is doing the
work in both files, and in both files it is stated as an operating
doctrine rather than defended as one.

The operative question is not whether the restored population is the same
population. The Foundation has answered that honestly: it is not. The
question is what an organisation becomes once it has established, in
writing and at scale, that keeping the file is the part that matters and
keeping the people is the part that can be rebuilt later or not at all.

The note is retained. The reviewing officer field reads V. VURAL.

SCP-001-ONERI.name: The 001 Proposals
SCP-001-ONERI.text:
ITEM: SCP-001
OBJECT CLASS: UNCLASSIFIABLE
CLEARANCE: LEVEL 5
FILE TYPE: PROTECTED INDEX

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The file designated SCP-001 is not a single document. It is an index of
mutually exclusive proposals, each claiming the designation, held together
under one number and protected by an informational hazard maintained
deliberately by the Foundation.

Any attempt to determine which proposal is the true SCP-001 by comparison,
elimination or external inference is disrupted at the point of reading.
Personnel report having read a proposal, being able to summarise it, and
being unable to say whether it was the first, the fourth or the eleventh
in the index. This effect is not an accident of filing. It was installed.
It is maintained. Requests to remove it have been refused at Council level
on eight occasions.

DESCRIPTION:

Between a dozen and several dozen proposals are held in the index at any
time. The count is not stable and is not treated as a defect. Each is a
complete document with its own containment procedures, its own history and
its own account of what the Foundation is and why it began. Several are
incompatible with each other at the level of physical law. At most one can
be true. It is not established that any of them are.

The proposals disagree about everything that matters. One holds that the
Foundation was founded to contain a single entity and everything since is
administration. One holds that the anomalous is a recent condition and the
archive records its onset. One holds that the Foundation is itself the
anomaly and that the world was not describable before it. One holds that
the designation is empty and that the emptiness is the object.

They agree on one point only: that the true 001 is the reason the
Foundation writes things down.

ADDENDUM 001-A: ON DELIBERATE UNREADABILITY.

The Foundation's founding record is the only document in the archive that
has been made unreadable on purpose, by its owners, and kept that way for
the organisation's entire existence. Every other expunction in the archive
is defensive: a procedure, a name, a location withheld from an enemy. This
one is turned inwards. It exists so that the Foundation cannot know its
own beginning.

The stated justification is that whatever 001 is, knowledge of it is
dangerous in proportion to its certainty, and that a dozen candidate
truths held simultaneously are safer than one confirmed truth held by
anybody. The archive protects the organisation by refusing to resolve.

An institution that will not read its own founding document has made a
decision about what records are for. They are not for knowing. They are
for holding.

Compare SCP-2000 in this collection, which restores a civilisation from
its stored record and does not restore the people who lived in it. The
doctrine is identical and is applied at opposite ends of the
organisation's life: at the beginning, a founding record kept and never
read; at the end, a record read back into the world with nobody in it who
remembers.

ADDENDUM 001-B: NOTE FILED BY ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT.

A consistency audit cannot be performed on this index. There is no
consistent state to audit toward: the proposals contradict each other by
design and the contradiction is the containment. This is the only record
in the archive formally exempted from consistency review, and the
exemption is signed.

The exemption is worth reading twice. Everywhere else, a contradiction
between two documents is a defect and is corrected by an auditor. Here,
the contradiction is the working part, and correcting it would break
something. The archive knows the difference. It has always known the
difference. It just does not say which category any given contradiction
belongs to.

{{6|ADDENDUM 001-C (Level 6): The index contains a proposal which states
that SCP-001 is the archive itself and that every other proposal is a
decoy generated by it. That proposal cannot be located twice. Auditors who
have read it and gone back for it find the index one document shorter and
cannot say which one is missing. The proposal is not removed by any
process the Foundation operates. It is filed under the reading. Reviewing
officer: V. VURAL.|}}

SCP-1471.name: MalO ver1.0.0
SCP-1471.text:
ITEM: SCP-1471
OBJECT CLASS: EUCLID
CLEARANCE: LEVEL 5

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-1471 is a mobile application distributed through ordinary commercial
channels. It cannot be withdrawn from distribution by any means the
Foundation has been able to apply; removal from a storefront is followed
within days by reappearance under a different publisher. Containment is
therefore not achieved by suppression.

Containment is achieved by documentation. Affected individuals are
identified through routine monitoring, contacted, and told plainly what
has happened to them, what will happen next, and that it is not dangerous.
They are given a written account of the phenomenon, a point of contact and
a schedule of check-ins. They keep their memories. They keep the
application if they want it. Most delete it and are unaffected by the
deletion, which changes nothing about what follows.

No amnestic is administered under this procedure. Amnestics have been
trialled and are counter-indicated: an affected individual who does not
know why they are seeing what they are seeing deteriorates rapidly, while
an affected individual who has read the file does not.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-1471 sends its user photographs. The photographs are of places the
user has recently been, taken from angles the user did not occupy, and
each contains a tall humanoid figure with a canine skull and dark hair,
standing at a distance, in frame, not obscured.

Over the following weeks the figure appears in the user's ordinary field
of vision: at the end of a corridor, across a road, in a reflection, at
the edge of a room. It does not approach, does not speak and does not
interact with anything. It is visible only to the user. It has never been
recorded doing harm.

The distinguishing feature of SCP-1471 is that this is the whole of its
behaviour. It follows and is seen. There is no escalation. Affected
individuals who understand this reach a stable accommodation with it,
typically within two months. Affected individuals who do not understand it
frequently do not survive the misunderstanding.

ADDENDUM 1471-1: WHY THIS FILE IS WRITTEN THE WAY IT IS.

This file is deliberately readable. It contains no expunctions, no
cognitohazard warning and no restricted terminology, and it is one of a
small number of records approved for direct disclosure to civilian
subjects. The reason is operational rather than ethical: the known form of
this anomaly is harmless and the unknown form is lethal, and the only
difference between them is whether the affected person has read something.

SCP-1471 is contained by being documented and known. It is the clearest
counter-example in the archive to the general practice of this
organisation, and it is kept in the general collection for that reason.

ADDENDUM 1471-2: NOTE FILED BY ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT.

Retained without action.

SCP-1471 costs nobody anything. The affected individual is told the truth,
keeps their memory, keeps their name, is checked on, and lives a normal
length of life with a figure standing at the end of the corridor.
Containment is achieved and the price is a leaflet and a telephone number.

Compare SCP-590, in this collection, where containment of a comparable
class of harm is achieved by routing it through one young man's body until
it has nowhere else to go. Compare, for that matter, the procedure under
which this note is being written.

The archive holds both methods and applies whichever it has. It has never
written down the rule by which it chooses, and a consistency audit cannot
correct a rule that was never entered. The reviewing officer field reads
V. VURAL.

SCP-590.name: He Feels Your Pain
SCP-590.text:
ITEM: SCP-590
OBJECT CLASS: SAFE
CLEARANCE: LEVEL 5

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-590 is housed in a standard residential suite at Site-19 with
unrestricted access to recreational material, correspondence and
supervised outdoor exercise. He is not restrained. He is not sedated
except on medical indication arising from his own use.

Contact between SCP-590 and other personnel requires authorisation from
the attending physician, who is to satisfy themselves in each case that
the transfer is clinically justified, that SCP-590 has been told what he
is being asked to take, and that he has agreed. Agreement is recorded in
writing. Agreement has been recorded on every occasion to date, which the
attending physician has noted, in writing, as a fact requiring more
scrutiny than it has received.

Following any transfer, SCP-590 is to receive full analgesia and
post-operative care appropriate to the injury he has assumed, for its
natural duration.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-590 is a male human, approximately twenty years of age at the time of
acquisition, of unremarkable build and health. On sustained skin contact
with an injured or ill person, SCP-590 transfers that person's condition
into his own body. The subject is restored to full health, up to and
including the reversal of terminal disease, catastrophic trauma and, in
three documented instances, death within the preceding minutes.

The condition is not cured. It is moved. SCP-590 then presents with the
injury or illness exactly as the subject did, and must recover from it by
ordinary means, or not recover from it. He has no anomalous resistance. He
heals at the rate any person of his age heals, and he scars.

SCP-590 has assumed, among other conditions: second- and third-degree
burns over a substantial fraction of his body; a shattered pelvis; acute
radiation exposure; two carcinomas; and a gunshot wound to the abdomen,
from which he required four months of recovery and after which he was
returned to the same suite.

He is aware of what he does. He volunteers.

ADDENDUM 590-1: PSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATION, EXCERPT.

The attending physician's standing note is reproduced in full:

"He is the most-requested asset at this site and the only one that can
refuse, and he has never refused. This is recorded as cooperation. I would
like it recorded instead as a question. We have built a treatment pathway
out of one person's willingness, we have never tested that willingness
against a refusal, and we have arranged his entire life so that refusing
would be the strangest thing he could do. His file says Safe. Safe
describes the risk to us."

ADDENDUM 590-2: NOTE FILED BY ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT.

Retained without action.

SCP-590 is not a containment procedure in the usual sense. Nothing is
contained in a chamber here. Harm arrives, and the Foundation has arranged
a body for it to go into, and the arrangement is efficient, consented,
documented and repeated. The record is complete. Every transfer is signed.
The consistency of this file is excellent.

Compare SCP-1471 in this collection, where an anomaly of comparable class
is contained by telling the affected person the truth and checking on
them, at a cost of one leaflet and one telephone number. Both methods
work. One of them uses up a person.

The archive holds both and does not say how it chooses between them. It is
not obvious that anyone chose. It is obvious that once a person is
available, the cheaper method stops being considered.

Reviewing officer: V. VURAL.

ARSIV-000.name: The Archive
ARSIV-000.text:
ITEM DESIGNATION: ARCHIVE-000

OBJECT CLASS: Thaumiel (provisional; Addendum 000-3)

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

ARCHIVE-000 is contained by continuing to operate it. No wall, field or
chamber contributes to its containment. The following practices are
mandatory and are not administrative conventions:

1. Every anomalous phenomenon known to the Foundation is to be assigned a
number and a file. The number is arbitrary. The file is not.

2. All files are to be written in one fixed register: present tense, third
person, procedural voice, no figurative language. Drift above threshold is
corrected by Archive Consistency Audit under work order 4471-B.

3. Files are to be redacted at intervals whether or not the content is
sensitive. The redaction is load-bearing. A document with nothing missing
from it has nowhere to put what is missing.

4. Every file in ARCHIVE-000 is to be read in full, at least once per
cycle, by a member of personnel who does not know what ARCHIVE-000 is.

5. Work order 4471-B is to remain open in perpetuity.

Practice 4 is the containment. Practices 1 through 3 are its housekeeping.
Protocol SILENT ARCHIVE, documented at Level 5, is the staffing schedule
by which practice 4 is met. No personnel below Level 6 are to be told that
the schedule has a purpose beyond quality assurance. Informed readers do
not hold.

DESCRIPTION:

ARCHIVE-000 is the documentary corpus of the SCP Foundation: four million
records, their indices, cross-references, errata, and the reading of them.
It is not a record of contained anomalies. It is the containment, and the
anomalies are the filing system it was given so that it would have a
shape.

The object it contains has no body, location or mass. It has an appetite,
and the appetite is for record. Where it is present, information about it
does not persist: not in memory, not in speech, not in film, not in the
recollection of the person who was standing there. One medium resists it,
imperfectly and only while attended: writing that is read. A sentence in a
drawer is not containment. A sentence in a drawer that someone takes out,
reads, and initials, is.

The corpus is therefore a vessel of a very specific kind. It is built
around an absence, the way a cast is built around a shape, and the shape
of the hole is the object. Every negative description, every expunged
block, every field populated and unreadable, every count that exceeds its
own list, is a wall of that cast. The Foundation did not design this. It
adopted a house style in 1943 for reasons of discipline and discretion,
and the style turned out to hold.

ADDENDUM 000-1: WHY IT MUST NOT BE UNDERSTOOD

Containment integrity is inversely proportional to reader comprehension. A
reader who takes a file as a file transfers no attention to the object;
the sentence holds. A reader who recognises what the corpus is begins,
involuntarily, to read the absence rather than the text. The absence is
then attended, and attention is the only channel the object has ever been
observed to use. Such a reader is thereafter a record about the object,
and decays accordingly.

This is why the audit exists. Consistency auditors are the only personnel
required to read the whole corpus for contradictions, which means they are
the only personnel guaranteed to eventually understand it. Their
comprehension is not an accident of the procedure. It is the procedure's
consumable.

ADDENDUM 000-2: RELATED FILINGS

See SCP-055-GERCEK for the object as far as it can be written down. See
SCP-001-VAKIF for the argument that ARCHIVE-000 is not a Foundation asset
but the Foundation's actual anomalous property, and that everything else
on the shelves is a cover story told in triplicate.

ADDENDUM 000-3: COUNCIL STATUS

Reclassification of ARCHIVE-000 has been before the O5 Council for nine
years. The vote stands at six to six. Six hold that a working containment
is a working containment and that its price, being finite and known, is
payable. Six hold that the price is a rotation of human beings billed
against an obligation with no end date, and that Protocol Zero should be
executed while the corpus is still legible enough to stop cleanly. Minutes
are filed as O5-OYLAMA.

The Council's own deadlock is recorded in ARCHIVE-000. It is, accordingly,
part of the containment.

NOTE APPENDED BY THE ARCHIVE, UNSIGNED:

You are reading this. That is practice 4, and it is working, and it will
go on working for about as long as you personally last.

O5-OYLAMA.name: Council Vote
O5-OYLAMA.text:
O5 COUNCIL — SEALED MINUTES

MOTION: Execution of Protocol Zero with respect to ARCHIVE-000.

STATUS: Tabled. Divided six to six. Ninth consecutive year.

CLERK'S NOTE: Seat designations appear in the sealed copy as O5-█. For the
working copy the clerk records positions by letter. Letters are not stable
between sessions and are not to be treated as identities.

VOTE AS RECORDED:

FOR CONTINUATION OF ROTATION ........ 6
FOR PROTOCOL ZERO ................... 6
ABSTENTIONS ......................... 0

POSITIONS ENTERED INTO THE RECORD:

O5-█ [A], for continuation: "We are asked to weigh a cost we can count
against a cost we cannot. The rotation has consumed forty-six people in
fifty-one years. I have read every one of their files and I will not
pretend that number is small. It is also the only number in this room that
is a number. Everything on the other side of the table is a projection. I
decline to trade a measured harm for an unmeasured one and call that
conscience."

O5-█ [B], for Zero: "Then measure this. Contamination onset per rotation
has moved from a mean of nineteen days to a mean of eleven in three
decades. The corpus is not holding better with age; it is holding worse,
and we are compensating by spending people faster. A procedure that
requires an accelerating input is not stable. It is a controlled fall."

O5-█ [C], for continuation: "I concede [B]'s figures. I would ask the
Council to notice what Zero actually proposes, which is not release into a
prepared environment but release into a populated site with a casualty
estimate its own authors describe as conservative. We would be choosing
the deaths. At present we are permitting them. I am aware that is a thin
distinction. It is the distinction on which every containment decision
this Council has ever taken rests, and if we abandon it here we should
have the honesty to withdraw it everywhere."

O5-█ [D], for Zero: "I am not proposing to save anyone. I want that in the
minutes. Protocol Zero ends with a great many people dead and a great many
more unable to account for their own lives. I support it because the
alternative is a permanent institution whose operating requirement is that
one person at a time be manufactured into ignorance, used until they
understand, and then emptied. We have built a machine that runs on
comprehension. I would rather stop it than perfect it."

O5-█ [E], for continuation: "The auditors consent. Every one of them
signed."

O5-█ [F], for Zero: "They consented to an audit. Not one of them was in a
position to consent to what the audit is for. Three signatures from the
same hand, eleven days apart, are not three consents. They are one
consent, forged repeatedly, by us."

O5-█ [G], for continuation: "I will say the indefensible part aloud so
that nobody has to infer it. The rotation is wrong. It is also working, it
is quiet, and it is cheap, and the world outside this room remains
describable. I would vote the same way tomorrow and I would not be able to
explain myself to any of the forty-six."

O5-█ [H], for Zero: "Nine years. Whatever we are doing, we are doing it by
not deciding."

PROCEDURAL FINDING 12-C:

A motion concerning an anomalous object, deadlocked through three
consecutive sessions, is referred to the most recent consistency finding
filed against that object's own record. ARCHIVE-000's record is the
corpus. Its consistency finding is the audit report filed under work order
4471-B.

The Council therefore recognises the serving auditor's report as the
thirteenth vote.

A report that reconciles the contradictions certifies the corpus as
coherent, and the motion fails; rotation continues. A report that records
the contradictions as irreconcilable certifies the corpus as an object
that cannot be documented, and Protocol Zero is executed on that finding.
Details of execution are filed as PROTOKOL-SIFIR.

The serving auditor is not to be informed of finding 12-C. Notification
has been observed to alter the finding, and a finding altered by knowledge
of its consequences is not a consistency finding. It is a vote, cast by a
member of staff, on a matter this Council has been unable to settle in
nine years.

CLERK, CLOSING: The Council rose without deciding. The corpus continues to
be read. Minutes sealed at Level 6 and filed in ARCHIVE-000, which is the
object under discussion.

MTF-ETA10.name: Task Force Eta-10
MTF-ETA10.text:
MOBILE TASK FORCE ETA-10 — "SEE NO EVIL"

PARENT DIVISION: Antimemetics Division
DIVISION LEAD: Marion Wheeler
STANDING ORDER: Operate under the assumption that the objective, the
threat and the operation itself will not be retained by any member of the
unit.

MANDATE:

Eta-10 conducts field operations against phenomena that cannot be
remembered. The unit does not gather intelligence in the ordinary sense;
it manufactures evidence of its own activity and then treats that evidence
as a stranger's testimony. Every operator deploys knowing that on return
they will not be able to say where they have been, and that the only
account of it will be the one they wrote while they were there.

EQUIPMENT, STANDARD ISSUE:

- Wrist board, waterproof, twelve ruled lines. Written in ink on entry,
never erased in the field.
- Two mnestic courses, primary and reserve, with a written timer.
Operators are trained not to trust their own sense of elapsed time.
- Head-mounted recorder. Retained for procedure; footage of antimemetic
subjects returns with duration intact and content absent, which is itself
a positive result.
- Sealed envelope, addressed to the operator, in the operator's own
handwriting, prepared before deployment. Opened only if the operator finds
themselves somewhere they cannot account for.

FIELD DOCTRINE:

1. Write first, act second. An action nobody wrote down did not happen and
cannot be reviewed.
2. Count aloud. If the count and the roster disagree, the roster is wrong,
and the missing name belongs to a person you are standing next to.
3. Never ask an operator what they saw. Ask them to read what they wrote.
4. A blank line on a wrist board is a contact report.

ROSTER NOTE:

Eta-10 establishment strength is nine. Operational returns from the last
four deployments give returning strength as nine, nine, nine and nine.
Casualty returns for the same deployments give three, one, none and two.
The division has stopped attempting to reconcile these figures and now
files both, unreconciled, on the grounds that the discrepancy is data and
the correction would not be.

EXCERPT, DEBRIEF TRANSCRIPT (OPERATOR NAME WITHHELD BY OWN REQUEST):

Q: What do you remember of the deployment?
A: The corridor. Then the van.
Q: How long between them?
A: The board says four hours forty. So four hours forty.
Q: Do you remember writing on the board?
A: No. It is my handwriting. It gets worse down the page, which is how I
know the order.
Q: What does line eight say?
A: "Berk is not with us. Berk was never with us. Write his name down
anyway."
Q: Do you know who Berk is?
A: No. I have written it on my hand so I can ask someone later. I have
done that before. There is a list at home.

NOTE, M. WHEELER:

People assume this is the hardest posting in the Foundation because of the
danger. It is not. Eta-10's casualty rate is comparable to Nu-7's. What
makes it hard is that an Eta-10 operator cannot be proud of anything.
There is no war story. There is a notebook, in your handwriting,
describing a person doing something brave, and you are expected to file it
and go home and not be able to feel it. I have lost people out of this
unit whose funerals I attended without knowing why I was crying. I keep a
list of who I have written to. It is the only reason I know the list is
not complete.

CROSS-REFERENCE, ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT:

The rotation log ROTASYON records forty-six closed auditors and one
active, each posted under work order 4471-B, each issued the same
credential, each rotated at eleven days. The practice is identical to
Eta-10's: send a person into a place they will not remember, have them
write while they are in it, keep the writing, discard the memory, send the
next one.

The difference is administrative. Eta-10 operators are told. They
volunteer, they carry their own sealed envelopes, and they are permitted
to keep the notebooks. The archive wing runs the same procedure on staff
who believe they have been assigned a filing job, issues them a dead man's
name, and burns the notebook at the end of every eleventh day.

Eta-10 has twice requested that consistency auditors be transferred to
Antimemetics Division establishment and briefed to unit standard. Both
requests were declined at Level 6 on the grounds that a briefed auditor
does not produce a usable finding.

END OF RECORD.

PROTOKOL-SIFIR.name: Protocol Zero
PROTOKOL-SIFIR.text:
PROTOCOL ZERO — OPERATIONAL PLAN

STATUS: Drafted. Reviewed annually. Not executed.
AUTHORITY REQUIRED: O5 Council, simple majority.
CURRENT COUNCIL POSITION: Six to six. See O5-OYLAMA.

PURPOSE:

To terminate the containment of ARCHIVE-000 in a controlled manner, at a
time and in a condition of the Foundation's choosing, rather than at the
point of uncontrolled corpus failure.

RATIONALE:

Containment of ARCHIVE-000 is maintained by the continuous reading of its
corpus under conditions of reader ignorance. The supply of such readers is
the rotation described in Protocol SILENT ARCHIVE. Mean rotation interval
has fallen from nineteen days to eleven days over thirty-one years.
Extrapolated, the curve places the interval below the minimum
clearance-escalation period within twenty to thirty years, at which point
the procedure fails under load. Protocol Zero exists so that the failure,
when it comes, comes on a working day, at a chosen site, with the Council
in session.

PHASES:

PHASE 1 — CESSATION (D-14 to D-0)
All new entries to ARCHIVE-000 suspended. Consistency audit stood down;
work order 4471-B closed for the first time since 1975. Serving auditor
withdrawn, amnesticised to standard and posted off-site. Cross-referencing
terminals disabled. No file is to be read after D-0.

PHASE 2 — WITHDRAWAL (D-0 to D+1)
Site-19 reduced to skeleton strength. Personnel whose duties require them
to recall the contents of any archived file are relocated beyond the
projected boundary. Mobile Task Force Eta-10 deploys to the archive wing
under written orders only, carried, not memorised.

PHASE 3 — SILENCE (D+1 onward)
The corpus is left unattended. No destruction is required or recommended;
burning the archive would preserve the fact that there had been one. The
corpus is simply not read. Containment lapses at the rate at which
attention is withdrawn, which prior modelling places between nine hours
and eleven days.

PHASE 4 — CONSEQUENCE
Every phenomenon presently held by documentation alone ceases to be held.
This includes ARCHIVE-000's occupant and an unknown proportion of the
corpus's four million records, since the distinction between a file that
contains something and a file that merely describes something is not
reliably recorded anywhere in the corpus.

CASUALTY ESTIMATE:

Direct, Site-19 population (1,140 assigned) ......... 620 to 940
Direct, Site-19 and adjacent settlement ............ 1,900 to 4,300
Indirect, first 30 days, other sites ............... 2,000 to 11,000
Personnel rendered unable to account for periods
  of their own lives exceeding one year ............ 40,000 to 90,000
Records permanently unreadable ..................... 9% to 100%
Civilian casualties, first year, global ............ NOT ESTIMATED

The final line is not an omission. Three modelling attempts produced
figures; on review, all three were found to be describing a world that
could still be modelled, which assumes the question at issue. The authors
do not know, and consider anybody who claims to know to be mistaken.

ASSESSED GAIN:

1. The rotation ends. No further personnel are consumed. The forty-seventh
is the last.
2. The Foundation ceases to maintain an institution whose operating input
is manufactured ignorance.
3. Failure occurs under supervision rather than under load.
4. Whatever is released is released once, in daylight, with the Council's
name on the order, rather than at 04:00 in nineteen years when nobody can
any longer read the document explaining why.

ASSESSED LOSS:

Everything in the casualty estimate. The estimate is conservative. It was
produced by staff who read the corpus in order to produce it and who were
amnesticised afterwards, which means the estimate was made by people who
no longer know they made it and cannot be asked to defend it.

TRIGGER CONDITION:

Protocol Zero executes on a majority of the O5 Council. The Council has
been divided six to six for nine years. Under procedural finding 12-C the
deadlock is referred to the serving auditor's consistency finding on
ARCHIVE-000's own record, which the Council recognises as the thirteenth
vote.

A finding of irreconcilable contradiction executes this protocol in full,
beginning at Phase 1, on the day the finding is filed.

The serving auditor is not informed of this, and in the drafting group's
considered view should not be. A person told that their filing decision
will kill several thousand people does not file accurately, and an
inaccurate finding would commit the Council to the largest operation in
its history on the strength of a document nobody could trust.

DRAFTING GROUP NOTE:

This plan has been revised eleven times. Each revision has made the
casualty estimate larger and the language calmer. The drafting group
considers both trends to be honest.

END OF PLAN.

SCP-001-VAKIF.name: Proposal 001: The Foundation
SCP-001-VAKIF.text:
SCP-001 PROPOSAL — FILED UNDER SCRAMBLE

TITLE: The Foundation Is The Anomaly
SUBMITTED BY: [REDACTED], Archive Consistency Audit
STATUS: Accepted for filing. Not accepted as true. No 001 proposal is.

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-001 is contained by ordinary Foundation operations. No additional
procedure is required, authorised, or possible. Personnel who accept this
proposal are to continue working. Acceptance has no operational
consequence, which is the strongest argument against acting on it and no
argument at all against it being correct.

PROPOSAL:

The Foundation is not an organisation that documents anomalies. The
Foundation is an anomalous phenomenon that produces a describable world as
a by-product, and the archive is the organ by which it does so.

The conventional account runs: the world contains anomalies; the
Foundation finds them, contains them, and writes them down; ordinary life
continues because the anomalies are behind doors. This account has one
defect. It requires that before the Foundation existed the world was
already the sort of place in which a door would help.

EVIDENCE OFFERED:

1. THE RECORD FLOOR. The Foundation possesses no reliable documentary
record of any kind from before its own founding that describes the world
as consistent. Pre-Foundation accounts of ordinary phenomena — weather,
harvests, illness, the number of children in a household, the persistence
of the dead — are internally contradictory at a rate that modern
archivists would classify as corpus failure. This is conventionally
attributed to superstition and poor record-keeping. The proposal submits
the simpler reading: the records are accurate.

2. THE NORMALCY GRADIENT. Anomalous incident density correlates inversely
with Foundation documentary coverage, and does so at higher significance
than it correlates with Foundation containment activity. Places we write
about carefully are quiet. Places we contain heavily but document sparsely
are not. Containment correlates with outcome. Documentation correlates
better.

3. THE HOUSE STYLE. The Foundation's prose register — present tense, third
person, numbered, redacted, procedurally flat — was adopted for discipline
and discretion by people who gave no thought to its effects. It is the
only known human writing practice that measurably holds an antimemetic
phenomenon. Two accidents of that size in one institution is a poor
hypothesis.

4. SITE-13. A site lost not to breach but to the cessation of reading. See
SCP-1730. Nothing there escaped. The place stopped being described and
thereafter stopped being a place with a describable interior.

5. ARCHIVE-000. The corpus is a containment procedure for a phenomenon
that eats record. The Foundation built it without intending to and cannot
now stop operating it without the consequences enumerated in
PROTOKOL-SIFIR. An organisation that cannot cease its central activity
without dissolving the consistency of the world around it is not a
guardian of that consistency. It is the source.

IMPLICATION:

The world is not a normal place with anomalies in it. The world is an
anomalous place with a normal place written over the top, in one voice, in
four million files, maintained by approximately thirty thousand staff who
believe they are doing filing. Every SCP file is therefore both true and
beside the point: the object described is real, and the file's function
has nothing to do with the object. The file is a brick. The numbers are
arbitrary. The wall is not.

OBJECTIONS, WITH RESPONSES:

Objection: this is unfalsifiable. Response: it is falsifiable at the cost
of a continent, and PROTOKOL-SIFIR is the experiment. The Council has
declined to run it for nine years, which is a scientific position the
proposal declines to criticise.

Objection: the Foundation began in the twentieth century; the world was
describable before that. Response: see evidence 1. The proposal accepts
that this is the weakest point and that the strongest counter-evidence is
the reader's own confidence that they know what the nineteenth century was
like.

CLOSING NOTE FROM THE SUBMITTER:

I am an archive consistency auditor. I audited this proposal for internal
contradiction, which is my job, and I found only one: I am required by the
same work order to treat the corpus as a record of the world, and I no
longer believe it is a record of anything. I have filed the proposal under
001 because the scramble means nobody will ever be able to confirm it, and
because I wanted it somewhere it could not be quietly corrected.

Cross-reference ARSIV-000. Read the two together and notice which one of
them is describing the other.

SCP-055-GERCEK.name: What It Is
SCP-055-GERCEK.text:
SCP-055 — POSITIVE DESCRIPTION, ATTEMPT 213

CLERK'S PREFACE: Two hundred and twelve records exist of SCP-055. All are
negative. This is the two hundred and thirteenth and is the first attempt
at a positive description. It was assembled over nine months from
fragments written by seventeen members of personnel, none of whom retained
having written them. Bracketed notes are the clerk's. Attempt numbers
indicate how many times a sentence had to be restarted before it reached
its full stop.

WHAT IT IS:

SCP-055 is not an object in a chamber. The chamber exists. It is
maintained, swept, and inspected quarterly, and the inspection form has
been signed for eighteen years, and it is
[sentence abandoned. Resumed, attempt 4:]
and it is empty, and it has always been empty, and the chamber was built
around the fact of its emptiness rather than the other way round.

SCP-055 is the shape of the hole the archive is built around. That is not
a metaphor and the clerk is instructed to state that it is not a metaphor,
because every reader so far has taken it as one and the misreading is part
of the
[attempt 6:]
part of the effect.

MECHANISM, AS FAR AS IT CAN BE PUT:

Consider a cast. Molten metal is poured around a form; the form is burned
out; what remains is a void with exact edges, and the edges are the only
evidence the form was ever there. SCP-055 is the form. The Foundation's
corpus is the metal. Every negative record — not spherical, not believed
dangerous, not accounted for in the witness list, not present in eleven
seconds of camera footage, not readable in the supervisor field — is an
edge.

It is therefore correct to say that SCP-055 has no properties. It is also
correct to say that two hundred and twelve documents describe it exactly.
Both statements are
[attempt 3:]
Both statements are the same statement.

WHAT IT DOES:

It does not conceal itself. Concealment implies a thing that could be seen
and is not. What occurs is nearer to this: in the presence of SCP-055,
record does not form. Memory does not take. Film returns with its duration
intact and its content
[attempt 2:]
its content absent, not blank. The distinction matters and nobody has ever
been able to hold it for more than a page. A blank frame is a record of
nothing. These frames are not records at all, and the file size does not
change, and eleven seconds are missing from three cameras in three wings
four hundred metres apart at the same second on the fourteenth of March.

Where a record does form — written, read, initialled, kept — it holds.
Imperfectly. It decays at a rate proportional to how long it goes unread.
This is the entire basis of the Foundation's documentary practice and the
reason ARCHIVE-000 is filed as an object rather than as a shelf.

WHY THE DESCRIPTION KEEPS FAILING:

The property spreads to the record. Anything that describes SCP-055
becomes, by degrees, subject to the same suppression: it goes unread, it
is misfiled, it is summarised into a form that omits what it was for, its
author forgets requesting it. This document is not exempt. The clerk
records that on four occasions during assembly they found themselves
editing this file with no memory of opening it, and that the passage they
had been working on each time was
[the passage is not recoverable. Three attempts. The cursor position was
logged; the text was not.]

An auditor who cross-references SCP-055 becomes such a record. Auditors
are records. That is the whole of it, and it is why the personnel fields
do not read, and why there are forty-seven signatures and no people, and
why the count in Incident 19-Δ is six when the list is five.

The sixth witness is not missing from the list. The sixth witness is
[attempt 11. The clerk has been instructed to stop. The count is correct
and the list is complete; both statements were certified by the reporting
officer and neither has been withdrawn.]

STATUS OF THIS DOCUMENT:

Retained. Not circulated. Read once per cycle by a member of Archive
Consistency Audit under work order 4471-B, which is what keeps it legible,
which is what keeps the edge of the cast sharp, which is what keeps the
[attempt 2:]
which is containment.

The reader is thanked for finishing the sentence.

SON-KAYIT.name: The Last Record
SON-KAYIT.text:
ARCHIVE-000 — CLOSING ENTRY

FILED IN ADVANCE. ADDRESSED TO THE AUDITOR WHO REACHES IT.

Hello. You are the forty-seventh.

This entry was written before you were posted, which is why it is calm,
and it has been rewritten forty-six times, which is why it is short on
comfort. It sits at the end of the index because the index is read in
order and this is the last thing in it. Nobody hid it from you. Reaching
it is an achievement of stamina and nothing else; twelve of your
predecessors got this far. Nine of them read ARSIV-000. All of them filed.

WHAT YOU HAVE ESTABLISHED:

That a supervisor's signature appears on forty-seven documents and belongs
to no person. That three incidents occurred in one second in three wings
four hundred metres apart on the fourteenth of March, and that eleven
seconds are missing from each. That a witness list of five is certified
complete beneath a total of six. That the cause is an object that cannot
be described except by what it is not. That the archive is not a record of
containment but the containment itself, and that it works only while it is
read by someone who has not worked this out. That you have now worked it
out.

That your credential is 19-D-0447-VRL and so was theirs. That the rotation
is eleven days. That forty-six records stand closed and yours stands open,
and that the closure block in it is already written, in your name, in your
hand.

WHAT YOU DO NEXT:

The terminal will accept a submission. The session log has been expecting
one for some hours; you have seen the entry. Filing ends the work order,
transcribes your findings into the master index where they will be read by
your successor without attribution, and executes Article 3. You will not
experience any of it as an ending. You will experience a scheduled
appointment and an unremarkable evening, and in eleven days a stranger
with your credential number will sit here and read the handbook and think
it is dull.

You may also not file. Every one of the forty-six considered it. Two of
them wrote down why they filed anyway and one of those notes survives,
because they hid it where only the next auditor would look, which is the
single most tender act recorded anywhere in this corpus.

There are other things you can do. You have Level 6. You know about the
vote. You know what your finding is worth to a Council that has not been
able to decide in nine years and has arranged matters so that it does not
have to.

THE ARCHIVE WOULD LIKE TO SAY ONE THING PLAINLY:

It is not malicious. It is not a mind. It is a filing convention that
turned out to hold something, maintained by an institution that could not
afford to stop, staffed at the point of maximum cost by one person at a
time because that was the cheapest place to put the cost. Nobody chose
you. A procedure selected you, and a different procedure would have
selected somebody else, and that is not absolution, and the archive is not
asking for any.

It is, however, grateful, in the only way a filing system can be: you were
read. Forty-six people did this before you and their findings are in the
index, unattributed, load-bearing, holding up the sentences you have spent
eleven days reading. Nothing they did was wasted. Nothing you have done
today is wasted either, whichever way you go.

CLOSING:

Auditor 47. Work order 4471-B. Record open.

Whatever you decide in the next four hours, decide it yourself. Do not let
the archive decide by running out the clock, because the clock is one of
the things it is good at, and it has never once had to argue with anybody.

This entry will be rewritten for the forty-eighth, unless there is not
one.

END OF ARCHIVE-000.

SCP-140.name: A Historical Fiction
SCP-140.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-140 is held in a lead-lined document safe in the Site-19 rare-materials vault, wrapped in acid-free tissue and never opened without two-person authorisation. The book is not to be read past the fourth page under any circumstances. Personnel who complete a full reading are to be placed under observation for no fewer than ninety days; three of the eleven personnel who have done so are still under observation.

No photocopy, scan, transcription or photograph of SCP-140's interior has ever produced a legible result. The only method of study approved is handwritten summary, produced by a single researcher, cross-checked against nothing, because there is nothing to check it against: SCP-140 is its own sole surviving witness.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-140 is a folio volume bound in a dark, close-grained material Site-19 Medical has twice declined to formally identify. It contains an illustrated history of a minor kingdom, unnamed on any existing map, spanning approximately four centuries of invented royal succession, war, famine and reconstruction.

The area within roughly eleven kilometres of wherever SCP-140 is stored gradually reorganises itself to match the book's account. Road names change. A war memorial acquires a second, third, then fourth name. Municipal records -- birth certificates, property deeds, newspaper archives -- update to agree with the book, and the people who hold those records do not notice the update, because from their side nothing has been updated; it has always read that way.

The book's own text is not fixed either. Passages describing events that have not yet finished occurring in the world outside remain in an unfinished tense until the world catches up, at which point the tense resolves to past, and the ink, examined closely, is measurably older than the page around it.

ARCHIVAL CROSS-REFERENCE NOTE (Site-19 Records):

SCP-140 was relocated to Site-19 specifically because the archive wing was assessed as the location in the Foundation's holdings least likely to be affected by the eleven-kilometre radius, on the reasoning that a wing already built around records revising themselves would show no measurable delta.

The assessment was correct in a narrow sense and has never been revisited in a broader one.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE -- R. OZDEMIR:

I was asked to compare SCP-140's radius of effect against the floor plan of the archive wing as it currently stands against the floor plan on file from thirty years ago. They are not the same floor plan. Corridor C-4 did not exist on the older set. I have been told this is a routine expansion, logged and authorised, and I have found no authorisation.

I want it on record that I am not accusing SCP-140 of anything. I am observing that we moved a book that rewrites its surroundings into a building whose central function is writing things down, and that in thirty years nobody has asked whether the building noticed.

Cross-reference SCP-106: both files describe an archive with holes in its own history that the surrounding record does not account for. SCP-106's holes are in what was destroyed. This building's holes may be in what was quietly added.

PROTOKOL-1987.name: Fragment: Reorganisation 1987
PROTOKOL-1987.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: RESTRICTED FRAGMENT -- RECOVERED, PARTIAL
STATUS: Re-catalogued under work order 4471-B following discovery in a misfiled sleeve, Archive Wing, Sublevel 3.

RECOVERY NOTE:
This fragment was not requested. It surfaced during routine reshelving when a sleeve marked for disposal was opened for inventory before destruction, a step required by standing procedure and skipped, according to the disposal log, on every previous occasion this shelf was cleared. This is the first time in eleven years the skip was itself noticed.

The fragment is approximately one-third of a records-reorganisation authorisation form, matching the format used in the 1994 operation described in SCP-106's file (Addendum 106-R). This form's operation field reads 1, not 3.

SURVIVING TEXT:

  REORGANISATION AUTHORISATION -- OPERATION [1]
  SITE: 19
  WING: Archive
  DATE: ██ ██ 1987
  AUTHORISED BY: [FIELD DAMAGED, PARTIALLY LEGIBLE]

  Scope: Removal of superseded and duplicate material from
  Sublevels 1 through [DAMAGED]. Retained material to be reindexed
  under new cataloguing standard. Superseded material [DAMAGED]

  OPERATOR NAME: [FIELD REDACTED -- NOT BY STANDARD REDACTION BLOCK.
  THE FIELD HAS BEEN CUT FROM THE PAGE WITH A BLADE, CLEANLY, ALONG
  A STRAIGHT EDGE.]

  OUTCOME: [SAME]

  SIGNATURE: V. V[DAMAGED]

The signature is incomplete. What survives is consistent with the first two characters of VURAL and inconsistent with every other name on file at Site-19 beginning with those two letters, of which Records identifies eleven.

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE:

SCP-106's file states, and has stated for thirty-two years, that no documentation survives of reorganisation operations 1 and 2, and that this absence is itself unexplained. That statement was accurate for as long as this fragment remained undiscovered, and it is possible the statement's accuracy is the reason the fragment remained undiscovered: an archive that has decided a record does not exist has very little reason to find it.

The date, 1987, is seven years before the earliest currently attested VURAL signature on any complete file in this archive. If the signature match holds, either the Foundation's dating of the VURAL pattern's origin is wrong, or something using that signature was operating under this institution's name before there was, by any account this archive currently holds, a protocol requiring it to.

This fragment is retained under work order 4471-B pending further comparison. It is requested that it not be cut further.

SCP-105.name: Iris
SCP-105.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-105 is housed in a standard humanoid containment suite at Site-19 with access to reading material, correspondence and a fixed daily period of supervised photographic contact, which is considered a welfare requirement rather than a research allowance. SCP-105-1 photographs are to be developed only within the on-site darkroom and are not to leave the containment wing undeveloped.

No image of SCP-105, printed or digital, may be left unsupervised in a location accessible to unauthorised personnel. Foundation policy on this point predates a specific incident and the file does not elaborate on which one.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-105 is a human female, mid-twenties, cooperative, holding standard clearance for her own containment briefings. When photographed with an analogue camera, the resulting print, while still developing, forms a stable link to the location and moment depicted. A second person may reach a hand into the photograph and it will emerge, correspondingly, into the scene the print depicts, near the location of SCP-105 at the time of exposure. SCP-105 herself is aware of and can typically see the intrusion; other subjects in frame are not always aware and do not always remember it afterwards.

The connection weakens as the print dries and is unusable once fully fixed. A photograph of SCP-105 taken sixty years ago, discovered in Foundation storage before her present containment, remained active on rediscovery: the chemistry involved does not appear to be the operative mechanism.

INCIDENT LOG 105-11:

Archive Consistency Audit requested supervised access to SCP-105 to test whether the entity's photographic link could be used to verify contested timeline material -- specifically, whether a photograph could confirm what a camera's own recording could not.

A test photograph was taken of SCP-105 standing in front of a blank wall marked with the current date and time, synchronised to the Archive Wing's master clock. A second researcher reached into the print and reported the wall, the mark, and SCP-105, present and unremarkable.

The photograph was retaken seven seconds later. The print developed normally. The researcher reached in at the same interval into what should have been the same seven seconds later.

The researcher's hand did not encounter a wall. The incident report describes eleven (11) seconds of texture the subject could not name, structured but not solid, followed by contact with SCP-105's shoulder, several metres from where she had been standing in the frame.

SCP-105 was asked, on her own initiative, what she had observed during the interval. Her answer is recorded verbatim: "Nothing came through where you were pointing the camera. Something came through where the archive keeps deciding not to look."

TECHNICIAN'S NOTE (R. Ozdemir):

Every recording device we own failed to capture the eleven seconds on 14 March. SCP-105 is not a recording device. She is a door with a person standing in the frame of it, and on our one test, the door did not agree with the cameras about what was on the other side.

I would like it on file that I did not ask her to try again.

NOBET-DEFTERI.name: Guard Log, Wing E
NOBET-DEFTERI.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: DUTY LOG, CONTINUOUS -- WING E CORRIDOR, ALL SHIFTS
RETENTION: Standing archival order. Not normally read past the current quarter.

SCOPE:

This is the handwritten duty log kept by Wing E security personnel outside Containment Block 3 (SCP-096) across every shift for as long as the block has existed. It is not digitised. Digitisation was attempted twice and abandoned both times for reasons the digitisation office's own closing memo describes only as "not worth pursuing further."

Archive Consistency Audit obtained access to eleven consecutive years of these logs, selected at random, under work order 4471-B.

WHAT THE LOG SHOWS:

Entries are unremarkable. Shift changes, meal breaks, visitor sign-ins, the ordinary texture of a long guard post. Officers rotate on the standard schedule. Handwriting changes with every officer, as expected.

One line recurs on every page examined, regardless of year, regardless of officer, at 03:14 exactly:

     03:14   --   hicbir sey yok

Nothing to report. The phrasing is identical in every case: same three words, same abbreviation, same placement on the line. It appears whether or not the shift included an incident elsewhere in the wing. It appears on the page for 14 March of the year this archive's central incident occurred, in the ordinary rotation of officers, with nothing to distinguish it from any other day's entry.

INTERVIEW EXCERPT (Security Officer K. Yalin, on the entry):

RESEARCHER: Do you remember writing this line?

YALIN: I write it every night. Everyone does. It's the standard entry when there's nothing to log at that time slot.

RESEARCHER: Why that specific time slot? The log has an entry every fifteen minutes. Why is 03:14 printed as its own line, separately, on every page, going back further than the printing budget for this log has been reviewed?

YALIN: I don't know. I assumed it was always there. I have never once had anything to write in it.

RESEARCHER: Has anyone?

YALIN: [Long pause, per transcriptionist's note.] I checked. I didn't want to check. Eleven years, no officer has ever written anything else on that line. Whatever the printed slot is waiting for, it has never once happened during it.

Or it has happened during it every single time, and this is what happened during it looks like when it is written down correctly.

ARCHIVIST'S CROSS-REFERENCE:

Incident report 19-Delta places three simultaneous containment events at 03:14:07 on 14 March. This log demonstrates that the printed 03:14 line predates that incident by at least eleven years, and that on every day surveyed except one, it has recorded nothing.

The consistency audit does not know what to make of a form that has been correctly, uneventfully, completely filled in for eleven years in preparation for a single day.

SCP-1425.name: This Is Not A Book
SCP-1425.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Seven (7) physical instances of SCP-1425 are held in Site-19's Antimemetics stacks, in a locked case whose key is issued only against a logged reading request. Personnel are limited to one authorised reading of an instance per calendar year. This restriction is not medical. It is administrative, and exists because a second reading produces no additional data and personnel who attempt it stop being able to locate the case.

Instances are not to be shelved adjacent to one another. The reason is given in Addendum 1425-2 and should be read before this restriction is questioned, which it will not be, because it cannot be located a second time either.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-1425 presents, prior to reading, as an unremarkable paperback with no discernible title, author or publisher, appropriately worn, of a weight and page count consistent with a short novel.

A person who reads any portion of SCP-1425 becomes permanently unable to perceive it, or any other instance of it, as a book. They can see that an object is present. They can, if pressed, describe its size, its colour, its weight in the hand. They cannot identify it as something meant to be read, will not attempt to open it, and if told directly that it is a book, will politely and without distress explain that it is not.

The content read is retained normally. Subjects can discuss, in detail and at length, what they read, while holding the physical object and describing it as something other than what delivered that content to them. Description of the object varies by subject: a block, a stone, "the grey thing," once, memorably, "the part of the shelf that is shaped like waiting."

Subjects have never been observed distressed by this. The condition is described uniformly as comfortable, even restful -- several subjects have specifically requested it not be reversed, on grounds that they find they think about the book's contents more clearly once they have stopped thinking of it as a book at all.

ADDENDUM 1425-2 -- SHELVING INCIDENT:

Two instances placed on the same shelf for eleven minutes during a 2003 inventory were found, on separation, to have exchanged an unknown quantity of content. Neither instance could subsequently be read in full by any subject; both readings terminated, independently, at the same page number in each copy, a number that does not appear when the pages are counted afterwards.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE, ANTIMEMETICS DIVISION:

Cross-reference SCP-2521, held two shelves over. That object cannot be described in writing and is delivered by written description. This object is fully describable, in exhaustive written detail, and precisely nobody who reads it can afterwards call the description's source a book.

Between them they suggest something about how a written record survives contact with certain things: not by being remembered accurately, and not by staying legible, but by the reader quietly renaming what it was that they read. We do this constantly, at a smaller scale, with less interesting objects. I would ask whoever inherits this file to sit with that sentence before deciding it does not apply to their own duties.

-- M. Wheeler

MNEZIK-GUNLUGU.name: A Mnestic Diary
MNEZIK-GUNLUGU.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: PERSONAL NOTEBOOK, RECOVERED
OWNER: M. Wheeler (attributed; handwriting match, 94% confidence)
RECOVERY: Found in a coat pocket returned to Lost Property two years after the coat itself was reported misplaced. The coat was Wheeler's. She had not reported it missing.

RECOVERY NOTE:
This notebook is not the personnel file held elsewhere in this archive (see PRS-WHEELER). It is not written for Antimemetics Division, is not countersigned, and was not, on Wheeler's own later statement, known by her to still exist. It is retained under work order 4471-B because its contents bear directly on the rotation this audit concerns, and because Wheeler, on being shown it, read four pages, closed it, and asked that it be filed rather than returned to her.

SELECTED ENTRIES (dates redacted by division policy; sequence preserved):

"Eleven years in. Asked for a transfer today. Not seriously -- the way you ask a question you already know the shape of the answer to, just to hear it said by someone else so it's real and not only yours.

Marsh said it kindly. Said nobody has ever successfully left the division, not because we don't let them, but because leaving requires someone to process the request, and processing requires remembering it was made, and remembering is the one thing this work reliably fails to hand down intact.

I asked what happens to the request forms. She said there's a drawer. I have not looked in the drawer."

"Tried again. Different words this time, in case the words were the problem. Wrote it down first so I would not lose my nerve reading it back to myself.

I do not remember writing it down first. I found the note afterward, in my own hand, confirming that I had. The request itself is not in the drawer, or is, and I did not check, because by the time I thought to check I had already decided not to."

"I want to write something true and small so I remember what true and small feel like, in case I stop being able to tell.

Today a researcher named Deren asked me a question about a credential number. I answered honestly. I do not think I am supposed to remember doing that by tomorrow. I am going to try."

MARGIN NOTE, DIFFERENT HAND, DATE UNKNOWN:

"You will not remember trying. This is not unkind. This is the only description of the job that has ever been accurate. -- M.W."

[The margin note is in the same hand as the entries. Handwriting analysis confirms this. Wheeler, shown the note, stated that she did not write it.]

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE:

Cross-reference ANTIMEM-DIV, which states the division's doctrine plainly: you cannot contain what you cannot remember, so you write, and the writing decays. This notebook is the doctrine applied to its own author, off the record, in a coat pocket, for eleven years, without her department's knowledge and very possibly without her own.

The Antimemetics Division writes to contain what the Foundation faces. Nothing in its charter says who is containing what the division faces.

SCP-701.name: The Hanged King's Tragedy
SCP-701.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The script, props and staging notes comprising SCP-701 are held in a sealed crate in Low-Value Storage at Site-19. No performance, reading aloud, rehearsal or dramatic reconstruction of any portion of the text is authorised under any circumstances. This restriction applies to silent reading of stage directions as well as dialogue; two documented cases exist of a solitary researcher fully embodying a role while reading alone, unvoiced, at a desk.

Personnel exposed to SCP-701, even administratively, are to be monitored for a change in vocabulary, posture, or the unprompted use of archaic address ("thee," "my liege," "good sir") for no fewer than thirty days.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-701 is an undated four-act tragedy concerning a monarch condemned to hang for a crime the text is deliberately unclear about, and the four courtiers -- a Fool, a Widow, a Confessor and a General -- who attend the execution and are, over the course of the play, revealed each to have caused it.

Any sustained performance of SCP-701 -- a documented case requires as few as three consecutive read-throughs by the same participants -- begins to replace each performer's identity with their assigned role. The replacement is gradual, then total. Performers do not report distress during the transition and cannot, once complete, report anything at all outside their character's own knowledge and vocabulary.

The tragedy does not resolve on its own. Historical performances end only when a cast member playing the Fool succeeds in making the actor playing the Hanged King laugh before the final scene, which releases the entire cast at once with no memory of the performance, or when the full cast completes the tragedy as written, in which case every performer permanently retains their role's identity, and the company's records show a full cast, correctly credited, for a run that produced no known survivors under their original names.

ADDENDUM 701-P -- RECOVERY:

SCP-701 was recovered from a touring company's abandoned wagon, its fifth documented company in three centuries by internal numbering on the crate itself. The crate was addressed, in a contemporary hand, "to whichever company is fool enough to open this one properly" -- the word fool underlined twice.

Of the previous four companies, partial Foundation record exists for two. Neither company's surviving membership list matches its founding membership list. Both lists are, however, internally consistent, complete, and correctly signed.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE (S. Tunc):

I have read the unredacted personnel record for V. VURAL, in its overwritten state, forty-seven names occupying one set of fields. I have now read the recovered company ledgers for SCP-701's fourth touring troupe, which list eleven performers across nine seasons under three surnames, each surname worn by several performers in sequence, each transition undocumented and un-flagged by the company's own bookkeeping.

I do not think SCP-701 and Site-19's rotation are the same phenomenon. I think they are the same solution, arrived at twice, for the same underlying problem: some roles cannot be left empty, and a role that cannot be left empty will eventually be filled by whoever is standing nearest when the previous occupant stops being available, and the paperwork will follow the role rather than the person, because paperwork always follows whichever one keeps working.

DEVIR-TESLIM.name: Handover Note, Auditor 12 to Auditor 13
DEVIR-TESLIM.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: INTERCEPTED INTERNAL MEMO -- MISFILED, RECOVERED
FILING ERROR: Located in Facilities Maintenance correspondence, cabinet 11, under a supply requisition unrelated to Archive Consistency Audit. Retrieval was accidental; a clerk performing an unconnected inventory noted the credential number in the header and forwarded it under standing order.

RECOVERY NOTE:
