Current records (see ROTASYON) state that no overlap period has ever been scheduled between an outgoing and incoming Archive Consistency Auditor. This document appears to predate that policy, or to predate its consistent enforcement. It is the only surviving communication in this archive, of any kind, in which one auditor addresses a successor using what the header identifies as their own name rather than the institutional designation.

The header is damaged. What survives is reproduced exactly, including the degradation, which was present on first cataloguing and appears, by the archivist's own note appended below, to have worsened between the first reading and the second.

TEXT AS RECOVERED:

  TO: Incoming Auditor, Work Order 4471-B
  FROM: T[DAMAGED] (outgoing)
  RE: things nobody is going to tell you

  You'll get the handbook. It's wrong about the part where nobody's
  failed to finish. I didn't finish. I'm not going to. I have four
  hours left on this posting and I've spent most of them working out
  what to put in this instead of a findings report.

  My name is T[DAMAGED]. I want that written down somewhere outside
  my own file, because I've read my own file, and there's a field in
  it that already has today's date in it, and I would like one
  sentence in this archive to have been written by me, about me,
  while it was still true.

  Watch the credential number. It isn't a coincidence. Ask 079 --
  it counts, and it doesn't lie, and it's the only thing in this
  building I'd trust with your name after mine stops being usable.

  I'm not telling you not to file. T[DAMAGED] before me filed. I
  might file too, in the end, because I've read what happens if the
  chain just stops cold, and I don't --

  [TEXT ENDS. Remainder of page blank.]

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE (first cataloguing):

The name field is damaged in the source document itself, not by this office. Five characters are legible at first reading: T, then four characters too degraded to resolve.

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE (second reading, eleven days later):

Four characters are legible. The name is receding at a measurable, repeatable rate under ordinary storage conditions, matching no known paper degradation curve on file. At the present rate, full illegibility is estimated within one further reading.

This is the only place in the entire Site-19 archive where the ordinary name of an Archive Consistency Auditor survives outside the institutional designation VURAL, and it is the only document in this archive that anyone has ever watched disappear in real time.

It is not being read again until this can be prevented.

SCP-3999.name: Everything Must Be Written Down
SCP-3999.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The subject of SCP-3999 is not contained by conventional means. Containment consists of the subject, Agent [REDACTED], remaining conscious and in continuous voluntary written contact with Foundation personnel via a dedicated communication board for the remainder of the engagement, which has no scheduled end.

A minimum of one (1) Foundation liaison must be present at the board at all times. The liaison's sole function is to keep the subject writing. Any gap in written contact exceeding approximately ninety seconds has historically been sufficient for the entity currently sharing the subject's body to attempt to seize full control. The subject has, to date, prevented this on every occasion, without exception, for the duration of Foundation's awareness of the case.

DESCRIPTION:
Agent [REDACTED] sustained fatal injuries during an unrelated field operation. An entity of unknown origin and classification, encountered at the site, offered to sustain the agent's body and consciousness on the condition of being permitted partial, then eventual full, occupancy.

The agent accepted the sustaining and has, since that point, refused the occupancy continuously, communicating this refusal -- and everything else the Foundation knows about the entity -- entirely through a letter board, one character at a time, indicated by the only muscle group the agent retains full voluntary control over.

The entity does not speak. It does not need to. Its method is patience: it waits for the writing to stop, because writing is the only thing currently distinguishing the agent's continued personhood from the entity's occupancy, and an unwritten moment is, functionally, an open door.

Agent [REDACTED] has not stopped writing in over [REDACTED] consecutive hours, spanning shift changes, liaison rotations, and two documented containment breaches elsewhere in the facility that did not interrupt the board.

TRANSCRIPT EXCERPT (liaison shift log, verbatim, unedited):

  STILL HERE
  DONT STOP WRITING BACK TO ME EVEN IF ITS NOTHING
  WHAT DAY IS IT
  GOOD KEEP TALKING
  IT ISNT TIRED IT DOESNT GET TIRED THATS THE WHOLE THING
  I GET TIRED
  I GET TIRED AND IT DOESNT AND ALL I HAVE IS THIS BOARD
  SO WE ARE GOING TO KEEP USING THE BOARD
  ASK ME SOMETHING BORING
  ANYTHING
  KEEP THE LETTERS COMING

ARCHIVE CONSISTENCY AUDIT NOTE, APPENDED UNDER WORK ORDER 4471-B:

This file was flagged for audit not for any contradiction in its own text -- there is none, the record is scrupulously, exhaustingly consistent -- but because it is, of every record in this archive, the one that states outright and without metaphor what every other file in this collection implies.

A written record, continuously maintained and continuously attended, is the only thing standing between a person and being overwritten by what is occupying them. Agent [REDACTED] knows this and has never once been permitted to forget it, because forgetting it, even for ninety seconds, is the failure condition.

The Archive Consistency Auditor assigned to this work order is asked to consider how long their own board has been running, and who, exactly, has been on the other end of it, keeping the letters coming.

SON-OY.name: The Unsent Fourteenth Vote
SON-OY.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: DRAFT COUNCIL STATEMENT -- NEVER TABLED, NEVER FILED
RECOVERY: Found folded inside the case file for O5-OYLAMA, behind the sealed minutes, in a hand the clerk's office has not been able to match to any current or former Council seat.

RECOVERY NOTE:

This document is not part of the official record of the Council's deadlock. It was never entered into evidence, never read aloud in session, and by its own internal evidence was written and then deliberately withheld by its author before the vote it addresses was even called. It survives only because it was hidden inside the document about the vote, rather than filed anywhere a vote could reach it.

TEXT AS RECOVERED:

  Colleagues, if you are reading this, I did not send it, which
  means I decided against my own recommendation, and I want the
  reasoning on record regardless, because a reasoning nobody
  acted on is still worth more than no reasoning at all.

  We have framed this as continuation against Protocol Zero. It
  is not the only shape available. Eta-10 proves a third one
  works: tell people what they are walking into, let them
  volunteer, give them the notebook honestly instead of issuing
  it to them as a filing assignment.

  I proposed, and did not table, a volunteer division for archive
  consistency work, briefed to Antimemetics standard, rotated on
  consent rather than manufactured ignorance. I believe it would
  work. I believe it would cost us less than either option
  currently before this Council.

  I am not sending this because of a note I received from a
  colleague whose seat I will not name, which read, in full:

    "Informed volunteers ask questions the uninformed do not.
    Questions are also a kind of record. We are not equipped
    to contain the number of records that arrangement would
    generate, and you know it, because you read the same file
    on comprehension that I did."

  They are right and I hate that they are right. An auditor who
  understood everything and consented to it anyway would still
  produce a mind full of accurate information about ARCHIVE-000,
  and accurate information about ARCHIVE-000 is the one substance
  this entire procedure exists to keep from accumulating anywhere
  it can be found twice.

  So we keep choosing people who do not know, because not
  knowing is not a cruelty we are inflicting. It is the actual
  containment measure. The cruelty is a side effect we have
  learned to describe as a cost.

  I am not going to be the one who says that in session. I am
  going to vote for continuation like I have for six years, and
  I am going to leave this where only the next person to open
  this file will find it, because apparently that is the kind of
  honesty this Council can afford: the kind that is filed, not
  spoken.

CLERK'S NOTE:

This document does not appear in any session's attendance record. Cross-reference O5-OYLAMA: the vote has stood at six-six for nine years. This draft, had it been tabled, would not have changed that number. It would only have named, correctly, why the number has never moved.

KAYIP-ESYA.name: Site-19 Lost Property Log
KAYIP-ESYA.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: LOST PROPERTY INVENTORY, CONTINUOUS
RETENTION: Standing order. Items unclaimed after five years are catalogued and retained rather than disposed of, on a rule nobody currently in Facilities can explain.

SCOPE:

Ordinary lost property: umbrellas, badges, reading glasses, a great many coffee mugs. Archive Consistency Audit obtained access under work order 4471-B after noticing a pattern in the unclaimed section.

THE UNCLAIMED SECTION:

Items logged as unclaimed do not, on inspection, lack an owner. Each has an entry: a coat, a wristwatch stopped at no particular time, a pen worn smooth on one side, a single desk nameplate blank on both sides. Each entry lists a staff credential number in the owner field. None lists a name. Facilities staff describe this as standard practice for items "pending identification," though several of these items have been pending for over a decade.

A coat, logged eleven years ago, credential field populated, owner field blank, was never collected. Cross-checking the credential against current staff records returns no active holder. Cross-checking it against Archive Consistency Audit's own rotation shows a match.

STAFF NOTE (Facilities, unsigned):

We get a jacket or a watch or a pen every few months from the archive wing specifically, more than any other department this size. Nobody ever comes for them. We asked once whether we should be flagging this to someone. We were told the items are being retained correctly and that no further action is required.

We kept asking for a while. We stopped because nobody could tell us who to ask.

ARCHIVIST'S NOTE:

A person who owned a coat is not a difficult thing to trace. A credential number attached to no name is a familiar shape in this archive by now. What is worth recording here is smaller and stranger than that: these are not documents. They are objects. Somebody wore this coat and put it down somewhere and did not come back for it, and the paperwork remembers the credential perfectly and never once caught the name, the same way the personnel file never does.

The unreadable field is not only a property of paper.

ISIK-GUNLUGU.name: Lighting Maintenance Log, Archive Wing
ISIK-GUNLUGU.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: ROUTINE MAINTENANCE LOG -- LIGHTING, ARCHIVE WING
RETENTION: Five years rolling, then destroyed. This copy retained under work order 4471-B, an exception to standing policy.

SCOPE:

A record of bulb replacement across the archive wing's overhead fixtures, logged by whichever maintenance technician is on rotation. Included here because Archive Consistency Audit requested five years of it after a technician's offhand remark was overheard and, unusually, written down by the researcher who heard it.

WHAT THE LOG SHOWS:

Bulbs in this wing do not fail individually at a rate consistent with any other wing in the facility, where failures are randomly distributed as expected. In the archive wing, replacement requests arrive in clusters. The cluster size, without exception across five years of logged data, is eleven.

Technicians rotate through this assignment and none has stayed long enough to notice the pattern independently; each new technician assumes the batch ordering is simply how the previous one did it. The purchase orders, examined together for the first time under this audit, show eleven bulbs requisitioned, eleven bulbs installed, on a schedule that does not correlate with any lighting circuit's expected lifespan.

MAINTENANCE NOTE (unattributed, stapled to the most recent order):

"Asked the previous guy why we always order in elevens. He said that's just the box size. Checked the supplier catalogue. There is no box size of eleven. The supplier sells in tens and in twenty-fours. Somebody is opening a box of ten and a box of twenty-four and using eleven bulbs from the combination, every time, and reordering to restock exactly enough to do it again next time.

I am not going to be the one who changes the order."

ARCHIVIST'S CROSS-REFERENCE:

Eleven seconds are missing from the camera log of 14 March. Eleven days separate each auditor's rotation. Eleven bulbs burn out together, in a wing that has never had a documented electrical fault, on a schedule that predates anyone currently on staff.

The number does not appear to require an incident to recur. It appears to be a background condition of this wing, the way weather is a background condition of a coastline, and it was here, doing this, quietly, before anyone thought to count.

KAYIT-DISI-GORUSME.name: Off-Record Conversation, Transcribed From Memory
KAYIT-DISI-GORUSME.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: RECONSTRUCTED TRANSCRIPT -- NOT AN OFFICIAL RECORDING
SOURCE: Written from memory, within minutes, by the researcher present, per standing Antimemetics practice for conversations near SCP-055 that recording devices fail to capture.

PREFATORY NOTE:

This document should not exist by its own account. The researcher's covering note states they do not believe they were meant to remember having this conversation at all, and wrote it down specifically because the act of writing seemed, in the moment, to be the only way to keep it from being taken back.

TRANSCRIPT, AS RECONSTRUCTED:

"I asked whether 055 knows it's being observed.

The answer I got was that the question assumes 055 is a single continuous thing capable of knowing anything, and that this assumption has never been tested, because testing it would require holding the question in mind long enough to design an experiment, and nobody has.

I asked what happens to the two hundred and twelve people who wrote the observation log.

The answer was: nothing happens to them. They go home. They have dinner. Some of them wrote a second entry, years apart, and did not recognise their own earlier handwriting as theirs. Nothing happens to them in the way an incident happens. Something happens to them in the way that weather happens to a coastline.

I asked -- and I want this exact, because I think it matters -- I asked if the same thing is happening to auditors.

There was a pause I would call significant if I trusted my own sense of time in that room. Then: 'That is not a question I am able to answer today. Ask it again on a day when I remember today.'"

RESEARCHER'S CLOSING NOTE:

I do not remember who I was speaking to. I have a physical memory of a chair, a desk at a slight angle to the door, and my own hand writing quickly. I do not have a face, a voice, or a name to attach to the answers.

I am filing this because it is the only account in this archive, to my knowledge, of someone asking the SCP-055 question directly about auditors and getting something other than silence back. I would like it cross-checked against Antimemetics Division's own records, if such records exist, which -- I recognise as I write this sentence -- is exactly the kind of thing I would not be able to check twice.

ARSIV-PERSONEL-ANKETI.name: Archive Wing Staff Survey (Anonymous)
ARSIV-PERSONEL-ANKETI.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: ANNUAL MORALE SURVEY -- ARCHIVE WING
ADMINISTERED BY: Site-19 Human Resources
CLASSIFICATION: Routine. Not normally cross-referenced against operational data.

PURPOSE:

A standard, anonymous, five-question survey administered annually to all archive wing staff, part of a Foundation-wide morale programme applied uniformly across departments. Archive Consistency Audit requested eleven years of results under work order 4471-B after noting that one question's trend line did not resemble any other department's.

QUESTION 3: "I feel my work is understood by my colleagues." (Scale 1-5.)

ELEVEN-YEAR TREND, ARCHIVE WING:

  Year 1:   mean 3.8
  Year 3:   mean 3.1
  Year 5:   mean 2.6
  Year 7:   mean 2.1
  Year 9:   mean 1.6
  Year 11:  mean 1.1

HR NOTE (attached to the raw data, routine):

"Flagging for awareness only, no action recommended. Small sample size, high staff turnover in this department likely explains volatility. Recommend continued monitoring at standard interval."

ARCHIVIST'S CROSS-REFERENCE:

The decline in Question 3 tracks, point for point, against the shortening of the mean interval between auditor postings recorded in ROTASYON -- nineteen days at the start of this survey's records, eleven days now. HR's "high staff turnover" is correct in its literal words and wrong in its ordinary meaning: the department does not lose staff to resignation or transfer. It loses them to closure, under a name that is not theirs, at a rate this survey has been faithfully measuring for eleven years without anyone reading the two datasets side by side.

Question 3 is not asking whether colleagues understand the work. Whoever wrote the survey did not know that. The question has been accidentally, precisely correct the entire time it has been ignored.

O5-YEDEK-PLAN.name: O5 Contingency Draft: If The Vote Never Breaks
O5-YEDEK-PLAN.text:
DOCUMENT TYPE: SEALED CONTINGENCY DRAFT -- COUNCIL ADMINISTRATIVE
RECOVERY: Filed alongside SON-OY, in the same case file as O5-OYLAMA, in a third hand matching neither.

PURPOSE:

This draft does not argue for continuation or for Protocol Zero. It addresses a third possibility neither side raised in nine years of six-to-six minutes: that the vote simply never breaks.

TEXT AS RECOVERED:

  Standing administrative rule, drafted for Council approval, never
  formally ratified because ratification would have required tabling
  it, and tabling it would have required admitting it already governs
  outcomes by default:

  In the absence of a majority vote either way within any given
  session, existing protocol remains in force unchanged. No motion
  is required to continue what is already running. A motion is
  required only to stop it.

  This is standard parliamentary procedure and was not written for
  this case. It was written decades before ARCHIVE-000 existed as a
  filed object. It applies to this case anyway, because nobody has
  ever proposed an exception, and proposing an exception would itself
  require a majority this Council does not have.

  CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: the deadlock is not neutral. Every
  session that ends six-to-six is a session that defaults to
  continuation, because continuation is what was already happening
  when the session opened. The Zero side needs to win a vote. The
  continuation side needs, literally, nothing. It only needs the
  Zero side to keep failing to reach seven.

  I do not believe this was designed. I believe it is an accident of
  which option was already running the day this became a six-to-six
  question, the same way the rotation was already running the day
  Deren's predecessor was assigned. I am recording it because I think
  the Zero side should be told, plainly, that they are not in a fair
  fight, and that the fairness of the fight is not something anyone
  on this Council decided against them. It is something nobody
  decided at all.

CLERK'S NOTE:

This draft was never tabled. Cross-reference O5-OYLAMA: nine years of six-to-six minutes read, on their face, as a stalemate. This document reframes them as nine years of a single, continuously renewed decision that never had to be made twice, cast by whichever side does not have to do anything to win.

SCP-4001.name: The Kitchen Timer
SCP-4001.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4001 is stored in a standard kitchen drawer in a break room at Site-64. No special enclosure is required. Personnel may use it for its stated purpose, which it performs correctly. It is not to be reset to more than sixty (60) minutes remaining under any circumstances.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4001 is a mechanical wind-up kitchen timer of unremarkable manufacture, dial marked zero to sixty minutes. It functions as an ordinary timer for any setting up to and including sixty minutes. When wound past sixty minutes, which the dial does not permit but which has been achieved twice by mechanical intervention, the timer does not count down from the set value. It counts down from a value nobody entered.

On both recorded occasions, the number that appeared, visible through a small window not present on the timer's exterior before the winding, corresponded to the remaining lifespan, in minutes, of the person who wound it. Subject 1 wound the timer to test the claim, already terminally ill, and it read 6,204. Subject 1 was deceased 6,204 minutes later, of causes unrelated to the illness.

The timer has not been wound past sixty minutes since. It is kept in ordinary service for its correct range because destroying or discarding it has not been attempted and is not recommended pending review.

ADDENDUM:
A sticky note is affixed to the inside of the drawer, in a hand Records has not identified: "Sixty minutes is fine. Don't be curious." The note predates the current break room by four years, according to the facilities log, which places it in a drawer that did not yet contain this timer.

SCP-4002.name: The Wedding Ring
SCP-4002.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4002 is held in a ring box in a standard secure locker. No electromagnetic or physical containment is required, as the object does not move or act without a wearer. Personnel are not permitted to wear SCP-4002 without written authorisation and a signed acknowledgement of Addendum 4002-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4002 is a plain gold band, engraved on the interior with a date and two initials that do not match any marriage record cross-referenced to date. When worn on the ring finger of either hand, the wearer becomes, within several hours, convinced they are married to a specific person of the wearer's acquaintance, who has never met the wearer romantically and is frequently unaware the wearer exists.

The wearer's memory is not altered. They know, if asked directly, that no wedding occurred. They are simply unable to hold this fact as more significant than the felt certainty of the marriage, and will explain the discrepancy fluently: a marriage annulled by an uncooperative registry, a ceremony the other party has forgotten, a spouse who is "working through something." The named spouse, informed of this, is not affected and typically finds the situation alarming.

Removing the ring ends the conviction within minutes. Subjects report the ended conviction as a loss, described uniformly as grief, regardless of how briefly the ring was worn.

ADDENDUM 4002-1:
Eleven test subjects have worn the ring. Nine named a colleague or acquaintance. Two named a deceased relative, and in both cases described the marriage as having taken place before the relative's death, at an age the relative never reached. Testing on this category is discontinued.

SCP-4003.name: Stepladder, Six Rungs
SCP-4003.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4003 is stored folded in a maintenance closet and may be requisitioned for ordinary use. It performs its function without incident when used for its intended purpose of reaching height. Personnel are not to count the rungs aloud while climbing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4003 is an aluminium stepladder with six rungs, identical in appearance and function to commercial models. Climbed normally, without counting, it behaves as an ordinary ladder of six steps and delivers the climber to a height consistent with six steps.

If a climber counts the rungs aloud while ascending, the ladder will, on that ascent only, have a number of rungs other than six, most commonly reported as seven, occasionally as five, once as eleven. The final rung always delivers the climber to the same height as a six-rung ascent would, regardless of the count. Climbers who count silently, moving their lips without vocalising, produce an inconsistent effect: the ladder appears to have six rungs in about half of trials and a different number in the other half, with no established variable distinguishing the two outcomes.

No climber has ever fallen from SCP-4003. No climber has ever agreed with another climber, present at the same ascent, on how many times they heard the count spoken.

ADDENDUM:
A facilities technician's incident-free service log for SCP-4003 runs eleven years. Asked in a routine interview whether he had ever counted the rungs, he said he made a point never to, and could not explain why, since he did not know the object was anomalous when he started the habit.

SCP-4004.name: Waiting Room Chair 4
SCP-4004.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4004 is kept in a designated waiting area and may be sat in without restriction. It is one of six visually identical chairs; the others are not anomalous. SCP-4004 is not to be labelled, moved to a different position in the row, or removed from rotation, as doing so has previously interrupted data collection without altering the object's behaviour.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4004 is a standard upholstered waiting-room chair. Any person who sits in it while waiting for an appointment, meeting, or result finds that the wait feels, subjectively, exactly as long as they expected it to be, regardless of the wait's actual duration. Subjects expecting a short wait and kept for two hours report the two hours as having felt short. Subjects expecting a long wait and seen after four minutes report the four minutes as having dragged.

The effect does not alter clocks, memory of events during the wait, or any measurable timekeeping; only the subjective texture of duration is affected, and only for the sitter, and only until they stand. Subjects who stand and sit again reset their expectation to whatever they now believe, and the chair honours the new belief.

SCP-4004 has never been reported as unpleasant. Facilities staff have twice recommended installing similar chairs throughout the Site. Both recommendations were declined without explanation on file.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
I would like it on record that I do not think this chair is doing anything to us. I think it is showing us, very precisely, that we were already doing it to ourselves, and that this is the part nobody wanted more of.

SCP-4005.name: The Spare Key
SCP-4005.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4005 is held in a sealed key safe. It is not to be tested against any lock the Foundation intends to keep secure. Testing is conducted only against decommissioned locks slated for disposal.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4005 is a brass door key of no distinguishing cut pattern. Inserted into any lock, it opens that lock, regardless of the lock's mechanism, on the condition that the door it secures has, at some point in its history, been left unlocked by mistake by someone who lived or worked behind it. Doors that have never once been mistakenly left unlocked cannot be opened by SCP-4005; the key simply will not turn.

This has made the key functionally useless against high-security Foundation installations, whose doors are reliably locked, and functionally omnipotent against ordinary residential and commercial premises, the overwhelming majority of which have, statistically, been left open by accident at least once. Foundation testing across 3,000 residential doors in a controlled municipal survey found the key opened 2,977 of them.

The twenty-three doors it did not open were flagged for follow-up. Interviews found that in nineteen cases the current occupant could not recall the address ever having been left unlocked, and in four cases, refused to answer the question.

ADDENDUM:
SCP-4005 does not open any door at Site-64. This has been independently confirmed on eleven occasions and is treated by facilities staff as a point of quiet pride rather than a security concern.

SCP-4006.name: Passport, Unissued
SCP-4006.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4006 is held in a document sleeve in a climate-controlled records vault. It is not to be presented at any border crossing, real or simulated, without O5-level authorisation.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4006 is a passport of a design consistent with a national issuing authority that, on verification, does not and has never existed. The document photograph shows a face that test subjects consistently describe as familiar and are unable to identify, and which does not match any subject who has viewed it.

When presented to a passport control officer, human or automated, SCP-4006 is accepted without exception. Officers report processing it as routine and retain no memory afterward of having done so; camera footage of the interaction is present and unremarkable but shows the officer's expression as, in the words of one reviewing analyst, "the face of someone doing something they will not be asked to explain."

The bearer, on crossing, experiences no anomalous effect and arrives at the expected destination. What changes is external: municipal records at the point of entry acquire a retroactive log of the crossing, dated to match, under the bearer's real name, with no reference to the passport used.

ADDENDUM 4006-1:
Five controlled crossings were conducted. In all five, a corresponding departure record appeared at the country of origin, timed precisely to make the visit look ordinary, on days none of the five subjects had, in fact, left. Three of the five subjects' families later stated they remembered the subject being away that week.

SCP-4007.name: The Housewarming Gift
SCP-4007.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4007 is held in a lined crate in deep storage. It is never to be gift-wrapped, and personnel are forbidden from bringing any wrapped parcel into a room containing it, as two prior incidents indicate the object can propagate its property into nearby wrapped items under conditions not yet isolated.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4007 is a ceramic serving dish of a common commercial pattern. Given as a gift to a person moving into a new residence, and accepted as such, it causes the recipient's new residence to retroactively acquire the property of having always belonged to the giver, in every legal, familial, and communal record, while the recipient's own prior claim to the property is redistributed among the recipient's next of kin as an inheritance, dated to a death that did not occur.

The recipient is not evicted, displaced, or made aware in any conscious sense that anything has changed; they continue to live in the residence, now as a guest of the giver, a status they accept without apparent discomfort and are unable to articulate as unusual if asked directly.

The giver acquires no memory of any of this and experiences no change in their own circumstances beyond a persistent, mild sense of having recently given away something valuable.

SCP-4007 was recovered after a chain of six consecutive housewarming gifts in one suburban cul-de-sac resulted in municipal records showing all six houses as belonging to a single elderly woman who had, by her own account, given a serving dish to a new neighbour thirty years prior and had not left her original house since.

ADDENDUM:
The woman is currently housed at Site-64 under care. She has asked, on several occasions, whether she has been a good neighbour. Staff are instructed to say yes.

SCP-4008.name: The Family Photo Album
SCP-4008.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4008 is stored closed in an acid-free sleeve. It may be opened only by personnel with no living family members, verified against Foundation personnel records prior to each authorised viewing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4008 is a leather-bound photo album of the style common to the 1970s-1990s, containing ninety-four photographs of a family of five at various ages and occasions: birthdays, holidays, a graduation, a wedding.

Any viewer who has living family members of their own finds, on the second viewing, that one photograph now depicts a member of the viewer's own family in place of one of the album's original five, correctly aged to fit the album's timeline, in clothing and settings consistent with decades the viewer's relative did not live through. By the fifth viewing, the substitution typically reaches three of the five family members.

The substituted relatives, contacted afterward, have no memory of the depicted events and are otherwise unaffected. The album's captions, handwritten, update to match: names change, in the same ink, in handwriting analysis has confirmed is consistent throughout the entire album, original and substituted entries alike.

No viewer has yet seen their entire family replace the album's original five. Testing was halted at four viewings per subject following Incident 4008-3, in which a subject's fourth viewing substituted a family member who had, in the viewer's stated recollection prior to the test, never existed, and who the viewer's own family subsequently confirmed as a forgotten, deceased sibling none of them could explain having forgotten.

ADDENDUM:
The album does not function for viewers with no living family. It has never been tested to completion for this reason, and no completion condition is currently theorised.

SCP-4009.name: The Return Policy
SCP-4009.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4009 is a laminated card held in an evidence sleeve. It is not to be posted, displayed, or photocopied where it might be read by unauthorised personnel, as the object's effect requires only reading, not physical possession.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4009 is a laminated store return policy of the kind typically posted at a customer service counter, printed in a generic retail house style, from a chain that Foundation research has been unable to identify. The text reads, in full: "All items may be returned within thirty (30) days, no receipt required, no questions asked. This includes items not purchased at this store. This includes items not purchased. Please have your item ready for return."

A person who reads the full policy becomes able, once, within the following thirty days, to "return" any object in their possession. The object vanishes. In exchange, the returner receives store credit in the form of an unshakeable conviction that they never wanted the object in the first place, applied retroactively to their own memory of ever having wanted it.

The effect has been tested on emotionally significant objects as well as mundane ones. Subjects who "return" a sentimental item report no grief, because they no longer recall the sentiment; they report, if asked why they don't have the item, mild confusion that anyone expects them to.

One subject attempted to return a physical injury. The injury did not vanish. The subject received store credit anyway, in the form of a conviction that the injury did not hurt, which by Medical's report was, on its own terms, effective and has persisted.

ADDENDUM:
The card cannot be used a second time by the same reader. It can be read by an unlimited number of different people.

SCP-4010.name: Umbrella, Left Behind
SCP-4010.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4010 is kept in an umbrella stand near a frequently used exit at Site-64, available for ordinary use during inclement weather. Personnel are not required to return it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4010 is a black folding umbrella of unremarkable manufacture. Any person who carries it out into rain and later leaves it behind — on a train, in a doorway, at a café table, anywhere outside their own residence — finds it in their umbrella stand, closet, or equivalent storage location the next time they need an umbrella, regardless of where it was left or how far away.

It does not return itself before it is needed; testing has shown it remains at the location it was left, verifiable and photographable, right up until the moment a person who has previously carried it reaches for an umbrella in rainy conditions, at which point it is retroactively confirmed to have been in their possession the entire time, and whatever record existed of it sitting abandoned elsewhere quietly ceases to exist.

The umbrella has been deliberately left in fourteen countries during testing. In each case, subsequent need for an umbrella produced it, in hand, indoors, dry, as though it had never left.

ADDENDUM:
A facilities log entry, unsigned, reads: "Every umbrella I have ever owned came back to me eventually except the one I actually miss." Records has been unable to determine whether this refers to SCP-4010 or is an unrelated personal note misfiled in this record.

SCP-4011.name: The Complaint Box
SCP-4011.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4011 is bolted to a wall in a disused corridor at Site-64 and is not to be emptied except under the schedule described in Addendum 4011-2. It is not to be removed, as the one attempt to relocate it resulted in Incident 4011-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4011 is a metal wall-mounted comment box of a type common to mid-century office buildings, with a slot for folded paper complaints and a small brass plate reading "Tell Us How We're Doing." It accepts written complaints normally.

Any complaint deposited in SCP-4011 concerning a specific, named member of staff is addressed within seventy-two hours: the named staff member is found, by whatever means, to have corrected the complained-of behaviour, with no memory of receiving feedback and no record of a conversation having taken place. Complaints about policy, facilities, or unnamed grievances are not acted upon and simply accumulate.

The corrections are not always improvements by any reasonable standard. A complaint that a named researcher was "too friendly" resulted in that researcher's measurable, permanent reduction in warmth toward all colleagues, not only the complainant. A complaint that a technician was slow resulted in the technician working through a documented back injury without reporting it, which Medical only discovered incidentally.

INCIDENT 4011-1:
An attempt to remove SCP-4011 from the wall resulted in seventeen simultaneous, anonymous complaints appearing inside it, each naming a member of the removal team, none of which had been physically deposited by anyone. The removal was abandoned. All seventeen named corrections occurred within the normal seventy-two-hour window.

ADDENDUM 4011-2:
The box is emptied monthly by a technician wearing gloves, who does not read the complaints, and who has asked, twice, to be rotated off this duty. Both requests were an unnamed grievance and were not acted upon.

SCP-4012.name: Business Card, No Name
SCP-4012.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4012 is held in a sealed transparent sleeve to prevent physical handling. It is not to be handed to any person under any circumstances. Viewing at a distance of no less than one metre is permitted for research purposes only.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4012 is a plain white business card, blank except for a single line of text reading "Call anytime," with a telephone number that changes between viewings and has never, on any occasion, been dialled successfully — connection attempts return either a disconnection tone or, in four recorded cases, a ring that was answered by a voice reporting itself to be the caller, at a later point in the caller's own life, unable to explain how it came to be holding the card.

If physically handed from one person to another, the recipient becomes, over the following days, professionally and then personally indispensable to whoever gave it to them, in a manner that escalates regardless of the two parties' prior relationship: employers cannot function without the employee, friends cannot make decisions without the friend, and in the two most severe recorded cases, spouses could not recall functioning as individuals prior to the exchange. The giver experiences no corresponding dependency and typically does not notice the shift.

The original circumstances of the card's recovery are themselves lost: the acquiring field agent's report describes receiving the card from a colleague, whose name and personnel file cannot be located, and whom no other member of the recovery team recalls being present.

ADDENDUM:
No current Foundation staff member admits to handling the initial hand-off. Personnel rosters from the recovery date show one position filled by a name that does not appear on any other document, past or since.

SCP-4013.name: The Latecomers
SCP-4013.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All physical photographs suspected of exhibiting SCP-4013 activity are to be sealed in archival-grade acid-free sleeves and stored in Secure Photographic Storage, Site-19, Locker 4013. Sleeves are not to be opened except for scheduled quarterly re-examination by two (2) assigned personnel, conducted under Level 2 photographic protocol. Digital reproductions (scans, photographs of photographs) do not exhibit the anomaly and may be freely handled; however, no digital reproduction has yet been made of an SCP-4013-exhibiting print without introducing a new print into the population, and this practice has been suspended pending review.

Newly discovered prints suspected of hosting SCP-4013 specimens are to be catalogued, given an accession number, and photographed digitally on discovery to establish a baseline insect count. Any print showing a count above its digitally recorded baseline on subsequent examination is to be flagged for Addendum review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4013 refers to a population of moth-like insects, individually designated SCP-4013-1, that exist exclusively within developed photographic prints depicting unoccupied interior spaces. No SCP-4013-1 specimen has been observed, captured, or recorded outside of a photograph. Specimens are approximately 2 cm in wingspan, pale grey, and resemble Lepidoptera of the family Noctuidae, with the exception of a faint white marking on the dorsal thorax resembling a closed eye.

A print does not gain an SCP-4013-1 specimen at the moment of exposure or development. Instead, specimens accumulate gradually across repeated examinations of the same print over months or years, with no correlation to the print's physical age, chemical stability, or storage conditions. A print with zero specimens on first cataloguing may show one, three, or more specimens on a later examination, despite no intervening exposure to light, chemicals, or handling capable of producing an image. The mechanism by which the print's silver-halide or dye layer is altered has not been identified; the print's chemical composition does not change in any way detectable by standard analysis.

Specimens do not move, blur, or appear in different positions between examinations. Once present in a given examination, a specimen occupies a fixed position in the frame. Specimens accumulate near the edges of the frame first, migrating toward its center over subsequent examinations, and specimens closest to the center are consistently oriented to face the camera.

ADDENDUM 4013-1:
Print 4013-A (Site-19, Stairwell C, unoccupied at time of original photograph, taken 1994) was catalogued with zero specimens. Re-examination in 2004 recorded four specimens, all near the frame's left edge. Re-examination in 2019 recorded nine specimens, four still near the edge and five arranged in a rough arc approaching the frame's center. The specimen nearest the center in the 2019 examination is the only one on file oriented directly toward the camera rather than in profile. Its wing markings, when magnified, are consistent with human fingerprint ridges. {{3|A partial match against Foundation personnel fingerprint records returned a 61% correspondence to Dr. E. Mercer, whose Foundation record lists him as active and currently assigned to unrelated duties.|}} No print of Stairwell C has been re-examined since.

SCP-4014.name: The Echo Eel
SCP-4014.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4014 is contained within Tank 4014, a 40,000-litre saltwater enclosure at Site-19's Aquatic Containment Wing, filled with water drawn from its point of recovery (Loch Aveline flooded mine workings, Scotland) and maintained at a constant 6Â°C. No hydrophone or other audio recording equipment is to be lowered into Tank 4014 without prior authorization from the Site Director, and any authorized recording is to be reviewed by two (2) personnel before either is permitted to listen to it alone.

Feeding is conducted remotely via a mechanized chute. Personnel are not to speak, hum, or otherwise vocalize within 15 metres of Tank 4014, and are to wear standard hearing protection when performing maintenance within that radius. SCP-4014 has not attempted to breach Tank 4014; containment protocol is directed entirely at preventing personnel from listening to it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4014 is an eel-like organism, approximately 3.1 metres in length, of a species not matched to any catalogued genus. It possesses no eyes and is believed to navigate and hunt entirely by sound. SCP-4014 was recovered in 1998 from flooded mine workings near Loch Aveline after local reports of drownings attributed by residents to "the singing water."

SCP-4014 hunts by producing, through an organ located in its lower jaw, a precise audio reproduction of the final heartbeat of its most recently killed prey, broadcast at a volume and frequency calibrated to carry through water at distances up to 800 metres. Human test subjects and recovered witness accounts describe the sound not as a heartbeat in the abstract but as recognizably, individually a specific heartbeat â€” subjects with cardiac monitoring backgrounds have independently identified irregularities (a missed beat, an arrhythmia) consistent between separate exposures to the same recording, indicating the organ does not generate a generic signal but retains and replays an exact recording of each victim in sequence, discarding the previous one only upon acquiring a new kill.

The purpose of the display is believed to be predatory: subjects exposed to the sound underwater report a compulsion to swim toward the source, consistent with mistaking it for a distressed swimmer. SCP-4014 is not otherwise noted for exceptional physical strength or venom; predation is understood to occur exclusively through this luring behavior followed by drowning.

ADDENDUM 4014-1:
During Site-19 processing of SCP-4014's recovery-site hydrophone archive (routine cataloguing, 2003), Audio Analysis Unit flagged Track 4014-H17 for containing a heartbeat signature matching, to a documented 97% confidence, the medical file of Diver R. Alcott, reported missing in the same mine workings in 1989, nine years before SCP-4014's recovery. Track 4014-H17 was recorded in 1998, the same week as SCP-4014's capture. No explanation has been offered for how a signature from a diver missing nine years prior could have been captured in SCP-4014's final recorded broadcast, nor why the broadcast would be from that specific year rather than a more recent kill. The track remains in the audio archive, unplayed since analysis, per standing containment protocol.

SCP-4015.name: The Slow Orchard
SCP-4015.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The physical range of SCP-4015 (currently 2.3 kmÂ² and expanding at an average of 4 m per year) is enclosed within a buried concrete-and-mycocide barrier extending three metres below grade, designated Perimeter Orchard, near â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ, Oregon. Personnel do not enter Perimeter Orchard except for quarterly barrier inspection in hazmat-rated suits with independent air supply. Recovery of SCP-4015-1 fruiting bodies for study is suspended following Incident 4015-Greenhouse (see Addendum).

Any individual reporting direct skin contact with SCP-4015 mycelial mat, ingestion of an SCP-4015-1 fruiting body, or inhalation of SCP-4015 spores is to be quarantined for no fewer than 30 days and evaluated daily for memory content inconsistent with their personnel file. Full mycocide barrier failure is to be treated as a Keter-class breach scenario; standing evacuation order covers a 12 km radius.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4015 is a fungal mycelial network, taxonomically unclassified, occupying the root systems of a former commercial apple orchard abandoned in 1961. The network is contiguous, genetically identical throughout its range, and is believed to constitute a single organism. SCP-4015 produces periodic fruiting bodies, designated SCP-4015-1, resembling apples in size and coloration, at points along its range roughly corresponding to the original orchard's tree rows, though no living trees remain.

Ingestion of SCP-4015-1 tissue by a human subject produces, within minutes, a complete and involuntary sensory recollection â€” not a description, but a full first-person re-experience â€” of a specific period in another individual's life, typically twenty to sixty minutes in subjective duration. The recollection is invariably accurate to verifiable detail where such verification has been possible. The identity of the person whose memory is delivered does not correlate with the specific fruiting body's location, size, or age in any pattern yet established.

Subjects who ingest SCP-4015-1 tissue exhibit, following the episode, a decrease in idiosyncratic memory content of their own and a corresponding increase in memory content matching the recollection received. This effect is cumulative and has proven irreversible in nine of nine documented cases {{4|; three of the nine affected personnel were assigned to SCP-4015's own research team prior to exposure, and their case files, cross-referenced, describe the same donor memory in each instance: a wood-panelled office, the smell of cut apples, and someone speaking a name that transcribes in every recorded case as an unresolvable audio artifact|}}.

ADDENDUM 4015-1 (Incident 4015-Greenhouse):
On â–ˆâ–ˆ/â–ˆâ–ˆ/2011, a fruiting body recovered for controlled laboratory ingestion under Test 4015-14 delivered to the test subject (D-9004) a memory subsequently identified, by physical description of the office contained within it, as belonging to Dr. E. Mercer, an SCP-4015 field researcher reported missing during the site's original 1994 survey. No fruiting body has since matched to a known Foundation researcher on genetic or documentary record. Recovery of SCP-4015-1 specimens for study was suspended the same day.

SCP-4016.name: The Quiet Vole
SCP-4016.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The current SCP-4016 population (six specimens) is housed in a single ventilated enclosure, Habitat 4016, lined with acoustic foam and fitted with a decibel meter monitored continuously by automated logging. No specimen is to be removed from Habitat 4016 except for approved sound-extraction procedures (see Addendum) conducted by two (2) personnel wearing hearing protection rated for sudden onset above 130 dB.

Specimens are not to be handled roughly, dropped, or subjected to trauma of any kind. In the event of specimen death by any cause, all personnel within 20 metres are to don hearing protection immediately and the area is to be evacuated to 50 metres pending Audio Containment Team assessment.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4016 designates a small burrowing rodent, superficially resembling Microtus (voles) but with enlarged internal cheek pouches lined with a dense, fibrous tissue not present in any known rodent species. SCP-4016 specimens are anomalously capable of absorbing ambient sound within an approximate 4-metre radius and storing it, apparently indefinitely, within these pouches. Rooms containing an active SCP-4016 specimen become measurably quieter over time on all frequencies, with reductions in ambient decibel level of up to 30% recorded after several weeks of continuous specimen presence.

Stored sound can be extracted under controlled conditions by mild compression of the cheek pouch, releasing a fraction of the stored audio in reverse-chronological order (most recently absorbed sound first). This property has led to limited operational use of SCP-4016 specimens for acoustic dampening in sensitive containment areas, subject to Site Director approval, and for recovery of ambient recordings from locations lacking recording equipment.

If a specimen dies with sound stored in its pouches, the full stored content is released simultaneously and at a volume proportional to the duration over which it was absorbed, with no observed upper limit.

ADDENDUM 4016-1:
On â–ˆâ–ˆ/â–ˆâ–ˆ/2016, Specimen 4016-4 was accidentally struck and killed during a routine enclosure cleaning, having been resident in Habitat 4016 undisturbed for approximately nine years. The resulting release measured 187 dB at the enclosure wall, sufficient to rupture the eardrums of the on-duty Technician despite hearing protection, and was audible, per external reports, up to 1.1 km from Site-19's perimeter. Analysis of the recovered audio, once slowed and filtered, resolved into nine years of overlapping ambient site noise, beneath which analysts identified a single continuous voice reciting a sequence of numbers, unbroken, for the entire nine-year duration. No source for the voice has been identified. The numbers do not correspond to any active Foundation designation, badge series, or file number.

SCP-4017.name: The Whispering Hive
SCP-4017.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The SCP-4017 hive is contained within a sealed acrylic enclosure, Containment Cell 4017, within Site-19's Entomological Wing. The enclosure's single access port is fitted with a one-way valve permitting feeding without direct contact. Personnel are prohibited from placing any part of the body, including gloved hands, within 30 cm of the hive's outer wall.

Listening to SCP-4017, defined as any personnel voluntarily placing an ear, microphone, or other receiving apparatus against or near the hive structure, requires written Level 3 authorization specifying a single question to be asked and is limited to one listening session per researcher per calendar year. All listening sessions are to be recorded on video and the researcher is to be interviewed by a staff psychologist within 24 hours.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4017 is a colony of wasp-like insects, individually unremarkable and of a species tentatively classified within Vespidae, notable exclusively for the structure of the communal nest they construct. The nest, built from a paper-like pulp identical in composition to ordinary wasp nest material, invariably forms into a shape closely resembling the external structure of a human outer and middle ear, scaled to approximately 40 cm in height, regardless of the size or shape of the cavity in which the colony is founded.

A researcher who places an ear against the nest's outer wall and silently formulates a question will, within one to three minutes, hear a response in a voice matching their own, answering a question they have not yet been asked by anyone else, including questions concerning future events. Verified responses have proven accurate in nineteen of twenty-two documented sessions.

Each listening session is accompanied by measurable growth of the nest structure, averaging 6% by volume. Post-session interviews indicate that researchers who have completed a listening session are consistently unable to recall a specific period of their own past corresponding, in duration, to roughly the growth increment recorded â€” though none have reported this deficit unprompted, and each denies any memory gap until shown their own prior statements.

INTERVIEW EXCERPT 4017-B:
Following Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ's third authorized session (nest growth +7.1%):

<Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ>: It answered before I finished thinking the question.
<Interviewer>: What did you ask?
<Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ>: Whether my father remembers my mother's name.
<Interviewer>: What did it say?
<Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ>: It said yes. It said he still says it every morning.
<Interviewer>: Doctor, your file states your father passed in 2009.
<Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ>: [43-second pause.] That's not right. I spoke to him last week.
<Interviewer>: Do you remember what you spoke about?
<Dr. â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ>: [No response logged.]

SCP-4018.name: The Unified Flock
SCP-4018.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The SCP-4018 herd (currently 340 individual bodies, see Description) is contained within Agricultural Containment Pasture 4018, a fenced 900-hectare facility surrounded by a triple perimeter fence and monitored by thermal camera at all times. No individual animal is to be separated from the herd under any circumstances; isolation of a single SCP-4018 body has, in all four attempted cases, resulted in rapid deterioration and death of the isolated body within six hours.

Personnel entering Agricultural Containment Pasture 4018 are limited to Grade IV biohazard suits and are prohibited from physical contact with any SCP-4018 body. Any Foundation livestock, working animal, or staff member's pet exhibiting synchronized movement, breathing, or vocalization with two or more other animals is to be reported immediately and quarantined pending SCP-4018 exposure assessment.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4018 originated as a flock of 340 domestic sheep (Ovis aries) at a farm near â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ, believed to have contracted a prion-analogous agent, designated SCP-4018-A, from contaminated feed of unknown origin. Infected animals initially displayed no symptoms distinguishable from healthy livestock. Approximately three weeks post-exposure, infected animals began to move, chew, breathe, and vocalize in complete synchrony with all other infected animals within a shared enclosure, regardless of individual position, sightline, or apparent means of coordination.

Pre-acquisition veterinary records, partially recovered from the original farm, include electrocardiogram monitoring of nine sheep {{3|showing a single shared cardiac signal across all nine despite separate physical bodies, hearts beating in unison to a precision beyond currently measurable synchronization mechanisms in ungulates|}}.

At advanced stages of infection, animals in direct physical contact for extended periods (documented minimum: nine consecutive hours) develop shared tissue at points of contact â€” typically flank-to-flank or head-to-flank â€” forming continuous skin, muscle, and in three documented cases, bone, between what remain nominally separate bodies. The herd has not yet been observed to complete fusion into a single mass, though Foundation veterinary staff project this outcome as the terminal stage of infection based on tissue-bridging rate.

SCP-4018-A has shown no capacity to infect non-ovine species in controlled testing to date. Object class is Keter based on unknown transmission vectors in the original outbreak and the unconfirmed status of the farm's human residents, who were not present at the property when Mobile Task Force personnel arrived and have not been located.

ADDENDUM 4018-1:
Necropsy of a naturally deceased fused pair (Bodies 214/215, fused at the flank for approximately fourteen months prior to death) found a single fused heart of double ordinary mass, beating, at time of discovery, at a rate matching neither animal's known baseline but instead a rate consistent with human resting cardiac rhythm. The heart was removed for study. It continued beating for six days outside the body before staff terminated the study early.

SCP-4019.name: The Patient Heron
SCP-4019.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4019 is contained within Aviary Enclosure 4019, a shallow artificial wetland habitat of approximately 200 mÂ² at Site-19's Biological Containment Wing, designed to replicate its original recovery habitat. SCP-4019 has never attempted to leave Aviary Enclosure 4019 and no physical containment beyond a standard 3-metre perimeter fence has proven necessary.

A rotating schedule of "acknowledgment shifts" is maintained: one (1) assigned staff member is required to be present within visual range of SCP-4019 and to verbally acknowledge its presence (a simple greeting is sufficient) not less than once per eight-hour period. Failure to maintain an acknowledgment shift for a period exceeding 36 hours is to be reported to the Site Director immediately (see Description).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4019 is a wading bird resembling Ardea (herons) in general morphology, approximately 1.4 metres in height, off-white plumage, recovered in 1971 from a wetland reserve in â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ after local record-keepers noted the bird's presence in photographs spanning at least eighty years without visible aging or change in plumage.

SCP-4019 remains motionless, in a single fixed posture, for extended periods ranging from weeks to years, interrupted only by acknowledgment (see below) or feeding. During these periods, small organisms (insects, fish, occasionally birds) that die within approximately 1 metre of SCP-4019 do not decompose. Recovered specimens have been found in a state of perfect tissue preservation regardless of elapsed time, up to the current maximum documented interval of thirty-one years, with no anomalous chemical preservative detected.

SCP-4019 will only feed, and will only break its stillness to do so, following direct verbal acknowledgment of its presence by a person. In the absence of any acknowledgment, SCP-4019 has been observed to remain stationary for periods in excess of three years without any indication of malnutrition, injury, or distress consistent with its apparent physiology.

Foundation acquisition followed the death of the reserve's last full-time caretaker in 1970, after which the reserve received no further staff visits for approximately fourteen months; when Foundation personnel arrived to assess the site for acquisition, SCP-4019 was found in the exact posture recorded in the caretaker's final photograph, and the immediate area contained the perfectly preserved bodies of six animals estimated, by surrounding vegetation growth, to have died at intervals across those fourteen months.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
Assigned acknowledgment staff report the duty as pleasant, low-stress, and are consistently willing to extend their rotation. Two staff members have independently requested permanent reassignment to SCP-4019 acknowledgment duty. Request denied in both cases pending psychological review; review found no anomalous attachment markers in either case, only, in the words of the reviewing psychologist, "a reasonable preference for being the reason something is fed."

SCP-4020.name: The Drowned Choir
SCP-4020.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4020 individuals are contained within Tank 4020-A through 4020-F, six interconnected saltwater tanks at Site-19's Aquatic Containment Wing, maintained at oceanic salinity and temperature matching the Bering Sea recovery site. Tanks are separated by removable acoustic baffles; no more than four SCP-4020 individuals are to be housed in audible range of one another at any time, as vocalization frequency and coordination increase measurably with group size.

Any vessel, buoy, or maritime recording equipment operating within 5 km of the original recovery coordinates is to be flagged for Foundation maritime intercept per Standing Order 4020. Civilian mariner reports of "singing" or "voices" from open water in that region are to be investigated and, where necessary, explained away through standard disinformation channels.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4020 designates a species of small schooling fish, approximately 12 cm in length, silver-scaled, superficially resembling herring (Clupea), that produce vocalizations through an anomalous swim-bladder structure capable of reproducing complex human speech and song with no observed anatomical basis for the capability.

SCP-4020 individuals vocalize exclusively in the recorded or approximated voices of deceased humans, typically persons who died by drowning in the vicinity of the school within the preceding several decades. Vocalizations are performed in unison by the full school, in harmony, producing an effect described by recovered witnesses as choral. Content ranges from wordless singing to coherent, if repetitive, phrases, most commonly requests for help or for a listener to "come closer" or "come down."

Vessels that approach a vocalizing SCP-4020 school report a strong, apparently anomalous compulsion among crew to enter the water. Of nine documented civilian encounters recovered from maritime incident reports prior to Foundation involvement, six resulted in at least one drowning death; in five of those six cases, the deceased's voice was subsequently identified in later SCP-4020 vocalization recordings within the following two years.

ADDENDUM 4020-1:
Hydrophone Recording 4020-R44, obtained during a routine containment audit, was submitted to Audio Analysis for voice-matching against the Foundation's own personnel roster as a precautionary measure following the discovery that SCP-4020 is not restricted to civilian victims. The recording returned a 91% voice match to Researcher T. Onal, assigned to Site-19's Maritime Recovery Division, who resigned from Foundation service in good standing eight years prior to the recording's date and has since been unreachable by standard personnel-tracking channels. The recording includes Researcher Onal's Foundation badge number, spoken clearly, once, followed by fourteen seconds of the full school singing in unison without further words.

SCP-4021.name: The Waiting Room Fern
SCP-4021.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Confirmed SCP-4021 specimens are to be maintained under standard botanical containment (Growth Chamber 4021) and are not to be placed in any occupied waiting area, corridor, or other space where non-essential personnel or Class-D personnel may be exposed for periods exceeding fifteen minutes. Any SCP-4021 specimen discovered growing outside of authorized containment (see Description) is to be recovered, potted, and transferred to Growth Chamber 4021 within 24 hours of discovery.

Personnel who have spent more than fifteen consecutive minutes within 3 metres of an SCP-4021 specimen are to be briefly interviewed regarding the reason for their presence in that location before being permitted to leave. This requirement applies regardless of clearance level.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4021 is a fern of the genus Polystichum, externally unremarkable, that has been recovered on seven separate occasions, always growing from a potted or in-ground position within a medical, administrative, or transportation waiting area (a clinic, a benefits office, a bus terminal), and never in any other context. Standard botanical analysis has found no distinguishing feature separating SCP-4021 from ordinary Polystichum specimens.

Individuals who remain within approximately 3 metres of an active SCP-4021 specimen for an extended period, as occurs naturally in the waiting areas where it is consistently found, report that the wait "felt shorter" than its measured duration; clocks, timestamps, and independent observers confirm no actual distortion of elapsed time occurs.

Extended proximity (documented threshold: fifteen minutes or more) produces a separate and more consistent effect: the individual retains full and accurate memory of the waiting period itself â€” the room, the chairs, other people present â€” but loses specific memory of the reason for their visit, recoverable only through external documentation (an appointment card, a claim number) and not through unprompted recall. The effect has not been observed to extend to any memory formed prior to entering the specimen's presence, nor to impair function or new memory formation afterward.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
SCP-4021 is one of the more frequently misfiled records in the archive, owing to a persistent clerical tendency to describe it as harmless on the strength of the absence of injury, illness, or measurable cognitive damage in any exposed subject. It is included here as filed. It should be noted that in five of seven recovery cases, the office or clinic in question had no record, on later inquiry, of what service the exposed individual had originally been waiting for either â€” a gap that predates SCP-4021's recovery in each instance and has not been otherwise explained.

SCP-4022.name: The Cathedral Newt
SCP-4022.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4022 is currently at large within the collapsed workings of â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ Colliery, â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ, Wales, following Breach Incident 4022-1 (see Addendum). The colliery and a 4 km surrounding radius are maintained under permanent Foundation cover as a condemned mine site closed for structural safety, with a fabricated methane-hazard designation preventing civilian access. Satellite and ground-penetrating radar monitoring of the site is conducted monthly to track growth of SCP-4022-1 formations.

Any structure identified as SCP-4022-1 within the exclusion zone is not to be approached, sampled, or disturbed without Level 4 authorization and a structural engineering assessment, owing to the formations' demonstrated instability and the confirmed lethality of contact with active secretion sites.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4022 is a salamander-like amphibian, approximately 2.4 metres in length at last confirmed measurement, recovered from â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ Colliery in 2003 following a series of miner disappearances subsequently attributed to the organism. SCP-4022 secretes, through glands along its dorsal ridge, a mineral-rich fluid that rapidly calcifies any organic or porous material it contacts, forming rigid structures, designated SCP-4022-1, that consistently develop architectural features â€” ribbed vaulting, pointed arches, buttressing â€” resembling Gothic ecclesiastical construction, at a scale and structural coherence inconsistent with the secretion of an unguided animal process.

SCP-4022 uses these formations as both shelter and hunting structure, luring prey (documented: rats, birds, and at minimum four human miners) into calcifying chambers that narrow progressively, restricting movement until the prey is fully encased. Encased remains are not digested externally; SCP-4022 is believed to feed on encased prey over extended periods through small apertures maintained in the calcified structure for this purpose, some of which have remained active, per radar imaging, for over a decade.

Following Breach Incident 4022-1, SCP-4022 itself has not been visually confirmed since 2015, though SCP-4022-1 formations continue to expand at the original site, indicating either continued specimen activity from an unlocated position or a self-sustaining secretion process independent of the specimen's direct involvement â€” the latter possibility has not been ruled out and would represent a significant reclassification concern.

ADDENDUM 4022-1 (Breach Incident):
On â–ˆâ–ˆ/â–ˆâ–ˆ/2015, SCP-4022 breached its original surface containment structure during a routine feeding operation, entering the colliery's flooded lower workings, which connect via natural fissure to an estimated 40 km of unmapped and structurally unstable tunnel network. Recovery was deemed infeasible given structural collapse risk. SCP-4022-1 formations have since been observed via satellite thermal imaging to have grown to the surface at two new points 1.8 km apart, both exhibiting the same architectural coherence as the original site, and both emitting, per passive acoustic monitoring, a low-frequency resonance at a frequency matching that of a functioning pipe organ, though no such instrument, nor any plausible source for one, has been located within the exclusion zone.

SCP-4023.name: The Loyal Remains
SCP-4023.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remains of SCP-4023 are to be permitted continued access to Site-19's designated patrol route Gamma-7 (external perimeter, Sectors 12 through 19) during standard night patrol hours, as restriction to a fixed enclosure has, in three prior attempts, resulted in property damage and one (1) personnel injury consistent with SCP-4023 attempting to resume its route by force. SCP-4023 is not to be physically restrained, touched, or fed.

All personnel assigned to Sectors 12 through 19 during night patrol hours are to be briefed on SCP-4023's appearance and route prior to their first shift. Personnel encountering SCP-4023 are to permit it to complete its patrol unimpeded and are to report the encounter, including exact time and sector, to the Site-19 Biological Anomalies desk by end of shift.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4023 designates the animate remains of Canine Unit 7 ("Bess"), a Foundation-trained German Shepherd assigned to Site-19 perimeter security, confirmed deceased during Containment Breach â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ-â–ˆâ–ˆ in 2009. SCP-4023's body was not recovered following the breach and was presumed lost; it was rediscovered in 2013 continuing to patrol Route Gamma-7 on the same nightly schedule it had maintained prior to its death.

SCP-4023's body exhibits ongoing decomposition consistent with a corpse of its age and has, since rediscovery, lost approximately 40% of external soft tissue and the complete use of its left hind limb, which is no longer physically present. SCP-4023 continues to complete the full 2.1 km patrol route in a time consistent with its pre-mortem performance record, adjusting gait to compensate for missing tissue and structure in a manner exceeding what remaining muscular and skeletal material should support.

SCP-4023 does not react to strangers with aggression or fear and does not appear to register personnel reassignments, retirements, or deaths; it approaches Foundation personnel who served at Site-19 during its operational period, including personnel now stationed elsewhere and personnel deceased in the interim (see Addendum), by scent, and performs the specific greeting behavior recorded in its training file for each individual, regardless of how long that individual has been absent from the site.

ADDENDUM 4023-1:
On â–ˆâ–ˆ/â–ˆâ–ˆ/2019, SCP-4023 was observed performing its recorded greeting sequence for Handler S. Okur at the Sector 14 checkpoint at 0247 hours. Handler Okur transferred to a Foundation site in â–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆâ–ˆ in 2011 and, per personnel records, died in an unrelated incident in 2017. Security footage of the encounter is intact and shows SCP-4023 approaching an empty section of corridor, sitting, and extending a forepaw in the exact posture recorded for Handler Okur in its original training documentation. No thermal, infrared, or motion signature consistent with a second party is present in the footage. SCP-4023 completed the remainder of its patrol route on schedule.

SCP-4024.name: The Cartographer Termites
SCP-4024.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All confirmed SCP-4024 colonies are to be destroyed by controlled incineration immediately upon discovery; standard pest control measures have proven ineffective (see Description). Following incineration, the affected structure and a 500-metre radius are to be searched for a secondary colony, which has been established in one hundred percent of cases to have already formed prior to the primary colony's destruction.

Any physical or photographic record of an SCP-4024 mound's internal structure is classified Level 4 and is to be stored separately from the general Entomological archive, owing to the mounds' demonstrated correlation with sensitive site information (see Addendum). Personnel discovering an SCP-4024 mound are not to photograph, map, or otherwise document its internal structure themselves; the mound is to be reported and incinerated unexamined wherever operationally possible.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4024 designates a termite species, externally consistent with Reticulitermes but distinguished by anomalous mound-building behavior. SCP-4024 colonies construct internal mound galleries that consistently and precisely replicate, at reduced scale, the floor plan of the building or complex in which the colony is founded, including rooms, corridors, and structural features not indicated by any visible external cue available to the insects, such as underground utility routing and interior walls on floors the colony has no physical access to.

Mound galleries update continuously to reflect structural changes to the source building, typically within 48 to 72 hours of a physical alteration (a new wall, a sealed doorway) being completed. This property has made SCP-4024 mounds a documented, if unintentional, intelligence risk: a colony founded within or near a Foundation facility produces, without any anomalous informational transfer identified by current instrumentation, an accurate architectural record of that facility, including non-public areas.

Incineration of a primary colony has never, across eighteen documented cases, prevented the appearance of a secondary colony elsewhere on or near the same site within fourteen days, mapping the same structure. No mechanism for the transfer of the structural information, or of colony formation instructions, between primary and secondary colonies has been identified; genetic sampling shows no relation between the colonies beyond species.

ADDENDUM 4024-1:
An SCP-4024 mound recovered from a maintenance sub-basement at a decommissioned Foundation records facility (Site designation withheld) was found, on the Level 4 documentation permitted under current protocol, to include a gallery corresponding to a corridor connecting two wings of the facility that does not appear on any current or historical architectural record held by Site Logistics. Physical inspection located the corridor, sealed behind drywall matching the surrounding construction era, containing file storage racks emptied except for a single intact folder, water-damaged beyond legibility, bearing a visible date stamp nine years prior to the facility's official opening. {{4|Site Logistics has no record of the facility, under any designation, existing at that date.|}}

SCP-4025.name: The Understudy
SCP-4025.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4025 is held in a standard humanoid containment cell at
Site-19, furnished to resemble a modest studio apartment rather
than a cell. SCP-4025 has made no attempt to leave containment
since intake and cooperates with all routine requests without
complaint. To satisfy its apparent need to hold a defined role
within a facility, SCP-4025 is issued a Foundation employee badge
under a rotating cover designation and assigned low-risk
administrative tasks: filing, inventory counts, transcription.
Personnel assigned to supervise these tasks are rotated every 90
days and are not briefed on the identity of the most recently
deceased staff member at their site.

Any Foundation staff death occurring on-site, by any cause, is to
be reported to the SCP-4025 monitoring team within one hour.
SCP-4025's cell is to be checked for occupancy immediately
following such a report. If SCP-4025 is absent, standard retrieval
procedure is suspended: SCP-4025 reliably presents itself at a
Foundation facility, typically the one where the death occurred,
within 48 hours. Retrieval teams are instructed to confirm its
identity tag and return it to containment without further
engagement.
