DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4025 is a humanoid male presenting as 40 to 50 years of age.
Its build, coloring, and minor features vary slightly between
sightings within a narrow range; recorded height ranges from 178
to 183 centimeters, and eye color has been logged as brown, hazel,
and grey across separate intake examinations, never consistently.

On nine documented occasions, SCP-4025 has adopted the complete
behavioral profile of a Foundation staff member who died within
the preceding 48 hours: handwriting, vocal cadence, food
preferences, private nicknames for coworkers, and specific
complaints about facility conditions that were never entered into
any personnel record and could not have been learned from one.
SCP-4025 asserts, without exception and without apparent distress,
that it has always held the position of the deceased and has no
memory of being anyone else. It does not react to being told this
is false. It reacts only when asked to account for a gap in the
deceased's history that it cannot fill, at which point it changes
the subject and does not return to it.

When shown a photograph of the actual deceased individual taken
before death, SCP-4025 identifies the photograph as an old picture
of itself and supplies an unprompted, plausible reason for the
discrepancy in appearance: it has lost weight, grown out a beard,
the lighting was poor. This response has been consistent across
all nine subjects.

ADDENDUM 4025-1:
On the badge audit dated 12 February, Site-19 security flagged a
duplicate credential under the name of Dr. ██████, a Level 2
researcher. Investigation located SCP-4025 seated at Dr. ██████'s
desk, in his chair, wearing a name tape reading "██████,"
approximately six hours before Dr. ██████ was found deceased in
his quarters of an apparent cardiac event.

SCP-4025 could not account for its presence at the desk prior to
the confirmed time of death and stated only that it had always sat
there. Time-of-death estimates place Dr. ██████'s death at
approximately 0200. Desk-adjacent camera footage timestamps
SCP-4025's arrival at 2015 the previous evening.

No mechanism for anomalous foreknowledge has been established.
Standing containment procedure has not been revised. No
intervention based on SCP-4025's early presence has been tested;
Ethics Committee review of such testing remains pending.

SCP-4026.name: Next of Kin
SCP-4026.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4026 cannot be reliably held in standard containment. Physical
restraint is possible, but any specimen held longer than 72 hours
exhibits progressive tissue transparency and eventual total
dissolution with no correlating decrease in reported activity
elsewhere, indicating restraint does not stop the anomaly's
function. Current procedure is administrative rather than
physical: Foundation liaisons embedded in 40 municipal vital
records offices across three countries flag any death certificate
on which the next-of-kin field is completed with a name that does
not appear in any prior record associated with the deceased.
Flagged cases are forwarded to Site-19 for review within 24 hours.

When a flagged appearance is confirmed as SCP-4026, a two-person
Foundation team is dispatched under civilian cover to observe the
claiming process without interference. Interference has been
attempted on 4 occasions; in each case, SCP-4026 completed the
claim regardless, through a different named individual matching
the same physical description within 48 hours. Current policy is
non-interference and documentation only.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4026 designates a recurring pattern rather than a single fixed
body. Between 1 and several dozen instances of a humanoid entity
appear annually at municipal records offices, hospitals, and
funeral homes, always in response to the death of an individual
with no documented living relative and no named emergency contact
on file. In each instance the entity presents government-appearing
identification matching a name it has just entered into the
deceased's next-of-kin field, claims the body or remains through
entirely legal channels, and completes all associated paperwork
correctly and without hesitation.

Entities matching SCP-4026's pattern vary in apparent age, sex,
and ethnicity, always plausibly matched to the deceased's
background, but share several traits: unusually still hands while
signing, a signature that is legible but unreproducible on a
second attempt, and an inability to answer any question about the
deceased beyond what is contained in the deceased's own public
records. When asked how they knew the deceased, all instances give
some variation of the same answer: that they have always been the
one who comes.

Foundation review of 118 archived cases matching this pattern, the
earliest dated 1961, found that in no instance did SCP-4026 fail
to appear for an eligible death, and in no instance was a claimed
body or set of remains ever recovered afterward.

INTERVIEW EXCERPT — LOG 4026-7:
The following exchange was recorded during the 6-hour detention of
an SCP-4026 instance at a municipal office in ███████, prior to
the dissolution effect being understood. Interviewer is Agent M.
██████.

Agent: What's your name?
Instance: [Name given on the certificate.]
Agent: Your real name.
Instance: That is the name for this one.
Agent: How did you know Mr. [deceased] had died?
Instance: The position was open.
Agent: What position?
Instance: The one I hold. Someone has to be listed.
Agent: Is that a job? Who assigned it to you?
Instance: It has never not been held.
Agent: What happens to the people who die with nobody?
Instance: There are none of those. That is the position.
Agent: You're saying you're the family of everyone who has no
family.
Instance: I am the entry in the field. Nothing is left blank if it
can be filled.

The instance was released after 6 hours following visible thinning
of the fingertips. It completed the claim of Mr. [deceased]'s
remains the following morning, under a different presented name.

SCP-4027.name: The Unbecome
SCP-4027.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4027 has never been physically detained. No containment cell
exists for it. Standing procedure is detection and damage control
only. Foundation-monitored missing-persons databases, social media
pattern analysis, and municipal records offices are flagged for
any report in which a living individual is described by multiple
independent parties as never having existed, provided physical
records (birth certificate, photographs, correspondence) still
exist and are being actively disputed by exactly one person who
insists they do not recognize the person in them. Such cases are
forwarded to Mobile Task Force Sigma-8 ("No Vacancy") for
verification and, where confirmed, quiet closure.

Confirmed cases receive no attempt at reversal. Nine attempts at
memory or record restoration across 22 confirmed incidents have
not succeeded; the erased individual's absence from the target's
memory and immediate physical records appears total and, to date,
permanent. Surviving photographs and documents referencing the
erased individual elsewhere in the world, not in the target's
direct possession, remain unaffected, which is the primary method
by which Foundation staff confirm that an erasure, rather than an
original absence, has occurred.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4027 is a humanoid entity, observed only in the moments
immediately preceding a confirmed erasure event, always on
security or personal device camera footage, never in person by a
surviving witness. Available footage is of consistently poor
quality regardless of the recording equipment's specifications;
SCP-4027 cannot be reliably assigned a height, build, sex, or skin
tone from any recovered frame, though it is bipedal, wears
clothing appropriate to the setting in which it is filmed, and
appears to make direct eye contact with its target in the final
frame before the target's device or camera experiences a brief
recording gap of variable length.

Following the gap, one person known to the target — a parent,
sibling, spouse, or close friend, selection criteria unknown — is
absent from the target's memory. The target does not experience
this as a loss. They report no grief, no sense of a missing
person, and no distress beyond confusion when confronted with
evidence: a name in their own handwriting, a face in a photograph
they are certain they did not take, a voice on a saved recording
they do not recognize as belonging to anyone.

In 3 of 22 confirmed cases, the erased individual was later
located alive, healthy, and entirely unaware that anything had
happened to them; in each of these cases, they reported that the
target — their parent, sibling, spouse, or friend — had simply
stopped returning calls.

INCIDENT LOG 4027-19:
Subject reported her father deceased of natural causes fourteen
years prior. Cross-reference of tax records located a man matching
her father's description, alive, employed, residing 60 kilometers
from the subject's home, who confirmed his identity and
relationship to the subject upon Foundation contact.

He stated his daughter had stopped calling around the date of the
confirmed erasure event and that he had assumed a falling out. He
had not attempted to reestablish contact. Asked why, he said he
had not wanted to make her uncomfortable. He was not aware, until
told, that she believed him dead.

No further contact between subject and father has been authorized
pending Ethics Committee review of the reintroduction risk.

SCP-4028.name: The Obituarist
SCP-4028.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4028 is held in a standard personnel-grade housing unit at
Site-19, granted the status of voluntary long-term research
subject, and is not physically restrained. SCP-4028 has declined
transfer to a less restrictive facility on each occasion it has
been offered, citing a preference for proximity to "the people
who'll need to check the draft."

SCP-4028 is provided with a notebook and is required to submit a
weekly handwritten draft of the obituary it expects to be
published following its own death. Drafts are collected by an
assigned researcher, photographed, and archived under Test Log
4028. SCP-4028 is not to be shown drafts submitted by any other
instance-adjacent subject, and no member of research staff is to
disclose personal information (marital status, children, cause of
death of relatives) to SCP-4028 under any circumstance, to
preserve the integrity of ongoing accuracy assessment.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4028 is a human male, currently 71 years of age, of otherwise
unremarkable medical and psychological profile. Since voluntary
intake 6 years ago, SCP-4028 has produced 312 weekly obituary
drafts. Each draft is internally consistent with the one
preceding it, amending only details that a genuine obituary would
plausibly update week to week: age, most recent employer, recently
deceased relatives added to the list of those who predeceased him.

SCP-4028 has never produced a draft containing information later
found to be false, including 4 instances in which drafts listed
the deaths of specific, named Foundation personnel by natural
causes, in each case 8 to 14 months before the death occurred and
matching cause of death exactly. SCP-4028 has not been informed of
these confirmations and does not request to know the outcomes of
predictions concerning people other than himself.

Of particular note: drafts from the first 3 years of the study
list SCP-4028 as survived by "no immediate family." Beginning in
year 4, drafts began listing a surviving spouse, first unnamed,
then named as "Researcher L. Emen" beginning in draft 209. Dr. L.
Emen was assigned to SCP-4028's research team 5 months after draft
209 was filed and had no prior connection to the study.

TEST LOG 4028, EXCERPT (DRAFTS 205-213):
Draft 205: "...survived by no immediate family..."
Draft 209: "...survived by his wife..." (name field left blank by
subject, who stated only "I'll know it when I see it")
Draft 213: "...survived by his wife, Dr. L. Emen..."

Dr. Emen was reassigned to a different research team following
Draft 213's review. SCP-4028's subsequent drafts continued to name
her as surviving spouse without amendment. As of this filing, Dr.
Emen has not been informed of the draft's contents, on Ethics
Committee instruction, and reassignment to a third team has been
requested but not yet approved due to staffing shortages in the
relevant department.

ADDENDUM 4028-2:
Dr. Emen has since married a civilian unconnected to the
Foundation. SCP-4028's most recent draft, filed after this event,
continued to list her by her prior surname as surviving spouse,
unchanged. When asked in a subsequent session whether the
notebook needed updating, SCP-4028 said no, and did not elaborate
further despite being given the opportunity.

SCP-4029.name: The Tenant
SCP-4029.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4029 is held in a residential structure built to replicate the
interior dimensions and materials of its origin building (Address
████████, hereafter Building-4029), acquired by the Foundation
under a shell property management company. A minimum of one
Foundation staff member, posing as a tenant, must occupy
Building-4029's replica at all times; unoccupied periods exceeding
6 continuous hours have been correlated with measurable
acceleration in SCP-4029's biological aging (see Description).
Tenancy assignments rotate every 30 days.

The original Building-4029, a condemned four-story apartment
structure at ████████, is to remain standing and is not to be
demolished, sold, or re-zoned under any circumstance without Level
4 approval and prior consultation with SCP-4029's research team.
Site acquisition of the surrounding lot is in progress to prevent
third-party interference.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4029 presents as a human child of apparent age 8 at the time
of its recovery 6 years ago from Building-4029, then recently
condemned and vacated following a structural inspection failure.
Medical examination at recovery estimated SCP-4029's biological
age at 8 to 9 years, consistent with apparent age.

Subsequent examinations, conducted annually, have found SCP-4029's
biological age increasing at a rate inconsistent with the passage
of calendar time. Current biological age is estimated at 38 to 42
years against 6 elapsed calendar years, a ratio that has not
remained constant: aging accelerates during periods when
Building-4029 (the original structure) stands unoccupied and
slows, on 2 recorded occasions nearly to a halt, during the
11-month period a squatter occupied the building's ground floor
before Foundation acquisition.

SCP-4029 retains the vocabulary, motor coordination, and emotional
affect of an 8-year-old child regardless of its measured biological
age, and has expressed no distress at its changing physical
appearance beyond asking, at each examination, whether "someone's
staying at the house." Radiographic and dermatological findings
are consistent with SCP-4029's current apparent physical age
rather than its stated 8-year-old affect, producing what examining
staff have described as the experience of interviewing a young
child inside an elderly body.

ADDENDUM 4029-2:
A municipal proposal to demolish Building-4029 as part of a
redevelopment initiative was quietly withdrawn following
Foundation intervention through a shell environmental-review firm
three years ago. A second proposal is anticipated within the
current fiscal cycle. Site acquisition remains the preferred
long-term solution; until it is complete, SCP-4029's research team
has requested standing authority to file further planning
objections without case-by-case Level 4 sign-off, a request still
under review. The team has also submitted a projection of how
quickly SCP-4029's biological age would advance should a second
proposal be approved, though confirming the projection would
require the building to actually stand vacant.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
We have not told it what happens to the building if it dies before
we can secure the block, and it has stopped asking why the same
three questions get asked every visit. I don't think it's
forgotten how to ask. I think it's stopped needing the answer. —
Dr. ██████

SCP-4030.name: Anticipated Damage
SCP-4030.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4030 is held in a padded, single-occupant isolation cell
containing no furniture, edges, or objects capable of producing
laceration, fracture, or burn injury. The cell is filmed
continuously by two independent, non-networked camera systems on
separate power circuits. Footage from both systems is reviewed in
real time by a rotating two-person monitoring team in an adjacent
room, never the same two individuals on consecutive shifts.

Monitoring staff who observe SCP-4030 displaying an injury on
either camera feed that SCP-4030 does not yet visibly have are to
immediately alert the on-site medical team and flag the footage
timestamp, without entering the cell or attempting physical
intervention. Physical intervention has been attempted on 7
occasions; in each case, the predicted injury occurred regardless,
by a mechanism unconnected to the intervention (see Test Log). As
of this revision, monitoring staff assigned to SCP-4030 are
limited to 4-hour shifts and are examined by medical staff for
unexplained injuries at the end of each shift, per Addendum
4030-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4030 is a human male, 34 years of age, held by the Foundation
since presenting at a public hospital with an unexplained
combination of injuries matching no consistent narrative he could
provide. SCP-4030's anomalous property was identified 9 days into
observation, when monitoring footage was reviewed and found to
show SCP-4030 with a laceration across his right forearm at 0340
that he did not sustain, visibly, until 0710 the same morning,
under sealed and monitored conditions in which no object capable
of producing the injury was present in the cell.

This pattern has recurred 26 times. The interval between the
injury's appearance on camera and its occurrence in observable
reality ranges from 40 minutes to 6 hours. The mechanism by which
the injury is ultimately sustained has varied and has never
matched an available cause within the cell: on 11 occasions
SCP-4030 has been found injured with no witnessed event producing
the injury at all, the wound simply present at the predicted time.

SCP-4030 reports no memory of sustaining any of the injuries and
does not react with distress to being shown the predictive footage
in advance, stating only that he has "stopped trying to dodge
it," as dodging has not altered the outcome in any tested
instance.

ADDENDUM 4030-2:
On the date below, Technician R. ██████, having completed a double
shift reviewing SCP-4030's footage, reported a stinging sensation
in her left palm. No injury was visible. Fourteen hours later,
footage from her personal phone camera — recovered per standing
policy from all staff assigned to SCP-4030 monitoring, though
never pointed at the cell or at Technician ██████ herself during
working hours — was found to contain an 8-second clip, timestamped
during her shift, of her own left hand with a laceration she did
not yet have. She sustained the matching injury 3 hours after the
footage was recovered, while off-duty and off-site, cause
unwitnessed.

Monitoring staff rotation and post-shift medical screening (see
Special Containment Procedures) were implemented following this
incident. SCP-4030's object class was revised from Euclid to Keter
the same week.

SCP-4031.name: Unimpeachable
SCP-4031.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4031 is housed in a standard personnel-grade quarters at
Site-19 and is permitted supervised movement within the
residential wing. SCP-4031's anomalous effect has a measured
radius of approximately 9 meters and cannot be suppressed or
reduced by any tested method (see Test Log 4031); containment
therefore focuses on scheduling rather than physical restraint.
SCP-4031 is not to be present in any meeting, interview, or shared
space involving more than 3 staff members without prior written
notice posted at the room's entrance, reading: SCP-4031 EFFECT
RADIUS ACTIVE.

Use of SCP-4031 for authorized interrogation of Foundation-held
individuals requires Level 3 sign-off and a debriefing officer not
otherwise involved in the interrogation, present to manage the
psychological aftermath for interviewing staff, who reliably
disclose true information beyond the scope of the interrogation as
an unavoidable side effect of proximity.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4031 is a human female, 29 years of age, who has been
documented as physically incapable of producing a false statement
since referral to the Foundation by a family member who described
her as "impossible to lie to and worse to lie around." Testing
confirms SCP-4031's inability to lie is total: she cannot produce
a false statement even under direct instruction, financial
incentive, or threat, and experiences acute physical distress
(elevated heart rate, difficulty breathing) when attempting to do
so, ceasing only once she reverts to a true statement.

The secondary and, for containment purposes, more significant
property is that any individual within approximately 9 meters of
SCP-4031 experiences a comparable, though less absolute,
compulsion toward honesty: subjects report difficulty completing
social lies, including reflexive courtesies ("I'm fine," "it's not
a problem"), and in extended proximity begin volunteering true
information they had not intended to share, including information
unrelated to any question asked. The effect does not extend to
written communication and ends within approximately 4 minutes of
the subject leaving the radius, with no lasting compulsion
afterward.

INTERVIEW EXCERPT — LOG 4031-C:
Recorded following a scheduling error that placed SCP-4031 in a
shared meeting for 40 minutes.

Dr. ██████: How are you feeling after that?
Subject (Researcher, name withheld): Not great. I told my
supervisor I thought his restructuring proposal was going to fail
and that I've thought that since the first meeting, and that I
didn't say so before because I wanted the transfer he's dangling.
I don't — I wasn't going to say any of that today.
Dr. ██████: Do you regret saying it?
Subject: I don't know how to answer that honestly right now, so
I'm not going to try.

Session ended at subject's request. SCP-4031's scheduling notice
protocol was revised the following week to require two independent
confirmations rather than one.

ADDENDUM 4031-1:
SCP-4031 has requested, on 3 separate occasions, to be informed
whenever a scheduling notice fails to prevent an unplanned
exposure, stating that she would rather know who heard something
they did not mean to say than not know. This request has been
denied on the grounds that informing her would itself constitute
a further disclosure requiring a notice of its own.

SCP-4032.name: The Missing Brothers
SCP-4032.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4032 is held at Site-19 under standard humanoid containment
with no unusual physical requirements. Primary containment effort
is directed not at SCP-4032 but at civil records pertaining to
████████, the town of SCP-4032's origin: birth registries, school
enrollment rolls, the original structural plan for the destroyed
residence, and 1990 census data are to be checked against a
securely stored offline backup on a monthly basis. Any discrepancy
between the live record and the backup is to be reported to the
SCP-4032 research lead within 24 hours and is not to be corrected
in the live record pending review.

Personnel are not to independently research SCP-4032's claimed
family history outside of assigned tasks. Three researchers have
done so without authorization; in each case, records they located
and printed for personal reference were found, on later
comparison, to no longer match records pulled from the same
source.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4032 is a human male, 44 years of age, the sole survivor of a
residential fire at ████████ that killed his parents 6 years ago.
SCP-4032 consistently states that he had two younger brothers,
ages 9 and 11 at the time of the fire, who also died in the house
that night. No record — hospital, school, census, or otherwise —
corroborates the existence of these siblings as of the date of
intake, and the original structural plan for the destroyed
residence shows a two-bedroom layout inconsistent with a household
of five.

Since intake, 14 separate verifications of the relevant civil
records have been conducted. In 6 of these 14 verifications,
discrepancies were found between the current record and a
previously archived copy: a hospital birth record for a second son
appeared in county archives between the 3rd and 4th verification;
a school enrollment card for a third child appeared between the
9th and 10th; the structural plan on file with the county was
replaced, without any submission on record authorizing the change,
with a three-bedroom version between the 11th and 12th.

SCP-4032 has not been informed of these changes and has never
altered his account, which has remained identical, word for word
according to transcript comparison, across all 19 interviews
conducted since intake.

ADDENDUM 4032-2:
A fifteenth verification, conducted after this entry was filed,
found the county's 1990 census summary table itself revised to
list a household of five at the ████████ address, though the
underlying enumeration sheets used to produce that table remain
unchanged and still show three. No explanation has been proposed
for a summary table diverging from its own source data. The
county records clerk reported no system log identifying who or
what had altered the table, noting only that the change was
detected by comparing the most recent backup against the current
state. The research team has recommended the county's public
terminal access be quietly suspended pending further study; the
recommendation has not yet been approved.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
We keep the backups offline because print copies discovered a
drift within days even when nobody had touched them. He isn't
asking us to believe him. He already knows he's right. He's just
waiting for the paperwork to agree. — Researcher S. ██████,
Site-19

SCP-4033.name: The Last Visitor
SCP-4033.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4033 cannot be physically contained; no confirmed instance has
resulted in capture, detention, or specimen recovery. Standing
procedure is limited to identification of at-risk individuals and
post-event documentation. Foundation-affiliated hospice,
elder-care, and long-term isolation facilities (currently 6, under
cover as private care providers) are instructed to report any
patient or resident, without qualifying family present, who
reports an unscheduled visit from someone the patient states they
had not expected and had not been informed was coming.

Any such report is treated as a probable SCP-4033 event. Facility
staff are not to attempt to remove, question, or otherwise
interact with the reported visitor and are to withdraw from the
room if physically present when the report is made, citing routine
care duties. In 41 of 44 confirmed events, the patient or resident
was found deceased within 6 hours of the reported visit, of a
cause consistent with the individual's existing prognosis.
Facility staff are debriefed but not informed of the anomaly's
classification.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4033 has never been directly observed by Foundation personnel;
its properties are reconstructed entirely from patient and
resident accounts collected before death, and from 3 confirmed
instances of survival following interruption of the visit (see
Addendum). In each account, the subject describes a visitor
matching, in appearance, voice, and manner, a specific person
significant to them — most frequently a deceased parent, spouse,
or child, though in 4 cases a living person the subject had been
estranged from for a period exceeding a decade. The subject is,
without exception, certain of the visitor's identity and reports
no confusion or fear, describing the visit as expected,
comforting, or overdue.

Subjects uniformly report that the visitor does not speak about
the subject's condition, does not offer comfort or reassurance
regarding death, and instead discusses ordinary matters: a meal
once shared, an unfinished disagreement, weather from decades
prior. Subjects who die during or shortly after a reported visit
are, without exception, recorded as having died without apparent
fear or distress, regardless of the severity of their underlying
condition.

ADDENDUM 4033-3:
In 3 confirmed cases, the reported visit was interrupted before
its conclusion, by unrelated facility routine (a scheduled
medication round, a fire alarm test, a roommate's arrival). In all
3 cases, the subject survived beyond the expected mortality window
associated with their prognosis, by 4, 9, and 22 months
respectively, and reported the visitor as "gone before we
finished." All 3 subjects, when their condition later became
terminal, reported the same visitor returning, and in all 3 cases
the visit reached its conclusion undisturbed. All 3 subjects died
within the following 6 hours.

ADDENDUM 4033-4:
Two of the 6 affiliated facilities have independently proposed
installing cameras in resident rooms to capture a confirmed visit
on video. Both proposals were declined by the research lead, who
noted that facilities where recording was attempted without
authorization in the past produced footage that, on review,
showed the room empty for the visit's full duration despite staff
and resident testimony placing the visitor there throughout.

SCP-4034.name: Self-Narrating
SCP-4034.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4034 is housed in a standard personnel-grade quarters at
Site-19. SCP-4034 narrates its own actions continuously and
involuntarily in a flat, third-person register, typically 2 to 5
seconds before performing the narrated action. This narration is
not to be interrupted, contradicted, or prevented by containment
staff under any circumstance, per Article 3 of this entry (see
Test Log 4034 for justification). Staff assigned to SCP-4034 are
permitted to converse with it normally; SCP-4034 narrates its own
speech alongside its physical actions ("He says he's fine")
without apparent distress or awareness that this is unusual.

Any occasion on which SCP-4034's narration describes an action it
does not go on to perform is to be logged immediately as a Class-2
anomalous event and reported to the on-duty site director
regardless of hour, per Test Log 4034, Entry 6.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4034 is a human male, 51 years of age, who has narrated his
own actions aloud, apparently without voluntary control, for a
period he estimates at 9 years prior to Foundation contact.
Independent verification across 300 recorded hours of observation
confirms the narration precedes the described action with 100%
accuracy and a consistent lead time, and that SCP-4034 cannot
suppress the narration through any tested method, including
sedation, though sedation slows the lead time proportionally to
reaction time.

SCP-4034 reports that the narration is not experienced as speech
he chooses to produce; he describes it as reading a caption that
appears slightly before he needs it. He has never found the
narration to be wrong.

TEST LOG 4034, ENTRY 6:
Test conducted to determine outcome if SCP-4034's narrated action
is deliberately prevented. SCP-4034 stated: "He reaches for the
cup." Researcher on duty removed the cup from the table before
SCP-4034's hand arrived.

SCP-4034's hand closed on empty air in the exact motion and
position it would have used to grip the cup. SCP-4034 did not
appear to notice the cup's absence, continued the motion as though
drinking, and resumed unrelated narration 4 seconds later ("He
sets it down"), at which point his hand opened at table height as
if releasing an object that was not there.

SCP-4034 was asked afterward whether he had noticed the cup was
missing. He stated the cup had been there. When shown footage, he
stated the footage must be wrong and declined to discuss it
further. Testing of this kind has been suspended pending Ethics
Committee review of the apparent disconnect between SCP-4034's
narrated reality and observable reality, and what continued
testing might produce if the two are ever forced fully apart.

ADDENDUM 4034-2:
Staff have noted that SCP-4034's narration occasionally precedes
a statement about a third party rather than itself, correctly
describing an action taken by a researcher elsewhere in the
facility before that researcher performs it. This has occurred 3
times, each confirmed against separate camera logs after the fact.
SCP-4034 has not been asked to narrate on command, per Ethics
Committee instruction, pending review of whether doing so would
extend the anomaly's apparent range deliberately. This finding has
raised the possibility that the source of SCP-4034's narration may
not be limited to its own awareness.

SCP-4035.name: Inconsistent Witness
SCP-4035.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4035 is held in solitary humanoid containment at Site-19.
Personnel assigned to SCP-4035 are limited to a fixed roster of 4
individuals, none of whom are to be rotated off assignment or
replaced except by Level 4 authorization, following Incident
4035-2 (see Incident Log). New personnel are not to be introduced
to SCP-4035 without prior review of Incident 4035-2 and written
acknowledgment that they may, following contact, sincerely and
permanently believe SCP-4035 to be someone other than who
Foundation records describe.

Photographic and video documentation of SCP-4035 is to be
maintained for administrative record only. Such documentation has
not been found to correct a witness's belief about SCP-4035's
identity in any tested case; witnesses instead report that the
documentation depicts the person they already believe SCP-4035 to
be.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4035 is a humanoid individual of consistent physical
measurements according to camera and instrument records (height,
weight, dental structure, fingerprints all stable across 6 years
of Foundation observation). No two individuals who have met
SCP-4035 in person, however, report the same name, life history,
relationship, or, in most cases, physical description for him. Of
22 personnel who have interacted with SCP-4035 for longer than 1
hour, 19 independently and sincerely identify him as a specific
person from their own past — a former classmate, an estranged
relative, a childhood neighbor — each providing a full name,
biography, and account of their relationship that cannot be
reconciled with any other witness's account, including witnesses
present in the room at the same time.

SCP-4035 itself does not know its own name, birthplace, or history
prior to an initial recovery date 6 years ago, and has, across 6
years of interview, offered 11 different self-descriptions to 11
different interviewers, each consistent with that interviewer's
independent belief about who he is rather than with any of
SCP-4035's own prior statements.

INCIDENT LOG 4035-2:
Two long-term assigned researchers, Dr. ██████ and Dr.
██████████, were scheduled into the same interview session with
SCP-4035 for the first time, an oversight in scheduling not
previously permitted. Both researchers greeted SCP-4035 by
different names, referenced entirely different multi-year personal
histories with him, and, when each corrected the other, became
increasingly distressed rather than reconsidering their own
account. Session was terminated after 12 minutes.

Both researchers subsequently requested and received psychological
evaluation; both retained their original, mutually exclusive
belief about SCP-4035's identity afterward and neither has since
agreed to discuss the incident with the other. Scheduling
safeguards described in Special Containment Procedures were
implemented the same day.

ADDENDUM 4035-3:
A retired staff member who worked with SCP-4035 for 2 years prior
to reassignment was recontacted for a follow-up interview 4 years
later. She provided, without prompting, the same name and
biography for SCP-4035 that she had given originally, word for
word according to comparison with her original transcript, despite
having had no further contact with SCP-4035 or its file in the
intervening period. This has reinforced the team's working view
that SCP-4035's identity is not a problem to be solved so much as
a condition to be monitored.

SCP-4036.name: The Countdown
SCP-4036.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4036 is held in a sealed, single-occupant cell at Site-19,
monitored by camera only; no personnel are to enter SCP-4036's
cell or remain within its direct line of sight for longer than
necessary to complete an assigned task. SCP-4036 is supplied
continuously with a countable, expendable, inanimate object source
— currently a hopper of 4,000,000 individually numbered plastic
tokens, refilled from an offsite stock before the count reaches
50,000 remaining — which SCP-4036 counts aloud, in descending
order, without instruction, for as long as tokens remain available
to it.

Personnel are never to enter SCP-4036's field of view during a
period in which its token supply has been exhausted or
interrupted, however briefly. Two Foundation-wide alert protocols
exist for this contingency (see Addendum 4036-1) and take
precedence over all standing site orders except a confirmed
SCP-682 or SCP-076 breach. SCP-4036 has not, since intake, been
permitted contact with any Foundation staff member without a
physical barrier between them.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4036 is a human male, 39 years of age, formerly designated
D-9188, who was assigned as a test subject for a now-terminated
experiment (Experiment Log ███, records restricted, Level 4)
involving SCP-████. Following the experiment's termination,
SCP-4036 was found to compulsively count aloud, in descending
order, toward any living being or discrete countable set of
objects within its perception, and unable to stop counting toward
a target once begun except by reaching a number it treats as an
endpoint, typically but not always zero or one.

Any living being SCP-4036 successfully counts down to completion
experiences a serious, medically inexplicable adverse event within
the following 24 hours: 6 of 8 confirmed cases prior to SCP-4036's
current containment resulted in death, from causes ranging from
sudden cardiac arrest to catastrophic organ failure in previously
healthy individuals, none linked by autopsy to any external cause.
The remaining 2 cases resulted in permanent, severe cognitive
impairment.

SCP-4036 does not choose its targets and has, on all tested
occasions, redirected its count toward the nearest available
countable subject when its current target is removed from
perception, provided the redirection occurs before the count
reaches its terminal number. Counting toward an inanimate,
sufficiently numerous set of discrete objects appears to satisfy
the compulsion without producing the described effect, which is
the basis for current containment.

ADDENDUM 4036-1:
Following a token hopper jam during a facility power fluctuation on
[DATE], SCP-4036's count reached zero with no object or person as
its stated target for approximately 40 seconds before backup stock
was manually loaded. No adverse event was recorded at Site-19
during this window. However, Site-██, located 210 kilometers away,
reported an unexplained, simultaneous cluster of 3 cardiac
incidents among unaffiliated civilian staff, one fatal, with no
shared risk factor identified. A causal link to SCP-4036 has not
been confirmed and is considered unlikely by the assigned research
lead on statistical grounds alone, and is considered likely by
every member of SCP-4036's containment team who was on shift that
day.

SCP-4037.name: The Fourth Stall
SCP-4037.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4037 is located within a decommissioned rest-stop facility off a rural state highway, acquired by the Foundation under cover of a condemnation order. The stall must remain marked "OUT OF ORDER" at all times. Public access is deterred by posted signage only; physical barriers have been tested and do not affect visitation frequency, and their removal did not increase incident rate. A calibrated laser rangefinder mounted above the stall's exterior lintel records interior depth automatically every six hours. Foundation personnel who must measure the interior directly are limited to sessions of no more than ten minutes and must carry a tethered guideline anchored to the stall door hinge.

Custodial staff assigned to the facility are rotated every 90 days regardless of reported incidents. The facility's original cleaning logbook, recovered at acquisition, is stored in Site-19 Archive Wing under item designation 4037-L and is not to be returned to the site under any circumstance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4037 refers to the fourth toilet stall in the men's restroom of a rest-stop facility built in 1987. The exterior of the restroom building measures 4.3 by 6.1 metres. Laser measurements of the stall's interior consistently return a depth between 9.4 and 41.2 metres from the door to the rear wall, the figure varying between readings with no pattern yet tied to time of day, season, or personnel present. A support pillar absent from the building's original architectural plans is visible at inconsistent distances within the stall and does not appear in any photograph taken from outside the doorway.

Objects placed just inside the stall and left overnight are recovered the following morning in the same position. Objects carried more than approximately nine metres past the doorway have not been recovered.

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): Ground-penetrating radar conducted around the restroom building's exterior in 2019 found no subsurface cavity consistent with the stall's deeper readings. The volume implied by the largest recorded measurement, if it existed as physical space, would place the stall's rear wall approximately 200 metres past the facility's parking lot, beneath the shoulder of the highway itself.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: The recovered cleaning logbook (item 4037-L) contains dated entries for the facility's restrooms beginning on its printed first page. Stall 4 is checked off as cleaned on 6 March 1981 — six years before the facility's recorded date of construction. Site records confirm no structure existed at these coordinates prior to 1987. Material analysis dates the logbook's binding, ink, and paper stock to no earlier than 1985. No explanation has been entered into the file. — Dr. Onat, Site-19

EXPLORATION LOG 4037-1: A tethered quadcopter drone with an onboard camera was flown into the stall to a maximum tether extension of 40 metres. The video feed showed a featureless tiled corridor continuing beyond visual range, lit by no visible fixture. Signal was not lost at any point; the tether remained taut and unobstructed throughout. Total flight duration logged by ground control: six minutes, forty seconds. Total flight duration logged by the drone's onboard clock upon retrieval: forty-six minutes, two seconds. The drone's battery charge on retrieval was consistent with the longer duration.

SCP-4038.name: Silo Six
SCP-4038.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4038 is contained within its original structure, a steel grain silo at a decommissioned agricultural cooperative, acquired by the Foundation through purchase of the surrounding parcel under an agricultural-easement cover story. The access hatch at the silo's base is welded shut; the only permitted entry is the roof hatch, monitored by a weight-bearing sensor array and a suspended microphone. Grain is no longer added or removed by Foundation personnel under any circumstance, following Incident 4038-3 (see below). A perimeter of 30 metres is maintained around the structure and monitored by motion-triggered camera.

Personnel assigned to overnight monitoring shifts report any change in the recorded settling-sound pattern to the on-call researcher immediately; no entry is authorized in response to such a report without Level 3 authorization.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4038 refers to a 12-metre steel grain silo constructed in 1974 and operated by an agricultural cooperative until 2016, when the cooperative reported the structure's fill sensors were "impossible" and ceased using it. The silo's fill-level sensor, mounted internally at the 80% capacity mark, has not read positive since Foundation acquisition despite an estimated 340 metric tons of grain having been added to the structure over the cooperative's final three years of use, calculated from purchase records. No corresponding volume of grain has been found outside the structure.

A directional microphone lowered through the roof hatch records a continuous low sound consistent with grain settling and shifting, at a volume and frequency inconsistent with a stationary mass. The sound does not correlate with wind, temperature change, or any Foundation activity at the structure and has been continuously present since monitoring began in 2016.

On four occasions, objects have been recovered from the silo's discharge auger that do not correspond to any inventory of material placed in the structure: a rubber overshoe, size 10, undamaged; a wristwatch, stopped, engraved with initials not matching any employee of the cooperative on record; a child's mitten; and, most recently, a laminated identification card issued by the cooperative to an employee whose personnel file lists a termination date of 1979 and no forwarding address.

ADDENDUM 4038-1: Cooperative payroll records list a Daniel Ostrow, silo operator, as having failed to report for his shift on 14 November 1979. No missing-persons report was filed; a note in his personnel file, unsigned, reads "assumed relocated." The identification card recovered from the auger in 2021 carries his name and photograph. Foundation search of public records has found no trace of Daniel Ostrow after 1979 in any capacity.

INCIDENT LOG 4038-3: D-9231 was directed to enter the silo through the roof hatch and retrieve a grain sample from a depth of approximately 2 metres for isotopic analysis. Entry was made at 0940. D-9231 did not respond to radio contact after 0947. Retrieval was attempted at 1000; D-9231 was located just inside the hatch, unresponsive to voice, and extracted without further incident.

Upon recovery, D-9231 reported having spent what they estimated as three days inside the silo, wading through grain that receded ahead of them "like it didn't want me touching the bottom," without locating a floor. D-9231's beard growth and observed hunger were consistent with this account despite an elapsed exterior time of twenty minutes. The silo's fill sensor showed no displacement corresponding to D-9231's reported movement through the grain. D-9231 was administered Class-A amnestics and reassigned. No further personnel entries have been authorized.

SCP-4039.name: The Countdown Ward
SCP-4039.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4039 occupies the fourth-floor east wing of a regional hospital, currently operated under Foundation front company [REDACTED] Healthcare Holdings as a legitimate long-term care ward. The wing's twenty-two rooms remain in clinical use; discontinuing admissions was assessed to create more anomalous exposure risk via investigative journalism than continuing normal operation under Foundation staffing. All wing nursing staff are Foundation personnel; non-Foundation physicians rotate through under standard hospital privileging and are not briefed.

Each room's door placard is photographed at every shift change (0700, 1500, 2300). Placards are never to be removed, covered, or altered by staff under any circumstance; three attempts to do so are on record and are detailed in Addendum 4039-2. Patients or family who inquire about the numbering are to be told it reflects "internal bed management" by briefed nursing staff. Patients confirmed to be within 5 days of their placard reaching 000 are not to be informed of this fact per Foundation Medical Ethics directive 4039-A, which remains under periodic review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4039 refers to an anomalous numbering system affecting the door placards of twenty-two hospital rooms. Placards display a three-digit number that decreases by exactly one at each local midnight, regardless of room occupancy, cleaning, renovation, or placard replacement. When a room's number reaches 000, its current occupant dies within the following 24 hours, of a cause unrelated to the numbering and, in 19 of 22 documented terminal cases, unrelated to the occupant's admitting diagnosis.

Discharge, transfer to another facility, or removal from the wing entirely does not halt the countdown or prevent the associated death; in seven documented cases, the patient died at another facility, at home, or in an unrelated accident on the date corresponding to their wing placard's 000 reading. The countdown appears attached to the individual who most recently occupied the room at the time monitoring began for them, not to the room itself, though a new occupant assigned to a room already mid-countdown for a previous patient begins a separate, independently tracked count of their own that the placard does not display simultaneously.

Numbers observed on intake range from 001 to 3,652, the latter interpreted as approximately ten years. No instance of a placard increasing, pausing, or reading a number inconsistent with a subsequent confirmed death date has been recorded.

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): On two occasions, unrelated patients in different rooms reached 000 on the same calendar date without any recorded connection between them beyond shared floor assignment. Both died within the 24-hour window: one of cardiac arrest, one in a stairwell fall at a facility 90 kilometres away. Statistical review found the coincidence rate consistent with chance given wing occupancy over the sample period, which Dr. Farrow's addendum notes is, if anything, a more unsettling finding than a hidden connection would have been.|}}

INTERVIEW EXCERPT — Nurse T. Beltran, Foundation-embedded staff, 6 years on the wing: "You stop looking at the door after a while. First year, I'd walk past and do the math without meaning to — okay, she's got four months, he's got a week. You can't carry that and keep working. Room 114, I remember, because it sat at triple-zero for three days and the woman in it was doing fine, sitting up, eating, talking about going home Thursday. She did go home Thursday. Hit by a delivery truck two blocks from the hospital, walking distance, on day three exactly. I checked the timestamp against the placard photo after. It matched to the hour."

SCP-4040.name: The Unlisted Platform
SCP-4040.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Access to SCP-4040 is restricted via a maintenance hatch on a transit line between Stations 14 and 15, disguised as a permanently sealed electrical junction on all transit authority documentation. The hatch is monitored by a pressure sensor logging any opening; unauthorized openings have not occurred since Foundation acquisition of the access point in 2015. Foundation personnel embedded within the transit authority's central control room monitor the system-wide digital map display for the unscheduled appearance of an unlisted station between Stations 14 and 15; such appearances have coincided exclusively with confirmed power interruptions to the control room's primary display system, lasting a mean duration of four minutes.

During a confirmed appearance, embedded personnel are to photograph the display and log the exact duration. No attempt is to be made to access SCP-4040 during an active appearance event; all controlled entries occur only while the platform is not listed on any active map.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4040 is a fully constructed subway platform, approximately 140 metres in length, located along an active transit line between two operating stations, with no corresponding entry in any historical or current transit authority planning document, construction record, or as-built survey. The line itself began operation in 2011; SCP-4040 exhibits wear patterns — polished platform edging, worn floor tile in pedestrian traffic patterns, and layered advertising poster residue — consistent with 40 to 60 years of continuous public use.

Trains on the line do not stop at SCP-4040 and give no indication of recognizing it as a station; conductors interviewed report no memory of slowing or any anomaly at the platform's location, and onboard timing logs show no discrepancy accounting for its length. The platform's public address system activates on an irregular schedule, averaging once every nine days, and announces the arrival of trains at station names that do not appear in any current or historical iteration of the transit system, in the recorded voice of the system's actual announcer, who has been consulted and denies recording the clips in question.

Graffiti recovered from the platform walls has been dated by aerosol composition analysis to a range beginning approximately 1968, predating the line's construction by over four decades.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We keep waiting for the platform to be finished being old. It isn't going to be. Every wear survey we run comes back further than the last one, like the platform is aging away from us rather than toward us. Recommend we stop dating it and just accept the number as a placeholder that gets worse. — Researcher Vance

INCIDENT LOG 4040-2: A transit authority maintenance worker, unaffiliated with the Foundation, reported over the authority's internal radio that he could "see the old platform again" from a service ladder near Station 14, during a power failure affecting three city blocks. Dispatch records show no such platform in his assigned work order. Foundation liaison intercepted the report before it reached a wider distribution list; the worker was located, administered Class-A amnestics, and reassigned to a route not adjacent to SCP-4040. His original radio call, twenty-two seconds long, has been retained for audio comparison against the platform's own unexplained PA activations; no match has been found.

SCP-4041.name: The Between Floor
SCP-4041.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The elevator car containing SCP-4041 is located within a Foundation-owned commercial office tower operating under shell company [REDACTED] Properties. The unlabeled button is covered by a keyed physical guard plate bearing a false "OUT OF SERVICE — CALL FACILITIES" label; the guard plate's key is held by on-site Foundation facilities staff only. A tamper sensor logs any attempt to remove the plate. Civilian tenants of the building are not briefed. Building facilities staff rotate every 18 months.

Any confirmed activation of SCP-4041 (guard plate removed, button pressed, doors opening onto a non-standard floor) triggers immediate elevator lockout for the remaining car bank and dispatch of a two-person retrieval team to the elevator shaft's nearest accessible floor.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4041 is an unlabeled button located on the control panel of elevator car 3 in a fourteen-storey office building, positioned between the buttons for floors 7 and 8. The building's floor plan and fire safety documentation, unchanged since original 1998 construction, show no intermediate floor at this position; the physical gap between floors 7 and 8's finished ceiling and floor heights measures approximately 3.4 metres, consistent with standard single-floor construction and insufficient to contain a full additional storey.

When pressed, the button causes the elevator to travel for a duration of between 40 seconds and 6 minutes (mean 90 seconds, no correlation found with any external variable) before opening onto a floor matching the building's general floor plan but configured as an office space last renovated, by fixture and signage style, in approximately the mid-1980s. The space is unoccupied, dust-laden in a manner consistent with prolonged disuse, and contains functioning electrical lighting and at least one active telephone line per exploration.

Personnel who enter SCP-4041's floor and remain for a subjectively measured duration return to find elapsed exterior time exceeding their subjective duration by a ratio that has ranged from 6:1 to just over 30:1 across nine controlled entries, with no floor-side clock or calendar available to personnel during entry to account for the discrepancy in advance.

ADDENDUM 4041-1: On Entry 4041-6, Researcher Oyelaran placed an outgoing call on the floor's active telephone line to a number pre-selected as belonging to a colleague's desk phone elsewhere in the building. The colleague, interviewed immediately after, confirmed receiving a call at the corresponding exterior time, four hours after Oyelaran's subjective two-minute call, and described the caller's voice as Oyelaran's but "talking like something had already gone wrong for her, apologizing before I said anything."

INCIDENT LOG 4041-4: D-6650 was directed to remain on SCP-4041's floor for a subjective period of ten minutes before returning via the elevator, which remains stationary and available for return throughout an entry. D-6650 did not return within four hours of exterior time. Retrieval team entry located D-6650 seated at a desk in the floor's northeast office, uninjured, with visible hair and nail growth consistent with several months' elapsed time. D-6650 reported a subjective duration of "maybe two weeks," during which they had answered the floor's telephone on nine occasions, spoken with callers who did not identify themselves, and eventually stopped waiting for someone to come get them.

SCP-4042.name: The Counting Hedge
SCP-4042.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4042 is located on the grounds of a decommissioned country estate acquired by the Foundation in advance of a repeat outbreak. The maze's perimeter hedge, 3.1 metres in height, is maintained at its original density; sections showing thinning are hand-replanted rather than mechanically groomed to avoid attracting local landscaping contractors. A single access gate is monitored by camera and guarded at all times by Foundation security personnel disguised as estate groundskeepers.

Entry to SCP-4042 for any purpose, including maintenance, requires an even number of entrants. Where an even number cannot be achieved, one tailor's mannequin of approximate adult height and weight, dressed in a manner indistinguishable from Foundation personnel at a casual glance, is added to the entering group to restore parity. Personnel are reminded that the mannequin's presence in the group must be maintained in headcount reporting throughout the exercise; groups are not authorized to exit without confirming their exit headcount, mannequin included, equals their entry headcount.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4042 is a boxwood hedge maze covering approximately 1.4 hectares on the grounds of an estate built in 1911. Measured total hedge-path length is constant at 2.6 kilometres regardless of entry point or exit taken. Any group of an odd number of individuals that enters SCP-4042 together exits, via the single access gate, with one fewer member than entered. The missing individual is not observed to leave by any other route; ground-penetrating radar, cadaver dogs, and thermal imaging of the maze interior following 14 documented disappearances have located no remains, and no missing individual has been recovered alive.

Surviving group members retain full memory of the missing individual, including grief and continued searching behaviour, distinguishing SCP-4042's effect from erasure-type anomalies; the loss is remembered, simply not preventable and not reversible. Groups entering with an even number, including those made even by the addition of a non-human proxy object of comparable mass and outline, have exited at full headcount in all 61 documented Foundation-supervised entries to date.

Solitary entrants (a group of one) have not been recovered under any circumstance; three such disappearances predate Foundation acquisition and are recorded in county historical archives as unsolved.

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): On Entry 4042-38, the mannequin substituted for a fourth D-Class member was recovered at the exit gate rather than passing through it normally; camera footage shows it arriving from within the maze interior roughly nine minutes after the human members, moving under no observed external force, its recorded clothing damp and its positioning consistent with an upright figure that had lost balance and partially recovered. It has not been reused.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We don't know what the maze is short by when it takes someone, and I don't want to know badly enough to test it with a headcount we can't restore. The mannequin works. We are not asking why. — Dr. Preiss

SCP-4043.name: The Printed Confession
SCP-4043.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4043 is located within a confessional booth in a rural church, deconsecrated and acquired by the Foundation under standard religious-property procurement following the closure of its parish in 2014. The booth remains in its original location; the church building is maintained in outward disrepair to discourage entry. Foundation ownership of the regional newspaper responsible for SCP-4043's associated effect is maintained through a holding company; the paper's obituary desk is staffed entirely by Foundation personnel under standard journalistic cover.

Testing of SCP-4043 is restricted to a controlled statement schedule; personnel delivering test statements select from a pre-approved list of minor, verifiably false admissions to avoid entering genuine compromising information into a public record. All print runs are reviewed prior to distribution; any unauthorized SCP-4043 output identified is redacted from copies before public sale using a secondary print pass, and the original unredacted run is retained in Site-19 archive.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4043 refers to an anomalous effect associated with a wooden confessional booth. Any spoken statement of personal wrongdoing made by an occupant of the booth's confessing side, regardless of the presence or absence of a listener on the opposite side, appears within 24 hours as a biographical detail within an obituary printed in that day's edition of the local newspaper, attributed to a deceased individual with no connection to the speaker. The obituary's subject is selected from among that day's actual deceased local residents; SCP-4043 has never generated an obituary for a fictitious or living person.

The inserted detail is reworded into the neutral, commemorative register typical of obituary composition and integrated seamlessly with the surrounding text, such that newspaper staff unfamiliar with SCP-4043 have historically approved the insertions without flagging them as inconsistent with information provided by the deceased's family. Family members contacted regarding inserted details have, in 31 of 33 documented cases, accepted the detail as accurate and previously unknown to them rather than disputing it, a response pattern not fully explained by ordinary grief bias according to Foundation psychological consult.

The effect does not function for statements made outside the booth, statements made by the booth's listening-side occupant, or statements not phrased as an admission of wrongdoing by the speaker.

INCIDENT LOG 4043-8: During an unauthorized visit by a descendant of the original parish (access breach detailed in Addendum 4043-1), the individual confessed, alone and unrecorded by staff, to an act of infidelity from approximately seven years prior. The following day's obituary for a 79-year-old deceased resident, unrelated to the speaker by any traceable connection, included the line: "He is remembered by his family as a man who never once, in fifty years of marriage, gave his wife cause to doubt him." The deceased's actual family did not request or approve this line and could not identify its source when asked; they nonetheless declined a correction, stating it was "a nice thing to have said about him."

SCP-4044.name: Fenn Point Light
SCP-4044.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The physical structure of SCP-4044 is maintained as a decommissioned lighthouse under Foundation ownership via a maritime heritage trust cover. The lamp mechanism was removed by the original coastal authority in 1974 prior to Foundation acquisition and is not to be reinstalled. The tower is fenced and marked as structurally unsound to discourage recreational visitors; the fencing has no measurable effect on the anomaly.

Foundation liaisons within regional coast guard and maritime traffic control monitor vessel radio logs and radar returns for reports of an active light at SCP-4044's charted position or bearing. Confirmed reports are followed up with a "decommissioned structure, disregard" advisory issued to the reporting vessel under standard coast guard procedure. Vessels that alter course based on the light and subsequently report running aground are to be met by Foundation-staffed rescue response disguised as coast guard personnel; salvage and any recovered debris are retained for Foundation analysis.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4044 refers to a light, consistent in color, rotation period, and flash pattern with the original lamp specification of a lighthouse decommissioned in 1974, that continues to be observed by mariners at the lighthouse's charted position and, in 60 of 214 documented reports, at bearings and distances that would place the light's apparent source several kilometres inland, underwater, or behind terrain that should obstruct line of sight from the reporting vessel's position.

No power source, bulb, or rotating mechanism capable of producing SCP-4044's effect has been present in the tower since the 1974 decommissioning; the lamp room has been sealed, empty, and confirmed dark by Foundation inspection on a monthly basis without exception. Photographic and video equipment aimed directly at the lamp room from land during a reported active period have recorded no light source; the effect appears only to be observable from a vessel at sea, or, in three documented cases, from aircraft.

Vessels that alter course toward or away from SCP-4044's apparent light, treating it as a hazard warning per standard interpretation of lighthouse signaling, have run aground on charted rocks in 9 cases and on rock formations not present in any chart, hydrographic survey, or subsequent inspection in 4 cases. In each of the latter 4 cases, no obstruction was found at the reported grounding coordinates during Foundation dive survey conducted within 72 hours.

INCIDENT LOG 4044-19: Fishing vessel Corinne B. altered course at 0240 in response to a reported light bearing 214 degrees from SCP-4044's charted position, consistent with the vessel's own location at the time being roughly 3 kilometres inland of the coastline — a position from which no line of sight to the tower should exist across intervening high ground. The vessel ran aground twenty minutes later on rock that a Foundation dive survey, conducted 6 hours after the incident, did not locate. Three crew were recovered; the fourth was not found and remains missing. Surviving crew report the light "got closer wrong," growing larger without the vessel appearing to approach it.

SCP-4045.name: The Answering Well
SCP-4045.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4045 is capped with a steel plate secured by a padlocked hasp, located at a fenced-off homestead site adjacent to a Foundation field research station. The plate has a single 15-centimetre access port fitted with a mechanical winch for lowering test objects; the port is otherwise sealed. No personnel are authorized to descend into SCP-4045 under any circumstance; this restriction has been in place since Incident 4045-2 and is not subject to research override.

Verbal testing of SCP-4045 is restricted to a standing list of pre-approved, semantically neutral phrases read from a script; open-ended speech, questions, or personal statements directed into the well are prohibited following Incident 4045-4. Audio recording equipment is mandatory for all sessions and must remain running for no less than ten minutes after the conclusion of any spoken test, regardless of apparent well activity.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4045 is a hand-dug well, 34 metres in measured depth, located on the site of a homestead abandoned in the 1930s. Any rope or cable lowered into SCP-4045 and retrieved is found, without exception, to have developed between one and four knots along its length that were not present when lowered, of a complexity increasing with the number of times that specific rope has been used in testing. Knot types have been catalogued by a Foundation maritime consultant as belonging to no single tradition, combining elements of nautical, mountaineering, and surgical knotcraft inconsistently.

A sound made at the well's mouth returns as an echo after a delay averaging 4.1 seconds; the well's measured depth would predict a physically possible echo delay of no more than 0.3 seconds. The returned sound is not consistently a repetition of the original: in 22 of 40 documented verbal tests, the echo has instead constituted a response to the content of the speech, in a voice matching neither the original speaker nor any previously recorded instance of SCP-4045's response, delivered in a tone Foundation psychological consult describes as "conversational rather than reflective."

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): Analysis of the 22 responsive echoes found that in 15 cases the response referenced information about the speaker not included in the spoken test phrase and not, per personnel interview, known to have been discussed near the well at any point — including, in one case, a researcher's mother's maiden name, and in another, the specific model of a car the speaker had sold nine years prior to their assignment to this site.|}}

INCIDENT LOG 4045-4: Researcher Halloran, during an authorized test using an approved neutral phrase, departed from the script to ask the well "who is down there," against standing procedure. The delayed echo, 4 seconds later, did not repeat the question. It answered, in a voice logged by the recording equipment as female, adult, unfamiliar to all present: a first name, stated once, calmly. The name was later confirmed by county records to match a homesteader's daughter reported missing from the property in 1936, never found. Researcher Halloran has since been reassigned away from SCP-4045 and the open-question restriction was implemented the same week.

SCP-4046.name: Sublevel B4
SCP-4046.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4046 is located within a six-level parking structure attached to a Foundation-owned office building operating under commercial lease cover. The structure's elevator and stairwell signage list levels B1 through B3 only. Access to SCP-4046 (level B4) is restricted by disabling its elevator call function through the control panel firmware; the stairwell door to B4 is secured with a keyed lock accessible only to Foundation logistics personnel with a documented operational need.

Vehicles assigned to SCP-4046 for authorized transport use must be logged out and in by dispatch, including odometer reading, fuel or charge level, and photographic documentation of tire tread and undercarriage, both before descent and after return. Civilian vehicles parked on levels B1 through B3 are not affected by SCP-4046 and require no special handling.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4046 refers to a fourth parking sublevel, accessible via elevator or stairwell, that does not appear in the structure's original architectural plans, building permit, or any subsequent renovation filing, and for which no additional excavation or construction has ever been recorded or budgeted. The level's physical appearance — support columns, parking stripe layout, lighting fixtures, and signage typeface — is visually consistent with levels B1 through B3, differing only in that it contains no visible exit ramp to street level and no connection to the structure's drainage or ventilation systems as documented in facility schematics.

Vehicles parked on SCP-4046 and later retrieved via elevator or stairwell consistently show an odometer increase inconsistent with the vehicle having remained parked, ranging from 40 to over 600 kilometres per use, despite drivers reporting no gap in memory between parking the vehicle and taking the elevator back to ground level. Recovered vehicles frequently show environmental residue — beach sand, pine needles, road salt, or standing rainwater in wheel wells — inconsistent with regional conditions at the time of use.

Drivers questioned about the discrepancy uniformly report the experience as unremarkable: they parked, they walked to the elevator, no time appeared to pass. Foundation logistics has since incorporated authorized SCP-4046 use into select transport operations requiring undocumented vehicle relocation, under Directorate approval.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We tried following a vehicle down the exit ramp instead of taking the elevator back up, on foot, to see where B4 actually goes if you don't take the shortcut. The ramp curves out of sight after about twenty metres same as any other level. Personnel who walked it report reaching a dead end wall, turning around, and finding the elevator lobby closer than it should have been by the distance they'd just walked. We stopped sending people down the ramp. — Logistics Coordinator Şule Ecevit

SCP-4047.name: The Early Bell
SCP-4047.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4047 is located within a storm drainage culvert running beneath an elementary school, accessed via a locked maintenance grate disguised as a standard utility access point. The grate is monitored by a remote audio pickup feeding continuously to Foundation monitoring staff posing as a school-district facilities contractor. No alteration to the culvert or the school's public address system is authorized; testing to date indicates the anomaly is not dependent on the specific hardware in use and would likely relocate to any replacement system.

All audio captured from SCP-4047 is logged with a timestamp and cross-referenced against the school's actual PA broadcast log by monitoring staff at the end of each school day. Any discrepancy between an SCP-4047 recording and its corresponding real broadcast, or any SCP-4047 recording with no corresponding real broadcast within 24 hours, is escalated to the assigned researcher immediately.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4047 refers to an acoustic anomaly by which the audio pickup at the described culvert location receives a recording of the school's public address announcements approximately 40 minutes, plus or minus 90 seconds, before the corresponding announcement is broadcast over the school's actual PA system. The pre-broadcast recording has matched the eventual real broadcast word-for-word, including ambient noise such as throat-clearing, paper handling, and background hallway sound, in 118 of 119 documented instances.

On three occasions, school staff, made aware informally of an impending announcement's content by Foundation-embedded personnel, attempted to alter the wording before broadcasting it. In each case, an unrelated interruption — a dropped microphone, a competing announcement from a different staff member unaware of the change, a brief PA outage — resulted in the original, SCP-4047-predicted wording being broadcast in full regardless of the intended change. Foundation intervention in this pattern has not been attempted beyond the three documented cases pending Ethics Committee guidance on causal-loop testing.

ADDENDUM 4047-1: The single non-matching instance (Recording 4047-77) captured an announcement calling for a student, name given in full, to report for early dismissal due to a family emergency. No corresponding broadcast occurred within the following 24 hours, or at any point since. School enrollment records, past and present, contain no student by the name given. Monitoring staff have not identified a source for the name and have been instructed not to pursue the discrepancy with school administration directly.

TEST LOG 4047-C: Recording captured at 1340: "...will be dismissed from Room 12 at 1425 due to the water main repair, please use the west exit only, I repeat, west exit only." Actual broadcast at 1421: identical wording, including a brief cough at the same point in the sentence, confirmed by waveform comparison to a 94% acoustic match, the remaining variance attributed to microphone placement rather than content difference.

SCP-4048.name: The Recurring Span
SCP-4048.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4048 is a two-lane highway bridge maintained under Foundation-influenced state transportation authority designation as "structurally deficient," a classification used to justify a permanent 15 km/h speed limit, a ban on crossing during fog or after sunset, and reduced traffic volume without public disclosure of the actual anomaly. Physical barriers preventing pedestrian crossing are maintained at both approaches. A Foundation-staffed maintenance checkpoint disguised as a toll authority office monitors all crossings via traffic camera around the clock.

Any vehicle that does not exit SCP-4048 within 4 minutes of entry, the maximum time consistent with the bridge's 340-metre physical length at the posted speed limit, triggers immediate closure of both approaches and dispatch of a recovery team. Recovery teams are instructed to approach on foot rather than by vehicle following Incident 4048-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4048 refers to an anomalous effect affecting a highway bridge, 340 metres in physical length, spanning a river gorge. A metal expansion joint at the bridge's structural midpoint, unremarkable in appearance and identical in construction to four other expansion joints along the span, causes any vehicle's odometer and trip computer to reset to zero upon crossing it, regardless of vehicle make, model, or odometer type (mechanical or digital).

In documented instances numbering 21 since Foundation monitoring began, a vehicle crossing SCP-4048 under conditions of fog, dusk, or dawn, with no other vehicle present on the span, has failed to complete the crossing within the expected time. In each such instance, the vehicle was later located stationary on the bridge, engine idling or vehicle powered off, at a position consistent with the bridge's actual midpoint, with an odometer reading increased by an amount ranging from 340 to over 4,800 kilometres since the point of reset — distance the vehicle could not have physically travelled within the elapsed exterior time, which in all 21 cases was under six minutes.

Drivers recovered from affected vehicles are, in 17 of 21 cases, found asleep or in a state resembling sleep, and report on waking no memory of the crossing beyond the moment of passing the midpoint joint. In the remaining 4 cases, the vehicle was found with no occupant; none of the four missing drivers has been located.

{{4|ADDENDUM (Level 4): The vehicle involved in Incident 4048-2, recovered with an odometer increase of 4,830 kilometres, contained a handwritten note on the passenger seat in the driver's own confirmed handwriting, undated, reading: "still going, tell them I kept to the speed limit the whole way, tell them I didn't try to turn around." The driver, recovered from the vehicle unconscious but alive, has no memory of writing it and does not recognize the handwriting as under duress or altered from her known baseline samples.|}}
