INTERVIEW EXCERPT — Driver recovered in Incident 4048-2, three days post-recovery: "I remember the fog getting thick right after the middle of the bridge, thicker than fog gets, like driving into a wall painted to look like more road. I kept my speed. I remember thinking if I sped up or slowed down something would notice. I don't remember writing anything. I don't remember six minutes, I remember what felt like all night, driving carefully, being good, being careful, and then the flashlight in the window."

SCP-4049.name: The Tideline Guest
SCP-4049.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Coastal segment [REDACTED], locally known as Uzunkum Point, is designated Observation Post 77-A and maintained as a restricted fishing exclusion zone under standard maritime cover (naval unexploded ordnance survey). Two remote cameras and one tide gauge log the site continuously. Personnel are not required to be on-site outside the annual observation window described below; maintenance visits outside the window are scheduled monthly to avoid overlap with the tide cycle.
Village civilian population within 4 km (currently 61 households) has been administered standing cover briefing and is monitored via a Foundation-run guesthouse posing as a bed-and-breakfast, which employs one embedded field agent.
Should a footprint trail matching the pattern on file be discovered outside the expected window, Site Director approval is required before any casting or excavation is performed on it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4049 denotes a recurring event at Observation Post 77-A occurring on the first low tide after the autumnal equinox, regional time. Between the hour the tide begins to recede and the hour it turns again, a single trail of bare footprints forms across roughly 40 metres of exposed sand between the waterline and a fixed dune at grid reference [REDACTED], and a matching trail forms returning to the water.
No camera footage, from any angle or frame rate tested, has recorded the trail's formation. Footage before and after the event is continuous and timestamped correctly; the file size of the intervening segment is consistent with its recorded duration. The footprints are simply present in the later frame.
The prints are adult-sized (approx. EU 43), consistent year to year in stride length, weight distribution, and a shallow drag mark on the left heel print consistent with an old injury or malformation. Foundation podiatric consultants have confirmed the same gait abnormality across 34 years of casts on file.
The pattern has repeated in all thirty-four observation windows on record since 1991; no year has passed without the event occurring. No individual has been observed making the trail, arriving, or departing by any other route, in 34 years of continuous surveillance.

ADDENDUM 4049-1:
The guesthouse at Uzunkum Point maintains a paper guest register predating Foundation involvement in the area, itself predating any living resident's memory of the building's construction. One entry appears in the register every year, dated to the observation night, under the name "Traveler." No payment is recorded. No room is recorded as occupied.
Handwriting analysis of the 1962 through 2025 entries returned a single confident conclusion: they were made by the same hand. Records predating 1962 were lost to a fire that struck the village in 1961; whether the register itself predates that date has not been determined.
No resident of Uzunkum Point has ever reported seeing anyone write in the register.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
We tried, in 1994, moving the register to a locked cabinet in the agent's room for the observation night. The entry was made anyway, the page left open as though the cabinet had never been shut. We do not know how, and the current guidance is not to try again.
— Dr. Costa, Maritime Anomalies Unit

SCP-4050.name: The Long Mile
SCP-4050.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The affected segment of Provincial Route 118, kilometre markers 212 to 213.2, is monitored by a permanent Foundation checkpoint disguised as a road maintenance depot. All civilian traffic is filtered onto a parallel detour between 22:00 and 05:00 using standard "resurfacing works" signage. Perimeter sensors at both checkpoints log external elapsed time to a tenth of a second and transmit this data to Site-23 monthly.
A single Foundation vehicle, occupied by no fewer than two personnel, is authorised to traverse the segment during monitoring windows to bait recurrence. Any civilian vehicle found to have entered the segment unescorted is to be intercepted at the far checkpoint regardless of elapsed time and its occupants debriefed under standard amnestic protocol if an event is confirmed.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4050 is a recurring event affecting the 1.2 km stretch of Route 118 described above. It occurs at irregular intervals, averaging once per eight months, always to a vehicle travelling the segment alone at night with no other vehicle visible ahead or behind.
During an event, the vehicle's occupant(s) experience continuous, uninterrupted driving of the same visible stretch of road for a subjective duration ranging from several hours to, in one case, nine days. Externally, elapsed time at both checkpoints has, in forty-two documented events to date, never exceeded 48 seconds.
Odometers consistently register mileage consistent with the subjective duration of the drive, not the 1.2 km of physical roadway. Subject 4050-3 (civilian, name on file) exited the segment with an odometer reading 30,415 km higher than at entry, a fuel tank that had been full at entry and was empty at exit, and a subjective account of nine weeks of driving that she declined, after initial debriefing, to discuss further.
Fuel consumption during events is consistent with the odometer reading, not the elapsed external time. The Foundation has not identified a source for the consumed fuel; tank capacity at all points during monitored events, measured by an installed sensor rather than the vehicle's own gauge, does not explain the discrepancy. No comparable discrepancy has ever been logged on the Foundation's own bait vehicle; the effect has to date only been confirmed on civilian vehicles.

INCIDENT LOG 4050-7:
Bait vehicle entered segment 03:41. Radio contact maintained on open channel. At 03:41:09, radio operator reported the bait vehicle's cabin audio changed character — background road noise consistent with several additional hours of driving, faint conversation between the two occupants discussing a rest stop neither checkpoint has record of. External clock at rear checkpoint: 03:41:51. Vehicle exited at 03:41:53. Total external elapsed time: 12 seconds. Occupants' accounts, taken separately, matched to within four minutes across a reported 6 hour 40 minute drive. Neither could explain the rest stop, and the vehicle's own odometer showed no increase.
— Agent Doyle, filing officer

SCP-4051.name: The Truthful Storm
SCP-4051.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Because SCP-4051 manifests as ordinary-appearing thunderstorm cells with no detectable signature prior to a strike, containment is limited to identification after the fact and prevention of pattern disclosure. The Foundation maintains a standing arrangement with fourteen national meteorological services to reclassify SCP-4051-associated strike reports (fatal lightning strikes on cloudless or near-cloudless days, or strikes with no matching cell on radar) as instrument error.
A statistical model (4051-MDL, maintained by Site-23 Probability Division) flags population clusters at elevated risk based on aggregate indicators; results are not actionable against individuals and are used only to position rapid-response medical teams.
Personnel with confirmed exposure to SCP-4051-pattern strikes as bystanders are not to be informed that the strike selected its target. The fourteen-nation arrangement is renewed annually and has, to date, required no explanation beyond routine instrument-calibration language.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4051 is a global, ongoing meteorological event first identified through statistical anomaly rather than direct observation: fatal lightning strikes occur at a rate approximately 1.6 times the expected baseline under clear or near-clear sky conditions, and radar data for a strike's associated storm cell frequently does not exist, or exists for a cell too small and short-lived to explain the discharge recorded.
Retrospective investigation of 340 confirmed SCP-4051 fatalities found that in 337 cases, the deceased had, within the preceding 72 hours, made a statement later independently verified as a deliberate and consequential falsehood: false testimony, a denied affair, a forged signature, a lie that caused a third party measurable harm.
SCP-4051 does not appear to weight strikes by the scale of the falsehood. Incident 4051-088 recorded the deaths of a subject under investigation for a securities fraud exceeding $40,000,000 and, in the same strike, on the same golf course, a caddie whose only relevant statement on record was to a marshal, denying he had moved a ball lying against a tree root. Both were struck within the same second. Weather records for the strike show clear skies over both men and no meteorological formation capable of producing a storm cell anywhere in the area within the preceding half hour.
The mechanism by which SCP-4051 identifies a qualifying falsehood, verifies it independently of any human investigation, and selects a discharge target from among any bystanders present, remains unknown. No case of a false statement later found to be true resulting in a strike has been recorded. The 1.6-times baseline elevation has held consistent across every continent where clear-sky fatal strikes have been logged, with no region showing significant deviation from the global average.

ADDENDUM 4051-2: Site-23 has not pursued research into whether Foundation classification documents that misstate an anomaly's properties — a known and tolerated practice — fall under SCP-4051's qualifying criteria. A request for such research was declined by the Site Director without a stated reason on file.

SCP-4052.name: The Miscounted Stairwell
SCP-4052.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Foundation holds ownership of the parking structure at [REDACTED] through the shell company Meridian Holdings. Stairwell B is fitted with permanent laser rangefinding equipment logging its physical dimensions every ninety seconds; to date every reading has confirmed four sub-levels and no more. Model 4052-1 (Addendum below) automatically flags any 5% deviation from baseline occurrence rate to the Site Director.
Personnel required to enter Stairwell B for maintenance or monitoring purposes must use the buddy protocol: two personnel, both counting landings audibly, cross-checking aloud at each one. Any discrepancy between the two counts requires immediate exit by the nearest available route, which may not be the route of entry.
Civilian access to the structure remains open under standard cover (public parking) to preserve the event's baseline occurrence rate, on which the statistical model in Addendum 4052-1 depends.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4052 denotes an intermittent discrepancy in Stairwell B of the structure above, which physically contains four sub-levels (B1 through B4) connected by a single continuous stairwell. On an estimated 1 in 6,000 individual descents, a person counting landings, whether aloud, silently, or by unconscious habit, counts five before reaching what they identify as the bottom. On an estimated 1 in 6,000 ascents, a person counts three.
The discrepancy does not correspond to any additional physical landing detected by fixed rangefinding equipment, handheld measurement, or photographic survey conducted during an active discrepancy. Comparison of the stairwell against its original architectural plans, construction permits, and the independent measurements of three separate engineering firms, undertaken while investigating the discrepancy's cause, produced the same result in all four cases: four landings.
Subjects who miscount on only one leg of a transit, either descending or ascending but not both, experience no further effect and typically do not notice the discrepancy unless asked to recount afterward.
Subjects who miscount on both legs of a single continuous transit have, in nine of ten documented cases, subsequently gone unaccounted for within the structure. In the remaining case, the subject was recovered on the B3 landing three days later, from a point neither the structure's cameras nor his own account could place him at before then.

INCIDENT LOG 4052-B: Security Officer Halloran entered Stairwell B for a scheduled 02:00 patrol, counting aloud per protocol, his partner counting from the landing above by intercom. Halloran's descent count reached five at what his partner's rangefinder confirmed was B4. Halloran reported the discrepancy and was instructed to exit immediately via the ground-floor door, eight metres away.
He began ascending instead. His partner's count, taken from his open radio channel, reached three before the transmission narrowed to a single channel of footsteps on concrete, evenly paced, continuing for roughly ninety seconds past the point his partner's own count reached the confirmed top of the stairwell. The footsteps did not slow before the channel went to static.
The structure was searched floor by floor, ground to B4, immediately afterward. No additional space was located. No trace of Officer Halloran has been recovered. His file, per protocol, will remain open for ten years before closure.

SCP-4053.name: The Extra Setting
SCP-4053.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The village of [REDACTED], population 214, is maintained under a standing Foundation cover arrangement (agricultural cooperative advisory presence, two embedded personnel) rather than relocation, per the Site Director's finding that removing the population would not halt SCP-4053 and would forfeit continuity of observation built over three generations.
Households are not required to participate in SCP-4053 but are, per longstanding local custom the Foundation has elected not to interfere with, universally observed to do so without prompting.
Any household reporting a change in the identity of the event's beneficiary (see Description) is to be interviewed within 48 hours. The village's medical records are reviewed annually through the regional health post as part of the cover arrangement, and any discrepancy is reported to the central office.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4053 is a recurring atmospheric and behavioural event affecting the village of [REDACTED] on the night of the first hard frost of the year, a date that varies annually and is not announced in advance by any recorded means, yet is anticipated correctly by the village without exception.
On the affected night, a dense ground fog, contained within the village boundary and not extending into surrounding farmland, persists from dusk until approximately 03:00. Meteorological review has found no correlation between the fog's onset and any measurable atmospheric variable; the fog itself does not register on regional radar. Fog density, measured repeatedly with standard visibility instruments, reaches the same values and the same measurable density curve per metre every year.
Independently and without coordination confirmed by interview, all 214 households prepare one additional place setting at the evening meal, for a guest none of them can name, describe, or recall inviting.
The place setting is cleared, unused, the following morning. In 31 years of Foundation observation, no household has reported the setting being used, disturbed, or its food consumed.
Interviews conducted in the days following the event consistently produce the same account: the household "felt it would be right" to set the extra place, and could not, under further questioning, say why, though none regarded the question as strange until it was asked.

ADDENDUM 4053-1: In 2009, a household newly relocated to the village from outside the region, with no prior exposure to local custom, was found on the morning after SCP-4053 to have set an extra place identical in all particulars to its neighbours'. The household had not been informed of the custom by any neighbour, per interviews of all adjacent households, conducted separately, which agree on this point. The village's weekly market days, the only plausible venue through which the household could have learned the custom informally, were separately investigated; no vendor or neighbour recalled any conversation on the subject.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
I asked the eldest resident, matriarch of the Vasilenko household, who she believed the setting was for. She said what her mother said, and her mother's mother: that it was for whoever did not come home that year. When I asked whether anyone from the village had failed to come home that year, she said no, not that year, and did not elaborate further, and did not look as though she expected to be asked again.
— Dr. Farrow, Anomalous Locations Division

SCP-4054.name: The Unanimous Toss
SCP-4054.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4054 zones are identified retroactively through statistical monitoring of regional gaming and lottery outcome data (4054-MDL, Site-23 Probability Division) and are contained by localized evacuation under public health cover once a zone's radius is confirmed to exceed 500 metres. The current largest contained zone measured 2.1 kilometres (Incident 4054-14, see below) and remained under standing exclusion for the duration of the event.
Coin flips, die rolls, card draws, and other binary or discrete random processes are not to be conducted for containment testing purposes inside an active zone by personnel who have not first completed a minimum 96-hour rest rotation; sustained exposure to an active zone beyond this window has produced disorientation escalating to unresponsiveness in test subjects (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4054 is a recurring event in which all binary or low-cardinality random processes occurring within a bounded, roughly circular zone resolve identically for the duration of the event. Coins land on the same face; dice, where multiple are rolled together, show the same number; simultaneous card draws from separate, unconnected decks return matching cards. Processes with more than approximately twenty possible outcomes are not measurably affected.
Zone onset is not preceded by any detected environmental change. Zone boundaries are sharp rather than gradient: a coin flipped one metre outside a mapped boundary behaves normally; one flipped a metre inside resolves identically to every other flip in the zone.
Duration of individual events ranges from under a minute to, in Incident 4054-14, sixteen days. Zone radius has been observed to increase over the duration of a single sustained event, though never to decrease before the event's end, at which point the zone ceases to exist entirely rather than shrinking.
No case of SCP-4054 activity has been linked to any single triggering individual or object; simultaneous onset has been recorded at sites with no personnel or object overlap.

INCIDENT LOG 4054-14: Zone detected via lottery-anomaly flagging, [REDACTED] Province, initial radius 40 metres. Foundation response team established a perimeter at 41 metres; radius 180 metres, day 2. Radius 900 metres, day 6. Radius 2.1 kilometres, day 11, at which point 340 civilians within the zone were evacuated under flood-warning cover; all coin- and die-based testing conducted by the response team inside the zone during this period returned unanimous results regardless of device, material, or operator. The zone ceased at 2.1 kilometres, day 16, 04:12, with no gradual reduction; testing at 04:13 returned normal distributions across every instrument still in place.
No correlation has been found between the sixteen-day duration of Incident 4054-14 and any regional or personnel variable investigated to date.

ADDENDUM 4054-2: Agent Moreau, held inside the Incident 4054-14 zone for 112 continuous hours by a communications failure rather than by design, was recovered unresponsive but physically uninjured. On recovery he was administered the standard coin-flip cognitive assessment used Foundation-wide; he called the outcome correctly nineteen consecutive times before the assessment was halted. He has since been reassigned to administrative duties at his own request and declines to discuss the incident.

SCP-4055.name: The Skywritten Flock
SCP-4055.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4055 is contained through control of publicly available migratory tracking data for the [REDACTED] Wetlands Nature Reserve, which the Foundation influences via an embedded ornithologist (currently Dr. Okafor) with authority to reroute publication of tracking-collar telemetry. No independent civilian ground-based observation of the reserve during the observation window described below has been permitted since 1988, maintained under cover of seasonal reserve closure for "conservation sensitivity."
Aerial photography of the annual formation is to be taken by Foundation personnel only, archived, and not published in any form, complete or partial. Civilian airspace over the reserve is closed to traffic for the duration of the observation window, presented publicly as a standard bird-migration safety measure.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4055 is a recurring event in which a flock of migratory [REDACTED] geese, numbering consistently between 900 and 1,100 individuals, deviates from its otherwise unremarkable migratory route on one night annually, generally within a week of the winter solstice, to fly in a sustained formation over the reserve's central wetland for a period of eighteen to forty minutes.
The formation, visible only from directly overhead and only for the duration of the flight, resolves into a legible character or short sequence of characters when photographed from above. The script matches no currently catalogued human writing system with full confidence, though Foundation linguists have achieved partial, contested matches to several historical scripts no longer in active use. Flight speed and altitude distribution during formation are consistent with the species' known physiological limits; only the route flown, not the manner of flight, is anomalous.
The formation is not constant year to year. A photographic archive extending to 1954, reconstructed from period aerial survey material acquired after Foundation identification of the site in 1987, shows a different formation each year, none repeated.
Foundation ornithological consultants confirm the flock's migratory behaviour is otherwise entirely unremarkable for the species outside the annual event, and the flock has been the subject of standard ecological study without incident.

ADDENDUM 4055-1: In 2019, Foundation linguists cross-referencing the 1954-2019 archive determined that, read in sequence, the annual formations form a continuous, grammatically coherent text in an unidentified language, missing no entries, with each year's formation constituting a discrete clause. The text has not been translated. It has not, to date, repeated a symbol, has not reached anything analysts are willing to describe as a stopping point, and no formation before 1954 has been located to determine where the text begins. Since the 2019 analysis, each new formation has been logged as a discrete clause appended to the previous one, and the text's total length continues to grow year over year.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: Dr. Okafor requests it be noted for the file that geese do not require thirty-four years to learn a shared behaviour, let alone continue one across generations with full mortality turnover well inside that span. No further comment has been logged.

SCP-4056.name: The Extra Monitor
SCP-4056.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Confirmed SCP-4056 sites (currently four hospitals, see Addendum 4056-3 for list) are staffed on the overnight shift by no fewer than two Foundation-embedded medical personnel, tasked with immediate reset of cardiac and vital-sign monitors following an event and interview of on-duty civilian nursing staff before the shift change allows memory drift.
Hospital administration at confirmed sites operates under a standard partial-disclosure agreement (Class B) attributing the phenomenon to "a known electrical interference pattern in the monitoring network," which is false but has proven sufficient to maintain civilian staff compliance with reset procedures. Three of the four sites were brought to Foundation attention independently, in different years, before any pattern connecting them was recognised.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4056 is a recurring event, currently observed only at four hospital sites with no identified common architectural, electrical, or historical feature, in which all patient cardiac monitors on a ward display a flatline reading simultaneously for a duration of between four and twelve seconds, beginning consistently between 02:50 and 03:10 local time, though not on every night. No patient's actual cardiac rhythm changes during the event; the discrepancy exists only on the monitor display and in the logged data, which records the flatline as though genuinely measured.
Following each event, a count of active monitor displays showing the flatline reading has, in 203 of 211 documented events, exceeded the count of monitors physically installed and operational on the ward by exactly one.
The additional reading cannot be attributed to a monitor from an adjacent ward, a decommissioned unit left connected, or any device identified through electrical tracing. Foundation engineers have, on six occasions, physically accounted for every monitor on a ward immediately before an event and confirmed the discrepancy still occurred. The four affected hospitals share no common equipment supplier, manufacturing batch, or maintenance contractor.
No patient or staff member has reported seeing an unaccounted monitor, bed, or patient during or after an event.

INCIDENT LOG 4056-C, [REDACTED] General Hospital: Ward 4, 14 beds, all 14 monitors confirmed operational and accounted for at 02:00 by a Foundation engineer prior to shift. At 02:57, all 14 displayed flatline for nine seconds, alongside a fifteenth reading logged by the central nursing station server under bed designation "15," a bed that does not exist on the ward's floor plan and has never existed in the hospital's architectural records.
Server logs for bed "15" show a full vital-sign history for the nine-second window, not merely a flatline: a heart rate declining from 61 to 0 over the recorded period, consistent with an actual death rather than a sensor artifact.
No further reading has been logged under bed designation "15" in the 340 events recorded at this site since.

SCP-4057.name: The Quiet Minute
SCP-4057.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4057 events cannot be predicted or prevented. Contained municipalities (currently three; see Site-23 registry 4057-REG) are monitored via civic infrastructure (traffic cameras, utility metering) repurposed for early detection; a site is placed under quiet lockdown cover (announced as a civil-defense drill) for 24 hours following any detected event, allowing Foundation interview teams to move through the population before the shared false memory (see Description) stabilises into local record.
Under no circumstances is a contained population to be informed that an event has occurred; disclosure has, in one documented case (Incident 4057-3), measurably lengthened the following event's duration. Traffic camera and security footage retained through the gap does not show residents standing motionless; it shows them absent from frame entirely for the duration of the event, with the same gap present in the recorded image as in the residents' own memory.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4057 is a recurring event affecting an entire municipality (populations observed range from 1,900 to 26,000) in which all residents present within municipal boundaries cease active behaviour simultaneously — mid-sentence, mid-stride, mid-task — for a duration ranging from four to ninety seconds, resuming afterward with no awareness that a gap has occurred.
Following an event, all affected residents share, with near-total consistency across separately conducted interviews, a single false memory of an ordinary event that did not occur during the gap: a delivery that was not made, a phone call that was not received, a dog that did not bark. The false memory is specific, low-stakes, and mundane, and differs from event to event, but is uniform across the entire population for any single event.
No resident has been observed to resist or question the false memory unprompted. Residents shown contradicting physical evidence (an undelivered package still in its warehouse, a phone log with no matching call) revise their account within minutes, without apparent distress, and without abandoning confidence in the underlying memory's general shape.
Municipality selection shows no correlation with population size, geography, or Foundation presence. Two of the three currently contained sites were identified only after a second event; the object responsible, if any, for a population's exposure risk has not been identified, and SCP-4057 remains classified as an event rather than tied to any located source. No injury, disappearance, or physical harm has ever been documented as resulting from an event itself.

INCIDENT LOG 4057-3: The contained population of [REDACTED] (pop. 8,400) was informed, under a field authorisation since revoked, that an event had occurred, in an attempt to test whether disclosure would prevent memory stabilisation. The false memory (a power flicker that did not happen) stabilised regardless, reaching full consistency across 340 sampled residents within six hours rather than the typical twenty-four. A second event, unprecedented for this site, occurred nine days later, lasting eighty-one seconds against a site average of twenty-two. The disclosure protocol has not been repeated.

SCP-4058.name: The Frost Obituary
SCP-4058.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The building at [REDACTED] (a disused rail signal box, current legal owner a Foundation shell trust) housing the affected window is maintained in structural stasis and monitored by a single fixed camera. The window itself is not to be removed, cleaned, or replaced; three prior replacement panes installed between 1976 and 1981, following breakage, each independently began producing SCP-4058 patterns within one frost season of installation, indicating the anomaly is sited to the location rather than the glass. The surrounding property is fenced and posted with standard "structural hazard" signage to discourage civilian visitors.
Any pattern formed on the window is to be photographed, dated, and the photograph sealed for a minimum of ninety days before analysis, per Protocol 4058-DELAY (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4058 refers to recurring frost patterns which form on the interior face of a single window pane at the location above, on the first sufficiently cold night of each winter and irregularly thereafter, averaging six occurrences per season. Unlike ordinary frost formation, SCP-4058 patterns are representational: each depicts, in a recognisable if simplified linear style, a specific scene involving a specific identifiable person, rendered with enough particular detail (clothing, setting, an object present) to allow positive identification after the fact. None of the patterns on file depict the moment of death itself; each shows only the minute immediately preceding it.
In thirty-one of thirty-four patterns cross-referenced against subsequent records, the depicted person died, by accident, within four to ninety days of the pattern's formation, in a manner and setting consistent with the depiction. The remaining three patterns have not been matched to any death on record and remain open.
The mechanism connecting the window to its subjects, who have no identified connection to the location, to each other, or to the building's history, has not been determined. Subjects have included residents of at least six countries, with no shared travel history, social connection, or Foundation exposure identified.
The Foundation does not intervene to prevent depicted deaths. Analysis under Protocol 4058-DELAY has confirmed, in the seven cases where intervention was attempted prior to the protocol's adoption, that the depicted death occurred regardless, by a different but comparably fatal mechanism, within the same window.

ADDENDUM 4058-1: Protocol 4058-DELAY was adopted in 1989 following Incident 4058-2, in which early identification of a depicted subject (a delivery driver in a city with no prior connection to the site) and a subsequent, well-resourced Foundation effort to keep him off the road for the ninety-day window resulted in his fatal fall from the stairs of his own apartment on day 91, one day after monitoring was stood down. The pattern that had depicted him showed, on later re-examination of the sealed photograph, a stairwell railing consistent in an architectural detail with his apartment building, a detail analysts had not identified before the intervention. The subject's own family, interviewed afterward under standard cover, described the railing as original to the building and unchanged in thirty years.

SCP-4059.name: The Borrowed Hour
SCP-4059.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4059 cannot be prevented or localized in advance; onset location is not predictable using any model developed to date (see Addendum 4059-2 for four discontinued approaches). Detection relies on a global network of 1,400 Foundation-monitored high-precision clocks (4059-NET) cross-checked against international atomic time; a discrepancy of exactly one hour, appearing and resolving within a bounded region typically under 20 kilometres across, is treated as an active event.
Personnel dispatched to a detected event are authorised to document but not to remove, retain, or interact physically with any object or structure encountered under Description, paragraph 2, without Site Director approval, regardless of apparent origin or ownership.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4059 is a recurring global event in which a bounded region experiences an additional, genuine hour not accounted for by standard timekeeping, occurring on average once per nine to fourteen years with no confirmed periodicity. Clocks and biological processes within the affected region run normally during the extra hour; outside the boundary, time passes normally and without interruption, such that the region's return to synchrony with the rest of the world requires no correction, as though the hour had always been there and merely gone unspent until claimed.
During the extra hour, structures, objects, and in six documented cases, individuals, that had been destroyed, demolished, or deceased prior to the event are physically and, where applicable, biologically present within the affected region, behaving consistently with a point in time prior to their destruction or death, generally unaware that anything is unusual.
At the hour's end, the region reverts without transition to its expected present-day state. Reappeared structures and objects are not retained; reappeared individuals do not return with the region's population. In four of six documented cases involving individuals, a single object the individual was in contact with during the hour was found, after the event, to have been retained in the present-day region, materially aged as though it had continued to exist the whole time.

INCIDENT LOG 4059-E: Event detected [REDACTED]; the Site-23 clock network flagged a bounded discrepancy of exactly one hour, radius approximately 800 metres, centred on the former site of a residential block demolished nineteen years prior following a structural fire. A response team arrived 34 minutes into the event and documented the block standing, occupied, undamaged, residents engaged in ordinary evening activity, none reporting awareness of the fire, the demolition, or the nineteen intervening years.
At the hour's end, the block reverted to the vacant lot presently occupying the site. A single item, a child's shoe, was recovered from the lot's perimeter fencing the following morning, matching a shoe visible in Foundation photographs taken during the event, aged consistently with nineteen years of weathering rather than one hour.
No occupant of the block has been identified in any present-day population record.

SCP-4060.name: The Counting Problem
SCP-4060.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4060 cannot be contained through conventional means; the Foundation's role is limited to advisory influence over the methodology and frequency of large-scale simultaneous population enumeration efforts (national censuses, mass surveys, synchronised biometric registration programmes) through embedded personnel in national statistical agencies across nine countries, aimed at reducing simultaneity and total enumerated population per event rather than preventing enumeration outright, which has been assessed as neither feasible nor advisable given the unknown consequences of an indefinitely deferred national census.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4060 is a recurring, global-scale event correlated with, and to date occurring without exception within 72 hours of, any population enumeration effort attempting to simultaneously and individually count more than approximately ten million people within a bounded administrative territory. Following such an effort, a number of brief, localized anomalous incidents occur across the counted territory, clustered in time, each individually unremarkable and classifiable under existing categories (minor probability anomalies, small temporal discrepancies, isolated cognitohazard exposures of limited scope), but collectively exceeding, for the 72-hour window, the territory's entire annual baseline rate of such incidents by a factor between six and forty.
The number of incidents in a given SCP-4060 cluster has, in every case where final enumeration figures and incident counts were both available, differed from the census's own official final population count by a consistent, small margin: the incident count exceeds the census count by between one and four.
No incident within a cluster has been traced to the enumeration process itself, to any specific counted individual, or to any object or location associated with data collection or storage. The Foundation's working hypothesis, unconfirmed, is that the act of arriving at a final, official, simultaneous count of a population produces a residual quantity — persons, positions, or events — that the count did not and structurally could not include, and which manifests rather than remaining absent.

INCIDENT LOG 4060-NAT: Following the finalisation of a national census (population returned: 41,204,853), nineteen independent anomalous incidents were recorded across the counted territory within 68 hours, including seven probability clusters consistent with SCP-4054 signatures [cross-reference] at sites with no prior SCP-4054 history, four short-duration temporal discrepancies under one minute, and eight cognitohazard exposures of a type previously unrecorded in the territory. Incident count: nineteen. Amount by which the census count was exceeded: [DATA WITHHELD PENDING REVIEW]. Site-23 Probability Division has requested but not received authorisation to publish the exact margin outside senior staff.

ADDENDUM 4060-1: No enumeration effort below the ten-million threshold has produced a confirmed SCP-4060 cluster. The Foundation does not conduct its own internal personnel counts — including of Foundation-wide staffing, D-class population, or contained-anomaly totals — above this threshold using simultaneous methodology, and has not done so since 1974.

SCP-4061.name: The Brigade That Dreams the Fire
SCP-4061.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All nineteen active and reserve
members of the volunteer fire department serving the township
designated Rural Asset 4061 are to remain in their current
positions of employment and residence under passive Foundation
monitoring. No member is to be reassigned, retired, or relocated
without Site Director approval; three historical attempts to
disband or relocate the brigade were each followed by a structure
fire within 30 km of the intended relocation site inside 72
hours. A cover identity (Rural Volunteer Fire Auxiliary Program)
sustains Foundation funding for equipment and training under the
pretense of a state grant. Each member's sleep is logged via a
wearable actigraph; any member reporting the recurring dream
described below is to notify the on-call brigade captain
immediately, regardless of hour. A Foundation liaison embedded as
a probationary firefighter (currently Firefighter D. Marsh)
confirms dispatch accuracy and reports discrepancies to Site-31.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4061 denotes a recurring dream shared collectively by members
of a volunteer fire brigade serving a township of approximately
900 residents. On nights preceding a structure fire within the
township's jurisdiction, between one and all nineteen members
report an identical dream: a single-story house, address unknown,
in which one specific and consistent object is burning. As of
this filing, the object is a kitchen table. Members who have
never met before joining the brigade report the dream in
identical language on the same night.

The dream has never been wrong about a fire occurring. It has, to
date, been wrong twice about the object: once reporting a burning
table when the eventual fire was confined to a stove, and once
reporting a table for a house that had already been demolished
and contained no furniture at all. The brigade has never dreamed
of a fire that killed a resident. Township records show no fire
fatality in sixty-one years, a rate outside three standard
deviations of comparable townships. No member has volunteered an
explanation for the table. Several, asked directly, describe it
as simply what is burning, in the tone of a fact rather than an
image.

ADDENDUM 4061-1 — INTERVIEW EXCERPT:
The following exchange occurred during a routine debrief with
Firefighter T. Colby, thirty-four years of service, two hours
after a dream-predicted fire at which no table was present.

Interviewer: The dream said a table again.
Colby: It's always a table.
Interviewer: There wasn't one tonight.
Colby: There will be. Give it time.
Interviewer: The house is condemned. It's scheduled for
demolition next month.
Colby: Then I expect we'll be back next month.
Interviewer: You understand that's an unusual thing to be sure
of.
Colby: I've been dreaming another man's kitchen for six years. I
stopped being sure of things a while back. I just go where it's
burning.

Firefighter Colby has since declined two follow-up interviews,
citing department policy against discussing the table with
non-members. The policy does not appear in any document the
Foundation liaison has been permitted to read.

SCP-4062.name: The Helpline Voice
SCP-4062.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Foundation maintains covert majority ownership of Meridian
Home Services, a residential appliance warranty and support
company, through a shell holding firm. All 34 employees of the
Ankeny call center location are to remain employed at their
current positions; termination or voluntary resignation is
discouraged through standard HR retention incentives, not
coercion. Employees who reach Terminal Register (see Description)
are to be reassigned to a fabricated "occupational voice disorder
clinic" on the same property, continuing to work assigned phone
queues, which is the only intervention found to prevent acute
nonverbal regression. Call center revenue is partially diverted
to Foundation acquisition accounts. Cumulative logged call hours
per employee are tracked automatically; HR is instructed to flag
any employee approaching 4,000 hours for quarterly monitoring.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4062 is a gradual vocal convergence observed in employees of
the Meridian Home Services call center after a cumulative average
of 4,200 hours spent answering customer support calls. An
affected employee's own speaking voice slowly shifts toward a
single, consistent adult voice not attributable to any specific
customer, colleague, or media source, regardless of the
employee's native language, sex, or age. Family members
consistently describe the change as the employee "answering the
phone like a stranger," including at home, on personal calls, and
in ordinary conversation.

Of 34 current employees, six have reached full convergence,
termed Terminal Register internally. At this stage the employee
continues to produce speech physically but can no longer generate
spontaneous sentences outside phrases functionally
indistinguishable from call center scripting, delivered entirely
in the composite voice. Written communication, comprehension, and
nonverbal expression remain unaffected. Separating a Terminal
Register employee from telephone work produced acute nonverbal
distress in all six cases within 48 hours, resolving only once
phone work resumed.

No customer recording matches the composite voice above a
coincidental similarity threshold across a sample of four million
logged calls. The composite instead correlates at 97% with the
averaged waveform of every hold-music announcement broadcast by
the company since 1988, a period predating the birth of three of
the six Terminal Register employees.

ADDENDUM 4062-1 — INTERVIEW EXCERPT:
Interview conducted with Terminal Register employee C.R.,
employed nine years, following a scheduled monitoring session.
Responses are transcribed verbatim; the interviewing researcher's
unscripted emotional state at time of interview is noted in
brackets.

Researcher: Can you tell me your name? [researcher had just
received news of a family member's hospitalization prior to
session, unrelated to subject, not disclosed to subject]
C.R.: I understand this is a difficult time for you. Let's see
what we can do together.
Researcher: That isn't an answer to my question.
C.R.: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Is there anything else I
can help you with today?

No further responses were obtained. The session was terminated at
the researcher's request. C.R.'s personnel file lists no
mechanism by which the subject could have been aware of the
researcher's personal circumstances.

SCP-4063.name: The Mending Circle
SCP-4063.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The eight members of SCP-4063 are to be left in their ordinary
weekly meeting pattern at the [REDACTED] Senior Center, Tuesdays,
undisturbed and unaware of Foundation interest. A Foundation
asset (currently posing as a center volunteer) collects completed
garments monthly under the pretense of a charity donation drive
and delivers them to Site-31 for storage. Garments are to be kept
at or below 4°C in the Object Storage annex; low temperature has
been empirically confirmed to suppress symptom transfer to
handlers without degrading the garment's material integrity. Any
garment inadvertently worn is to be treated as an active medical
device and removed only by personnel briefed on the presenting
symptom. Requisition of SCP-4063 garments for Foundation
humanitarian use requires Level 3 approval and a documented,
verifiable ailment in the intended recipient.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4063 refers to an anomalous effect produced collectively by
eight women, ages 68 to 81, who meet weekly to knit and
needlework at a senior center in a former mill town. When a
member is told, in passing conversation during a session, about a
genuine physical ailment affecting a third party not present at
the meeting, and the group subsequently completes a full garment
(observed only with scarves and hats to date) before the ailment
is mentioned to anyone else that week, the ailment transfers at
approximately full severity from the afflicted person into the
completed garment. The original sufferer recovers within 24
hours. The garment, if worn, transfers the symptom to the wearer
for as long as it remains on the body.

Members show no awareness of producing this effect and
consistently describe their meetings as ordinary social
gatherings. The transfer functions only when the ailment is
relayed casually, framed as news or concern rather than as an
explicit request; a controlled Foundation test in which an
ailment was deliberately and formally requested from the group
produced no effect across eleven [see Note] attempts. Note:
numeral corrected in filing to seven attempts per Site-31
records office; original figure struck through in the source
document and not further explained.

One founding member, Mrs. Agnes Burrell, is deceased; garments
she completed prior to death remain fully active. The group's
origin predates any surviving center record.

ADDENDUM 4063-1 — RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
We have not told the Circle what their scarves do. Two ailments
have been sourced from terminal Foundation patients under
hospice-adjacent care, both with informed consent from the
patient, neither disclosed to the Circle, who believe they are
simply gossiping about a stranger's bad knee. A third transfer
occurred outside documented trigger conditions entirely: a
researcher mentioned a kidney stone diagnosis to Circle member
Mrs. Dolan at a grocery store, not during a session, with no
garment in progress at the time. A pair of mittens completed
three weeks later carried the stones. We do not know how the
group located an ailment mentioned nowhere near their meeting. We
have elected not to ask them.

SCP-4064.name: The Extra Chair
SCP-4064.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Whitcombe family gathering (SCP-4064) is to be attended
annually by a minimum of two embedded Foundation assets posing as
family friends or distant in-laws, tasked with photographing all
attendees discreetly upon arrival. A sealed control set of
photographic negatives is to be produced off-site before each
gathering begins and stored in a Site-31 vault inaccessible to
any asset present at the event, for post-event comparison. Direct
intervention to prevent the annual disappearance event described
below is currently prohibited pending Ethics Committee review; two
prior intervention attempts produced no change in outcome and are
documented in Addendum 4064-2 (Level 3).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4064 is an annual autumn gathering of the extended Whitcombe
family, held at a family-owned farmhouse, attended by a
fluctuating membership that returns each year to a total of
approximately 23 people. At each gathering, exactly one attendee
present at the meal's start is, by its end, retroactively absent
from the memory of every other attendee and from all physical
records produced at or brought to the event — photographs,
guestbooks, place cards — with the sole exception of their
physical chair and place setting, which remains occupied for the
remainder of the meal by a new relative whom no attendee can
supply a birth record, childhood memory, or wedding date for, and
whom all attendees accept without question as having always held
an equivalent role in the family (an uncle is replaced by an
uncle, a cousin by a cousin of matching approximate age).

The family's multi-decade photograph album shows this drift
directly: the same position, the same handwritten caption, a
genuinely different face, gradually, year over year. Foundation
assets embedded at three consecutive gatherings found that their
own personal cameras, developed the following morning off-site,
matched the family's revised membership — meaning the anomaly
revises records not present at the event and not in the family's
possession at the time of alteration.

Only the Foundation's sealed, off-site control negatives, compared
afterward, reliably preserve the pre-event guest list. In every
documented case, the control set shows one guest absent from the
post-event family narrative in any form — not replaced under a
new identity, not remembered as missing, simply gone, the seat
filled socially and left empty in every other sense.

ADDENDUM 4064-1 — INTERVIEW EXCERPT:
Conducted with family matriarch E. Whitcombe, age 84, the
gathering's longest-attending member, one week after that year's
event.

Interviewer: Has anyone ever stopped attending?
Whitcombe: Not once. Look at the pictures, we're all right there,
every year.
Interviewer: I have a photograph taken the morning of the
gathering, before anyone arrived.

Mrs. Whitcombe was shown a Foundation control print depicting a
guest list of 24 names. She identified 23 with confidence and
fluency. Regarding the twenty-fourth, she began crying and could
not produce a name, a relationship, or a reason for her reaction,
stating only that the face "shouldn't still be in a picture like
that." She declined to elaborate further.

SCP-4065.name: The Betterment Society
SCP-4065.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Betterment Society of [REDACTED], a twelve-member civic
improvement club in a town of approximately 2,400 residents, is
to remain unaware of Foundation observation. A Foundation asset
maintains access to the town's water utility billing office, the
only recordkeeping system confirmed unaffected by SCP-4065, and
reviews new ledger entries monthly for unindexed lines matching
the established pattern. Society meetings are not to be
cancelled, disrupted, or attended by Foundation personnel in any
capacity; one authorized cancellation test is documented in
Addendum 4065-1 and is not to be repeated without Site Director
approval.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4065 refers to a paired anomalous effect associated with the
monthly meetings of a small-town civic improvement club. At each
meeting, the twelve members vote on a single proposed town
improvement — repainting a public structure, repairing a fence,
planting trees along a street. By the following morning, the
approved improvement is completed to professional standard at no
material cost to the club or town, by means neither witnessed nor
explained. On the same night, exactly one town resident, not
necessarily a Society member, is rendered permanently missing:
all municipal records, personal effects, and photographs
referencing them are removed from every system the Foundation has
audited, with a single exception, detailed below.

Society members appear genuinely unaware of any connection and
attribute the improvements to an anonymous benefactor grant they
have never questioned. Cross-referencing forty years of meeting
minutes against the town water utility's orphaned billing entries
— unindexed lines with no associated account holder — shows exact
1:1 correspondence: forty improvements, forty missing residents.
Last month's improvement was the repainting of the town clock
tower. The missing resident's final water bill shows usage of
exactly zero gallons for a still-occupied address for that
billing period, indicating someone continued paying the account
after the resident's disappearance.

ADDENDUM 4065-1 — FIELD REPORT:
On one occasion, a Foundation asset anonymously prevented that
month's meeting from occurring by reporting a false gas leak at
the meeting hall. No improvement was completed that month.
However, a resident still went missing that night, selected by an
unknown criterion consistent with prior selections, with no
corresponding town improvement of any kind recorded before or
since. The finding indicates that cancelling the Society's
meetings prevents only the benefit of SCP-4065, not its cost.
Further cancellation tests are not authorized pending review.

ADDENDUM 4065-2 — RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
Cross-referencing the forty missing-resident names against current
Society membership rolls found no living overlap. It did find one
typed surname, misspelled in an identical, specific way — a
transposed pair of letters no other town record repeats — on both a
missing-resident ledger entry from thirty-one years before the
Society's founding and the birth certificate of its current, sitting
secretary. We have not asked the secretary whether she has noticed.
We do not currently have a reason to think she has.

SCP-4066.name: The Last Line
SCP-4066.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4066 requires no physical containment. Foundation cyber
intelligence maintains covert backend access to the private
online peer-support forum used by the affected hospice nurse
network, monitoring membership rolls and new documented cases
without altering forum content or contacting members directly.
No intervention, disclosure, or study protocol requiring member
awareness is currently authorized; see Addendum 4066-1 for the
reasoning behind this policy.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4066 denotes an anomalous auditory effect experienced
exclusively by members of an informal, multi-facility network of
hospice nurses connected through a private online forum (current
membership: 340; subset exhibiting the anomaly: approximately 60).
When a network member nurse is present at a patient's death, she
or he independently reports hearing a final statement spoken by
the patient in the patient's own voice, regardless of the
patient's actual medical capacity for speech, including in
documented cases of patients who were unconscious, intubated, or
otherwise physically incapable of vocalization at time of death.

Across 218 documented cases collected via the forum over nine
years, the content of the heard statement varies but its
structure does not: a short, warm, specific reassurance addressed
by name to a person significant in the patient's life. The named
person has been independently verified as meaningful to the
patient — a spouse, a estranged child, a childhood friend — in
every case where verification was possible, though the name
itself is different in every instance and does not correspond to
any fixed phrase.

No corresponding effect has been documented in non-network
hospice staff present at the same deaths. Repeated simultaneous
interviews confirm this: a network nurse at a bedside reports a
complete sentence; a non-network colleague at the same bedside,
same moment, reports only labored breathing or silence.

ADDENDUM 4066-1 — RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
We have decided not to pursue further study of SCP-4066 beyond
passive monitoring. The effect is benign, appears to comfort both
the dying patient's attending nurse and, when later relayed to
family, the family itself, and has never been observed to produce
harm in 218 cases. Deeper investigation would require either
disclosing the phenomenon to the network, which the Ethics
Committee assesses would degrade or end the effect through
self-consciousness, or covertly exposing members to controlled
death scenarios, which is not something this department is
willing to authorize regardless of scientific yield. Some findings
are filed and left alone. This is one.

ADDENDUM 4066-2 — TEST LOG EXCERPT:
On one occasion two network nurses attended the same death together.
Both reported the same reassurance and the same addressed name,
word for word, independently transcribed in separate rooms
immediately afterward. This is the only documented case of
corroboration between two hearers of SCP-4066's effect at the same
event. Attempts to schedule further paired attendances for controlled
corroboration were declined by network administrators, who cited
staffing constraints and did not respond to a second request.

SCP-4067.name: The Quiet Circle
SCP-4067.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The retreat organization known as the Quiet Circle, operating a
rural retreat house and holding 15 to 20 rotating members at any
given time, is to remain under passive observation by a Foundation
asset maintained within its administrative staff. Attendance at
Quiet Circle retreats by Foundation personnel is prohibited
without Level 3 authorization due to documented long-term effects
on former members (see Description). Individuals who have left the
group and exhibit ongoing symptoms are to be offered, not
compelled, standard Foundation counseling services under an
unrelated cover diagnosis.

DESCRIPTION:
The Quiet Circle is a private self-help and meditation
organization that conducts week-long total-silence retreats
several times annually at a rural retreat house. For a period of
approximately 30 days following a shared retreat, attending
members can complete one another's sentences with word-for-word
accuracy, including sentences the original speaker has not yet
begun and, in a controlled Foundation test, had not yet
consciously decided to say.

In the controlled test, a subject was given a randomly selected
topic on an index card unseen by other members. A second member,
seated in an adjoining room with no audio or visual contact,
dictated the subject's eventual sentence aloud, verbatim, before
the subject began speaking, across nine of ten trials. Members
describe the sensation of being "read" in this manner as
uncomfortable, comparing it to having a sentence taken out of your
mouth before you knew it was there.

Members who leave the organization entirely report that the
effect does not fully fade with time or distance. Several
longstanding former members state that they continue, years
later, to unpredictably "hear" a sentence about to be spoken by a
current Quiet Circle member located elsewhere, with no apparent
distance limit and no method identified to opt out of the
phenomenon voluntarily.

ADDENDUM 4067-1 — INTERVIEW EXCERPT:
Conducted with former member R. Aldous, who left the organization
four years prior to interview.

Interviewer: You mentioned you no longer use telephones.
Aldous: I stopped taking calls from numbers I don't know. A call
from a stranger might have someone else's sentence riding along
inside it. Somebody at the retreat house finishing a thought two
states away, and it just arrives in my head wearing the stranger's
voice as a coat.
Interviewer: How often does this happen?
Aldous: Less than it used to. It hasn't stopped.
Interviewer: Do you know whose sentence it will be, before it
arrives?
Aldous: No. That's the part nobody tells you about the silence.
You think you're choosing to stop talking. You're not being told
who picks it back up.

SCP-4068.name: The Night Frequency
SCP-4068.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
CB radio Channel 22 is to be monitored continuously by automated
Foundation listening posts along all rural highway corridors
where SCP-4068 encounters have been documented. The informal
network of approximately 30 long-haul drivers who habitually use
Channel 22 is not to be disbanded or warned; disruption of the
channel's ordinary traffic has been assessed as more likely to
disperse the phenomenon into unmonitored frequencies than to
reduce encounter frequency. Any driver reporting a completed
pickup is to be intercepted at their next scheduled weigh station
stop for a discreet, cover-consistent medical and cargo check.
Delivered cargo is not to be seized or inspected in a manner that
delays delivery, as all documented cargo has arrived correctly
despite driver amnesia.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4068 refers to a recurring anomalous hitchhiker phenomenon
reported by long-haul truck drivers who communicate on a specific
CB radio channel. Drivers travelling alone at night on rural
highways periodically report picking up a hitchhiker matching a
consistent physical description. Any driver who does so
subsequently loses all memory of that trip's cargo manifest and
delivery destination, discovering only afterward, via delivery
confirmation, that the cargo was delivered successfully to the
correct address, as though the amnesiac driver had continued
driving correctly without them.

Of the roughly 30 drivers in the informal Channel 22 network, each
has picked up the hitchhiker an average of twice. No driver has
ever witnessed another driver's encounter directly. However,
recorded channel chatter shows multiple drivers describing the
same hitchhiker, in the same words, in the same minute, from
locations up to 600 kilometres apart.

A Foundation dash-camera installation during one monitored
encounter recorded audio consistent with two-way conversation,
recorded the passenger seat visibly depressing under weight, and
recorded the seatbelt fastening itself, while the passenger seat
remained visibly empty on video for the entire encounter,
approximately 40 minutes.

ADDENDUM 4068-1 — FIELD REPORT:
Driver interview conducted at a weigh station following a
monitored pickup, driver identity withheld per standard asset
protection.

"I know I picked someone up. I know we talked. I couldn't tell
you one word of it, and I couldn't tell you what's in the trailer
or where it's going, and that scares me more than the rest of it,
because I signed for that cargo myself six hours ago and I don't
recognize my own signature on the paperwork. It's mine. It's just
not mine from when I can remember being me."

The cargo referenced was delivered to the correct destination two
hours after this interview, confirmed by consignee signature.

SCP-4069.name: The Long Table Club
SCP-4069.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Long Table Club, a private dining society of 40 dues-paying
members meeting monthly in a leased city dining hall, is to
remain operational under passive Foundation monitoring. A
Foundation medical asset is embedded among the club's serving
staff of nine to log longitudinal biometric aging data on both
members and staff. Staff resignations are to be processed through
normal channels; the mandatory one-year notice period specified in
club bylaws is not to be waived by Foundation intervention, as
doing so has not been demonstrated to halt in-progress abnormal
aging in the resigning employee and Foundation legal has assessed
intervention in club bylaws as likely to draw member attention.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4069 is an anomalous aging-conservation effect observed among
the membership and staff of a private dining club. Longitudinal
medical monitoring confirms that club members' biological aging,
measured via standard cellular senescence markers, slows in
direct proportion to their cumulative lifetime dues paid to the
club. The club's nine permanent serving staff, who are employees
rather than members and pay no dues, age at a correspondingly
accelerated rate. The aggregate biological aging-years accrued by
all 49 individuals present in the dining hall on any given dinner
night remains constant across the group as a whole; the anomaly
appears to redistribute aging rather than eliminate it.

A staff member who resigns or is terminated stops accruing
abnormal aging within approximately one week. However, aging-years
already absorbed during employment do not return to the pool or
redistribute to remaining staff; the damage is retained
permanently by the individual who absorbed it.

The club's current president has held membership and paid dues
since the club's founding 52 years ago; medical examination is
consistent with a chronological age in the mid-fifties despite a
verified birth date placing her at 79. The club's
longest-serving staff member has been employed for 12 years;
medical examination is consistent with a person in their eighties
despite a verified chronological age of 34. This employee has
submitted resignation requests on three occasions, each denied
under the bylaw requiring one year of notice, during which period
abnormal aging does not pause.

ADDENDUM 4069-1 — RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
The club's bylaws regarding staff notice periods were drafted 61
years ago, nine years before the club's own founding date as
stated in its charter. We have not yet resolved this
inconsistency and have not raised it with club leadership, who
have declined two prior requests to review historical bylaw
drafts, citing member privacy.

SCP-4070.name: The Succession Table
SCP-4070.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The actuarial department of [REDACTED] Life Insurance Company,
comprising seven analysts, is to continue ordinary operation
under passive Foundation monitoring via a covertly acquired copy
of the department's internal mortality-table software
installation. Department personnel are not to be informed of
SCP-4070's existence. A Foundation asset holding a junior analyst
position within the department reports any internally generated
exact-date output to Site-31 without alerting other department
staff. Requests by department staff to disclose a generated date
to its subject are to be intercepted and redirected through
standard HR channels without confirming or denying its accuracy.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4070 refers to an anomalous output produced by the standard
mortality-table calculation software used by the actuarial
department of a mid-size life insurance company, under a single
specific condition: when a department analyst uses the software
to generate a risk calculation for another employee of the same
department, rather than for an external insurance applicant, the
software does not return a probabilistic risk table as designed.
Instead, it returns a single exact calendar date, always in the
future relative to the calculation.

Of four cases in which the queried employee has since died of
causes unrelated to the calculation, the generated date matched
the date of death precisely in all four. Further analysis
established that the date does not correspond to the queried
employee's death specifically, but to the date on which that
employee's desk and role are next scheduled to change hands
within the department, whether through retirement, transfer, or
death — a distinction that happened to be identical in all four
confirmed cases, as each departure was itself caused by death.

The software generates a date only when queried by whichever
analyst is, per ordinary department succession planning, next in
line to inherit the queried employee's position.

ADDENDUM 4070-1 — INTERVIEW EXCERPT:
Conducted with the department head, who has run the calculation
for her own eventual successor's successor, two positions down
the department's succession chain, on two separate occasions.

Interviewer: Can you share the date the software produced?
Department Head: No.
Interviewer: You understand this request comes under Foundation
authority.
Department Head: I understand you have a badge. I have a
company policy on the disclosure of personnel data, and it does
not carve out an exception for whoever you people actually are.
Interviewer: Has the date changed between the two times you ran
it?
Department Head: [no verbal response logged; interview
terminated at subject's request after a pause of approximately
forty seconds]

SCP-4071.name: The Full Roster
SCP-4071.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The city metro system's night-shift crew, a fixed roster of eight
positions (two drivers, two signal operators, two platform staff,
two maintenance technicians), is to remain in ordinary operation.
Foundation liaison staff embedded within the transit authority's
scheduling office monitor shift assignments and flag any night on
which all eight assigned positions are simultaneously confirmed
present and on-duty at the same recorded minute, an overlap termed
a Full Roster event. On a flagged night, a Foundation observation
team boards the final scheduled run as ordinary passengers.
Passengers who exit at SCP-4071's anomalous stop are to be
monitored discreetly for 72 hours; to date no exiting passenger
has been identified, as none have been observed on any station's
exit camera system following the anomalous stop.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4071 denotes an anomalous additional stop made by the city
metro system's final scheduled nightly run under a specific
condition: when all eight members of the fixed night-shift crew
are simultaneously on duty and present in their assigned stations
at the same recorded minute, a rare overlap given standard shift
handoff scheduling, logged 14 times across available transit
authority history. On a Full Roster night, the final train
completes its scheduled route and then makes one additional stop
at a station absent from every city map, engineering blueprint,
and the line's own official track schematic, for a duration of
exactly two minutes with doors open, before resuming normal
operation to the terminal station.

Passengers aboard during the anomalous stop report no unusual
perception at the time and cannot recall the stop when
interviewed afterward, regardless of interview timing. Station
platform pressure and weight sensors, unaffected by passenger
memory, log a measurable change consistent with one to six
additional persons boarding during the stop. None of these
additional persons have been observed exiting the train at any
subsequent station on the recorded remainder of that night's
line.

City transit authority signage and onboard displays number every
official station consecutively from one through the system's
actual total station count. Onboard readout footage from four
separate Full Roster events shows the anomalous stop's platform
number displayed as the integer immediately following the
system's total station count — a number that, within the
numbering scheme as designed, should not exist. In each recorded
instance the digit is rendered in the exact font, size, and
formatting used for every genuine station number on the same
display.

ADDENDUM 4071-1 — FIELD REPORT:
Foundation observers aboard the train during the twelfth
documented Full Roster event reported the doors opening onto a
platform visually consistent with an ordinary station of the
system's older architectural style, unlit except for the train's
own interior light spilling onto the platform edge, and no
signage of any kind visible in that light beyond the displayed
number. No sound was recorded from the platform during the
two-minute stop except, in the final eleven [sic, see Note]
seconds before doors closed, what the observation report
describes only as "several people, not hurrying." Note: duration
figure could not be independently verified against train audio
timestamp data, which shows a two-second gap immediately
preceding door closure with no corresponding data loss elsewhere
in the file.

SCP-4072.name: The Listening Guild
SCP-4072.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The rural gravedigger and mortuary assistant trade guild
designated SCP-4072, comprising approximately 20 active members
across twelve small regional cemeteries, is retained as a
Foundation early-detection asset under an ordinary contracting
cover ("independent cemetery consulting"). Guild members are not
to be informed of Foundation involvement or of the anomalous
nature of their ability; all contracting communication is
conducted through a shell consulting firm posing as an insurance
audit contractor. Guild-reported cases matching Foundation
criteria for anomalous suspended-animation or false-death
conditions are to be forwarded immediately to the nearest mobile
medical unit. Legal costs arising from guild members' unauthorized
exhumation activity are covered discreetly through the shell
firm's standard contractor liability fund.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4072 refers to an anomalous perceptual ability shared among
members of an informal, generations-old trade guild of
gravediggers and morticians' assistants operating across a rural
region, passed down exclusively through apprenticeship and never
formally documented outside oral tradition. A guild member who
presses an ear to freshly turned earth over a grave within 72
hours of burial can determine, with 100% accuracy verified across
30 double-blind Foundation trials, whether the interred individual
was biologically alive at the time of burial. Members do not
describe the sensation as a sound. The most consistent description
offered is a "held breath" felt through the ground, distinct from
any known auditory or tactile phenomenon.

Unwritten guild bylaws, transmitted only through apprenticeship
and never recorded, require any member who detects this condition
to begin exhumation immediately, regardless of cemetery
permission, time of night, or legal consequence to themselves.
Guild members maintain a standing, multi-generational informal
agreement to cover one another's resulting legal costs, including
trespassing and vandalism charges, without exception and without
requiring repayment.

Over the guild's documented 30-year history of Foundation
awareness, four verified successful live exhumations have
occurred, in each case self-reported by guild members to local
authorities as fortunate accidents or unexplained miracles rather
than disclosed as anomalous in nature. The Foundation has since
formalized covert use of the guild as a wide-reaching, low-cost
early-detection network for anomalous premature-burial and
suspended-animation cases across its jurisdiction, classifying
SCP-4072 Thaumiel for its consistent net-positive utility at
minimal operating cost and negligible security exposure, given
the guild's total lack of awareness of Foundation involvement.

ADDENDUM 4072-1 — FIELD REPORT:
Contracted guild member J. Reyes, unaware of Foundation
affiliation, reported the following to the shell consulting
firm's ordinary intake line, transcribed as received: "Fourth
grave this year that isn't sleeping right. Told the family it's a
consulting audit thing, standard procedure, nothing to worry
about. Dug through the night. She was breathing when we got the
lid open. Cemetery's filing a complaint against me again. Guild'll
cover it, same as always. Just tell whoever's paying us that the
fee this month is going to be higher than usual on account of the
new casket." The invoice was paid in full without comment.

SCP-4073.name: The Silent Ash
SCP-4073.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 14 kilograms of SCP-4073 are stored in a sealed steel drum in Site-19 Low-Risk Storage, Wing C. The drum's gasket is rated to prevent accidental discharge through vibration during transport. Personnel handling SCP-4073 must wear a positive-pressure respirator; inhalation has not been shown to cause physical harm but is prohibited pending further study. Withdrawal of SCP-4073 for testing requires Level 2 authorization and must be logged with the exact mass removed, to the nearest gram, in the site inventory ledger. Newly recovered stock is not to be consolidated with existing stock until each batch has completed independent spectral analysis.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4073 is a fine grey powder, chemically consistent with ordinary wood and structural ash. The original sample, approximately 22 kilograms, was recovered from the site of a residential structure fire in [REDACTED], Ohio.

When approximately 40 grams of SCP-4073 is scattered across a surface, all sound originating within a 3-metre radius of the powder is suppressed absolutely for as long as the powder remains undisturbed. This is not muffling. Instrumentation placed inside the radius registers a complete absence of acoustic signal, including each instrument's own internal electrical noise floor. Conversation, footsteps, and a controlled small-arms discharge conducted inside the radius during testing produced no measurable waveform of any kind.

The fire from which SCP-4073 originated was reported by neighbors only after the structure had visibly collapsed. A canvass of the surrounding six houses found that no resident recalled hearing the fire at any point, including the two residents whose homes shared a wall with the burned structure.

ADDENDUM 4073-1:
Recordings made with hydrophones placed inside the 3-metre radius, later processed outside containment, are not perfectly silent.
