Below the threshold of human hearing, a periodic waveform recurs at an interval of 41 seconds. Pitch-shifted upward into the audible range, three audio analysts, working independently of one another, described the waveform the same way: a single adult voice, screaming, cut short.

The residence had one listed occupant. No remains were recovered from the site. The occupant's case remains open with local authorities as a missing person.

TEST LOG 4073-B:
Forty grams of SCP-4073 scattered in Testing Chamber 3, unoccupied. Result: standard suppression radius confirmed. A metronome set at 60 beats per minute, placed at the center of the radius, was silent on all external recording equipment for the duration of the 30-minute test. The metronome's internal counter confirmed it continued to operate mechanically throughout. Relocated to 2.9 metres from the powder, just inside the boundary: no change. Relocated to 3.1 metres, just outside the boundary: full audio returned instantly, at a volume consistent with 30 minutes of continuous operation. The metronome had not stopped, had not been silenced retroactively. It had simply not been heard.

The case file has not been updated since Foundation recovery of the sample; local records continue to list the occupant's status as active and pending, reviewed annually and closed by no one. No next of kin has been located to request closure.

SCP-4074.name: Foreknowledge Blend
SCP-4074.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining 1.8 litres of SCP-4074 are stored in its original stainless steel service urn inside a standard refrigeration unit in Site-19 Anomalous Materials Storage. The urn's fill level must be recorded at the start and end of every shift. Testing on human subjects requires Level 3 authorization and full psychometric baseline evaluation of the subject not less than 48 hours prior to and following exposure. Consumption of SCP-4074 by unauthorized personnel is treated as an anomalous exposure incident regardless of volume ingested.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4074 is a coffee-like liquid, dark brown, with a flavor profile consistent with a moderately over-roasted commercial blend. It was recovered, still warm, from an unattended service urn in the break room of [REDACTED] Logistics, a shipping firm whose offices had been vacated eight months prior to recovery with no forwarding information filed.

A subject who consumes 200 millilitres or more of SCP-4074 will, over the following 20 to 35 minutes, experience intrusive and highly specific memories of events that have not yet occurred in their remaining day, reported by subjects as indistinguishable in texture from ordinary recollection. Accuracy of these memories, verified across 61 trials, is consistent with true precognition in 58 cases.

Each confirmed exposure is followed by the permanent, undetected loss of one unrelated long-term memory from the subject's past, of apparently random selection and significance. Subjects do not notice the loss at the time; it is identified only by comparing pre- and post-exposure interview transcripts, where the subject will supply a confident, detailed, and internally consistent account of a memory they earlier described in identical, unprompted detail, for an event research subsequently establishes never took place.

The urn's fill level has not decreased since recovery despite 43 recorded withdrawals totaling 26 litres.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE (Dr. Aksan):
We have stopped asking subjects to recall their pre-test baseline interview after exposure. It was not producing useful data. It was producing subjects who insist, calmly and at length, that they have always known us.

TEST LOG 4074-9:
Subject D-8112 given 250 millilitres of SCP-4074 at 09:00.
09:22 — Subject reports "remembering" a fire alarm test scheduled for 14:00 that day. No such test was scheduled.
14:00 — Fire alarm test conducted at Site-19, ordered independently by Facilities fifteen minutes prior for unrelated maintenance reasons, unknown to the subject or testing staff at time of dosing.
Post-exposure interview: subject correctly named the technician who would perform the test, a person the subject had never met and whose duty roster placement that day had not yet been finalized at 09:00.
Memory loss identified on transcript comparison: subject's account of a childhood dog, previously given in consistent detail across two unrelated interviews conducted nine months apart, is absent. Subject now reports no childhood pet and grows mildly irritated when shown the earlier transcript, stating it must belong to someone else's file.

SCP-4075.name: Boneglass Vapor
SCP-4075.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4075 is contained as a compressed gas in a triple-sealed cylinder within Site-19's Hazardous Atmospherics Vault, itself maintained at negative pressure relative to the surrounding corridor. Any breach of the cylinder's primary seal automatically triggers full vault lockdown and site-wide atmospheric alert. No sample of SCP-4075 may be vented, tested, or transferred outside the vault under any circumstances short of written O5 authorization. Personnel assigned to the vault rotate on a standard biohazard exposure schedule and undergo skeletal density imaging before and after each shift.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4075 is a colorless, faintly sweet-smelling gas recovered from an abandoned pharmaceutical research facility in [REDACTED], designation and ownership at time of operation unrecovered. Inhalation of SCP-4075, even in trace quantities, initiates a process by which the calcium content of the subject's skeleton is gradually replaced with a transparent, glass-like crystalline structure of unknown composition. The process is not painful by subject report and does not impair mobility until its final stage, roughly 40 minutes after exposure, at which point the affected skeletal structure loses mechanical integrity without warning.

Subjects remain conscious, coherent, and largely unaware of the progression absent direct imaging; several test subjects have described a sensation of increasing physical lightness, which they uniformly characterized as pleasant. One subject, informed of the imaging results at the 30-minute mark, asked only whether the process could be slowed rather than reversed.

INCIDENT LOG 4075-2:
During recovery operations at the source facility, a filing cabinet in what had been the facility's administrative wing was found intact. Personnel effects recovered from a locked drawer included a single handwritten card, unsigned, addressed to "the next shift," describing the gas's effect not as a weapon but as a treatment, and referring to the subject population as "the first to see clearly." The facility's production logs, also recovered, list a manufacturing quota in units consistent with individual dosing rather than bulk chemical weapon deployment. No personnel records for the facility have been located. The site contained forty workstations. Recovery teams accounted for thirty-nine chairs.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE (Dr. Tunc): We asked three independent chemists to account for why the replacement structure is transparent rather than opaque, since no known biological calcification process produces a comparable result under any pressure or temperature we have been able to reproduce in the lab. None of the three reports agreed with one another, and none survived internal peer review. The most recent draft describes the material only in terms of the wavelengths it fails to refract, which is not a description of composition, only of absence. Facilities has asked, twice, whether the vault's dry chemical suppression system is rated for a gas that appears to consume calcium rather than react with it chemically in any conventional sense. The request for a formal answer remains open.

SCP-4076.name: The Tailor's Bolt
SCP-4076.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining 9 metres of SCP-4076 are stored on a standard bolt rack in Site-19 Anomalous Materials Storage, wrapped in opaque cloth to prevent visual measurement by passing personnel, a precaution instituted after Addendum 4076-1. Any cutting, sewing, or measuring of SCP-4076 requires Level 3 authorization and must be performed by a Foundation-cleared tailor under observation. Garments completed from SCP-4076 are stored separately in individually sealed garment bags and are not to be tried on except under active testing conditions.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4076 is a bolt of grey wool-blend cloth, machine-woven, recovered from an estate sale in [REDACTED] alongside otherwise unremarkable household goods. Any garment constructed from SCP-4076, regardless of the pattern used or the measurements taken by the tailor at time of cutting, will fit its first wearer with tailored precision after being worn continuously for approximately six hours, during which observers report audible creaking sounds from within the fabric weave not attributable to normal cloth movement.

Garments made from SCP-4076 given to a second wearer do not adjust to the second wearer's measurements. Instead, the garment retains the exact measurements of its first wearer indefinitely, including measurements altered by later weight change, amputation, or death, and will visibly strain or gape on any second wearer whose body differs from that original fit.

Prior to Foundation recovery, the bolt had furnished at minimum four generations of a single family's formal wear, per family records recovered with the estate. Measurements taken from three garments in the estate's possession, cross-referenced against family photographs, matched the same body across all three garments despite the garments being dated across a span of sixty-one years and credited in family records to three different named relatives.

ADDENDUM 4076-1:
A femur, believed non-anomalous and stored separately per standard osteological protocol, was found packed inside the bolt's cardboard core during a routine inventory re-shelving. Its measurements are consistent with the recurring fit described above. The femur has not been assigned to any garment currently held in containment.

ADDENDUM 4076-2: An attempt to unravel a 30-centimetre test swatch of SCP-4076 for fiber analysis was suspended after the swatch produced the same audible creaking described in first-wearer garments, despite never having been worn by anyone. The sound was traced to a single point within the weave, consistent in location across three separate swatches cut from different sections of the bolt. A fourth swatch, cut at twice the standard testing distance from the core, produced no sound and has been retained separately for comparative study. No mechanism for the sound has been identified. Fiber analysis has not been completed. The Ethics Committee has since asked whether unravelling should be classified as measurement for purposes of the standard authorization requirement; the question has not yet been resolved. The record recommends that any future test swatches be subject to a separate authorization track going forward.

SCP-4077.name: The Foretelling Rust
SCP-4077.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The primary sample of SCP-4077, a hull plate measuring 60 by 40 centimetres, is stored in a humidity-controlled case in Site-19 Anomalous Materials Storage to prevent uncontrolled oxidation. Personnel are prohibited from bringing personal identification, nametags, or any object bearing their own name within 2 metres of SCP-4077 without Level 3 authorization. Any new rust formation on SCP-4077 is to be photographed, transcribed, and reported to the on-duty researcher within one hour of discovery, before the message is scraped and archived. Scraped rust regenerates within 24 to 96 hours.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4077 is a corroded steel plate recovered from the hull of a fishing vessel found adrift and unmanned off the coast of [REDACTED]. The plate's rust does not behave as ordinary oxidation. New rust formations arrange themselves into short, legible phrases in the language of whichever Foundation personnel are nearest at formation, describing a minor, mundane, near-future event: a delayed delivery, a spilled drink, a canceled meeting, a misplaced set of keys. In 233 recorded formations, 231 have been verified accurate after the fact, typically within 72 hours of the message's appearance. The remaining two were not verified due to the predicted event's subject declining to confirm details.

The rust does not form predictions concerning matters of scale it has not previously demonstrated: no formation predicted an anomalous event, a Foundation operational matter, or, prior to Incident 4077-4, a personnel matter of any severity.

INCIDENT LOG 4077-4:
A formation was discovered during a routine morning check reading, in translation, "[SUBJECT NAME] will not wake on [DATE]." The named subject was a member of the overnight maintenance staff with no scheduled proximity to SCP-4077's storage case. The plate has since been moved to permanent isolation pending review. [DATE] has not yet occurred. The named subject was reassigned off-site pending Ethics Committee review; the plate produced a second, unscraped formation eight days after the first, reading only, "It does not matter where he sleeps."

ADDENDUM 4077-5: A proposal to destroy SCP-4077 by full submersion in an acid bath was tabled after a preliminary formation, produced during preparation for the test, read simply, "Not this way." The formation was scraped and archived per standard procedure. No formation since has referenced the disposal proposal, which remains under Ethics Committee review rather than approved or withdrawn. Personnel assigned to the review have been instructed not to carry identification within the standard 2-metre exclusion radius while the proposal remains open. The archive of scraped rust transcripts, maintained since the plate's recovery, currently totals 233 entries bound in a single ledger. Cross-referencing has found no instance of a formation repeating a previous message verbatim, and no instance of two formations contradicting one another. The ledger itself has never produced a formation of its own; only the plate does. An informal debate persists among Site-19 personnel over whether the plate is aware of its own archive; no formal study of the question has been opened.

SCP-4078.name: The Unspoiling Honey
SCP-4078.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The single jar constituting SCP-4078 is stored at standard room temperature on an open shelf in Site-19 Anomalous Materials Storage; refrigeration and airtight sealing have both been tested and shown to have no effect on the anomaly and are not required. The jar's fill level is to be measured to the nearest millilitre at the start of each month. Testing involving ingestion by human subjects requires Level 2 authorization, informed consent where the subject is capable of providing it, and full medical monitoring for the 24-hour duration of each dose's effect.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4078 is a 900-millilitre glass jar of honey, light amber in color, of otherwise unremarkable composition under standard laboratory analysis. A subject who consumes one standard tablespoon of SCP-4078 will, for the following 24 hours, be held at their exact physical state at time of consumption: no further aging, healing, deterioration, or progression of any condition present at the moment of ingestion occurs. Injuries sustained after consumption heal or worsen normally. Injuries or conditions present before consumption remain precisely, measurably static; a fever holds its exact temperature, a fracture neither knits nor worsens, a terminal diagnosis does not advance.

SCP-4078 was recovered from a residential kitchen in [REDACTED] alongside the remains of an elderly resident whose most recent medical chart, recovered separately, listed a diagnosis with an estimated prognosis of nine weeks remaining at time of diagnosis. Municipal records indicate the resident continued to fill and pay for prescriptions, receive mail, and interact with neighbors for six years following that diagnosis before their eventual, and by all evidence entirely mundane, death of unrelated causes.

The jar has never been observed to be refilled. Despite 118 recorded withdrawals totaling approximately 6 litres, the fill level recorded each month has not decreased below its first recorded measurement. No hive, colony, or apiary of any kind has been located in connection with the residence or its prior occupants.

ADDENDUM 4078-1:
A Foundation researcher under long-term palliative care for an unrelated non-anomalous illness has, with Ethics Committee approval, been maintained on a daily dose of SCP-4078 since [DATE]. The researcher's condition has not changed in 340 consecutive days. The researcher has asked, in writing, to be taken off the dosing schedule. The request is under review.

ADDENDUM 4078-2: A follow-up canvass of the resident's former neighbors found general agreement that the resident had "seemed fine, all things considered" in the years following the diagnosis, and general surprise, on being told the diagnosis's original prognosis, that the resident had never mentioned being ill at all. Municipal utility records reviewed as part of the same canvass show no gap in service at the residence at any point between diagnosis and death, consistent with a household that continued to function without interruption. No family members have come forward to claim the estate; the jar remains cataloged under the original property case number, awaiting a disposition ruling that has been pending for longer than the residence's prior tenant was expected to live.

SCP-4079.name: Chronosalt
SCP-4079.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The 4 kilograms of SCP-4079 recovered to date are divided into 100-gram sealed glass ampoules stored in a temperature-stable vault in Site-19's Deep Storage annex. Ampoules are not to be stored within 10 metres of any water source, including fire suppression systems; the wing housing SCP-4079 uses a dry chemical suppression system exclusively. Any breach resulting in dissolution of SCP-4079 in water requires immediate Level 4 notification and activation of Biological Containment Protocol Delta.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4079 is a translucent crystalline salt, chemically anomalous and resistant to standard spectroscopic classification, recovered from the site of the former town of [REDACTED], population 214 at last census. When dissolved in water at any concentration, SCP-4079 generates an expanding spherical field within which organic matter is subjected to a severe, sustained reversal of biological time. Affected organisms first display rapid apparent healing and de-aging, proceeding within minutes through infancy, gestation, and finally into an undifferentiated biomass that continues to grow in volume without further organizing into tissue of any kind. The field does not stop at this stage; it expands to incorporate additional organic matter at its boundary, growing without an observed upper limit in testing to date.

The town of [REDACTED] was not evacuated prior to Foundation intervention; no evacuation order was ever filed. Recovery teams found the town site occupied by a single contiguous mass of undifferentiated organic tissue, its volume calculated by displacement to be within 4 percent of the combined estimated body mass of the town's last recorded population.

TEST LOG 4079-C:
One gram of SCP-4079 dissolved in 500 millilitres of water within a sealed containment sphere, applied to a sample of Class-D tissue (200 grams). Field expansion halted successfully at sphere boundary. Sample fully reverted to undifferentiated biomass within 6 minutes, weight increased to 240 grams with no additional organic input identified. Sphere breached for retrieval; growth resumed immediately upon exposure to ambient humidity, reaching 1.1 kilograms before re-containment. Test suspended. Recommend all further testing occur exclusively within double-walled dry containment.

ADDENDUM 4079-1: Aerial imaging of the former town site, taken eighteen months after recovery, shows the biomass has not decreased in volume despite continuous cold, dry storage of all recovered SCP-4079 stock and no further dissolution events. Structural engineers attached to the recovery operation have noted that the biomass's outer surface has begun to develop a texture consistent with bark, though no botanical structures have been identified beneath it on core sampling. The site remains designated a standing exclusion zone. Local records describing the town's prior population have been quietly withdrawn from public archives pending an official explanation for its disappearance, a task that has not yet been assigned to any active Foundation office. The expansion rate at the biomass's edge is monitored monthly and has to date remained constant.

SCP-4080.name: The Greeting Sand
SCP-4080.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4080 is maintained in its original wooden tray, dimensions 60 by 90 centimetres, in a standard research office in Site-19's Low Risk wing. The tray is accessible to on-duty researchers for observation and interaction without special authorization, though any written exchange with SCP-4080 must be photographed before the standard 24-hour fade and logged in the SCP-4080 correspondence file. SCP-4080 requires no physical containment measures beyond the tray itself; movement of the tray has been tested extensively and does not affect the anomaly.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4080 is approximately 40 kilograms of fine white sand of a mineral composition not matching any commercially available or naturally occurring sand within 900 kilometres of its recovery site, a since-demolished roadside rest stop in [REDACTED]. Words or drawings made in SCP-4080's surface by hand fade to smoothness within exactly 24 hours of being made, regardless of depth, protection from disturbance, or ambient conditions.

Approximately once every nine to fourteen days, a short message appears in SCP-4080's surface that was not written by any known person. The message is invariably addressed by first name to whichever cleared researcher is currently assigned nearest to the tray, is invariably mundane in content, a comment on the weather, a question about the researcher's day, an observation about an object on the researcher's desk that the message could not have had visual access to, and is invariably written in a hand consistent with the addressed researcher's own handwriting, confirmed by comparison against personnel file samples.

Cross-referencing message dates against personnel assignment records has established, in seven of nine cases reviewed, that the message addressed a researcher by name between one and three days before that researcher's formal assignment to the SCP-4080 project was finalized in the personnel system.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE:
I was told before I started that this file was the closest thing the archive has to a joke. I want it on record that the sand asked me, by name, how my drive in was, four days before I accepted the transfer.

ADDENDUM 4080-1: Three researchers previously addressed by SCP-4080 before their assignment were interviewed after the pattern was identified. None recalled having discussed the SCP-4080 project, informally or otherwise, with any staff member prior to the date their message appeared. Two described the experience as comforting in retrospect. The third has requested reassignment away from the project and, per standard policy, the request has been granted without requiring justification. SCP-4080 has not produced a message addressed to that researcher since the reassignment was finalized, nor has it produced any message referencing the reassignment itself. The tray's correspondence file now runs to sixty-one logged exchanges across four years of observation, the great majority unremarkable. Facilities has twice proposed relocating the tray to a more secure wing; both proposals were declined by the assigned research lead without further comment on the record. Security camera footage covering the tray has never once captured the moment a message forms.

SCP-4081.name: The Quiet Oil
SCP-4081.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining 40 litres of SCP-4081 are stored in unmarked, unlabeled steel drums in Site-19 Deep Storage to reduce the likelihood of accidental use as conventional lubricant. All Foundation facilities are required to maintain a verified inventory of mechanical lubricant stock on a quarterly basis; any unaccounted-for lubricant volume site-wide triggers a mandatory SCP-4081 exclusion audit. SCP-4081 is not to be used, under any circumstances, on load-bearing, occupied, or life-safety mechanical systems, including elevators, cranes, and emergency egress hardware.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4081 is a clear, faintly amber mechanical oil of unknown origin, recovered in a sealed 200-litre drum from a scrapyard purchase lot with no traceable prior owner. Any mechanical system lubricated with SCP-4081 operates permanently and completely without noise: no squeak, hum, vibration-borne sound, or mechanical report of any kind is produced by the treated system for the remainder of its operational life, regardless of wear, damage, or approaching failure.

Standard mechanical systems produce escalating audible warning signs before catastrophic failure, grinding, squealing, knocking, that allow operators or maintenance staff to intervene. Systems treated with SCP-4081 produce no such warning. Failure occurs abruptly and without acoustic precedent, at a rate of mechanical degradation research indicates is otherwise unaffected by the oil; only the sound of that degradation is removed.

INCIDENT LOG 4081-6:
A drum of SCP-4081, mislabeled during a storage reorganization, was issued to Site-19 Facilities and used to service Service Elevator 3's primary cable assembly. The elevator operated without incident for sixty-one days. On day sixty-two, the cable assembly failed completely between the third and fourth floors. The only record of the failure is a floor indicator log showing an instantaneous position change and a stopped-elevator alarm triggered by the cab's final impact, not by any sound preceding it. Two occupants were aboard. Facilities maintenance logs for the sixty-one preceding days record no anomalies, no complaints, and no scheduled concerns, because there was, audibly, nothing to report.

Recovered drum stock has since been re-labeled and moved to Deep Storage under current procedures.

ADDENDUM 4081-1: A site-wide audit conducted after Incident 4081-6 identified two further drums of unlabeled oil in general Facilities stock, neither confirmed as SCP-4081 by chemical analysis, both destroyed as a precaution. Facilities has since implemented a mandatory chemical fingerprinting step for all bulk lubricant stock prior to issue, adding an average of six hours to routine maintenance requests. Complaints about the added delay have been noted and declined for review, on the stated grounds that the alternative has already been demonstrated once. The new fingerprinting step has not, to date, identified any additional sample of SCP-4081.

SCP-4082.name: The Common Stranger
SCP-4082.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining SCP-4082 gas stock, approximately 30 litres at standard pressure, is stored in a sealed cylinder within Site-19's Hazardous Atmospherics Vault. Testing requires Level 3 authorization and is limited to one exposed subject per calendar month, a limit imposed following Addendum 4082-2. All exposed subjects are debriefed by a psychologist not themselves exposed to SCP-4082, to prevent cross-contamination of description.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4082 is a colorless, odorless gas recovered from a sealed ventilation shaft in a disused mine outside [REDACTED]. A subject exposed to even brief concentrations of SCP-4082 will, beginning approximately one hour after exposure and continuing indefinitely, perceive a stationary human figure standing at the edge of their visual field, always just beyond direct focus, vanishing when looked at directly and reappearing at the periphery once attention moves elsewhere.

Subjects consistently describe the figure, without prior coordination or access to other subjects' statements, as a man of approximately sixty years, wearing clothing subjects describe as old-fashioned without further specificity, with a scar or fold of skin above the left eyebrow described in near-identical terms across 38 of 41 exposed subjects to date: a straight line, pale, roughly 3 centimetres, as if from a healed cut.

No subject has reported the figure speaking, approaching, or otherwise interacting with the environment. Subjects report the sensation of being mildly, continuously observed. No treatment has reduced the perception's frequency; subjects report the figure becomes, over a period of months, easier to ignore rather than less present.

ADDENDUM 4082-2:
A retired Foundation researcher, exposed during an uncontained release thirty-four years prior to a facility since decommissioned, was located during an unrelated records audit and voluntarily interviewed. The researcher, now elderly, described the figure in terms matching current subjects exactly, including the scar, and stated that in recent years the figure has begun, on rare occasions, to be joined at the periphery by a second, younger figure standing slightly behind the first. The researcher was unable to describe the second figure's face. Testing has not yet reproduced a second figure in any currently monitored subject.

ADDENDUM 4082-3: A comparative review of exposure case files across all three currently active gas-anomaly containment projects at Site-19 found SCP-4082 to be the only one in which every exposed subject describes the same unrelated figure regardless of the subject's age, background, or prior psychiatric history. Statistical review has ruled out coincidental convergence at a confidence level the assigned analyst described, in an internal memo, as "higher than I am comfortable putting in writing." The memo has since been filed alongside the subject debrief transcripts rather than the statistical appendix, at the analyst's own request. The second figure has to date been described by only one subject.

SCP-4083.name: The Duplicating Alloy
SCP-4083.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All recovered SCP-4083 mass, currently 640 kilograms across 1,140 discrete objects, is stored in Site-19's Non-Ferrous Isolation Bay, a chamber lined with a ceramic composite barrier to which SCP-4083 has shown no replicative response. No object composed of iron, steel, copper, or any metal alloy is permitted within 15 metres of the Bay without prior written authorization from the assigned Senior Researcher. Any metal object reported missing within Site-19 must be cross-checked against the SCP-4083 object inventory before being logged as lost.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4083 refers to a self-propagating anomalous property first identified in a single brass ship's fitting recovered from a decommissioned shipyard in [REDACTED]. Any metal object brought within approximately 2 metres of an object already affected by SCP-4083 will, within 12 to 30 hours, produce an exact structural duplicate of itself from its own mass, fusing outward from a single point of contact. The duplicate is chemically and structurally identical to the original at the molecular level, including manufacturing tool marks, prior wear, and any engraved text, reproduced without error including manufacturing defects present in the original. The duplicated object is itself immediately affected by SCP-4083 and capable of producing further duplicates.

The shipyard from which the original object was recovered was found to contain 1,140 objects, later confirmed to derive from an original recovered set of eight personal items belonging to shipyard workers, expanded through successive duplication across an unknown period estimated at no less than four decades based on corrosion consistent with the oldest duplicates.

Among the 1,140 recovered objects are 94 exact duplicates of a single engraved identification tag, stamped with a worker's badge number and a name partially legible on 31 of the 94 copies. Personnel records for the shipyard's operating company, where recovered, list no employee under that badge number. The name, where legible, does not match any name in the recovered employment roster.

INCIDENT LOG 4083-1:
A junior technician's wedding ring, non-anomalous, was inadvertently left within contact range of a duplicated fitting during a routine object transfer. Recovery teams located and re-isolated 3 duplicate rings within 30 hours. A fourth has not been recovered. The technician has been informed only that the ring was lost during processing.

ADDENDUM 4083-2: A structural engineer attached to the containment review has proposed that the 1,140 recovered objects may not represent the full extent of duplication at the source shipyard, noting that the recovered count corresponds closely to the shipyard's documented storage capacity rather than to any natural stopping point in the replication process. The proposal implies duplication ceased only because there was no further space for duplicates to form, not because the underlying property exhausted itself. The implication has not been formally addressed in any subsequent containment review. The inventory count within the Bay is repeated monthly.

SCP-4084.name: The Waiting Shroud
SCP-4084.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4084 is stored folded in an acid-free archival box in Site-19 Anomalous Materials Storage. The shroud is not to be draped over any subject, living or deceased, except under active testing conditions with Level 2 authorization and a Foundation medical examiner present for the full duration of the effect. SCP-4084 is not to be used on any deceased Foundation staff member without prior approval of the deceased's designated next of kin or, absent such kin, the assigned Ethics Committee liaison.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4084 is a shroud of unbleached linen, approximately 2 by 1 metres, recovered from a funerary supplier in [REDACTED] under investigation for issuing fraudulent death certificates. When draped fully over a recently deceased human body, SCP-4084 suppresses all externally visible signs of death for a period of exactly 72 hours from the time of draping. During this period, the body's skin retains coloration and apparent warmth consistent with life, rigor mortis and lividity do not develop, and the body does not visibly decompose under any tested condition, including elevated ambient temperature. Standard medical instrumentation confirms the subject remains, by every other measure, dead throughout the 72-hour period.

At the conclusion of the 72-hour period, the shrouded body undergoes decomposition consistent with several weeks of unrefrigerated elapsed time within approximately seven minutes.

The supplier from which SCP-4084 was recovered had, per recovered business records, issued 23 death certificates over a six-year period for clients whose bodies were never presented for burial, cremation, or any other verifiable disposal, each listing a cause of death and no listed date of disposal.

TEST LOG 4084-4:
SCP-4084 applied to Class-D subject D-9903 (deceased of cardiac arrest during unrelated testing, time of death confirmed by medical examiner). Standard signs of death suppressed as described. At 46 hours post-draping, monitoring equipment recorded a single, isolated instance of slow, tracked eye movement beneath the closed lids, lasting approximately four seconds, not repeated for the remainder of the test. Medical examiner confirmed no brain activity present on concurrent EEG. Movement was not reproduced in tests 4084-5 through 4084-9. Testing continues at reduced frequency.

ADDENDUM 4084-2: Foundation legal review of the supplier's 23 fraudulent certificates has closed without identifying next of kin for nineteen of the twenty-three listed decedents; in each of those nineteen cases, the original certificate's informant field, normally completed by a family member, lists the supplier's own proprietor. The proprietor has not been located since the site's raid. Foundation amnestic teams administered standard Class-A treatment to first responders at the time of the raid; none reported having handled or observed anything resembling SCP-4084 during the operation, though the shroud was recovered, logged, and photographed on site by the same responders. No test involving the shroud may begin without medical examiner sign-off.

SCP-4085.name: Please Hold.
SCP-4085.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4085 is stored in a standard
audio-isolation locker in the Site-19 Audio Archive. The cassette is
not to be inserted into any playback device without written
authorization from a Level 2 researcher. A sign-out log is kept
beside the locker; each entry requires a stated purpose, an
estimated playback duration, and a countersignature.

Personnel who listen to SCP-4085 for a cumulative total exceeding
twenty minutes are placed on a seventy-two hour behavioral watch and
are not permitted to work alone during that period. A plastic chair
is kept outside the Audio Archive door for personnel awaiting
authorization. This chair is not to be removed, relabeled, or
explained to new staff, per Site-19 Facilities directive 4085-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4085 is a ninety-minute audio cassette recovered in 2003 from
the disused telephone switching system of a demolished office
building in Dayton, Ohio. The recording is a loop of instrumental
music, unremarkable in composition, of the type historically used to
fill telephone hold queues. The loop is nine minutes and forty
seconds long and repeats without audible seam.

Subjects who listen to SCP-4085 report that the recording appears to
slow down the longer it is played, although instrument-level
analysis confirms the tape does not change speed. Subjective time
dilation of approximately 4:1 has been measured in controlled
listening sessions: a subject asked to estimate elapsed time after
ten minutes of exposure will typically estimate forty minutes or
more.

Subjects exposed for longer than twenty cumulative minutes exhibit
queue behavior: standing when previously seated, facing a door or
intercom speaker, and waiting to be addressed before moving,
speaking, or leaving the room, even when alone. Subjects released
from this state report no memory of choosing to stand.

{{3|ADDENDUM: subjects exposed for longer than sixty cumulative
minutes have been observed queuing outside rooms they were never
instructed to wait outside of, including rooms with no assigned
function. Three subjects have independently selected the same
disused stairwell on Site-19 Sub-Level 2 as a waiting location. No
instruction to do so has been recovered from any playback of
SCP-4085, and no two of the three subjects had met before testing.|}}

TEST LOG 4085-3:
Subject D-8112 was seated in a standard interview room and issued
SCP-4085 through a single earpiece, timed at fifteen minutes.

00:00 — Subject begins listening. Reports no unusual sensation.
05:00 — Subject asked to estimate elapsed time. Estimate given:
'maybe two minutes.'
10:00 — Subject stops responding to verbal prompts. Posture shifts
from seated-slouched to seated-upright, hands folded in lap.
15:00 — Recording stopped. Subject does not react to the silence.
Subject remains seated, facing the door, for eleven further minutes
before a researcher enters and addresses him directly. Subject
reports he was waiting for his number to be called. No number had
been issued to him, on this or any prior occasion.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We have stopped asking which number. Every
subject so far has had an answer ready. — Dr. Marchetti

SCP-4086.name: The Wedding Reel
SCP-4086.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4086 is stored in a lightproof canister in Site-19 Film
Archive, Cold Room 2. Projection is permitted only for approved
research under the supervision of two Level 2 personnel. Following
any viewing, the viewing subject is to be debriefed and administered
Class-A amnestics within one hour. Verbal description of SCP-4086's
content by a viewer to a non-viewer carries a documented, though
reduced, risk of partial effect transfer; such description is to be
logged as an exposure event.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4086 is a sixteen-millimeter silent film reel, running time
eight minutes eleven seconds, labeled on its case only with the
characters 'M & T' and a handwritten year that is illegible.
Chemical analysis of the film stock dates its manufacture to no
earlier than 2004, which is inconsistent with the black-and-white
stock, period clothing, and silent-film format depicted, none of
which were in common production after the 1960s.

The film depicts a wedding reception in an unidentified banquet
hall. Approximately thirty guests are visible across various shots;
no guest's face is ever shown in full focus. Any subject who views
the complete reel reports, within minutes of the viewing ending,
a set of detailed personal memories of having attended the wedding
as a guest, including recollection of conversation, food served, and
a toast given by an unnamed best man. These memories are held with
the same confidence and emotional weight as the subject's genuine
autobiographical memory and do not diminish under questioning.

Subjects further report, without exception, that the bride depicted
in the film — given a first name by each subject, which varies
between subjects — died young, generally described as within two
years of the wedding, of an unspecified cause. No death is depicted
or implied within the film itself. Subjects asked to describe the
circumstances of the bride's death become visibly distressed and
give answers that grow more specific with repeated questioning
rather than less, contrary to the pattern normally seen when a
fabricated memory is challenged.

Across forty-one recorded exposures, no two subjects have reported
the same bride's name, though nineteen subjects have independently
reported a burgundy tablecloth on the head table, a detail not
visible in the black-and-white print.

INTERVIEW EXCERPT, Subject D-9033, four hours post-exposure:

Dr. Ibarra: Tell me about the bride.
D-9033: Marisol. She was — she laughed with her whole face. You'd
have liked her.
Dr. Ibarra: You've never met her.
D-9033: I sat two tables back. I have the napkin.
Dr. Ibarra: There is no napkin.
D-9033: (pause) Then where did I put it.

Subject was administered amnestics at the conclusion of the
interview. Follow-up interview eleven days later found the subject
unable to recall the wedding, the interview, or the name Marisol,
but reported an unexplained impulse, twice, to buy flowers.

SCP-4087.name: Corridor Print 14
SCP-4087.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4087 is housed in a lead-lined viewing box in a sealed chamber
at Site-19, viewable only through a one-way optical relay that
limits observation to no more than ninety seconds per session. All
corridors within a four-hundred-metre radius of SCP-4087's storage
location are photographed weekly and compared against a 2011
baseline survey; any deviation in tile pattern, door count, or
lighting fixture placement is to be reported immediately and the
affected corridor sealed pending assessment.

All known reproductions of SCP-4087 are to be tracked and recovered.
As of this writing, three of an estimated eleven reproductions
remain unrecovered.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4087 is a silver gelatin photographic print, twenty by
twenty-five centimetres, depicting an unornamented corridor of a
type consistent with a mid-twentieth-century institutional
building: pale tile, evenly spaced doors, no windows, a light
fixture every third ceiling panel. The corridor in the photograph
does not correspond to any building on record.

Real corridors sharing sufficient architectural similarity to the
print — tile colour, door spacing, and fixture rhythm within a
measured tolerance — undergo slow, physical alteration to more
closely resemble the depicted corridor, at a rate proportional to
proximity to the print and inversely proportional to the corridor's
foot traffic. This alteration includes changes to fixed structural
features: door counts along a given corridor have been recorded to
increase or decrease between successive surveys with no corresponding
construction or demolition record.

Personnel who view the print for longer than the permitted ninety
seconds report a sensation of the corridor depicted extending
laterally in their peripheral vision, and subsequently lose the
ability to accurately count the number of doors in a corridor they
are physically standing in, giving counts that are consistently
either one more or one fewer than the true number, a discrepancy
that does not resolve on recount.

{{4|ADDENDUM: in 1997, prior to the present containment procedure,
a recovered copy of SCP-4087 was incinerated under Level 4
authorization on the assessment that destroying the print would end
the effect. Structural drift consistent with SCP-4087's influence
continued to be recorded in the corridor nearest the incineration
site for the following six weeks, at a rate higher than had been
observed while the print existed intact. The practice of destroying
recovered copies has been discontinued.|}}

INCIDENT LOG 4087-C:
A fourth reproduction, previously unlisted, was identified in 2019
when structural drift matching SCP-4087's signature was recorded in
a corridor of an unrelated municipal building six hundred kilometres
from Site-19, with no known chain of custody linking the location
to any Foundation holding. The reproduction was recovered. Its
existence prior to discovery cannot be accounted for; the building's
records show no photograph matching SCP-4087 was ever logged,
photographed, framed, or hung on the wall where it was found. Staff
at the municipal building, when interviewed, consistently described
the photograph as having 'always been there.'

SCP-4088.name: Frequency 40.6
SCP-4088.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A dedicated monitoring station at Site-19 continuously scans the
40.6 MHz shortwave band. All Foundation personnel with Level 2
clearance or higher are enrolled in the Frequency 40.6 Notification
Protocol; monitoring staff who detect a broadcast are to immediately
record it in full and are not to state aloud whether a listed
employee's name is mentioned. Broadcasts are reviewed only by
personnel not named within them. Any employee whose name is
identified in a broadcast is not to be informed of this fact under
any circumstance; the employee's file is instead flagged for
discreet monitoring under Protocol WAITING-ROOM.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4088 is a recurring shortwave broadcast occurring at irregular
intervals on 40.6 MHz, a frequency with no registered civilian,
military, or amateur allocation. Broadcasts last between four and
nine minutes and consist of a single calm, unaccented voice of
indeterminate gender addressing a named listener in the second
person.

The broadcast describes, in blandly specific terms, events in the
named individual's near future — an argument, a diagnosis, a change
of employment, a minor accident — before concluding with a
specific date, an approximate time, and a brief, unemotional
description of the manner of the named individual's death. The
broadcast then cuts to static for a fixed nineteen seconds before
ending.

Of sixty-one confirmed instances in which a Foundation employee's
name was broadcast and identified through monitoring, fifty-seven
subjects died within six hours of the stated time in a manner
consistent with the broadcast's description, despite no subject
ever being informed of the prediction. Cause of death in these
cases has in thirty-one instances been ruled, independently of any
knowledge of SCP-4088, as unavoidable given information available
only after death.

{{3|ADDENDUM: four subjects did not die as predicted. All four
share no identified commonality in role, health, or location.
Protocol WAITING-ROOM has been quietly extended to indefinite
duration for these four employees on the theory that the discrepancy
may be temporary rather than permanent.|}}

INTERVIEW EXCERPT: the following interview was conducted with
Researcher Solano, one of the four subjects named above, eleven
months after her name was broadcast, with Researcher Solano unaware
of her own status as a subject and believing the interview
concerned an unrelated audio-analysis project.

Dr. Petrov: Do you sleep well?
Solano: Some nights. Why.
Dr. Petrov: Do you ever feel you're waiting for something you
can't name.
Solano: (long pause) That's a strange thing to ask a person.
Dr. Petrov: Answer isn't required.
Solano: Then, yes. I do.

The interview was terminated at this point per standing instruction.
Researcher Solano remains an active Site-19 employee.

SCP-4089.name: Aquarium.exe
SCP-4089.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4089 is to be run continuously on a single isolated,
network-disconnected workstation in Site-19 Software Archive, Room
 C-4. A feeding log is maintained beside the workstation. On-duty
Software Archive technicians are assigned in rotation to open
SCP-4089's interface and select the 'Feed' icon at least once every
twenty-four hours; this action must not be missed for longer than
forty-eight consecutive hours under any circumstance. No personnel
are to allow SCP-4089 to run on any device intended for their
personal or continued use.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4089 is a screensaver application, file size 1.4 megabytes,
distributed on a 3.5-inch floppy disk labeled 'AQUARIUM DEMO v1.2'
and consistent in code structure with shareware screensaver
utilities common between 1994 and 1998. When run, it displays a
simple animated aquarium containing between four and seven fish of
an unidentified, non-photorealistic design, alongside a small
'Feed' icon in the lower right corner of the screen.

SCP-4089 does not exhibit anomalous properties for approximately
the first thirty days of continuous, uninterrupted runtime. Beyond
this threshold, the individual operating the host machine — defined
as the person who most recently interacted with the 'Feed' icon, or,
in its absence, the machine's registered primary user — begins to
report a persistent sensation of hunger that is not relieved by
eating and does not correspond to any measurable metabolic deficit.

This sensation resolves within minutes of the affected individual
clicking SCP-4089's 'Feed' icon, regardless of whether the
individual is aware of SCP-4089's anomalous status. It recurs
approximately every twenty-four hours thereafter for as long as the
program continues to run. Subjects who are prevented from feeding
SCP-4089 for longer than seventy-two hours report the hunger
sensation as distressing but not medically significant; no case of
lasting physical harm has been recorded.

SCP-4089 was recovered in 2016 from the estate of a private
individual found deceased of unrelated natural causes, whose
computer had run the program continuously, according to system
logs, for eleven years. Neighbours interviewed independently
described the individual as keeping to a strict daily schedule that
included, at the same time each morning, what they assumed was
feeding a household pet, though no living pet was found on the
premises.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We have not identified any benefit to letting
SCP-4089 lapse. It does not escalate, spread, or resist
containment. It only, eventually, needs to be fed, and someone,
eventually, needs to be the one who remembers. — Researcher Okafor,
Software Archive

SCP-4090.name: One More Try
SCP-4090.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4090 is stored in a Faraday-shielded case in Site-19 Hardware
Archive. All testing is conducted via a remote input rig: a
servo-driven controller operated by researchers from an adjoining
room, with the console and display isolated behind reinforced glass.
No human subject is permitted to hold SCP-4090's controller
directly. Testing is limited to a single life per session; the
session is terminated immediately upon the first death screen, and
the cartridge is powered down for no less than six hours before any
further use.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4090 is an unlicensed cartridge, compatible with a common
late-1980s home game console, containing a side-scrolling platform
game of standard construction with no publisher information, credits
screen, or copyright notice. The game is, by design or otherwise,
extremely difficult; no test session using the remote rig has
progressed past what internal level-counting suggests is the fourth
of an unknown total number of stages.

Upon a player-character's death, SCP-4090 displays a standard
'GAME OVER' screen for four seconds before returning to the title
screen. Beginning with a player's third death within a given
testing relationship with the cartridge — deaths do not reset
between sessions — the death screen additionally displays a single
line of text beneath the standard message, stating a true, specific
fact about the individual currently operating the controller: a
full name, a home address, a childhood scar, a named fear. No
external data connection exists between SCP-4090 and any Foundation
network or personnel database.

Each subsequent death within the same testing relationship
produces a new fact, escalating in specificity and, per available
assessment, in relevance to how the individual might plausibly die.
Testing protocol now mandates rotation of operating personnel after
every second death for this reason.

{{4|ADDENDUM: prior to the current remote-rig protocol, two D-class
personnel operating SCP-4090 by hand reached death counts of
nine and twelve respectively before testing was halted. Both
died within the following month, in circumstances matching the
final death-screen fact displayed to each: D-7745 of a fall
consistent with the described scar's original injury, D-7746 in a
manner the surviving log entry declines to specify further than
'as displayed.' Direct controller contact by any subject is no
longer authorized under any protocol.|}}

TEST LOG 4090-9, remote rig, Researcher Chowdhury operating:
Death 1: standard screen only.
Death 2: standard screen only.
Death 3: additional line reads operator's full legal name.
Death 4: additional line reads operator's current commute route.
Operator rotated per protocol prior to death 5. Session terminated.
Cartridge unplugged for mandatory cooldown.

One known cartridge remains unaccounted for, believed sold as an
unlabeled item at a flea market in 1991 prior to Foundation
discovery of SCP-4090's properties.

SCP-4091.name: The Congregation
SCP-4091.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4091 is housed in Site-19 Art Storage, Vault 3, facing the wall.
Any approved viewing is limited to forty-five seconds and is to be
timed by a second observer who does not look at the painting
directly. Photographic and mirrored observation of SCP-4091 is
prohibited. Following any viewing, the viewing subject's face is to
be photographed and compared against their personnel file image;
any subject for whom this comparison cannot be completed is to be
quarantined immediately under Protocol MIRROR-BLANK.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4091 is an oil-on-canvas painting, dimensions 140 by 95
centimetres, executed in a style consistent with the mid-nineteenth
century, unsigned. It depicts a seated crowd of approximately forty
individuals arranged in rows within an unadorned hall resembling a
chapel or meeting house. Every figure's face is rendered as a
smooth, featureless oval, painted with the same care and shading
given to the surrounding hair, clothing, and posture, such that the
blankness appears deliberate rather than unfinished.

A subject who views SCP-4091 for longer than sixty seconds
cumulative will, within the following hour, find their own face
absent from any mirror or photograph taken of them, replaced by a
smooth featureless surface consistent with the painting's figures.
Other observers looking directly at the affected subject continue
to see their face normally; the effect is confined to reflected and
recorded images.

During the same window, one previously blank figure within SCP-4091
begins to display, at first faintly, the suggestion of a human
face. Repeated viewing sessions by the same affected subject cause
this suggestion to sharpen. In the two fully documented cases in
which a subject's exposure was not interrupted, the figure's face
became a complete and recognizable likeness of the subject at the
same time the subject's own face permanently ceased to register in
any mirror, camera, or optical recording device, with no effect on
the subject's face as seen by the unaided eye of another person
present in the room.

{{4|ADDENDUM: the number of figures in SCP-4091 has never been
observed to increase. Each newly resolved face occupies a
previously blank position; none has ever been observed to occupy a
position already resolved. It follows that the painting's capacity
is fixed at approximately forty, and that whoever first commissioned,
posed for, or painted it did so with that number already assumed to
be sufficient, which raises the unresolved question of whom the
first resolved figure — attested in restoration notes to have
existed before Foundation acquisition — was.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We no longer keep a group photograph of the
containment team on file. We tried, twice, and both times the same
person was missing from the print without anyone present at the
session able to say who. — Dr. Ferro, Art Storage

SCP-4092.name: Wish You Were Here
SCP-4092.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4092 is stored in a sealed archival sleeve in Site-19 Document
Archive. Personnel are not to handle SCP-4092 while consciously
thinking of a specific named individual. Handling is restricted to
gloved personnel during scheduled inspection only, conducted by a
single researcher reciting a neutral counting sequence aloud
throughout the inspection to occupy conscious attention. SCP-4092
is not to be mailed, copied, photographed for public reference, or
placed within reach of visiting personnel.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4092 is a standard postcard, 10 by 15 centimetres, printed on
one side with a colour photograph of a seaside town identified in
small type as 'Port Verrin.' No town by this name appears on any
current or historical map, gazetteer, or postal directory consulted.
The reverse is blank card stock with a pre-printed postage indicium
of an unidentified issuing authority.

Any individual holding SCP-4092 while thinking clearly of a
specific named person experiences a strong, non-compulsive-in-onset
but rapidly escalating urge to write a short message on the blank
side and mail the card. If mailed through any postal system, or
simply released from the holder's possession with an address-
intent in mind, SCP-4092 reliably reaches the named individual
within three to five days regardless of whether a correct or any
address was written, and regardless of the physical distance
involved.

The recipient, upon reading the card, reports a persistent, low-
level desire to visit Port Verrin, typically described as similar
to homesickness for a place never visited. This desire does not
resolve with time and has in four documented cases prior to
Foundation containment led the recipient to relocate nearer to
whichever coastal region they personally associated with the
photograph, no two recipients choosing the same real location.

SCP-4092 was recovered by the Foundation after tracing a chain of
eleven forwarded postcards across three countries, in which each
recipient, upon reading the card, was subsequently documented
writing and sending it onward to a new named individual of their
own acquaintance, the physical card in each case confirmed via
serial imperfections in the print to be the same object.

The card shows no measurable wear consistent with its documented
handling over more than three decades; edges, corners, and print
quality remain unchanged across every recovered instance in the
traced chain.

ADDENDUM: SCP-4092 has never been observed to affect anyone who
reads it without having handled it, and photographs of its printed
side, when viewed by personnel who have not held the physical card,
produce no effect. Containment therefore focuses entirely on
restricting physical contact, not viewing.

SCP-4093.name: Civil Defense Filmstrip 12
SCP-4093.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4093 is stored disassembled: the film reel, projector bulb, and
sound drum are held in three separate secure lockers in Site-19
Film Archive, each requiring independent Level 3 authorization to
withdraw. Reassembly for testing requires the sign-off of two
researchers and the presence of a Tactical Response team positioned
outside the projection room for the duration of any screening.
Any testing subject is restrained by non-vocal, non-speaking
personnel only prior to and during screening.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4093 is a sixteen-millimeter educational film, running time
nine minutes forty seconds, presenting itself via title card as
'CIVIL DEFENSE FILMSTRIP 12: IN THE EVENT.' It is narrated on-screen
by an adult male actor in a grey suit, address unrecorded, speaking
in a calm, instructive tone consistent with period civil-defense
material of the 1950s.

Any subject who views SCP-4093 to completion enters a state, lasting
between four and six hours, of unconditional behavioral compliance
with any verbal instruction delivered by a person exhibiting a
sufficiently similar vocal register and calm, instructive affect —
not limited to the narrator himself, and not limited to instructions
resembling those given in the film. Compliance has been observed to
extend to instructions given by individuals with no knowledge of
SCP-4093 or the affected subject's state, provided the tone is
matched.

The final ninety seconds of SCP-4093 consist of a sequence not
present in the earliest catalogued print recovered by the
Foundation in 1974; a splice line is visible at the transition, and
no corresponding excised footage or outtake has been located in any
searched archive. This later sequence instructs the viewer, in the
same calm register as the rest of the film, to disable a series of
ordinary household safety measures — a smoke detector, a stair
railing, a stove's automatic shutoff — framed as routine
maintenance advice.

{{4|ADDENDUM: the splice is of a film stock consistent with
manufacture no earlier than 1988, meaning the added sequence was
physically inserted into the reel at least thirty years after the
film's apparent original production, by a means and at a time the
Foundation has not been able to determine, without the reel leaving
secure storage according to every available chain-of-custody
record.|}}

INCIDENT LOG 4093-2:
In 1996, a duplicate broadcast master of SCP-4093, source unknown,
aired without Foundation knowledge as part of a UHF station's
overnight programming of donated 'vintage educational reels.' Local
emergency services subsequently logged a forty-one percent spike in
reported household accidents involving disabled smoke detectors and
removed stair railings within the broadcast region over the
following week. The incident was resolved through Foundation
intervention and publicly attributed to a manufacturing recall of an
unrelated safety product. The broadcast master has not been
recovered.

SCP-4094.name: Sleep, Little One
SCP-4094.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4094 is stored in a sound-dampened case in Site-19 Audio
Archive. Playback is prohibited within one hundred metres of any
minor under twenty-four months of age, Foundation-affiliated or
otherwise. Testing involving infant subjects requires Ethics
Committee approval on a per-session basis and is limited to a
single five-minute playback per subject, with a minimum ninety-day
interval between sessions for any individual subject.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4094 is a 45-rpm vinyl single, privately pressed, with no label,
catalogue number, or performer credit on either the disc or its
plain paper sleeve. Playback produces a lullaby, approximately
three minutes in length, sung in a language identified by Foundation
linguists as containing structural features of at least three
unrelated language families, performed by an unidentified adult
female voice with no accompanying instrumentation.

When SCP-4094 is played within audible range of a sleeping subject
under twenty-four months of age, the ambient surfaces of the room —
walls, furniture, and fixtures — begin to resonate, first below and
then within the range of human hearing, producing vocalizations
described consistently by adult observers as wordless but clearly
expressive, and matching in emotional register what the subject's
recorded eye movement and heart rate data suggest is the content of
the subject's dream at that moment. Observers uniformly describe the
effect as the room appearing to hum what the infant is dreaming.

Repeated exposure, defined as five or more sessions, produces
measurable divergence between the subject's apparent cognitive
development and physical development. Affected subjects have
exhibited complex, grammatically unusual vocabulary and markedly
formal affect at ages where neither would ordinarily be expected,
without corresponding advancement in motor development, growth
rate, or any other physically measurable marker, producing a
widening and clinically concerning mismatch the longer exposure
continues.

SCP-4094 was recovered from the estate of a single parent following
an unrelated welfare inquiry. She reported that the record, found
among inherited belongings, had 'helped him sleep through anything'
from his first weeks, and did not report the resonance effect as
unusual, describing it instead as 'the house settling.' Her son,
subsequently examined by Foundation medical staff at nine months of
age, was found to speak in complete, unusually formal sentences and
could not be induced to babble or vocalize in any manner typical for
his measured physical age.

ADDENDUM: the subject and his mother were relocated and placed
under a standard long-term monitoring arrangement. SCP-4094 has not
been played in his presence since recovery. No reversal of the
developmental divergence has been observed to date.

SCP-4095.name: The Very Good Boy
SCP-4095.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4095 is stored in Site-19 Document Archive. Use of SCP-4095 in
approved therapeutic or research contexts is limited to a maximum
of six readings per individual child subject, tracked in a
dedicated log; this threshold is not to be exceeded under any
circumstance, including well-intentioned use by attending
personnel. Requests for use in Foundation family-support programs
require Ethics Committee sign-off and disclosure of the six-reading
limit to the requesting guardian, though not of the reason for it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4095 is a thirty-two page illustrated children's book, self-
published appearance, no ISBN, no printer's mark, title page reading
only 'The Very Good Boy.' The book concerns an unnamed dog that
'waits by the door for you' through various simple, warmly
illustrated scenes of a child's day.

When SCP-4095 is read aloud to a child under approximately seven
years of age, that child — and only that child, not the reader or
other children present — intermittently perceives an actual dog
present in the room: calm, silent, well-behaved, matching no
specific breed description and varying slightly between child
subjects in size and colouring. The dog is not visible to adults or
other children and produces no measurable physical trace. Child
subjects across documented cases, including several in bereavement
or trauma-adjacent contexts, describe the dog's presence as calming
and have shown measurable reduction in reported distress following
sessions.

Beyond six readings to the same child, the perceived dog ceases to
be intermittent. Affected children report the dog as continuously
present from that point onward, including while alone, and
specifically describe it as watching from doorways rather than
approaching. This perception has been confirmed to persist,
unchanged in description, into adulthood in the one long-term case
available to the Foundation, with no report of harm and no known
method of ending the perception once the threshold is crossed.

A physical copy of SCP-4095 that has produced this permanent effect
in a given child will, for that child specifically, appear to have
blank pages if the child attempts to read it again as an adult; the
same physical copy shows normal printed content to any other reader,
including the same child's own children.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: Subject 4095-1, now an adult and long since
discharged from monitoring, still keeps a bowl of water by her back
door. She has told us this is out of habit and declined to discuss
it further. We have not pressed. — Researcher Hale

SCP-4096.name: You Have Reached—
SCP-4096.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4096 is stored disconnected from any power source in Site-19
Audio Archive, Cold Room 1. Testing requires the unit be connected
to an isolated power supply with no telephone line attached. Each
subject is permitted a single supervised listen of the outgoing
message only, followed by mandatory disconnection of SCP-4096's
power supply. Subjects are scheduled for a psychological follow-up
at twenty-four hours, seven days, and thirty days post-exposure. No
subject is to be permitted a second listen under any circumstance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4096 is a microcassette answering machine of a model
discontinued in 1991, recovered from a storage unit whose contents
had gone unclaimed for six years. The unit has no functioning
telephone line connection and, per internal inspection, no physical
ring-detection circuit; it cannot receive calls by any conventional
means.

When the unit's playback button is pressed to review its outgoing
message, the listener does not hear the pre-recorded greeting.
Instead, they hear a message, between thirty seconds and two
minutes in length, delivered in the voice of a specific deceased or
estranged person known personally to that listener, addressing them
by name and referencing shared, verifiable private history. No two
subjects have reported hearing the same voice or content. SCP-4096
contains no data storage medium capable of holding subject-specific
audio content, and no mechanism by which it could identify a
listener prior to playback has been found.

The message concludes with a single tone, consistent in pitch and
duration across all recorded instances, resembling the callback
prompt of period answering-machine equipment. Subjects exposed to
the message consistently attempt, without prompting, to trigger it
again, repeatedly pressing playback, and in six documented cases
attempted to speak into the unit's built-in microphone, which
internal testing confirms is non-functional and has been since
before Foundation acquisition. No case has produced evidence that
the source of the message can perceive or respond to a subject's
reply.

Subjects who are prevented from further interaction report a
persistent urge to remain near any telephone equipment for several
days following exposure, gradually diminishing without
intervention. No corresponding line item for the unit's original
purchase has been located in the storage facility's billing
records. No subject has requested amnesticisation following
exposure; several have specifically declined it when offered.

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: I asked D-8891 afterward if he'd tell me who it
was. He said no, and that he understood now why nobody who'd heard
it ever wrote it down. I have not asked another subject since. —
Dr. Nakashima

SCP-4097.name: Welcome to Meridian
SCP-4097.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4097 is stored on an air-gapped storage device in Site-19
Software Archive, never to be connected to any network, printer, or
secondary storage device. Viewing is permitted only on a single
dedicated, disposable terminal reserved solely for SCP-4097, to be
physically destroyed and replaced after each viewing session
regardless of outcome. Any personnel record, resume, or reference
document belonging to a subject who has viewed SCP-4097 in full is
to be flagged and cross-checked monthly against baseline copies
held in a separate, disconnected archive.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4097 is a forty-three slide digital presentation file in a
proprietary format not matching any commercial software the
Foundation has identified, recovered from a laptop of unknown prior
ownership. The presentation is a corporate onboarding deck for a
company identified throughout as 'Meridian Logistics,' including a
mission statement, an organizational chart, and photographs of an
office space and personnel. No business registration, tax record,
property lease, or employment record corroborating Meridian
Logistics' existence has been located by Foundation researchers in
any jurisdiction searched.

A subject who views all forty-three slides in sequence will, within
twenty-four hours, acquire a set of detailed false memories of
having been employed at Meridian Logistics for a period matching
the tenure implied by the slide deck, typically between two and
seven years. These memories displace a corresponding portion of the
subject's genuine employment history, which the subject can no
longer accurately recall.

Unlike comparable memory-altering media on record, SCP-4097's effect
is not confined to the viewing subject's memory. Documents the
subject subsequently creates, edits, or has legitimate access to —
resumes, reference letters, internal personnel databases, even the
recollections of coworkers interviewed about the subject's career —
have in documented cases begun to independently corroborate the
false employment history, with no identified mechanism and no
single point of alteration researchers have been able to isolate
and reverse.

{{4|ADDENDUM: SCP-4097 was recovered from a subject who reported
receiving it as a 'team-building exercise' forwarded from a
colleague. The colleague, when traced, reported the same, naming a
third colleague, who named a fourth. The chain has been traced back
nine forwards and has not yet reached an originating sender. The
number of external, non-Foundation hosts who have viewed SCP-4097
in full is unknown and is assessed to be substantially larger than
nine.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We pulled Subject 4097-4's real resume from
archive backup before exposure. It now reads identically to her
post-exposure version, backup and all. We are no longer confident
the backup is where we think it is. — Dr. Suzuki, Software Archive

SCP-4098.name: 37 Across
SCP-4098.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All print and digital publications flagged by the Foundation's
standing media-scan contract are checked against the SCP-4098 grid
fingerprint prior to public release; any match is intercepted and
replaced with a standard filler puzzle before distribution. Any
copy of SCP-4098 recovered is stored in Site-19 Document Archive.
Approved research use is limited to Class-D personnel completing
clues under direct supervision, or to controlled sessions in which
a researcher deliberately fills incorrect but grid-valid answers to
study the substitution effect; correct completion by non-expendable
personnel is not authorized.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4098 is a standard fifteen-by-fifteen crossword puzzle grid that
has appeared, with identical clue numbering and grid structure but
attributed to different named puzzle setters and published in
unrelated newspapers and puzzle magazines, on at least fourteen
documented occasions across six decades. Clue wording varies
slightly between appearances; the grid's black-square pattern does
not.

A solver who writes a correct answer into any clue position
immediately and involuntarily recalls a true, verifiable, but
trivial fact tangentially related to the clue's subject matter,
experienced as an ordinary act of remembering rather than as new
information. This effect has been confirmed harmless in isolation
and poses the primary research interest in SCP-4098's containment.

A solver who writes an incorrect answer that nonetheless satisfies
the grid's letter constraints — a wrong but structurally valid
word — undergoes an involuntary replacement of one genuine personal
memory with a false memory thematically consistent with the
incorrect answer. The solver does not notice the substitution
occurring and, when later questioned, defends the false memory with
the same confidence given to any genuine one. The specific clue
position '37 Across' has produced this effect in one hundred percent
of tested incorrect completions, more reliably than any other
position in the grid, for reasons not currently understood.

TEST LOG 4098-11:
D-8802 was issued a controlled copy of SCP-4098 with instruction to
deliberately enter the incorrect but grid-valid answer 'ANCHOR' at
position 37 Across, clue reading 'A place one returns to.' Correct
solution, per the puzzle's own later-recovered answer key, is
'HOMETOWN.'

Following completion, D-8802 was asked to describe his hometown. He
described, in specific and consistent detail across two follow-up
interviews one week apart, growing up aboard a fishing vessel that
Foundation records confirm he has never set foot on. When shown a
photograph of his actual, verified childhood home, D-8802 identified
it as 'somebody else's house, I think we visited once.'

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: We do not yet know what fills the space of the
memory that ANCHOR replaced. D-8802 was not asked, and given the
results so far, we are not inclined to. — Dr. Lindqvist

SCP-4099.name: Ever-Fresh
SCP-4099.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation-monitored broadcast infrastructure continuously scans
for SCP-4099's audio-visual signature across licensed and unlicensed
television transmission. Any confirmed broadcast is interrupted at
the source within ninety seconds where technically feasible, and
affected stations are issued a standard 'technical difficulties'
cover notice. Any individual reporting having seen SCP-4099 is to
be interviewed within forty-eight hours and, if found to possess
any sealed container prepared during or after viewing, that
container and its contents are to be recovered and incinerated
unopened.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4099 is a television commercial, forty-six seconds in length,
produced in a visual and editing style consistent with regional
United States broadcast advertising of the early-to-mid 1980s. It
advertises a product called 'Ever-Fresh Preserving Jars,' claiming
the jars 'keep anything fresh, forever,' shown via a demonstration
sequence of ordinary food items sealed and later opened apparently
unspoiled. No company, trademark registration, or product
matching Ever-Fresh Preserving Jars has ever been identified in any
manufacturing, advertising, or retail record searched.

SCP-4099 does not appear to be transmitted from a fixed, locatable
source. It has been confirmed airing during dead air and test-
pattern periods on at least nineteen unconnected broadcast stations
across four decades, with no two incidents traced to a shared
master tape, uplink, or personnel.

Viewers who watch SCP-4099 in full report a strong compulsion to
acquire Ever-Fresh Preserving Jars specifically, which cannot be
fulfilled, as no such product exists to purchase. In documented
cases, affected individuals have substituted ordinary glass jars,
beginning with preserving food items without any preservative,
brine, or sealing method beyond a standard lid, and escalating in
