several cases to sealing personal effects and, in six confirmed
incidents, small living animals, sealed dry with no puncture for
airflow.

Of jars prepared under SCP-4099's compulsion and later recovered
by the Foundation, a statistically significant proportion have been
found, upon later inspection, to contain contents in a state of
preservation inconsistent with the absence of any preservative
method, including the six animal incidents, in which contents were
found clinically alive despite sealed duration exceeding the known
survival time for the species and container volume involved. This
effect has not been reproduced under controlled conditions using
jars sealed by unaffected personnel using an identical procedure.

INCIDENT LOG 4099-7:
A jar recovered from Subject 4099-14's residence, sealed under
compulsion eleven days prior to recovery and containing a garden
snail with no food, water, or air access provided, was found upon
opening to contain a snail assessed by veterinary staff as healthy.
Subject 4099-14, when interviewed, could not explain why she had
chosen the snail specifically, only that 'it seemed like it would
keep well.'

SCP-4100.name: Symphony in Absence
SCP-4100.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4100 is stored in Site-19 Audio Archive in a lead-lined,
sound-isolated vault. Playback is prohibited except under direct
O5 Council authorization. Where authorized, playback is restricted
to no more than two listeners present in any acoustically
continuous space, with listeners physically separated by no less
than twenty metres and unable to see or hear one another during
playback. Foundation media-monitoring assets are tasked with
identifying any of the symphony's four movements circulating
outside Foundation custody; two such fragments are confirmed extant
and unrecovered as of this writing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4100 is a reel-to-reel magnetic tape recording, forty-one
minutes in length, of an orchestral performance attributed on its
label to the '[REDACTED] State Philharmonic,' an ensemble with no
corroborated existence in any national or regional performance
record. The recording was obtained by the Foundation in 1988 from a
private collector who stated it had been broadcast once, in full,
via shortwave radio in 1962, and never again by any station he was
aware of.

Musicological analysis of the recording's texture indicates passages
requiring a minimum of two hundred and ten distinct simultaneous
string voices, a number exceeding the seating capacity of any
concert hall matching the recording's acoustic signature, and no
documented orchestra of the era fielded a string section
approaching this size.

SCP-4100's primary anomalous property manifests only when the
recording is heard by three or more individuals within the same
acoustically continuous space. Under this condition, all listeners
present report, simultaneously and without prior collaboration, an
identical and highly specific hallucinatory vision: an unnamed
coastal city, its skyline described consistently down to the number
and arrangement of specific structures, going dark in a fixed,
repeatable sequence beginning at its harbour and ending at what
listeners uniformly describe as a tower at the city's centre.
Listeners who have never met, tested independently on different
continents, have produced matching sketches of the vision accurate
to the placement of individual windows.

A single listener, or listeners unable to hear one another, report
only a generalized sense of unease and no shared visual content.
The effect therefore requires plurality and acoustic proximity, not
mere exposure, a property unique among cross-referenced Foundation
media holdings.

{{4|ADDENDUM: SCP-4100 is understood to be a partial recording of a
larger work. Two additional fragments, apparently corresponding to
separate movements of the same symphony, have surfaced independently
since the 1962 broadcast — one recovered from a defunct radio
archive in 2003, one purchased at an estate sale in 2017 — neither
traceable to any Foundation holding or to each other. It is not
known how many movements the complete work contains, nor what
effect, if any, would result from three or more listeners hearing
all movements played in sequence. No attempt to assemble a complete
performance has been authorized.|}}

RESEARCHER'S NOTE: Every listener asked to draw the tower afterward
draws it the same way, down to a window that is dark while every
other window in the sketch is lit. Nobody has been able to tell us
why that one window, specifically. — Dr. Bauer, Audio Archive

SCP-4101.name: The Relay Stopwatch
SCP-4101.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4101 is stored powered down in a padded steel case in Site-19's Safe-class object annex. The case may only be opened by personnel with Level 2 clearance or higher, and SCP-4101 may not be run for any duration exceeding sixty (60) minutes without the written authorization of the assigned Task Force Lead. All testing involving SCP-4101 requires the presence of a staff physician and a chronometry specialist for the full duration of the test, regardless of how that duration is experienced by the test subject.
Personnel who have operated SCP-4101 are subject to a mandatory psychological debrief within twenty-four hours of the stopwatch being stopped.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4101 is a handheld analog chronograph stopwatch of a design commercially available in the United States between approximately 1965 and 1978: a chrome case on a woven lanyard, a white dial marked in fifths of a second, and two spring-loaded plunger buttons for start/stop and lap/reset. SCP-4101 does not respond to metallurgical, radiographic, or magnetic analysis in any way that distinguishes it from a mundane stopwatch of the same make. Its anomalous effect is behavioral rather than physical and manifests only when the start plunger is depressed by a human hand and the stopwatch is held or worn continuously by that same person until it is stopped.

Once started, SCP-4101 counts up normally, audible in its mechanical ticking to all observers, and its internal mechanism can be independently verified to be advancing. However, the individual who started it (designated the "operator") experiences no passage of subjective time between depressing the plunger and depressing it again to stop, regardless of the elapsed duration, up to a documented maximum of nine days, fourteen hours. The operator reports the interval as instantaneous — a single unbroken moment — and retains no memories, dreams, or sensory impressions from within it. Electroencephalography performed on operators during SCP-4101 tests shows continuous, unremarkable waking brain activity for the entire elapsed duration; operators are, by every external measure, awake, mobile, and responsive during this period, and in the majority of trials continue routine tasks (walking, giving instructions, recording splits for other timed athletes) without any behavioral indication of anomaly. They simply do not remember doing so, and afterward describe the return of memory as indistinguishable from blinking.

Non-operators in the vicinity of a running SCP-4101 — including other individuals who could, in principle, have started it themselves — experience the interval normally in every respect.

SCP-4101 was recovered from the athletics equipment room of ████████ High School, ██████, Ohio, following a report submitted to a local field agent by an assistant swim coach who stated that the head coach had "gone somewhere" for what she insisted was four hours during a single timed practice, despite having continued to call splits, adjust lane assignments, and supervise the pool deck competently throughout, and having no memory of doing so afterward. The coach in question has since been administered a standard amnestic and relocated.

ADDENDUM 4101-1: On ██/██/2019, Researcher Voss started SCP-4101 for the maximum tested duration at that time (six hours) during an overnight monitoring shift, citing boredom, in violation of protocol requiring pre-authorization above thirty minutes. During the six-hour interval, Junior Researcher Adaeze Okoro, stationed in an unrelated wing of the site, died as the result of a containment breach unrelated to SCP-4101. Voss was informed of Okoro's death upon stopping the watch and, per his own account, experienced this as the first event to occur after depressing the plunger — he did not report the six-hour gap as absent, but stated, unprompted and before being told how much time had passed, that he had been "dreaming, the whole time, about the lap not being over yet." No dream content beyond this was recovered. Voss has since requested reassignment away from further contact with SCP-4101. The request was granted.

SCP-4102.name: The Filing Cabinet
SCP-4102.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4102 is secured in Vault C-12 of the Site-19 document annex, positioned against a reinforced interior wall with no adjoining structure on the opposite side. The cabinet's three functional drawers are to remain closed and sealed with numbered tamper tape when not in active use. Use of SCP-4102 requires the written approval of a standing three-member sub-committee (rotating membership, Level 3 minimum) and is logged in the Continuity Ledger, a physical document maintained independently of SCP-4102's own effects for the purpose of cross-referencing known reality against its alterations.
No document may be placed in SCP-4102 without prior review by the Department of Analysis for downstream legal, genealogical, or jurisdictional consequences. A minimum six-month waiting period is required between any two uses affecting overlapping record systems (e.g., the same county, the same family line).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4102 is a four-drawer, gray-enameled steel filing cabinet of a type manufactured for municipal government use between 1940 and 1965. Of its four drawers, only the top three open; the bottom drawer is fused shut at the seams in a manner consistent with the metal having been welded, though no welding is externally visible and the cabinet's provenance includes no record of such work being performed.

When a document is placed in one of SCP-4102's functional drawers and the drawer is closed for a period of no less than twenty-four hours, the document is retroactively incorporated into the official record of the institution to which it pertains, as though it had been filed through ordinary process at the time of its nominal date. This incorporation extends outward through the surrounding documentary and institutional record — related files are updated, cross-referenced entries appear in indices that predate SCP-4102's discovery, and the memories of institutional personnel (clerks, officials, and record-keepers acting in their professional capacity) adjust to reflect having processed the document at the appropriate time.

Critically, SCP-4102's effect is confined to institutional record and institutional memory. It does not alter the direct, personal recollection of individuals regarding events they experienced firsthand, nor does it alter physical reality outside the documentary chain (a fabricated deed will place a building in a person's legal ownership, but will not transport that person's furniture into it). The result, in nearly every documented use, is a period of low-grade administrative inconsistency: a landlord who has no memory of selling a property they are now, by every record, shown to have sold; a woman legally married to a man she has never met, who nonetheless has clear personal memories of her actual, unmarried life running in parallel to a marriage certificate, tax filings, and a mother-in-law's Christmas cards. These discrepancies are rarely investigated by the affected parties, who tend to defer to the paperwork over their own recollection within an average of eleven days.

SCP-4102 was recovered from the sub-basement of the ██████ County Records Annex after a records clerk used it, without knowledge of its nature, to "correct" a discrepancy in a property deed. The correction was successful. The clerk was later interviewed and reported no awareness that anything unusual had occurred; the Foundation was alerted only because the deed in question named, as the property's original 1911 grantee, a corporation that would not be legally incorporated for another sixty-three years.

ADDENDUM 4102-1: During Test 4102-07, a birth certificate was placed in the cabinet's third (functional) drawer and left for the standard interval. Upon retroactive integration, the county archive's index — not the cabinet, not the document itself — recorded the certificate as having been filed in "Drawer 4, County Annex Cabinet 11-B." No such drawer opens on SCP-4102. The index entry has not been corrected, at the Ethics Committee's standing instruction, pending further study of what, precisely, the fourth drawer files into.

SCP-4103.name: The Bathroom Scale
SCP-4103.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4103 is stored in a standard storage locker in the Site-19 Safe-object annex when not in use for testing. Because SCP-4103's anomalous effect can only be elicited once from a given individual, subjects must be pre-approved by the Ethics Committee prior to any test, and no subject may be tested against their will or without being informed, in general terms, that the object may produce a reading of a personal nature. A camera fixed above SCP-4103's dial photographs each reading in full before the subject is permitted to view it directly; the subject may then decline to look.
All readings are filed as Level 3/4103 and are not to be discussed with, or disclosed to, the subject's coworkers, family, or associates under any circumstances.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4103 is an analog bathroom scale of a common design manufactured in the early-to-mid 1970s: a chrome-edged platform, a rotating dial calibrated in kilograms from 0 to 150, and a small rectangular window above the dial that, on a mundane scale of this model, displays a manufacturer's logo plate.

SCP-4103 functions as an ordinary, accurate bathroom scale for all individuals, with one exception: the first time — and only the first time — any given individual stands on it, the needle disregards the subject's actual body weight entirely, spins for an anomalous duration of between four and thirty seconds, and settles on a number that bears no consistent relationship to mass. Simultaneously, the window above the dial, rather than showing the manufacturer's plate, displays a person's full name, rendered in the same die-stamped, backlit style as the original branding. Every subsequent use by the same individual produces a normal, non-anomalous weight reading, and the name window reverts permanently to the manufacturer's plate.

Interview of 61 test subjects to date indicates that in 54 cases (88.5%), the displayed name is identified by the subject, generally with visible distress, as a specific person — living, estranged, or deceased — from whom the subject is currently withholding a specific piece of information they have not disclosed and do not intend to. Subjects are not asked, and do not volunteer, the content of the withheld information. In the remaining 7 cases, subjects either did not recognize the name or declined to state whether they did.

The displayed number does not correspond to the subject's weight, height, age, or any tested biometric. Retrospective analysis has found that in 41 of the 54 identified cases, the number correlates closely with the elapsed duration, in some consistent but non-obvious unit (days in the majority of cases; in four cases, weeks; in one case, hours), between an identifiable point in time and the test — most often the day the secret was first formed, occasionally a later or unrelated date the subject could not explain. No further pattern in unit selection has been established.

SCP-4103 was recovered from the private office of Dr. ██████ ██████, a licensed marriage and family therapist in ███████, Texas, after a patient reported the object to local authorities, believing it to be a "trick scale" the therapist was using to manipulate patients. Dr. ██████ denied any knowledge of the object's origin or anomalous properties and has since been administered a standard amnestic.

ADDENDUM 4103-1: During Test 4103-52, Junior Researcher Priya Nair — assigned to the test as an observer, not a subject, and standing on SCP-4103 only to demonstrate its mundane operation to a new hire — received an anomalous reading. The displayed name was that of Senior Researcher Halloran, with whom Nair had no documented personal relationship. The displayed number, cross-referenced, corresponded to the exact number of days since Nair's security clearance had been elevated to include partial knowledge of Project 4103-internal, a classification whose existence had not yet been disclosed to her at the time of the test. Nair has not been informed of this correlation. The file has been sealed pending review of how SCP-4103 accessed information regarding a Foundation compartmentalization decision that had not, at the time of the reading, been committed to any document SCP-4103 could plausibly have accessed.

SCP-4104.name: The Passed-Down Locket
SCP-4104.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4104 is stored in a sealed locket case within a lined containment locker in the Site-19 Euclid-object wing. The box may only be opened using insulated tongs; direct skin contact with SCP-4104 by on-duty personnel is prohibited outside of sanctioned testing. Any accidental contact resulting in the locket being clasped around a subject's neck for longer than sixty seconds is to be treated as an involuntary test and reported immediately, as the effect cannot be reversed once initiated and the affected individual will require monitoring and, following the mandatory seven-day period, debriefing and amnesticization.
No two members of Foundation personnel with an existing romantic or familial relationship may be assigned to sequential testing of SCP-4104.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4104 is a hinged 14-karat gold locket, its inner surfaces worn smooth, bearing no maker's mark, hallmark, or engraving. Standard assay confirms the metal itself is unremarkable.

When SCP-4104 is clasped around the neck of a human subject and remains there, uninterrupted, for sixty seconds or longer, it cannot subsequently be removed by any means for a period of exactly seven days. This is SCP-4104's only directly observable physical anomaly: tools capable of cutting the chain (bolt cutters, wire cutters, lasers) pass through its apparent location without resistance and without effect, as though cutting an afterimage rather than an object, while the locket itself remains fully intact and in place around the wearer's neck. At the conclusion of the seven-day period, SCP-4104's clasp releases on its own and it may be removed normally.

During the seven-day period, the wearer (designated "current spouse") gradually acquires a complete set of autobiographical memories describing a long-term marriage to whichever individual wore SCP-4104 during the cycle immediately prior (designated "prior spouse"). These memories include a wedding, an ordinary domestic history of variable but plausible length (documented range: two to thirty-one years), specific recurring arguments, and, in eight of nineteen documented cases, memories of one or more children. The memories are internally consistent and are reported by subjects as subjectively indistinguishable from memories of their actual, factual life, which they retain in full and undamaged parallel. Subjects uniformly describe the seven-day period as acutely distressing, arising not from either set of memories individually but from the impossibility of reconciling two complete, mutually exclusive pasts.

The prior spouse is affected asymmetrically and far less severely. Over the same period, their memory of the marriage — which they themselves acquired during their own wearing cycle — does not vanish but attenuates: subjects describe it, by the fourth or fifth day, as a fact they know rather than a thing they feel, comparable to recalling a relative's divorce from before their own birth. No prior spouse has reported acute distress from this fading.

SCP-4104 was flagged for Foundation attention after a pawn shop owner in ███████, Kentucky, contacted police to report that a regular customer had attempted to file a missing-persons report for a wife the shop owner had never seen and who did not appear in any available record. Investigation traced the locket through six prior owners via pawn receipts, each of whom, when located, independently described a period of marital memory matching the pattern above.

ADDENDUM 4104-1: During Test 4104-3, D-9821 and D-9844 wore SCP-4104 in sequence seven days apart and subsequently underwent standard debriefing and amnesticization per protocol. Four months later, both subjects were independently reassigned, through unrelated scheduling, to the same custodial rotation at Site-19. Supervising staff noted an immediate and pronounced rapport between the two, escalating within three weeks to a voluntarily disclosed romantic relationship, which both subjects maintain neither can account for. Neither D-9821 nor D-9844 has been informed of their shared history with SCP-4104. The relationship has not been intervened upon and remains under passive observation.

SCP-4105.name: The Reel-to-Reel Recorder
SCP-4105.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4105 is contained in Isolation Chamber 12-Keter, a windowless room with no fixed furnishings beyond a table bolted to the floor and a single chair. The chamber's audio is continuously monitored and recorded via non-anomalous equipment as a control baseline. SCP-4105 may not be operated for any purpose other than approved research under direct O5 Command authorization, following the events of Incident 4105-Kilo (see Addendum 4105-2). Recordings produced by SCP-4105 are classified Keter-Restricted upon creation and may not be played for, summarized to, or otherwise disclosed to any individual named or plausibly identifiable within the recording's content, regardless of clearance level.
Under no circumstances is SCP-4105 to be operated inside any active containment area, crew quarters, or any location where its output could reach personnel not read into Project 4105.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4105 is a reel-to-reel magnetic tape recorder, model and manufacture consistent with commercial broadcast equipment sold in the United States circa 1966, showing moderate wear consistent with professional radio station use. It operates on standard household current and accepts standard 1/4-inch magnetic tape, which is not itself anomalous once removed from the device and can be played on any compatible equipment without further effect.

When SCP-4105 is used to record ambient audio at a given physical location, the resulting recording — upon playback, on SCP-4105 or otherwise — does not reproduce the audio captured during the recording session. Instead, it reproduces ambient audio from the same physical location at a later point in time, offset forward from the moment of recording by an interval that is not fixed but increases with each successive use of SCP-4105 at that location, following no formula yet identified (documented offsets at a single test location, in sequence: 40 seconds; 11 minutes; 6 hours; 3 days; 17 days). The offset resets if SCP-4105 is relocated to a previously unused location, beginning again from a short interval.

The recovered audio is reliably accurate to events that do subsequently occur at the recorded location, including speech, verified in 100% of controlled tests conducted to date (n=34). This reliability has made SCP-4105 attractive for predictive use; it has also produced Incident 4105-Kilo.

ADDENDUM 4105-1: SCP-4105 was recovered from WVRX, a defunct AM radio station in ██████, West Virginia, after the station's sole remaining overnight host contacted a Foundation-monitored tip line, reporting that a tape recorder in the station's equipment closet had, on three occasions, recorded him making on-air mistakes — dead air, mispronounced sponsor names, a stumbled sign-off — before he had made them. He stated that on the third occasion, having heard the recording in advance, he attempted to avoid the mistake and made a different one instead, of comparable severity, at the same point in the broadcast. This detail was not solicited and is considered significant.

ADDENDUM 4105-2 (Incident 4105-Kilo): During an authorized 96-hour test in Chamber 12, SCP-4105 produced a recording, offset by nine days, of two identifiable Foundation staff voices discussing the imminent failure of an unrelated containment procedure elsewhere on Site-19. Command elected to act on the recording and pre-emptively reinforced the referenced procedure. The reinforcement held. Nine days later, at the timestamp corresponding to the recorded conversation, the two staff members in question were recorded — by mundane means — having the conversation as predicted, discussing not the (now-prevented) original failure, but a newly emerged and unrelated containment failure of comparable severity in the same location. Command has not authorized further predictive use of SCP-4105 pending review of whether the object's recordings describe a fixed future or select, from among possible futures, whichever one is least disrupted by the act of being foreseen.

SCP-4106.name: The Hallway Mirror
SCP-4106.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4106 is stored face-in against a wall in a covered frame in the Site-19 Euclid-object annex, draped at all times with an opaque cloth cover secured by ties at all four corners. The cover may only be removed for approved testing, and removal requires two personnel: one to observe SCP-4106 and one to monitor the observer, positioned so as not to be visible in SCP-4106's reflection. No individual is to stand before an uncovered SCP-4106 for longer than five continuous minutes under any circumstances. A countdown timer audible to the observer is mandatory for all tests.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4106 is a free-standing, full-length mirror in a carved walnut frame, of a style consistent with manufacture in the early 20th century. The mirror's glass and silvering show no anomalous properties under material analysis.

SCP-4106 produces an accurate, real-time reflection of any subject and their surroundings for the first several seconds of observation. If a subject remains stationary before the mirror — motion is defined operationally as any full-body displacement exceeding 30cm — the reflection begins to lag behind the subject's real-time movements, initially by fractions of a second. This delay increases the longer the subject remains still, at a rate that is not linear and has not been successfully modeled, though it accelerates sharply after approximately ten minutes of continued stillness.

If a subject remains before SCP-4106 for a documented threshold of seventeen minutes (± 40 seconds across trials), the delayed reflection ceases to track the subject's movements at all and begins to move independently. This independent movement is not random: the reflection performs coherent, purposeful actions — walking to other points within the reflected room, sitting, in two documented cases mouthing words inaudible to observers — that do not correspond to any action taken by the subject, before, during, or after the threshold event. The subject, for their part, reports no memory of the mirror's behavior during this period and typically no awareness that unusual time has passed, similar in character (though not confirmed to be related) to reports associated with other temporally anomalous objects in Foundation custody.

In three of eleven trials permitted to reach the threshold before Ethics Committee restriction, the independent reflection subsequently walked to the edge of the mirror's frame and passed out of view, after which SCP-4106 displayed a reflection of the test chamber that did not contain the subject at all — an empty room, correctly reflecting all other stationary contents of the chamber but omitting the subject entirely, who remained visibly and verifiably present and unharmed before the glass. In all three cases, the mirror returned to producing an accurate reflection of the subject between eleven and nineteen minutes later, with no reflected re-entry observed; the subject's reflection was simply present again, mid-frame, as though it had never left.

SCP-4106 was recovered from the estate of Mrs. ██████ ██████, ███, following her death, after her live-in caretaker reported to a Foundation-monitored county welfare line that Mrs. ██████ had, on multiple occasions in her final months, been found standing motionless before the mirror for periods the caretaker estimated at "hours," and that on the final such occasion, prior to the resident's death by unrelated natural causes, the caretaker observed the reflected room to be empty for a period of roughly twenty minutes while Mrs. ██████ remained visibly present in front of the glass.

ADDENDUM 4106-1: Testing beyond the seventeen-minute threshold has been suspended by Ethics Committee order pending investigation into the destination and current status of Mrs. ██████'s reflection during the final documented instance of the effect, which — unlike all subsequent Foundation trials — has no recorded terminus.

SCP-4107.name: The Street Lamp
SCP-4107.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4107 is stored disconnected from any power source in Site-19's exterior secure yard, covered by a weatherproof tarp at all times. Its bulb is removed and stored separately, in Vault 7, under standard low-security lock. Site security performs a twice-daily visual check to confirm SCP-4107 remains dark and its bulb remains absent from the fixture. SCP-4107 may not be reconnected to power or fitted with a bulb without a standing Level 3 test authorization specifying, in advance, the personnel permitted to approach the lit circle and the maximum permitted exposure time.
The Foundation maintains passive monitoring agreements, through front organizations, with the municipalities currently possessing the 41 other identified surviving units of SCP-4107's manufacturing batch, the majority of which have been quietly decommissioned or relocated to non-functional display.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4107 is a cast-iron street lamp of a model manufactured by the ██████ Ironworks Company and sold to approximately 700 municipalities across the United States between 1958 and 1961, of which 42 units, including SCP-4107, are confirmed to survive. The lamp itself, absent power, is non-anomalous.

When lit, SCP-4107 casts a roughly circular pool of light on the ground, approximately 4.1 meters in diameter. An individual who walks into this circle and continues in a straight line to its opposite edge will, upon exiting, find themselves at the edge of the lit circle cast by a different surviving unit of the same manufacturing batch — regardless of the physical distance between the two lamps — provided that unit is, at that same moment, also lit. If no other unit of the batch is currently lit anywhere, the individual exits SCP-4107's circle normally, at the expected location, with no anomalous effect.

The specific unit to which SCP-4107 connects is not fixed. It is, in every tested instance, the unit that is geodesically nearest to SCP-4107 among all currently-lit units at the moment of crossing — meaning the network's topology changes continuously as individual lamps are lit, extinguished, decommissioned, or (in three known cases) destroyed. The Foundation's ability to contain SCP-4107 by keeping it dark does not extinguish the anomaly network at large; it only removes SCP-4107 as one of its nodes.

SCP-4107 was identified after local police in ██████, Vermont, filed a report — later flagged by a keyword-monitoring algorithm — regarding a persistent rumor among high school students that "the park lamp" could get a person to school in under a minute if you "walked all the way through the light." Two students who claimed to have used it for this purpose independently described locations and interior details of a school in ████████, Michigan — approximately 900 kilometers away — that they had no other means of knowing and which were subsequently confirmed accurate.

ADDENDUM 4107-1: On ██/██/2009, prior to Foundation containment, local resident Daniel Fitch (age 17) was documented by a since-recovered home video entering SCP-4107's lit circle and not exiting the far side. Fitch was reported missing the same night and was never recovered.
Subsequent investigation identified Fitch's probable destination as a specific lamp unit in ████████, Ohio — but determined that this unit was not installed and first illuminated at that location until 1962, three years prior to SCP-4107's own manufacture and more than fifty years before Fitch's disappearance.
In 2015, Site-19's blind postal drop received a sealed, hand-addressed letter bearing a postmark consistent with 1962, correctly routed through ordinary postal channels to an address that did not exist as a Foundation front until 1978. The letter, signed "D. Fitch," described the sender's circumstances in general but coherent terms and requested, explicitly, that "nobody come looking." Handwriting analysis found no material inconsistency with exemplars of Daniel Fitch's handwriting on file from before his disappearance. No further correspondence has been received.

SCP-4108.name: The Typewriter
SCP-4108.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4108 (the typewriter body) and SCP-4108-1 (its associated ribbon) are stored in separate vaults on non-adjacent levels of Site-19, each requiring independent two-person Level 4 authorization to access. SCP-4108 is non-anomalous without SCP-4108-1 installed and may be handled under standard object protocols in this state; SCP-4108-1 is non-functional and inert when not installed in SCP-4108.
Any authorized use of SCP-4108 with SCP-4108-1 installed requires prior review of the intended phrasing by no fewer than two staff linguists, specifically tasked with identifying ambiguity, unintended literal readings, and available low-cost interpretive pathways, followed by written authorization from an O5 Council member. Given the finite and non-replenishing length of SCP-4108-1 (current remaining length: approximately 340cm, sufficient by current estimate for 60-90 further sentences depending on length), use is restricted to circumstances of severe institutional necessity as determined by standing directive 4108-Alpha.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4108 is a manually operated typewriter of a design consistent with mass-produced office machines of the 1930s, bearing no legible manufacturer markings. It is mechanically unremarkable and, fitted with an ordinary ink ribbon, types normally with no observed anomalous effect.

SCP-4108-1 is a single, continuous ink ribbon of unidentified composition, non-replicable by any method attempted to date (Department of Analysis has ceased further attempts following Incident 4108-3, described below). When SCP-4108-1 is installed in SCP-4108, any sentence typed and subsequently removed from the machine — removal of the paper appears to be the operative trigger, not the act of typing — will be rendered true, generally within a window of minutes to several days, through whatever available sequence of events represents the least overall disruption to the current state of reality.

This last property is the source of SCP-4108's Keter classification. "Least disruption" is evaluated by the anomaly according to criteria that do not correspond to human notions of desirability or cost, and the pathway selected frequently satisfies the literal wording of the typed sentence through means the author did not intend and would not have chosen, at a cost the author did not anticipate and typically cannot undo — SCP-4108 offers no mechanism for reversal, retraction, or correction other than typing an additional, equally literal sentence, which introduces its own risk of compounding unintended consequences.

SCP-4108 and SCP-4108-1 were recovered together from the apartment of novelist ██████ ██████, ██ years old, of ████████, New York, following a welfare check requested by his literary agent after he failed to deliver a promised manuscript. The apartment was empty of its occupant; no trace of ██████ has been located to date. A single page remained in the machine.

ADDENDUM 4108-1: Departmental reconstruction of ██████'s typed pages, recovered from the apartment, establishes the following documented sequence of use, presented as an illustrative record of the object's operating principle:
Page 1 (undated, estimated 14 months prior to disappearance): "My novel will be finished and published." Result: ██████'s work-in-progress manuscript was stolen from his apartment during a burglary six weeks later; the thief, unable to sell the physical manuscript, retyped and submitted it under a pseudonym, and it was accepted for publication. ██████'s name does not appear on the published work.
Page 4: "I want credit for my own book." Result: the pseudonymous author was exposed as a plagiarist by an unrelated fact-checker eleven weeks later, in a public scandal that named ██████ as the true author — but by this time attached his name principally to the scandal itself rather than to the work, and publishers subsequently declined to work with him, citing reputational risk.
Page 9: "I want people to stop associating my name with the plagiarism scandal." Result unconfirmed; ██████'s disappearance occurred within 72 hours of this page's removal from the machine, and no further public reporting concerning either ██████ or the scandal has occurred since, despite no corroborating record of any deliberate suppression effort by any identified party.

The final page remaining in the machine at time of recovery was blank, except for a single line, left un-removed from the platen: "I want to take it all back." SCP-4108-1's current remaining length was measured against pre-incident photographs taken by the agent's assistant several months earlier; the ribbon has advanced by a length consistent with one additional sentence beyond the four already accounted for.

SCP-4109.name: The Chess Set
SCP-4109.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4109 is displayed in a climate-controlled case in the Site-19 Thaumiel-object wing and may be removed from the case only for a sanctioned game session, authorized in writing by a sitting O5 Council member and coordinated through the Office of Probability Assessment. Each session requires a "White" player drawn from Roster 4109, a standing list of Foundation personnel who have volunteered under informed consent protocol 4109-C and been cleared by both Ethics and Medical.
The White player is never informed of the specific real-world event nominated for correlation prior to or during a session. This blinding is mandatory; historical sessions in which the player was aware of the stakes showed no statistically significant correlation with the nominated outcome.
SCP-4109 itself does not leave Site-19 under any circumstance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4109 is an ornately carved chess set of 32 pieces, sixteen in a black stone-like material and sixteen in white, on a matching inlaid wooden board. Material analysis has been unable to classify the stone; it is denser than any known mineral of comparable appearance and shows no reaction to standard chemical or spectroscopic testing. Provenance research traces the set to a disbanded early-20th-century esoteric society active in Prague, dissolved in 1931 under circumstances not fully documented in recovered society records.

When a human player ("White," by fixed convention) is seated opposite the board and makes a legal opening move, the black pieces subsequently make their own legal responding moves without observed physical mechanism, at intervals ranging from approximately 40 seconds to 6 minutes. All recorded games proceed according to standard chess rules and produce a standard result: checkmate, resignation, draw, or stalemate.

Statistical analysis conducted by the Office of Probability Assessment across 214 sanctioned sessions has established a significant correlation (p < 0.0001) between the outcome of a completed game and the resolution of a specific real-world event of high uncertainty, formally nominated by O5 Command through a fixed declaratory procedure prior to each session's start. A White win correlates with favorable resolution of the nominated event; a White loss correlates with unfavorable resolution; draws and stalemates correlate with the event remaining unresolved beyond the study's observation window. The Foundation currently deploys SCP-4109 as a standing asset for nudging the resolution of otherwise unmanageable high-entropy scenarios — weather-dependent extraction operations, the containment status of volatile objects with probabilistic breach conditions, and comparable cases — accounting for its Thaumiel classification.

The mechanism by which a chess outcome correlates with an unrelated world event remains entirely theoretical. The Foundation does not claim to understand why or how SCP-4109 functions; it is deployed empirically, as an instrument whose reliability has been established without an accompanying model of its operation.

Every White player exhibits, following a completed session regardless of outcome, a small but measurable and permanent decline in an area of cognitive or motor function unrelated to the game itself — commonly fine motor precision, short-term verbal recall, or affective range. This decline is cumulative across sessions and has not been observed to reverse. Roster 4109 is rotated accordingly; to date, six personnel have been retired from the Roster after reaching a threshold decline judged incompatible with continued field or research duty, and are maintained in supported administrative roles at their own request.

ADDENDUM 4109-1: Roster candidates are briefed, prior to consent, in general clinical terms regarding "measurable cumulative cost to participating personnel of undetermined long-term severity." The Ethics Committee has on three occasions reviewed whether this briefing constitutes adequate informed consent given the Foundation's simultaneous institutional dependency on the Roster's continued willingness to volunteer, and has on three occasions declined to alter the protocol.

ADDENDUM 4109-2: On two documented occasions, SCP-4109 has been found, between scheduled sessions and inside its sealed display case, with its pieces arranged in a position consistent with an in-progress or recently concluded game that no White player initiated. In the second occurrence, the board position was subsequently matched, after the fact, to a stalemate configuration statistically associated (per the established correlation model) with an unresolved, ongoing global event that had not been nominated by O5 Command and was not, at the time the position was discovered, known to Foundation analysts to be occurring.

SCP-4110.name: The Thermos
SCP-4110.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4110 is stored empty in the Site-19 Safe-object annex when not in active testing. Personnel introducing liquid to SCP-4110 for testing purposes must complete a brief mandatory mood-state questionnaire immediately prior to pouring, logged alongside the resulting reading, to support ongoing correlation research. SCP-4110 is not to be issued for personal or recreational use by staff under any circumstances.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4110 is a steel vacuum flask (thermos) of unremarkable commercial manufacture, holding approximately 750mL, showing moderate external wear consistent with regular outdoor use.

Liquid poured into SCP-4110 does not behave thermodynamically once inside. Rather than gradually equalizing with ambient temperature as in a mundane vacuum flask, the liquid's temperature locks, within roughly ninety seconds of the lid being sealed, at a fixed value that remains constant — regardless of ambient temperature, elapsed time, or the flask's storage conditions — until the liquid is entirely removed from the flask by pouring or drinking. Liquid left inside SCP-4110 has been observed to hold its locked temperature for a documented maximum of six years, four months (ongoing at time of writing, see Addendum 4110-1) without measurable drift.

The locked temperature does not correspond to the temperature of the liquid at the moment of pouring, nor to any temperature a mundane thermos might plausibly produce. Correlational testing across 88 trials indicates the locked temperature corresponds instead to the self-reported emotional state of the individual who poured the liquid, collected via the mandatory questionnaire described above: liquids poured by subjects reporting grief, nostalgia, or unresolved longing consistently lock at a temperature at or near the liquid's initial serving temperature, regardless of how long the flask subsequently sits (i.e., they do not cool); liquids poured by subjects reporting acute fear or anxiety lock at temperatures near 4°C regardless of starting temperature, including in three trials where boiling liquid was poured by a distressed subject and measured, ninety seconds later, at 3.8°C with no observed loss of latent heat to the surrounding environment. Subjects reporting neutral or mixed mood states produce inconsistent results that do not correlate cleanly with any tested variable.

SCP-4110 was recovered from the pack of hiker Warren Aldis, found alongside his equipment in the ██████ National Forest, Colorado, following a search-and-rescue operation for Aldis and his hiking partner after the latter went missing in a storm. Aldis's partner was not recovered. Aldis's own thermos, sealed and undisturbed, was found to contain coffee measured at 71°C, consistent with a temperature at which coffee is typically served, despite an ambient recorded low of -9°C over the six days between the storm and the item's recovery. Aldis was not administered a questionnaire prior to the original pour and could not be located for follow-up; he has since declined all further contact with the Foundation.

ADDENDUM 4110-1: The 750mL of coffee recovered in SCP-4110 at the time of its acquisition has not been emptied. It remains, at time of writing, held at a constant 71°C. No test protocol currently in place requires its removal, and no researcher assigned to SCP-4110 has, to date, submitted a request to empty it.

SCP-4111.name: The Stepladder
SCP-4111.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4111 is stored folded and zip-tied shut in a standard containment locker in the Site-19 Euclid-object annex. The locker is mounted at floor level only; SCP-4111 is not to be stored, tested, or transported at any elevation above ground floor under any circumstances, per standing incident review recommendation following Test 4111-9. Any authorized ascent of SCP-4111 requires a tethered subject wearing a continuous-transmission locator harness and a two-person ground team with a physical, non-anomalous ladder of matching height staged as an immediate recovery option.
SCP-4111 may not be extended to more than four rungs under any circumstances; the object does not currently possess a fifth rung, and Department of Analysis has recommended against fabricating a replacement to test whether one would function.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4111 is a wooden folding stepladder, four rungs, of a common hardware-store design manufactured domestically and sold widely between approximately 1975 and 1995. The wood shows ordinary wear; no anomalous properties have been detected through material analysis.

An individual who climbs SCP-4111 to its top rung and then steps off in a continued upward motion — rather than stepping back down the way they climbed — does not arrive at the ceiling or elevated surface expected given the ladder's physical height and immediate surroundings. Instead, they arrive on a floor of the building in which SCP-4111 is currently standing that does not appear in that building's official architectural plans, floor numbering, or utility schematics, and is not accessible by any conventional means (stairwell, elevator, or otherwise) from within the building. This floor is, in every documented instance, physically consistent with the building's general style, period, and materials, furnished and maintained to varying degrees, and — in 6 of 14 documented ascents — showing signs of very recent human occupancy (unmade bedding, food not yet spoiled, lit but unattended light fixtures) despite no occupant ever being found present.

A second ascent of SCP-4111, performed from within one of these floors, produces access to a further floor, and so on; the Foundation has confirmed at least eleven such floors accessible in linear sequence from a single building before losing contact with the ascending test subject (see Addendum 4111-1). No subject has yet climbed back down through the sequence to ground level using SCP-4111 in reverse; all successful returns to date have occurred via subjects locating and using a conventional stairwell believed (but not confirmed) to be present on each anomalous floor, which reliably terminates at the building's actual, mundane ground floor rather than at the floor from which the subject originally ascended.

SCP-4111 was flagged for Foundation attention after an unusually high missing-persons rate was noted, via routine anomaly-statistics monitoring, at a single apartment building in ██████, Illinois: nine tenants unaccounted for over a four-year period, each having last been seen, per witness statements, "going up to fix something" with a borrowed stepladder kept in the building's shared utility closet and lent between units for household repairs. The building superintendent, interviewed under a research cover identity, provided a hand-drawn map of "floors that aren't on the blueprint," which he stated he had stopped updating after "running out of floors to draw."

ADDENDUM 4111-1: During Test 4111-9, D-11402 ascended eleven confirmed anomalous floors in sequence, maintaining voice contact throughout. At the twelfth ascent, contact was lost mid-transmission, during which D-11402 stated only: "There's a ladder up here already. It's already up. Somebody's on it." No further transmission was received. The physical, non-anomalous recovery ladder staged at ground level was not deployed, as no return point had been established above the first anomalous floor. D-11402 has not been recovered.

SCP-4112.name: The Music Box
SCP-4112.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4112 is stored in a sealed, soundproofed containment unit in Site-19's Keter-object vault, its winding key removed and stored separately under independent Level 4 lock. The containment unit is fitted with redundant, continuously monitored audio dampening sufficient to prevent SCP-4112's tune (see Description) from propagating beyond a sealed inner chamber under any foreseeable operating condition, including containment breach.
Personnel are reminded that SCP-4112's effect has been documented to propagate through accurate secondhand reproduction of its melody (humming, whistling, or instrumental replication) and not solely through direct exposure to the object. Under no circumstances is any recording, transcription, or musical notation of SCP-4112's tune to be created, retained, or transmitted, including for containment or research purposes. Personnel who believe they have been exposed, directly or secondhand, are to report immediately for the standard 4112 memory-audit interview (see Procedure 4112-Delta) rather than attempting self-assessment, as self-assessment has proven unreliable for reasons described below.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4112 is a carved wooden music box, mechanism-driven, producing a single continuous melody of approximately ninety seconds when wound and opened. The melody itself has no anomalous acoustic properties detectable by instrumentation; its effect appears specific to human cognitive processing of the pattern rather than to any physical property of the sound.

Any individual who hears SCP-4112's melody in full, whether from the object directly or from an accurate secondhand reproduction, subsequently and permanently loses all memory of one specific person from their life. The identity of the forgotten individual varies between listeners and has not been shown to follow any pattern related to the listener's stated closeness to, or opinion of, that person; documented cases include forgotten spouses, forgotten children, forgotten deceased parents, and, in four cases, the listener's own twin.

Critically, SCP-4112's effect is not limited to the listener's memory. Over a period of approximately one to three weeks following exposure, physical and documentary evidence of the forgotten individual's existence — photographs, correspondence, official records, and, per twelve independently corroborated cases, the memories held by other people who are not themselves SCP-4112 listeners — fades or is retroactively altered to be consistent with the forgotten individual never having existed, or having existed in some substantially diminished capacity (e.g., a forgotten spouse's marriage license persisting while every photograph depicting them is found, on review, to depict only the listener alone). This effect scales with the number of exposures; family units in which multiple members have separately heard the melody show correspondingly more complete erasure of the individuals forgotten between them.

The forgotten individual is not directly harmed and, when locatable, retains full, unaltered memory of their own life and of the relationships now being erased around them — including, in every documented case, an awareness that this erasure is actively occurring to them.

SCP-4112 was brought to Foundation attention after a welfare check was requested for an elderly woman in ████████, who had submitted seven separate missing-persons reports over eleven months for family members that responding officers, her remaining relatives, and eventually her own case file could not identify or corroborate as ever having existed. The woman, subsequently interviewed by Foundation personnel, was able to describe in consistent, emotionally specific detail a total of six people — by her account, her husband and five of her children — whom no surviving documentation, and no other living relative, acknowledged.

ADDENDUM 4112-1: The woman described in the discovery account (subject is now designated PoI-4112-1) remains alive and, as of the most recent contact, cooperative with Foundation monitoring. She has stated, across multiple interviews conducted by different personnel, that she believes she herself will eventually be forgotten by "whoever is left to do it," and has asked, on each occasion, that her account of her husband and children be recorded somewhere that will not itself be forgotten. This documentation is understood by the assigned research team to be, in part, an attempt to fulfill that request.

Following standard rotation, three personnel previously assigned to PoI-4112-1's case have since been reassigned to unrelated duties for reasons unconnected to SCP-4112. None of the three, when asked in a follow-up review unrelated to SCP-4112, were able to recall the specifics of PoI-4112-1's account, though all confirmed working the case. This discrepancy has not been resolved.

SCP-4113.name: The Somnial Lichen
SCP-4113.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Specimens of SCP-4113 are to be stored in light-sealed containers lined with untreated cedar at Site-██ Biological Annex 3. Direct sunlight exposure is not required for specimen survival and is to be avoided, as extended exposure has been observed to accelerate mat growth by a factor of three. Each contained specimen is paired administratively with a designated "null" specimen never exposed to human sleep environments, for comparative study.

Personnel who have hosted an SCP-4113 specimen in their sleeping quarters for a cumulative period exceeding six months, whether before or after Foundation acquisition, are to be enrolled in the Longitudinal Dream Content Monitoring Program (Protocol 4113-Green) and interviewed on a quarterly basis. Any host reporting dream content matching Anomalous Convergence Pattern Alpha (see Description) is to be flagged for immediate interview and, at the Site Director's discretion, transferred away from active specimens.

Recovery of new specimens is ongoing via a standing request to Foundation-affiliated pest control and property management contacts; approximately one new specimen is recovered every four months.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4113 is a lichen-like colony organism of otherwise unremarkable composition, growing in flat grey-white mats between 8 and 40 centimeters across. It does not undergo standard photosynthesis and shows no measurable metabolic draw on its physical substrate. All 41 specimens recovered to date have been found on the underside of furniture — bed frames, headboards, and in three cases, the ceiling directly above a mattress — in rooms where at least one human occupant slept for a minimum of five nights per week over a period of three months or longer prior to discovery.

Occupants of rooms hosting an active SCP-4113 specimen report an elevated incidence of recurring dreams. Content varies by individual but, after a hosting period of approximately eight to fourteen weeks, converges toward a shared set of images irrespective of the dreamer's background, language, or prior sleep history: a single-story house with a green door, a hallway lit from an unseen source at its far end, and a room the dreamer is unable to enter. This convergence has been documented independently in 34 of 41 cases, including in subjects with no contact with one another and no shared media consumption that could account for the similarity.

Physical mats of SCP-4113 develop faint discolored striations over time. When photographed and processed digitally, at growth stages beyond twenty weeks, these striations resolve into line patterns consistent with an architectural floor plan. No two specimens have produced an identical pattern-in-progress, but all patterns to date, if projected to their apparent completion, describe the same structure: a single-story house with a hallway terminating in an unmarked room, matching the dream reports.

ADDENDUM 4113-1: In ██/2023, a floor plan produced by Specimen 4113-19 was compared against municipal records at the request of Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes. It corresponds, to a tolerance of eleven centimeters, with the floor plan of a residence at [REDACTED], currently unoccupied and held in probate since 2011. No specimen has been recovered from this address, and no known host has visited it. The resident who died in 2011 is not survived by immediate family. The property has not been entered by Foundation personnel. This addendum will be updated if that changes.

SCP-4114.name: The Continuous Worm
SCP-4114.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Six known SCP-4114 colony-sites are maintained under remote observation via automated benthic camera arrays; no physical containment of the seafloor sites themselves is attempted. Paired laboratory specimens (currently four pairs, designated 4114-A through 4114-D, each pair drawn from two colony-sites no less than 400 kilometers apart) are held in separate saltwater tanks at Site-██, physically isolated in different buildings to control for undetected signaling.

Testing involving injury to any SCP-4114 specimen requires Level 3 authorization and is capped at wounds no greater than one centimeter in any single test, with a mandatory 14-day recovery interval between tests on the same pair. This restriction is not to be waived under any circumstances; see Incident 4114-3.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4114 is a polychaete worm species, externally unremarkable and classifiable within existing taxonomy but for one behavior: individual specimens at geographically separated colony-sites exhibit simultaneous, mirrored contraction responses to injury. When a specimen at one site sustains damage, its paired counterpart at a separate site — regardless of the distance between them, up to the maximum tested separation of 1,900 kilometers — contracts in an identical pattern at the same instant, with no measurable propagation delay.

This pairing is not established through any known signaling mechanism. Specimens have never been observed to leave their colony-sites, and no material or energetic connection between sites has been detected via any instrument fielded to date, including those the Foundation uses to detect subspatial folding. The Foundation's working theory holds that what are observed as multiple specimens are cross-sections of a single organism whose body occupies a topology that does not conform to the seafloor's apparent three-dimensional geometry — that is, the worm is not many worms in different places, but one worm passing through the same place more than once.

Removal of a specimen from its site for study does not interrupt the mirrored response, provided the specimen remains alive. Specimens do not appear to age in the conventional sense; four specimens in long-term captivity have shown no morphological change across eleven years of observation.

ADDENDUM 4114-1 (Incident 4114-3): During an unauthorized test on ██/██/2019, Researcher Voss severed Specimen 4114-B2 completely, exceeding the permitted wound threshold. Within the same second, all 34 then-known SCP-4114 specimens across all six colony-sites and all captive pairs ceased movement and showed no vital signs. Colony-sites were unresponsive to remote probing for six days.

On the seventh day, camera arrays recorded new specimens emerging at all six sites simultaneously. Tissue sampling confirmed these to be genetically consistent with, but not identical to, the prior population. Behavioral synchronization testing resumed once specimens reached maturity (approximately 40 hours, notably rapid for the species) and mirrored-response pairing was found to be intact between sites — including between sites that had never previously been tested against one another. Dr. Imelu's note appended to the incident file reads only: "It did not lose count."

Researcher Voss has been reassigned to non-biological research pending review.

SCP-4115.name: The Unlanding Bird
SCP-4115.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4115 is not to be captured. Foundation assets embedded in wildlife monitoring stations across its known range (currently a migratory corridor spanning three countries in [REDACTED]) are tasked with tracking flock movements via long-range optics and reporting any individual observed descending below 30 meters of altitude near a human settlement. Drone deterrents are authorized for use in these instances to disrupt landing behavior before it completes, but personnel operating the deterrents must not personally observe the landing through direct line of sight; camera feed monitoring only.

Civilians who report witnessing SCP-4115 land are to be located, interviewed under Protocol 4115-Watch, and administered Class A amnestics only after the 90-day observation window described below has closed, to preserve data integrity. During the window, subjects are covertly monitored for health and mortality outcomes and are not to be informed of their inclusion in the study.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4115 designates a population of approximately 1,100–1,400 individuals of a bird species externally resembling Apus apus (common swift) but distinguished by fused, non-functional leg bones consistent with an obligate aerial lifestyle more extreme than any known avian species; unlike true swifts, which land rarely, SCP-4115 individuals have never been recorded landing during 340 cumulative hours of Foundation aerial surveillance footage.

The anomalous property of SCP-4115 is not physiological but statistical and behavioral. Of 61 documented civilian reports of an SCP-4115 individual landing (collected from regional folklore records, hospital intake interviews, and direct Foundation contact), 58 witnesses were confirmed deceased within 90 days of the reported sighting, from causes ranging from natural illness to accident, with no consistent pathology, toxicology, or mechanism linking the deaths. This rate substantially exceeds baseline mortality for the demographic in question. No mechanism connecting the sighting to the outcome has been identified; the Foundation has not ruled out that the birds are attracted to, rather than causative of, impending death, though this does not explain why they otherwise never land at all.

Regional folklore predating Foundation contact with the area refers to the species under a name translating approximately to "the bird that keeps no ground," and holds that a household visited by a grounded specimen should not speak of it aloud, on the belief that naming the event aloud shortens the remaining interval. Ethnographic interviews conducted in 19██ found this practice still observed in 11 of 14 surveyed households with a family history of a reported sighting, independent of whether the household was aware of the Foundation's mortality statistics. No causal link between the practice and survival outcomes has been established, and the sample size is insufficient for statistical review, but the correspondence between local custom and the Foundation's own 90-day observation window has been noted internally without further comment.

ADDENDUM 4115-1: Subject 4115-W-12, a civilian witness interviewed under Protocol 4115-Watch after reporting a landing on ██/██/2021, remains alive as of this writing, 1,140 days past the 90-day threshold. Subject reported gradual vision loss beginning approximately 85 days after the sighting, reaching complete bilateral blindness on day 91. Ophthalmological examination found no retinal, neurological, or other structural cause. Subject has declined further Foundation contact. Case remains open.

SCP-4116.name: The Hour Swarm
SCP-4116.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4116 cannot be physically contained. Foundation assets track the swarm's position via weather radar signatures cross-referenced with seismic sensor arrays along its historical migratory paths. Settlements within 40 kilometers of a projected flight path are to be evacuated under cover story "agricultural pest control operation" no less than 18 hours in advance. Direct extermination attempts are prohibited without O5 authorization; see Incidents 4116-1 and 4116-2.

Sites that have experienced an SCP-4116 overflight are to be surveyed for lingering chronometric anomalies for no less than 30 days following the event, and all mechanical, electronic, and biological timekeeping data from the affected population cross-checked against Foundation atomic clock references.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4116 is a swarm of an unidentified orthopteran species, externally consistent with Schistocerca gregaria (desert locust) but never captured intact; specimens recovered post-mortem decompose at a rate approximately 40 times faster than baseline biological tissue, complicating study. Swarm size fluctuates between approximately 80 million and 400 million individuals and has never been observed to fall below a floor count correlating with global leap second insertions: each positive leap second added to Coordinated Universal Time since 1972 corresponds to a documented increase in swarm population of approximately 600,000–900,000 individuals within the following lunar cycle. No leap second has ever coincided with a population decrease.

The swarm's anomalous behavior is not one of appetite or destruction in the conventional locust sense — crop damage from SCP-4116 overflights is minimal and inconsistent with its size — but of temporal synchronization. The swarm exhibits sharp, coordinated behavioral phase shifts (course alteration, altitude change, vocalization changes recorded via ultrasonic monitoring) precisely on the hour according to the civil time of the ground beneath it, adjusting within seconds when crossing a time zone boundary, including boundaries defined only by political rather than geographic distinction. This has been confirmed even where the swarm's flight path crosses a time zone boundary at altitude, over terrain with no visual or geographic marker of the boundary's location.

Populated areas beneath an active overflight report clocks losing or gaining time inconsistently (a documented range of 4 minutes lost to 11 minutes gained across recorded incidents) and a shared subjective sense among residents of time "skipping" or "dragging," lasting for the duration of the overflight plus an average of 22 additional minutes after the swarm has passed from sight.

ADDENDUM 4116-1 (Incidents 4116-1, 4116-2): Two large-scale aerial extermination attempts (19██ and 20██, details on file) using conventional and anomalous ordnance both resulted in localized temporal distortion events at the strike site, in one case producing a documented 6-hour discrepancy between site clocks and the outside world that resolved itself without Foundation intervention. Swarm population showed no measurable reduction following either attempt. Extermination is no longer considered a viable containment strategy. Current doctrine is evacuation and avoidance only.

SCP-4117.name: The Grave Orchid
SCP-4117.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Twelve live SCP-4117 specimens are maintained in the botanical annex at Site-██, each potted in a sealed soil sample taken from its original germination site (see Description) and transplanted within 72 hours of first sprout to prevent loss of the specimen to natural decomposition of the burial site. No further soil contact with the original grave is required or provided after transplantation.

Site personnel and cooperating funeral homes under standing agreement are to notify the Foundation of any burial where SCP-4117 seed matter is suspected to be present in the surrounding soil (identifiable by a faint blue-grey seed casing, approximately 2mm, visible under sieving). Collection must occur within 72 hours of interment or the germination window closes.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4117 is a flowering plant of the orchid family, anomalous in its germination trigger and blooming schedule rather than its physical structure, which is otherwise consistent with terrestrial orchids of temperate climates. Seeds germinate exclusively in soil disturbed by a human burial, within 72 hours of interment; soil disturbed by any other cause, including animal burial, does not produce germination under any tested condition.

Once germinated, SCP-4117 does not bloom on a seasonal cycle. Instead, the plant produces a single bud that opens on the calendar date corresponding to the anniversary of the interred individual's death and closes again by the end of that day, remaining dormant for the remainder of the year. This cycle repeats annually for a number of years matching the actuarial life expectancy the deceased would statistically have reached had they not died, calculated from their age, sex, and recorded health data at time of death; the plant then dies without further blooming, regardless of the specimen's own physical condition at that time.

Genetic analysis of SCP-4117 petal tissue, despite the plant having no material contact with human remains, has in all 12 current specimens returned a partial genetic match to the interred individual associated with the germination site, sufficient for familial identification purposes though not for full profiling. The mechanism by which this genetic material is incorporated into the plant's tissue is not understood.

Botanical staff have additionally noted that the actuarial figure governing a given specimen's blooming duration is recalculated, without instruction from any Foundation researcher, if updated health records for the deceased are later entered into the annex's reference database — for instance, the retroactive addition of a previously undocumented medical condition has, in three cases, caused a specimen's remaining bloom count to shorten on its next anniversary date to match the revised figure, despite the plant having no network connection to the database and no apparent means of accessing it. Site botanists have taken to calling this behavior "the correction" and have, per informal internal practice rather than any written procedure, avoided updating deceased individuals' records outside of scheduled annex review windows.

ADDENDUM 4117-1: Specimen 4117-04, associated with the 1958 burial of a Foundation-unaffiliated civilian, was relocated to Site-██ in 1962, approximately 800 kilometers from the original grave. Blooming continued on the anniversary date without interruption or delay, confirming that the anomalous schedule is fixed to the original burial event by calendar date rather than maintained through any ongoing connection to the soil or location. Specimen 4117-04 is projected, per actuarial calculation, to bloom for the final time in 20██, after which it will be retained in a dormant, non-flowering state for continued study.

SCP-4118.name: The Backward Frog
SCP-4118.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4118's home range, a 6.4-hectare wetland designated Site-██-Wetland within a Foundation-acquired nature reserve in [REDACTED], is to remain undisturbed and closed to public access under standing cover story "protected amphibian habitat." Foundation biologists are permitted to observe and photograph but not to remove specimens from the wetland boundary without Level 3 authorization; see Description regarding consequences of removal.

A census of the wetland's SCP-4118 population is to be conducted monthly via non-invasive photographic survey. Any deviation from the established baseline count of 340 individuals (±0, historically) is to be reported to the Site Director within 24 hours.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4118 is a population of amphibians resembling Lithobates sylvaticus (wood frog) confined to the boundaries of a single wetland site. Individual specimens undergo reversed developmental cycling: rather than aging forward from egg to tadpole to adult, tagged specimens have been observed to regress from adult form back through juvenile and larval stages, culminating in dissolution into an unfertilized egg mass, which subsequently vanishes from observation for a period ranging from 6 to 19 days before an adult specimen reappears elsewhere within the wetland boundary, generally though not always in a location distant from where the previous cycle ended.

The population count of the wetland has remained fixed at 340 individuals (verified via photographic and tag-based census) across 47 years of intermittent record-keeping, including 31 years of consistent Foundation monitoring, despite observed predation, disease mortality, and at least six deliberate culling operations conducted for study purposes between 19██ and 20██, in each of which removed individuals were replaced within the standard 6–19 day window by newly cycled specimens maintaining the same total.

Specimens removed entirely from the wetland boundary for off-site study do not undergo the reversal cycle and instead age forward at an accelerated rate, reaching apparent senescence and death within 4 to 11 days regardless of the specimen's developmental stage at time of removal. No specimen removed from the site has survived transport beyond two weeks. The wetland's population count is not affected by such removals; a replacement specimen cycles into existence within the site on the same schedule as if the removed individual had simply completed its cycle normally.

ADDENDUM 4118-1: In 20██, photographic cross-referencing identified Specimen 4118-119, tagged in 1981 during an early non-Foundation herpetological survey of the site, as still present in the current population. The specimen has cycled through an estimated 200+ full developmental reversals in the intervening 43 years based on cycle-length averages, yet shows no cumulative morphological drift, genetic mutation load, or size increase beyond the species baseline. It was most recently photographed in a juvenile stage. Researchers have noted, without further elaboration in the file, that its tag — a small aluminum band applied in 1981 using techniques no longer practiced by the Foundation — shows no anomalous wear consistent with 43 years of exposure.

SCP-4119.name: The Cosmetic Rot
SCP-4119.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All confirmed SCP-4119 infection sites are subject to immediate Foundation medical quarantine under the cover designation "necrotizing soft tissue infection, novel strain." Infected individuals are to be sedated and restrained prior to disclosure of prognosis, as subjects have consistently resisted diagnosis and treatment (see Description). Deep-tissue ultrasound or MRI imaging is mandatory for any wound presenting abnormally rapid visual healing in a Foundation medical facility, regardless of stated cause.

Due to three confirmed instances of civilian-to-civilian transmission via direct wound contact prior to Foundation containment, all regional hospitals within a 200-kilometer radius of a confirmed outbreak site are to be provided updated diagnostic bulletins through Foundation-embedded medical liaisons, without disclosure of the anomalous nature of the condition.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4119 is a bacterial strain, gram-negative and otherwise unremarkable under standard culture, which infects open wounds in mammalian hosts, including humans. Infection is not detectable through visual inspection of the wound site: within 6 to 30 hours of infection, the wound's outward appearance resolves to a state consistent with healthy, largely healed tissue — closed margins, faded discoloration, and scar tissue formation at a rate the host's actual healing capacity does not support.

This outward presentation is produced by a biofilm layer SCP-4119 generates over the wound site, which additionally replicates the tactile properties (elasticity, surface temperature, minor pain response to pressure) of healed tissue closely enough to deceive both self-examination and routine physical examination by medical personnel. Beneath this biofilm, the underlying tissue does not heal; necrosis proceeds at a rate consistent with, or in most documented cases exceeding, an untreated wound, undetected by the host or examining clinicians without deep-tissue imaging.

Hosts additionally report a subjective sense of improved wellbeing, increased energy, and reduced pain correlating with infection progression rather than wound severity, a symptom the Foundation has not yet mechanistically explained. This effect appears to actively discourage hosts from seeking further treatment once initial wound closure is observed; of 44 confirmed cases prior to Foundation intervention, 31 hosts declined follow-up medical care after the wound's outward appearance normalized, citing feeling "better than before the injury." Untreated, infection has a documented 100% progression to sepsis, organ failure, or systemic necrosis, with median time to critical presentation of 19 days and median time from critical presentation to death of 31 hours — the latter figure notable for how little warning the outward appearance of the wound provides prior to collapse.
