ADDENDUM 4119-1: SCP-4119 is classified Keter primarily on the basis of detection difficulty rather than raw lethality; standard containment breach protocols are complicated by the strain's incubation period (6–30 hours) during which infected but visually healed individuals may pass through Foundation and civilian medical screening undetected. Site-██ Outbreak (20██) resulted in 6 Foundation personnel deaths before deep-tissue screening was made mandatory for all wound presentations; two of the six declined medical evaluation after visual assessment showed no cause for concern, consistent with the pattern in civilian cases.

SCP-4120.name: The Drowning Fish
SCP-4120.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4120 has never been physically recovered, and no containment of a physical specimen is currently possible or attempted. Foundation containment consists of information management: civilian witnesses recovering from near-drowning incidents who report SCP-4120 sightings are to be interviewed by Foundation medical liaisons embedded in regional hospital drowning/resuscitation wards under the cover of standard post-resuscitation psychological assessment, and administered Class A amnestics following interview unless enrolled in ongoing study under informed-consent equivalent protocols (see Addendum 4120-1).

Bodies of freshwater with a documented history of three or more SCP-4120 sighting reports ("hot sites") are to be flagged in Foundation hydrological databases for continued monitoring of drowning incident statistics; no physical intervention at these sites is authorized.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4120 designates a consistent set of reported sightings of a large aquatic entity, described uniformly across unconnected witnesses as approximately the length and mass of a compact automobile, pale grey to white in coloration, without visible eyes, and moving alongside the witness without direct physical contact. No witness has reported the entity displaying aggressive behavior. SCP-4120 has been reported exclusively by individuals who were, at the time of the sighting, in the physiological process of drowning in fresh water and were subsequently resuscitated; it has never been reported by a witness in any other circumstance, including by other individuals present at the same drowning incident who were not themselves in the water, or by witnesses who nearly drowned in saltwater.

Of 213 documented cases in the Foundation's records (compiled from resuscitation ward interviews, hospital incident reports, and folklore archives cross-referenced against verified drowning statistics), 213 witnesses described the entity independently using consistent core details prior to being made aware of other reports, despite no evidence of prior mutual contact or shared source material.

Statistical review of drowning outcomes at documented "hot sites" found a survival rate among resuscitated individuals who reported an SCP-4120 sighting of 91%, against a baseline survival rate of 34% for comparable near-drowning incidents at sites without SCP-4120 reports. The Foundation has not established a causal mechanism and considers it equally possible that the entity's presence correlates with survivable drowning conditions rather than contributing to survival directly. SCP-4120 is classified Safe on the basis that no confirmed harm has been attributed to it and its statistical association, if causal, would be net beneficial.

ADDENDUM 4120-1: In 20██, with O5 authorization and full informed consent, a controlled near-drowning test was conducted on volunteer Foundation researcher [REDACTED] under continuous medical supervision, in a hot site with a documented sighting rate of 40% among prior witnesses. The subject, who had not been briefed on prior witness descriptions of the entity, reported seeing it during the test and independently described two physical details — a series of faint parallel ridges along its dorsal surface, and a slow pulsing bioluminescence at what would correspond to its ventral midline — that had not previously appeared in any witness report on file, Foundation or civilian. No further testing of this kind has been approved.

SCP-4121.name: The Warning Moss
SCP-4121.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Cultivated strains of SCP-4121 are deployed as an active early-warning layer at 30 designated high-priority Foundation containment sites, integrated into perimeter greenhouse installations and, at 11 sites, directly into containment cell wall linings under Protocol 4121-Sentinel. Each installation requires a living host organism (currently standardized to Mus musculus, laboratory mouse, housed within the growth medium under Foundation animal welfare oversight) which SCP-4121 requires to remain viable; host replacement occurs on a 14-day rotating schedule performed by trained husbandry staff.

Site security teams are to treat any SCP-4121 discoloration event (see Description) as equivalent to a Level 2 security alert regardless of whether corroborating instrumentation has registered an anomaly, and to escalate to Level 1 status if discoloration exceeds 60% of the installation's surface area. Discoloration events that precede a confirmed anomalous event or containment breach by more than 20 minutes are to be logged and forwarded to the O5 Council's Predictive Anomalies working group.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4121 is a moss-lichen symbiotic organism, cultivated by the Foundation from a wild strain recovered in 1987, which undergoes a rapid, localized blackening response in the presence of anomalous activity or localized reality distortion occurring within an approximate 50-meter radius, with response intensity scaling to the severity of the triggering event. In 94% of documented cases across 37 years of deployment, SCP-4121's discoloration response has preceded confirmed detection of the corresponding anomaly by conventional Foundation instrumentation, with a median lead time of 4 minutes and a maximum recorded lead time of 11 days.

SCP-4121 requires ongoing physical contact with living mammalian tissue to remain viable; isolated from a host, cultivated mats die within 96 hours regardless of other environmental conditions. The mechanism by which the organism detects anomalous activity, and the reason for its dependency on animal tissue, are not understood; the Foundation's Thaumiel classification reflects SCP-4121's active operational use in the protection of numerous other contained anomalies, not an understanding of how it functions.

The 11-day maximum lead time referenced above is treated internally as the organism's most operationally significant and least understood property. In each documented instance of extended lead time, no plausible instrumentation error or delayed-onset event has been identified as an alternative explanation; the triggering anomalous event, when it later occurred, showed no detectable precursor activity during the intervening period that any other Foundation asset was able to register.

ADDENDUM 4121-1: Research into deliberately extending SCP-4121's apparent detection range through strain modification has produced inconsistent results and is ongoing under Dr. Farrow's supervision. A 2021 internal memo notes, regarding host mortality during high-lead-time discoloration events specifically: "the mice die anyway, on schedule, whether or not anything happens. We would like to know if that's incidental." No further comment has been appended to the file.

SCP-4122.name: The Constant Herd
SCP-4122.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The territory occupied by SCP-4122, a 22-square-kilometer valley designated Site-██-Valley within a Foundation-controlled land holding in [REDACTED], is to remain closed to public access under standing cover story "private hunting reserve, no trespassing." No fencing or physical boundary marking is required, as SCP-4122's territorial limits are self-enforcing (see Description).

A full photographic census of SCP-4122 is to be conducted quarterly. The population count is expected to remain at 217 individuals; any deviation is to be reported immediately to the Site Director and cross-checked against possible census error before being logged as anomalous.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4122 designates a herd of ungulates externally consistent with Cervus canadensis (elk) confined to the boundaries of Site-██-Valley. The herd's total population has remained at exactly 217 individuals across 61 years of intermittent record-keeping, including 34 years of continuous Foundation monitoring, despite natural predation, disease, and repeated deliberate culling operations (11 documented instances between 19██ and 20██, removing between 1 and 40 individuals per operation) intended to test the mechanism.

In every tested instance, a replacement individual — physically ordinary, showing no anomalous properties under examination, and generally though not invariably matched in approximate age and sex to the animal it replaced — appeared within the valley's boundary within 72 hours of a population-reducing event, restoring the count to 217. Necropsy of culled animals has found nothing anomalous in their biology; the population mechanic operates at the level of the herd's count, not the individual animal.

SCP-4122 does not tolerate expansion of its territory. Individuals that cross the valley's boundary, whether driven out during testing or through natural wandering, do not survive; tracked specimens fitted with GPS collars that exit the valley cease all vital signs within an average of 6 hours, with no consistent cause of death identified on subsequent examination (several were found with no external injury and no discernible internal pathology). The herd's population count is not affected by these losses; unlike culling within the valley, an animal that dies after crossing the boundary is not replaced, as it is understood to remain, for the purposes of the count, still alive within the valley.

The Foundation initially considered whether SCP-4122's mechanism might extend to compensating losses using individuals of other species, but no cross-species substitution has been documented; when other ungulate species (deer, confirmed non-anomalous) stray into the valley and are subsequently killed by predation, no replacement occurs and the intruding species' local population behaves normally.

ADDENDUM 4122-1: Indigenous accounts from communities historically resident near the valley, recorded by Foundation ethnographic staff in 19██, describe the valley itself as "keeping the count" and specifically warn against removing "more than the land gives back," predating Foundation involvement and contemporary study by at least several generations. No informant interviewed could identify the origin of the belief or recall a specific founding incident.

SCP-4123.name: The Sound-Weaving Spider
SCP-4123.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Living SCP-4123 specimens (currently 8) are housed in acoustically isolated enclosures at Site-██, each fitted with a controllable ambient sound source, as specimens denied ambient sound input show stunted web development and reduced silk production within 72 hours. Standard enclosure ambient sound is limited to recorded white noise and non-informational tonal patterns to prevent unintentional recording of sensitive material.

Harvested webs are to be handled by personnel with at least Level 2 clearance and stored in vibration-isolated containers, as ambient vibration during storage and transport has been observed to degrade recorded content. Analysis of harvested web playback requires sign-off from the Site Director given the unpredictable nature of captured content (see Description).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4123 is a spider species, orb-weaving and externally consistent with genus Araneus, which constructs webs functionally analogous to an analog recording medium rather than a prey-capture structure. Silk strands produced by SCP-4123 exhibit a fine internal structural variance, undetectable to the naked eye but confirmed under electron microscopy, that appears to encode ambient sound present during the silk's production, in a manner the Foundation has not been able to fully reverse-engineer despite successfully triggering playback (see below).

Prey capture by SCP-4123 is opportunistic and secondary; individuals have been observed to feed normally on trapped insects but show no anomalous property connected to this behavior. The web itself, when later disturbed by wind, touch, or vibration, "plays back" fragments of previously captured ambient sound at audible volume, apparently generated by resonant vibration of the structurally encoded silk strands rather than any active biological process — the spider need not be present, and webs continue to play back recorded fragments for a period of 5 to 14 days after being abandoned or after the spider's death, gradually degrading in fidelity.

Playback is fragmentary, non-continuous, and frequently — though not consistently — plays in reverse chronological order relative to when the sound was captured. Rooms or enclosures with insufficient ambient sound produce webs that either fail to develop past an early juvenile structure or, in six documented cases, collapse entirely within days of construction.

ADDENDUM 4123-1: Following Containment Breach Incident ██-██ at Site-██ (20██), a naturally occurring SCP-4123 web was recovered from a ventilation shaft near the breach's point of origin. Playback of the web over the following nine days reproduced audio fragments consistent with, and independently corroborating, Foundation camera and radio log records of the incident. However, three fragments contained a voice not identified in any personnel roster, camera audio, or radio transmission from the incident, speaking in a language subsequently identified as a dialect no longer in active use, not attributable to any known specimen, breach entity, or Foundation asset present at the site during the relevant window. The web has since fully degraded and is no longer capable of playback. No further recordings containing the voice have been recovered from any other SCP-4123 specimen.

SCP-4124.name: The Convergence Grove
SCP-4124.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Confirmed SCP-4124 growth sites are to be perimeter-fenced at a minimum radius of 3 kilometers from the outermost visible root filament, with all human habitation within the fenced zone relocated under cover story "regional subsidence hazard." Relocation is mandatory regardless of the resident population's apparent stage of exposure (see Description) and is not to be delayed pending further study.

Any settlement identified as having been in continuous proximity to a suspected SCP-4124 site for a period exceeding 15 years is to be flagged for retroactive review of municipal, medical, and photographic records under Protocol 4124-Threshold, to assess whether convergence has already reached an advanced stage prior to detection. Seven such settlements have been identified to date; see Addendum 4124-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4124 designates a colonial organism of uncertain taxonomic affiliation, presenting externally as a grove of tree-like growths ranging from 4 to 30 meters in height, with an internal structure combining lignified plant tissue with a calcified, coral-like matrix not otherwise documented in terrestrial biology. Confirmed sites (9 to date) are typically situated within 5 kilometers of a human settlement of at least 200 residents.

SCP-4124 extends fine, largely subterranean root-like filaments toward nearby human habitation, generally undetected due to their depth and thinness (average 0.4mm) until deliberately sought. Human residents within the filaments' effective range — established at approximately 6 kilometers from the grove's center, though this may reflect settlement placement rather than a hard physiological limit — exhibit, over a period of years, gradual convergence of distinguishing physical characteristics: facial structure, dermatoglyphic pattern (fingerprints), voice timbre, and in later stages, gait and handwriting, drifting toward a shared template inconsistent with any individual resident's genetic baseline, ancestry, or prior appearance. Early-stage convergence (2–5 years of exposure) is subtle and typically unnoticed by affected individuals or their acquaintances; late-stage convergence (typically 12+ years) produces residents who are, per Foundation forensic comparison, not reliably distinguishable from one another by any conventional biometric method, despite continuing to be recognized and named as distinct individuals by their own community, who report no subjective awareness of the change.

The mechanism by which SCP-4124 benefits from this process is understood only in outline. Grove specimens produce spore matter at increased volume correlating with the convergence stage of the nearest exposed population; spore analysis has confirmed the presence of degraded but identifiable genetic and biometric information drawn from exposed residents, consistent with the hypothesis that the grove is, in some fashion not yet understood, extracting and consuming the residents' individuating biological data. Documented cases show that once a settlement's population reaches full convergence, the originating grove specimen dies within 6 to 18 months, and unaffiliated spore-derived growths have subsequently been confirmed at new sites, restarting the process with a new population.

ADDENDUM 4124-1: Municipal archive review of the town of [REDACTED] (Protocol 4124-Threshold, conducted 20██) recovered photographic records spanning 1946 to 1991 in which individuals recorded under different names across different decades are, per forensic photogrammetric comparison, facially indistinguishable to a confidence exceeding standard identification thresholds. Town records list a population fluctuating narrowly around 340 residents throughout the archive period; no growth site associated with this settlement has yet been located, and the town's current residents, when approached under standard Foundation cover, showed no awareness of anything unusual in the archive photographs shown to them.

SCP-4125.name: The Reflection That Moves First
SCP-4125.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4125 resides in a standard on-site personnel apartment at Site-77, furnished with one (1) non-reflective acrylic mirror substitute for daily grooming use. All reflective surfaces exceeding 15 cm² within SCP-4125's designated quarters have been removed or covered. SCP-4125 has voluntarily agreed to weekly monitored sessions in Testing Chamber 12, which contains a single controlled mirror (designated SCP-4125-1) for observation purposes. Footage of these sessions is reviewed by on-duty psychologists for behavioral drift. SCP-4125 is permitted supervised access to public areas of Site-77 provided an escort confirms the absence of reflective surfaces along the route. Personal effects such as phone screens, polished cutlery, and window glass at night are logged as incidental risks and are not actively restricted, per SCP-4125's request.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4125 is Ms. Elif Sarman (b. 1994), a Turkish national employed prior to containment as a physical therapist in Bursa. SCP-4125-1 designates any reflective surface capable of producing a mirror image of Ms. Sarman; under normal optical conditions this image behaves as expected, with one exception: SCP-4125-1 initiates minor voluntary movements — shifts in weight, the beginning of a hand gesture, a change in facial expression — between 0.6 and 1.1 seconds before Ms. Sarman consciously performs, or decides to perform, the corresponding movement.

The anomaly does not extend to involuntary movement (blinking, breathing) and cannot be used to predict actions further than roughly one second in advance. Ms. Sarman reports being unaware of the lag from her own perspective; she experiences her actions as originating from herself, in ordinary sequence. The discrepancy is detectable only by a third-party observer watching both Ms. Sarman and her reflection simultaneously, which is how the anomaly was first noticed, by a coworker during a hospital shift change.

Of note is a secondary behavior first logged during Testing Session 12-004: on eleven (11) documented occasions, SCP-4125-1 has begun a movement — most often the start of a step, or the mirror's hand rising as if to reach for something — that Ms. Sarman did not go on to perform. In each case, the reflection's incomplete gesture matched, per Ms. Sarman's own subsequent testimony, an action she reported "almost" wanting to take but consciously suppressing (declining to answer a question, reaching for a cigarette she has been trying to quit). No instance has yet been recorded of SCP-4125-1 beginning a movement corresponding to an action Ms. Sarman denies having considered.

ADDENDUM 4125-A: Following Testing Session 12-004, Ms. Sarman requested that testing frequency be reduced from weekly to monthly, stating in her formal request: "I don't need help remembering what I decided not to do." The request was approved by Site-77 Ethics Committee on the grounds that continued high-frequency testing offered diminishing research value relative to subject distress. Long-term study of SCP-4125-1's predictive behavior remains an open research priority, pending Ms. Sarman's continued willingness to participate.

SCP-4126.name: The Boy No One Remembers
SCP-4126.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4126 is housed in a dedicated observation suite at Site-19, staffed on a rotating basis by no fewer than two (2) assigned personnel at all times, such that SCP-4126 remains within direct line of sight of at least one staff member for the duration of any shift. Handoffs between shifts require an overlap period of no less than five (5) minutes during which both outgoing and incoming staff maintain simultaneous visual contact with SCP-4126, to prevent a lapse during which no living person retains active memory of him.

All personnel assigned to SCP-4126 are required to submit a brief written log at the end of each shift summarizing interactions, as personal memory of these interactions reliably fades within 30–90 seconds of SCP-4126 leaving the recaller's sight. These logs, along with photographic and video records (which are unaffected by the anomaly), constitute the primary continuity of SCP-4126's case history. SCP-4126 is provided with a personal journal, which he maintains voluntarily, and which is not to be read by staff except with his express permission.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4126 is a boy of apparent age 9–11, legal name and date of birth unknown. Any individual who directly observes SCP-4126 forms ordinary short-term and long-term memories of him for as long as observation continues. However, once SCP-4126 passes out of an individual's direct line of sight, that individual's episodic memory of him begins degrading immediately and is fully gone within one to three minutes, regardless of the significance or duration of the preceding interaction. This forgetting is total: subjects do not recall that a memory has been lost, and express no sense that anything is missing.

The anomaly does not affect non-biological records. Photographs, written notes, audio recordings, and administrative documents referencing SCP-4126 remain intact and legible, and a subject who is shown such a record after forgetting him will recognize the record as accurate without necessarily recovering any independent recollection.

SCP-4126 was located via a cross-reference of Turkish provincial orphanage intake records dating back at least fourteen years, all of which describe a boy matching his description being repeatedly logged as a new admission at facilities from which no discharge or transfer paperwork could subsequently be found, the staff at each facility having apparently forgotten him and, in the absence of any adult who recalled placing him, processed him again as an unaccompanied minor. Foundation researchers estimate SCP-4126 has been administratively "readmitted" to state care no fewer than nineteen (19) times.

SCP-4126 is cooperative and displays no hostility toward staff. He is fully aware of his own condition. Interview logs indicate he has developed private strategies for coping with it, including keeping the aforementioned journal and, per his own account, "introducing himself the same way every time, so it doesn't feel new to either of us."

ADDENDUM 4126-A: When asked by Dr. Voss whether he remembered their conversation from the previous day, SCP-4126 answered: "No. But I wrote it down, so I know we had a good one." No further action has been taken regarding this statement.

SCP-4127.name: The Man Who Files Himself In
SCP-4127.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4127 is held in a sub-level isolation cell at Site-45 constructed without paper, cardboard, or any writable analog document within a 20-meter radius. All personnel interacting with SCP-4127 must submit to a mandatory search preventing the introduction of pens, printed forms, identification cards, or other inscribable materials into the containment area. Communication with SCP-4127 is conducted verbally through reinforced glass or via a digital intercom system; no physical documents are to be passed into or out of the cell under any circumstance.

Due to the ongoing risk that SCP-4127 has already altered an unknown number of Foundation personnel records, all Site-45 administrative staff are required to undergo quarterly cross-verification of personal identity documents against Foundation biometric archives predating SCP-4127's containment (2009). Any discrepancy is to be reported immediately to the Site-45 Records Anomaly Task Force. As of this writing, eleven (11) such discrepancies have been confirmed and are catalogued under Incident 4127-Delta through -Kappa.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4127 presents as a man of approximately 70 years of age, cooperative, soft-spoken, and consistently polite with containment staff. When SCP-4127 makes physical contact with any official document — defined for these purposes as a document recognized by a governmental, institutional, or organizational body as authoritative regarding a person's identity, status, or relationships (birth certificates, employment records, medical charts, next-of-kin forms, etc.) — and subsequently signs his name to it in any capacity, the named individual on that document is retroactively and universally replaced by SCP-4127 in the memories of every person who has, is, or will consult that document, as well as in all linked or cross-referenced records.

The original named individual is not physically harmed and does not disappear; rather, all documentary and testimonial evidence of that individual's prior identity is seamlessly reassigned to SCP-4127, while the original individual retains their own memory of who they are but discovers that no institution, and increasingly no acquaintance, recognizes them as such. Nine (9) cases of this occurring to civilians prior to SCP-4127's containment have been confirmed via retrospective analysis; the fates of the displaced individuals remain unknown, though several have been located living under entirely new, seemingly self-assigned identities, unable to convince anyone, including Foundation interviewers shown corroborating physical evidence, that they are who they claim to be.

SCP-4127 was apprehended after Foundation auditors noted that three separate deceased staff members' pension and next-of-kin files at Site-45 had, without any logged administrative action, come to list an "Ahmet K." as beneficiary, spouse, or dependent, a name with no prior personnel record. Subsequent investigation traced SCP-4127 to a municipal records office in İzmir, where he had been employed as a filing clerk for eleven years under circumstances his former coworkers could not, when questioned, actually recall.

SCP-4127 has offered no explanation for his behavior beyond describing a compulsion he calls "just tidying." He denies malicious intent and has expressed mild distress when informed that his actions displace others. He has not been observed to remove his own hand from a document voluntarily once contact is made, and containment staff have adopted a strict no-contact protocol accordingly.

ADDENDUM 4127-B: The full extent of records already altered by SCP-4127 prior to containment cannot be determined, as any investigation into his history necessarily consults the very records he may have amended. Site-45 Records Anomaly Task Force operates under the standing assumption that its own founding charter should be periodically re-verified against physical archives predating 2009.

SCP-4128.name: The Undivided Memory
SCP-4128.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4128-1 and SCP-4128-2 are housed together in a standard double-occupancy residential unit at Site-64, per their own request and the recommendation of Site-64 psychological staff, who have determined that separation produces measurable distress in both subjects without containment benefit. Weekly individual interviews are conducted separately to maintain data integrity on divergent aspects of their recollection. SCP-4128-1 and -2 retain standard humanoid subject privileges, including supervised outside recreation and correspondence with two (2) pre-approved family members, screened to exclude any individual who might independently corroborate or dispute contested memories.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4128 designates Mehmet (-1) and Ali (-2) Doğaner, monozygotic twins, age 34, who share what appears to be a single continuous set of autobiographical memories corresponding to only one lived childhood, despite both having independently and consistently existed as separate physical individuals since birth, per hospital birth records and continuous photographic documentation showing both twins present at the same events from infancy onward.

Neuropsychological testing (see Document 4128-C) confirms that both subjects possess functionally identical episodic memory engrams for events between ages 0–17, down to sensory details neither would ordinarily be expected to recall independently (the specific wording of a teacher's reprimand, the exact sequence of a fall from a bicycle, and so forth). Each twin reports these memories as his own, experienced from a single first-person perspective, and each is able to describe the other twin's presence during these events only as a secondary character, not as a simultaneously-experiencing party. When shown video evidence of both twins independently present and behaving differently during a recorded childhood event, both subjects express genuine confusion, and each will typically state that the footage must be "of the day it actually happened," while insisting that his own memory, in which the other twin's independent behavior does not feature, is what he "actually lived."

No divergence in memory has been detected for the period after each twin's eighteenth birthday, following which they began attending separate universities; from this point forward, both maintain entirely ordinary and mutually distinct memories. The mechanism responsible for the shared childhood memory, and whether it in fact originates from only one twin's lived experience "duplicated" into the other, remains undetermined. Both subjects have declined further invasive testing (including imaging that would require sedation) to investigate the question further, citing no desire to "find out which one of us wasn't really there."

ADDENDUM 4128-A: During a joint interview, when asked directly which of them "really" experienced the shared childhood, Ali Doğaner responded on behalf of both: "It doesn't matter. We were both there for it, even if only one of us was." Mehmet did not dispute this statement. The Ethics Committee has recommended the question not be raised again absent a compelling research justification.

SCP-4129.name: The Woman Out of Order
SCP-4129.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4129 resides in a padded, low-stimulus containment suite at Site-64 designed to minimize injury during disorientation episodes. Because SCP-4129 cannot reliably be informed in advance which point in her subjective timeline she will "wake up" into on a given day, all containment staff begin each shift by presenting a standardized orientation card listing the current date and a summary of SCP-4129's containment status, worded neutrally enough to be comprehensible regardless of which period of her life she currently believes herself to be experiencing. Physical restraint is not authorized except during documented instances of self-harm risk, as SCP-4129 has not been observed to pose a danger to others.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4129 is Ms. Nurcan Ateş (b. 1979), who, since an undetermined point believed to be early 2015, experiences each 24-hour period as corresponding to a different, effectively random point along her own personal timeline, spanning from approximately age six to several apparent "future" states not yet reached by her chronological body. On a given day, SCP-4129 may report, and appear to genuinely believe, that she is experiencing a specific day from her childhood, her twenties, or an event she has not yet lived through according to standard chronology, including at least one instance in which she described, in specific and later partially verified detail, the death of an acquaintance who was, at the time of the description, still alive and in good health (see Incident 4129-3).

SCP-4129's body does not physically regress or change; she remains, in all measurable physical respects, a woman of her true chronological age. However, her behavior, vocabulary, apparent physical coordination, and self-reported knowledge consistently and convincingly match whichever period she believes herself to be in, including displaying skills she has not yet learned (in "past" states) or has since forgotten (in states corresponding to age-related decline she has not yet chronologically reached).

SCP-4129 does not form continuous new memories of her time in Foundation custody; each day, she must be reoriented, and from her perspective, days in containment do not follow one another in sequence but are experienced as isolated points scattered across a lifetime she cannot place in order. She is aware, within any given day, that "something is wrong" with her sense of time, but is not consistently aware that she is a contained Foundation subject, as this fact does not appear to exist in most of the periods she visits.

Family members interviewed prior to containment describe a woman who "aged unevenly" in the years preceding her disappearance from public records in 2015, at times behaving with the maturity and memory of a small child and at other times displaying knowledge of events that had not yet occurred.

ADDENDUM 4129-A: Incident 4129-3 remains under review by the Site-64 Temporal Anomalies Liaison. The acquaintance described by SCP-4129 died under the specific circumstances she described approximately fourteen months after the interview. No further predictive statements from SCP-4129 have been solicited, per standing ethical guidance, though several have reportedly been made unprompted.

SCP-4130.name: The Man Who Was Always Here
SCP-4130.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4130 continues in his prior role as general maintenance staff at Site-19 under the cover designation "Facilities Technician Yusuf Karaca," a role he has occupied, per personnel records, since the site's construction in 1987. SCP-4130 has not been formally informed of the full scope of his anomalous status and continues to believe himself to be an ordinary, long-tenured Foundation employee of unusually good health. This arrangement is maintained under Directive 4130-Green, authorized at O5 discretion, which classifies SCP-4130 as a Thaumiel-designated asset whose continued unawareness is deemed necessary to preserve behavioral baseline for study and for his availability during high-lethality site incidents. Personnel with a legitimate need to interact with SCP-4130 regarding his true nature must first obtain clearance from the Site-19 Director.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4130 presents outwardly as a man in his early sixties. Personnel records place his birth in 1951, which would make him 75 at time of writing; medical examination is consistent with a biological age of approximately 55–60 and has not changed measurably across at least fourteen years of periodic covert physical assessment. SCP-4130 does not appear to age at a normal rate, does not scar from injuries sustained in the course of his duties, and has, per incident logs, been present at and apparently unharmed by no fewer than six (6) site-threatening containment breaches, structural collapses, or exposure events since 1987 that resulted in fatalities among other on-site personnel.

SCP-4130's continued employment at Site-19 predates any documented awareness by Foundation personnel of his anomalous nature; internal audits suggest that his unusual survival record was, for approximately two decades, attributed by successive site administrations to "good luck" and procedural caution, and was not formally flagged for review until a 2009 records audit noted that his personnel file had not been meaningfully updated in over twenty years.

Discreet inquiry (see Interview 4130-1) suggests SCP-4130 has no awareness that his survival or apparent longevity is anomalous. When indirectly asked by an interviewer posing as an HR auditor about his time at the Foundation, SCP-4130 attributed his continued employment to enjoying the work and stated that he had "been lucky, health-wise," attributing a shrapnel injury during a 1994 containment breach, which produced no lasting scar tissue on subsequent examination, to "a good doctor."

Current Foundation policy, as set by Directive 4130-Green, is not to disclose SCP-4130's status to him, on the stated grounds that doing so carries unknown risk to whatever mechanism underlies his survivability, and that his continued willingness to perform maintenance duties in hazardous site areas provides operational value that a fully informed subject might decline to continue providing.

ADDENDUM 4130-A: A minority dissent was filed by Dr. Oyelaran of Site-19 Ethics Committee, arguing that SCP-4130's consent to hazardous duty, obtained without disclosure of the relevant facts about his own body, cannot be considered informed. The dissent was noted and Directive 4130-Green was upheld without amendment.

SCP-4131.name: The Shadow That Confesses
SCP-4131.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4131 is housed in a private quarters at Site-64 equipped with adjustable, redundant lighting designed to minimize the casting of sharp-edged shadows; complete elimination of SCP-4131's shadow is not achievable under any lighting configuration tested to date. Personnel entering SCP-4131's quarters must be briefed in advance that SCP-4131-1 (the anomalous shadow) may verbally address them and are instructed not to respond to or otherwise engage SCP-4131-1 directly, but to direct any concerns raised by its statements to the assigned on-site psychologist. SCP-4131 has requested, and been granted, minimal social contact.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4131 is Mr. Barış Keskin (b. 1988), whose cast shadow, under any light source, behaves as an ordinary shadow in terms of shape and movement but is additionally capable of speech, audible to any person within approximately four meters, in a voice resembling a quieter, flatter register of Mr. Keskin's own. SCP-4131-1 does not require Mr. Keskin's participation or awareness to speak and has been recorded doing so while Mr. Keskin was asleep.

SCP-4131-1's statements consistently take the form of factual-sounding disclosures about Mr. Keskin's private thoughts, feelings, or past actions, typically ones Mr. Keskin has not voluntarily disclosed and would prefer not to. Verified examples include SCP-4131-1 informing a visiting relative of an affair Mr. Keskin had concealed for six years, and informing containment staff, unprompted, of the precise wording of derogatory thoughts Mr. Keskin reported having had about a specific staff member earlier that day. Mr. Keskin has confirmed the accuracy of all such statements when subsequently questioned, generally with visible distress.

Mr. Keskin was referred to Foundation attention after his prior employer terminated him following SCP-4131-1's disclosure, during a client meeting, of Mr. Keskin's private opinion of the client. Mr. Keskin did not initially believe his own shadow was speaking and sought psychiatric treatment for auditory hallucination prior to Foundation contact; he has since accepted the anomaly's reality but describes it as "like being followed by someone who already knows I'm guilty."

Of particular concern is a developing pattern first logged in Session 4131-19, in which SCP-4131-1 has, on four occasions, disclosed information about an action Mr. Keskin had not yet taken at the time of disclosure but went on to take within the following 48 hours (in each case, a minor act Mr. Keskin later described as impulsive and out of character, including one instance of shoplifting). Mr. Keskin denies having consciously planned any of these actions in advance. Whether SCP-4131-1 is disclosing intentions Mr. Keskin is unaware of holding, or is in some manner influencing his subsequent behavior, has not been determined.

ADDENDUM 4131-A: Mr. Keskin has requested that his shadow be surgically or otherwise permanently removed, a request the Foundation has declined to act on pending further research, citing both uncertain medical feasibility and the unknown consequences of severing SCP-4131-1 from its source.

SCP-4132.name: The Child Who Rewrites Constants
SCP-4132.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4132 is contained in a specially constructed nursery-style suite at Site-88, isolated by a minimum of two structurally independent containment shells to limit the physical range of anomalous effects. SCP-4132 is provided with writing materials restricted to a single supervised classroom period per day; all paper used during this period is collected, sealed in a Faraday-shielded document safe, and reviewed off-site by no fewer than two Level 3 mathematics personnel before disposal or archival. SCP-4132 is not, under any circumstance, to be provided with a writing instrument outside of supervised sessions, nor permitted access to a chalkboard, tablet, or any other surface capable of retaining a written mark.

Any written material produced by SCP-4132 that is read and cognitively parsed as mathematical notation by another individual carries a containment risk and must not be transmitted, photographed, or verbally described in detail outside of cleared review personnel. Personnel assigned to SCP-4132 review are limited to two consecutive sessions before mandatory forty-eight-hour rotation off duty, per recommendation following Incident 4132-1.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4132 is a boy, age 8, referred to Foundation attention following a classroom incident at a primary school in Konya in which a locally isolated but measurable and repeatable alteration of gravitational acceleration (recorded between 8.9 and 11.3 m/s², reverting to standard values after approximately six minutes) occurred in a 4-meter radius around SCP-4132's desk while he completed an unassigned arithmetic exercise in the margin of his notebook.

Subsequent controlled testing has established that SCP-4132, when permitted to write mathematical expressions of his own invention (rather than copy existing formulae, which produces no effect), is capable of producing notation that, when read and mentally processed by a second party, induces localized, temporary alteration of one or more physical constants within an area roughly proportional to the complexity of the expression and the number of individuals who have read it. Confirmed alterations to date include local gravitational acceleration, the apparent speed of falling objects independent of mass (Incident 4132-1, addressed below), and, in one instance, a temporary and localized alteration to the freezing point of water within the testing chamber.

SCP-4132 does not appear to understand that his writing produces these effects and has expressed enjoyment and pride when shown (heavily redacted, indirect) evidence that his "number games," as he calls them, are considered special. He has requested, on multiple occasions, to be allowed to "show" his equations to other children, a request that has been declined without explanation acceptable to him. Foundation child psychologists assigned to his case have expressed concern regarding the long-term psychological impact of restricting a child's primary creative outlet without providing him a comprehensible reason.

Incident 4132-1: During a supervised session, a reviewing researcher read an unredacted equation before proper isolation protocol was completed. The researcher and one additional staff member present in the observation room experienced localized alteration of perceived gravitational direction for approximately ninety seconds, resulting in one minor injury. SCP-4132, observing the incident through one-way glass, is reported to have asked why the researcher had "fallen sideways," apparently unaware of any causal connection to his own work.

ADDENDUM 4132-A: Foundation mathematics staff have thus far been unable to determine whether SCP-4132's capability is a property of his cognition, of a specific inherited or acquired trait, or of some external influence on him. No family history of similar phenomena has been identified.

SCP-4133.name: The Sister Who Returns
SCP-4133.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4133 is housed in a standard humanoid containment suite at Site-64, modified with dual nameplates and dual sets of personal effects to accommodate both resident personas. Staff interacting with SCP-4133 are required to check the illuminated indicator outside the containment suite, updated by SCP-4133's own report at the onset of each transition, denoting which of the two personas identified below is currently in control, and to address SCP-4133 accordingly. Both personas have been granted equal standing under Foundation subject-welfare policy pending resolution of Legal Advisory 4133-1 (see below).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4133 is the body of Ms. Derya Aksoy (b. 1996), who presents, on an unpredictable but roughly weekly basis, a secondary and behaviorally distinct persona identifying herself as Ms. Aksoy's twin sister, Deniz, who per all available civil records did not survive infancy, having died at eleven days old in 1996 of causes recorded as unrelated to Ms. Aksoy's own survival. SCP-4133-2 ("Deniz") displays a distinct handwriting sample, distinct food preferences, a divergent (though overlapping) set of childhood memories from Ms. Aksoy's own, and consistent, testable recall of details regarding the Aksoy family's life in a small town in Rize that Ms. Aksoy herself either does not know or has never mentioned, several of which have been independently corroborated by surviving family members who were not made aware of the nature of the inquiry.

Transitions between SCP-4133-1 ("Derya") and SCP-4133-2 ("Deniz") occur without external trigger identified to date, typically over a period of one to four minutes, during which the subject reports disorientation, and are accompanied by a measurable and repeatable shift in EEG pattern of a magnitude not ordinarily associated with dissociative identity presentations absent this anomaly's documented physical correlates (see Document 4133-B). Each persona reports full awareness of "losing time" during the other's control but no access to the other's memories from that period.

Ms. Aksoy has stated she does not experience the arrangement as unwelcome, describing it as "having gotten used to sharing," but has also stated, during a period of persona control identified as SCP-4133-2, that she (as Deniz) resents "being let out only sometimes" and asked Foundation staff directly whether "the sister who got to live" was aware that Deniz remembered dying. Ms. Aksoy, upon returning to control, had no memory of this specific statement having been made.

Legal Advisory 4133-1, filed by Site-64 Ethics Committee, notes unresolved questions regarding whether SCP-4133-2 constitutes a legally and ethically distinct person entitled to independent consideration in matters of subject welfare and containment consultation, and recommends that no procedure be performed on SCP-4133 without the concurrent, informed consent of whichever persona is in control at the time such consent is sought, with any procedure requiring the consent of both to be deferred.

ADDENDUM 4133-A: SCP-4133-2 ("Deniz") has, on three occasions, requested access to Deniz Aksoy's unmarked grave, located in a family plot in Rize. The request has not been approved, pending unresolved logistical and security concerns regarding transport of SCP-4133 outside Foundation facilities.

SCP-4134.name: The Man Who Cannot Be Executed
SCP-4134.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4134 is held at Site-45 under a modified high-security asset agreement (see Document 4134-Consent) rather than standard humanoid containment protocol, in recognition of his classification as a Thaumiel-designated operational asset. SCP-4134 is deployed exclusively on Mobile Task Force operations designated maximum-lethality-risk, under the operational name "Recovery Asset Onbaşı," and is returned to Site-45 medical monitoring following each deployment for a mandatory 72-hour recovery and evaluation period regardless of apparent physical status. SCP-4134 retains, per the terms of Document 4134-Consent, the standing right to decline any specific deployment without penalty, a right he has exercised on four documented occasions.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4134 is Mr. Kaan Yıldıray (b. 1982), formerly an inmate held under capital sentence at a maximum-security facility, whose scheduled execution in 2016 did not result in death despite confirmed and complete cessation of cardiac and respiratory function for a documented period of eleven minutes, following which SCP-4134 spontaneously resumed normal physiological function without medical intervention. Subsequent covert Foundation investigation, prompted by irregularities in the facility's incident reporting, confirmed that SCP-4134 does not retain injuries sustained through conventional lethal trauma, regenerating from wounds including, per controlled testing under Foundation supervision, penetrating gunshot trauma, exsanguination, and asphyxiation, with full functional recovery typically occurring within 20–40 minutes depending on injury severity.

SCP-4134 retains full awareness of his condition and has stated that he first became aware of it following an unrelated, near-fatal assault during incarceration years prior to his scheduled execution, an incident he did not report to facility staff at the time out of what he has described as fear of "becoming someone's experiment," a characterization he has since stated he considers to have been accurate regarding his present circumstances.

SCP-4134 was extended a formal offer of conditional employment as a high-risk operational asset in exchange for review of his original criminal conviction, which Foundation legal liaisons have since determined to have relied on since-discredited forensic testimony; this review remains procedurally frozen, as SCP-4134's continued classification as deceased in civil records (a status never corrected following his 2016 non-execution, which the original facility recorded as successful) has been assessed by Foundation legal staff as operationally convenient and has, to date, not been corrected.

SCP-4134 has participated in eleven MTF operations to date, sustaining injuries assessed as fatal to an ordinary human in six of these instances, and has recovered from each. He has expressed, in mandatory post-deployment psychological evaluation, ambivalence regarding both his continued survival and his continued employment, stating on one occasion: "I didn't ask to stop being able to die. I don't know that I'd have asked to keep going, either."

ADDENDUM 4134-A: A formal request by SCP-4134 for restoration of his legal civil status has been noted by Site-45 Legal but has not been acted upon as of this writing, cited internally as "pending operational review."

SCP-4135.name: The Interpreter Whose Words Become True
SCP-4135.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4135 is housed in a sound-isolated suite at Site-19, and, per amended protocol following Incident 4135-2, is not to be verbally addressed regarding, nor permitted to verbally translate, any statement, document, or artifact whose content is not first cleared by a Level 4 review panel and assessed for retroactive-alteration risk. SCP-4135 communicates with assigned personnel exclusively in writing, which has not been observed to produce anomalous effects, and is permitted to speak aloud only during scheduled, isolated testing sessions in a chamber lined with passive audio dampening and staffed by a minimum number of personnel necessary, all volunteers briefed on and accepting the specific risk involved.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4135 is Ms. Ceyda Yalman (b. 1985), a former conference interpreter fluent in eleven languages, who possesses the ability, activated exclusively through spoken (not written or signed) translation of a statement from one language to another, to cause the historical record — encompassing not only documents and recordings but the memories of all persons aware of the original event — to retroactively conform to the content of her spoken translation, rather than to the original statement, in any case where the two differ.

Under ordinary circumstances, where SCP-4135 translates accurately, this property produces no detectable effect, as her translation and the original statement's meaning align. The anomaly was identified after a 2018 diplomatic function at which SCP-4135, working as a contracted interpreter, made an inadvertent translation error rendering a minor procedural remark as a substantially different statement; multiple attendees, including the original speaker, subsequently and consistently recalled having said the substituted statement, and official meeting minutes, transcribed in real time by an unrelated stenographer, reflected the altered wording rather than what had been said.

The scope of SCP-4135's prior professional interpretation work, conducted over a fourteen-year career across numerous unspecified international and governmental settings prior to Foundation containment, cannot be fully audited, as any investigation into the accuracy of her past translations would necessarily rely on records that may themselves already reflect her alterations rather than original events. A dedicated Foundation working group (Task Force Delta-19 "Loanwords") has been assigned to attempt reconstruction of the extent of historical divergence attributable to SCP-4135's career, with limited success to date.

Incident 4135-2: During an authorized testing session in which SCP-4135 was asked to translate a passage from a recovered anomalous text under controlled conditions, a minor unscripted mistranslation of a single term produced a measurable and still only partially reverted alteration to the recorded provenance history of the source artifact, affecting Foundation archival records dated as far back as 1962, three decades prior to the artifact's actual documented recovery. The full scope of Incident 4135-2's downstream effects on related archival material remains under active investigation.

SCP-4135 is cooperative, describes her ability as "the only thing I was ever good at, gone wrong," and has voluntarily restricted her own spoken communication since learning the nature of her anomaly, reportedly out of specific concern for accidentally altering the history of people she cares about.

ADDENDUM 4135-A: Following Incident 4135-2, SCP-4135 requested that all future testing be conducted using material with no surviving witnesses or corroborating original-language record, "so that if I get it wrong, there's nothing true left to overwrite."

SCP-4136.name: The Couple Who Share One Voice
SCP-4136.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4136-1 and SCP-4136-2 are housed together in a single adapted residential unit at Site-77 furnished to approximate an ordinary retirement home apartment, per the recommendation of Site-77 psychological staff that separation of the two subjects be avoided except for brief, monitored intervals required for independent medical assessment. Any such separation is capped at a maximum of ninety (90) minutes and is to be immediately discontinued if either subject displays the distress indicators catalogued in Document 4136-B. Weekly, non-separating interviews are conducted with both subjects present to assess condition stability.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4136 designates Mr. Hasan Erim (-1, b. 1943) and Mrs. Nermin Erim (-2, b. 1945), a married couple of 52 years at time of containment, who present a consistent and, to date, unexplained anomaly in verbal communication: when speaking on any topic in each other's presence, SCP-4136-1 and -2 do not merely finish one another's sentences in the conventional sense achieved by long-familiar couples, but produce continuous grammatically coherent statements in which individual words, and at times mid-word syllables, alternate between the two speakers without any observed hesitation, overlap, or communicative error, at a pace and precision inconsistent with conscious turn-taking.

Neurological monitoring conducted during Session 4136-7 recorded near-simultaneous activation of language-production regions in both subjects' brains during these exchanges, beginning consistently 40–80 milliseconds before either subject began vocalizing their portion of the shared sentence, a timing inconsistent with one subject reacting to the other's speech and more consistent with both subjects producing a single, shared linguistic output simultaneously planned between two separate nervous systems by a mechanism not yet identified.

When separated, both subjects retain the ability to speak normally and independently, though both report the experience as "talking with one hand" and both have, independently and using notably similar language, described prolonged separation as feeling "like losing half my words, not half my thoughts." Foundation psychological staff have not yet determined the origin point of the anomaly; family interviews and available medical records indicate the behavior was not present, or was not noted, during the first three decades of the couple's marriage and appears, per the couple's own account, to have begun gradually sometime after Mrs. Erim's 2009 stroke, from which she recovered with no lasting language impairment according to her treating physicians at the time.

Both subjects are aware of the anomaly, regard it without apparent distress, and have declined all offers of intervention aimed at "restoring" independent speech patterns, with Mr. Erim stating during intake interview: "We've been finishing each other's sentences for fifty years. I don't know why it would frighten anyone that we finally got good at it."

ADDENDUM 4136-A: Site-77 medical staff have flagged, without further comment pending Ethics Committee review, the unresolved question of what will occur to the surviving spouse's speech pattern in the event of the other's death, and whether continued containment planning should account for the possibility that the anomaly does not resolve into "normal" independent speech but into some form of persistent linguistic absence.

SCP-4137.name: The House on Kestrel Court
SCP-4137.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The property at [REDACTED] Kestrel Court, ██████, Ohio has been acquired by the Foundation through the shell holding company Meridian Property Trust and is maintained in a vacant, unlisted state. A two-person team is stationed in an unmarked vehicle outside the property at all times. The interior is not to be entered by fewer than three personnel simultaneously.

All entry personnel must carry a mechanical, non-electronic room counter and record a room count immediately upon entry and immediately prior to exit. Any discrepancy between these counts is to be reported to the on-site supervisor before the team proceeds further into the structure. Electronic recording equipment may be used but its footage is considered unreliable for real-time verification (see Description) and is to be reviewed only after the fact, by personnel who did not participate in the entry.

An entry team that misses two consecutive 20-minute radio check-ins is to be considered lost, not overdue, and no further personnel are to be sent in pursuit without written authorization from a Level 4 supervisor.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4137 is a two-story single-family residence built in 1962, presenting a stable, non-anomalous exterior consistent with its listed floor area of approximately 140 square meters. Personnel physically present inside SCP-4137 and actively counting rooms will count seven: a kitchen, a living room, a dining room, three bedrooms, and one bathroom, matching the structure's original blueprints and tax records.

Recorded footage of the interior, reviewed after the fact, does not agree with this figure. Hallways confirmed by an entry team to terminate in a load-bearing wall are shown, on the recording, to instead continue to a door the team did not open and in most cases did not perceive at all. This discrepancy is never present during the entry itself — only in the recording, and only once the recording is reviewed by someone who was not present for the events depicted. A second review of the same footage by the same or a different viewer will show the same discrepancy in the same place, provided that viewer was likewise absent during the original entry.

The mechanism does not require an unattended camera, an empty house, or any period of total non-observation. It requires only that a given section of the structure's interior cease to be the specific focus of a person's attention, however briefly, and however many other people remain elsewhere in the house at the time.

Personnel who do walk through one of these anomalous doors report no sensation of exceeding the confirmed exterior boundary of the house. Nine such expansions (SCP-4137-1 through -9) have been documented since Foundation acquisition. Four have since become inaccessible; the hallways that led to them once again terminate in the original wall, and no personnel who entered them have been recovered. Five remain accessible, including 4137-4, a windowless room furnished as a nursery with no correlate in any blueprint, permit, or prior-owner interview, and 4137-7, a descending stairwell that has been walked eleven times without personnel reaching its end, each attempt halted by mandatory one-hour recall.

ADDENDUM 4137-A: Incident 4137-3. On ██/██/20██, a three-person team (D-9231, D-9245, Researcher Voss) entered to survey 4137-4. Voss's counter read seven rooms at entry. Radio contact was lost at the 40-minute check-in. A recovery team entered nine minutes later and found the house's interior matching its baseline seven-room configuration exactly. No door corresponding to 4137-4 was present. No occupant of the house, prior owner, or contractor has ever independently corroborated that a nursery existed at that location, though photographs taken by earlier Foundation teams confirming 4137-4's existence remain on file and have not changed. D-9231, D-9245, and Researcher Voss remain unaccounted for.

SCP-4138.name: The Patient Mile
SCP-4138.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4138 comprises a 1.6-kilometer segment of [REDACTED] Route ██ between mile markers 41 and 42, in a sparsely populated rural stretch of ██████ County. The Foundation, operating under the cover identity of a state highway resurfacing contractor, has posted a permanent reduced-speed construction zone (25 mph) across the affected segment, supported by radar-triggered warning signage and two unmarked speed-camera units.

Civilian traffic is not restricted from the segment, as consistent compliance with the posted limit fully prevents anomalous activation. Foundation vehicles transiting SCP-4138 for containment purposes must not exceed 25 mph under any circumstances and must carry a functioning odometer log. Any vehicle observed on camera to enter SCP-4138 above 45 mph is to be flagged for Mobile Task Force Epsilon-6 (Roadkill) follow-up, including a welfare check on the registered owner if the vehicle does not exit the segment within four minutes of entry.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4138 induces temporal displacement in any vehicle that exceeds 45 mph while inside its boundaries. Upon exceeding this threshold, the vehicle's exit point at mile marker 42 is replaced by a re-entry at mile marker 41, with occupants experiencing no discontinuity of motion or consciousness. Externally elapsed time resets to the moment of the vehicle's original entry into the segment; internally, occupants perceive four to seven minutes of continuous driving between iterations, and vehicle systems (odometer, fuel gauge, engine hour meter) register this driving as genuine, accumulating mileage and consuming fuel accordingly across repeated loops.

The loop terminates under either of two conditions: the vehicle's speed drops below and remains below 45 mph for a continuous 30-second interval, or an external factor forces the vehicle to stop entirely (fuel exhaustion, mechanical failure, collision). In the former case, the vehicle exits SCP-4138 normally at mile marker 42 with external elapsed time matching only the time of the final, sub-threshold pass — prior loop iterations are not reflected in the outside world's clock, though they are reflected in the vehicle's fuel consumption and mileage, producing a discrepancy noted in several police reports predating Foundation awareness of SCP-4138 (drivers running out of gas after driving what they insist was a single, short stretch of road).

In the latter case, outcomes vary. Personnel interviews with surviving civilians recovered from forced stops describe the landscape outside the vehicle during the loop as static and repeating — the same fence post, the same dead tree, the same mile-42 sign approaching and never quite arriving before the loop resets. No civilian has reported seeing another vehicle during an active loop, including vehicles independently confirmed by camera to have entered SCP-4138 within the same window.

Six vehicles are known to have entered SCP-4138 above the activation threshold and never exited by either termination condition. Roadside search of the segment's shoulder and adjacent field in each case recovered no wreckage. Owners of these vehicles were issued standard missing-persons amnestic cover stories.

ADDENDUM 4138-A: Foundation test driver testimony (Agent Corel, authorized single-loop trial, 52 mph, terminated after one loop by voluntary deceleration) states that the fence post and dead tree described by civilian survivors were visible and unmistakably identical on each pass, and that the mile-42 sign was legible enough, in the final seconds before the loop reset, to note that its posted distance read '1 MI' regardless of how much of the segment had actually been driven.

SCP-4139.name: The Adaptive Elevator
SCP-4139.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4139 is located within the north passenger elevator of the ██████ Building, a 22-story commercial office tower in downtown ██████. The Foundation maintains control of the building through a majority-owned property management subsidiary. The elevator remains in public use; occupancy is passively regulated by adjusting arrival intervals and lobby signage to discourage groups of exactly six persons from boarding together, as this specific occupancy count is the sole known trigger for anomalous activation.

Should a group of six board SCP-4139 despite these measures, on-site personnel (posted as building security) are to monitor the floor indicator from the lobby security desk. If the indicator displays any value above 22 or below 1, the elevator is not to be recalled or interrupted; personnel are to await its return to the lobby and debrief any exiting passengers under the pretense of a maintenance inspection, administering Class A amnestics as needed.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4139 is a standard hydraulic passenger elevator serving all 22 floors of the ██████ Building, installed during the building's 1988 renovation. Under normal occupancy (any number of passengers other than exactly six), the elevator functions without deviation from manufacturer specifications.

When exactly six passengers are present in the car at the moment its doors close, the floor selection panel displays two additional, unlabeled buttons below the button for Floor 1. Pressing either button, or failing to press any button within 40 seconds, causes the elevator to travel to a floor not present in the building's architectural plans. The indicator above the doors displays a number consistent with continued descent (observed values include -3, -11, and, in one instance, -140), though the duration of travel does not scale with the apparent distance; all recorded descents have concluded within 90 seconds regardless of indicated floor.

The floors accessed in this manner consistently present as unoccupied, fluorescent-lit office space architecturally identical to a genuine floor of the ██████ Building — same carpet, same partition layout, same restroom placement — furnished with cubicles, desks, and personal effects (family photographs, desk plants, coffee mugs bearing employee names not found in any tenant company's personnel records) suggesting recent, ordinary occupancy. No windows are present on these floors; exterior-facing walls where windows would be expected are solid and, when tested, register as significantly thicker than the building's actual exterior walls. Wall clocks on these floors, when present, consistently read 3:17, regardless of the actual time of arrival.

Passengers who exit onto an anomalous floor and re-board the elevator are returned to the lobby without incident, typically reporting mild disorientation but no missing time. Passengers who remain on an anomalous floor beyond approximately eleven minutes (the interval is inferred, not confirmed, from the two cases below) have not been recovered by elevator; both known cases were later found using the building's standard stairwell, on a legitimate floor, with nine days of missing time and no memory of the elevator ride that preceded it.

ADDENDUM 4139-A: A phone found among the personal effects of an anomalous floor's cubicle, recovered during an authorized Foundation sweep, retained partial charge and displayed a lock screen wallpaper depicting a group photograph of six unidentified individuals standing in the ██████ Building's actual lobby. None of the six match any employee, tenant, or visitor on record for the building.

SCP-4140.name: The Well That Remembers
SCP-4140.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4140 is a stone-lined well located on private agricultural land near the village of ██████, ██████ Province, Turkey. The Foundation acquired the surrounding 4-hectare parcel through a local agricultural cooperative front and has restricted access with fencing consistent with livestock containment. A two-person team monitors the site from an adjacent structure disguised as a tool shed.

Objects are not to be deliberately thrown into SCP-4140 without Level 3 authorization and a pre-registered description of the object, logged in the SCP-4140 Return Registry prior to the throw. Villagers historically permitted informal access to the well; this access has been discontinued under the cover story of groundwater contamination. Any object recovered in the village or its surroundings matching a registry entry is to be retrieved and the finder amnesticized if the object's altered condition was noticed and remarked upon.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4140 is a well of conventional construction, approximately 11 meters deep, dry at the bottom, and dated by masonry style to the late Ottoman period. Objects deliberately dropped into SCP-4140 vanish before striking the bottom, consistently and without exception, as confirmed by weighted-camera drops that record the object's disappearance between 6 and 7 meters of depth.

Between three days and several years later (interval unpredictable and not correlated with object type, size, or composition), a corresponding object reappears somewhere within approximately 12 kilometers of SCP-4140, altered in a manner consistent with having undergone a plausible, complete history in the intervening period — one it did not actually have. A wristwatch dropped into the well in 1987 (per informal village record, predating Foundation involvement) resurfaced in 2004 among the effects of a deceased villager who had never owned it, worn smooth in a pattern matching seventeen years of use, and inscribed on the reverse with a repair shop's mark from a shop that, per municipal records, had closed in 1979.

The reappeared object is never observed in transit; it is simply found, already integrated into some circumstance — tucked in a drawer, sewn into a lining, buried at a depth suggesting years of soil accumulation — that a straightforward, uneventful history would produce, without any witness account of it arriving there. In 41 of 44 fully documented cases, the object's fabricated history is internally consistent and independently corroborable against unrelated records (receipts, other individuals' memories, wear patterns matching known usage). In the remaining three cases, the object's apparent history could not be reconciled with any known person, event, or transaction, suggesting either an undiscovered node of the effect's false history or a history assigned to no one.

Live subjects who have fallen into SCP-4140 (four documented instances, all prior to Foundation containment) were not recovered by the well. Two were later identified: one returned to the village nineteen years after falling in, by his own account absent no more than a few minutes, while the rest of the village had aged accordingly around him; the other has not been seen but is referenced, twenty-two years after his disappearance, in a set of forged-appearing but internally consistent letters postmarked from a city he has no independent record of ever having visited, addressed to a sister who insists she never received them until they were found, undelivered and unexplained, at the bottom of the well.

SCP-4141.name: Level B-Minus
SCP-4141.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4141 comprises parking stall B3-117 within the ██████ Street underground parking structure, ██████, and its associated anomalous effects. The Foundation has acquired the parking structure through a municipal contracting front and permanently marked stall B3-117 as reserved for structural inspection, blocking it with a physical barrier.

Vehicles are no longer permitted to park in stall B3-117. Standing containment consists of weekly inspection of levels B1 through B4 for the presence of vehicles not accounted for in the structure's current parking log, and monthly inspection of the two confirmed anomalous sub-levels (designated B4-A and B5-A; see Description) via the single known access route, a maintenance stairwell door on B4 that leads to B4-A on approximately 1 in 30 attempts and to the ordinary ground floor lobby on all others, unpredictably.

DESCRIPTION:

Prior to 2019, stall B3-117 was in ordinary use. Between 2019 and the present, 26 vehicles parked in this stall for a duration exceeding four hours have failed to be present in the stall upon owner return, despite no exit having been logged by the structure's automated gate system and no report of theft yielding recovery.

Of these 26 vehicles, 19 were subsequently located elsewhere within the same parking structure, on levels and in stalls inconsistent with their owners' possession of a valid gate ticket for that level, with odometer readings elevated by amounts ranging from 4 to 380 kilometers beyond the reading at time of parking, and in six cases bearing damage (scraping, denting) not present when parked and not matched to any recorded incident within the structure.

Five vehicles were located on B4-A, a level physically resembling B4 in construction, lighting, and signage but absent from the structure's architectural plans, accessible (as noted above) only via unpredictable use of the B4 maintenance stairwell. B4-A's stall numbering duplicates B4's exactly; Foundation personnel who have parked test vehicles on B4-A and attempted to relocate them via the interior ramp system report the ramp terminating, after several turns fewer than the true structure requires, in a level resembling B5, subsequently designated B5-A, and not further explored following the loss of Agent Halloran during the second such attempt (see Addendum).

Two vehicles remain unaccounted for.

Personnel entering B4-A report no unusual sensation and no difficulty believing themselves to be on the structure's true B4 level; the discrepancy is apparent only through comparison with the vehicle log, direct architectural measurement, or prior familiarity with B4's actual layout sufficient to notice absent features (a fire extinguisher cabinet present on true B4 is absent on B4-A; a support column is present on B4-A that has no corresponding column on true B4 or in any structural drawing).

ADDENDUM 4141-A: Agent Halloran entered B4-A via the maintenance stairwell to retrieve a test vehicle and, per radio contact, proceeded via interior ramp toward B5-A after the vehicle could not be located on B4-A. Contact was lost 4 minutes later. A search team entered the same stairwell eleven times over the following six hours; the door led to B4-A twice, and to the ordinary lobby the remaining nine times. Halloran was not found on either occasion access to B4-A was achieved. The stall Halloran's test vehicle had occupied on true B4 has, as of this writing, not been reassigned.

SCP-4142.name: The Recitation Room
SCP-4142.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4142 is contained within Special Collections Reading Room 3 (the Room) of the ██████ Library, acquired by the Foundation in 1974 following Incident 4142-1 (see Addendum) and relocated, structurally intact, to Site-77. Access requires Level 3 clearance and pre-approval of any text to be read aloud within the Room by the SCP-4142 Textual Review Committee.

No individual is to read aloud from any unapproved text while inside the Room under any circumstance. Approved texts are restricted to material assessed by the Committee as low in descriptive specificity (technical manuals, tabular data, legal boilerplate); narrative or richly descriptive material of any kind, including material submitted for containment-adjacent research purposes, is prohibited. Reading sessions are limited to two personnel and 20 minutes, with a designated reader and a designated observer who does not read.

Manifestations accumulated within the Room prior to Foundation acquisition (see Description) are not to be removed, destroyed, or interacted with beyond passive observation without separate authorization, as several are non-inert.

DESCRIPTION:
