SCP-4142 causes descriptive text, when read aloud by a human voice within the boundaries of the Room, to partially manifest as physical matter within the Room, proportional in completeness and fidelity to the specificity and vividness of the description. A passage describing a table in general terms may produce nothing perceptible; a passage describing a specific, richly detailed table will produce a table matching that description, appearing without transition at a location consistent with the passage's description of its position, or at the nearest available floor space if unspecified.

Manifestations do not reliably cease when reading stops or the text is closed. Approximately 60% of manifestations documented prior to Foundation acquisition have persisted indefinitely; the Room's interior currently contains an estimated 340 to 400 individual manifested objects and structural elements accumulated over a documented reading history beginning no later than 1861, including furniture, partial architecture (an internal doorway leading to four meters of manifested hallway terminating in unmanifested — i.e., ordinary, solid — wall), and eleven manifestations classified as non-inert, exhibiting independent motion or response to stimuli consistent with descriptions of living or animate subjects in the source texts.

The Room's true dimensions are approximately 9 by 12 meters; the accumulated manifestations, despite their combined described volume substantially exceeding this footprint, do not appear to violate it from any exterior measurement, a discrepancy Foundation researchers have not resolved.

Manifestation fidelity does not correlate with the manifesting reader's intent, belief, or awareness of SCP-4142's properties; unaware or skeptical readers manifest objects at the same rate as informed ones, provided the text read is sufficiently descriptive. Manifestation also does not require comprehension of the language read; a French-language passage read aloud, without translation, by a monolingual English speaker manifested successfully in Test 4142-19.

ADDENDUM 4142-A: Incident 4142-1. Prior to Foundation acquisition, a library patron read aloud, apparently for personal amusement, an extended passage from an unrecovered novel describing a structure fire in detail. Contemporary accounts describe a fire beginning at the described point of origin within the Room and behaving, in its early spread, consistently with the text rather than with the Room's actual materials and layout, self-extinguishing after approximately four minutes without external intervention and without consuming any pre-existing (non-manifested) material, though two of the Room's prior manifestations were destroyed. The Room was sealed by library staff shortly afterward, unopened for eleven years prior to Foundation contact.

SCP-4143.name: The Town That Isn't Empty
SCP-4143.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4143 refers to the town site of ██████, ██████ County, Nevada, officially depopulated in 1936 and currently designated on public records as a restricted zone under Department of Defense jurisdiction (cover identity: unexploded ordnance testing area). The Foundation maintains this cover through a standing arrangement with military liaison. A 6-kilometer perimeter fence is maintained with warning signage consistent with the cover story.

SCP-4143 is to be monitored remotely via satellite and fixed ground-based camera; physical entry is prohibited except during confirmed non-manifest states (see Description) and requires Level 4 authorization. Manifestation is presently correlated with the combination of ambient temperature below 4°C and sustained wind speeds exceeding 30 km/h from a westerly direction, though this correlation is not fully predictive (11 recorded manifestations under non-matching conditions). Personnel are not to enter SCP-4143 under any circumstances during a confirmed or suspected manifest state.

DESCRIPTION:

Under baseline conditions, SCP-4143 presents as an ordinary ghost town: approximately 40 structures in varying states of collapse, consistent with 90 years of abandonment and Mojave Basin climate exposure, containing no anomalous properties detectable by any instrumentation deployed to date.

Under the conditions described above, SCP-4143 undergoes a manifestation event, typically lasting between 40 minutes and 6 hours. During a manifestation, the town's structures appear, via satellite and ground camera, intact and occupied: lit windows, smoke from chimneys, and approximately 80 to 110 individual human figures visible engaging in activity consistent with domestic and commercial routine in a style of dress dated by Foundation historians to between approximately 1905 and 1925 — predating the town's own recorded founding in 1911 by figures observed in the earliest confirmed manifestation footage (1962), a discrepancy not yet resolved.

Roads leading into SCP-4143 during a manifestation event do not terminate at the town regardless of distance traveled; vehicle and foot approaches, confirmed by GPS tracking in three separate tests, loop back to the perimeter fence after a distance corresponding to the road's actual mapped length, without any subjective sensation of having turned around. This effect is specific to manifestation states; SCP-4143 is freely enterable under baseline conditions.

Personnel who have entered SCP-4143 during a manifestation event (three confirmed instances, all predating Foundation containment protocols) did not experience the road-looping effect and did report successful entry into the town itself. Two of these three did not return. The third, a hunter who entered by report of local law enforcement in 1971, returned 31 years later, in 2002, having by his own account been inside for what he estimated as under an hour, exhibiting no physical aging inconsistent with the elapsed 31 years and expressing confusion regarding the passage of time; he was located by Foundation personnel prior to further public exposure and is currently held under long-term amnestic maintenance and monitoring at Site-77, class alpha, his condition unchanged as of most recent review.

ADDENDUM 4143-A: The 1971 returnee, under interview prior to amnesticization, described the town during his entry as populated but non-interactive — figures visible and audible but unresponsive to his presence, continuing routine activity without acknowledgment, with one exception: a figure he identified as behaving as though it were waiting for him, standing at the town's central intersection for the duration of his visit, which he declined, across eleven subsequent interview sessions, to describe in further detail.

SCP-4144.name: The Thirteenth Bed
SCP-4144.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4144 refers to recurring occupancy anomalies within Ward 4C of ██████ General Hospital, ██████. The Foundation maintains covert monitoring of Ward 4C through two embedded personnel (posted as a charge nurse and a hospital administrator) and access to the ward's electronic records system.

Ward 4C's official licensed capacity is 12 beds. Embedded personnel are to conduct an unannounced physical headcount of the ward once per shift. Should headcount exceed bed count, embedded personnel are to identify the excess patient (designated SCP-4144-1 for the instance in question) without alerting hospital staff to the discrepancy, and are to review that patient's chart for the inconsistencies described below. SCP-4144-1 is not to be directly confronted, restrained, or prevented from occupying a bed, per Incident 4144-2 (see Addendum). Discharge of SCP-4144-1 is to be allowed to proceed without Foundation interference.

DESCRIPTION:

Since at least 1998 (the earliest year for which Ward 4C's records have been digitized and cross-checked), physical headcounts of Ward 4C have intermittently returned a count of 13 patients against the ward's 12 physical beds, with the 13th individual (SCP-4144-1) nonetheless found occupying a bed, indistinguishable in presentation from a legitimate patient.

SCP-4144-1 is not a fixed individual; across 61 documented instances, no two have matched in appearance, sex, apparent age, or presenting condition. In each instance, SCP-4144-1 possesses a complete medical chart, admission record, and identifying documentation indistinguishable in format and content from genuine hospital records, and is treated by staff as an unremarkable, if occasionally forgettable, patient — nursing staff interviewed after the fact frequently cannot recall specific interactions with SCP-4144-1 despite documented care having been provided.

SCP-4144-1's occupied bed corresponds, in each instance, to whichever of the ward's 12 beds is, at that specific moment, in the shortest interval of vacancy between the discharge of one legitimate patient and the admission of the next — typically under two hours. Extended cross-referencing of admission timestamps in 44 of the 61 instances confirms that no bed is ever simultaneously claimed by both a legitimate patient and SCP-4144-1 according to the ward's own records, despite the physical headcount showing 13 occupied beds among 12 physical beds at the moment of counting.

SCP-4144-1 is discharged, on average, within 30 hours of first being noted, via ordinary hospital discharge procedure, and does not reappear under the same chart identity. Following discharge, headcount returns to 12, and SCP-4144-1's chart, while remaining in hospital records, cannot subsequently be matched to any billing record, insurance claim, or follow-up contact, and repeated attempts to locate the discharged individual at their listed address have failed in all cases where attempted.

In four instances, embedded personnel directly addressed SCP-4144-1 with a question regarding their identity or manner of admission. In all four, SCP-4144-1 answered fluently and without apparent distress, but gave an answer subsequently found to be impossible to verify or internally contradictory (in one case, naming an admitting physician who was not on shift, in hospital records, at any point during the previous six months).

ADDENDUM 4144-A: Incident 4144-2. Embedded personnel attempted, in 2011, to physically prevent an identified SCP-4144-1 instance from being assigned a newly vacated bed, redirecting the instance to a waiting area under a false administrative pretext. Ward headcount at the following hourly check nonetheless returned 13, with SCP-4144-1 occupying the intended bed and no staff member, including the embedded nurse who had personally redirected the instance one hour prior, recalling having done so. The instance was not further interfered with. Current protocol reflects the outcome of this incident.

SCP-4145.name: The Single-Crossing Bridge
SCP-4145.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4145 is a pedestrian and single-lane vehicle bridge spanning the ██████ River at ██████, population 900. The Foundation maintains the bridge under cover of a county infrastructure trust and has installed license-plate and pedestrian-recognition cameras at both approaches, feeding a same-day crossing database.

Local residents are not to be prevented from ordinary single daily crossings, which carry no anomalous effect. Any individual flagged by the recognition system as attempting a second crossing within the same calendar day (local time, midnight to midnight) is to be discreetly monitored but not intercepted before the bridge, per Protocol 4145-Return (see Description for rationale). Foundation personnel requiring access to the far side of SCP-4145 more than once per day must use the alternate county road, a 40-minute detour, rather than re-cross the bridge.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4145 permits exactly one uninterrupted crossing per individual per calendar day, in either direction. The bridge itself is unremarkable in construction: stone piers dated to 1911, an iron truss superstructure added in 1948, a span of 74 meters.

An individual attempting a second crossing on a day when they have already completed one does not perceive the bridge as anomalous at the outset. They begin crossing normally. However, the far end of the bridge — visible, apparently approaching at a normal walking or driving pace — does not arrive. GPS tracking of test subjects during a second-crossing attempt confirms the subject's absolute position oscillating within a span of approximately 3 meters near the bridge's midpoint, despite the subject's own sensation of continuous forward progress and despite the far shore remaining visibly, if not measurably, closer with each step.

This state persists until the individual turns back toward their point of origin, at which point they arrive there — not at the bridge's midpoint, but at the original starting bank — within a timeframe consistent with a normal walk of that same distance, and with no subjective memory of the failed crossing, the turning-back, or the intervening time. External observers positioned off the bridge report no comparable discontinuity; they observe the individual walk onto the bridge, and, some minutes later, walk off the same end they entered from, at a pace and manner consistent with an uneventful stroll, with no visible confusion on the individual's part until informed of the elapsed time.

Of 34 documented second-crossing attempts (23 unwitting local residents prior to full Foundation awareness, 11 controlled Foundation tests), 33 resolved via the turning-back mechanism described above. One did not: a resident who, per witness report, continued walking despite apparent effort and increasing distress, was not observed to turn back, and was not subsequently located on either bank, on the bridge itself, or anywhere within the town. No trace of a return crossing was logged by the recognition system, and no first-day crossing exit was ever logged either — the individual's presence on the bridge that day exists only in witness testimony.

ADDENDUM 4145-A: A controlled Foundation test (Agent Iyer, second crossing, tethered with a 90-meter physical line to a fixed point on the origin bank) recorded the tether paying out at a rate consistent with normal walking speed throughout the failed crossing, despite Agent Iyer's GPS-confirmed position not advancing. The full 90 meters of line was extended before the test was aborted by voluntary turning-back at the 6-minute mark. The tether has not been recovered from the bridge; Agent Iyer reports releasing it before turning back but has no memory of doing so.

SCP-4146.name: The Booth of Unmaking
SCP-4146.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4146 is housed within a decommissioned confessional booth relocated to a secure, ecclesiastically-consecrated chamber at Site-77. Use of SCP-4146 is restricted to Foundation operations explicitly authorized by the SCP-4146 Oversight Panel (minimum three O5-appointed members) and is logged under Protocol Yellow-Rite.

Only personnel holding current ordination or equivalent recognized clerical status, independently vetted and cleared for SCP-4146 duty (designated the Listener), may occupy the booth's receiving side. A rotation of four cleared Listeners is currently maintained. Confession content is not to be recorded by any mechanical or electronic means; the Listener's own verbal debrief, given after the session, is the sole permitted record, and is itself subject to partial retroactive alteration (see Description).

SCP-4146 is not to be used to excise events involving civilian casualties, mass-scale anomalous exposure, or any incident above a Foundation-internal severity threshold of 6, absent unanimous Oversight Panel authorization and O5 notification, per Addendum 4146-B.

DESCRIPTION:

An individual who enters SCP-4146's booth and confesses, with sincerity and specific factual detail, to a genuine transgression they personally committed, causes that transgression — and, to a degree correlated with the transgression's severity and the confession's specificity, its downstream consequences and evidentiary record — to be retroactively removed from consensus reality.

The scope of removal varies. Minor transgressions (a personal betrayal, a small theft, a lie with limited consequence) are typically excised cleanly: the act did not happen, no party retains memory of it, and no documentary trace survives, confirmed across 118 controlled tests using pre-registered minor infractions committed by consenting Foundation personnel specifically to be confessed and verified absent afterward.

Larger transgressions are excised less completely, and with side effects that scale unpredictably. In 14 of 31 tests involving moderate-severity confessed incidents (property destruction, non-fatal injury, breach containment events below severity 6), some fragment of the removed event persisted: a single witness retaining a partial, dreamlike memory; a document altered in content but not fully absent; a physical location bearing evidence (a repaired wall, a healed injury) inconsistent with an event that, by every other available record, never occurred.

SCP-4146 is presently classified Thaumiel and deployed operationally to excise Foundation-attributable incidents that would otherwise require conventional, resource-intensive amnestic and cover-story containment: minor anomalous exposure of civilian witnesses, small-scale containment breaches with limited casualties, and comparable events, via confession sessions conducted by personnel who directly caused or are otherwise eligible to confess to the incident in question.

ADDENDUM 4146-A: [Foundation-internal ethics review, name of authoring committee redacted]. The Panel notes that SCP-4146 requires a genuine confessor — Foundation personnel confessing to incidents they did not personally cause, or fabricating detail to increase excision scope, have failed to trigger any anomalous effect in 100% of attempted tests. This constrains SCP-4146's use to personnel with actual, and frequently disciplinary, culpability, a dependency the Panel has flagged as an unresolved operational and ethical liability.

ADDENDUM 4146-B: Incident 4146-9. Following unanimous Oversight authorization, Senior Researcher ██████ confessed to an incident involving [DATA EXPUNGED, severity classification 8] in an attempt to excise Foundation liability for civilian casualties at ██████. The incident was successfully removed from all located documentary and testimonial record. Senior Researcher ██████ was not: subsequent personnel records, background check archives, and payroll history contain no trace of their employment, and Foundation staff who worked directly alongside them for the preceding eleven years report no memory of them upon prompted interview. SCP-4146 has not been used above severity threshold 6 since this incident, pending Panel review that remains, as of this writing, open.

SCP-4147.name: The Stairwell at One Thirty-Seven
SCP-4147.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4147 is located within the main stairwell of Building 3, ██████ housing block, ██████, a nine-story residential structure constructed in 1974 and currently maintained by the Foundation as a low-occupancy building via a municipal housing front, with remaining legitimate residents relocated under standard rehousing cover as leases expire.

Signage has been posted at all stairwell entrances in the local language reading 'COUNTING PROHIBITED — FIRE HAZARD,' which has proven sufficient to prevent the majority of incidental triggers among remaining residents. Personnel required to use the stairwell for containment purposes must be briefed to avoid counting steps, floors, or landings in any form — aloud, subvocally, or via deliberate mental tracking — and are to be accompanied by a second individual tasked solely with interrupting any counting behavior observed or reported by the first.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4147 activates when an individual ascending the stairwell (descent has never triggered the effect) reaches a cumulative count of exactly 137, whether counting individual steps, half-landings, or full floors, provided the counting is continuous from the point of entry and not restarted. The specific number required does not vary between individuals or instances; 137 is confirmed as a constant across all 22 documented activations.

Upon activation, the individual's continued ascent does not exit the stairwell at the building's ninth and final floor as physical measurement confirms it should. Instead, the stairwell continues upward, presenting landings and floor-access doors numbered in a manner consistent with the building's real numbering (10, 11, 12, and so on) despite the building itself terminating at nine floors as confirmed by both exterior observation and non-counting personnel using the same stairwell simultaneously — a discrepancy indicating the effect is localized entirely to the counting individual's experience of the stairwell rather than to the stairwell itself.

Floor-access doors encountered during an active instance of SCP-4147, when opened, lead to hallways and apartment layouts visually identical to Building 3's genuine floors, unoccupied, and are not distinguishable by affected individuals from the building's real interior. Ascent continues, and the loop persists, for as long as the individual continues counting; 19 of 22 documented instances resolved when the affected individual lost count, was interrupted, or deliberately stopped counting, at which point they found themselves on the stairwell's true landing corresponding to their actual, uncounted position, typically within one flight of where they began counting, having subjectively experienced an ascent of a much greater number of floors than the building contains and reporting no injury, though several reported significant fatigue inconsistent with the true, short distance climbed.

The three remaining instances did not resolve via loss of count. Two individuals continued counting past 300 before losing consciousness (attributed to exertion) and were recovered, unconscious, on a genuine floor landing consistent with the building's true layout, with no memory of the ascent past approximately floor 40 in their own recollection. The third individual, a resident who reported to neighbors an intention to 'see how high it goes,' has not been located.

ADDENDUM 4147-A: Building maintenance records predating Foundation acquisition note recurring, unresolved tenant complaints beginning as early as 1979 regarding the stairwell 'not matching itself,' alongside at least four prior tenant disappearances attributed at the time to unrelated causes (three ruled voluntary departure, one unsolved). No prior investigation identified counting as the relevant variable.

SCP-4148.name: The Silo
SCP-4148.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4148 is a decommissioned missile silo complex located in a restricted rural zone of ██████ Oblast, acquired by the Foundation in 1994 through negotiated transfer following the dissolution of the facility's original operating authority (designated hereafter as the Prior Custodians; see Addendum 4148-B). The complex's exterior presents as an active military restricted zone under joint Foundation-state security arrangement.

A rotating staff of no fewer than six personnel (the Maintenance Detail) must be present at SCP-4148 at all times. The Maintenance Detail is required to perform the Sequence (a specific, non-functional procedure inherited from the Prior Custodians involving the manual operation of two control-room key switches and verbal recitation of a fixed script; full text restricted to Maintenance Detail personnel, on file as Document 4148-Sequence) at the silo's original launch-authorization console once every six hours, without exception and without deviation from the recorded script, regardless of the console's disconnection from any functional missile system (the original missile was removed by the Prior Custodians prior to transfer; its current whereabouts are unknown).

A missed or incomplete Sequence is to be treated as an active containment breach. See Addendum 4148-A for associated emergency protocol.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4148's silo shaft, 61 meters in depth, no longer contains a missile or any launch apparatus. Sensor equipment lowered into the shaft registers a mass at the base of the shaft inconsistent with any recovered blueprint or inventory of the original installation, of indeterminate composition, approximately 4 meters in its largest recorded dimension, and slowly but measurably increasing in mass at a rate of approximately 0.3% per year since Foundation monitoring began.

Direct visual or physical examination of the mass has not been conducted; three attempts using remote camera equipment lowered past the 45-meter mark have resulted in equipment failure not attributable to any identified electrical or mechanical fault, and personnel present in the control room during these attempts have independently and consistently reported acute anxiety, auditory disturbance described as 'something breathing wrong,' and in two cases involuntary recitation of fragments of the Sequence script by personnel who had not yet been briefed on its content.

The relationship between the Sequence and the mass's behavior is inferred rather than confirmed: no Foundation test has directly measured the mass's response to a missed Sequence, as the sole occasion on which the Sequence was not completed on schedule (see Addendum 4148-A) was treated as an emergency and corrected within 40 minutes of the missed window, a response time insufficient to establish causality with confidence. Foundation researchers assess, based on Prior Custodian documentation recovered at transfer, that the Sequence does not affect the mass directly but maintains a separate condition — the nature of which remains undetermined — whose failure state is what personnel are intended to prevent.

ADDENDUM 4148-A: Incident 4148-3. During a personnel rotation failure, the Sequence was not performed within its six-hour window, resuming 40 minutes late. During the gap, all six on-duty personnel reported a uniform sensation described as 'the floor breathing,' seismographic equipment elsewhere in the complex recorded a localized vibration with no identified source, and the shaft's mass registered a temporary 6% increase in apparent volume that receded to baseline within an hour of the Sequence's resumption, though the underlying mass measurement did not correspondingly decrease, indicating the volume change was not simple expansion and contraction of the same material.

ADDENDUM 4148-B: Prior Custodian documentation, partially recovered and untranslated in full, indicates the silo was constructed around a pre-existing feature rather than the reverse, and that the original missile occupying the shaft alongside the mass — not instead of it, per structural analysis of the shaft's original fittings — was, per one translated fragment, 'not the deterrent.' The fragment is unsigned and its date of authorship could not be established.

SCP-4149.name: The Third Ring
SCP-4149.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All landline telephone exchanges within a 40 km radius of confirmed manifestation sites are monitored by Foundation-embedded software (Protocol KILOWATT) capable of detecting the acoustic signature of a call terminating exactly on its third ring without being answered. Detected instances are logged automatically; no physical intervention is required unless a Class II informational leak is flagged (see Addendum 4149-1). Personnel are not required to answer or decline incoming calls in any specific manner, as manual intervention has shown no effect on phenomenon frequency. Front organization "Meridian Telecom Diagnostics" maintains cover access to relevant exchange logs.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4149 is a recurring telephonic anomaly affecting analog and digital landline networks. When any telephone call is allowed to ring exactly three times and is not answered on or before the third ring (the call terminating naturally, through caller disconnection or automated timeout, precisely at that count), a conditional probability shift of 0.4% +/- 0.05% is imposed on the next incoming call received on that same line, regardless of elapsed time (observed delays up to 11 months).

The affected subsequent call, designated SCP-4149-1, connects the recipient to a source that Foundation switching analysis cannot trace to any existing subscriber, tower, or IP endpoint. Audio recovered from SCP-4149-1 instances consists of between four and thirty-one seconds of one-sided conversation, as though the recipient were overhearing a call already in progress. Content varies but reliably includes: a name (in 89% of cases matching a person known to the recipient), a location, and an incomplete sentence cut off mid-word by termination of the call. No instance of SCP-4149-1 has repeated content between subjects, and no subject has experienced SCP-4149-1 more than once.

Cross-referencing of 340 recovered transcripts against recipient biographical data indicates that in 61% of cases, the referenced person, location, or event described in the overheard fragment came to correspond to a real event in the recipient's life within the following 4-16 months. The remaining 39% show no correlation, or correlation could not be established due to recipient death, relocation, or refusal to cooperate with follow-up interview.

The mechanism by which SCP-4149 selects its trigger lines, or constructs the content of SCP-4149-1, remains unidentified. No causal pathway between the "third ring" trigger and the anomaly's informational content has been established, and Foundation telecommunications theorists regard the trigger condition as arbitrary rather than functional -- see Addendum 4149-2.

ADDENDUM 4149-1: On 3/14/2017, Agent XXXXXX received an SCP-4149-1 call referencing her own name, an address she had not yet moved to, and the fragment "--don't let her go back for the--" before termination. Eight months later, Agent XXXXXX relocated to the referenced address for an unrelated assignment. The remainder of the sentence was never recovered. Agent XXXXXX has requested reassignment to non-4149-adjacent duties. Request granted.

ADDENDUM 4149-2: Dr. Voss's proposal that SCP-4149 be reclassified as a passive precognitive relay was rejected by the O5 liaison on grounds that "a phenomenon which tells you almost nothing, almost correctly, on a schedule it did not choose, is not a relay. It is a tell." No further explanation was provided.

SCP-4150.name: The Convergence Hum
SCP-4150.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Containment of SCP-4150 is not feasible at the point of origin, as manifestation is a property of crowd size rather than location. Instead, the Foundation maintains a standing advisory (Directive 4150-BLUE) distributed to event organizers, transit authorities, and venue operators in affected metropolitan areas, recommending capacity management software flag any enclosed gathering approaching 47 occupants. Embedded Foundation observers (cover: acoustic consultants, event staff) attend flagged gatherings where feasible to record onset and administer the Standard Amnesticization Protocol to affected hummers if the event proceeds to Stage 3 (see below). Recordings of SCP-4150-1 audio are restricted to Level 3 personnel; unauthorized playback has produced Stage 1 onset in listening rooms of fewer than 47 occupants (see Addendum 4150-3).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4150 is a behavioral phenomenon occurring in enclosed gatherings of 47 or more humans, regardless of venue, purpose, acoustics, or prior acquaintance among attendees. Onset (Stage 1) is defined as three or more individuals producing an audibly identical hummed tone without eye contact, verbal cue, or apparent coordination. Affected individuals report no awareness of humming until informed, and no memory of deciding to begin. The tone itself, designated SCP-4150-1, measures consistently at 136.1 Hz across all 212 recorded instances, regardless of ambient acoustics, national origin of participants, or recording equipment.

If the gathering is not dispersed, Stage 2 follows within 6-40 minutes: the proportion of humming participants increases logarithmically, typically reaching 15-30% of total attendees before plateauing. Stage 2 humming is involuntary; affected individuals who are asked to stop report being able to do so for no more than 90 seconds before resuming. No participant has reported hearing SCP-4150-1 as originating from a specific direction or source; all describe it as "just present," comparable to tinnitus or the hum of building infrastructure.

Stage 3 has been recorded in 4 of 212 instances and involves the humming population reaching audible unison -- not merely identical pitch but identical rhythm, phrasing, and, in 2 instances, beginning to shape the tone into words. Recovered "words" from these two instances have not corresponded to any known language; linguistic analysis is ongoing. All four Stage 3 instances were interrupted by Foundation intervention (evacuation or acoustic disruption) before further escalation could be observed. The behavior or content of an uninterrupted Stage 3 event remains unknown, and no attempt to deliberately allow one to proceed has been authorized.

ADDENDUM 4150-1: SCP-4150 has been documented at concerts, religious services, transit terminals, courtrooms, and a Foundation all-hands briefing (D-classes reassigned; supervising staff amnesticized). The variety of settings has ruled out several early hypotheses linking the phenomenon to specific architecture or acoustic properties.

ADDENDUM 4150-2: Dr. Amara Ibe's analysis of the 136.1 Hz figure notes it does not correspond to any standard tuning reference, but sits almost exactly one syntonic comma below the C above middle C in just intonation -- a discrepancy she describes as "too precise to be coincidence and too small to matter to anyone who isn't listening for it."

ADDENDUM 4150-3: Following unauthorized playback of SCP-4150-1 audio to 6 researchers in Containment Wing 12 (occupancy: 6), no Stage 1 onset occurred. Playback to 51 researchers in an auditorium produced Stage 1 onset within 4 minutes. The count of 47 has since been confirmed as a hard threshold rather than a statistical tendency, though its significance is unexplained.

SCP-4151.name: The Missing Tuesday
SCP-4151.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation front company Halbrook Regional Records maintains parallel archival systems (physical and digital) for all municipalities within the current affected region (Auldkirk County and surrounding parishes), duplicated outside the region's boundary at 72-hour intervals to preserve a record of events independent of local memory. Residents of the affected region are not informed of SCP-4151 and are not amnesticized following an occurrence, as no intervention has proven necessary; affected populations spontaneously integrate the discrepancy without apparent distress. Monitoring personnel assigned to Auldkirk County rotate out of the region every 90 days as a precaution against unconfirmed cumulative effects.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4151 is a recurring temporal-mnemonic discrepancy affecting a bounded geographic region, currently centered on Auldkirk County, [REDACTED], though the affected region has relocated twice since first documented in 1961 (see Addendum 4151-2). At irregular intervals averaging one occurrence per 3.4 years, a single calendar Tuesday within the affected region fails to be retained in the personal memory of any resident present in the region on that date, despite objective records (photographs, financial transactions, written correspondence, CCTV where available) confirming that the day occurred and that residents' activities proceeded normally within it.

Residents questioned about the missing date do not report a gap or blackout; rather, their recollection smoothly transitions from the preceding Monday to the following Wednesday, with the intervening Tuesday simply absent from the sequence, unremarked upon unless the discrepancy is pointed out. When shown evidence of the missing day's events (e.g., a receipt, a completed task, a sent email in their own hand), subjects typically accept the evidence without distress, often attributing the gap to routine forgetfulness, and the false attribution persists even when its inadequacy (a receipt for an event nobody recalls initiating) is explained to them directly.

No missing Tuesday has ever coincided with a nationally or regionally significant date, holiday, or anniversary. Cross-referencing of the 19 documented instances has failed to identify any common astronomical, meteorological, or administrative trigger. Objective records from missing Tuesdays show no anomalous content; the day's events, where reconstructable, are mundane.

The affected region's boundary has been observed to drift by an average of 40 km per relocation, always to a demographically and geographically similar rural county, and always preceded by a period of 6-14 months in which no occurrences are recorded anywhere. The mechanism selecting the next affected region is unknown.

ADDENDUM 4151-1: Dr. Renate Holt's proposal to interview a resident during the missing Tuesday itself, using an embedded observer unaffected by the amnesia (candidates: personnel who entered the region less than 24 hours prior), was approved and conducted on 11/07/2019. Agent T. Fairclough's account of that Tuesday, filed before her own memory of the day was retroactively excised at midnight, describes "nothing" -- an ordinary day of interviews and grocery shopping. Agent Fairclough's written report exists; her memory of writing it does not.

ADDENDUM 4151-2: The affected region's first documented location (Bishop's Hollow, coordinates unrecorded) was abandoned by SCP-4151 in 1988 following the county's dissolution and merger with an adjacent municipality. Foundation records do not indicate whether the merger caused the relocation or coincided with it.

SCP-4152.name: The Unfinished Word Fog
SCP-4152.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation liaisons embedded within funeral service networks in affected metropolitan areas (current coverage: 14 cities) monitor scheduled interments and cremations for the meteorological precursors associated with SCP-4152 manifestation (barometric drop exceeding 3 hPa within the preceding hour, localized humidity spike unaccounted for by regional forecast). Upon precursor detection, embedded personnel implement Protocol GRAVEYARD-SHIFT: attendees are not evacuated, as evacuation has been shown to increase manifestation severity, but are instead administered a mild anxiolytic disguised as bereavement support and monitored for Stage 2 exposure symptoms. Direct verbal engagement with SCP-4152 during manifestation is prohibited for all personnel regardless of clearance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4152 is a localized fog phenomenon that manifests exclusively at funerary events (interment, cremation attendance, or memorial services held within 72 hours of the subject's death) worldwide, with no observed correlation to climate, season, or geography beyond the precursor conditions described above. The fog is visually unremarkable, presenting as standard radiation fog with 15-40 meter visibility, and does not register as anomalous on standard meteorological instruments; its anomalous property is exclusively auditory.

Individuals within SCP-4152 who had a personal relationship with the deceased (family, close acquaintance, minimum 2 years documented contact) report hearing, within the ambient sound of the fog, a voice matching the deceased delivering a sentence that terminates before completion -- typically 4 to 12 words, always grammatically mid-clause. Recovered fragments are highly varied in content and do not correspond to any statement the deceased is known to have made in life. Approximately 30% of recovered fragments contain information the hearer could not have previously possessed (a name, an address, a specific date) which in 22 of 71 documented cases was later independently verified as accurate.

Exposure duration within SCP-4152 correlates with psychological effect: hearers exposed for under 3 minutes report distress consistent with grief exacerbation, generally resolving without intervention within 2 weeks. Hearers exposed for over 8 minutes (Stage 2) report a persistent compulsion to return to the location of manifestation, seek out further fog events, or attempt to complete the heard sentence aloud; 6 of 19 documented Stage 2 subjects have required containment as anomalous themselves after developing the ability to independently generate localized micro-fog events of the same auditory character, unrelated to any specific death (see SCP-4152-A, filed separately).

The source of the auditory content, and the mechanism connecting it to a specific deceased individual rather than fog conditions generally, has not been determined. SCP-4152 does not manifest at every qualifying funerary event; current data suggests a manifestation rate of approximately 1 in 340 such events meeting precursor conditions, with no identified variable distinguishing manifesting from non-manifesting cases.

ADDENDUM 4152-1: Researcher Okonkwo-Lund's request to have SCP-4152 manifest at a controlled interment using a Foundation-selected decedent with no surviving relationships (to test whether the phenomenon requires a griever or merely a corpse) was denied by the Ethics Committee. The request has been resubmitted three times.

SCP-4153.name: The Lamplight Code
SCP-4153.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation-controlled subsidiary Gridwell Municipal Systems maintains remote monitoring access to street lighting infrastructure in all currently affected cities (see Document 4153-CITIES, restricted). An automated pattern-recognition system (Project LANTERN) continuously analyzes flicker telemetry from monitored grids for sequences matching prior SCP-4153-1 events. Upon detection of a sequence assessed above 70% confidence, the geographic area indicated by the affected light cluster is flagged for priority medical and emergency response monitoring for the following 8 hours; Foundation assets do not intervene to prevent the indicated event directly, per O5 standing order, but discreetly monitor outcomes to refine predictive accuracy. Civilian pattern-recognition (i.e., independent observation of the phenomenon by non-Foundation parties) is suppressed through standard misinformation channels where detected.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4153 refers to a recurring anomalous flicker pattern observed in municipal street lighting (sodium-vapor, LED, and mercury-vapor fixtures alike) across at least 30 cities on four continents, first formally documented in 2013 though retrospective analysis of maintenance logs suggests occurrence since at least 1994. During an SCP-4153 event, a cluster of between 6 and 40 streetlights within a contiguous area (typically 200m-1.5km in diameter) will flicker in a synchronized pattern of long and short interruptions consistent with International Morse Code, encoding a short message in the local majority language.

Decoded messages (SCP-4153-1) follow a consistent format: a time expressed in a 6-hour-forward offset from the event, a location description (street intersection, landmark, or address, always within the affected light cluster's radius), and a two-to-four word description of an event category (observed categories: "collapse," "collision," "fall," "cardiac," "fire," "struck," and 11 others). In 118 of 143 fully decoded and verified instances (82.5%), an emergency event matching the predicted category occurred at or within 150 meters of the predicted location, within 90 minutes of the predicted time.

SCP-4153 does not predict the identity of persons involved, and no instance has included information suggesting the message's origin is aware of Foundation observation. The remaining 17.5% of instances have not been confirmed to have failed; Foundation coverage of all indicated locations for the full predicted window has not been achievable in all cases, and a null result may reflect observational gaps rather than a genuine non-occurrence.

The mechanism producing the coded flicker, and its relationship (if any) to the predicted event, is unknown. Electrical engineers consulted have been unable to identify how the pattern propagates across lighting fixtures on independent circuits, often supplied by different substations, without any detected signal in the underlying grid infrastructure.

ADDENDUM 4153-1: On 6 occasions, Foundation assets have covertly intervened to alter conditions at a predicted location (e.g., cordoning a predicted collapse site) prior to the predicted time. In 4 of 6 cases, the predicted event occurred regardless, relocated to the nearest unobstructed point matching the location description. In 2 cases, no event was observed. The O5 Council has not authorized further intervention experiments pending review.

ADDENDUM 4153-2: A 2021 event in [REDACTED] decoded to a location, time, and category matching the death of Foundation Agent Priya Desai, off-duty and unrelated to any Foundation operation. This is the only confirmed instance of SCP-4153 predicting an event involving Foundation personnel.

SCP-4154.name: The Phantom Catalog Numbers
SCP-4154.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation-affiliated library and archive systems (currently 41 institutions under Agreement 4154-LIBRIS) run modified catalog software that intercepts and logs any search query returning an SCP-4154 phantom entry before displaying results to the patron, substituting a "no results found" message in its place. Logged phantom entries are forwarded weekly to Site-77 Archives Division for review. Non-affiliated library systems experiencing SCP-4154 activity are not contacted or altered; Foundation policy holds that intervention in ordinary cataloging systems draws more attention than the phenomenon itself generates.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4154 is an anomaly affecting library and archive catalog systems, both physical (card catalogs) and digital (OPAC databases, digital repository search indices), across at least 200 documented institutions with no identified technical or organizational connection between them. Approximately once per 4,000-6,000 searches conducted in an affected system, the search will return a "phantom entry": a fully formatted catalog record, indistinguishable in structure from genuine entries, describing a book, document, or item that does not exist in the institution's holdings and cannot be located through any subsequent search, physical retrieval attempt, or inter-library loan request.

Phantom entries are internally consistent (correct ISBN checksum formatting where applicable, plausible publisher and call number, dates within the range of the collection's actual holdings) but the described item cannot be verified to have ever been published, printed, or held by any institution, Foundation or otherwise. Approximately 40% of recovered phantom titles describe content thematically or structurally related to the search query that produced them; the remainder appear unrelated.

Patrons who encounter a phantom entry and attempt to request or locate the item report no unusual psychological effects in the majority of cases. However, 34 documented individuals (of an estimated several thousand total exposures, exact figure unknown due to limited monitoring outside Foundation-affiliated systems) have subsequently reported vivid, detailed false memories of having read the phantom item, including specific plot points, passages, or data, despite the item's confirmed non-existence. These 34 individuals' described "memories" of a given phantom title are consistent with one another when cross-referenced, despite no contact between subjects, suggesting the false memory content is fixed to the specific phantom entry rather than generated independently by each subject.

The origin of phantom entries -- whether generated by the cataloging systems themselves, inserted externally, or representing information about genuinely nonexistent works with a fixed and shared content -- has not been determined. No phantom entry has ever repeated verbatim across separate institutions, though thematic overlap has been noted in 6% of cross-referenced cases.

ADDENDUM 4154-1: Site-77 currently holds a standing request (Form 4154-RETRIEVE) inviting any researcher who independently recalls the content of a phantom title, without prior exposure to Division records describing it, to submit a full account for comparison. Fourteen submissions have been received to date; eleven matched existing phantom-entry metadata on file that the submitting researcher denies having previously accessed.

SCP-4155.name: The Triplicate Filing
SCP-4155.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4155 is maintained as an active Foundation asset under Procedure 4155-GAMMA, restricted to personnel holding Administrative Clearance Level 3 or higher and certified in Form 4155-A completion. Physical copies of Form 4155-A (title: "Notice of Intent to Formally Regret an Administrative Decision") are stocked at all Sites with Keter-class containment and at 6 designated rapid-response Thaumiel support facilities. Deployment of SCP-4155 requires: (1) identification of a qualifying anomalous effect within 800 meters, (2) completion of Form 4155-A in triplicate by hand, in ink, by the same individual for all three copies, (3) submission of one copy each to the site's on-duty administrative officer, the effect's designated case file, and a sealed archive box maintained for this sole purpose, and (4) completion of all three submissions within the same clock hour. Deviation from this sequence has never produced the intended effect in testing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4155 refers to the reliably reproducible neutralizing or suppressive effect produced by correct completion of the Procedure 4155-GAMMA filing ritual (colloquially "the triplicate filing") on a defined category of ongoing anomalous phenomena. The effect was discovered accidentally in 1979 when Site-19 administrator R. Hollis, attempting to formally protest a supply requisition denial through triplicate paperwork submitted within an unusually compressed timeframe, observed the immediate and complete cessation of an unrelated Keter-class reality-distortion event (SCP-XXXX, designation now retired) active in an adjacent wing at the moment of the third submission.

Subsequent controlled testing has established that Procedure 4155-GAMMA reliably suppresses anomalous effects meeting the following criteria: the effect must be ongoing (not a discrete past event), must be occurring within a Foundation-administered facility, and must, per the operational definition adopted by Site-19 researchers, "have consequences for someone whose job it would be to file a complaint about them." Effects failing to meet this third criterion -- described internally as "procedural relevance" -- do not respond to Procedure 4155-GAMMA regardless of technical similarity to effects that do respond. No formal metric for procedural relevance has been established; researchers instead rely on precedent and a maintained log of successful and failed deployments (Document 4155-LOG).

Procedure 4155-GAMMA has been successfully deployed 61 times since 1979, with a 74% success rate against qualifying effects. Failed deployments show no consistent distinguishing characteristic from successful ones prior to attempt. The mechanism by which bureaucratic self-documentation suppresses reality-altering phenomena remains entirely theoretical; leading hypotheses within Site-19's Metaphysics Division hold that the Foundation's administrative apparatus has, through sufficient scale and duration of operation, acquired a form of narrative authority independent of any individual's belief or intent -- a hypothesis neither confirmed nor testable by any means currently available.

ADDENDUM 4155-1: Dr. Hollis, prior to retirement, filed a formal recommendation that Procedure 4155-GAMMA never be simplified, automated, or converted to digital submission, on the stated grounds that "it works because someone has to mean it, in their own hand, three times, within the hour. I don't know what happens if we make it easier. I would rather not find out."

ADDENDUM 4155-2: Thaumiel classification was approved following the 2003 deployment that halted an active Site-19 containment breach (SCP-2XXX) with zero additional resource expenditure beyond three sheets of paper and 40 minutes of an administrator's time.

SCP-4156.name: The Erased Floor Dream
SCP-4156.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Demolition or major renovation sites confirmed as SCP-4156 origin points are marked in Foundation geological survey databases under innocuous zoning classifications to discourage residential development within a 900-meter radius where possible. Where residential development cannot be prevented, the Foundation monitors local mental health service utilization and social media activity for keyword clusters associated with SCP-4156 exposure (see Document 4156-KEYWORDS) and deploys embedded counselors (cover: standard community mental health outreach) to affected residents reporting qualifying dreams. Direct suppression or amnesticization of dreamers is not standard procedure, as trial application in 2015 (Site-77 Case 4156-C) produced no reduction in incidence among the broader affected population, suggesting individual memory is not the vector of transmission.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4156 is a recurring shared-dream phenomenon reported by residents living within approximately 900 meters of a site where a multi-story building was demolished, provided the demolished building's original architectural plans included at least one floor, room, or structural feature that was altered, omitted, or never built as originally designed. Affected individuals need not have any personal connection to the demolished structure, prior knowledge of its former existence, or access to its blueprints.

The dream, reported independently by unconnected individuals with consistent structural detail, depicts the dreamer navigating a floor of the now-demolished building that does not appear in any surviving construction record -- most commonly located between two floors that, per available blueprints, should be directly adjacent with no intervening space. The floor is consistently described as underlit, incompletely furnished, and populated by the sound (never the sight) of ordinary activity: conversation, footsteps, a radio, cutlery. Dreamers report being unable to locate a source for these sounds despite extensive dream-navigation, and consistently report the dream ending when they attempt to open a specific door, at which point they wake.

Cross-referencing of 44 collected dream reports across 6 separate SCP-4156 sites shows structural consistency exceeding chance (independently reported floor layouts, sound sources, and door placement matched within site clusters at a rate of 71%, verified via blind sketch comparison), despite no communication between dreamers confirmed. In 3 of 6 sites, subsequent archival research uncovered evidence (unfiled permit amendments, contractor correspondence, a single case of a coroner's report) that the described floor corresponded to a genuine, undocumented alteration to the original building -- a mezzanine converted to storage and later sealed, a room removed from final construction after a fire, and in one case a floor whose existence is attested only by a demolition subcontractor's unpublished invoice for "sealed void, 3rd interstitial, do not disclose."

The mechanism by which unbuilt or erased architectural information transmits to unconnected dreamers has not been identified. No SCP-4156 dream has depicted the interior of the door dreamers report being unable to open.

ADDENDUM 4156-1: At the site associated with the sealed subcontractor invoice, exploratory excavation authorized under Site-77 oversight located a void matching the dreamed floor's dimensions within 4%. The void was empty. No further excavation below the void has been authorized.

SCP-4157.name: The Early Broadcast
SCP-4157.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation-controlled monitoring stations (designation EARSHOT-1 through EARSHOT-9) continuously scan emergency alert system frequencies, civil defense bands, and designated AM/FM/shortwave ranges across all Foundation member-nation territories for SCP-4157 broadcast signatures. Upon detection, Protocol MISHEARD is enacted: the broadcast is recorded in full, the affected frequency range is jammed with innocuous filler content within 40 seconds to prevent civilian reception, and the described disaster category, location, and timeframe are cross-referenced against Document 4157-DEVIATIONS to identify the broadcast's single factual inaccuracy (see Description). Personnel are prohibited from using SCP-4157 content to inform emergency response planning; four prior instances of unauthorized use resulted in resource misallocation when responders acted on the broadcast's inaccurate detail rather than the otherwise-correct remainder of the message.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4157 is a recurring anomalous radio broadcast phenomenon, first identified in 1988, that intermittently overrides standard emergency alert system frequencies with a synthesized voice message describing an emergency event (natural disaster, infrastructure failure, mass-casualty incident) using the register and structure of genuine civil emergency broadcasts. Broadcasts range from 20 to 95 seconds and are received only on frequencies within Foundation member-nation broadcast infrastructure; no instance has been detected originating from or received within non-member-nation territory, a pattern for which no explanation has been established.

In 97% of the 211 recorded instances, the described emergency event subsequently occurred, matching the broadcast's description in event category, general location (accurate to a named municipality or smaller), and timing (within a stated window, typically 6-72 hours following broadcast), with a lead time sufficient in principle for effective evacuation or mitigation response. However, every confirmed SCP-4157 broadcast has contained exactly one factual inaccuracy relative to the eventual real event -- a discrepancy in a single detail (a street name one digit removed from the actual address, a magnitude or casualty figure altered by a small but non-trivial margin, a described time zone offset by one hour, a named facility referring to a decommissioned or fictional predecessor of the actual site). The inaccurate detail is never identifiable as such prior to the real event's occurrence, and has in at least 6 documented cases caused emergency responders acting on unauthorized leaked broadcast content to be misdirected, delaying effective response.

No message content, inaccuracy pattern, or broadcast timing has permitted reliable advance identification of which detail within a given broadcast is the false one. Linguistic and signal analysis of the synthesized voice has not matched it to any known text-to-speech system, past or current commercial or governmental.

The Foundation's continued non-intervention in disaster events predicted by SCP-4157 (per O5 standing order, broadcasts are not used to inform official response despite documented accuracy) remains a subject of internal dispute; see Addendum 4157-2.

ADDENDUM 4157-1: Analysis by Dr. Petra Voss suggests the single inaccuracy may not be incidental to the phenomenon but load-bearing -- her working hypothesis holds that SCP-4157 is constitutionally incapable of transmitting fully accurate information about a future event, and that the inaccuracy is the minimum "cost" the phenomenon must impose to broadcast at all. This hypothesis remains unconfirmed and unfalsified.

ADDENDUM 4157-2: A formal petition (Ref. 4157-P-06) to authorize limited, deniable use of SCP-4157 broadcasts in disaster response, accepting the risk of the single inaccuracy in exchange for the 6-72 hour lead time, was denied by O5 Council vote of 9-4. The dissenting minority's objection remains on file, unresolved.

SCP-4158.name: The Thirteenth in Line
SCP-4158.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4158 requires no active containment, as manifestation is self-limiting and has produced no confirmed harmful outcome to date. Foundation monitoring is limited to a standing data-scraping arrangement with 12 partnered retail and government service providers (queue-management software vendors) permitting anonymized flagging of instances where a 13th queued individual's transaction timestamp gap exceeds 8 minutes (see Description). Affected individuals are not contacted or debriefed unless self-reporting occurs; to date, 3 individuals have contacted Foundation-adjacent hotlines (established for unrelated purposes) describing SCP-4158 exposure, all of whom were administered standard Class A amnesticization after voluntary interview.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4158 is a recurring temporal anomaly affecting the 13th person in a linear, single-file physical queue, provided the queue has formed organically (not pre-assigned numbered positions) and contains at least 20 total individuals at the moment the 13th position's transaction or service interval begins. Under these conditions, the individual in the 13th position experiences a subjective service interaction (being served at a counter, completing a transaction, passing through a checkpoint) that, from their own perspective, lasts the ordinary duration expected for the interaction (10 seconds to 4 minutes, depending on transaction type). However, objective records -- service timestamps, other queue members' accounts, CCTV where available -- confirm that between 6 and 14 minutes have elapsed for all external observers during the same interval.

The 13th individual is not aware of the discrepancy unless informed; no case has documented an affected individual noticing objective evidence of the gap unprompted. When informed, affected individuals report no memory of the missing interval and describe their subjective experience as wholly unremarkable, matching the ordinary content expected of the transaction (i.e., a bank teller interaction feels, to the affected individual, exactly like a bank teller interaction, containing no anomalous content, simply occupying less subjective time than objective time).

The queue members immediately before and after the 13th position (12th and 14th) do not experience the discrepancy themselves but consistently report, when interviewed, a vague sense that "something took longer than it should have," without further detail. No queue member beyond positions 12-14 reports any awareness of the anomaly.

The gap duration shows weak positive correlation with total queue length beyond the minimum 20, and no correlation with transaction type, location, or queue composition. SCP-4158 has been documented in retail checkouts, passport control lines, medical waiting rooms, and voting locations, across 19 countries, with the earliest confirmed instance dated 1974 (a supermarket receipt discrepancy noted independently by a customer, recovered from an unrelated consumer complaint archive).

The purpose or mechanism of the missing time -- whether it is genuinely lost, relocated, or consumed by some unidentified process -- has not been established. No attempt to instrument the 13th position directly (e.g., embedding a Foundation observer as the queue's 13th member) has yet succeeded in producing a manifestation; SCP-4158 has not occurred in any of the 40 controlled attempts to date, a null result presently unexplained.

ADDENDUM 4158-1: Statistical review notes that SCP-4158 appears to select the queue position by ordinal count alone, independent of the number 13's cultural significance in the queue's local context; manifestation frequency and severity show no variation between regions where 13 is considered unlucky and regions where it is not.

SCP-4159.name: The Unseen Curtain Call
SCP-4159.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Venues confirmed as recurring SCP-4159 sites (currently 9 theaters, concert halls, and auditoriums across 5 countries) are monitored via embedded ushers and sound technicians (Foundation cover personnel) equipped with concealed timing devices to log onset and duration of anomalous applause events. Audiences are not warned, evacuated, or otherwise informed prior to or during an event, as all 61 documented instances have resolved without injury or lasting harm to attendees; Foundation intervention is limited to post-event debriefing of venue staff and amnesticization of any attendee who explicitly requests explanation of the phenomenon (approximately 4% of a given audience).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4159 is a crowd-behavioral phenomenon occurring at approximately 1 in 3,000 live public performances (theater, concert, opera, and comparable ticketed events with a defined "end point" marked by curtain, final bow, or equivalent) in which the audience, following the performance's genuine conclusion and the performers' exit from the stage or performance area, continues applauding in full unison -- matched tempo, matched intensity, without the ordinary decay pattern of natural applause -- for a duration of exactly 17 seconds beyond what would be expected from audience behavior alone, before stopping simultaneously without an identifiable cue.

Audience members surveyed following an SCP-4159 event do not report awareness of applauding longer than usual, and do not report any subjective compulsion, awareness of synchrony, or unusual sensation during the extended applause. When shown video evidence of the anomalous duration and unison, subjects generally acknowledge the recording's accuracy but do not recall experiencing it as unusual at the time, a discrepancy that has resisted explanation through standard suggestibility or crowd-conformity models (control audiences shown fabricated "normal" applause footage of the same performance did not produce comparable false confidence).

In 14 of 61 documented instances, embedded observers or stage-adjacent personnel reported a secondary phenomenon during the 17-second interval: a sensation, not corroborated by any recording equipment, of the performance space being occupied by additional, unseen presence beyond the audience and performers -- described variously as "someone still on stage," "the feeling of eyes from the wings," or "an extra bow being taken." No visual, thermal, or audio recording has ever captured evidence corroborating these reports, and the personnel reporting them have shown no pattern distinguishing them from those who do not.

The number 17 has shown no correlation with performance length, audience size, or venue acoustics, and its consistency across all 61 documented instances (verified independently through frame-accurate video analysis in 40 cases) remains unexplained. SCP-4159 has never been documented at a rehearsal, a performance without a paying audience, or a recorded/broadcast performance without a live audience physically present.

ADDENDUM 4159-1: Dr. Imelda Cruz's proposal to test whether SCP-4159 requires performer belief in an audience (by staging a performance before an audience secretly informed the "performers" were prerecorded holograms) is pending Ethics Committee review, citing concern that the secondary phenomenon reported in 14 cases may represent an undocumented risk to performers specifically.

SCP-4160.name: The Forbidden Census Figure
SCP-4160.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4160 is maintained as a passive Thaumiel asset through Foundation influence over statistical reporting methodology in 6 partner national census bureaus (see Agreement 4160-STAT, restricted to Level 4). No active suppression of the phenomenon is conducted; the Foundation's role is limited to monitoring the self-correcting behavior described below and ensuring that anomalous demographic data does not surface in public-facing statistical releases, which is achieved through standard rounding and margin-of-error language already native to census methodology, requiring minimal additional concealment. Personnel are reminded that SCP-4160's classification as Thaumiel reflects its use as an early-warning indicator (see Addendum 4160-2) and not any confirmed beneficial property of the anomaly itself.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4160 refers to a statistical anomaly observed in the population records of 11 municipalities across 6 countries, in which the recorded population count self-corrects across successive counting periods (census cycles, municipal registries, utility hookup records) to avoid the population figure reaching a specific integer value, hereafter the "excluded figure," unique to each affected municipality and ranging in documented cases between 40,000 and 4,000,000.

In affected municipalities, population figures approaching the excluded figure from below exhibit anomalous stagnation (birth/immigration rates measured independently do not decline, but recorded net population growth flattens as the excluded figure is approached) or, in 4 documented cases, an unexplained single-cycle population decrease (recorded emigration, mortality, or record correction sufficient to reduce the count below the excluded figure) despite no corroborating evidence of the specific deaths, departures, or errors cited in the correction. Municipalities whose population has, through administrative reclassification or annexation, been forced across the excluded figure in a single reporting period have in 3 of 3 documented cases subsequently generated a new excluded figure, always higher, within the following 2 reporting cycles.

The 11 excluded figures identified to date show no numerical relationship to each other, to the affected municipality's other statistics (area, founding date, historical population), or to any commonly significant number. Foundation demographic analysts have been unable to identify the informational or causal content of any given excluded figure -- that is, no researcher has determined what, if anything, would happen if a municipality's true population reached its excluded figure, as no instance of this occurring has been documented.

Foundation interest in SCP-4160 escalated following the 2019 discovery (Addendum 4160-1) that one excluded figure corresponded, to three significant digits, with an internal Foundation risk-assessment threshold unrelated to demographics or the municipality in question, a correspondence assessed by the O5 Council as too improbable to be coincidental and insufficiently understood to act upon.

ADDENDUM 4160-1: The excluded figure for the municipality of XXXXXXXXXX (population as of last reporting cycle: 211,406, excluded figure: 211,900) was found by Dr. Amos Reyes to match, at three significant figures, the population threshold above which Foundation contingency planning designates an urban area as requiring pre-positioned Keter-class response assets. Dr. Reyes's memo characterizes this as "either the least meaningful coincidence in the history of this Foundation, or the most quietly terrifying one we have on file. I have no way to determine which, and I am not confident I want to."

ADDENDUM 4160-2: Thaumiel classification was approved on the basis that SCP-4160's self-correcting behavior, should its excluded figures prove to correlate with genuine risk thresholds more broadly, may constitute a naturally occurring early-warning system for population-scale hazards the Foundation has not yet identified. This remains an operating hypothesis, not a confirmed finding.

SCP-4161.name: The Thursday Circle
SCP-4161.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation personnel embedded within [REDACTED] municipal senior services maintain passive observation of the informal group designated the subject of this file. A standing arrangement with the county coroner's office flags any death within the group's five-kilometer catchment area for review of possible correlation. Agents are not to interfere with meetings, membership changes, or completed garments unless a stated intention meets Class III intervention criteria (Document 4161-B); in such cases the garment is acquired prior to delivery via a substitute-gift protocol and replaced with a mundane duplicate.

Yarn samples and donated hair are collected quarterly under pretext of a textile charity drive and archived at Site-64. No member is to be approached for recruitment, detainment, or amnesticization while a donor's memory loss is actively manifesting, as prior contact under these conditions has caused the loss to generalize beyond its typical scope (Incident 4161-3).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4161 designates a social group of nine to eleven women, aged 61 to 89 at last review, who meet each Thursday afternoon at the [REDACTED] Senior Community Center to knit. Membership carries no application or invitation process; when a seat is vacated by death or relocation, a previously unaffiliated woman from the surrounding area begins attending within one to three weeks, already proficient in a knitting technique specific to the group that corresponds to no documented pattern tradition. No interviewed member can describe how she learned it, and several insist they have "always known."

The group's anomalous property manifests when a garment is completed from yarn hand-spun from hair donated by a living person, provided the knitter states aloud, at the moment of casting on, a specific outcome intended for the garment's eventual recipient ("she passes the exam," "the tumor shrinks," "he comes home safe"). A garment completed under these conditions causes the stated outcome to occur for its recipient within approximately thirty days of the item being worn, regardless of prior medical or statistical likelihood. The causal mechanism is undetermined; in documented cases the outcome has arrived through mundane, retrospectively unremarkable means — a rescheduled surgery, a shift in wind direction, a phone call arriving one day earlier than expected.

The hair donor invariably loses a quantity of autobiographical memory roughly proportional to hours spent producing the garment, at a ratio near one hour of knitting to forty minutes of lost memory, clustered around events related to the stated outcome or to the donor's relationship with the recipient. Donors are not informed of this cost beforehand and have not been observed to notice the loss afterward. In fourteen of twenty-two documented cases, the donor was the recipient's parent, spouse, or child.

The Circle maintains an internal waiting list, handwritten in a ledger that has not been recovered by Foundation personnel. Requests are prioritized by criteria that remain unknown; at least two terminal pediatric cases on record were declined without explanation given to the requesting family.

ADDENDUM 4161-1: Incident 4161-3. A mother requested the outcome "she wakes up" on behalf of a comatose daughter; the hair donor was the patient's younger sister, age 11. Foundation agents made contact with the donor's household during the thirty-day window to confirm sourcing. Following this contact, the donor's memory loss generalized beyond the typical cluster; she no longer recognizes her sister, who did, in fact, wake up nine days later. The Circle has not been asked to explain this deviation, and no member has volunteered one.

SCP-4162.name: The Fifth Ward Arbitration Board
SCP-4162.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation asset within the [REDACTED] County Clerk's Office maintains covert oversight of the jury-selection algorithm used to seat SCP-4162, ensuring at least three of five seats each rotation are filled by individuals pre-screened as Foundation-compliant or otherwise unlikely to render rulings with strategic value to hostile parties. All case filings submitted to the Board are reviewed by an embedded clerk (Agent designation 4162-Intake) prior to docketing; filings assessed as carrying reality-alteration potential exceeding Level 2 per Document 4162-C are redirected to a mundane small-claims court via substitution of docket number.

Approximately four times per fiscal year, the Board is petitioned by Foundation-affiliated plaintiffs using cover identities to resolve site-security matters requiring localized reality correction (see Addendum 4162-2). No more than one such petition may be filed per rotation, per internal Ethics Committee restriction 4162/EC-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4162 designates the five-member citizen arbitration board empaneled biennially in [REDACTED] to hear small-claims property and neighbor disputes below a $10,000 threshold, nominally a routine function of municipal civil court. Panelists are selected from the county's standard jury pool via an ostensibly random lottery and serve mandatory two-year terms; no summoned individual has successfully declined service, deferred it, or been excused on medical or hardship grounds since at least 1974, the earliest year for which Clerk's Office records survive.

A ruling issued by SCP-4162, once signed by a quorum of three panelists and filed with the Clerk's Office, does not merely resolve the dispute as a legal matter: the physical and documentary state of the world updates to conform to the ruling's language, including corroborating evidence not created at time of filing. A ruling stating a disputed fence "has always stood" at a given property line produces period-appropriate survey stakes, aged fence posts, and consistent recollections in neighbors and county records predating the ruling by years or decades. Affected parties do not perceive the change and treat the corrected state as having always been the case; only individuals possessing prior documentation stored outside the affected area's causal reach (e.g., digital backups on Foundation servers) retain record of the discrepancy.

Each ruling extracts an undisclosed cost from the panelists who signed it, applied without their awareness: an object, relationship, ability, or period of good health of roughly proportionate significance to the magnitude of the ruling is quietly removed from the panelist's own life within the following year. Panelists do not connect these losses to their service. Exit interviews with eleven former panelists identified, in aggregate, four divorces, two terminated pregnancies attributed to "unexplained" causes, one early-onset diagnosis of a degenerative condition, and three cases of sudden, total estrangement from a close friend, all occurring within fourteen months of a signed ruling and none recognized by the subject as connected.

ADDENDUM 4162-1: The Board itself does not appear aware of the scope of its authority; panelists interviewed describe their work as "ordinary," express mild irritation at the mandatory service, and show no indication of noticing that their rulings alter physical evidence. Foundation policy as of this review is to preserve this ignorance rather than risk the Board's dissolution or relocation, both previously attempted by the O5 Council for Site-64 area-denial ends and aborted after 4162/EC-1 was drafted.

SCP-4163.name: The 3:47 Board
SCP-4163.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains three sockpuppet accounts with moderator-adjacent trust ratings on the forum hosting SCP-4163, sufficient to monitor new-member intake and thread activity without triggering the community's informal but effective ban-evasion detection of outside observers.
