The forum's physical hosting infrastructure is not to be seized or shut down; Incident 4163-1 demonstrated that removing member access to the forum does not halt symptom onset or the associated departures, and merely removes the Foundation's primary observation channel.

Any individual confirmed to be newly symptomatic is not to be quarantined, sedated, or prevented from posting, per Ethics Committee finding 4163/EC-2, which noted no instance of induced onset correlating with continued forum access, and two instances of accelerated adverse outcome following attempted removal.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4163 designates the membership of an unaffiliated web forum, currently numbering approximately 14,000 registered accounts with 200 to 600 active in any given week, organized around shared experience of a recurring dream. Members report waking at 03:47 local time, independent of time zone, from a dream depicting a windowless hallway terminating in a closed door, on which a name is legibly written. No two members have ever successfully transcribed, typed, or verbally reproduced the same name twice, nor has any single member reproduced their own reading of it consistently between tellings. Text believed to contain the name becomes illegible specifically and only to individuals who have themselves had the dream; non-symptomatic readers, including Foundation researchers without onset, perceive ordinary if unremarkable handwriting that resists OCR and photographic reproduction by unrelated means.

Onset is not transmitted by forum membership, exposure to other members, or discussion of the dream; a survey of 340 members found no shared prior contact, location, or media consumption sufficient to explain the correlation, though 61% report the first occurrence within one week of proximity to a specific but non-recurring category of event (a house fire, a stillbirth, a lightning strike within 100 meters) unconnected to any of the others by further analysis. New members locate the forum through search terms specific to the dream's imagery within days of onset, despite the forum's absence from indexed search results as verified by Foundation web crawls; members are unable to explain how they found it.

A minority of members (41 documented since the forum's earliest archived posts in 2009) report, prior to disappearance, a final post describing having opened the door. All 41 have subsequently ceased all online and offline activity traceable to their identity; none have been located, alive or deceased, by Foundation or law-enforcement search. The forum's pinned "In Memory" thread, maintained by unknown administration, updates to include each departed member's username within hours of their final post, before any other member has flagged the absence.

SCP-4164.name: The Marchetti Inheritance
SCP-4164.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains legal cover as a private trust management firm ("Cavanaugh Fiduciary Partners") retained by the Marchetti family estate, providing embedded observation of all family members without their knowledge of Foundation involvement. Firstborn family members approaching their fortieth birthday are flagged for increased monitoring frequency (Protocol 4164-Amber); documented behavioral drift consistent with onset (see Description) is not to be interrupted absent Level 4 authorization, as prior interruption attempts have accelerated drift in two recorded cases (Incidents 4164-2, 4164-5) rather than halting it.

Access to genealogical and legal records identifying living Marchetti descendants is restricted to personnel cleared for Project MERIDIAN-FEN. Descendants who legally change surname prior to onset are to be monitored for a minimum of ten years; three such individuals have subsequently experienced onset regardless of the name change, indicating surname is correlated with but not the operative mechanism of the anomaly.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4164 designates a hereditary behavioral and psychological phenomenon affecting firstborn children (by birth order, regardless of gender or the marital status of parents) of the Marchetti family line, traceable in Foundation records to a common ancestor, Aurelio Marchetti (1791-1858), and continuing through at least eleven subsequent generations to the present.

Beginning within several months of an affected individual's fortieth birthday, the individual exhibits progressive drift in handwriting, vocal cadence, expressed political and religious opinions, culinary preference, and long-term memory recall toward a consistent profile matching Aurelio Marchetti as reconstructed from surviving correspondence and testimony, despite no affected individual having had access to these primary sources prior to onset. Drift is gradual, typically reaching a stable plateau within 18-30 months, after which the individual retains their own name, relationships, and short-term functioning but reports (when willing to discuss it) a persistent sense that their earlier personality was "a costume" or "practice."

Firstborns who die before onset (whether of natural or other causes) do not transmit the phenomenon to their own firstborn; the line of onset passes instead to the next living firstborn in eligible descent, suggesting a single continuous process seeking embodiment rather than independent heritable triggers in each individual. Aurelio Marchetti's recorded biography contains no anomalous elements; Foundation historical research has not identified a cause for his apparent persistence, nor confirmed whether the personality reconstructing itself across generations is an accurate copy of the historical Aurelio or a construct that has come to resemble him through eleven generations of partial, lossy transmission.

Three living affected individuals, having reached full plateau, have independently initiated contact with one another without prior acquaintance, using genealogical detail about Aurelio's life not available in any archive accessed by Foundation research. Their stated shared intention, per Interview 4164-9, concerns "finishing the Fenholm claim," a 19th-century land dispute lost by Aurelio Marchetti in 1849 and involving property now occupied by unrelated parties. The claim has not been pursued through legal channels. It has not been raised again since the interview.

SCP-4165.name: The Partners of Hail, Voss & Whitcombe
SCP-4165.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A Foundation-affiliated accounting analyst maintains permanent employment within Hail, Voss & Whitcombe LLP at senior associate level, a position deliberately kept below partnership to preserve unaffected perception of firm ledgers. This asset conducts quarterly reconciliation of all documents bearing partner signatures against parallel copies retained by Foundation financial oversight, without informing firm personnel.

The firm is not to be dissolved, audited by outside regulatory bodies, or have its partnership structure altered by Foundation action; three attempts by external agencies (unrelated to the Foundation) to formally audit the firm between 1988 and 2009 were independently redirected or abandoned by mundane bureaucratic causes before completion, suggesting an undetermined self-protective property of SCP-4165 unrelated to Foundation intervention and not to be relied upon as primary containment.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4165 designates the equity partnership of Hail, Voss & Whitcombe LLP, a mid-sized accounting and audit firm headquartered in [REDACTED], currently comprising seven individuals. Partnership is attained through a private vote of existing partners following a minimum associate tenure of nine years and is not otherwise available; no individual has been observed to buy, inherit, or otherwise obtain partner status outside this process.

Upon confirmation of partnership, an individual permanently and irreversibly loses the capacity to consciously perceive arithmetic discrepancies in any financial document bearing the firm's letterhead or corporate seal, specifically limited to discrepancies whose net value resolves, after all listed adjustments, to a multiple of $47,000. Affected partners can perform standard arithmetic accurately in all other contexts, including documents from other firms and personal finances, and score normally on Foundation-administered numeracy assessment; the deficit is specific to the described condition and appears only when reviewing firm paperwork.

Ledger analysis by Foundation asset 4165-1 has traced discrepancies matching this pattern to firm accounts continuously since the firm's 1962 founding, with a cumulative unreconciled total, as of last review, of approximately $9.2 million distributed across client trust accounts, none of which any partner has been observed to draw upon personally. No partner interviewed (under pretext) expresses awareness of financial irregularity, personal enrichment beyond documented salary, or any conscious intent related to the discrepancy. Partners who retire or are removed from partnership do not regain the ability to perceive prior discrepancies retroactively, though newly generated documents post-retirement are perceived normally.

The firm has never been found in violation of any audit, tax filing, or malpractice claim in its sixty-two-year operating history. The recipient(s) of the unreconciled funds, and the mechanism transferring them out of client accounts without partner action or external transaction record, remain undetermined.

ADDENDUM 4165-1: A junior associate promoted to partnership in the current fiscal year was, per standard protocol, interviewed by asset 4165-1 under pretext of a routine benefits orientation. When shown a firm ledger page containing a flagged discrepancy, the new partner glanced at the figures, remarked that the columns "looked fine to him," and returned to discussing his retirement plan contributions without further prompting.

SCP-4166.name: The Fallow Congregation
SCP-4166.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains agricultural and veterinary supply contracts with the Fallow Congregation's compound in [REDACTED] through two shell distributors, ensuring the commune's continued self-sufficiency and discouraging contact with unaffiliated persons who might inadvertently learn or utter the restricted name (see Description). A four-kilometer radius surrounding the compound is designated a Federal Wildlife Management Area under cover jurisdiction, restricting civilian access.

All Foundation personnel assigned to SCP-4166 monitoring duty undergo mandatory redaction briefing; the restricted name is never to be recorded in full in any document, spoken aloud during operations within nine kilometers of the compound, or transmitted over unencrypted channels. Personnel exposed to accidental utterance are to be withdrawn from the area and administered Class-A amnesticization regardless of apparent effect.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4166 designates the Fallow Congregation, an agricultural commune of approximately 190-210 members occupying a 1,600-acre compound, founded in 1974 by Elias Warrick (deceased 1991) following the stillbirth of his son. Congregation doctrine, transmitted orally and never written, holds that the stillborn child was given a name at birth that must never again be spoken, written, sung, or otherwise represented in any medium, on the belief that doing so would "open the gate he came through partway."

Foundation investigation, prompted by three unrelated anomalous events in the surrounding county between 1994 and 2003 later traced to isolated utterances of the name by individuals with no Congregation affiliation, has confirmed the doctrine's practical basis. In each traced instance, utterance of the specific name within approximately nine kilometers of the compound preceded, within 48 hours, a localized manifestation matching no known SCP-classified entity: a spreading, sourceless grief response affecting all mammalian life in a 200-400 meter radius, in two cases resulting in mass livestock death and in one case three human fatalities recorded as simultaneous cardiac arrest. No manifestation has occurred when the name is spoken beyond the nine-kilometer radius, nor when spoken by Congregation members within their own doctrine's permitted context (there is none; the Congregation has never, in any observed instance, uttered the name).

Congregation membership is obtained by birth, marriage to an existing member, or a minimum five-year probationary residency for outside adults, during which the applicant is never informed of the specific restricted name, only that one exists. Departure from the Congregation requires a private rite conducted by the eldest living member, in which the departing individual is told the name once, in full, and in exchange surrenders (by a mechanism neither the Foundation nor, per interview, the Congregation itself can explain) a portion of personal memory equivalent to their years of membership. Nineteen former members interviewed post-departure retain no memory of the name itself, consistent recall of having left, and significant, proportionate gaps in memory of their time inside.

The Foundation's current position, formalized under Thaumiel classification, treats the Congregation's doctrine and membership structure as an effective, self-sustaining containment mechanism for whatever phenomenon the name accesses, and prioritizes its preservation over disclosure, dissolution, or study of the name itself.

SCP-4167.name: The Standing Appointment
SCP-4167.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains an anonymous trust fund, administered through a cover grief-counseling nonprofit, which pays for a private meeting room at rotating locations within [REDACTED] every twenty-one days, ensuring surviving members of SCP-4167 are not prevented from convening by cost, scheduling conflicts, or venue availability. A Foundation liaison posing as a facilitator confirms attendance and reports any member's absence to Site-64 medical staff no later than four hours before the twenty-one-day deadline.

Members are not to be relocated, hospitalized long-term, or otherwise separated from the group by Foundation action except with Level 3 approval and a documented remote-attendance contingency (telepresence has been confirmed sufficient in Incident 4167-4, provided audio and video are bidirectional and uninterrupted for the full duration).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4167 designates the thirteen living survivors, as of last review, of the March 1983 partial submersion of a chartered passenger bus in the [REDACTED] River, an incident in which all forty original occupants were trapped in a rising air pocket for approximately fifty minutes before rescue. No emergency responder, diver, or bystander present at the rescue exhibits any anomalous property; the effect is confined exclusively to the forty original occupants and does not extend to family members, subsequent close contacts, or the two occupants who died of unrelated causes within a year of the incident (their deaths did not trigger onset in remaining members, indicating natural death exits the affected pool cleanly).

Surviving members must convene in person, in a single enclosed space, for a continuous period of no less than forty-seven minutes, at intervals not exceeding twenty-one days. Members refer to this requirement among themselves as "the meeting" and, when questioned by outsiders, describe it as voluntary grief counseling; several members interviewed separately deny any compulsion is involved and describe attendance as a personal choice, though none has missed a scheduled meeting in the fifty-plus years of documented history, including during documented hospitalizations, during which the meeting was instead held bedside.

Should the twenty-one-day interval lapse without a qualifying meeting, all living members simultaneously begin exhibiting an involuntary water-inhalation reflex — coughing, gagging, and gasping consistent with aspiration — in the complete absence of water or other fluid, at an intensity that has increased in observed correlation with the shrinking size of the surviving group. The only recorded lapse, a fourteen-hour delay in 1996 caused by a snowstorm, produced reflex symptoms severe enough to require intubation in four of the then-twenty-two survivors; symptoms resolved within minutes of the meeting finally convening by conference call.

The group has declined all Foundation offers of medical intervention to identify or remove the underlying mechanism, citing a shared, unexplained certainty that doing so would be "worse." At current attrition rates, model projections estimate the group's membership will reach zero within twenty-five to thirty years. No member has yet raised, in any monitored conversation, the question of what happens at the final meeting, or whether one is required at all once only a single member remains.

SCP-4168.name: The Marginalia Society
SCP-4168.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A Foundation researcher holds continuing adjunct faculty status at [REDACTED] University School of Law, providing pretext for periodic access to the university's rare book archive housing the Society's ritual text (item 4168-Book, see Description). The volume is not to be removed, photographed in full, or destroyed; Incident 4168-3 confirmed that damage to an existing marginalia entry does not reverse the associated erasure and instead produces localized, uncontrolled memory disturbance in Foundation personnel present.

Foundation monitoring of the Society is limited to annual review of its alumni directory (obtained via a compromised contact in the university's development office) cross-referenced against Foundation population records to flag newly-erased individuals for retroactive documentation before their records fully lapse from non-Foundation sources. No attempt is to be made to prevent a nomination, initiation, or naming ceremony absent Level 4 authorization, as the Society's membership includes individuals in positions (see Addendum) that make overt Foundation action against it operationally costly.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4168 designates a secret society operating within [REDACTED] University School of Law since at least 1911, membership in which is limited to twelve current students at any time, extended by anonymous nomination of existing members and never solicited. Nominees are approached individually and, if they accept, undergo a private initiation involving 4168-Book, a bound ledger of unknown manufacture kept in the university's restricted archive under an unrelated catalog listing.

During initiation, the nominee writes, in the book's margin beside a blank ruled line, the full name of a specific living person to whom they have a close personal attachment, along with a brief personal detail identifying that person (occupation, relationship, or defining memory). From this point until the member's graduation or voluntary departure from the Society, the member experiences uninterrupted, disproportionate academic and professional success: no failed examination, no rejected application, no unsuccessful interview has been recorded among the Society's approximately 340 documented alumni since 1911, several of whom now hold federal judicial and legislative positions.

Concurrently, the named individual undergoes progressive erasure from external record and memory, unrelated to the member's own recollection, which remains intact. Documentary references to the named individual (employment records, school transcripts, family photographs, others' memories of them) degrade gradually over the member's tenure in the Society, typically reaching completion within three to five years, after which no institution, acquaintance, or public record retains any trace of the person's existence except the marginalia entry itself and the initiating member's own memory, which persists but which the member has, without exception, declined to discuss in any interview conducted under pretext.

The Society does not recruit outside the twelve-member cap; a vacancy created by graduation is filled the following term. No member has been observed attempting to warn a prospective nominee, refuse initiation after being approached, or intervene on behalf of a person they have previously named. The current location and content of the completed volume, containing an estimated 300 or more names, has not been fully catalogued by Foundation personnel, who retain access to only the twenty-six most recent pages.

SCP-4169.name: The Windgate Pilotage Guild
SCP-4169.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains a maritime insurance underwriting front ("Cormorant Mutual") through which all vessels transiting Windgate Strait are indirectly required to engage a Guild-certified pilot, preserving the Guild's operational monopoly and consequently its membership structure. Coast Guard-equivalent records of pilot mortality in the region are reviewed quarterly by an embedded Foundation records clerk and cross-referenced against Guild roster changes; discrepancies suggesting an overdue "settling" (see Description) are flagged for Site-91 review but not acted upon absent Level 3 authorization, per standing non-interference policy.

The Guild is not to be informed of Foundation awareness of the mechanism underlying its safety record. Two prior attempts (1961, 2003) to introduce redundant piloting capacity via non-Guild personnel resulted in vessel losses within the following eighteen months at a rate statistically inconsistent with the strait's baseline hazard, and both initiatives were discontinued.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4169 designates the Windgate Pilotage Guild, a maritime guild of exactly thirteen active harbor pilots responsible for guiding vessels through Windgate Strait, a navigationally hazardous channel, continuously since at least 1871, the earliest year for which Guild records survive. Membership has never, at any point in documented history, numbered more or fewer than thirteen, regardless of fluctuation in shipping volume, a consistency the Guild attributes to tradition and Foundation has been unable to disrupt through indirect means.

No vessel piloted by a certified Guild member has been lost, grounded, or seriously damaged in the strait in at least 153 years of continuous record, a safety record with no comparable analog among maritime pilotage bodies of similar tenure worldwide. New members join only upon a vacancy and, uniquely, demonstrate complete practical knowledge of the strait's currents, seasonal hazards, and underwater topography from their first supervised passage, despite verified absence of prior training, family connection to piloting, or access to Guild records; interviewed new members describe the knowledge as simply "already there" upon accepting membership.

Vacancies arise at an average interval of 8.4 years and are disproportionately caused by the death of a serving pilot at sea, typically recorded as accidental (falls, sudden illness, unexplained disappearance overboard in calm conditions) and never resulting in litigation, inquiry escalation, or suspicion of foul play among surviving members or local authorities, who treat the losses as an accepted hazard of the trade. Foundation statistical review of the eighteen documented at-sea deaths since 1871 found the intervals between them to correlate with cumulative tonnage safely piloted during the preceding period at a level inconsistent with chance (p < 0.01), suggesting the deaths function to offset accumulated passages rather than occurring independently of Guild activity.

No surviving Guild member, across eleven individuals interviewed under pretext, acknowledges awareness of this pattern, and each describes their thirteen colleagues' deaths, when raised individually, as personal tragedies unconnected to any other. The mechanism by which a death transfers navigational knowledge to an incoming member, and whether incoming members are selected by the same process that determines which serving pilot next dies at sea, remain undetermined.

SCP-4170.name: The Night Channel
SCP-4170.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains continuous automated monitoring of CB radio traffic on Channel 19 and adjacent frequencies across the interstate highway network via existing Foundation-operated weather and traffic monitoring infrastructure, flagging transmissions matching the linguistic pattern of SCP-4170 warnings (Document 4170-D) for retention prior to their characteristic self-erasure from written or recorded transcription (see Description). No recovered transcription has remained legible for more than 19 minutes after capture regardless of storage medium; current best practice is simultaneous transcription by no fewer than six independent Foundation stenographers, cross-referenced immediately, to recover partial route data before universal illegibility onset.

Truck drivers confirmed as active participants in the network are not to be detained, debriefed under duress, or removed from active driving duty, per Incident 4170-7, in which a detained driver's withheld warning correlated with three vehicles subsequently lost on the route in question within the following week. Recruitment of a Foundation-affiliated driver as a passive listening asset is authorized but has to date failed in four attempts; each recruited asset ceased receiving legible warnings within one to three months despite continued presence on the network.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4170 designates an informal, leaderless network of an estimated 2,000-6,000 long-haul commercial truck drivers across North America who use short-wave and CB radio to exchange warnings, primarily overnight, advising other drivers against specific highway segments, exit ramps, or route-and-timeframe combinations ("don't take the cutoff past the Route 9 scale house after two, not tonight"). Network participation has no formal entry point; drivers report simply "picking it up" after some months on long-haul routes, and describe an unspoken understanding to relay any warning received to the next driver who might need it, typically within the same shift.

No participant has been observed to retain, record, or repeat a specific warned-against route once more than approximately nineteen minutes removed from the original transmission or more than roughly 40 kilometers from the warned location, at which point the specific detail (road name, exit number, mile marker) becomes irretrievable to memory, note, or recording, replaced by a generalized and accurate sense that a warning existed without content. Drivers who nonetheless attempt the warned route inside its active window are disproportionately represented among the approximately 60 annual unresolved commercial vehicle disappearances on the North American interstate system that meet Foundation anomalous-loss criteria, though causal linkage remains statistical rather than confirmed.

The set of warned routes is neither fixed nor geographically clustered, and Foundation trend analysis indicates the rate of new route warnings has increased approximately 140% over the past decade, with no corresponding pattern in infrastructure, traffic law, or regional anomalous activity sufficient to explain the growth. The network itself does not appear to be coordinating this expansion; participants uniformly describe the warnings as originating from other drivers rather than personal observation, and no participant interviewed under pretext claims to have directly witnessed whatever the warnings protect against. SCP-4170 is classified Keter on the basis that the underlying phenomenon generating the warnings remains wholly uncontained, unidentified, and, per current trend data, is not being adequately offset by the network's informal transmission of protective information.

SCP-4171.name: The Harvest Choir
SCP-4171.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A Foundation agronomist embedded within [REDACTED] County extension services monitors regional crop yield and mortality statistics for the choir's home town and eleven historically comparable control townships, providing baseline data to assess SCP-4171's protective correlation (see Description) without alerting local population to Foundation interest. The choir's annual Harvest Eve performance is not to be cancelled, relocated, or altered in membership composition by Foundation action; Incident 4171-2, in which a snowstorm prevented full attendance, correlated with the town's worst agricultural year in thirty-one years the following season.

Members who lose vocal function per the mechanism described below are to be offered, but not pressured to accept, standard Foundation medical evaluation and disability accommodation through existing town-facing cover identities. No affected member has, to date, accepted an offer to attempt anomalous or experimental restoration of vocal ability.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4171 designates the Harvest Choir, a volunteer church choir of sixteen members maintained continuously in [REDACTED] since at least 1889, the earliest year for which town records confirm its existence, though oral tradition places its founding earlier. The choir performs a fixed, unwritten repertoire once annually at a Harvest Eve service; membership is otherwise unremarkable, drawn from the general adult population of the town's church congregations, with turnover through ordinary attrition (relocation, disinterest, death) filled by open volunteer sign-up.

Statistical review of available town records from 1889 to present indicates a consistent inverse correlation between the choir's uninterrupted annual performance and the incidence of crop failure, unexplained livestock death, and excess mortality within the township, at a level substantially outside the range observed in eleven demographically comparable control townships without an equivalent choir tradition. The mechanism of this protective correlation is undetermined.

During or shortly after each performance, exactly one choir member permanently and irreversibly loses functional use of their singing voice, and in nine of the sixty-one documented cases, a proportionate degree of ordinary speaking voice as well. Selection of the affected member follows no pattern identified by Foundation analysis: it does not correlate with tenure, vocal part, age, health, or willingness, and has affected first-time volunteers as often as forty-year members. Affected individuals report the loss as sudden and painless, typically noticed only when attempting to speak following the performance's conclusion, and none has been able to describe any sensation coinciding with its onset.

The choir does not discuss the mechanism openly, refers to an affected member's loss using the euphemism "carrying," and has, in at least four documented instances, replaced a departed member's seat within the same season, maintaining sixteen active singers at all subsequent performances on record. No member interviewed under pretext expresses reluctance to join or continue despite general town awareness of the risk, and the choir has never lacked for volunteers to fill an open seat, a recruitment consistency Foundation sociological review has not been able to attribute to ordinary town social pressure alone.

SCP-4172.name: The Board of Somerset Place
SCP-4172.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A minimum of two Foundation agents, posing as unit owners under sustained cover identities including forged deeds and tax records, are to hold seats on the five-member board of SCP-4172 at all times, providing veto-adjacent influence over meeting minutes prior to their ratification at the subsequent monthly meeting (see Description for the ratification mechanism). All proposed minutes are to be reviewed by Site-64 structural analysis prior to the ratification vote; language assessed as introducing Class II or greater architectural alteration is to be blocked through procedural delay (motions to table, quorum challenges) rather than open refusal, to avoid drawing board attention to Foundation awareness of the anomaly.

The building is not to be evacuated, condemned, or demolished; structural modeling indicates the building's current physical configuration is sustained in part by the continuity of board ratification, and Incident 4172-6, a forty-minute lapse in quorum during a fire evacuation drill, produced a temporary structural inconsistency (a stairwell terminating in solid concrete, affecting four residents mid-descent, one fatally) that resolved only after the next meeting's minutes were ratified.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4172 designates the elected homeowners' association board of Somerset Place, a 14-story residential condominium in [REDACTED], consisting of five unit-owner residents serving staggered one-year terms via annual election, typically attended by fewer than 15% of eligible unit owners. The board's function is nominally limited to routine building administration (maintenance approval, budget, bylaw enforcement); its regular monthly meetings are recorded in written minutes which, per the association's bylaws, become official upon a majority vote to ratify the previous meeting's minutes at the start of each subsequent meeting.

Foundation involvement began following identification of a discrepancy between the building's original 1974 architectural filings (twelve stories, 96 units) and its current physical structure (fourteen stories, an unverified but higher unit count, and at least six documented interior spaces — a second basement level, a windowless eastern corridor, a stairwell connecting floors 7 and 9 without an intervening floor 8 landing — absent from any filed blueprint). Comparative review of the association's archived minutes indicates the discrepancy accumulated gradually across approximately fifty years through minor administrative language: a typographical "14th floor" in a 1988 parking allocation motion, ratified without correction, is the earliest identified instance of the mechanism, after which the building's physical structure updated to include the referenced floor within approximately three weeks, along with corroborating resident memory, prior lease records, and fire code filings.

Once ratified, minutes containing any descriptive claim about the building's physical structure, regardless of the claim's original intent or the board's awareness of its implication, cause the building to conform to that description, including retroactive adjustment of unrelated records and resident recollection, following a pattern structurally identical to that documented in SCP-4162 (see also) but confined to Somerset Place's physical structure rather than external legal outcomes. No board member across nineteen years of monitored membership has demonstrated awareness of this property; language changes have uniformly originated from ordinary drafting error, secretarial transcription mistakes, or ambiguous phrasing rather than intentional test or exploitation.

The building's current internal geometry is no longer fully consistent with itself, containing at least three documented spaces unreachable by any traceable route and two resident-reported room numbers with no corresponding physical unit. SCP-4172 is classified Keter on the basis that the anomaly's escalation is self-sustaining, requires only ordinary bureaucratic error to continue, and that Foundation influence over the board has proven capable of slowing but not reversing accumulated structural inconsistency.

SCP-4173.name: Correspondence Ink
SCP-4173.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 3.8 liters of SCP-4173 are stored in sealed glass vials in a climate-controlled cabinet in the Anomalous Materials Wing of Site-19. Access requires Level 2 clearance and written justification describing the intended test correspondence. Personnel are prohibited from using SCP-4173 for personal correspondence outside sanctioned testing.

Any letter written with SCP-4173 that has not yet been sealed inside an envelope is to be treated and stored as SCP-4173 itself, as the substance does not fully cure until enclosed. Once sealed, a letter loses its anomalous properties for containment purposes but retains its delivery behavior (see DESCRIPTION) and must be logged as an active instance until recovered or confirmed destroyed.

Foundation front organizations maintain postal intercept addresses in twelve countries to recover SCP-4173 correspondence that reaches unintended recipients before Foundation retrieval teams can respond. Recovered letters are photographed, logged, and incinerated after 90 days unless flagged for long-term retention by the Site Director.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4173 is a viscous blue-black fluid with faint bioluminescent properties, currently held in an unmarked apothecary bottle recovered from an estate sale in Leiden, Netherlands, in March 2013. Chemical analysis indicates a base of iron gall ink adulterated with an organic compound that has, to date, resisted full identification.

When SCP-4173 is used to address and write a letter to a named individual, the letter will reach that individual within 72 hours regardless of the accuracy of the address provided, the postal viability of the route, or whether the recipient is deceased, fictional, or otherwise inaccessible by conventional means. The delivery mechanism has never been directly observed; letters simply cease to be present at their point of origin and are later confirmed, via recipient testimony, to have arrived through mundane means -- a mail slot, a doormat, a coat pocket.

The more consistently documented anomaly concerns content. The wording as written by the sender's hand does not match the wording that arrives. Comparison of retained duplicates against recovered originals (see Document 4173-3) shows that the ink revises a letter's phrasing during transit to reflect the sender's actual emotional state and unstated intentions toward the recipient, frequently contradicting the letter's consciously composed message. A test subject instructed to draft a routine business apology to a former colleague produced a letter that arrived containing an unprompted admission of professional sabotage the subject had committed eleven years earlier and had never disclosed to Foundation personnel.

This revision does not occur when no divergence exists between the letter's surface content and the sender's private intent; in such cases the letter arrives unaltered. Of 214 controlled test letters, 187 arrived with content diverging from the original draft, at rates increasing with the emotional significance the sender assigned to the recipient.

ADDENDUM 4173-1: On 2/17/2021, a researcher used SCP-4173 to draft a routine incident report, misaddressing it in a moment of distraction to a deceased sibling rather than a supervisor. The letter was delivered to the sibling's last known residence -- now occupied by an unrelated family -- within 61 hours. The current occupants reported that the letter appeared inside a sealed kitchen drawer that had not been opened since they purchased the house. The contents of the delivered letter are sealed under Level 4 clearance at the researcher's request, an exception to standard disclosure policy approved without further comment by the reviewing O5 Council member.

No instance of SCP-4173 has ever produced a letter addressed to its own point of origin.

SCP-4174.name: Patient Soil
SCP-4174.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The active deposit of SCP-4174 is confined to a fenced plot of 0.6 hectares outside [REDACTED], Ukraine, disguised as a decommissioned agricultural research station. The perimeter fence is monitored by motion sensors and two rotating guard patrols. Soil samples for study are to be removed only in quantities under 5 kg per request and stored in sealed containers within the Site-64 Biological Hazards vault.

Cultivation of any plant matter in SCP-4174 soil for purposes other than sanctioned research is strictly forbidden. All produce grown from SCP-4174 during testing is to be incinerated after data collection; under no circumstances is such produce to be distributed for consumption, including to Class-D personnel, without explicit authorization from a Level 4 researcher citing this document.

Local agricultural distribution from the surrounding region is monitored quarterly for anomalous nutritional density as a precaution against undocumented offshoot deposits.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4174 is a dense, black-brown soil with an unusually high count of mineral and organic content, occupying a natural depression believed to be a filled-in pond bed. The soil's origin predates Foundation involvement; regional agricultural records suggest unusually productive yields from the plot as far back as the 1920s, attributed locally to a natural spring since dried.

Any seed or seedling planted in SCP-4174 reaches full maturity in 6 to 34 hours, depending on species, yielding produce of significantly greater size, density, and measured nutrient content than baseline. No mechanism for this acceleration has been established; soil temperature, microbial activity, and moisture content fall within normal ranges for comparable arable soil.

Produce grown in SCP-4174 is anomalous upon consumption. Test subjects who ingest SCP-4174-grown produce exhibit accelerated biological aging at a rate roughly proportional to the mass consumed, averaging 0.4 years of physiological aging per 100 grams. This aging manifests through standard indicators -- bone density loss, telomere shortening, dermal changes -- consistent with natural aging compressed into hours or days rather than years. The effect is irreversible by any method tested to date.

Of greater concern is the generational component documented in Addendum 4174-2. Children conceived by test subjects after exposure to SCP-4174 produce show elevated rates of accelerated aging markers present from birth, at approximately 8% of the parent's cumulative exposure-aging, despite the child never having consumed SCP-4174 material directly. The mechanism of inheritance is unknown; genetic sequencing has found no consistent anomalous markers distinguishing affected offspring from controls.

ADDENDUM 4174-1: Foundation acquisition of the site followed the 2003 hospitalization of eleven members of an extended family in the nearby village, all presenting with age-related pathologies inconsistent with their recorded ages, following a harvest festival at which produce from the plot had been served. The eldest apparent case was a boy of seven displaying bone density and joint deterioration consistent with a man in his sixties. Village elders interviewed by Foundation agents described the plot as "patient" -- insisting that it did not steal years so much as collect on ones already owed, though none could clarify the debt referenced.

ADDENDUM 4174-2: Long-term monitoring of the three known affected family lines continues under a standing agreement with regional health authorities disguised as a chronic illness study. No family has been informed of SCP-4174's existence.

SCP-4175.name: Whisper Fog
SCP-4175.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4175 originates from a subterranean fissure beneath the former town of [REDACTED], Romania, now designated Exclusion Zone-4175. A three-kilometer perimeter is maintained by a rotating cover story of industrial contamination, enforced by Foundation-affiliated regional authorities. Atmospheric sensors positioned at 200-meter intervals detect SCP-4175 emission events, which currently occur at irregular intervals averaging once every 11 days, and trigger automated sealing of the two access roads.

Personnel entering the exclusion zone during a confirmed non-emission period must wear sealed positive-pressure respirators rated for particulate matter below 0.3 microns; standard gas masks have proven insufficient in three documented containment breaches (see Incident 4175-Sigma). No perimeter expansion protocol currently exists that has reduced affected radius; all containment measures to date have only slowed radius growth, which averages 4 meters per year.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4175 is a pale grey, faintly luminescent fog with no measurable chemical composition distinguishable from ambient air aside from trace concentrations of an unidentified aerosolized protein. It is emitted in irregular pulses from the fissure and disperses across the exclusion zone before dissipating naturally over 6-9 hours.

Individuals within an active SCP-4175 emission report no adverse sensory effects at the time of exposure. Effects instead manifest as a shared perceptual event, beginning approximately 40 minutes post-exposure, in which all exposed individuals within a contiguous area report an identical hallucinatory experience -- described consistently across unconnected subjects as an unlit room, a body of still water, or a corridor with a fixed number of doors. Subjects can converse with one another within the hallucination and later corroborate details of it with precision inconsistent with simple suggestion or contamination of testimony.

During the shared hallucination, subjects in the physical environment exhibit synchronized minor motor behavior -- matched breathing rates, simultaneous blinking, identical small gestures -- despite being unable to see one another. This behavior ceases when the hallucination ends, typically after 15-40 minutes, with subjects reporting no memory loss but consistent difficulty distinguishing, in retrospect, which of their subsequent thoughts and preferences originated with themselves.

Cumulative exposure is the primary containment concern. Subjects exposed to more than six documented SCP-4175 events show measurable convergence in personality assessment metrics, vocabulary usage, and stated personal history details, including three cases in which unrelated exposed individuals independently reported the same childhood memory in matching detail. No subject exposed more than fourteen times has been successfully returned to baseline individuality by any tested method, including memory-suppressing amnestics, which appear to have no effect on SCP-4175's cumulative influence.

ADDENDUM 4175-1: Incident 4175-Sigma resulted in the exposure of nine Foundation personnel during equipment failure. Seven were recovered and later exhibited standard cumulative symptoms. Two remain unaccounted for; exclusion zone search teams report intermittently receiving radio transmissions on the missing personnel's assigned frequencies consisting of the same three sentences, spoken in unison by what audio analysis identifies as more than one voice.

SCP-4176.name: Undying Bread
SCP-4176.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The active culture of SCP-4176 is maintained in a single ceramic crock within a refrigerated unit in Site-19's Anomalous Materials Wing, fed a weekly ration of 200g flour and 150mL water by assigned kitchen staff under Level 2 supervision. Removal of any portion of SCP-4176 for testing requires Level 3 authorization and must be logged by mass to the nearest gram, as the culture regenerates removed portions within 24 hours regardless of quantity taken.

Bread baked from SCP-4176 is not to be consumed by Foundation personnel outside sanctioned trials. Any bread product confirmed to have been baked from SCP-4176 starter that has left containment is to be recovered and destroyed by incineration; personnel who have consumed such bread are to be monitored per Protocol 4176-Green for no less than six months.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4176 is a sourdough-type leaven culture of indeterminate origin, acquired by the Foundation in 1987 following the dissolution of a religious commune in [REDACTED], Oregon. The culture does not visually differ from a conventional sourdough starter; standard microbiological assay identifies the expected wild yeast and lactobacillus populations, alongside trace genetic material that has not been matched to any catalogued organism.

SCP-4176 does not diminish in volume regardless of quantity removed, baked, or discarded, replenishing to its prior mass within 24 hours. Bread baked using SCP-4176 as leaven does not spoil, mold, or stale under any tested storage condition, remaining edible indefinitely.

The primary anomalous effect concerns consumption. Subjects who eat bread baked from SCP-4176 report, within days, an escalating sense of gratitude and attachment toward the individual who baked or served the bread, disproportionate to the circumstances of the meal. Subjects consuming SCP-4176 bread on three or more occasions from the same baker exhibit measurable prioritization of that individual's preferences and directives over previously established relationships, loyalties, and, in four documented cases, personal safety. This effect does not require the baker's awareness or intent and has been observed to develop even when the baker is a stranger to the subject.

The effect scales with frequency of shared consumption within a group; communities regularly eating SCP-4176 bread together exhibit rapid consolidation around a single leader figure -- typically, though not exclusively, whoever most consistently bakes it -- with documented cases of group members surrendering personal property, severing outside relationships, and adopting shared belief systems within eight to fourteen weeks. The 1987 commune, the source of the Foundation's acquisition, had grown from 6 to 340 members over eleven years using this mechanism before local authorities intervened following a mass unexplained wealth transfer.

ADDENDUM 4176-1: The founding baker of the 1987 commune, interviewed under amnestic-assisted debrief prior to Class-A administration, stated that she had "found the starter already alive" in an abandoned bakery in 1974 and denied any understanding of its properties, insisting she had "just wanted people to stay for dinner."

SCP-4176 has never required feeding by the same individual twice in a row to maintain viability, and Foundation kitchen staff rotate on a mandatory weekly basis as a containment precaution.

SCP-4177.name: Reweaving Thread
SCP-4177.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 900 meters of SCP-4177 are stored on wooden spools within a lead-lined case in Site-19's Temporal Anomalies Vault. The case may only be opened for authorized testing under the supervision of at least one member of the Temporal Studies Division. SCP-4177 is not to be cut, unspooled beyond 2-meter test lengths, or incorporated into any garment without Level 4 authorization, given the difficulty of reversing effects on test subjects (see DESCRIPTION).

Any garment confirmed to contain SCP-4177 thread that is recovered in the field is to be handled with insulated gloves and transported without being worn, folded, or mended by any party, as mending appears to be the primary trigger for anomalous effects.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4177 is a spool of grey, faintly warm-to-the-touch thread of unidentified fiber composition, recovered in 1998 from a tailor's shop in [REDACTED], Portugal, following the disappearance of its proprietor. The thread does not correspond to any known natural or synthetic fiber under microscopic or spectrographic analysis.

Garments woven or mended using SCP-4177 thread exhibit no anomalous properties until the garment sustains damage -- a tear, a missing button, a worn seam -- that is subsequently repaired using SCP-4177 thread by the act of mending itself. At the moment mending is completed, the wearer (if the garment is being worn) or the most recent wearer (if not) experiences a temporal loop: the preceding several minutes of their subjective experience repeat, with the wearer's consciousness and memory retained across the repetition while their physical body, including any injuries or fatigue accumulated during the looped period, resets to its state at the loop's beginning.

The duration of the loop decreases with each subsequent mending of the same garment, from an initial average of 14 minutes to under 90 seconds by the seventh recorded mend, while the garment itself appears to sustain damage requiring mending with increasing frequency, independent of wearer activity or garment stress. Subjects retained in a repeatedly-mended SCP-4177 garment for extended testing report the loops becoming difficult to distinguish from one another, and by the twelfth loop, subjects consistently fail to recognize that a repetition is occurring at all despite retained memory of previous loops on direct questioning.

No subject has been observed to age, physically injure, or otherwise permanently harm themselves while wearing an actively-looping SCP-4177 garment, as all physical changes are reverted at loop completion. This property has led to informal proposals within the Temporal Studies Division to investigate SCP-4177 for use in field recovery of injured personnel; all such proposals have been denied by the Ethics Committee pending resolution of the unexplained subjective effects described in Addendum 4177-1.

ADDENDUM 4177-1: Subjects removed from an SCP-4177 garment after more than twenty cumulative loops consistently report a persistent sensation of having "already finished" whatever task they are currently performing, regardless of the task's actual completion status, accompanied in six of nine cases by a marked reluctance to begin new tasks at all. This effect has shown no measured decay over eighteen months of post-exposure monitoring in the earliest affected subject, designated D-4177-1, who has since been reassigned to indefinite observational housing.

SCP-4178.name: Corroding Alloy
SCP-4178.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Bulk stock of SCP-4178 (currently 41 kg, distributed across nine sealed titanium containers, as titanium has shown complete resistance to SCP-4178 propagation) is held in the Site-64 Metallurgical Containment vault. Titanium containers must undergo weekly ultrasonic inspection for microfractures, as any breach permitting metal-to-metal contact with SCP-4178 risks propagation beyond the vault.

Any object confirmed contaminated with SCP-4178 corrosion is to be isolated in a titanium-lined bag and transported to Site-64 for either conversion to bulk stock (if the object is non-essential) or containment in a dedicated titanium sleeve (if the object cannot be destroyed, e.g. load-bearing structural components). Contaminated objects are never to be scrapped through conventional means, as SCP-4178 particulate survives smelting and has previously contaminated an entire foundry's output (see Incident 4178-Delta).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4178 is a corrosion effect affecting ferrous and most non-ferrous metals, first identified in 2009 following the recovery of an iron ingot of unknown origin from a shipping container mislabeled as scrap steel. Metal surfaces exposed to SCP-4178-contaminated metal, whether through direct contact or prolonged proximity (contamination has been observed to bridge gaps of up to 4mm through unknown means), develop a reddish-brown corrosion pattern resembling ordinary rust or oxidation, distinguishable only by its tendency to form legible characters in the language most recently read or spoken aloud by the nearest human within a 3-meter radius during the contamination's formation, typically over 6-30 hours.

The messages formed are grammatically coherent and, in approximately 60% of documented cases, contain information the nearest human could not plausibly have known, ranging from minor (the correct time of an unannounced meeting) to significant (the future date and circumstances of a subsequent SCP-4178 containment breach, in eleven confirmed instances, seven of which occurred as described). Message content has never been observed to reference events more than 90 days in advance. Attempts to induce specific messages by controlling the language and content spoken near forming corrosion have failed to produce reliable results.

Contaminated metal that has fully corroded (typically after 12-18 months) becomes structurally identical to SCP-4178 stock and will itself propagate contamination on contact, functioning as a self-replicating vector. This property is the basis of SCP-4178's Keter classification: no chemical, thermal, or electromagnetic treatment tested to date halts propagation once contact has occurred, and only physical isolation from other metal has proven effective.

ADDENDUM 4178-1: Incident 4178-Delta resulted from a containment breach in which 40 grams of SCP-4178 stock entered a scrap recycling stream, contaminating an estimated 30 metric tons of finished steel before detection. Recovery is ongoing. A corroded support beam recovered from the contaminated batch bore the fully legible message, in English, "TELL THEM TO STOP READING AT SEVEN," formed prior to any Foundation involvement being disclosed to the personnel present at its discovery. Seven personnel were present. Analysis of this incident is ongoing.

SCP-4179.name: Boundary Solvent
SCP-4179.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4179 is retained exclusively for authorized Thaumiel-classification operations under direct oversight of the O5 Council and the Overwatch Command Thaumiel Working Group. Stock is limited to 2.1 liters, held in a boundary-reinforced containment flask at Site-88, and no further quantity is to be synthesized or acquired without unanimous O5 approval, given the catastrophic potential outlined in DESCRIPTION.

Application of SCP-4179 to any target requires a filed Boundary Dissolution Request, approved by no fewer than three O5 Council members, specifying the exact conceptual or physical boundary to be dissolved, the anticipated resulting state, and a contingency plan for reversal, though no reversal method has yet succeeded (see Addendum 4179-2). Personnel administering SCP-4179 must wear boundary-insulated gloves at all times; ungloved contact with SCP-4179, even momentary, has produced irreversible identity-boundary effects in three personnel to date.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4179 is a clear, faintly viscous liquid with no detectable odor, first synthesized by Foundation Thaumaturgic Chemistry Division in 1994 through a process that current staff describe as only partially reproducible; two subsequent synthesis attempts using identical documented methods failed to produce an anomalous product.

When applied to the boundary between two physically or conceptually distinct entities, SCP-4179 causes that boundary to become permeable and, with sustained contact (typically 4-11 minutes depending on boundary complexity), to dissolve entirely, merging the previously distinct entities into a single entity possessing the combined properties of both. This has been successfully employed in fourteen sanctioned operations to merge redundant anomalous object instances (reducing containment overhead), to dissolve the boundary between a contained entity and its hostile containment breach state (see Operation SATED WALL, which resolved a Keter-level breach by merging the escaped entity with its own empty containment cell, after which the entity ceased to exhibit escape behavior, instead remaining "contained" as an inseparable property of the cell itself), and, in one instance, to dissolve administrative boundaries between two redundant Foundation records databases.

SCP-4179 does not discriminate between physical, legal, conceptual, or psychological boundaries, and has been observed to act on boundaries not explicitly targeted if they lie within the solvent's working radius (approximately 0.5 meters, expanding with quantity applied). This has resulted in three documented instances of unintended boundary dissolution, most severely in Incident 4179-Reyes, in which the boundary between two personnel members' individual identities began dissolving following incidental proximity during an authorized operation.

ADDENDUM 4179-1: Operation SATED WALL is considered the Foundation's most significant deployment of SCP-4179 to date and is cited in ongoing proposals to expand its authorized use against additional Keter-class threats characterized by containment breach cycles. The Ethics Committee has repeatedly withheld endorsement, citing unresolved concerns from Incident 4179-Reyes.

ADDENDUM 4179-2: The two personnel affected by Incident 4179-Reyes remain housed together in a single reinforced habitation suite at Site-88. Both individuals continue to be administratively tracked under a single personnel file, designated Kowalski/Reyes, at their own repeated and consistent insistence that separate files "don't make sense anymore." Neither has requested reversal.

SCP-4180.name: Grief Salt
SCP-4180.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Stock of SCP-4180 (currently 6.2 kg of crystallized material) is stored in a climate-controlled, light-restricted cabinet in Site-19's Anomalous Materials Wing, divided into individually labeled containers by documented source when known. Personnel handling SCP-4180 must wear nitrile gloves at all times; direct skin contact with unconsumed crystal has not produced anomalous effects to date but remains prohibited as a precaution.

SCP-4180 is not to be dissolved or administered to personnel outside sanctioned testing protocols. Any testing involving human consumption requires prior psychological screening of the test subject and mandatory post-test counseling session with a Foundation-cleared therapist, per Protocol 4180-Hollow, given the consistent emotional severity of documented effects.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4180 is a translucent, pale amber crystalline mineral resembling halite, which forms spontaneously when human tears shed during an episode of acute grief contact any dry, porous surface (soil, wood, unglazed ceramic, fabric) under conditions not yet fully characterized; approximately 1 in 4,000 documented instances of grief-related crying in monitored source locations produces detectable SCP-4180 formation. Crystal mass formed appears proportional to the duration and, per subjective self-report, the intensity of the grief episode, with formations ranging from single granules to, in one case, a deposit of 340 grams following the extended mourning of an entire village following a mining accident in 1961.

When a quantity of SCP-4180 no less than 0.5 grams is dissolved in a neutral liquid and consumed by a human subject, the subject experiences a sensory-complete recollection of the specific grief episode during which the crystal formed, from the perspective and with the physiological sensations of the original griever, lasting between 40 seconds and 4 minutes. The subject retains full awareness that the experience is not their own memory but reports an inability, during the episode, to access or act on this awareness. All subjects have reported the experienced grief as more emotionally immediate than any comparable memory of their own.

Subjects show no lasting physiological harm from a single dose. However, subjects administered SCP-4180 sourced from the same griever on more than two occasions report a persistent, low-level grief affect between doses that does not fully resolve, and, in nine of twelve such cases, subjects reported an inability to recall whether specific subsequent personal losses of their own had been "properly" grieved, expressing this concern in terms that researchers noted as unusual for subjects prior to testing.

ADDENDUM 4180-1: The 1961 village deposit remains the largest documented single source. Interviews conducted at the time by an unwitting Foundation agent posing as a geologist recorded a local belief, predating the mining accident by at least two generations, that grief which is not expressed "will find its own way out of the ground." Foundation records show no earlier source for this belief.

SCP-4181.name: Migrating Pigment
SCP-4181.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Stock of SCP-4181 (400mL, refined pigment suspension) is stored in a UV-blocking container within Site-64's Biological Containment Wing. SCP-4181 is not to be used for tattooing outside sanctioned testing under Ethics Committee approval, given the irreversible multi-generational effects documented below. Any civilian identified as bearing an SCP-4181 tattoo (whether an original recipient or a descendant manifestation) is to be placed under discreet long-term monitoring rather than detainment, per standing policy, unless the individual displays active distress requiring intervention.

The Foundation maintains a monitored genealogical registry of 34 known family lines descended from the seven identified original recipients of SCP-4181 tattoos, updated through obituary and public records tracking, disguised as a demographic research initiative.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4181 is a dark blue-black tattoo pigment of unknown manufacture, recovered in 2006 from a defunct tattoo parlor in Marseille, France. Chemical composition resembles conventional India-ink-based tattoo pigment with trace concentrations of an unidentified proteinaceous compound.

A tattoo applied using SCP-4181 behaves conventionally on the original recipient, showing no anomalous properties during that individual's lifetime. The anomaly manifests in the recipient's biological descendants: at a variable point in the descendant's life, typically but not always coinciding with a period of significant personal stress or emotional upheaval, an identical tattoo -- matching the original in design, placement, and dimension -- gradually appears on the descendant's skin over 3 to 11 days, with no mechanical application process observed despite continuous surveillance in six documented cases.

Descendants who develop an SCP-4181 marking consistently report, alongside the mark's appearance, intrusive sensory fragments -- a smell, a partial visual scene, a specific physical sensation -- which affected individuals are, without exception and without prior knowledge of the tattoo's origin, able to correctly identify as not belonging to their own life experience. Cross-referencing with interviews of surviving original recipients indicates these fragments correspond to specific memories associated with the circumstances under which the original recipient obtained the tattoo, though descendants receive no narrative or explanatory content -- only isolated sensory pieces, described by test subjects as "someone else's memory with all the context removed."

The marking and associated sensory fragments have manifested in descendants as distant as five generations from the original recipient and have appeared in descendants who were never informed that a tattooed ancestor existed. The mark has, in all 34 tracked family lines, appeared in at least one descendant per generation, with no identified rule governing which descendant is selected.

ADDENDUM 4181-1: One original recipient, interviewed prior to her death in 2019, stated that she had gotten her SCP-4181 tattoo -- a small anchor design -- "to remember the worst night of my life so I wouldn't have to carry it around not remembering it." She expressed distress upon learning of the marking's generational transmission and requested, unsuccessfully, that the Foundation attempt to intervene before it reached her granddaughter. The granddaughter developed the marking in 2022, at age fourteen.

SCP-4182.name: Vitreous Sand
SCP-4182.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The source deposit of SCP-4182, a 200-meter stretch of beach on the coast of [REDACTED], Western Australia, is quarantined under the cover of a permanent environmental protection order. Removal of raw SCP-4182 sand for Foundation use is restricted to quantities under 2 kg per authorized request, logged and tracked individually.

All glass objects confirmed manufactured from SCP-4182 sand are cataloged under sub-designations (currently SCP-4182-1 through SCP-4182-19) and stored individually in opaque, sealed containers at Site-64. Under no circumstances is any SCP-4182 glass instance to be positioned where it may be viewed by unauthorized personnel. Viewing of any SCP-4182 instance by Foundation personnel is limited to single sessions of under 30 seconds, with a mandatory 72-hour interval between sessions for any individual subject, per Protocol 4182-Mirror.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4182 refers to a deposit of fine white silica sand which, when processed into glass through any standard glassmaking method, produces a finished glass object with anomalous reflective properties. Raw SCP-4182 sand displays no anomalous properties and is chemically unremarkable.

An individual viewing their own reflection in SCP-4182 glass for longer than approximately 4 seconds will, with a probability that increases with cumulative prior exposure, briefly perceive the reflection not of themselves but of a different individual who has, at some point, viewed a reflection in any other instance of SCP-4182 glass, regardless of that instance's physical location or the date of the prior viewing, including viewings that occurred before the current viewer's SCP-4182 glass instance existed as a finished object. The perceived individual appears to be looking back at the current viewer with apparent awareness, and 41% of paired test subjects have independently reported perceiving and briefly communicating with one another through this mechanism despite being held in separate, sealed testing chambers at the time.

Repeated viewing produces escalating effects. Subjects with more than fifteen documented viewing sessions report increasing difficulty determining, when looking into any reflective surface (not limited to SCP-4182 glass), whether the reflection observed is genuinely their own. Four subjects have reached a state, termed "reflective drift" by attending researchers, in which the subject can no longer reliably identify their own reflection under any tested condition and require external confirmation of their appearance to complete basic grooming tasks.

SCP-4182's Keter classification derives primarily from its self-propagating behavior: individuals who have viewed SCP-4182 glass on three or more occasions exhibit a strong, consistently reported compulsion to acquire additional sand from the source deposit and manufacture additional glass instances, a behavior that has resulted in at least four documented civilian glassmaking operations before Foundation intervention, and remains the primary vector by which SCP-4182 instances have proliferated beyond Foundation containment to date.

ADDENDUM 4182-1: The nineteen currently catalogued instances are believed to represent a minority of total manufactured SCP-4182 glass. Foundation web-monitoring has flagged several online secondhand marketplace listings for antique mirrors matching physical descriptions consistent with SCP-4182 origin, currently under investigation.

SCP-4183.name: Anonymous Blood
SCP-4183.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Stock of SCP-4183 (1.9 liters, whole blood, refrigerated) is stored at Site-64's Biological Containment Wing in blood bank conditions, drawn periodically from the sole living carrier, designated SCP-4183-A, under informed consent obtained per Agreement 4183. Transfusion of SCP-4183 into any subject requires Level 4 authorization and a filed justification, as the effects have proven irreversible in all 22 documented cases to date.

Personnel administering or otherwise directly handling SCP-4183 must complete transfusion procedures using standard universal precautions; no anomalous transmission via non-transfusion contact (skin contact, aerosol, etc.) has been observed. SCP-4183-A is housed in humane, voluntary long-term residence at Site-64 and retains standard personnel privileges.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4183 refers to the blood of SCP-4183-A, a 58-year-old individual of otherwise unremarkable physiology first identified in 2011 after Foundation agents noted that hospital, financial, and civil records referencing the individual consistently failed to remain consistent between successive queries, despite the individual's continued, verifiable physical existence.

When SCP-4183 is transfused into a recipient in a volume exceeding approximately 400mL, the recipient undergoes progressive loss of externally-verifiable identity over a period of 3 to 9 weeks. This manifests first as clerical anomalies: the recipient's name begins to be recorded incorrectly, inconsistently, or not at all in newly created documents, while existing records referencing the recipient degrade in specificity or vanish outright from non-Foundation systems, including records predating the transfusion. By the fourth week, most recipients report that acquaintances, including close family members in nine of twenty-two cases, express difficulty recalling the recipient's name or specific facial features during conversation, despite continuing to recognize the recipient as a familiar and non-threatening presence.

Recipients retain full self-awareness, memory, and personality throughout the process and do not report subjective distress attributable to the anomaly directly, though all recipients have reported significant secondary distress arising from the practical consequences of functional un-identifiability, including inability to access financial accounts, renew identification documents, or, in three cases, be reliably recognized by their own minor children after an extended absence.

The process has never reversed spontaneously, and no tested intervention -- including transfusion with unaffected blood, memory-related anomalous items, or standard medical treatment -- has restored recipient identifiability. Seven of twenty-two affected individuals have, following counseling, elected to enter Foundation employment in roles benefiting from reduced external documentation, citing practical necessity rather than preference.

ADDENDUM 4183-1: SCP-4183-A, when asked during intake interview whether the condition preceded or followed any specific life event, stated only that she "stopped being written down sometime after my mother died, and I never really minded, until people started asking." Foundation records show no anomalous individual matching this description among SCP-4183-A's known maternal relatives.

SCP-4184.name: Archive Paper
SCP-4184.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4184 stock (currently 340 sheets, unused) is held at Site-01 under O5 Council direct authority. Use of SCP-4184 for new document production requires unanimous O5 Council approval and is currently limited to eleven active archival documents of Foundation-critical information, designated SCP-4184-1 through SCP-4184-11, each stored in individual sealed archival cases.

Any individual authorized to read an existing SCP-4184 document must first submit to a mandatory pre-reading interview to establish a baseline memory inventory, and undergo a mandatory post-reading debrief to identify the specific memory removed, per Protocol 4184-Ledger. No individual may read more than one SCP-4184 document in a twelve-month period without Ethics Committee override, given cumulative effects documented in Addendum 4184-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4184 is a cream-colored, cotton-fiber paper of otherwise unremarkable composition, manufactured by the Foundation Thaumaturgic Chemistry Division using a process developed in 1976 and classified above Level 5. Ink is not required to be anomalous; standard writing implements applied to SCP-4184 paper produce the described effect.

Text written on SCP-4184 cannot be physically or chemically removed, altered, forged, or duplicated by any tested method; attempts to photograph or transcribe SCP-4184 text produce accurate copies that lack the anomalous properties of the original, making SCP-4184 originals functionally impossible to counterfeit. This property has made SCP-4184 the Foundation's preferred medium for records requiring absolute, unforgeable, permanent integrity, including True Containment Procedures for six active Thaumiel-class assets and the confirmed, unredacted identities of the current O5 Council.

The anomaly's cost is incurred by the reader. Any individual who reads a complete SCP-4184 document loses, at the moment of finishing, a single autobiographical memory, selected by a mechanism not understood by Foundation research staff, which becomes irretrievable to the reader through any means, including hypnosis and memory-restorative anomalous items. Comparison of pre- and post-reading interviews indicates the removed memory is consistently one the reader independently rated, in pre-reading assessment, among their most personally significant, though readers show no ability to predict which specific memory will be taken.

The removed memory is not destroyed. Analysis of SCP-4184 paper under [REDACTED] conditions has detected a latent, non-visual informational imprint corresponding to the removed memory, embedded within the document itself alongside the original text, retrievable only through a process the Foundation has not yet developed. Eleven documents currently in circulation are believed to collectively contain no fewer than 340 removed memories belonging to Foundation personnel, the majority of which were reportedly memories of family members, dating relationships, or early childhood.

ADDENDUM 4184-1: The Ethics Committee's standing objection to expanded SCP-4184 use remains formally unresolved. The O5 Council's most recent response to this objection, itself written on SCP-4184 paper as SCP-4184-11, is known to exist; its content and the identity of the Council member who read it, and what that member subsequently forgot, are not recorded anywhere accessible below Level 5.

ADDENDUM 4184-2: Of the eleven personnel who have read more than one SCP-4184 document across their careers under emergency override, four report a persistent, unresolved sense that "something is missing" unrelated to any identifiable memory gap, a symptom for which no diagnostic correlate has been found.

SCP-4185.name: The Fourth Exposure
SCP-4185.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All confirmed instances of SCP-4185 (currently 15) are stored in acid-free photographic sleeves within a single fireproof archival cabinet in Site-77's Low-Risk Media Vault. Handling requires Level 2 clearance and cotton gloves. Viewing sessions are limited to two personnel at a time, logged by timestamp, and capped at ninety seconds per instance per session. Personnel who view an instance depicting a Foundation employee, contractor, or a person subsequently identified as such must report to the Site psychologist within 24 hours regardless of self-assessed distress.

Foundation-affiliated photobooths (see Addendum 4185-1) are inspected quarterly. Any strip pulled from circulation for suspected SCP-4185 properties is to be bagged, tagged, and transported to Site-77 without development-lab review, as commercial photo labs have on three occasions attempted to reprint the fourth frame, producing blank output and, in one case, minor equipment damage.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4185 designates individual photobooth strips — the continuous vertical strip of four black-and-white or sepia exposures produced by coin-operated photobooth machines — in which the fourth and final exposure does not depict the photographed subject as they appeared during the sitting. Instead, it depicts the same individual at the approximate age, and in the approximate physical condition, they will have at the time of their death, including visible indicators of the eventual cause where such indicators would be externally apparent (e.g., emaciation, bruising, missing limbs; SCP-4185-7 depicts its subject with a tracheostomy scar not present at any later point the subject was independently photographed while alive).
