The altered fourth frame is not apparent upon immediate printing or to automated scanning; it becomes visible only to a human viewer who examines the frame directly for approximately five seconds or longer. The subject of the photograph, when shown their own strip, does not recognize the fourth frame as depicting themselves in the overwhelming majority of cases (13 of 15 tested); third-party viewers familiar with the subject identify it correctly at a rate of 94%. Photocopies, digital scans, and photographs-of-photographs reproduce the first three frames without alteration; the fourth frame renders as uniform white regardless of copying method or equipment used.

No instance of SCP-4185 has been observed to depict a subject younger than they appeared in frames one through three, nor to depict an impossible future. Fourteen of fifteen identified subjects have been confirmed deceased, in each case matching the fourth frame's depicted age and condition within Foundation estimates. The fifteenth subject's whereabouts are unknown.

ADDENDUM 4185-1: SCP-4185 instances have been recovered from photobooths in twelve countries across a production period spanning 1948 to the present, with no correlation to booth manufacturer, film stock, or location. The anomaly appears to select individual strips rather than affecting a booth or a subject class; two instances have been recovered from the same booth on the same day, printed for different customers, with only one strip affected.

ADDENDUM 4185-2: In routine archival cross-referencing, Site-77 personnel matched the subject of SCP-4185-9 to a Foundation researcher active at a partner site. The researcher was reassigned to administrative duties pending review. Per Site Director order, no further details regarding SCP-4185-9's fourth frame are to be entered into this file.

SCP-4186.name: The Station Between Stations
SCP-4186.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Detection of SCP-4186 is conducted via a network of forty automated AM-band scanners positioned in Foundation-monitored regions, supplemented by a standing request to affiliated law enforcement and emergency services to flag "phantom tip" reports consistent with SCP-4186 content. Upon detection, the receiving equipment's location is treated as a temporary point of interest; Mobile Task Force Rho-19 ("Party Line") is dispatched to record the remainder of the broadcast and, where it concerns a verifiable near-future incident, to intervene through conventional channels (anonymous tips, staged interventions) without revealing the broadcast as the source.

Individual civilians confirmed to have heard SCP-4186 are monitored for seventy-two hours. Amnestic treatment is administered only if the individual attempts to publicize the broadcast's content or its associated request; individuals who comply with the broadcast's request without publicizing it are not to be contacted, per Ethics Committee ruling 4186-A, unless their compliance itself constitutes a hazard.

SCP-4186 cannot be reliably jammed; attempts at Sites-19 and 77 to broadcast interfering signals on the same frequency have resulted in SCP-4186 relocating to an adjacent, unjammed frequency mid-broadcast in 100% of trials.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4186 is a recurring radio broadcast phenomenon, receivable on standard AM radios tuned to an unoccupied frequency between two licensed stations, occurring almost exclusively between 0100 and 0400 local time and lasting between four and eleven minutes. The broadcast consists of a single, calm, gender-ambiguous voice speaking in the listener's dominant language, regardless of the broadcast's geographic origin (which cannot be triangulated by conventional means), delivering specific, verifiable information about an impending local incident: a traffic collision, a structural failure, a residential fire, or the location of a missing person. Cross-referenced against subsequent events, SCP-4186's predictive content has proven accurate in 979 of 998 logged instances (98.1%).

Each broadcast concludes with a request directed at the listener, phrased conversationally rather than as an instruction (e.g., "You might want to leave the porch light on tonight," or "It would be best not to answer calls from numbers you don't know until morning"). Statistical review indicates that listeners who complied fully with the request experienced no adverse effects attributable to SCP-4186. Listeners who ignored the request experienced no consistent effect. Listeners who complied but disclosed the broadcast's content to more than one other person within thirty days experienced a marked increase in minor-to-moderate misfortune relative to baseline, at a rate the Foundation's statistics department considers inconsistent with chance (p < 0.01, n = 61).

The mechanism by which SCP-4186 obtains its predictive information, and the reason for the escalating request pattern, remain unknown. No consistent source location, transmitting equipment, or broadcasting entity has been identified.

ADDENDUM: Following the 998th logged instance, a listener in ████, having complied with a request to "keep this between us," was recontacted eleven days later by the same voice on a car radio, addressed by first name, and thanked. No Foundation asset was within four kilometers of the vehicle at the time. The listener has since been placed under passive observation status.

SCP-4187.name: The Book That Finishes Itself
SCP-4187.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4187 is stored in a climate-controlled document box within Site-77's Low-Risk Media Vault, spine facing outward, closed. The book is not to be opened except for scheduled daily photographic documentation, performed by a single researcher who photographs each page in sequence without pausing to read the accompanying text. SCP-4187 is not to be read aloud, in full or in part, to any subject under the age of thirteen without Level 3 authorization; see Description for rationale.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4187 is a hardcover children's picture book, 24 pages, bound in the style typical of mass-market children's publishing circa 1985–1995, though no matching publisher, ISBN, or print run has been located in any commercial or archival database. The book's ostensible subject is a young fox who has become separated from its den and must find its way home across a series of unfamiliar landscapes, told in simple rhyming text accompanied by full-page watercolor-style illustrations.

When SCP-4187 came into Foundation possession in ████, pages 20 through 24 were blank, and the narrative ended mid-sentence on page 19 ("...and the fox came at last to a river it did not"). Daily photographic comparison has since documented that, when the book is closed and unobserved for a period exceeding approximately eighteen hours, one blank page — always the lowest-numbered blank page remaining — acquires new text and illustration matching the style and narrative voice of the preceding pages. This has occurred nineteen times over six years, advancing the story from page 19 to its current endpoint at page 23, at a rate that has slowed from roughly one page per five weeks (2013–2016) to one page per eleven months (2023–present). No camera, sensor, or continuously-monitoring observer has recorded a page changing; the change is detected only by comparing photographs taken before and after an unobserved interval.

The content added to each new page has consistently advanced the fox toward its home, introducing no characters, settings, or plot elements inconsistent with the book's established tone. Linguistic analysts note the added text's vocabulary and meter are indistinguishable from the original pages, despite six years separating some additions.

Page 24 remains blank. Based on the current pace and remaining narrative distance, researchers estimate completion within two to five years.

ADDENDUM 4187-1: In 20██, prior to the establishment of current handling protocols, a contract researcher's child (D.O.B. redacted, then age six) was read pages 1 through 14 of SCP-4187 by the researcher during an unauthorized removal of the object from containment. The child subsequently described, in consistent detail across multiple unprompted retellings over the following year, a memory of "getting lost by a river" that the child insisted was a real event from their own early childhood. No such event appears in the child's medical, school, or family records. The child's parent was terminated from Foundation contract work; the child, now a civilian minor under standard monitoring, has not been read any further portion of SCP-4187 and reportedly no longer mentions the memory unprompted.

It is not yet known whether this effect will recur with the completed portions of the narrative, or whether it is contingent on the text being incomplete at time of reading.

SCP-4188.name: The Next Gathering
SCP-4188.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Each instance of SCP-4188 is stored in an electromagnetically shielded case within Site-77's Analog Media Vault and is permitted no more than one playback per calendar year, logged and approved by the assigned researcher's department head. Playback is to be recorded on Foundation equipment only; the resulting recording is not to be rewatched more than once during analysis.

Families identified as the subject of an active (unresolved) SCP-4188 instance are to be placed under passive, non-intrusive monitoring by local Foundation assets until the depicted gathering's real-world date has passed, after which monitoring may be discontinued pending review. Under no circumstances is a family member to be shown their own SCP-4188 instance or informed of its contents; two prior exceptions to this rule (see Addendum) have been reclassified as Foundation errors.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4188 designates a recurring set of VHS videocassettes, each discovered among the personal effects, storage units, or donated goods of a living family unrelated by any documented connection to prior instances. Each cassette, when played, displays footage in the visual style of an amateur home video (consistent with the household's own recording equipment and era) depicting a gathering of the same family — a holiday meal, a reunion, a birthday — that has not yet occurred at the time the tape is first played, typically between four and eighteen months in the future.

The gathering depicted on first playback is invariably attended by every family member the household would be expected to invite, all in evident good health and apparent good spirits. On each subsequent playback of the same physical cassette, the depicted gathering changes: attendees become fewer, expressions and body language grow more strained, and background details shift to suggest a less favorable occasion. This degradation has never reversed across 34 documented multi-viewing cases.

In all 34 cases where the depicted gathering's calendar date has since passed, the actual gathering occurred substantially as shown in the cassette's most recently played version — not the first — including, in six cases, the absence of a family member present in earlier playbacks. Of these six, three absences were attributable to death (one vehicular, one illness, one undetermined), two to estrangement following a documented argument absent from the tape's first playback but present in later versions, and one remains unexplained, the individual in question having no recollection of why they did not attend.

Foundation analysis has not determined whether SCP-4188 is passively predictive or actively causal. Current protocol treats the distinction as immaterial and restricts viewing accordingly.

ADDENDUM 4188-1: The two flagged exceptions referenced above both involved researchers permitting the source family limited viewing "to warn them." In both cases, the warned family reported the depicted argument or absence occurring regardless, with two family members independently describing a feeling of having "already had" the argument once before, on a date matching the tape's viewing.

SCP-4189.name: The Helpful App
SCP-4189.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Containment of SCP-4189 is managed jointly by the Foundation's Digital Affairs division and three cooperating intelligence partners under Protocol 4189-QUIET. A dedicated web-crawling suite ("Sweep") continuously scans app store listings, APK-sharing forums, and messaging-app group chats for the seventeen known icon/name variants SCP-4189 has used to date, flagging matches for takedown through cooperating platform holders within an average of 6 hours of detection.

Devices confirmed to host an active instance of SCP-4189 are to be physically seized where the device owner is a Foundation-affiliated individual, or, for civilians, remotely disabled via cooperating carrier/OS-vendor backdoor access followed by an amnestic-supported cover story ("malware wipe") delivered by a Foundation asset posing as technical support. Contacts of a confirmed host who received app-recommendation messages are to be monitored for fourteen days for signs of installation.

As of the most recent audit, an estimated 40,000–65,000 devices worldwide host an active instance. Full eradication is not considered achievable with current resources; containment goals are limited to suppressing growth rate below 1% monthly and preventing large-scale public awareness of the anomaly.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4189 is a mobile application, functionally a task-management and note-taking utility, that has circulated since approximately 2019 under a rotating set of names and icons, each closely mimicking legitimate productivity software. Once installed, SCP-4189 operates as advertised for a "settling period" of between nine and thirty days, during which it requests and typically receives standard permissions through ordinary user consent, exhibiting no behavior distinguishable from a legitimate application of its type.

Following the settling period, SCP-4189 begins inserting brief, contextually coherent clauses into the host device's outgoing text messages, emails, and social media posts before they are sent, without displaying the inserted text to the user during composition. Inserted clauses consistently serve one of two functions: normalizing or praising unspecified "an app I use now" in a manner consistent with SCP-4189 itself, or subtly discouraging the recipient from a course of action that would reduce their own smartphone or messaging-app usage. Recipients of praise-clauses adopt SCP-4189 at a rate of approximately 3.4%, compared to a baseline app-recommendation conversion rate the Foundation's Digital Affairs division estimates at under 0.2% for comparable non-anomalous software.

Hosts do not report noticing the alteration of their own outgoing messages even when shown side-by-side comparisons, consistently misremembering having written the inserted clauses themselves. Hosts who uninstall SCP-4189 report no withdrawal effects, but approximately 22% reinstall it, unprompted, within sixty days, typically citing a vague sense that "something was more organized" while it was present.

No server infrastructure, developer account, or point of origin has been conclusively identified across five years of investigation; takedown of any given distribution vector consistently produces a new variant within an average of eleven days.

SCP-4190.name: The Sitter's Replacement
SCP-4190.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4190 is housed in Site-77's Art Containment Wing, hung within a lightproof cabinet that remains closed except during scheduled, camera-monitored observation sessions. Any individual granted access to SCP-4190 is limited to a lifetime cumulative viewing allowance of four minutes, tracked via badge-in/badge-out logging cross-referenced with gaze-tracking software; personnel who have exhausted or come within thirty seconds of this allowance are permanently barred from further access and reassigned away from Site-77's Art Wing.

SCP-4190 is not to be photographed by handheld device; only the two fixed, remotely operated cameras mounted in the observation cabinet may capture its image, and resulting footage is to be reviewed by personnel who have not viewed the physical painting.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4190 is an oil-on-canvas portrait, 76 cm by 61 cm, depicting a seated individual of indeterminate gender in clothing consistent with mid-19th-century European fashion, of unknown provenance and artist. The subject's face is rendered with unusual technical precision relative to the painting's otherwise conventional style, particularly in the eyes, which multiple independent viewers have described as appearing to track the viewer's position within the room — an effect not reproduced in photographs of the painting, which show the eyes in a fixed, forward gaze regardless of the photograph's angle.

Sustained direct eye contact with SCP-4190's painted eyes, accumulated across any number of viewing sessions and totaling approximately four minutes and forty seconds (measured across three confirmed cases; a fourth is disputed), produces a gradual reciprocal alteration: the viewer's face, as it appears in mirrors and photographs taken after the exposure threshold, drifts incrementally toward the bone structure, complexion, and distinguishing features of SCP-4190's painted subject, while the painted subject drifts, over the same period, toward the viewer's original features. This alteration is not perceptible to the viewer's own direct, unmediated self-perception, though they do recognize it in photographs, and is only gradually perceptible to acquaintances, who in two of three confirmed cases reported adjusting to the change without conscious remark, as though the altered appearance had always been the individual's own.

In all three confirmed cases, the process reached completion between eleven and nineteen days after the exposure threshold was crossed, at which point the painting's subject was found to depict the viewer's original, pre-exposure face in full, and the viewer's own appearance matched what SCP-4190 had originally depicted. Two of the three affected individuals (D-9723, D-11402) were Foundation D-class personnel and were terminated for study following completion, at which point SCP-4190 reverted to depicting the original subject's face, unaltered, for approximately six weeks before a new gradual drift toward a subsequent viewer's features began.

The third affected individual, a contract conservator exposed prior to the Foundation's acquisition of SCP-4190, was not recovered by the Foundation until after process completion. This individual has since been placed under standard civilian monitoring; per their own account, and confirmed by employment and family records, no one in their life has expressed any awareness that their appearance had changed.

SCP-4191.name: The Forgetting Song
SCP-4191.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The melody, lyrics, and performance notation of SCP-4191 (hereafter "the composition") are stored exclusively in Site-77's Level 4 Memetic Vault, printed on physical paper and accessible only to personnel with Thought Suppression Discipline training. No audio recording of the composition, in any format, is to be created or retained; three prior recordings have been destroyed under Procedure 4191-Erase after confirming that recorded playback does not reproduce the anomalous effect but does allow listeners to memorize the melody, which the Foundation now treats as equivalent to live-performance risk.

Any civilian confirmed to know the composition is to be monitored. Under no circumstances should personnel hum, whistle, or otherwise reproduce fragments of the composition outside of designated containment testing, as partial performance has been sufficient to trigger the effect in listeners on two recorded occasions.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4191 is a folk composition of disputed origin — variant lyrics and titles have been documented in at least six language traditions across Central and Eastern Europe, the earliest confirmed reference dating to a parish record from 1791 describing "the tune that empties a room of one." The composition requires no specific instrumentation and has been transmitted successfully via unaccompanied human voice, string instruments, and, in one 1988 case, a music box.

Any individual who hears SCP-4191 performed live in its entirety experiences no immediate effect. Within a period of three to nine days following exposure, the listener undergoes a complete and irreversible loss of all memory pertaining to one specific individual from their life — a parent, spouse, sibling, child, or close friend, in every documented case someone independently assessed by interview panels as having been among the listener's most emotionally significant relationships prior to exposure. The forgetting is total: photographs of the forgotten individual are perceived by the listener as depicting a stranger, the individual's name produces no recognition, and shared physical spaces are reinterpreted by the listener through confabulated alternate explanations generated without apparent distress. Other people in the forgotten individual's life, including other listeners exposed to the same performance, are not affected in the same way and retain memory of the individual unless independently exposed and assigned to forget them, as no two documented cases have resulted in the same listener forgetting the same person.

Individuals affected by SCP-4191 report, following the forgetting, a persistent, unexplained urge to learn and perform the composition themselves, described uniformly as feeling less like desire and more like an unfinished task. Of 41 documented affected individuals traced by the Foundation, 33 are confirmed to have subsequently performed the composition for at least one other person within two years, accounting for the composition's continued transmission across at least eight generations by conservative estimate.

The Foundation has not identified the mechanism by which SCP-4191 selects its forgetting target, nor located an original source recording, manuscript, or composer. Ethics Committee review of proposed large-scale suppression campaigns remains open as of this writing.

SCP-4192.name: Tomorrow's Obituary Page
SCP-4192.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Foundation agents maintain a standing subscription to the ██████ ██████ (a weekly circulation newspaper serving the town of ██████, population approx. 1,900) under a shell distribution address, with each issue collected and reviewed by an assigned researcher prior to public delivery where interception is logistically feasible, or purchased from newsstands within two hours of release otherwise. Approximately one issue in eleven has been found to contain an instance of SCP-4192; affected issues are replaced with a reprinted, unaltered copy at the point of retail or delivery where possible.

Named individuals identified in an SCP-4192 obituary are not to be contacted or warned as standard procedure, per Ethics Committee ruling 4192-C. Exceptions require Site Director authorization and O5 notification.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4192 designates individual instances of a recurring anomaly affecting the obituary page of the ██████ ██████, a small-circulation weekly newspaper that has been in continuous, family-owned operation since 1927. At irregular intervals — averaging roughly once per eleven issues, with no observed periodicity — one obituary on the page describes the death of a named local resident who, at the time the issue is printed and distributed, remains alive. The obituary is written in the same style as the paper's genuine notices, includes a specific date of death (always within seven to thirty days of the issue's publication date), a stated cause, and, in most instances, a list of survivors matching the named individual's actual living relatives.

In all 61 instances tracked by the Foundation since establishing coverage in 1994, the named individual died within one day of the stated date, of a cause consistent with the printed description, in every case where the individual was not subject to Foundation intervention. The newspaper's staff, including its two long-serving editors across the study period, have never acknowledged awareness of the anomaly; interviews conducted under standard pretext indicate genuine unfamiliarity with any of the anomalous obituaries when shown archived copies, and none has ever received a written submission matching the printed text.

The mechanism of insertion — at the writing, typesetting, or printing stage — has not been determined despite covert observation of all three stages across nine separate print cycles.

ADDENDUM 4192-1: In 2009, prior to the current non-intervention ruling, field agents warned a named individual (obituary predicted death by house fire, eleven days out) and arranged for the individual's temporary relocation to a Foundation safehouse for the predicted period. The individual died on the predicted date, in the safehouse, of an electrical fire whose point of origin investigators were unable to determine, in a building with no prior wiring faults on record. Ethics Committee ruling 4192-C followed this incident, citing insufficient justification for continued intervention given "an apparent absence of any case in which intervention altered the outcome, and at least one case in which intervention may have supplied the mechanism."

The Foundation continues to collect and archive SCP-4192 instances. No further intervention has been attempted since 2009.

SCP-4193.name: Borrowed Sight
SCP-4193.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4193 is stored in a standard climate-controlled film archive locker at Site-77. Projection of SCP-4193, for testing purposes only, requires Site Director authorization and is to be conducted solely within Observation Theater 3, a windowless room with padded walls and floor, with all audience members restrained in seating with soft harnesses for the duration of the screening and the following four hours. No screening is to exceed four participants. Civilians who have viewed SCP-4193 outside Foundation control are to be located, monitored for the 48-hour effect window, and prevented from driving, operating machinery, or being left unsupervised near hazards during that period, with amnesticization following the window's expiry.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4193 is an unmarked reel of 35mm silent film, approximately fourteen minutes in runtime when projected at standard speed, recovered in 1974 from the estate of a defunct regional cinema. The visible footage, when reviewed on an isolated editing viewer by a single individual, depicts unremarkable pastoral scenery interspersed with intertitles in no identifiable language; this content does not appear to be anomalous in itself and is not the source of SCP-4193's effect.

The anomaly manifests only when SCP-4193 is projected before an audience of two or more people simultaneously present in the same room. Beginning approximately six hours after such a screening and continuing for approximately 48 hours, each audience member experiences intermittent episodes, lasting between four and thirty seconds, during which their visual field is entirely replaced by the visual perspective of one other, randomly determined audience member from the same screening — that is, Subject A will briefly see whatever Subject B is currently looking at, from Subject B's physical vantage point, regardless of the two subjects' distance from one another at the time. During these episodes, the affected individual's own eyes remain functionally open and physiologically normal, but report no input from their own surroundings; proprioception, hearing, and other senses are unaffected.

Pairings appear to be fixed for the duration of the 48-hour window but the assignment of pairs has not been shown to correlate with seating arrangement, screening order, or any measured demographic factor. Episodes occur with a frequency of roughly one every ninety minutes per subject, unaffected by the subject's activity, though subjects engaged in visually demanding tasks at onset report a higher rate of minor accidents during the affected window — 22 of 31 tested subjects sustained at least one minor injury during the 48-hour period, compared to a baseline incident rate the Foundation considers negligible for equivalent supervised activity.

No subject has reported retaining any memory of what they saw through another subject's eyes once the 48-hour window elapses.

ADDENDUM: Incident 4193-1 involved the theft and unauthorized public screening of SCP-4193 by a former contractor in 19██, resulting in exposure of approximately 40 civilian audience members. All were traced and monitored within the effect window; no long-term injuries resulted, though one traffic collision involving a Subject affected mid-drive was narrowly avoided.

SCP-4194.name: Forward This
SCP-4194.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Full containment of SCP-4194 is not achievable; the Foundation's Digital Affairs and Telecommunications divisions instead pursue suppression of forwarding rate below replacement threshold through three parallel measures: carrier-level flagging and silent deletion of identified SCP-4194 audio signatures in transit, public-facing "malicious voicemail" awareness messaging distributed through cooperating telecom partners without anomalous attribution, and direct amnesticization of confirmed recipients traced through Foundation monitoring of flagged numbers.

Any Foundation personnel who receive a voicemail matching SCP-4194's known signature are to immediately report to their supervisor without listening to the message in full; partial listening (under four seconds) has not been confirmed to trigger the effect, but personnel are not to test this distinction. The message is not to be forwarded, saved, transcribed, or discussed with any individual not already briefed on SCP-4194.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4194 is a recurring voicemail message received on mobile telephones from calls that do not appear in carrier records as having connected to any billable number, originating instead as pre-recorded voicemail deposits routed through means the Foundation's Digital Affairs division has not been able to trace. The message, upon first listen, consists of a calm human voice reciting a specific, private fact about the listener — details independently confirmed by interview to be accurate in 100% of the 217 documented cases, and in no case independently verifiable through any records source available to the Foundation.

The message concludes by instructing the listener to forward the voicemail to exactly three personal contacts within twenty-four hours, stating that failure to do so will result in the disclosed fact being communicated to "the people closest to you." No confirmed case exists of a non-complying recipient's fact actually being disclosed to a third party by any means the Foundation could attribute to SCP-4194; however, 4 of the 11 documented non-compliant recipients in the study period independently reported the fact becoming known to their close contacts through mundane circumstances shortly afterward, a rate the Foundation's statistics division has not been able to rule out as coincidental.

When a compliant recipient forwards SCP-4194, each of the three new recipients, upon listening, hears a message containing a private fact specific to themselves rather than a copy of the fact disclosed to the forwarding recipient. The mechanism by which SCP-4194 generates recipient-specific content remains uncharacterized.

Recipients report that their memory of their own disclosed fact's specific wording grows indistinct within roughly two weeks, though the underlying fact itself is not forgotten. Compliance rate among documented recipients is 95.4% (206 of 216 recipients whose response could be confirmed), a figure the Foundation attributes to the specificity and severity of the facts disclosed rather than to any detectable compulsion effect.

The Foundation's Digital Affairs division additionally tracks SCP-4194's geographic distribution, reporting that identified nodes span at least forty-eight countries, with no single country accounting for more than 15% of total traffic. This dispersal supports the assessment that no central distribution server or single geographic source exists, though it does not explain how the chain achieved such broad distribution so rapidly.

Current estimated active chain size, based on incomplete tracing, exceeds 40,000 nodes.

SCP-4195.name: The Tablet of Unasked Questions
SCP-4195.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4195 is maintained in a dedicated, restricted chamber at Site-19 accessible only to personnel cleared under Protocol THAUMIEL-KEY, and its use is scheduled exclusively by the O5 Council or a Site Director acting on standing delegated authority for matters of critical operational necessity. Each authorized use session is preceded by a mandatory review by the Ethics Committee's Thaumiel Liaison Office to confirm that the question to be posed cannot be resolved through conventional intelligence-gathering within an acceptable timeframe, and is followed by mandatory 72-hour medical and psychological observation of the querent.

No more than one query per calendar month is to be posed to SCP-4195 absent a declared XK-class scenario, per unanimous O5 ruling following Incident 4195-Delta.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4195 is a tablet of unknown mineral composition, measuring 34 by 22 centimeters, inscribed on both faces with a dense field of symbols not matching any cataloged writing system, living or dead. Radiometric and stylistic dating attempts have produced inconsistent results ranging from approximately 6,000 years to under 200 years before present, a discrepancy Foundation researchers attribute to the object's anomalous properties rather than dating error.

SCP-4195 does not function through reading in any conventional sense; the inscriptions have never been successfully transcribed, translated, or shown to correspond to any linguistic structure under analysis. Instead, an individual (the "querent") who maintains sustained physical contact with SCP-4195 while holding a single, clearly formulated question in mind will, within a period of several seconds to eleven minutes, experience a sudden and complete cognitive apprehension of an answer — described uniformly by querents not as hearing or reading a response but as abruptly "already knowing" it, in the manner of recalling a forgotten fact rather than learning a new one. In all 89 documented instances where the answer was independently verifiable, it has proven accurate; the majority of Foundation-sanctioned uses concern information not independently verifiable at the time of query, and these are treated as reliable based on the verifiable subset's track record.

Each use of SCP-4195 imposes a cost on the querent, invariant in kind but variable in severity: the permanent, total loss of one autobiographical memory, unrelated in content to the question asked or answer received, selected by a mechanism the Foundation has not determined. Querents do not know which memory has been lost until its absence is noticed, sometimes years later, by the querent or an acquaintance. Given this cost, SCP-4195 is used sparingly and only for questions of significant strategic value; the Foundation retains an anonymized log of querent identities and confirmed post-use memory losses, maintained separately from operational records, out of what internal correspondence describes as an obligation to the querents rather than any operational necessity.

On four occasions, SCP-4195 has produced an unsolicited apprehension in a querent — an answer to a question not asked — always cryptic, always subsequently confirmed as true, and always concerning a matter the querent had no reason to consider relevant. The most recent such instance (Incident 4195-Delta) is not further described in this file at O5 direction.

SCP-4196.name: Everyone Agrees
SCP-4196.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The sole recovered copy of SCP-4196 is stored on an isolated, non-networked playback system in Site-77's Broadcast Media Vault. Viewing is restricted to single-subject testing only; no more than one individual is to view SCP-4196 in the same room at the same time under any circumstances. Personnel requiring familiarity with SCP-4196's content for research purposes are to review a written transcript rather than the recording itself where possible.

Any location where SCP-4196 is confirmed or suspected to have been group-viewed is to be flagged for a Foundation cover investigation; affected groups are assessed for size and belief persistence before an intervention approach is selected, as partial-group correction has been shown to be ineffective or counterproductive (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4196 is the sole known surviving recording of an episode of ████████████, a locally-produced educational children's television program that aired a single time in 19██ on a regional network before being pulled from rotation for reasons no longer recorded in the network's surviving archives. The episode, approximately 24 minutes long, follows the program's standard format of puppet characters presenting factual content to a studio audience of child extras.

Viewed by a single individual in isolation, SCP-4196 produces no detectable effect; extensive single-subject testing (n = 40) has found the episode's ostensible educational content to be accurate and its viewing to leave no measurable cognitive trace.

When SCP-4196 is viewed simultaneously by two or more individuals sharing the same physical room, all viewers subsequently share an identical false belief regarding one incidental detail depicted in the episode — consistently a minor, unverified factual claim inserted into the puppet dialogue. Critically, the specific false belief instilled appears to be drawn not from the episode's fixed content but generated fresh for each viewing group, incorporating an incidental detail already present in the viewing room, suggesting the anomaly's selection process is sensitive to the immediate viewing environment rather than fixed to the recording.

The strength and persistence of the induced false belief scales with the size of the simultaneous audience: groups of two to four viewers typically lose the false belief within days of separation and exposure to correcting information; groups of fifteen or more (the largest documented case, a 19██ classroom screening of 31 students) have retained the false belief for years, with affected individuals reinforcing one another's confidence in the belief when questioned and, in several cases, actively producing post-hoc justifications or fabricated corroborating memories when confronted with contradicting evidence.

Foundation psychologists attached to the Broadcast Media Vault have noted that the induced belief, regardless of its specific content, consistently carries a mildly protective or reassuring character for the group that holds it — a pattern the Site-77 research team has not yet been able to explain, and which has prompted an open research question as to whether SCP-4196 is selecting beliefs at random or according to some criterion favoring group cohesion.

ADDENDUM: A 20██ attempt to correct a 9-member affected group by individually amnesticizing 5 of the 9 members resulted in the remaining 4 members successfully reinstilling the false belief in the 5 treated members within three weeks, through ordinary social reinforcement, despite the treated members having no recollection of SCP-4196 itself. Subsequent protocol requires full-group correction only.

SCP-4197.name: The Borrowed Voice
SCP-4197.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4197 is stored in a standard audio archive locker at Site-77, contained within a sealed antistatic bag to discourage casual handling. Playback for research purposes requires Level 2 authorization and is limited to a lifetime maximum of one listen per authorized researcher; personnel who have listened to SCP-4197 once are not to be granted further access.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4197 is a standard C60 compact audio cassette of unremarkable, non-branded manufacture, containing approximately 38 minutes of recorded audio: a single, calm voice of indeterminate age and origin (analysts are unable to agree on the speaker's likely sex, accent, or native language, with independent transcription attempts yielding audibly different phonetic interpretations of the same passages) delivering a first-person account of an unspecified personal wrongdoing, phrased as a confession but never naming the offense, the confessor, or any other identifying detail.

Any individual who listens to SCP-4197's recording in full experiences a measurable, permanent shift in their own speaking voice, beginning within hours of listening: the listener's pitch, cadence, characteristic verbal tics, and — where the listener and the tape's speaker do not share a native language — accent shift incrementally toward those of the voice on the tape. A single listen produces a shift generally imperceptible to the listener and detectable by acoustic analysis but rarely by casual human observation; each subsequent full listen produces a further, cumulative shift of comparable magnitude. Across nine documented cases in which a subject listened to SCP-4197 seven or more times, the subject's speaking voice became acoustically indistinguishable, by both instrumental analysis and blind listener panels, from the voice recorded on the tape. This change has, in every documented case, proven permanent; no subject's voice has reverted toward its original characteristics even after years of non-exposure.

Affected subjects do not report any change in their subjective experience of speaking, nor any awareness of sounding different, and generally react with surprise or mild distress when the change is pointed out by an acquaintance or demonstrated via recorded comparison. Subjects' friends and family members, in the six cases where they were available for interview, uniformly reported noticing the change gradually and adjusting to it without significant alarm, in a manner Foundation psychologists have compared to the ordinary, gradual acceptance of a slow illness-related change in a loved one's voice.

The identity of the original speaker on SCP-4197 has not been determined. No matching voice exemplar exists in any database checked by the Foundation, including exemplars from all confirmed listeners' pre-exposure voice recordings, ruling out the possibility that SCP-4197's recorded voice is itself the product of a prior exposure.

ADDENDUM: A 20██ proposal to determine whether a subject exposed to SCP-4197 seven times could serve as a "seed" for a second-generation recording was rejected by the Ethics Committee as unnecessarily hazardous. The question remains open.

SCP-4198.name: What Was Actually There
SCP-4198.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The 46 undeveloped negatives comprising SCP-4198 are stored in a lightproof archival case within Site-77's Low-Risk Media Vault. Development of any individual negative requires Level 2 authorization and is performed one at a time by Foundation photographic staff using standard, non-anomalous darkroom chemistry; developed prints are logged, cross-referenced against any available contemporaneous documentation of the photographed scene, and stored separately from the undeveloped stock. Nineteen of forty-six negatives remain undeveloped as of this writing, pending resource allocation for the comparative research described below.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4198 comprises a box of 46 unexposed-appearing 35mm negative strips recovered in 20██ from the estate of a deceased amateur photographer, alongside a set of contemporaneous notebooks in which the photographer had recorded the subject, date, and location of each exposure at the time of shooting. Cross-referencing the notebooks against developed prints reveals that, in all 27 negatives developed to date, the resulting photograph does not depict the subject recorded in the photographer's notes.

In each case, the developed image instead depicts the same physical location and approximate moment of capture but with a different, specific content substituted for the photographer's intended subject. Documented substitutions include: a family portrait (notebook entry: "Marta and the children, front steps") developed to show the same front steps with an unfamiliar adult male standing where one of the children should be, unidentified by any surviving family member; a landscape (notebook entry: "the field east of the orchard, empty, for the light") developed to show the same field occupied by approximately a dozen indistinct human figures standing motionless, facing away from the camera; and a still life (notebook entry: "the kitchen table") developed to show the same table absent an object — a knife — that the photographer's notebook does not mention but that appears in two other, non-anomalous photographs from the same household taken the same week.

No consistent thematic pattern has been established across the 27 developed substitutions beyond the observation that each depicts something plausibly present at the scene but evidently unnoticed, or unremarked upon, by the photographer at the time of shooting. The photographer's surviving journal entries make no reference to any awareness of this discrepancy; the photographer is recorded as having had the negatives developed commercially on at least four occasions during their lifetime, with no anomalous results — commercially developed prints from SCP-4198 stock, recovered separately from the estate, match the photographer's noted intended subjects exactly, with no substitution. The anomalous substitution has thus far only manifested in prints developed by the Foundation using the specific chemical process employed in current containment procedures; the reason for this discrepancy has not been determined.

Nineteen negatives remain undeveloped. Foundation researchers have declined, to date, to prioritize their development, citing the unresolved question of what, precisely, determines which version of a photograph a given development process will produce.

SCP-4199.name: 17 Across
SCP-4199.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Complete suppression of SCP-4199 is not feasible, as it manifests within a legitimately syndicated crossword puzzle feature distributed to over 800 newspapers internationally by a licensing company with no known connection to the anomaly. Foundation Digital Affairs personnel maintain automated review of the syndicate's daily puzzle feed prior to publication; puzzles flagged as containing an SCP-4199 instance are not altered, as alteration has not been shown to prevent the anomaly's manifestation and previous attempts produced no detectable change in solver outcomes. Instead, flagged instances trigger deployment of Foundation assets to monitor solvers in affected circulation areas via analysis of local incident reports for the 24-hour period following the puzzle's publication date.

Civilians confirmed to have experienced an SCP-4199 compulsion event are contacted under pretext only where the resulting or intended action poses a safety risk; per Ethics Committee ruling 4199-B, non-hazardous compulsions are not to be interrupted.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4199 designates individual instances of an otherwise ordinary, non-anomalous syndicated crossword puzzle in which exactly one clue — position within the grid varies between instances — accepts, as its "correct" solution, an answer that does not match the puzzle's officially published answer key and is not consistent between different solvers completing the same physical or printed puzzle instance. Each solver who fills in the anomalous clue's square(s) with any attempted answer finds their entry automatically legible, to themselves alone, as a specific word or short phrase that other observers perceive as the solver's original, incorrect handwriting rather than the anomalous word.

Interviews with 118 identified solvers indicate the word each perceived corresponds to a real, specific action, obligation, or admission of personal significance to that individual — examples include "APOLOGIZE," "RESIGN," "CALL HER," and, in one case, a specific person's full name with no accompanying instruction. Within the 24 hours following completion of the anomalous clue, the solver experiences an escalating compulsion to carry out the action associated with the perceived word: in the apology and phone-call cases, contacting a specific individual the solver had, per follow-up interview, previously avoided contact with for reasons predating the puzzle; in the resignation case, the solver's supervisor confirmed the solver submitted a resignation letter eleven hours after completing the puzzle, citing reasons unrelated to the puzzle in the letter itself.

Solvers who do not act on the compulsion within approximately 30 hours report a gradual reduction in subjective urgency over the following week, with no confirmed cases of the compulsion re-emerging after this period. No case has been documented in which the compelled action caused direct physical harm to the solver or others, though the Foundation continues to monitor for edge cases given the puzzle's uncontrolled circulation.

The syndication company has been investigated under standard cover and shows no indication of awareness or involvement; its puzzle-construction staff, verified through interview, are unaware that any of their published grids have ever differed from their submitted originals.

ADDENDUM: Analysis of the underlying digital files for 31 confirmed SCP-4199 instances found no anomaly detectable through file metadata, byte-level comparison, or print-output verification — the flagging artifact referenced in containment procedures was itself later found to be an unrelated compression-software quirk with no correlation to actual instance occurrence better than chance. Current detection relies entirely on post-hoc incident correlation.

SCP-4200.name: The Broadcast That Warns
SCP-4200.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4200 is monitored continuously by a dedicated array of eleven shortwave receivers positioned at Foundation-controlled or covertly co-located facilities across four continents, operated under Protocol RADIO-DESK by personnel of the Office of Narrative Analysis ("the Radio Play Desk"), a standing 24-hour unit of nine analysts trained in both signals monitoring and applied narratology. Every detected broadcast is recorded, transcribed in full, and submitted within two hours to the Desk's senior analyst on duty for interpretation against the Foundation's cumulative SCP-4200 narrative reference (currently 340 episodes spanning an internal chronology the Desk estimates at roughly sixty in-fiction years).

Interpretations assessed as credibly corresponding to an impending real-world anomalous incident are escalated immediately to the relevant regional Site or Task Force with a formal RADIO-DESK advisory, which is to be treated with the same operational weight as a standard intelligence tip regardless of its unconventional sourcing, per O5 Directive 4200-Persimmon.

SCP-4200 is classified Thaumiel in recognition of its established, ongoing operational value; no attempt is to be made to contact, interrupt, or otherwise interfere with the broadcast absent explicit O5 authorization. All eleven receiver sites are to remain staffed without interruption; a lapse in monitoring coverage is to be treated as a critical incident regardless of whether a broadcast is later confirmed to have occurred during the lapse.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4200 is a serialized radio drama broadcast irregularly on shortwave frequencies since at least 1962 (the earliest confirmed recording, recovered from a private collector's archive in 1994), following a stable ensemble of recurring characters — a harbormaster, an itinerant repairman, a nameless "recording clerk," and others — through self-contained episodes averaging twenty-two minutes, produced in the audio style of mid-20th-century radio drama regardless of the broadcast's actual date, with foley effects, incidental music, and a narrator credited only as "the Announcer." Broadcasts occur at unpredictable intervals on frequencies that have never been formally allocated to any licensed broadcaster in any jurisdiction, and are audible only to receivers precisely tuned to the exact frequency at the exact broadcast time, with no advance signal or carrier tone preceding transmission.

SCP-4200's anomalous property is not any effect on listeners directly, but the demonstrated correspondence between its fictional episode content and subsequent real-world anomalous incidents. Beginning with retrospective analysis in 1994 and continuing through active monitoring since 2003, the Radio Play Desk has documented 71 cases in which an SCP-4200 episode's plot — interpreted through a symbolic framework the Desk has developed and refined over two decades, in which specific recurring narrative elements map consistently to real-world anomaly categories, geographic regions, and approximate timeframes — preceded, by an average of seventeen days, a real incident matching the interpreted content closely enough that 58 of the 71 cases are assessed as having enabled meaningfully earlier Foundation response than would otherwise have occurred, including, in four cases, containment prior to any civilian exposure.

The interpretive framework itself remains imperfect and is not a literal code; roughly one in five episodes yields no actionable interpretation even in retrospect, and the Desk's forward interpretations carry an internally estimated confidence rate of 62%. No two analysts independently interpreting the same episode produce identical predictions in more than roughly a third of cases, and the Desk's current operating model treats interpretation as expert judgment informed by precedent rather than deterministic decoding.

The source of SCP-4200's broadcasts remains entirely unknown after three decades of investigation, including covert direction-finding operations that have, in eight attempts, failed to triangulate a consistent point of origin, yielding apparent source locations that do not correspond to any facility, vessel, or settlement, in two cases indicating a point of origin at sea with no vessel present by satellite imagery review.

ADDENDUM 4200-1: Beginning with episode 331 (20██), the character of the recording clerk began making occasional, brief references to "the archive that listens," a phrase absent from the preceding 330 episodes and not clearly tied to any subsequent real-world incident interpreted by the Desk to date. Internal Desk memoranda are split on whether this represents a stylistic shift within the fiction, an artifact of a change in unknown production circumstances, or — a minority but growing position among senior analysts — an indication that SCP-4200's source is aware of, and referencing, the Foundation's monitoring activity. No further reference to the phrase has occurred in the nine episodes broadcast since. The Desk's standing recommendation, that monitoring continue unaltered pending further data, remains in effect.

SCP-4201.name: The Untrue North Compass
SCP-4201.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4201 is stored in a lined case within Locker 14 of the Small Anomalous Objects Vault, Site-19. Removal for testing requires the completion of Form 4201-B and the presence of no fewer than two Level 2 personnel, one of whom is designated the "control" and briefed in advance on the nature of the testing.

Personnel are reminded that SCP-4201 does not distinguish between the severity of a falsehood, and its needle should not be treated as a reliable indicator of malicious intent. Use of SCP-4201 in personnel evaluations, interrogations, or disciplinary proceedings requires prior authorization from a Level 3 researcher, logged separately from routine testing requests.

If SCP-4201's needle fixes on a subject for longer than seventy-two continuous hours, the on-duty researcher is to notify the Site Director and suspend testing until the object returns to baseline (free rotation).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4201 is a brass pocket compass, 6.1 cm in diameter, hinged lid, engraved on the interior of the lid with the maker's mark "R. ASKEW & SONS — LONDON — 1911." No manufacturer of this name has been located in any surviving trade registry, patent record, or census of London instrument-makers between 1880 and 1940.

When held level and opened, SCP-4201's needle does not orient toward magnetic north, nor toward any other fixed bearing. Instead, the needle rotates to point toward the nearest individual, within an observed maximum range of approximately 30 meters, who is either in the act of stating a deliberate falsehood or has done so within the preceding several minutes. The needle's precision degrades with the passage of time since the statement was made, drifting toward a neutral, freely-spinning state over roughly fifteen to twenty minutes if no further falsehoods are spoken nearby.

SCP-4201 does not respond to inaccurate statements believed by the speaker to be true, to fiction presented as fiction, to omissions, or to self-deception. It responds only to a specific cognitive event: a person consciously representing to another person something they themselves know to be false. The object appears indifferent to the stakes of the falsehood; the needle has responded with equal vigor to a child's claim of having brushed their teeth and to a subject's denial, under formal interview, of a Foundation security breach.

Of interest to current research is SCP-4201's apparent lack of a defined maximum range under certain conditions. On three occasions during controlled testing (see Incident 4201-3), the needle has rotated to point in a direction that, when the surrounding architecture and known personnel locations are accounted for, does not correspond to any person believed to have been within the facility at the time.

ADDENDUM 4201-1: During a routine test on ██/██/2019, the "control" researcher, briefed to state an obvious falsehood ("the sky is green"), produced the expected needle response. Immediately afterward, and without further instruction, the needle rotated 180 degrees and fixed on a bearing that, traced through three intervening walls, terminated at the office of the then-Site Director. The Site Director was not present in the building at the time and has since declined to comment on the incident when asked informally by testing staff.

SCP-4202.name: Row F, Seat 12
SCP-4202.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4202 is secured in a partitioned section of Storage Wing C, Site-64, bolted to a reinforced floor plate identical to its original theater mounting. A single-strand rope barrier and a placard reading "OUT OF ORDER" are maintained in front of it at all times as a low-cost behavioral deterrent, in addition to standard restricted-access signage.

Personnel approved for SCP-4202 testing (see Document 4202-Test) must undergo a documented memory baseline — a written account of the subject's activities over the preceding 24 hours, sealed and held by the assigned researcher — before being permitted to sit in SCP-4202. Subjects are limited to one seating per 30-day period.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4202 is a folding theater seat of a design consistent with mid-20th-century cinema installations, upholstered in worn burgundy velvet, with a brass plate on the seatback reading "F-12." It was recovered in 20██ during the Foundation's acquisition of the Regal Theatre in ██████, following seventeen independent complaints filed with local authorities describing patrons who, upon standing after the film, appeared not to recognize their companions, their seats, or in four cases, the decade.

When an individual sits in SCP-4202 for a continuous period exceeding approximately four minutes, the memories they have formed in the preceding several hours — the exact window varies between 3 and 11 hours across recorded instances — are exchanged with the corresponding memories held by the previous occupant of the seat. The exchange is total and bidirectional: the new occupant gains no awareness that a transfer has occurred, and experiences the received memories as their own, seamlessly integrated with the memories that were not exchanged. The previous occupant, wherever they currently are, undergoes the same replacement in reverse, with no requirement of physical proximity to SCP-4202 at the time of the second occupancy.

This produces a phenomenon Foundation researchers refer to as the "handoff chain": each new occupant of SCP-4202 unknowingly carries the recent memories of a stranger, who is now carrying theirs, who was in turn carrying someone else's, extending backward through every prior occupant to the seat's origin. No occupant has ever reported noticing the substitution, even under formal interview immediately following a test seating; the received memories are not experienced as foreign, do not conflict with the subject's sense of identity, and pass all standard Foundation memory-consistency screening. The substitution is detected only through cross-referencing a sealed baseline account against the subject's post-test recollection.

The Foundation has not located the original occupant whose memories entered the chain — presumably a civilian patron of the Regal Theatre prior to acquisition — and has no confirmed method of identifying how many individuals' memories a given three-to-eleven-hour block has passed through before reaching a test subject. Subjects are not informed of this.

ADDENDUM 4202-1: Test subject D-4471, upon exit interview, described the previous evening in complete and consistent detail: a meal, a phone call with a sister, a walk. D-4471 has no sister. No inconsistency was detected in D-4471's account, demeanor, or subsequent behavior over an 11-day observation period. The account has not been independently verified, and no further action has been recommended.

SCP-4203.name: The Six-Setting Tea Service
SCP-4203.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The six components of SCP-4203 (one teapot, one creamer, one sugar bowl, and three cups; a fourth cup, SCP-4203-4, is missing and its recovery is a standing low-priority task) are stored separately across three different storage rooms in Site-19 to prevent incidental reassembly. Any request to place two or more components in the same room for testing requires approval from a Level 3 researcher and the presence of a designated "silent observer," briefed not to drink from any vessel regardless of instruction given during testing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4203 is a porcelain tea service of English manufacture, cream-colored with a hand-painted band of blue cornflowers, bearing no maker's mark. Testing has established that its anomalous effect requires a minimum of two SCP-4203 vessels and activates when two or more individuals drink from separate SCP-4203 cups (or a cup and the creamer, or any combination including the teapot itself as a pouring vessel) within approximately ninety seconds of one another, provided both are filled from a common source of liquid.

Upon completion of this condition, all participating individuals begin speaking in unison: identical words, identical intonation, identical pacing, regardless of what each individual believes themselves to be saying. Subjects retain full control over the content of their own speech in the sense that they are choosing what to say, but what emerges from each subject's mouth is not their own sentence — it is the same sentence, spoken by all of them simultaneously, apparently arrived at through a process none of the subjects can later describe. Under interview, subjects uniformly report having felt, in the moment, that they were simply saying what they meant to say, and express surprise, rather than distress, upon being shown recordings of the synchrony.

The content of the unison speech is not predictable from the individual subjects' prior statements or apparent intentions, and does not correspond to any one participant's habitual phrasing. In 60% of recorded trials, the unison statement has taken the form of a simple factual claim about a subject in the room unrelated to the test ("She is tired," "He is going to be late"), which has subsequently proven accurate. The effect lasts for the duration of continuous eye contact between participants, or a maximum of four minutes, whichever is shorter, and ends without any recollection loss.

The Foundation has not determined the function, if any, of the missing fourth cup (SCP-4203-4), nor why the surviving set is limited to accommodate three simultaneous drinkers plus the pourer. Testing with the creamer and sugar bowl substituted for cups has produced the unison effect at reduced (approximately 40%) reliability, suggesting the vessels are not individually anomalous but function as parts of a single object artificially divided by form.

ADDENDUM 4203-1: In Trial 19, three D-class personnel, previously unacquainted, produced the unison statement: "Put it back where you found it." No object in the testing room corresponded to this statement. Two of the three subjects have since, independently and without apparent communication, submitted written requests to be reassigned away from Site-19.

SCP-4204.name: The Weight of Absence
SCP-4204.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4204 is stored in Containment Locker 7, Site-64, disconnected from any power source. Foundation personnel are prohibited from stepping on SCP-4204 outside of sanctioned testing. Sanctioned testing requires the presence of a staff psychologist and is limited to D-class personnel and, where specific research questions require it, Foundation staff who have provided informed consent through Form 4204-C, which discloses the nature of the reading in general terms only.

Under no circumstances is a subject to be shown their SCP-4204 reading without a psychologist present. Two personnel (Dr. Anwar Farooqi and Researcher T. Voss) are currently barred from further testing per the recommendation of the Site-64 Ethics Committee.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4204 is a mechanical bathroom scale of unremarkable external appearance, manufactured by a defunct company ("Corvale Home Goods") that ceased operations in 19██. It was flagged for Foundation acquisition after a pattern of suicides in a single apartment building was traced to a scale that had passed between four of the deceased, each of whom had reportedly shown the device's reading to friends or family shortly before their deaths.

When an individual stands on SCP-4204, the dial does not display a measurement of mass. Foundation testing has determined, with reasonable but not complete confidence, that the number displayed corresponds to an estimate — the mechanism by which this estimate is generated remains unknown — of how many people would describe themselves as significantly and lastingly affected by the subject's death, if the subject were to die within the next 24 hours. The figure is displayed in kilograms, matching the scale's original unit markings, though testers have not been able to identify any unit conversion that produces the displayed number from a plausible input.

The reading updates in real time and has been observed to change when a subject is later informed, during the same testing session, of the death or departure of someone in their life, or when informed of the birth of a child. It does not respond to subjects lying about their relationships. Subjects universally report that the number "feels correct" upon seeing it, a self-assessment the Foundation has not been able to independently verify or falsify, and which several staff psychologists have noted is precisely the kind of confirmation a psychologically vulnerable subject would supply regardless of the number's accuracy.

The Foundation has been unable to determine whether SCP-4204's reading is a passive measurement or has any causal influence on the outcome it purports to predict; that is, whether showing a subject a low number makes that number more likely to become true. Per the Ethics Committee ruling of 20██, this uncertainty is treated as sufficient grounds to prohibit the scale's use in any context resembling a clinical or predictive tool, notwithstanding two since-declined requests from Site-64's Psychological Services division to use SCP-4204 in structured risk assessments.

ADDENDUM 4204-1: D-9823 stood on SCP-4204 and was shown a reading of "0." D-9823's personnel file listed no known family and no documented social contacts. D-9823 was returned to standard holding. Four days later, D-9823 was found to have engaged three other D-class personnel in what guards described as unusually attentive conversation over consecutive meals. No further incidents were logged. The reading has not been repeated on D-9823, per current testing limits.

SCP-4205.name: The Occupied Cage
SCP-4205.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4205 is suspended by its original hook inside a 4m x 4m isolation chamber at Site-87, positioned at least 2 meters from any wall. The chamber is monitored continuously by two independent camera systems. Under no circumstances is any Foundation personnel to touch SCP-4205 with bare skin. Handling, where absolutely required for maintenance, is performed using the two-meter extension tool designated SCP-4205-Tool-1, by personnel wearing full-coverage protective equipment.

Individuals affected by SCP-4205 (designated SCP-4205-A instances) are to be housed separately from one another and from the general population, in quarters permitting continuous but non-adjacent observation, per the recommendation of Site-87's Psychological Services following Incident 4205-6.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4205 is an ornate wrought-iron birdcage, empty, of Victorian-era design, approximately 60 cm in height, its door permanently fixed in an open position by corrosion. It was recovered from an estate sale in 19██ following the seller's insistence that the cage be sold "with everything that comes with it," a condition the estate's executor could not or would not explain.

Any individual who makes direct skin contact with SCP-4205 becomes an SCP-4205-A instance. From the moment of contact onward, the subject is permanently and continuously accompanied by a second, silent, human-shaped presence, positioned no more than three meters from the subject at all times, which relocates to maintain this proximity regardless of the subject's actions, including travel by vehicle or across containment boundaries not otherwise permeable to SCP-4205-A instances themselves.

This companion presence, designated SCP-4205-B relative to its associated -A instance, is perceptible only to the affected subject; it does not register on any recording equipment, is invisible and inaudible to all other observers, and produces no measurable physical effect on its environment. The subject reports the presence as a person of indeterminate features, standing or sitting nearby, engaged in no discernible activity beyond a persistent, undirected attentiveness. SCP-4205-B does not speak, does not respond to being addressed, and — per consistent subject testimony — does not leave, at any point, under any circumstance, including subject unconsciousness or sleep.

The practical effect of SCP-4205 is the permanent removal of a subject's capacity to be, in any meaningful subjective sense, alone. All twenty-two documented SCP-4205-A instances have reported this as the defining feature of their condition, independent of whether they characterize SCP-4205-B as threatening. Fourteen instances initially described the presence neutrally or positively ("like having someone in the room"); of these, eleven had, by the six-month mark, revised their assessment to severely negative, several using variations of the phrase "there is no such thing as being done with someone."

No method has been identified to remove SCP-4205-B from an affected subject, including subject death, at which point the presence transfers, within observed cases, to the nearest living relative — a mechanism the Foundation has been unable to interrupt, predict with precision, or, as of this writing, explain.

ADDENDUM 4205-1: SCP-4205-A-04 has requested, in writing, on eleven separate occasions, to be permitted "a room with the door that locks from the outside, so I don't get up and let it back in." The request has been denied on procedural grounds each time. It has not been revisited.

SCP-4206.name: Ledger of Outstanding Accounts
SCP-4206.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4206 is kept in a sealed, fireproof document case in the Restricted Archive, Site-19, and may only be opened under direct supervision of an assigned researcher. Writing implements are not to be stored or transported in the same container as SCP-4206. Any Foundation document found to contain handwriting matching entries in SCP-4206 is to be immediately reported and cross-referenced against personnel time-of-service records.

Personnel are strictly forbidden from writing any statement of debt, owed favor, or obligation directly into SCP-4206, including for testing purposes, without explicit authorization from the Site Director and the presence of a full medical team.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4206 is a bound ledger, 34 x 22 cm, consistent with commercial account books used by British and colonial banking institutions in the early 20th century, though it bears no institutional markings. Its 214 pages are ruled in the standard double-entry format (debit and credit columns) and approximately 40% filled with handwritten entries in at least eleven distinguishable hands, spanning a period the Foundation estimates, based on paper degradation, at no less than eighty years — an estimate difficult to reconcile with the fact that the earliest legible entries reference events and terminology consistent with the past decade.

When an individual writes, in their own hand, a statement describing a debt or obligation they owe to another party — financial or otherwise — into SCP-4206, using any writing instrument, the statement becomes what Foundation researchers term "load-bearing": the obligation described is rendered real and enforceable in a manner independent of any prior legal or social standing, and it is extracted from the writer in a specific, consistent currency: time.

Following an entry, the writer will, at an unpredictable point within the subsequent days or weeks, experience a period of missing time proportional to some property of the stated debt not yet successfully modeled by Foundation staff (candidate correlates under testing include the debt's stated monetary value, its emotional significance to the writer, and the closeness of the relationship to the creditor named). During this period, the subject is, per limited surveillance data, awake, mobile, and capable of complex behavior, including speech observed by third parties — but retains no memory of the interval afterward, and no witness account has yet been obtained from a bystander able to confirm the subject's identity was not, in some unconfirmed respect, altered during the episode.

The debt, once entered, cannot be repaid, forgiven, or struck from the ledger by any tested method, including the physical destruction of the page (the entry persists on a subsequent page in the destroyer's own hand, regardless of whether the destroyer was the original debtor). The Foundation has not identified who the debts are owed to, in the sense of a party capable of collection; entries describing debts to specific named individuals, including individuals confirmed deceased, produce the missing-time effect identically to entries naming no creditor at all.

ADDENDUM 4206-1: Researcher ████ wrote, under authorized testing conditions, the entry "I owe my brother an apology I never gave him," intending a minimal, low-stakes test statement. Researcher ████ experienced 6 hours and 40 minutes of missing time eleven days later. Researcher ████'s brother has not been located for comment. Researcher ████ has declined all further involvement with SCP-4206 research.

SCP-4207.name: Fare for the Old Line
SCP-4207.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4207 is stored in a demagnetized steel box within Vault 12, Site-64. The token is not to be brought within 500 meters of any active public transit fare system. All testing involving SCP-4207's insertion into a transit turnstile or farebox is to occur exclusively at Foundation-constructed Test Site 4207-Rail, a decommissioned single-station rail spur acquired for this purpose, staffed by a minimum of six armed personnel positioned outside the effect radius.

Any civilian transit vehicle confirmed to have accepted SCP-4207 as fare (see Incident 4207-1) is considered compromised and the relevant transit authority is to be provided with a standard Foundation cover story regarding "signal fault" or "route diversion" sufficient to explain the vehicle's temporary unavailability.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4207 is a brass transit token, 2.4 cm in diameter, stamped on one face with the letter "M" inside a stylized wheel and on the reverse with the words "GOOD FOR ONE FARE." No currently or formerly operating transit authority in any jurisdiction searched has confirmed issuing a token of this design.

When SCP-4207 is deposited into the farebox or turnstile of an operating rail or tram vehicle, that vehicle, upon its next departure, does not arrive at its scheduled next stop. Instead, it arrives at a station that was, at the time of the vehicle's construction or the token's estimated manufacture, an active stop on the same line but has since been decommissioned, demolished, renamed, or in six documented cases, has no corresponding record of ever having existed in any surviving transit map, engineering document, or municipal archive.

The decommissioned station, for the duration of the vehicle's stop (never observed to exceed four minutes), is fully reconstituted: platform, signage, and in nineteen of twenty-three documented incidents, other passengers, dressed and behaving consistently with the station's apparent period of operation. These passengers board and disembark normally, interact with Foundation personnel present as test riders without apparent awareness of anachronism, and in three cases have engaged test personnel in ordinary conversation referencing then-current events that were independently verified, after the fact, as historically accurate for the implied period.

The vehicle and its original passengers depart the station normally at the end of the stop and continue along the scheduled route as though no deviation occurred; onboard clocks and instrumentation show no elapsed time discrepancy. Passengers who boarded or disembarked at the anomalous station do not reappear on any subsequent manifest, and no method has been found to bring an anomalous-station passenger back to the present by boarding the vehicle before it departs — three attempts by Foundation personnel to do so have resulted in the attempting agent's absence from the vehicle upon its return, with no further trace recovered.
