The Foundation has not determined the mechanism selecting which decommissioned station is reached, nor whether the "passengers" encountered are, in any meaningful sense, the historical individuals they resemble, records of them, or something else presenting as both.

ADDENDUM 4207-1: During Incident 4207-1, SCP-4207 was inserted, without authorization, into the farebox of a civilian tram by then-Agent ██████████, reportedly to "see if it would actually work outside of testing." The tram arrived at a station identified by three independent elderly witnesses as the former ██████ Street stop, closed in 19██. Agent ██████████ did not reboard. The token was later recovered from the tram's farebox mechanism, undamaged, by Foundation cleanup personnel; its return is unexplained.

SCP-4208.name: The Unclaimed Coats Stand
SCP-4208.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4208 is kept in Storage Room 4208, Site-19, positioned at least 3 meters from any reflective surface exceeding 0.5 m² in area. Mirrors and other reflective materials are not to be introduced into the storage room for any purpose, including maintenance or cleaning equipment.

The Foundation maintains a standing list of 214 missing-persons cases (Document 4208-List) associated with garments compatible with SCP-4208. Any garment matching a case on this list that comes into Foundation custody is to be reported to the SCP-4208 research team before disposal, donation, or return to family, and is not to be hung on SCP-4208 without Level 3 authorization, which will not be granted for cases involving minors.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4208 is a freestanding wooden coat rack, dark-stained oak, with six curved hooks arranged around a central pole, of a style common to hotel and office lobbies between approximately 1930 and 1970. It bears a small brass tag reading "LOST & FOUND — RM. 4," though no hotel or institution matching this designation has been located in connection with the object's provenance.

SCP-4208 accepts, functionally, any garment hung on one of its six hooks. If the garment belonged to a person who is, at the time of hanging, missing (defined operationally as: reported to relevant authorities as missing, and unlocated for a period exceeding 30 days), an effect manifests in any mirror or other genuine reflective surface within approximately 15 meters of SCP-4208, for as long as the garment remains hung: the reflection of the room shows, in addition to its accurate contents, a reflection of the missing individual, wearing the hung garment, positioned and moving in a manner not corresponding to any real object or person in the room. The figure does not appear in the room itself under any tested observation method, only in reflection, and shows no awareness of being observed.

The reflected individual behaves consistently with idle, unremarkable activity — standing near the reflected coat rack, occasionally moving to another part of the reflected room, in four cases appearing to look toward the viewer without any behavioral escalation. In one case (SCP-4208-A-09, associated with the disappearance of ███████ ██████████ in 19██), the reflection has been continuously present for the entire seven years the associated coat has remained hung, without the reflected individual visibly aging, an inconsistency with the six years that have elapsed in the world outside the mirror that Foundation researchers have not resolved.

Removing the garment from SCP-4208 ends the reflection immediately. The Foundation has not established whether the reflected figure constitutes any meaningful trace of the missing individual — a survival, a record, or an artifact with no bearing on the person's actual fate — and has, per standing policy, declined to inform any next-of-kin of a missing-persons case of SCP-4208's existence or behavior.

ADDENDUM 4208-1: Following the hanging of the garment associated with SCP-4208-A-09, a technician assigned to routine monitoring requested reassignment after eleven months on the project, stating in her exit report only that she had "stopped being able to tell, some mornings, which one of us got there first."

SCP-4209.name: Spectacles of Plain Meaning
SCP-4209.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4209 is stored in a padded case in the Small Anomalous Objects Vault, Site-19. Testing sessions are limited to a cumulative maximum of ninety seconds of wear per subject per calendar month, strictly enforced by a timed testing protocol (Document 4209-T). Subjects must complete a baseline linguistic competency assessment in their first language immediately before and after every test.

Subjects who have accumulated more than four minutes of lifetime wear are permanently barred from further testing and are to be flagged for standing monitoring of language competency during routine psychological evaluation.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4209 is a pair of wire-framed reading glasses with plain, slightly convex lenses, of a style consistent with mass production in the mid-20th century. No prescription has been measured for the lenses; optometric analysis finds them functionally equivalent to plain glass.

When worn, SCP-4209 does not alter the visual appearance of a text. Instead, subjects report that any written text viewed while wearing the glasses is comprehended not as originally phrased, but according to what the subject describes as its "plain" or "intended" meaning — a euphemistic, evasive, legally hedged, or rhetorically manipulative passage is understood by the wearer with the specific claims, omissions, or intentions the text's author is assessed to have been concealing or softening, presented as though stated outright.

This effect has proven consistent and useful across controlled tests: contracts, terms of service, and redacted historical documents read through SCP-4209 have yielded interpretations subsequently confirmed, where independently verifiable, to be substantially accurate. SCP-4209 does not translate between languages, does not reveal factual information absent from the source text, and does not function on text the author did not intend to be misleading in some respect — neutral or good-faith writing produces no altered comprehension.

The cost of use is a corresponding, cumulative, and to date irreversible degradation of the wearer's competency in their first-acquired language, beginning with an increased frequency of word-finding difficulty and progressing, in subjects with cumulative exposure exceeding four minutes, to significant impairment in grammatical construction and, in the single case of extended unauthorized use (see Addendum), a reported total loss of fluency in the subject's native language, with unimpaired fluency retained in a second language acquired in adulthood. The mechanism by which reading a text's honest meaning depletes an unrelated linguistic faculty has not been modeled, and no correlation has been found between the volume of anomalous comprehension performed and the degree of resulting impairment — exposure duration alone appears determinative.

The Foundation continues to authorize limited SCP-4209 use for analysis of high-priority obfuscated documents, judged to outweigh the accruing cost to assigned personnel, a calculus reviewed annually by the Ethics Committee without, to date, revision.

ADDENDUM 4209-1: Researcher H. Öztürk, assigned to SCP-4209 documentation review, exceeded authorized wear time by approximately six minutes across an unlogged series of sessions before the discrepancy was caught by routine timestamp audit. Öztürk has since reported, and clinical assessment has confirmed, the inability to produce grammatically complete sentences in Turkish, her first language, while retaining full fluency in English, acquired at age twenty-two. Öztürk has requested that this addendum be translated for her records. The request has been denied as procedurally irregular.

SCP-4210.name: The Perfect-Circle Compass
SCP-4210.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4210 is stored disassembled — its two arms separated and held in adjacent but non-adjoining foam cutouts — in Locker 22, Site-19. Reassembly requires two-person authorization. No circle is to be drawn using SCP-4210 for any purpose other than sanctioned testing without a specific, revocable exception logged in Document 4210-Access.

Note: Facilities and Logistics maintains standing authorization to request SCP-4210 for containment-adjacent applications (see Addendum 4210-2). All such requests are reviewed individually; SCP-4210 is not to be treated as a routine containment tool despite its demonstrated utility.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4210 is a brass drafting compass of a design consistent with 19th-century technical drawing instruments, its two arms joined by a worn but functional pivot screw, one arm terminating in a steel point, the other in a fitted graphite lead holder.

A circle drawn by SCP-4210, provided it is drawn as a single continuous motion with the steel point held fixed and the drawing arm completing a full 360-degree rotation without lifting, becomes a functional boundary. The boundary applies to the surface the circle is drawn on and, where the surface is not flat or is porous (fabric, water, loose soil), extends in a manner Foundation researchers describe as "the geometrically simplest consistent interpretation" — a circle drawn on the surface of water produces a cylindrical boundary extending to the container's floor; a circle drawn on a wall produces a boundary extending through the wall's full thickness.

No physical object, and to date no tested anomalous entity or effect, has been able to cross a boundary produced by SCP-4210 without the permission of the individual who drew the circle — permission that may be granted verbally, in advance, to a named individual, group, or defined category of individual ("Foundation personnel with Level 2 clearance or higher"), and revoked at will, with immediate effect, by the drawer regardless of the drawer's location relative to the boundary. The boundary persists indefinitely, does not degrade with time or drawing-surface damage short of the erasure of the circle itself, and has, in nine of nine tested cases, contained SCP designated entities up to and including Keter-class subjects with no other tested reliable containment method, provided a circle of sufficient diameter could be physically drawn around the subject.

The compass has one notable limitation: it functions only in the hand of the individual who drew the circle for purposes of subsequent modification (extending permission, revoking permission, or erasing the boundary); a second individual holding SCP-4210 cannot alter a boundary they did not draw, even with the original drawer's stated consent, a restriction the Foundation has not found a documented workaround for. In practical terms, this means every boundary drawn by SCP-4210 remains permanently dependent on a single living individual's continued availability, willingness, and — per one incident — continued sound judgment.

ADDENDUM 4210-1: SCP-4210 has been used in eleven sanctioned containment applications to date, including the emergency re-containment of SCP-████ in 20██. The researcher who drew that boundary, Dr. ██████, retired from Foundation service in 20██. Per standing procedure, Dr. ██████ remains on a confidential retainer contract requiring their availability for boundary modification requests, an arrangement Dr. ██████ has, according to Human Resources, described in an exit interview as "the only part of this job I never actually left."

SCP-4211.name: The Binding Seal
SCP-4211.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4211 is stored in a locked case within the Restricted Archive, Site-19, separated from all sealing wax and wax-substitute materials, which are stored in a different wing. Any written material bearing an unbroken seal impressed by SCP-4211 is to be treated as a live containment hazard and is not to be opened except under Level 4 authorization, in a blast- and effect-isolated testing chamber, with full medical standby.

Personnel are forbidden from drafting, dictating, or approving the wording of any sealed statement without review by the assigned Ethics Committee liaison, given the object's demonstrated tendency to render threats and warnings, and not only formal obligations, enforceable.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4211 is a brass seal stamp of a design consistent with private correspondence seals used in continental Europe in the 18th and 19th centuries, its face engraved with an unidentified heraldic device: a hand holding a closed book, encircled by a phrase in a script Foundation linguists have been unable to conclusively identify, tentatively rendered as "what is set is set."

When SCP-4211 is used to press a wax seal onto a folded or enclosed written document, any statement contained within that document describing a consequence, promise, or threat contingent on the document being opened, read, or acted upon becomes binding on reality in a manner independent of the sealer's own capability to enforce it. The Foundation's working model, informed by 34 controlled trials, holds that breaking the seal triggers the described consequence exactly as written, with no provision for hyperbole, idiom, or figurative language: a sealed note reading "if you read this, you'll wish you hadn't" has, in testing, produced outcomes ranging from mild regret to, in one incident, an undiagnosed illness in the reader lasting six weeks, apparently calibrated to whatever the sealer subjectively meant by the phrase at the time of sealing rather than to its literal content.

This last property — that the enforced consequence reflects the sealer's private intent rather than the statement's plain wording — has made SCP-4211 unsuitable for the deterrent or containment applications initially proposed by Site-19's Tactical Applications division, since a sealer's intent at the moment of sealing cannot be reliably audited after the fact, and two Foundation-authored test seals have produced consequences the drafting researcher stated, under subsequent interview, they had not consciously intended.

The seal cannot be broken without triggering its effect; documents sealed by SCP-4211 have proven resistant to attempts to access their contents by means other than breaking the wax directly, including X-ray imaging, careful steaming, and, in one authorized test, controlled incineration of the surrounding paper while leaving the seal itself structurally undisturbed until the moment of failure, at which point the described consequence occurred regardless.

The Foundation has sealed and archived, unopened, four documents produced by unknown parties prior to acquisition, on the assessment that their contents are unrecoverable without cost and that the risk of leaving them permanently unopened is lower than the risk of reading them.

ADDENDUM 4211-1: One archived, unopened SCP-4211 document (Item 4211-C) is addressed, in a contemporary hand, to a specific living Foundation researcher by name and current title — a title the researcher did not hold at the time the document is estimated to have been sealed. The researcher has not been informed of the document's existence.

SCP-4212.name: The Summoning Knocker
SCP-4212.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4212 remains mounted, per operational requirement, on Door 12-A, a purpose-built door frame standing freely in Operations Room 4212, Site-19, not connected to any wall or passage. Use of SCP-4212 for its designated Foundation function (see Addendum 4212-1) requires the authorization of a Level 4 researcher and is logged in a dedicated operations ledger separate from standard testing documentation.

Unauthorized personnel are forbidden from touching SCP-4212. A standing Foundation directive requires that any individual who becomes aware, through any means, of SCP-4212's function be briefed on the containment risk posed by idly thinking about knocking on a door fitted with a similar knocker, and be advised, without being given further technical detail, to avoid dwelling on the thought.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4212 is a brass door knocker cast in the shape of a stylized lion's head, of a design common to institutional and residential doors in continental Europe from the 19th century onward, functionally unremarkable in construction.

When SCP-4212 is struck against its mounting plate by an individual with Foundation-verified authorization, the object identifies the living individual who, at that moment, holds the most recent and clearest memory of consciously intending or imagining knocking on a door fitted with SCP-4212 or an object the target's mind treats as equivalent to it, and relocates that individual, instantaneously and without apparent regard for intervening distance, to a position immediately in front of Door 12-A. The mechanism of relocation has not been characterized; the target experiences no subjective transit, reporting only an immediate discontinuity between their prior location and arrival at the door, and objects or persons not in direct, continuous physical contact with the target at the moment of transfer are left behind.

This property has been adapted by the Foundation into a limited-use operational asset: by ensuring that a specific individual — most often Foundation personnel briefed to think, on a fixed schedule or on specific cue, about knocking on Door 12-A — holds the "freshest" qualifying memory at the moment SCP-4212 is struck, the object can be used to retrieve that individual from an otherwise inaccessible or hazardous location with a reliability of approximately 94% across 61 sanctioned operational uses to date, including two extractions from active containment breaches and one retrieval of a field agent from a location the Foundation has, per standing policy, declined to specify further in this document.

The object's chief limitation, and the basis for its Thaumiel classification alongside its documented utility, is the absence of any confirmed method to guarantee which individual, of an unknown and unbounded population, currently holds the qualifying memory at the moment of any given strike. Applications outside of deliberately engineered retrieval operations are considered categorically unsafe, since SCP-4212 cannot distinguish an intentionally cued memory from an incidental one, and the object's use consequently carries a standing, low but nonzero, risk of relocating an uninvolved civilian — anywhere in the world, without warning, consent, or subsequent memory of why — to a secured Foundation site.

ADDENDUM 4212-1: Operational Use Log excerpt, entry 47: retrieval of Agent M. Kowalczyk from [DATA EXPUNGED] successful, elapsed time from strike to arrival under one second, Agent Kowalczyk uninjured. Entry 52, filed six weeks later and never satisfactorily resolved: an unidentified civilian, later confirmed to be a resident of a city with no documented Foundation presence, appeared before Door 12-A during a scheduled retrieval test not associated with any authorized strike. The civilian was administered standard amnestics and returned. The scheduled strike that produced the appearance has not been identified.

SCP-4213.name: The Forgetting Doorway
SCP-4213.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All confirmed fruiting bodies of SCP-4213 are to be photographed, tagged, and left in situ unless their host doorway is scheduled for demolition or relocation, in which case the fungal mat is to be excised under Level 2 biohazard protocol and transferred to Site-77's mycological archive in a humidity-controlled case. Personnel are prohibited from using any doorway bearing visible SCP-4213 fruiting bodies without prior D-class testing of that specific specimen, as fruiting frequency and spore potency vary between individuals for reasons not yet determined.

Foundation front companies retain listings on at least forty vacant commercial and residential properties believed to contain unmapped SCP-4213 colonies; these properties are monitored remotely and are not to be shown to prospective buyers or tenants. Any civilian report of "a room I forgot I had" filed with local property records offices is to be cross-referenced against this list and investigated by a two-person MTF liaison team within seventy-two hours.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4213 is a basidiomycete fungus, tentatively classified within the family Polyporaceae, that fruits exclusively along the lintels and jambs of doorways that have gone continuously unused for no fewer than thirty-one days. Fruiting bodies are shelf-like, grey-brown, and rarely exceed 4 cm in width; they are frequently mistaken for ordinary wood-rot bracket fungi and go unreported for this reason.

SCP-4213's anomalous property manifests only at the moment the associated doorway is used again after its dormancy period. At this moment, the fruiting body releases a cloud of spores too fine to be seen without magnification. Any individual who inhales these spores while crossing the threshold retains full and accurate memory of the space beyond the door -- its contents, its layout, any events that occurred within it -- but loses entirely the specific memory of the period during which the doorway went unused. The subject instead recalls having passed through the doorway at ordinary, unremarkable intervals throughout that period, despite no such passage having occurred. External records (dust accumulation, security logs, testimony of unaffected third parties) confirming the door's disuse do not restore the memory and are typically rationalized away by the subject without distress.

The effect is retroactive only to the most recent dormancy period; it does not compound across multiple fruiting-and-use cycles unless the door is again left unused for the requisite interval. SCP-4213 fruiting bodies release no further spores after this single event and become inert, though they do not visibly decay for several years afterward.

ADDENDUM 4213-1: During routine collection at Site-77, a culture of SCP-4213 maintained in a sealed growth chamber with no doorway present began, over an 11-day period, to arrange its mycelial growth into a shape closely resembling a door frame, oriented toward the chamber's single access hatch. Foundation mycologist Dr. Onat Peker noted in his log that the hatch, opened only for scheduled feeding, "had not yet gone unused for thirty-one days, but would, on the specific date the growth pattern seemed to be counting toward." The chamber was subsequently sealed and the hatch used on a strict daily schedule going forward. No further anomalous growth has been recorded. Dr. Peker's log entries for days 8 through 11 have not been located.

SCP-4214.name: The Herald Eel
SCP-4214.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Structures confirmed to house an active SCP-4214 specimen are not to have the specimen removed, destroyed, or otherwise interfered with under any circumstances without direct authorization from a Level 4 researcher, per the findings of Incident 4214-3 (see Addendum). Foundation-affiliated plumbers, well inspectors, and pest control contractors operating within a 40 km radius of any of the six confirmed "eel towns" are briefed to report, rather than remove, any eel-like organism found in domestic water systems, and to falsify service paperwork indicating the fixture was cleared.

Households currently hosting SCP-4214 are placed under passive surveillance by embedded Foundation assets where feasible. No household is to be informed of the specimen's presence or its implications under any circumstances.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4214 refers to a population of anguilliform fish, superficially resembling Anguilla rostrata but bearing faint bioluminescent striping along the lateral line, which appear without observed introduction inside the plumbing, wells, cisterns, or other enclosed water systems of residential structures. A specimen's arrival cannot presently be predicted; its presence is discovered only when a resident notices the animal in a sink trap, toilet tank, or similar fixture.

In one hundred percent of cases verified before the death occurred (n=34), the appearance of an SCP-4214 specimen within a structure preceded the death by natural causes of a resident of that structure by a period of 58 to 94 days (mean 71). The specimen shows no aggressive behavior and does not appear to target a specific individual within multi-occupant households; the correlation is with the structure, not the person, though in every recorded case the eventual decedent was a resident at the time of the eel's arrival.

SCP-4214 specimens cannot be traced to any point of entry consistent with the plumbing's physical layout and are never observed in transit. Following the associated death, the specimen is invariably absent at the next inspection, with no trace of exit.

ADDENDUM 4214-1: Water quality and biological testing performed on captured specimens show no anomalous properties in tissue, blood, or behavior under laboratory observation; specimens outside their host structure die within 6-9 hours despite standard freshwater husbandry.

ADDENDUM 4214-2 (Incident 4214-3): In a 20██ field test, a specimen was removed from a residence and euthanized in an attempt to determine whether the associated death could be prevented. The resident who would otherwise have died at day 71 died at day 19 instead, of an unrelated cardiac event. A second specimen appeared in the same household's plumbing within 48 hours of the first resident's death, preceding the death of a second occupant by the expected interval. Foundation policy since Incident 4214-3 is strict non-interference. It remains undetermined whether SCP-4214 specimens detect impending deaths or are in some manner responsible for them, and further live-subject testing to resolve this question has been denied by the Ethics Committee. Personnel note that, across the four recorded multi-death households, the interval between the first specimen's disappearance and the second specimen's appearance has never varied by more than six hours, a consistency for which no proposed biological explanation currently accounts.

SCP-4215.name: The Last-Word Moths
SCP-4215.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Specimens of SCP-4215 are not actively contained; the species is treated as a monitored wild population distributed across at least eleven temperate regions. Foundation-affiliated hospice facilities and long-term care wards in monitored regions are fitted with fine-mesh window screening rated to exclude adult moths, and staff are trained to bag and refrigerate, rather than kill or discard, any specimen found within 48 hours of a patient death.

Recovered specimens are transported to Site-31 for wing preservation and are catalogued according to the number of scale-groove impressions present, believed to correlate with syllable count. Playback equipment and protocols are restricted to Level 3 personnel; recordings recovered from specimen wings are treated as classified testimony and handled under standard next-of-kin disclosure restrictions, i.e., not disclosed.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4215 is a moth species, family Erebidae, physically unremarkable except for an unusually fine, ridged scale structure on the dorsal forewing. Adult SCP-4215 specimens are not observed in significant numbers except in the presence of a dying mammal (any species; approximately 70% of recorded gatherings involve human subjects, likely reflecting observation bias rather than moth preference), typically arriving within the final ten minutes of life and departing within minutes of death.

The number of individual moths present at a gathering corresponds, in verified cases, to the number of syllables spoken by the dying individual in their final utterance, with one moth per syllable. Silent deaths draw no moths. Microscopic analysis of the wing-scale ridges of recovered specimens has demonstrated that these ridges encode an audio waveform in a manner mechanically analogous to a phonograph cylinder; dragging a fine stylus across the ridges under proper equipment reproduces a degraded but intelligible recording of the syllable the moth is believed to correspond to, apparently captured via an unknown sensory mechanism at the moment of utterance.

ADDENDUM 4215-1: Standard behavior is understood, if not explained, as a response to an already-occurring death. Field Agent Dilara Soysal's report from 20██ describes a gathering of six SCP-4215 specimens observed outside the window of a hospice patient who was, at the time of the gathering, sedated, non-verbal, and by all clinical measures at least four hours from death. The patient regained brief lucidity approximately eleven minutes after the moths' arrival and spoke a six-syllable sentence to an attending nurse before dying nine minutes later. The moths dispersed immediately following the utterance, consistent with standard behavior -- except that their arrival preceded the words by eleven minutes, and preceded the patient's capacity to speak at all.

This case remains the only well-documented instance of SCP-4215 gathering activity preceding, rather than accompanying, a final utterance. Foundation entomologists have not proposed a mechanism by which the species could anticipate speech content prior to its occurrence, and the case file remains open pending further data.

SCP-4216.name: The Duplicating Crab
SCP-4216.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The SCP-4216 breeding population (currently 22 individuals) is housed in a climate-controlled brackish-water enclosure at Site-77, divided into individual molting chambers to prevent uncontrolled duplication events. No object is to be placed within 1.5 meters of a specimen approaching its molting cycle (identifiable by a 36-48 hour appetite cessation) except sterile, Foundation-manufactured "feeder" objects consisting of inert ceramic discs of standard mass, which are provided in place of any incidental materials.

Any object confirmed or suspected to have been duplicated by SCP-4216 is to be tagged, and both the duplicate and the diminishing original are to be weighed weekly until the original's mass reaches zero, at which point the original is disposed of as biohazard waste and the duplicate is retained under standard object storage pending further study. Personnel are reminded that a duplicate is, for all practical and legal purposes, indistinguishable from the original, and this fact has created documented provenance concerns (see Addendum 4216-2).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4216 is a species of land-dwelling decapod crustacean, approximately 6-9 cm in carapace width, superficially resembling members of the family Coenobitidae but lacking the borrowed-shell behavior typical of hermit crabs. SCP-4216 specimens undergo a molting cycle roughly every 40 days; the anomalous property manifests during this molt.

Rather than shedding a hollow exoskeleton, a molting SCP-4216 specimen produces a solid, fully detailed physical duplicate of a single inert object within its immediate environment, provided the object's mass does not exceed approximately 500 grams. The duplicate is chemically, structurally, and by all available forensic measures identical to the source object at the moment of duplication, including surface wear, internal composition, and -- in the case of tested written documents -- ink chemistry and paper fiber structure.

Over a period of two to nine weeks following duplication, the original object undergoes a gradual, measurable loss of mass, eventually becoming hollow, structurally unsound, and non-functional, while showing no external signs of the process (no dust, residue, or byproduct has been recovered). The duplicate correspondingly does not gain mass beyond its initial value; the transferred mass does not appear to move from original to duplicate through any detectable medium, and total system mass is not conserved at any single point in time, though it balances before and after the multi-week process completes.

ADDENDUM 4216-1: The mechanism by which SCP-4216 selects a target object for duplication during molt is unknown. In observed cases, if no object is present within range, the specimen instead duplicates a portion of the enclosure's own substrate, or, in one instance, a fragment of its own prior molt.

ADDENDUM 4216-2: Site-77 briefly lost track of provenance on a piece of SCP-4216-adjacent research correspondence in 20██ after an unsecured document was left within range of a molting specimen and subsequently hollowed. The duplicate, being indistinguishable from the original, was filed and referenced for eleven months before the discrepancy was noticed during an unrelated audit. Object security protocols near SCP-4216 enclosures have since been revised. The original, hollowed document could not be located for retrieval.

SCP-4217.name: The Unbound Colony
SCP-4217.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The primary SCP-4217 nest, located beneath [REDACTED], is contained within a reinforced concrete perimeter fitted with continuous thermal and seismic monitoring. Perimeter breach -- defined as any newly detected tunnel segment crossing the containment boundary -- triggers immediate deployment of MTF Eta-11 ("Moleworks") to locate and seal the terminus.

Because SCP-4217 tunnel segments have been confirmed to intermittently and unpredictably connect to wall cavities, crawlspaces, and subterranean structures at distances of up to 340 km from the primary nest with no continuous physical tunnel accounting for the distance, full physical containment is not presently achievable. All confirmed remote tunnel termini are to be sealed with expanding anomalous-resistant foam (see Document 4217-F) within 24 hours of detection. Personnel are not permitted to enter any tunnel segment exceeding 3 meters in mapped length without Level 3 authorization and a tethered egress line.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4217 is a eusocial ant species, morphologically consistent with the subfamily Myrmicinae, distinguished from known species by consistent tunnel-construction behavior that violates expected spatial constraints. Excavated nest chambers and connecting tunnels regularly measure, by internal survey, between 4 and 60 times the volume that the surrounding soil or structural material could physically accommodate, without corresponding surface subsidence, structural displacement, or any other externally observable evidence of the excavated material's removal.

At irregular intervals corresponding to colony population thresholds (estimated at every 8,000-10,000 additional workers), newly excavated tunnel segments have been found to terminate not at a natural rock stratum or aquifer, as is typical, but within enclosed wall cavities, ductwork, or subfloor spaces of standing structures unconnected to the primary nest site by any continuous excavated path. These remote termini permit worker traffic and, in four documented cases, permitted the passage of small objects and one juvenile domestic cat, recovered alive 60 km from its point of disappearance.

SCP-4217 workers additionally cultivate a fungal species (see SCP-4217-B, pending separate designation) along tunnel walls that appears to metabolize structural material -- wood, drywall, and in one case reinforced concrete -- at a rate inconsistent with the fungus's observed biomass, with no proportional increase in fungal mass or byproduct accounting for the material consumed.

ADDENDUM 4217-1: A survey team mapping a newly discovered tunnel segment in 20██ reported that the passage terminated at a wall opening into a room matching no blueprint, satellite record, or Foundation database entry for the structure it was assumed to be part of. The room was photographed before the survey team's equipment failed; recovered images show a furnished interior consistent with mid-20th-century construction. The structure above the confirmed nest site was built in 1994. The tunnel segment collapsed naturally 6 hours after discovery and has not been re-located despite extensive re-excavation.

SCP-4218.name: The Cipher Flock
SCP-4218.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4218 is not physically containable due to population size (estimated 40,000-65,000 individuals) and migratory range. Foundation front organization "Meadowline Ornithological Trust" maintains overt cover for continuous aerial and ground-based photographic monitoring of the flock across its migratory circuit. Footage is transmitted to the Cryptography Division at Site-19 for ongoing analysis.

Publication of any amateur or professional footage of SCP-4218 murmuration events that captures more than 90 continuous seconds of flock movement is to be suppressed or acquired through standard information control channels, as extended footage has proven sufficient in at least two cases for independent civilian analysts to begin approximating the encoding pattern described below.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4218 designates a flock of common starlings (Sturnus vulgaris) exhibiting standard murmuration behavior with one confirmed anomalous property: when aerial footage of a murmuration event is converted to a time-lapse bitmap and analyzed as a two-dimensional signal, the flock's shifting density produces a repeating sequence of discrete symbol-like patterns consistent with a substitution cipher of approximately 40 unique glyphs.

Cryptography Division has achieved partial decryption of recurring segments, which resolve to what is believed to be a numeric countdown, though the unit of measurement and the event the countdown refers to remain undetermined. The countdown value, cross-referenced across footage spanning eleven years of observation, has decreased consistently and without exception, at a rate suggesting completion within the next 40-70 years, depending on interpretation of an ambiguous recurring glyph believed to modify the count's temporal unit.

The flock's individual composition turns over completely within 3-4 years through normal mortality and recruitment of new fledglings, none of which are removed from the wild population or trained by Foundation or outside parties. No mechanism has been identified by which the encoded pattern is preserved across complete population turnover; standard starling murmuration behavior is understood to arise from simple local flocking rules with no capacity for information storage or transmission between generations.

ADDENDUM 4218-1: Following the Site-19 fire of 20██ (see Incident 4218-9, classification pending), archived footage indicates the countdown pattern's rate of decrease increased by a factor of approximately 1.4 for a period of eleven days before returning to its prior rate. No causal connection to the Site-19 fire has been established, and Cryptography Division notes that the correlation may be coincidental. The division's current recommendation is continued monitoring without intervention, as no proposed method of accelerating, halting, or otherwise interfering with the pattern has been assessed as safe to attempt.

ADDENDUM 4218-2: Comparative footage of eleven unrelated starling flocks migrating through the same region shows standard, non-encoding murmuration behavior in all cases, confirming that the anomalous property is specific to the SCP-4218 population rather than a species-wide characteristic. Cryptography Division has proposed, but not yet received approval for, a controlled test involving temporary relocation of a small subset of the flock, intended to determine whether the encoding behavior would travel with removed individuals or remain tied to the parent flock. The Ethics Committee has requested additional justification, citing the uncertain welfare impact of isolating individual starlings from an otherwise cohesive migratory group whose social structure is not well understood.

SCP-4219.name: The Classification Mold
SCP-4219.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The active SCP-4219 culture is maintained in a single 4m x 4m sealed agar terrarium at Site-19's Document Analysis Wing, fed on a rotating diet of nutrient-agar and decommissioned paper stock. Use of SCP-4219 for logistics or routing optimization tasks requires submission of the problem via approved physical documents only (no digital transcription) and must be logged with Document Analysis supervisory sign-off.

Documents bearing classification markings of Level 3 or higher are not to be placed within the terrarium under any circumstances. Following Incident 4219-2, all documents intended for SCP-4219 exposure are pre-screened by a second researcher unfamiliar with the document's content to confirm the absence of prohibited classification markings, as the primary researcher's awareness of a document's classification has been found insufficient to prevent submission errors.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4219 is a plasmodial slime mold, genus consistent with Physarum, exhibiting standard foraging behavior -- extending pseudopodial networks toward nutrient sources and retracting from unfavorable ones -- with one confirmed anomalous property. When presented with a field of paper documents arranged as nodes in a physical maze (used by Foundation logistics analysts to model supply routes, evacuation plans, and similar optimization problems), SCP-4219 reliably converges on near-optimal solution paths within 18-30 hours, consistent with published research on slime mold network optimization and not considered anomalous in itself.

The anomalous property is SCP-4219's behavior toward documents bearing Foundation classification markings above the level the mold's current handlers are cleared to access, or bearing redaction blocks. Presented with such documents, SCP-4219 pseudopodia approach to within approximately 2 cm and then retract sharply, a response visually and temporally consistent with a chemical repellent, despite no repellent substance being present and despite the classification marking being conveyed solely through printed ink pattern, font, and stamp -- information with no identified chemical or physical signature that a plasmodium lacking eyes, a nervous system, or any known sensory organ should be capable of detecting.

Control tests using documents with fabricated, meaningless "classification" stamps of similar visual density produced no retraction response, ruling out simple visual avoidance of dense ink markings. Tests using genuine classified documents with the classification stamp physically removed also produced no retraction response, even when researchers present in the room were aware of the document's true classification level, suggesting the response is not mediated by researcher behavior.

ADDENDUM 4219-1: SCP-4219 is presently approved for limited use solving Foundation logistics problems using specially prepared unclassified analogue documents. Document Analysis Wing has noted, without further comment, that the mold has not yet been presented with a genuinely unsolvable optimization problem, and has requested guidance on what its retraction behavior would indicate if it were. Cryptography and Document Analysis staff have jointly noted that the retraction response's consistency across handlers of differing clearance levels suggests SCP-4219 responds to a document's classification itself rather than to any individual researcher's awareness of it, though this hypothesis has not been formally tested.

SCP-4220.name: The Inherited Sting
SCP-4220.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Confirmed SCP-4220 specimens (currently 3, designated -1 through -3) are housed in individual saltwater tanks at Site-77's Marine Containment Wing under standard cnidarian husbandry protocols. All personnel administering feeding or maintenance must wear puncture-resistant gloves rated to at least 3mm nematocyst penetration depth; no exceptions are authorized regardless of research priority.

Any envenomation event, accidental or authorized, requires the affected individual to be placed under 72-hour observation and debriefed by a staff psychologist cleared for SCP-4220 exposure protocol. Debriefing transcripts are cross-referenced against Foundation personnel and incident records to attempt identification of transmitted memory content; positive identifications are forwarded to the Department of Temporal Anomalies for review (see Addendum 4220-2).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4220 is a small coastal jellyfish species, bell diameter 3-5 cm, morphologically consistent with the class Cubozoa. Its sting is not lethal and produces localized pain consistent with known cubozoan envenomation. The anomalous property manifests in affected individuals within 10-40 minutes of envenomation, in the form of a brief, vivid, and fully sensory intrusive memory experience -- sight, sound, and proprioception included -- that is not drawn from the subject's own life.

Debriefing of 61 documented envenomation cases has established that the transmitted memory is, in the overwhelming majority of cases, traceable to a memory that would have belonged to whatever organism the same individual jellyfish most recently stung prior to the current subject. In cases where the specimen's prior sting target could be identified and interviewed, the transmitted memory has in several instances matched, in exact sensory detail, a memory the prior victim confirms as genuinely their own. This has held true across a documented chain of up to six sequential victims for a single specimen, with memory content passing backward through the chain (i.e., subject 6 receives a memory belonging to subject 5, who received a memory belonging to subject 4, and so on) rather than forward.

SCP-4220 specimens have a natural lifespan believed not to exceed 14 months. In nine documented cases, transmitted memories have been identified as belonging to individuals with no discoverable connection to any known prior sting victim, and in three cases, to individuals whose identifying details (names, locations, technology visible in the memory) do not correspond to any period within the specimen's lifespan, nor to any period prior to it consistent with a plausible originating chain.

ADDENDUM 4220-1: Subject D-8112, stung by SCP-4220-2, reported a transmitted memory of standing in a room not yet constructed at any Foundation site, viewed from what the subject described as "eye level for someone I've never been," reading a document whose visible letterhead did not match any current or historical Foundation department designation. D-8112 was unable to recall further detail under subsequent questioning.

ADDENDUM 4220-2: The Department of Temporal Anomalies has requested continued monitoring but has not yet issued a formal position on whether SCP-4220's memory chain extends only backward through past victims or, in some unconfirmed cases, forward.

SCP-4221.name: The Anniversary Wasp
SCP-4221.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: No reliable method presently exists to detect SCP-4221 larvae within a living host prior to emergence; standard imaging (MRI, CT, ultrasound) has consistently failed to locate larvae in confirmed cases. Containment therefore focuses on post-emergence capture and case tracking. Foundation-affiliated veterinary and medical personnel in regions with confirmed SCP-4221 activity are briefed to report mammalian patients presenting with a single, painless subdermal emergence wound occurring on a calendar date the patient or their family identifies as personally significant.

All identified adult specimens are to be captured alive where possible and transferred to Site-42 for containment in individual sealed enclosures. Euthanasia of captured specimens is not authorized pending further research into whether specimen death affects previously affected hosts.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4221 is a parasitoid wasp species, family consistent with Ichneumonidae, whose females oviposit into living mammalian hosts via a mechanism not yet observed directly -- no oviposition event has been witnessed despite continuous monitoring of eleven confirmed host animals, and eggs are found already present upon first detectable trace. Confirmed hosts include domestic and wild canids, felids, and in four documented cases, human subjects, though the Foundation notes human cases are addressed under separate ethical review and are not detailed further in this document.

Following oviposition, SCP-4221 larvae remain dormant and undetectable by standard means for a gestation period of approximately seven years. During this period, the host exhibits no physical symptoms. Psychological assessment of affected hosts capable of self-report (human cases) has established that over the gestation period, the host progressively and permanently loses detailed episodic memory of a single specific recurring date -- invariably a date of prior personal significance, such as the anniversary of a loss -- in a pattern the host cannot initially perceive is occurring, described by one subject as "the day getting quieter each year, like it was always going to end up being nothing."

By the end of the gestation period, the host retains no specific memory content associated with the date, though awareness that the date once held significance is sometimes, inconsistently, preserved. Larvae emerge painlessly through a small subdermal wound precisely on the anniversary date in question, in every confirmed case, and disperse without further host interaction. The host survives emergence without further known effect.

No mechanism has been proposed by which a non-sapient insect species could identify which calendar date holds subjective, rather than objective or biologically cyclical, significance to a given host, nor how this determination is made at the moment of oviposition, seven years prior to emergence.

ADDENDUM 4221-1: Object class is maintained at Keter due to the combination of an undetectable dormant stage, an uncontained wild population of unknown size, and the specific selection criteria described above, which suggest a sensory or predictive capability inconsistent with the species' observed neurological simplicity. The Ethics Committee has denied three consecutive requests to test whether host selection can be induced or redirected experimentally.

SCP-4222.name: The Unread Louse
SCP-4222.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The active SCP-4222 population is contained within a single climate-controlled archive room at Site-19 ("the Reading Room"), stocked exclusively with decommissioned, non-critical print materials rotated in on a monthly basis by Document Analysis staff. Population size is to be estimated quarterly by circulation-rate sampling of the room's stock rather than direct insect count, as SCP-4222 specimens are near-microscopic and direct census has proven unreliable.

No document of active research, historical, or evidentiary value is to be stored within three rooms of the Reading Room. Librarians and archivists Foundation-wide are briefed, without being informed of SCP-4222's existence, to report any pattern of a specific catalogued item becoming persistently difficult for patrons or staff to locate, recall, or successfully retrieve despite correct shelving and catalog entries; such reports are investigated for possible SCP-4222 contamination.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4222 is an insect species of the order Psocoptera (booklice), physically unremarkable and virtually indistinguishable from mundane booklice under standard entomological examination. SCP-4222 does not consume paper, binding glue, mold, or any material substrate in the manner of ordinary booklice; specimens have been maintained for over four years without measurable loss of body mass despite apparent total abstention from conventional feeding.

The confirmed anomalous property of SCP-4222 is a measurable reduction in the statistical likelihood that any book or document infested by the species will be selected, noticed, recalled, or successfully located by a human being, in proportion to infestation duration and (to a lesser extent) population density. This effect does not operate through memory alteration -- individuals who have previously read an infested volume retain full memory of having done so -- but through a persistent reduction in the probability of future selection, noticing, or successful retrieval. Library patrons browsing shelves containing infested volumes consistently report their eyes "sliding past" the specific titles in question; catalog and database searches for infested items return results at statistically depressed rates inconsistent with search algorithm behavior on uninfested control items; and staff attempting deliberate retrieval report that items are "never quite where the catalog says," despite physical verification confirming correct shelving.

Circulation records for the eleven longest-documented SCP-4222 infestations (average infestation period 6.2 years) show a mean 94% reduction in patron access events, with three items showing zero recorded access despite continuous physical presence and correct cataloging throughout the observation period.

ADDENDUM 4222-1: Document Analysis maintains the Reading Room's SCP-4222 population specifically to "feed" the species a controlled supply of decommissioned materials, reducing pressure on the wild population (believed to persist in at least four major public library systems) to infest documents of genuine value. This arrangement is understood by senior staff to constitute passive, ongoing containment rather than a permanent solution, and its long-term viability if the wild population's infestation targeting proves non-random has not been assessed.

ADDENDUM 4222-2: A 20██ internal review raised the question of whether SCP-4222 could be deliberately introduced to suppress patron access to a specific document without formal redaction or removal. The review was closed without a recommendation. No further action has been taken on this question as of the current revision of this file.

SCP-4223.name: The Mirror Algae
SCP-4223.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4223 blooms are not individually containable due to unpredictable onset and short duration (mean 68 hours). Seven bodies of still or slow-moving freshwater with a documented history of recurring SCP-4223 activity ("bloom sites") are fitted with continuous camera monitoring and water sampling equipment. Civilian access to bloom sites is restricted through standard cover measures (posted contamination or algae-bloom warnings, which are not entirely fabricated, as SCP-4223 blooms do coincide with genuine minor water-quality changes).

Any civilian who reports having observed a reflection inconsistent with the current surrounding landscape at a bloom site is to be interviewed by Foundation personnel posing as environmental health officials and administered a standard Class A amnestic if the report includes specific, checkable detail. Personnel assigned to bloom-site monitoring are limited to 30 minutes of direct visual observation of an active bloom's reflective surface per 24-hour period.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4223 is a photosynthetic algal species producing a dense surface bloom with a distinctive silver-grey, mirror-like sheen, occurring unpredictably on still or slow-moving freshwater bodies at the seven confirmed sites, with isolated unconfirmed reports from other locations. Blooms persist for 40-96 hours before dispersing without observable residue and without the reduction in dissolved oxygen typically associated with algal bloom die-off.

During an active bloom, the water's surface produces a reflection of the surrounding landscape that is visually coherent and behaves according to normal optical principles (it responds correctly to the position and movement of observers and light sources) but depicts the landscape as it existed or will exist at a point in time other than the present. Displacement has been documented as far back as 40 years and, in three site-verified cases, forward by as much as 11 years, confirmed retrospectively when the reflected features (a since-constructed building; a since-removed structure appearing prior to its actual removal) later matched reality.

The mechanism by which a given bloom selects a temporal displacement, or its direction and magnitude, has not been determined, and no bloom has been successfully triggered under controlled conditions; all documented blooms have occurred spontaneously.

ADDENDUM 4223-1: Subjects who observe a bloom reflection for extended periods report mild disorientation and, in four cases, temporary difficulty distinguishing the reflected landscape from the actual one upon looking away. Subject accounts are otherwise unremarkable with one exception.

ADDENDUM 4223-2: In 20██, civilian witness ██████████ reported observing, in a bloom reflection at Site 4223-C, a figure she identified as her father, deceased three years prior to the observation, standing at the reflected shoreline in a position corresponding to no known photograph. The witness entered the water and attempted to reach the reflected figure before being restrained by a companion. The bloom dispersed nine minutes later, within its normal duration range. Foundation review of the incident could not determine whether the reflected figure represented a genuine temporal displacement of a real past moment, given no verifiable record of the man at that shoreline exists, or a phenomenon SCP-4223 has not previously exhibited. The witness was administered a Class A amnestic. This case remains the only documented instance of an SCP-4223 reflection depicting a deceased individual.

SCP-4224.name: The Ledger Bees
SCP-4224.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The SCP-4224 apiary (currently four hives, designated Hive-1 through Hive-4) is maintained at Site-64's Biological Applications Wing under conditions matching wild Apis mellifera husbandry, with the addition of continuous vibrational and acoustic monitoring of comb activity. Hive access for honey extraction is limited to trained Foundation apiarists and is scheduled to minimize colony disturbance; unscheduled or emergency extraction requires Level 3 authorization.

Given the species' demonstrated sensitivity to colony stress (see below), any hive exhibiting elevated defensive behavior, comb abandonment, or swarming precursor activity is to be immediately isolated from other hives and from all ongoing anomaly-suppression operations pending review, per Protocol 4224-Calm.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4224 is a honeybee species, morphologically near-identical to Apis mellifera, distinguished by comb architecture and a resulting anomalous property in its honey. SCP-4224 comb cells, while visually standard hexagonal construction, have been shown through controlled testing to produce a measurable, localized dampening effect on minor probabilistic and low-magnitude anomalous fluctuations within approximately 2 meters of an active, undisturbed hive -- a property understood to arise from the comb's precise geometric regularity rather than any biological or chemical agent, though the mechanism remains unconfirmed.

Honey produced by SCP-4224 colonies retains a reduced but measurable version of this dampening property when consumed by humans under controlled dosage (established safe range: 5-15 grams per administration, no more than three administrations per 24-hour period), producing a temporary (4-7 hour) suppression of susceptibility to minor reality-bending, probability-manipulation, and low-tier cognitohazardous effects in the subject. This property has been adopted for limited operational use, primarily to protect Foundation personnel during transport or short-duration containment procedures involving Safe- and Euclid-class anomalies with probabilistic or minor cognitive components.

SCP-4224 honey has no confirmed effect on Keter-class or high-magnitude anomalies and is not authorized for use as a substitute for standard containment measures.

ADDENDUM 4224-1: Colony stress -- induced by overharvesting, relocation, or exposure to active anomalies exceeding the dampening threshold -- has been observed in six documented cases to invert the effect, with the affected hive's honey instead measurably amplifying nearby anomalous activity for a period of 24-72 hours following the stress event. This risk is the basis of Protocol 4224-Calm and is considered the primary operational hazard associated with SCP-4224.

ADDENDUM 4224-2: Site-64 apiary staff have noted, across four years of records, that each hive's honey yield corresponds almost exactly to current Foundation operational demand for the substance, with surplus honey (beyond scheduled extraction needs) never observed and shortfalls occurring only during documented colony stress events. Requests to investigate how hive productivity appears to track a demand figure the colony has no conventional means of accessing have been filed three times and closed each time as "insufficiently resourced to pursue," per Site-64 administration.

SCP-4225.name: The Unfelt Wound
SCP-4225.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4225 is housed in a standard personnel-grade quarters at Site-19, functionally unrestrained, as containment protocols pertain less to SCP-4225 himself than to the anomaly's unpredictable secondary subjects. SCP-4225 wears a wrist-mounted biometric monitor at all times recording heart rate, cortisol levels, and dermal galvanic response. Any spike consistent with traumatic injury, absent a corresponding wound on SCP-4225's body, is logged and cross-referenced against Foundation-monitored hospital admission and mortuary intake records within a 40 km radius for the following 96 hours.

Personnel assigned to SCP-4225 are rotated on a strict six-month cycle and are prohibited from disclosing his location, occupation title, or physical description to any individual outside Foundation personnel, following Incident 4225-3 (see Addendum). SCP-4225 has standing approval for supervised recreational activities but is barred from any activity carrying elevated risk of injury (contact sports, food preparation involving blades, unsupervised use of power tools).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4225 is a 44-year-old Caucasian male, formerly a structural engineer, who does not experience physical pain, regardless of the severity of injury sustained to his body. Lacerations, burns, and in one documented case a compound fracture of the tibia have produced no subjective pain response, verified under clinical interview and corroborated by direct neurological monitoring; SCP-4225's nociceptors function normally and transmit signal, but the signal does not appear to resolve into a conscious sensation for him.

Instead, at the moment SCP-4225 sustains an injury of sufficient severity (Foundation's working threshold is approximately equivalent to a Wong-Baker pain score of 4 or greater), a person elsewhere — selection criteria unknown, subject has ranged in age from 6 to 81 and shows no consistent relationship to SCP-4225 by geography, occupation, or any tested variable — experiences the full subjective pain of SCP-4225's injury without any corresponding physical damage to their own body. These individuals report the pain as immediate, precisely localized to match SCP-4225's wound, and lasting for the same duration as SCP-4225's injury would ordinarily take to become bearable. Several recipients have sought emergency medical treatment for pain with no discoverable cause; medical records for at least eleven such cases have been quietly acquired by the Foundation.

SCP-4225 was capable of injuring himself severely and often before Foundation intervention, reporting that the absence of pain made him "careless in a way I didn't notice until people started asking questions." He has since stated, in interview, that he finds the arrangement "worse than pain would be," and has requested information on the identities of the people who suffer in his place. This request has been denied.

ADDENDUM 4225-1: Incident 4225-3 occurred when a junior researcher, in violation of protocol, informed SCP-4225's assigned physical therapist of the general nature of his condition. The therapist subsequently allowed a training exercise involving controlled resistance that produced a minor sprain in SCP-4225. The recipient in this instance was later identified, through hospital admission cross-referencing, as a nine-year-old child in a burn ward in a different city, who reported sudden, severe ankle pain with no corresponding injury, delaying his own treatment by several hours. The therapist involved was reassigned. SCP-4225 was not informed of the child's condition.

SCP-4226.name: The Persistent Witness
SCP-4226.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4226 resides in an unmarked apartment in Site-19's adjoining township under the cover identity of a freelance insurance adjuster, a profession chosen because it does not raise suspicion when he is asked, repeatedly, to give statements to authorities. SCP-4226 is fitted with a GPS-tracked mobile device at all times. Foundation personnel monitor regional police, fire, and emergency dispatch frequencies within a 50 km radius of SCP-4226's tracked location; when an incident is logged, an embedded agent confirms whether SCP-4226 is listed among the witnesses interviewed at the scene, despite GPS data placing him elsewhere at the time of the incident.

Local law enforcement contacts who have interviewed the scene-duplicate of SCP-4226 are to be issued standard amnesticization following file review, and case paperwork bearing his witness statement is to be acquired and archived by Foundation liaisons embedded in regional records departments. SCP-4226 himself is not to be informed of specific incidents unless required for interview purposes.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4226 is a 51-year-old male who, whenever an unplanned event resulting in injury, death, or significant property damage occurs within approximately 50 km of his tracked physical location, additionally and simultaneously appears at the scene of that event as a bystander witness. This secondary instance of SCP-4226 is, by all available evidence — fingerprints, testimony from unaffiliated witnesses, photographic and video documentation — physically identical to and continuous with the primary SCP-4226, and gives coherent, consistent, first-person witness statements to responding authorities. The primary SCP-4226, meanwhile, retains no memory of the event and can typically be confirmed, via independent corroboration, to have been engaged in an unrelated activity elsewhere at the same time.

The secondary instance does not appear to be capable of preventing, causing, or otherwise materially affecting the incident it witnesses; it has never been observed to render aid, and departs the scene within minutes of giving its statement, at which point Foundation tracking of the primary SCP-4226 shows no corresponding anomaly. Attempts to physically detain the secondary instance have twice succeeded; in both cases, the detained instance behaved, spoke, and responded to medical examination as an entirely ordinary human being, expressing calm confusion at being restrained, before ceasing to exist — without physical trace — at a point between eleven and forty minutes after the primary SCP-4226 was independently confirmed to be occupied elsewhere.

SCP-4226 has been informed, in general terms, that he possesses an anomalous property and has consented to Foundation monitoring in exchange for housing and compensation. He has stated that he does not wish to know what he has witnessed. Foundation policy currently honors this request except where operational necessity requires disclosure.

ADDENDUM 4226-1: Of the 63 documented incidents involving SCP-4226's secondary instance to date, in four cases the "witness statement" given at the scene contained information about the incident's cause that was not independently verifiable by any other witness and was later confirmed accurate by forensic investigation conducted after the statement was recorded. The implications of this — that the secondary instance may, in some unconfirmed manner, know more about these incidents than a bystander plausibly could — remain uninvestigated pending O5 clearance for expanded interview protocol.

SCP-4227.name: Inherited Promises
SCP-4227.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4227 is housed in a Standard Humanoid Containment Cell at Site-19 with medical-grade monitoring. All blood draws, transfusions, or other exchanges of bodily fluid involving SCP-4227 require Level 3 authorization and must be logged in the SCP-4227 Obligation Ledger (see below). SCP-4227's blood is not to be used in any Foundation medical procedure except under controlled experimental conditions approved by the assigned researcher.

Any individual who has received a transfusion, graft, or other transfer of SCP-4227's blood or tissue ("recipient") is to be identified where possible and placed under quiet, non-intrusive monitoring for a period of no less than five years, as inherited obligations have in documented cases activated years after transfer.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4227 is a 37-year-old male, blood type O-negative, formerly a registered blood donor of above-average frequency (approx. 40 documented donations over 11 years prior to Foundation acquisition). Any individual who receives a sufficient quantity of SCP-4227's blood via transfusion, or in two documented cases via open-wound contact, subsequently becomes bound to fulfill one unresolved promise, debt, or stated obligation that was, at the time of transfer, outstanding in SCP-4227's own life — regardless of whether the recipient has any knowledge of SCP-4227, the obligation in question, or the party to whom it is owed.

Affected individuals report a sudden, specific, and unshakeable compulsion to complete a particular task: repaying a named sum to a named person, fulfilling a promise made in specific language, or otherwise discharging a debt of conscience. Compulsions have included a recipient traveling unprompted to a town she had never visited to repay a loan SCP-4227 had taken from a now-deceased acquaintance's estate, and a recipient who, with no prior knowledge of carpentry, spent four months building a piece of furniture SCP-4227 had once promised to make for his estranged sister. In each documented case, once the obligation was discharged, the recipient reported the compulsion lifting immediately and could not clearly explain, in retrospect, why they had felt driven to complete it.

SCP-4227 reports no memory of forming most of the obligations later discharged by recipients on his behalf and has expressed distress that his blood appears to "empty him of things I owed people, into people who never met them." He has requested that his donations cease. Ethics Committee review of this request is ongoing as of this writing.

ADDENDUM 4227-1: Foundation acquisition of SCP-4227 followed the identification of Recipient-3, who fulfilled an obligation traced to a debt SCP-4227 owed a man who had, by that point, been deceased for six years. Recipient-3's compulsion specified repayment be left at a grave rather than delivered to any living party, which she did without prior knowledge of the deceased's burial location. This suggests the anomaly transfers not merely SCP-4227's outstanding obligations, but some more precise record of how, specifically, he intended or was required to resolve them — a record SCP-4227 himself does not consciously possess.

SCP-4228.name: The Deciding Pulse
SCP-4228.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4228 is housed in a reinforced medical containment suite at Site-45 equipped with continuous cardiac and EEG monitoring. Given the entity's demonstrated effect on collective decision-making within its vicinity, no more than three Foundation personnel are permitted in SCP-4228's presence at any time, and all personnel rotations, resource allocations, or procedural votes concerning SCP-4228's own containment must be decided by personnel who have had no direct physical proximity (within 20 meters) to SCP-4228 in the preceding 72 hours.

SCP-4228 is not to be present, in person or via live audio/video feed, during any Foundation meeting in which a vote, consensus decision, or unanimous agreement is to be reached, following Incident 4228-Delta.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4228 is a 29-year-old female possessing a verified second cardiac structure, approximately the size of a human fist, situated inferior to her natural heart and connected to it by tissue of undetermined type. This secondary organ ("the second heart") does not appear necessary to SCP-4228's survival and exhibits an independent rhythm unsynchronized with her natural heartbeat.

When SCP-4228 is present among a group of three or more people who are, knowingly or not, approaching a shared decision — a vote, a consensus, an informal agreement on where to eat — the second heart's rhythm measurably changes in the moments before the group reaches that decision, in a manner that Foundation researchers have learned to read with 94% predictive accuracy as to the decision's eventual outcome, typically between 40 seconds and 6 minutes in advance. The second heart does not predict decisions made by SCP-4228 alone, nor decisions made by groups from which she is physically or electronically absent.

More concerning is evidence that the organ's rhythm does not merely predict but, in a minority of documented cases, appears to narrow the outcome: groups observed by researchers monitoring the second heart in real time have, on four occasions, reached a decision that directly matched an early, faint signal from the organ, even when initial verbal discussion trended toward a different outcome — as though the group's eventual choice were drawn toward what the heart had already, in some sense, decided. SCP-4228 herself reports no awareness of the organ's activity and cannot perceive or influence its rhythm.

ADDENDUM 4228-1: Incident 4228-Delta occurred during a Site-45 resource allocation meeting in which SCP-4228 was present as a monitored subject rather than a participant. Minutes before a 7-person committee vote on an unrelated matter, her second heart's rhythm sharply matched the eventual, unanimous vote outcome — a result three attending researchers described afterward as "the wrong kind of unanimous," noting that at least two committee members had entered the meeting with stated opposing positions and could not, under later interview, explain why they had changed their votes. SCP-4228 was not consulted on and did not attend the vote in question in any capacity beyond passive physical presence. She has since been excluded from all decision-adjacent proceedings.

SCP-4229.name: Two Birthdates
SCP-4229.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4229 resides in assigned housing at Site-19 under standard Safe-class monitoring. Exactly one (1) verification of SCP-4229's legal age is to be conducted by Foundation records personnel per calendar month, using only one of the two identity documents held in his file (Document A, dated 1974, or Document B, dated 2014) as determined by a randomization protocol maintained by the Site Director. Under no circumstances are both documents to be checked, referenced, or cross-verified within the same 30-day period. Personnel who inadvertently view or verify both documents in the same period are to submit to immediate medical evaluation.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4229 is an adult male in apparent good health who is in possession of two complete, independently verifiable sets of identity documentation — birth certificate, early school records, childhood medical history, and correlating photographic evidence — establishing two separate and non-overlapping birth years exactly 40 years apart. Both documentary histories are internally consistent, supported by third-party records (hospital archives, school enrollment logs, family testimony from individuals who, in each case, recall raising him from infancy), and show no evidence of forgery under Foundation forensic document analysis.

SCP-4229's physical age — as measured by bone density, cellular telomere length, and other standard biological age indicators — corresponds at any given time to whichever of his two documented birth years was most recently formally verified by an authority figure (a notary, a physician performing an age-relevant exam, a government official, or, as established through containment testing, Foundation records personnel performing scheduled verification). Following verification against the 1974 document, SCP-4229 physically presents as a man in his early fifties; following verification against the 2014 document, he presents, within approximately six hours, as a man in his early teens, with corresponding changes to musculature, bone structure, and dentition that have been documented via medical imaging but not otherwise medically explained.

SCP-4229 retains continuous memory across these transitions and reports subjective awareness of "which age" he currently is, though he cannot predict or control which will be selected next; he has described the sensation of transition as "someone else deciding how old I've been." He has requested that the Foundation cease all verification procedures. This request has been denied on the grounds that both of his official histories require periodic government-mandated renewal (driver's licensing, tax filings) that the Foundation currently performs on his behalf under cover identities, and that indefinitely avoiding verification carries unknown risk.

ADDENDUM 4229-1: A single incident of accidental dual verification occurred during Site transfer processing in 20██, when both documents were referenced within the same clerical session. SCP-4229 reportedly experienced both physical states in rapid alternation for approximately eleven minutes before stabilizing at the age matching the more recently referenced document. He described the interval as "the worst eleven minutes I can remember being," and has since declined to elaborate further.

SCP-4230.name: The Sleep-Told
SCP-4230.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4230 sleeps in a soundproofed, continuously recorded containment chamber at Site-19. Audio and video of every sleep cycle is reviewed by no fewer than two assigned linguists/transcriptionists within four hours of SCP-4230 waking, given that his verbal sleep-talk has, in prior instances, contained time-sensitive information. Findings assessed as referring to a specific, identifiable, and imminent event of consequence (death, disaster, disappearance) are to be escalated to the Site Director within one hour of identification for a determination on possible intervention, subject to Temporal/Precognitive Data Handling Protocol 12.

SCP-4230 himself retains no memory of his sleep-talk upon waking and is not to be informed of specific transcribed content unless his input is required to clarify ambiguous phrasing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4230 is a 38-year-old male who, during REM sleep cycles only, speaks aloud in a clear, unaccented voice distinct from his ordinary waking speech patterns, describing events in flat, present-tense narration. Approximately 30% of transcribed sleep-talk to date has been subsequently confirmed to describe real, specific, verifiable events occurring between 18 hours and 9 days after the sleep session in which they were spoken, with sufficient detail (names, locations, causes of death, exact phrasing later used by uninvolved third parties) to rule out coincidence under Foundation statistical review.

SCP-4230 has no waking access to this information.
