Interviews conducted immediately upon waking, before he can be exposed to transcripts, show no evidence he retains any impression, vague or otherwise, of what he described in his sleep. He has been informed only in general terms that he "talks in his sleep" and has consented to recording on this basis; the Foundation has elected not to disclose the predictive accuracy of this speech, citing psychological welfare concerns pending Ethics Committee review.

The content of SCP-4230's sleep-talk does not appear restricted to events involving himself, Foundation personnel, or any consistent category of subject; transcribed material has described, among other things, a factory fire in a country SCP-4230 has never visited, the specific wording of a stranger's obituary six days before that individual's recorded death, and — on three occasions — brief, unverifiable fragments describing events that have not yet been confirmed to have occurred, remaining open in the file pending future correlation.

ADDENDUM 4230-1: On 20██-██-██, SCP-4230's sleep-talk included a sentence transcriptionists flagged as referring, by name, to a currently active Foundation researcher not otherwise associated with SCP-4230's file, describing an injury the researcher would sustain "on the stairs, the ones they're told not to use." The named researcher was reassigned to ground-floor duties as a precaution. No incident has yet occurred. The researcher has not been informed of the reason for their reassignment.

SCP-4231.name: The Simultaneous Man
SCP-4231.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Both instances of SCP-4231 — designated SCP-4231-A (apparent age 24) and SCP-4231-B (apparent age 43) — are held in separate containment wings no less than 15 km apart at all times, following Foundation determination that reducing physical distance between instances produces adverse physiological effects in both (see Addendum). Each instance is to be housed under a distinct cover identity and is not to be informed, except where already independently discovered, of the other's existence.

Any medical procedure performed on one instance is to be immediately mirrored, in a controlled setting, by monitoring of the other instance's corresponding physiological readings, given documented cases of sympathetic response across distance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4231-A and SCP-4231-B are, per exhaustive genetic, dental, dermatoglyphic, and osteological analysis, the same individual — matching in all respects except apparent age — existing simultaneously as two distinct, independently conscious, and independently embodied people. This is distinguished from cases of shared or alternating consciousness in that both instances are, at all times, awake, aware, and mentally independent of one another; neither instance reports any perceptual access to the other's experiences, memories formed after a shared point of origin, or thoughts.

Both instances share identical memories up to a divergence point corresponding to SCP-4231-A's 24th birthday, after which their memories are entirely separate, reflecting 19 years of apparently lived, independent experience for SCP-4231-B and a comparatively brief period for SCP-4231-A, despite both instances having been first documented by the Foundation within the same eight-day window in 20██. Neither instance has an accepted explanation for the other's existence; SCP-4231-B, on first learning of SCP-4231-A, described the younger instance as "not a memory, not a photograph — him, right now, being twenty-four right now, while I'm not."

Distance testing has established that when the two instances are brought within approximately 8 km of one another, both begin to exhibit acute physiological distress: elevated heart rate, disorientation, and in one trial, a shared, simultaneous nosebleed occurring in both instances within four seconds of each other despite no physical contact. The mechanism producing or sustaining this duplication remains unidentified; Foundation temporal physicists have proposed the instances represent a single timeline "folded" such that two non-adjacent points along it are, locally, co-present, though this model does not explain why the fold has persisted for over two years of continuous observation without collapsing.

ADDENDUM 4231-1: SCP-4231-B has requested, on separate occasions, to meet SCP-4231-A "just once, from farther away than eight kilometers lets us." This request remains denied pending further research into the cause of the proximity effect, which Foundation medical staff have assessed carries unacceptable risk of severe injury or death to one or both instances.

SCP-4232.name: The Living Marginalia
SCP-4232.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4232 is housed at Site-19 in quarters adjacent to Secure Records Storage. The physical and digital file for [DATA EXPUNGED] ("the Bound File"), to which SCP-4232 is anomalously linked, is held in a segregated archive accessible only to personnel with both Level 4 clearance and specific authorization from the Site Director. Any amendment, redaction, correction, or addition to the Bound File must be approved through the SCP-4232 Editorial Review Board and is to be performed only with SCP-4232 under direct medical observation, given documented physiological effects of file edits on her body.

Personnel are reminded that SCP-4232 is not herself the subject of the Bound File and holds no clearance to read its contents in full.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4232 is a 33-year-old female Foundation archivist who, at a still-unexplained point during her employment, became physically and irreversibly linked to the case file of a separate, redacted anomalous entity. Any textual change made to the Bound File — a correction of a date, the addition of a new containment note, a reclassification of the entity's object class — produces a corresponding, immediate physical change in SCP-4232, ranging from minor (a scar appearing or fading in accordance with an edited incident description) to severe (temporary loss of a limb's sensation following a procedural amendment describing injury to the bound entity).

SCP-4232 has no access to and has never been permitted to read the Bound File in its entirety; her knowledge of its contents is limited to inference from the changes enacted upon her own body, which she has taken to recording in a personal log the Foundation permits her to keep. She has, through this method, independently reconstructed a partial and almost certainly inaccurate account of the entity to which she is bound, which she refers to, in her log, only as "the one I'm being written for."

Foundation Ethics Committee review has repeatedly raised the question of whether editorial changes to the Bound File should be restricted on the basis of their effect on SCP-4232, who is not the file's subject and has not consented to bearing its consequences; this question remains formally unresolved, and in practice, edits deemed operationally necessary to the Bound File's subject are made regardless of anticipated harm to SCP-4232, with her informed only after the fact.

ADDENDUM 4232-1: Following a containment procedure update to the Bound File in 20██ — details restricted above SCP-4232's clearance — SCP-4232 experienced a sustained, unexplained fever of 39.4°C for eleven days with no identifiable pathogen, concurrent with the bound entity's own file noting an unrelated "period of containment instability" of matching duration. SCP-4232 was not informed of this correlation. Her log entry for the period reads, in full: "Something is wrong with the one I'm being written for. I don't know what. I don't think I'm allowed to.

SCP-4233.name: The Quiet Name
SCP-4233.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4233 is to be referred to at all times, in speech and writing, exclusively by her Foundation designation or an approved alias. Personnel assigned to SCP-4233 are briefed on her given name only in written form and are drilled extensively to avoid vocalizing it under any circumstance, including reading aloud, singing, or foreign-language translation. SCP-4233 resides in standard housing at Site-19 with sound-monitoring equipment installed to detect and log any instance of anomalous ambient silence for correlation purposes.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4233 is a 26-year-old female whose given first name — withheld here and restricted to written form only in all Foundation documentation, per protocol above — produces a brief, absolute cessation of ambient sound within an approximate 500-meter radius of wherever it is spoken aloud, by any speaker, in any language, tone, or context, including recorded or synthesized speech. The silence lasts 1.3 seconds (± 0.2s across 71 recorded instances) and affects all sound indiscriminately: speech, machinery, recorded audio played through speakers, and, notably, sound already in transit, such that a bell struck a half-second before the name is spoken will cut off mid-tone.

The effect does not appear to require SCP-4233's presence, consciousness, or awareness; it has occurred when her name was spoken in her absence, including once by a researcher reading it silently aloud from a transcript without realizing the name in question was hers, and once, per an unconfirmed but internally consistent report, in a location where no Foundation record indicates SCP-4233 has ever been or has any connection.

SCP-4233 was unaware of the anomaly prior to Foundation contact; her name had, throughout her life, been avoided by teachers, employers, and family members who reported an unexplained, unconscious reluctance to say it, generally substituting nicknames without recalling deciding to do so. She has stated in interview that she finds this fact "more upsetting than the silence itself" — that people closest to her had, for her entire life, quietly declined to say her name, and that she had never noticed until it was explained to her.

ADDENDUM 4233-1: A controlled test in which the name was spoken simultaneously by fourteen speakers in fourteen separate soundproofed rooms across Site-19 produced fourteen simultaneous silences, confirming the effect is not radius-limited to a single point of origin in any conventional sense, but occurs, apparently, wherever and however often the name is spoken, with no attenuation. Further large-scale testing has been suspended pending review of unknown upper limits.

SCP-4234.name: The Unrecorded Face
SCP-4234.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4234 is housed at Site-19 under standard containment. All photography, filming, or artistic rendering of SCP-4234 is prohibited except for approved research purposes, and any resulting image is to be immediately reviewed and stored in the SCP-4234 Image Archive under Level 3 access restriction, owing to the disturbing nature of resulting images (see below). SCP-4234's identification badge and personnel file photo are to be replaced quarterly, as previous images degrade in administrative usefulness once personnel become accustomed to the depicted face and can no longer reliably match it to SCP-4234 in person.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4234 is a 46-year-old male whose likeness cannot be captured by any known method of image reproduction. Photographs, video recordings, and hand-drawn or painted portraits produced of SCP-4234, regardless of medium, equipment, or artist, depict not SCP-4234 but a consistent, specific individual who does not otherwise appear to exist: a man of approximately the same build and coloring as SCP-4234, but with distinct facial structure, estimated by consulted forensic artists to be in his early sixties. This substitute face, hereafter "the Composite," is stable across all known images of SCP-4234 taken over an 11-year Foundation observation period, down to consistent minor details (a scar above the left eyebrow, a specific dental gap) not present on SCP-4234 himself.

Extensive Foundation database searches, including comparison against missing persons records, unsolved case files, and populations of other contained anomalies, have failed to identify the Composite as a real or previously documented individual. No image of SCP-4234 taken prior to Foundation involvement — family photographs, a driver's license issued in 19██, a school yearbook — has been recovered showing his true, unaltered likeness in reproduction; all substitute the Composite retroactively, including photographs SCP-4234's own family confirms, from living memory, depicted him accurately at the time they were taken.

SCP-4234 states he has never seen the Composite's face in a mirror, a still-water reflection, or any other non-reproductive means of viewing himself, and that his own understanding of his appearance matches what Foundation personnel report seeing when looking directly at him. He has requested to see a photograph of the Composite exactly once, during intake processing; his reaction to the image is not recorded in his file beyond a note that the interview was suspended early "at subject's request, following visible distress," and the matter has not been revisited.

ADDENDUM 4234-1: A retired detective's cold case file, acquired during an unrelated Foundation records sweep in 20██, contained a composite sketch of an unidentified suspect in a decades-old missing-persons case. The sketch depicts a man matching the Composite's face in every measured particular. The case remains, as of this writing, unsolved. SCP-4234 has not been informed of this file's existence.

SCP-4235.name: Still Water
SCP-4235.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4235 is housed in a dry containment suite at Site-19 with no standing water permitted within the chamber; all cleaning, bathing, and drinking water is to be provided exclusively via non-reflective, continuously agitated or opaque delivery systems. Personnel entering SCP-4235's presence are prohibited from carrying any container capable of holding still water (open cups, uncapped bottles) and are briefed to avoid natural still-water bodies (puddles, ponds) when escorting SCP-4235 outside containment, which requires Level 3 authorization and a minimum two-person supervision team.

Any instance of SCP-4235 approaching or being brought within viewing distance of still water is to be treated as a Class-2 containment breach pending immediate removal.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4235 is an apparently 9-year-old female of unconfirmed origin (see Addendum) whose proximity to any still, reflective body of water — a puddle, a pond, a filled sink, a glass left undisturbed — causes that water's surface to reflect not the viewer looking into it, but that viewer's own body, at a future point, drowned. The reflection shows the viewer's face and upper body as they will appear at the moment of drowning, including apparent age at time of death, visible injuries or lack thereof, and the immediate environment surrounding the body, though not, notably, any information identifying the location, date, or circumstance beyond what is visually inferable.

The reflection is visible only to the individual looking into the water at the time and cannot be photographed, recorded, or independently verified by a second observer looking into the same water simultaneously, who instead sees their own future drowning reflected in turn. SCP-4235 herself reports seeing, in her own reflection, "an old woman, older than anyone I've met," which — given her apparent age has not changed across eleven years of Foundation observation — remains uninvestigated as to whether it constitutes evidence of eventual, extended survival or a separate anomalous property.

Of 34 documented cases of Foundation-authorized viewing under controlled conditions, no viewer has yet died by drowning; four viewers have since developed severe aquaphobia and requested reassignment away from water-adjacent duties. Whether the reflected death is fixed, probabilistic, or contingent on future circumstance remains an open research question, complicated by the Foundation's inability to ethically test the question by exposing viewers to controlled drowning risk.

SCP-4235 was recovered from a flooded residential basement in 20██ with no accompanying adults and no records establishing her identity prior to that date; all attempts to trace her origin through missing-persons databases, DNA familial matching, and regional records have failed.

ADDENDUM 4235-1: SCP-4235 has asked Foundation caretakers, on multiple documented occasions, whether she can "see someone who already died," a question that has not been answered and that she has, per caretaker notes, stopped asking as of approximately eight months ago.

SCP-4236.name: The Blind Spot
SCP-4236.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4236 is designated a Thaumiel-class asset and is housed under voluntary containment at Site-87 with clearance commensurate with active field deployment. SCP-4236 is deployed exclusively under direct authorization of the Site-87 Director or higher for operations involving confirmed or suspected telepathic, empathic, or other mind-affecting hostile entities, per Deployment Protocol 4236. SCP-4236 is not to be deployed against non-hostile telepathic entities or used for unauthorized surveillance of Foundation personnel, a restriction added following Incident 4236-1 (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4236 is a 34-year-old male, formerly a Foundation security contractor, who is entirely undetectable by any known telepathic, empathic, or other consciousness-scanning method employed by a specific, consistent class of anomalous entities exhibiting mind-affecting properties (hereafter "Class-T entities"). Class-T entities capable of perceiving, reading, or influencing the thoughts of every other tested human subject, including trained Foundation telepaths and other anomalous humanoids with confirmed resistance to lesser mental intrusion, register SCP-4236, when in their perceptual range, as simply absent — not shielded, not resistant, but not present at all, a gap in their perception that several tested entities have described, when questioned, as "not even a hole, because a hole is still there."

This property does not extend to conventional (non-anomalous) detection; SCP-4236 is visible, audible, and physically present by any ordinary means, and Class-T entities that rely on both anomalous and conventional senses have, in limited testing, shown confusion consistent with sensory contradiction rather than complete failure to detect him. The mechanism remains unidentified; SCP-4236 has undergone extensive neurological and metaphysical screening with no anomalous property identified within him that would independently account for the effect, leading current research to treat his condition as defined entirely in relation to Class-T entities rather than as an intrinsic property of SCP-4236 himself.

SCP-4236 has been deployed successfully in eleven documented Foundation operations to date, functioning as an unperceivable presence during negotiations, extractions, and reconnaissance against Class-T threats, and has voluntarily continued this role under standard Foundation employment contract, compensation, and psychological support. He has, in interview, described the work as "the only thing I've found I'm specifically good for," and has not requested reassignment.

ADDENDUM 4236-1: Incident 4236-1 involved SCP-4236's unauthorized use, by a since-reprimanded field supervisor, to observe a meeting of Foundation personnel suspected of policy violations, under the reasoning that his undetectability would extend usefully to human targets. It did not: the personnel in question perceived SCP-4236 normally throughout, and the incident was resolved as a straightforward, non-anomalous breach of interpersonal privacy rather than a demonstration of any broader surveillance capability. The supervisor's proposal was denied on both procedural and ethical grounds, and Deployment Protocol 4236 was amended accordingly.

SCP-4237.name: Washer Six
SCP-4237.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Foundation acquired the building at [address], operating under a shell company as "Sudsy Suds Laundromat" cover. Public access is maintained during limited hours (10:00-16:00, Tue/Thu), staffed by two embedded agents posing as attendant and customer. All machines except Washers 1-5 and Dryers 1-4 are non-functional replicas; SCP-4237 effects are isolated to Washer 6. Visitors are permitted to use Washer 6 only under Foundation observation; civilian use is discouraged via a hand-written "Out of Order" sign, though this has not reliably prevented incidents (see Incident Log). Any item retrieved from Washer 6 that does not match the item deposited is to be photographed, cataloged, and stored in the Site-77 Low-Risk Anomalous Object Archive without attempting to trace or return it to its apparent original owner. Personnel are forbidden from placing personal items in Washer 6 for any reason, including verification testing, without O5 clearance.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4237 refers to a coin-operated clothes washing machine ("Washer 6") in a laundromat in [town], first identified in [date] following three independent missing-persons-adjacent complaints filed with local police, later closed as "clerical confusion." When a load of laundry is placed in Washer 6, the machine's normal wash cycle (approximately 34 minutes) proceeds without incident. Upon opening the machine at the end of the cycle, the items retrieved are, in 61% of observed cycles, not the items that were deposited.

Returned items are always clean, damp, and of a size and type broadly consistent with the original load (e.g., a load of men's clothing returns other men's clothing), but bear no relation to the depositor's ownership: brand, size, wear pattern, and any identifying marks (nametags, embroidery, stains) differ. Concurrently, Foundation-embedded observation of other machines in the same building, and in at least four other unaffiliated laundromats within a 40-kilometer radius, has recorded the simultaneous, unexplained appearance of the depositor's original items inside an unrelated washing machine mid-cycle, retrievable by whoever opens that machine next.

No consistent rule governs which laundromat receives a given depositor's items; the exchange appears bidirectional and non-reciprocal, meaning a given depositor's items may be received by a stranger who never used Washer 6, and that stranger's own items may go to a third, uninvolved machine. Foundation modeling has failed to identify a distance, time, or population variable that predicts the destination. Of 214 tracked exchanges, only two have been traced to a specific recipient, both through coincidental Foundation presence; the fate of the remaining 212 original items, and their new owners, is unknown.

Civilians who lose items to SCP-4237 typically report mild frustration rather than alarm, and rarely pursue the matter once refunded or given store credit by Foundation-embedded staff. No injury, illness, or lasting psychological effect has been linked to receiving a stranger's laundry. This has not prevented the Foundation from noting that several recovered items, when returned to circulation as evidence in unrelated closed investigations, were later identified as belonging to individuals who had been reported missing prior to SCP-4237's discovery.

ADDENDUM 4237-1: On [date], Agent ██████ deposited a control load of five marked towels in Washer 6 under authorized testing conditions. The cycle completed normally; the machine was opened to find it empty. No corresponding appearance of the towels has been recorded in any monitored machine in the eleven months since. The three items retrieved in place of the towels — a child's mitten, a hospital gown, and a single black glove — were never claimed.

SCP-4238.name: The Early Lookout
SCP-4238.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The tower and surrounding 2 km exclusion perimeter within [National Forest] are held under a permanent "structural hazard, no entry" designation by a cooperating forestry agency. A Foundation two-person rotation staffs the tower under the cover of routine fire-watch duty, replaced every 96 hours regardless of observed anomalous activity, per Protocol 4238-Rest. Personnel are prohibited from looking through the tower's north-facing window for longer than the duration of a single unbroken breath. Any smoke plume observed through SCP-4238's windows is to be logged with compass bearing, estimated distance, and apparent time-of-day lighting, then relayed to Site-19 for cross-check against regional fire dispatch logs; confirmed matches are not to be reported to civilian fire services except through the Foundation's standing arrangement with [Agency], which treats such reports as originating from a contracted early-detection sensor network.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4238 is a fire lookout tower constructed in [year] and decommissioned by its original owning agency in [year] following unresolved discrepancies in ranger incident reports. The tower's four windows, one per cardinal direction, present views of the surrounding forest that do not consistently correspond to the tower's present external conditions.

Through the north-facing window, observers report seeing the forest under lighting, weather, and seasonal conditions inconsistent with the exterior at time of observation, most often (approximately 70% of instances) later in the same day. Smoke plumes visible through this window have, in 44 of 51 documented instances, preceded an actual, verifiable fire at the indicated bearing by an interval ranging from eleven minutes to nine days. The remaining seven instances correspond to no fire on record, though Foundation investigation of two of these sites found burn scarring consistent with an extinguished fire of unknown origin and undocumented date.

The other three windows (east, south, west) show comparatively minor and unpredictable temporal offsets, typically under four hours, and have not been linked to any predictive value. Objects passed through any window frame — the panes do not open, but a gap of approximately six centimeters exists where deteriorated caulking has separated frame from glass — return altered in a manner consistent with the elapsed subjective time on the other side: a slip of paper left wedged in the north window's gap for one observation shift (eight hours) was recovered showing nine days of accumulated dust and UV fading.

The tower's interior clock, a wind-up model original to the structure, has never been observed to require rewinding. Personnel report that extended observation through the north window (beyond roughly four seconds) produces a mild but consistent disorientation lasting up to twenty minutes, characterized by subjects misjudging the tense of their own statements ("there is a fire" spoken with the confidence normally reserved for a completed event). No case of this effect persisting beyond thirty minutes has been recorded.

ADDENDUM 4238-1: Analysis of the seven non-predictive smoke sightings remains unresolved. Dr. ████████ has proposed that SCP-4238's north window may display fires from a forest that no longer exists in the tower's local timeline, rather than fires yet to occur in it — a hypothesis that would account for the burn scarring at two sites but not for the remaining five, at which no scarring, of any age, has been found despite repeated survey. The tower continues to be staffed. No fire originating from within the exclusion perimeter itself has yet been observed through any window.

SCP-4239.name: The Door Between Firms
SCP-4239.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4239 is contained within its original location, the ground-floor lobby of [Office Building], under Foundation ownership of the building via a shell holding company. The revolving door is to remain in operation during standard business hours to maintain cover as a functioning office lobby entrance; a secondary, non-anomalous entrance has been installed for the exclusive use of the building's three cover-identity tenant companies. Civilians and untrained personnel are barred from using SCP-4239 through discreet signage directing foot traffic to the secondary entrance. Any individual who completes four or more consecutive rotations of SCP-4239 without exiting is to be intercepted by lobby security (Foundation personnel) upon their eventual exit and administered Class A amnesticization if determined to be a non-Foundation civilian, following standard debrief to determine which building variant they exited into.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4239 is a four-panel revolving door serving as the primary ground-floor entrance to [Office Building]. Under standard use — a single rotation, entering and exiting within the same continuous motion — the door functions with no anomalous effect. The anomaly manifests when an individual completes two or more full rotations without exiting between them.

An individual completing a second consecutive rotation will exit into a lobby that is structurally identical to the building's true lobby but is tenanted by different, non-existent companies, staffed by personnel who do not recognize the exiting individual and who have no record of them in any building directory or employment system, despite otherwise behaving as ordinary office employees going about unremarkable workdays. Each additional consecutive rotation (documented up to a maximum of seven) produces a further, distinct variant lobby, each retaining the building's exact floor plan, elevator placement, and fire exit signage, but differing in tenant company names, employee rosters, wall art, and in six recorded cases, the view from the lobby windows, which has shown weather or lighting conditions inconsistent with the true building's exterior at time of entry.

Individuals who exit into a variant lobby are, without exception, able to leave the building normally through its other exits and return to consensus reality; the anomaly affects only the contents and apparent tenancy of the lobby itself, not the building's broader structure or the individual's ability to depart. No case has been recorded of a person failing to exit SCP-4239 into some lobby variant, consensus or otherwise. Individuals who have entered variant lobbies report that employees within address them by name — a name that is, in 80% of cases, not the entrant's actual name but one which the entrant, upon later reflection, describes as feeling "as correct" as their real one.

Foundation testing beyond seven rotations has been suspended following Incident 4239-3 (see below), pending review.

ADDENDUM 4239-1 (Incident 4239-3): During an authorized eighth-rotation test, Researcher Voss exited into a lobby matching all prior structural parameters but found the reception desk unstaffed and every interior light fixture on but producing no measurable illumination. Voss exited the building through the standard fire stair without further incident and has since been cleared by psychological evaluation, but has, on three separate occasions during unrelated Site duties, referred to colleagues by names matching no personnel roster. When asked, Voss reports no memory of doing so.

SCP-4240.name: Platform Zero
SCP-4240.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Foundation assets embedded within [City] Transit Authority maintain false maintenance records for the tunnel segment containing SCP-4240 to prevent civilian transit workers from receiving assignments there. Access to SCP-4240 is restricted to Foundation personnel holding Level 3 clearance or higher, entering only via the maintenance hatch at [designated station], and only in pairs equipped with tethered communication lines to surface monitoring. No individual is to remain on SCP-4240's platform for longer than eleven minutes; a rotating alarm system enforces recall. Under no circumstances is any Foundation personnel to board a train that arrives at SCP-4240. Six such trains have arrived during the containment period; each has been allowed to depart unboarded. Any civilian discovered on the platform is to be extracted immediately regardless of their stated willingness to remain, administered Class B amnesticization, and returned to the nearest functioning station.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4240 is a subway platform located within the [City] transit tunnel network at a position that does not correspond to any station, junction, or maintenance access point on official transit authority schematics, current or historical. The platform is accessible via a maintenance hatch discovered during Foundation-directed inspection of unrelated tunnel damage in [year]. The hatch itself does not appear on any blueprint of the tunnel section in which it is located.

The platform is tiled, lit, and signed in a style consistent with the transit system's construction period, bearing a station name plate reading only "———" in the system's standard font. No trains are scheduled to pass through this section according to any dispatch record, yet trains do arrive at SCP-4240, at intervals ranging from nine days to just under fourteen months, with no observed pattern. Each train has been of a rolling stock model consistent with the transit system's fleet, but bearing a route number not assigned to any current or former line. Interior lighting and apparent passenger occupancy are visible through the windows of arriving trains; passenger figures do not respond to tapping on the glass or any other stimulus from the platform side, and have, across all six recorded arrivals, shown no variation in posture or position between the train's arrival and departure, despite dwell times of up to four minutes.

Audio recording equipment left on the platform during unoccupied periods has, in 90% of retrieved recordings, captured a standard transit announcement chime followed by silence, with no corresponding train arrival logged by platform sensors during the silence's duration. The remaining 10% of recordings contain the chime followed by an announcement in a language not matched by Foundation linguistic analysis to any known human language, though certain phonemic patterns recur across separate recordings with sufficient consistency to suggest genuine grammatical structure rather than noise.

No Foundation personnel or civilian has been observed boarding a train at SCP-4240. The platform's classification as Keter reflects not an observed escalating threat but the Foundation's inability to determine what would happen if one did, combined with mounting circumstantial evidence — three missing-persons cases in [City] with last-known locations near the maintenance hatch's surface access point, none Foundation-connected — that someone eventually will, or already has.

ADDENDUM 4240-1: Voiceprint analysis of the untranslated announcement has been forwarded to the Department of Linguistic Anomalies. Preliminary review notes a structural similarity, described as "cadence rather than content," to recordings associated with SCP-████, itself under separate containment. Cross-referencing is ongoing.

SCP-4241.name: The Quarry That Answers First
SCP-4241.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The abandoned quarry designated SCP-4241, located [distance] from [town], is secured under cover of an active blasting-hazard closure order obtained through Foundation influence over the regional mining authority. A double perimeter fence with sound-dampening barriers has been installed at the quarry rim; the dampening is cosmetic and has no measurable effect on SCP-4241's phenomenon. Personnel entering the quarry floor for authorized testing are limited to a single vocalization per visit and must submit the specific word or phrase to be used in writing no less than one hour prior to entry, sealed and held by a second researcher who does not accompany them, to permit comparison against the resulting echo. Unauthorized or repeated vocalization by the same individual within a 24-hour period is prohibited.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4241 is a disused limestone quarry, approximately 80 meters at its deepest point, excavated between [year] and its closure in [year] following an unrecorded incident. Any vocalization made by a person standing at any point within the quarry's excavated basin produces an echo that is audible between 1.2 and 4.8 seconds before the vocalization occurs, rather than after, as would be consistent with normal acoustic reflection.

In approximately two-thirds of documented cases, the anticipatory echo is an accurate acoustic reproduction of the vocalization that follows it, differing only in its inverted temporal relationship. In the remaining third, the echo does not match: it may return a different word, a different voice, a full sentence where only a single word was later spoken, or, in nine recorded cases, a scream where the subsequent vocalization was unremarkable speech. In every documented instance of mismatch, subjects who proceeded to speak did so with the word or phrase they had pre-registered in writing, ruling out suggestion or memory contamination from having heard the echo first. The source of a mismatched echo — whose voice it is, and under what circumstance it might have been, or will be, produced — has not been identified in any case.

Physical objects dropped into the quarry do not exhibit any anomalous behavior; the effect is confined to vocalization and, in three recorded instances, to sustained non-verbal sound (a struck metal pipe, a car alarm, a sneeze), each of which produced a preceding echo as well. Instruments incapable of independent utterance — recorded audio played through a speaker at the quarry floor — do not reliably produce anticipatory echoes, succeeding in only 6 of 40 trials, suggesting the phenomenon may respond to some quality of the sound's origin beyond acoustic waveform alone, though the Foundation has not established what that quality is.

No echo, matched or mismatched, has ever failed to occur when a vocalization was made. No vocalization has been recorded as failing to occur after its echo, even when the speaker attempted, as part of testing, to withhold or alter their prepared statement at the last moment.

ADDENDUM 4241-1: On [date], during an unauthorized visit by two local teenagers (subsequently amnesticized), audio recovered from a phone left recording on the quarry floor captured an anticipatory echo of a full name and a date, spoken in a child's voice, approximately six seconds before one of the teenagers — unprompted, and by his own later account for no reason he could identify — spoke the same name and date aloud. The name matches no missing-persons record on file. The date given has not yet occurred.

SCP-4242.name: Screen Four
SCP-4242.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The Foundation acquired [Cinema Name] in its entirety in [year] following three unexplained disappearances linked to Screening Room 4. The theater continues limited public operation as cover, with Screen Four permanently marked "closed for renovation" and its door secured by a keycard lock restricted to Foundation personnel. Civilian ticket sales are not to be permitted for any showing scheduled in Screen Four; the room's projector is disconnected from the building's film distribution system and is not to be operated except during authorized testing. No individual is to enter Screen Four alone. Testing requires a minimum of two personnel, with the non-viewing member stationed at the open door with a direct line of sight to the viewing subject and standing instructions to physically remove the subject from the room at the twenty-minute mark regardless of the subject's stated objections.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4242 refers to Screening Room 4 of [Cinema Name], a 40-seat auditorium of standard construction for the building and period. The anomaly manifests only when a single individual occupies the room without any other person present; a room containing two or more people, or a lone individual accompanied by a second person standing in the doorway (see Containment Procedures), does not trigger the effect.

When a lone individual is seated and the projector is active, the screen displays footage that subjects consistently describe as depicting their own life, filmed in a style consistent with ordinary handheld or security-camera footage rather than professional cinematography, and depicting events the subject has not yet experienced. Subjects report recognizing locations, other people, and in several cases specific unremarkable objects (a particular mug, a car with a subject's later-acquired dent) before those elements existed in their own life, with 12 of 31 documented subjects later confirming the footage's accuracy against events occurring in the following weeks or months.

The footage's runtime is not fixed; it continues for as long as the viewer remains in the room and stops, mid-scene, the instant they leave, resuming from the same point if they return within the same calendar day, and restarting from an apparently new sequence if they return on a later date. Footage reviewed by Foundation personnel via remote camera (rather than direct viewing) shows only static; the content is not recorded by any means other than the direct experience of the lone viewer, making independent verification of any given viewing's content impossible except retroactively, through the subject's later life.

In four documented cases prior to Foundation containment, individuals who remained in Screen Four beyond twenty minutes reported the footage's content shifting into scenes the subject could not identify as their own life at all — described by the sole cooperative surviving witness as "further along than anything that could still be me." In three of these four cases, the viewer did not exit the room; a subsequent search found Screen Four empty, with no sign of the individual and no alternative exit from the sealed auditorium. The fourth individual exited unassisted at the nineteen-minute mark, before any content shift was reported, and has since undergone quarterly psychological monitoring without incident.

Foundation testing has not reproduced content resembling that reported in the three disappearance cases, as no test subject has been permitted to remain beyond the twenty-minute recall threshold.

ADDENDUM 4242-1: Interviews with surviving subjects indicate near-universal reluctance to describe specific footage content in detail, not from apparent distress but from what several subjects independently termed a feeling that "saying it out loud might use it up." The significance of this phrasing, repeated with minimal variation across unconnected subjects, has not been explained.

SCP-4243.name: The Ripening Row
SCP-4243.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The orchard row designated SCP-4243, part of a larger working orchard near [town] acquired in full by the Foundation under an agricultural holding company, is fenced separately from the rest of the property with signage indicating a pesticide-treatment exclusion zone. The row consists of eleven fruit trees of mixed, inconsistent species not matching the surrounding orchard's planted varieties, nor any combination of rootstock and graft the current property's agricultural records can account for. Access is restricted to Level 3 personnel for authorized observation only. Standing order prohibits any Foundation staff member from consuming, or permitting any test subject to consume, fruit picked from SCP-4243 under any circumstance. Fruit that falls naturally from the row is to be collected, photographed, and incinerated within 24 hours; it is not to be analyzed in any laboratory where the resulting data could be cross-referenced with personnel records.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4243 is a row of eleven fruit trees within an otherwise unremarkable commercial orchard. Each tree bears fruit that does not match its own apparent species with any consistency — a single tree may bear what appear to be apples, plums, and an unidentified fruit matching no cataloged species, sometimes simultaneously on the same branch. The trees' anomalous property was first identified when orchard workers, none Foundation-affiliated at the time, noted that the fruit nearest a given person, standing within approximately three meters of the row, would change in color, firmness, and apparent ripeness over the course of minutes, correlating with no observable environmental factor.

Foundation study has established that the ripeness state of the nearest fruit — ranging, on an internally developed six-stage scale, from "hard, green, immature" to "spoiled, blackened, fallen" — correlates with the proximate individual's remaining lifespan, though the correlation is neither linear nor precisely calibrated. Stage 1 (immature) has been observed only in the presence of infants and, in one case, a terminal cancer patient in extended remission whose prognosis was later revised favorably. Stage 6 (spoiled) has preceded the proximate individual's death, by natural or accidental cause, by intervals ranging from four hours to eleven days in 34 of 34 documented cases, a correlation strong enough that SCP-4243 has been informally used, against explicit standing policy, by at least two researchers to check on family members, a practice now grounds for immediate reassignment.

The fruit's stage is not fixed to a given individual; it changes when they leave proximity and reflects whoever next stands nearby, including Foundation personnel, and updates in real time as circumstances change — two subjects have observed a fruit's stage visibly regress following the proximate individual's successful emergency medical treatment. No fruit has been observed to display a stage-6 reading for an individual who did not subsequently die within the recorded window; however, the Foundation has not identified any case in which advance knowledge of an impending stage-6 reading was used to prevent the associated death, as no such intervention has been authorized.

The trees produce no anomalous effect on individuals standing more than approximately three meters from the row, and the fruit itself, when tested away from any living proximate subject, shows standard botanical composition for its apparent species, aside from taxonomic inconsistencies already noted.

ADDENDUM 4243-1: A formal request by Dr. Anholt to authorize monitored proximity testing on terminally ill, informed-consenting Foundation staff as a possible early-warning application was declined by the Ethics Committee, citing SCP-4243's Safe classification and the absence of any demonstrated protective use for the information it provides.

SCP-4244.name: Rink Two
SCP-4244.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The community ice rink designated SCP-4244, located in [town]'s recreational center, was acquired by the Foundation in [year] and continues limited public operation under cover as a functioning municipal facility, staffed by Foundation personnel in maintenance and rental-counter roles. Public skating sessions are capped at 45-minute intervals to prevent any single skater from completing more than approximately 60 continuous laps of the rink's standard 60-meter circuit, based on average recreational skating pace. Any skater observed approaching 90 laps within a single session, tracked via ceiling-mounted counting sensors disguised as scoreboard equipment, is to be removed from the ice by staff under the pretext of a Zamboni resurfacing pass. The rink's ice surface is never to be fully melted and refrozen without prior authorization from the Site Director, per Incident 4244-2.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4244 is the ice surface of a standard indoor recreational skating rink. Under typical use, reflections visible in the ice beneath and around skaters behave as ordinary specular reflections, albeit with reduced clarity consistent with a skated-upon ice surface. Extended observation, beginning at approximately lap 40 of continuous skating by a single individual, reveals that the skater's reflection begins to lag behind their actual movements by an interval that increases with each subsequent lap, from under one second at lap 40 to approximately eleven seconds by lap 95, in a relationship the Foundation has modeled as roughly logarithmic rather than linear.

At lap 100, in 100% of trials conducted under controlled conditions (total n=19, prior to the moratorium described in Containment Procedures), the skater's reflection completes its lagged final circuit and, rather than continuing to mirror the ice surface, appears to rise from it, taking on the solidity and independent motion of a physical figure on the rink rather than a reflection within it. The original skater reports no unusual sensation at the moment of separation and typically does not notice the reflection's departure from the ice unless specifically observing it. The resulting figure, indistinguishable from the original skater in appearance and dressed identically, continues skating the rink's circuit indefinitely, without apparent fatigue, hunger, or acknowledgment of other skaters, Foundation staff, or the original individual, including when directly addressed.

The separated figure cannot be made to leave the ice surface by any method attempted to date, including physical removal (subjects report the figure "isn't quite where it looks like it is" when grasped, with contact producing a sensation subjects describe as reaching into cold water) and full resurfacing of the rink, which the figure survives by a mechanism not understood — Incident 4244-2 recorded a resurfacing pass during which the figure was, for approximately four seconds, indistinguishable from the wet ice itself before reappearing on the newly resurfaced, unmarked surface, mid-stride.

As of this writing, four separated figures, corresponding to four original skaters across the containment period (two Foundation test subjects, two civilians present before containment), continue to skate SCP-4244's circuit. The original individuals in all four cases report no physical or psychological aftereffect beyond the reflection's absence in mirrors and other reflective surfaces for a period of approximately six weeks following separation, after which normal reflection resumes. None of the four original skaters have requested to view or interact with their separated figure a second time.

ADDENDUM 4244-1: Overnight thermal and motion sensors confirm all four figures remain in continuous, indistinguishable motion regardless of the rink's operational hours, including during the several hours nightly when the facility, lights included, is fully powered down.

SCP-4245.name: The Room That Buries Someone Else
SCP-4245.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The Foundation maintains ownership of [Funeral Home], acquired in [year], operating it as a functioning funeral service under Foundation-embedded management to preserve its role as a community fixture and to allow continued observation of SCP-4245. All services scheduled for Viewing Room B are to proceed as normal funeral proceedings; family members and attendees are not to be informed of, or knowingly exposed to evidence of, the anomaly. A Foundation mortuary technician verifies the identity of the casket's occupant via fingerprint or dental record comparison no less than one hour before each scheduled viewing and again immediately following the departure of the last attendee; any discrepancy identified in the post-viewing check is to be handled under Protocol 4245-Silent, which supersedes standard body-handling procedure and does not require notification of the deceased's family of record.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4245 designates Viewing Room B of [Funeral Home], a standard-fittings viewing parlor used for open-casket services. When the casket in Viewing Room B is closed and left unwatched, even briefly, between the pre-service identity verification and the arrival of the first attendee, its occupant is, in 71% of documented services, no longer the deceased individual whose funeral is being conducted, having been replaced with a different human body.

The replacement body is, without exception, embalmed and dressed consistent with the original funeral's arrangements (matching or near-matching size and general appearance to avoid casual notice), and shows no anomalous properties under standard mortuary or forensic examination beyond its unexplained presence: cause of death, when determinable, is unrelated to the original deceased's, and time of death is inconsistent with any period the body could plausibly have spent in Foundation or funeral home custody. Fingerprint and dental comparison against 89 replacement bodies examined to date has matched none to any individual in Foundation, INTERPOL, or connected national missing-persons databases.

Attendees viewing the casket during the service consistently perceive and describe the original deceased individual, including specific identifying features (scars, jewelry placed by family, a wedding ring); this holds true even when Foundation personnel, viewing the same open casket at the same time, plainly observe a different body. This discrepancy has never been remarked upon by any civilian attendee in 61 documented services, including four in which family members touched or kissed the substituted body during the viewing. The mechanism producing this perceptual discrepancy has not been identified and does not resemble any cataloged memetic or reality-bending effect on record; standard anti-memetic countermeasures have no observed effect on it.

Following each service's conclusion and the casket's closure for burial or cremation, the substitute body is, in all cases to date, found to have reverted to the correct original deceased individual by the time of Foundation post-service verification, with no observed transition and no indication, from either the body or the casket's interior, that a substitution occurred. Foundation attempts to intercept and retain a substitute body prior to this reversion — by opening the casket mid-substitution and removing the body for study — have succeeded on six occasions; in all six, the removed body was later found to have reverted to the correct original deceased despite being held in a separate, monitored, and continuously observed containment locker, with no camera footage capturing the moment of change.

The fate, origin, and number of distinct individuals cycling through SCP-4245's substitutions remain unknown. Comparison of the 89 collected substitute-body dental records against one another has found no repeats: each has, to date, been a different, unidentified person.

ADDENDUM 4245-1: Protocol 4245-Silent's continued operation — permitting unidentified human remains to be interred or cremated under a deceased stranger's name, without notification to any authority — remains under quarterly ethics review. It has not, to date, been altered.

SCP-4246.name: Relay Nine
SCP-4246.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4246 is maintained in full operational condition at its original location, a decommissioned AM relay tower and adjoining control room near [location], now designated Site-4246 and staffed continuously by a rotating team of three Foundation radio operators holding Level 3 clearance and completion of Thaumiel-track operator certification. The tower's original broadcast license has been allowed to lapse; SCP-4246 transmits no outgoing signal and exists solely as a receiver. Operators are to maintain a continuous listening log across all designated frequencies (see Description) during each eight-hour shift and are prohibited from attempting to respond to, broadcast toward, or otherwise signal any source received through SCP-4246. Any received transmission assessed as meeting Warning Criteria (Document 4246-W) is to be escalated to the Site-4246 duty director within four minutes of identification, per the tower's designated function within Foundation disaster-mitigation protocol.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4246 is a radio receiver and associated control room within a decommissioned relay tower, in continuous operation by the Foundation since [year] under the operational designation "Relay Nine." When tuned across a specific, non-contiguous set of eleven AM frequencies unassigned to any licensed broadcaster in the region, past or present, SCP-4246's receiver intermittently picks up transmissions of human speech, music, and emergency broadcast tones in formats consistent with mid-20th-century radio programming, none traceable to any station, network, or recording in Foundation or civilian archives.

The majority (approximately 85%) of received transmissions are inert: fragments of unremarkable programming, advertisements for products and businesses that do not appear in any historical record, and, on 14 occasions, what operators describe as ordinary phone-in conversation between unidentified speakers discussing unremarkable daily matters. These transmissions have no established practical value and are logged but not acted upon.

The remaining transmissions periodically include content meeting one or more Warning Criteria: a simulated emergency broadcast tone followed by a spoken advisory specifying a location, a hazard type, and a time window, phrased in the register of a genuine civil emergency broadcast. Of 203 such warnings received and logged since Site-4246's establishment, 174 have corresponded to a verifiable subsequent hazard event (localized flooding, structure fire, gas leak, or, in nine cases, a small-scale seismic event) at or near the named location within the specified window, with sufficient lead time in the large majority of cases (mean 6.4 hours) to permit Foundation-coordinated advisory action through cooperating civilian channels, without revealing SCP-4246's existence. The Foundation credits SCP-4246's warnings, acted upon through arranged-appearing coincidence (anonymous tips, adjusted utility inspection schedules, weather-service-attributed advisories), with a conservatively estimated 40 to 60 civilian fatalities prevented to date.

The source of the warnings remains unidentified. Signal triangulation has failed consistently, returning inconsistent and physically implausible bearings on each attempt. The register and cadence of the warning voice, analyzed across 174 confirmed instances, has been assessed by Foundation linguists as consistent throughout, suggesting a single, unidentified, and apparently sustained source, though no operator has reported the same voice describing itself or responding, even indirectly, to anything other than the hazard it is reporting.

Twenty-nine received warnings have not corresponded to any subsequent verifiable event as of this writing. Fourteen of these named locations or dates that have not yet arrived.

ADDENDUM 4246-1: Site-4246 leadership has formally recommended against any attempt to establish two-way contact with the warning source, citing both the operational risk of disrupting a functioning early-warning asset and the unresolved question of what, if anything, the source might want in return. The recommendation has been accepted without further comment from the O5 Council.

SCP-4247.name: The Vending Machine With No Prices
SCP-4247.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The rest-stop alcove containing SCP-4247, located along [highway] at mile marker [___], has been sealed within a Foundation-constructed maintenance enclosure disguised as a defunct restroom facility, accessible only through a keyed service door. The rest stop itself remains in civilian use; signage directs travelers away from the enclosure via a "Closed for Repairs" notice, reinforced where necessary by a stationed Foundation groundskeeper. SCP-4247 is not to be unplugged, moved, or restocked by any means; its apparent product inventory has not changed since initial containment and Foundation testing indicates it does not deplete. Personnel authorized for interaction testing are limited to one interaction per 90-day period and must undergo a full inventory of personal effects immediately before and after, per Protocol 4247-Inventory.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4247 is a coin-operated vending machine of a make and model not currently or previously manufactured by any identified company, installed in a rest-stop alcove of standard highway-service construction. The machine's product display shows physical items rather than the snack or beverage packaging typical of the machine's apparent category; the specific items visible behind the glass are not consistent between observations, and no two individuals viewing the machine simultaneously have reported seeing the same selection.

The machine displays no prices. When approached by a lone individual, the machine's keypad and coin slot become active regardless of prior inactivity, and the individual is able to select and receive exactly one item by pressing any keypad combination, without inserting currency. The item dispensed is, in all 118 documented interactions, small, physical, and unrelated in market value or category to a typical vending machine product (examples include: a single key of unknown provenance, a folded and unopened letter addressed to the recipient by name, a smooth stone, a child's drawing, an unworn wedding band). Subjects consistently and independently report that the dispensed item relates, often in a manner they describe as uncomfortably precise, to a specific regret or unresolved matter from their recent past, though the connection is rarely stated aloud without prompting and several subjects have declined to elaborate on it during debrief.

Post-interaction inventory checks conducted under Protocol 4247-Inventory have identified, in 61% of interactions, the absence of one minor personal item the subject possessed prior to approaching the machine — examples recorded include a shoelace, a single earring from a pair, a specific coin, a guitar pick, and, in three cases, a photograph subjects could not otherwise account for the loss of. Subjects are, without exception, unable to recall the missing item's absence until it is specifically pointed out, at which point they typically express only mild surprise rather than the searching concern usually associated with realizing a personal item has gone missing. No subject has reported successfully relocating a missing item taken by SCP-4247.

No correlation has been established between the nature of the item dispensed and the nature of the item taken. The machine's interior mechanism, when the enclosure was inspected during initial containment, contained no product stock, currency, or wiring consistent with functional vending equipment; the machine has not been opened since, per standing order, following the disappearance of the technician who conducted that inspection from all subsequent personnel records six weeks after his report was filed, a discrepancy that remains under investigation.

ADDENDUM 4247-1: The technician's report itself remains on file and has not been altered or redacted. It ends mid-sentence.

SCP-4248.name: The Dome That Miscounts
SCP-4248.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4248 is contained within the university observatory building it has occupied since [year], acquired by the Foundation via a research-partnership cover with [University]. The dome and its refracting telescope remain nominally available for supervised student and faculty use to maintain cover, with a Foundation-embedded staff astronomer present at all sessions. A designated reference field, Catalog Sector 4248-R (a specific 2-degree patch of sky containing 118 stars of magnitude 9.0 or brighter, independently verified by photographic plate), is to be visually counted through the eyepiece at the start and end of every clear-night session and logged. Any discrepancy from the 118-star baseline is to be reported to the Site Director before sunrise. Photographic or digital imaging of Sector 4248-R has not, to date, reproduced any discrepancy and is not considered a substitute for direct visual counting.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4248 is a 40-centimeter refracting telescope housed in its original observatory dome, manufactured and installed in [year] with no recorded modification. The telescope functions as an ordinary optical instrument in all respects verifiable through standard testing, and photographs or sensor captures taken through it show no deviation from expected astronomical data for any given date and coordinate.

When Sector 4248-R is observed directly through the eyepiece by a human eye, the star count deviates from the baseline of 118 on approximately one night in four, always by a reduction (no session has recorded more than 118 stars) ranging from one to, in a single recorded instance, nineteen missing stars. The missing stars are not obscured, dimmed, or displaced; they are, to direct observation, simply absent, while any photographic or CCD capture of the identical field taken in the same moment shows the full, correct complement of 118. The discrepancy resolves without explanation by the following clear-night session, at which point the full count returns, and no instance has been recorded of the same star or stars being absent on two separate nights.

Foundation research beginning in [year] established a correlational study comparing nightly missing-star counts against verified mortality records for the town of [town], population approximately 14,000, within whose limits the observatory sits. Of 71 nights with a recorded discrepancy, 52 have shown a missing-star count matching, within a margin of one, the number of town residents who died within the following 29 days (a period the Foundation has adopted as a working lunar-cycle proxy, though no confirmed relationship to the actual lunar cycle has been established). No method has been identified for determining which specific individuals a given night's count corresponds to, and no correlation has been found between the missing-star count and any other town-level statistic tested (births, arrivals, departures, weather).

The remaining 19 discrepant nights show missing-star counts with no corresponding mortality match within any tested window from 14 to 60 days, and no alternative correlate has been identified for them. Dr. Pruitt's standing hypothesis — that SCP-4248 tracks a category of event broader than death, of which death is only the portion the Foundation has thought to measure — remains unconfirmed and, per her own written note appended to the most recent quarterly review, "not one I am eager to test the completeness of."

ADDENDUM 4248-1: On the single nineteen-star night, no corresponding mortality event of any kind, expected or excess, was recorded in [town] within the following sixty days.

SCP-4249.name: Concordant Toss Series
SCP-4249.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation monitoring of SCP-4249 is conducted through data-sharing agreements with six mobile gaming applications and three university statistics departments that log coin-flip outcomes with millisecond timestamps. Flagged correlation events ("concordant series") are forwarded automatically to Site-77's Applied Cryptanalysis Unit. No physical containment is possible or has been attempted, as SCP-4249 does not manifest at a fixed location and cannot be reliably triggered on demand.
Personnel are not to attempt to assemble intentional concordant series outside of approved test windows (see Addendum 4249-2). All translated fragments are classified 4/4249 pending review by the Ethics Committee.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4249 refers to a statistically anomalous correlation observed among the outcomes of coin flips performed by three or more people in physically separate, non-communicating locations within the same 1.8-second window. Across 41,000 sampled multi-flip windows since discovery, correlated events occur at a rate approximately 340 times higher than chance would predict for independent fair coins, with a mean correlation coefficient of 0.91.
Correlated outcomes are not uniformly identical; a given series may show any combination of heads and tails, but the specific pattern within a series is stable and repeatable if the same group of individuals is retested under similar conditions, which does not occur under normal circumstances since series membership appears to be determined externally to the participants and cannot be predicted in advance.
When flip outcomes within a captured series are recorded in chronological order as a binary string (heads = 1, tails = 0) and concatenated across all recorded series in the order they occurred, portions of the resulting sequence align, under a rolling substitution key derived by Foundation cryptanalysts, with segments of coherent text in no confirmed language. Approximately 4.1% of the accumulated 2.3-million-character dataset has been provisionally translated. Translated fragments do not form a continuous narrative; recovered phrases to date include "the third will not stay closed," "recount before the hour changes," and "not everyone flipping is counted." The cryptanalysis team has not reached consensus on whether the translation represents genuine communication or an artifact of pattern-matching bias; a formal review is pending.
Series size ranges from the minimum of three to a maximum recorded instance of 214 individuals, which occurred on 2019-11-03 at 04:12:07 UTC and included participants on five continents with no known point of contact. No series has repeated the same total participant count.

ADDENDUM 4249-1: Following the 214-participant event, the cryptanalysis unit noted that the translated fragment recovered from that specific series read, in full: "counted, and the count was wrong." No corrective action has been identified, as the nature of the "count" referenced remains undetermined. Monitoring continues.

ADDENDUM 4249-2: A proposal to deliberately assemble a large concordant series under controlled conditions, in order to accelerate data collection, was submitted and denied twice by the Ethics Committee on the grounds that the mechanism by which series membership is selected is unknown, and that Foundation personnel volunteering as flip participants cannot be confirmed to be selecting themselves rather than being selected.

SCP-4250.name: The Vacancy Tone
SCP-4250.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
No physical containment is required. Site security and custodial staff are instructed not to leave audio-recording equipment running in unoccupied rooms without prior authorization from the SCP-4250 research liaison, as unauthorized recordings have caused administrative confusion (see Addendum 4250-1). A standing collection order allows the liaison to requisition any recording suspected of containing SCP-4250 for analysis. Analysis of confirmed recordings is restricted to personnel with Level 2 clearance or higher, as raw waveform review has been associated with mild but consistent reports of anticipatory unease (see Description).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4250 is a recurring acoustic anomaly detected exclusively in post-recording playback, never during live monitoring, of audio captured in enclosed indoor rooms within the first ten minutes after the room's last occupant departs. Approximately 1 in 6,000 qualifying recordings contains SCP-4250: a continuous tone at 18.5 Hz (within the low end of human infrasonic perception, generally felt rather than heard), inaudible during the original recording session to anyone present or monitoring live, but clearly present in the recorded waveform upon later analysis.
The defining property of SCP-4250 is that the duration of the tone corresponds, without exception in 212 confirmed cases, to the exact length of time the room subsequently remained unoccupied before the next person entered it — information that did not exist at the time of recording, since occupancy patterns for the rooms tested are not fixed or scheduled. In one representative case, a tone lasting 4 hours, 12 minutes, and 40 seconds was recorded in an unused Site-19 break room; the room was not entered again until 4 hours, 12 minutes, and 41 seconds later, when a maintenance worker arrived one second past the tone's end for reasons unrelated to any Foundation scheduling.
SCP-4250 does not manifest in rooms that are never fully vacated (i.e., where at least one person remains continuously), in outdoor spaces, or in rooms below approximately 8 cubic meters. It has been recorded in over thirty structures of varying age, construction material, and geographic location, with no identified common factor beyond enclosure and vacancy. The tone cannot be used for practical prediction, as it is only ever discovered retroactively; live monitoring for the frequency during an ongoing vacancy has never detected it, suggesting the tone does not exist in real time during the vacancy but is somehow imprinted onto the recording only after the vacancy has already ended.
No hypothesis to date accounts for how a recording captures information about an event (the moment of re-occupancy) that had not yet occurred when the recording was made and finished.

ADDENDUM 4250-1: An unauthorized recording made by a janitorial staff member curious about the phenomenon captured a tone lasting 11 days, 6 hours, and 2 minutes in a rarely used storage closet at Site-19. The closet was not reopened until the recorded interval had elapsed, at which point it was opened for a scheduled inventory unrelated to the recording. The staff member has requested reassignment away from areas where SCP-4250 has previously been detected. The request was granted.

SCP-4251.name: The Ward Clocks
SCP-4251.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The long-term care ward in which SCP-4251 was first documented (Ward C, Site-19 affiliated care facility "Meadowbrook") has been fitted with twelve identical wall clocks, each independently referenced against a cesium clock via a Foundation-monitored radio time signal and logged at five-minute intervals. Attending medical and nursing staff are not to be informed of the correlation described below, in order to prevent the data from influencing clinical decisions or patient/family morale; cover briefing describes the logging as an unrelated facilities-maintenance study. Deviation logs are reviewed weekly by the assigned researcher and forwarded to the Ethics Committee without patient names attached.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4251 refers to a consistent statistical correlation between the rate of time drift exhibited by mechanical and electronic clocks within Ward C and the subsequent clinical outcome of patients housed in the room nearest each clock. Clocks are otherwise unmodified consumer or hospital-standard units; disassembly and component replacement has not eliminated the effect, and clocks moved to other wards cease drifting until returned to Ward C, at which point drift resumes within an average of 60 hours.
In aggregate data collected over the four years since discovery (n=340 patients), a clock that runs slow relative to the reference signal by more than 40 seconds per 24-hour period correlates with a 71% higher likelihood that the nearest patient's condition will improve to the point of discharge within the following month. A clock that runs fast by the same margin correlates with a 66% higher likelihood that the nearest patient's condition will decline to the point of death within the following month. Clocks within normal drift tolerance (under 10 seconds per 24 hours) show no correlation either way. The effect has never been observed to predict the manner or exact timing of decline or improvement, only its general direction and rough one-month window, and has a documented false-positive rate that the assigned research team considers too high for any clinical use, though repeated proposals to use the clocks as a supplementary prognostic tool continue to be submitted and rejected.
No mechanism connects the clocks to specific patients beyond room proximity; when patients are moved between rooms, the correlation follows the room, not the patient, within one to two days. Clocks have never drifted in a direction correlating with an outcome that did not subsequently occur, though in nine documented cases a clock showed no drift at all for a patient whose outcome, in retrospect, could not be classified as clearly "improved" or "declined" — these patients were discharged to indefinite ongoing care, neither recovered nor deteriorated, and remain the subject of separate inquiry.

ADDENDUM 4251-1: A proposal to relocate a "fast-drifting" clock away from a specific patient's room, made informally by a nurse unaware of the study's true purpose but aware of ward gossip regarding "the bad clock," was denied per standing protocol. The patient's condition subsequently declined in line with prior correlation data. The nurse was not informed of the outcome comparison.

SCP-4252.name: The Second Signal
SCP-4252.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains monitoring taps on emergency alert system (EAS) test transmissions across 14 partner broadcast regions via arrangement with front company "Meridian Broadcast Standards." Any test transmission found to contain the embedded secondary track (see Description) is archived and the instruction it conveys logged, but not publicly disclosed or acted upon by Foundation personnel except for passive observation, per standing order following Incident 4252-3.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4252 refers to a secondary audio track embedded beneath approximately 1 in 900 scheduled Emergency Alert System test broadcasts (the monthly or weekly non-emergency tests broadcasters are required to air), detectable only by listeners within a narrow hearing sensitivity band centered around 15 kHz — a range most commonly retained by children under twelve and a small percentage of adults, and lost gradually with age-related hearing decline in the general population. The Foundation identified the phenomenon following unrelated reports of children responding to test broadcasts with specific unprompted behavior (see Incident 4252-1).
The secondary track consists of a synthesized voice, gender and accent inconsistent between instances, delivering a short instruction, typically two to nine words, unrelated to any emergency content in the primary broadcast. Recovered instructions include "leave the window open tonight," "do not answer if it rings twice," "give the smaller one to your sister," and "walk home the other way today." Instructions are mundane, specific to no identifiable recipient, and their source cannot be traced to the broadcaster, the EAS origination equipment, or any Foundation-identified third party with access to the signal chain.
Tracking of 61 confirmed instances found no correlation between compliance with the instruction and any subsequent negative outcome; in 8 cases, subjects who could be confirmed to have followed the instruction avoided a subsequent minor mishap that a comparable control population did not (Incident 4252-1 involved a child who left a window open per instruction, later found to be the means of escape when the same child's bedroom filled with smoke from an unrelated electrical fault). No case has yet linked non-compliance to harm. The Foundation has not identified any beneficiary of the instructions' effects, nor determined whether the correlation with beneficial outcomes is causal or coincidental given the small sample size.
