ADDENDUM 4252-3: A proposal to insert Foundation-authored instructions into the secondary track, exploiting the same delivery mechanism, was tested once under controlled conditions and failed; the inserted test instruction did not propagate through the normal EAS test chain and was not received by any test-panel listener, despite all technical parameters matching confirmed genuine instances. The mechanism inserting SCP-4252 content therefore appears foundation-external and non-replicable. Standing order restricts Foundation involvement to archival observation only.

ADDENDUM 4252-4: A cross-reference of the 61 confirmed instances against national EAS test-broadcast schedules found no bias toward any particular broadcaster, time slot, or day of week; instructions have been received by panel members as young as four and as old as thirty-one, the oldest confirmed recipient being an audiologist whose hearing sensitivity at 15 kHz was documented as unusually well-preserved for her age during an unrelated hearing study.

SCP-4253.name: Pre-Delay Formation
SCP-4253.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation observation of SCP-4253 is limited to Platform 2 of [REDACTED] Metro Station, the only confirmed active site, via existing station CCTV accessed through a cover agreement with the transit authority's security contractor. No intervention is authorized; two attempts to disrupt SCP-4253 by seeding the platform with confederate agents behaving randomly produced no change in outcome (see Addendum 4253-2).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4253 is a recurring behavioral phenomenon observed among commuters waiting on Platform 2, in which waiting individuals numbering approximately 30 or more spontaneously arrange themselves into a specific, repeating geometric pattern — a rough nested-triangle formation with a consistent 1.4-meter minimum spacing — between 90 and 150 seconds before the arrival of a train that is delayed by six minutes or more. Individuals involved do not communicate, make eye contact, or otherwise visibly coordinate, and when interviewed afterward, no subject has reported awareness of participating in a pattern; most describe simply "finding a good spot to stand."
The formation has been documented in 118 of 121 qualifying delay events (delays of six or more minutes with 30 or more platform occupants) since monitoring began, a rate inconsistent with coincidental clustering, and has never been documented in a delay under six minutes regardless of crowd size, nor with fewer than 30 people regardless of delay length. The formation dissolves without residual pattern within seconds of the train's arrival, and commuters proceed to board normally, with no observed relationship between position in the formation and position in the boarding queue.
No functional benefit to the formation (e.g., more even car loading, reduced boarding time) has been measured; boarding times for delayed trains preceded by the formation do not differ significantly from boarding times for delayed trains at other stations without the phenomenon. The Foundation has not identified why Platform 2 specifically exhibits the behavior; the station's other platform (Platform 1, same line, opposite direction) has never shown the pattern despite comparable crowd sizes and delay frequency.

ADDENDUM 4253-1: Behavioral analysts note the formation superficially resembles historical crowd-control drill patterns used at the station during its construction decades prior, though no institutional memory or training could plausibly account for spontaneous adoption by a population with near-total generational turnover since that period.

ADDENDUM 4253-2: A test in which four Foundation agents were instructed to stand in deliberately disruptive positions during a predicted-delay window did not prevent the formation; the surrounding crowd completed the pattern around the agents, treating their positions as fixed obstacles rather than incorporating or correcting them.

ADDENDUM 4253-3: Archival footage predating the monitoring program, recovered from the transit authority's decommissioned analog security system and covering eleven years prior to Foundation involvement, was reviewed for comparison. Of 43 qualifying delay events visible in the archival footage, image quality was sufficient to confirm the formation in 31, a rate consistent with current findings and indicating SCP-4253 is not a recent-onset phenomenon, though the earliest point at which it began remains undetermined given the limits of available recordings.

SCP-4254.name: The Flooded Reading Room
SCP-4254.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4254 cannot be contained, as it manifests as a subjective dream experience among an unpredictable and geographically dispersed population. Foundation front organization "Aurelia Sleep Research Cooperative" maintains a standing incentive-compensated panel of 4,000 volunteer dream journalers across [REDACTED] national territory, recruited under the pretense of ordinary sleep-pattern research, whose entries are algorithmically scanned each morning for the specific imagery described below. A positive detection threshold of 40 or more independent reports within a single 24-hour period triggers Condition Amber notification to regional power infrastructure liaison contacts (see Description) for passive monitoring only; no advance warning is issued to civil authorities, as correlated events have historically occurred within a window too short for meaningful preventive action.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4254 refers to a recurring dream image reported, independently and without prior contact between reporters, by geographically dispersed individuals the night before regional electrical grid failures affecting 10,000 or more customers. The image, described with high consistency across unconnected reporters, is of a large institutional reading room, generally identified as a library, in which water has risen to approximately knee height; the water is still, cold, and rising almost imperceptibly slowly; overhead lighting remains lit and functioning throughout the dream; no other people are present; and the dreamer reports an urge to continue reading or searching for a specific book whose title or subject cannot be recalled upon waking.
Across 61 months of panel monitoring, 34 grid failure events meeting the reporting panel's geographic coverage met or exceeded the 40-report detection threshold in the 24 hours preceding the failure; no failure event has occurred without a preceding elevated report count, though report counts below the 40-report threshold have occurred without any subsequent failure (specificity approximately 81%, sensitivity approximately 100% within the panel's limited coverage area). The mechanism connecting the dream image to grid infrastructure, which has no thematic relationship to water, libraries, or reading, remains unexplained. The Foundation's Electromagnetic Anomalies Division has found no correlation between the dream reports and any measurable pre-failure electrical signature.
The panel's coverage is limited to approximately 6% of the national grid's service area, and it is assumed but not confirmed that the phenomenon occurs at comparable rates in unmonitored regions. Expansion of the panel has been proposed repeatedly but is limited by the difficulty of recruiting and retaining volunteer dream journalers at the required density without revealing the study's true purpose.

ADDENDUM 4254-1: Three panel members, independently and in different reporting cycles, have described the reading room dream a second time on nights not followed by any grid failure. In each of these three instances, the dreamer noted the water level was measurably lower than in their first report. No failure event of any kind has followed a "low water" report to date. The research team has not determined whether this represents a partial or attempted event, a different phenomenon entirely, or noise.

SCP-4255.name: Synchronized Residents of Building 14
SCP-4255.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The apartment building in which SCP-4255 occurs (hereafter Building 14) has been fully acquired by Foundation front company "Larkspur Residential Holdings" and its 22 occupied units are leased exclusively to Foundation-affiliated personnel and their families, briefed at Level 1 on the general nature of the phenomenon and issued wearable cardiac monitors under the cover of a corporate wellness program. Residents are not restricted from moving out and have done so on nine occasions since acquisition; departing residents are debriefed and their monitoring data retained.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4255 refers to a nightly synchronization of resting heart rate among current residents of Building 14, verified via continuous cardiac monitoring since 2021. Beginning at a time that varies nightly but consistently falls between 2:00 and 4:00 AM local time, the heart rates of all residents present in the building at that time (sleeping or awake) converge toward a common value, typically within a final range of 3-5 BPM of each other, and remain synchronized for a period the Foundation terms the "window." Residents outside the building during the window, including those merely on the building's exterior grounds, do not synchronize; residents who enter the building mid-window synchronize within an average of six minutes of entry.
The synchronized rate itself varies nightly and does not correspond to the average, median, or any other simple statistical derivation of individual residents' baseline rates; it is frequently outside the normal resting range for some or all residents present (observed range 48-101 BPM), without associated reports of physical distress, and residents' own subjective sense of exertion or calm during the window does not change, i.e., a resident whose heart rate has been externally driven to 95 BPM while asleep does not wake or report increased perceived heart rate.
The most notable feature of SCP-4255 is that the length of the nightly window has increased steadily since first measurement, from an initial recorded average of 11 minutes in 2021 to a current average of 94 minutes as of the most recent quarterly review. Extrapolation of the current rate of increase suggests the window would encompass a full 24-hour period within approximately 6 years, though the research team notes available data does not support confident long-term extrapolation and the rate of increase itself has not been perfectly linear.
No cause for either the synchronization or its lengthening trend has been identified. Structural surveys of the building, geological surveys of the surrounding area, and interviews with all current and former residents have not identified a common exposure, event, or shared history among residents predating their tenancy that could account for the effect.

ADDENDUM 4255-1: A resident who requested reassignment after five years' tenancy cited, as her primary reason, "not wanting to find out what happens when it doesn't stop." No formal Foundation position exists on what, if anything, would occur should the window lengthen to cover a full day; a working group has been convened to develop a response prior to the projected 6-year horizon.

SCP-4256.name: The Countdown Checksum
SCP-4256.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Full containment of SCP-4256 is not currently achievable, as it manifests within software error-logging systems across an unknown and apparently expanding number of unrelated codebases worldwide. Foundation Digital Anomalies Division maintains automated scraping of public bug-tracking repositories and crash-report aggregation services for the specific error signature described below (see Description). Confirmed instances are logged in the SCP-4256 tracking database maintained at Site-77. Software engineers who report the error publicly are not to be contacted directly by Foundation personnel except through the standing amnesticization protocol described in Document 4256-A, following Incident 4256-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4256 is a checksum verification error message that has appeared, beginning in March 2021, in the logs of software systems across at least 340 confirmed unrelated codebases, written in eleven different programming languages, maintained by individuals and organizations with no established connection to one another. The error takes the general form of a standard checksum mismatch report (e.g., "expected [value], got [value]"), a category of error message common to legitimate software and therefore easily overlooked, but is distinguished by two consistent anomalous properties.
First, the function or module name cited as the error's origin does not exist anywhere in the affected codebase, in any version history, or in any dependency, and cannot be found by any code search performed after the fact; engineers investigating the error frequently report being unable to reproduce or even locate the referenced code path, and several have independently described the experience as the error appearing to originate from "outside the program."
Second, and of primary concern to the Foundation, the "expected" value reported in the error, when instances are collected chronologically across all confirmed codebases and the numeric values converted from their reported hexadecimal or base64 encoding to plain integers, form a strictly decreasing sequence with no repeated or skipped values, currently standing at 60,142 as of the most recent confirmed instance (Incident 4256-2, 2026-08-30). The sequence began, per the earliest recoverable log matching the signature, at 8,412,777. At the current average rate of decrease (approximately 4.1 per day, though the rate has been observed to fluctuate and, on three occasions, briefly reverse before resuming its overall decline), the sequence is projected to reach zero within approximately 40 years, though the Foundation has no basis for predicting what, if anything, will occur at that point, nor has any hypothesis explaining the countdown's origin, purpose, or relationship to the software systems it appears within gained sufficient support to be adopted as a working theory. This uncertainty regarding both mechanism and eventual outcome is the primary basis for this object's Keter classification.

ADDENDUM 4256-1: Statistical analysis has found no correlation between the codebases in which SCP-4256 appears and any shared hosting provider, programming framework, hardware architecture, or development team, beyond the observation that all affected codebases were under active development at the time of the error's appearance. Dormant or archived repositories have never produced an instance.

ADDENDUM 4256-2 (Incident 4256-2): An engineer at an unaffiliated software company, after independently noticing the decreasing pattern across public bug reports and posting an analysis to a technical forum, was administered Class B amnestics under Document 4256-A after Foundation monitoring flagged the post. The post itself was procured and removed prior to significant public engagement (14 views recorded). Continued discreet monitoring of public technical forums for independent discovery of the pattern is ongoing and considered an escalating containment concern given the sequence's public visibility.

SCP-4257.name: Delayed Delivery from Branch 19
SCP-4257.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The former postal branch associated with SCP-4257 (Branch 19, closed 1987, building since demolished) requires no physical containment. Foundation maintains an arrangement with the national postal service's regional sorting facility to flag and reroute any mail item bearing a Branch 19 postmark to Site-19 for interception prior to delivery. Approximately 60% of documented instances have historically evaded this arrangement and reached their addressee directly; intercepted items are photographed, documented, and, per standing policy, forwarded to their addressee with a delay of no more than 5 business days to preserve the appearance of normal (if slow) postal service.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4257 refers to the continued delivery of physical mail bearing the postmark of Branch 19, a postal branch that ceased operations in 1987 and whose building was demolished in 1994, to correct current addresses of intended recipients, including recipients who have since relocated multiple times, changed names through marriage, or in three confirmed cases, recipients who were not yet born at the time of the branch's closure and who received mail addressed to a parent or grandparent, correctly redirected to the living recipient's current address by means consistent with legitimate postal forwarding but with no corresponding forwarding order on file with the postal service.
Items delivered under SCP-4257 are, without exception among 203 documented instances, ordinary correspondence: bills, greeting cards, personal letters, and similar mail that would have been unremarkable had it been delivered promptly in 1987. Postmark dates on the items are contemporary to their delivery date, not to 1987, despite bearing Branch 19's discontinued postmark stamp design, a design not held or reproducible by the current postal service. Contents of the letters, where reviewed, reference contemporary-to-1987 events and contain no anachronistic information; senders, where traceable, are in all cases deceased, and none has been reached for comment prior to their death regarding any of the delivered items, nor do postal service records show these items as ever having entered the mail stream in 1987.
The mechanism of delivery — sorting, routing, and physical transport — has never been observed directly; items are found already delivered (in mailboxes, through mail slots, or in three cases involving prior interception, appearing in a sealed evidence container at Site-19 despite documented unbroken chain of custody) without any employee of the postal service, current or former, able to account for their handling. No pattern has been identified in delivery frequency, which has ranged from zero to eleven items in a calendar year since first documented in 1994, nor in the selection of which decades-old correspondence is delivered next.

ADDENDUM 4257-1: A letter delivered in 2023 to a recipient's grandson (the original addressee, and the addressee's child, both confirmed deceased) contained a birthday card dated for an event in 1987 that, per family records, did take place as planned, the original card having presumably gone undelivered at the time. The recipient has requested to keep the card. The request was granted following Ethics Committee review, as the item's continued retention by the Foundation served no research purpose beyond documentation already completed.

SCP-4258.name: The Fold That Remembers
SCP-4258.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All printed paper maps confirmed or suspected to exhibit SCP-4258 properties are stored flat, unfolded, in acid-free sleeves at Site-77's Cartographic Anomalies Archive to prevent uncontrolled crease formation. Personnel handling regional maps of [REDACTED COUNTY] for any Foundation purpose must fold new maps only along Foundation-approved reference creases (see Document 4258-Fold) under supervision, and any map folded by an unaffiliated party and later found to exhibit the effect is to be acquired through routine means (purchase, discreet exchange, or amnestic-assisted recovery per standard protocol) rather than left in circulation.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4258 refers to a property exhibited by paper maps of [REDACTED COUNTY] that have been folded along a specific crease pattern, first documented on a 1962 gas station road map and since reproduced on at least 40 independently printed maps of the same region spanning six decades and four different publishers, provided the fold is made in a specific sequence originally attributed to convenience of storage rather than any deliberate design.
When a map of the county is folded along this sequence, the resulting crease lines, overlaid on the printed geography, consistently pass through or immediately adjacent to the locations of anomalous, unusual, or otherwise flagged events occurring within the county in the twelve months following the fold, at a rate inconsistent with chance given the crease pattern's coverage of less than 4% of the county's total area by crease-adjacent length. This holds regardless of whether the map is folded before or, notably, discovered to have been folded years prior with the events already having occurred, suggesting the correspondence is not predictive foreknowledge acted upon by any party but a fixed property of the fold-geography relationship itself.
The effect requires no specific edition or print run; photocopies and digitally reprinted versions of the same map, folded identically, reproduce the effect, but maps of adjacent counties, or the same county at different historical boundaries, do not, and the same fold sequence applied to a county map with the geography deliberately mislabeled or altered prior to printing has, in three controlled tests, still correlated with the true underlying geography rather than the printed (false) one, indicating the effect responds to actual terrain rather than to the printed representation.
The Foundation has not determined why this specific county, this specific fold sequence (which does not correspond to any standard commercial map-fold pattern), or paper printed maps specifically (the effect has not been reproduced on any digital or projected map surface) are necessary conditions. A standing research question, unresolved as of this writing, is whether the crease is discovering a pre-existing property of the county or whether the county's anomaly rate has, over six decades of maps being folded this way by ordinary consumers, been shaped by the folding itself.

ADDENDUM 4258-1: A 2024 test fold performed on a newly commissioned, deliberately fictional map of a county that does not exist, using the same fold sequence, produced no correlative effect over a twelve-month observation period, as expected given the absence of real underlying geography. The test is considered to weakly support the "true terrain" hypothesis over a purely representational one.

SCP-4259.name: The Fourteenth Press
SCP-4259.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4259 cannot be contained at the level of individual elevators, as the required conditions (see Description) can theoretically be satisfied by any traction or hydraulic passenger elevator installed prior to 1979 with a mechanical or early-digital call panel, an estimated 40,000-plus surviving installations within Foundation-monitored territory alone. Current policy prioritizes containment of knowledge: the specific button sequence and timing that satisfies SCP-4259's trigger conditions is classified Keter-level and restricted to the assigned research team. Building owners of elevators confirmed to have produced a manifestation are approached under standard front-company pretexts to authorize decommissioning; 14 elevators have been decommissioned to date, none of which is known to be the only qualifying unit in its building.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4259 refers to an anomalous event that occurs within qualifying elevators (see Containment Procedures) when a specific sequence of fourteen floor-button presses, including repeated presses of already-illuminated buttons, is entered within a continuous 22-second window by a single occupant riding alone. The exact sequence, which the Foundation has confirmed functions identically across all 61 documented manifestation sites despite no shared manufacturer, installation date, or building type, is withheld from this record (see Document 4259-Seq, Keter clearance required).
Upon successful entry of the sequence, the elevator car does not stop at any floor indicated on its panel. Doors open, after a delay ranging from 40 seconds to just under 11 minutes across documented cases, onto a hallway not part of the host building, of consistent general appearance across all 61 cases: a corridor of indeterminate length in both directions beyond the range of the elevator's interior lighting, floored in worn institutional tile, lined with unmarked doors spaced at approximately four-meter intervals, and lit by fixtures that do not illuminate beyond roughly three meters from the elevator threshold regardless of fixture density.
Of 61 confirmed occupants who triggered SCP-4259, 4 exited the elevator into the hallway and did not return; none has been recovered. 38 remained inside the car, which after a further period (ranging from 6 minutes to just over 4 hours) closed its doors and returned to normal operation at the floor from which the sequence was initiated, with no memory gap reported by the occupant and no anomalous readings detected on their person. The remaining 19 cases involve occupants who partially exited (one or more limbs across the threshold) and were forcibly or voluntarily retrieved by other parties; of these, 6 reported subsequent minor but persistent changes in personal habit (see Addendum 4259-2) not present before the incident, and 2 have since triggered SCP-4259 again independently, both stating they did not intend to and could not recall entering the sequence deliberately.
The Foundation has not determined the origin, destination, or nature of the hallway, nor why the specific sequence functions across unrelated elevator installations with no shared manufacturing history, nor why a small number of occupants appear to re-trigger the phenomenon involuntarily after initial exposure. This combination of broad potential trigger availability, inability to achieve physical containment, and unresolved risk to personnel who re-trigger without apparent intent is the basis for Keter classification.

ADDENDUM 4259-1: Analysis of the 4 unrecovered occupants found no prior connection between them beyond having ridden a qualifying elevator alone; none is believed to have entered the sequence with knowledge of its function, as the sequence involves no printed or commercially known combination and has not been observed to be transmissible by instruction (three attempts to have briefed agents enter a known sequence under controlled observation failed to produce a manifestation, for reasons not understood — see Addendum 4259-3).

ADDENDUM 4259-2: Habit changes reported among partial-exit survivors include a persistent preference for stairs over elevators (5 of 6 subjects, though none reported fear or distress as the stated reason, describing the preference instead as simply "better"), and, in one subject, a new and unexplained habit of counting doors when walking down any hallway, which the subject has stated they are aware of but unable to stop.

ADDENDUM 4259-3: Controlled re-creation attempts using briefed Foundation agents entering the known sequence in a decommissioned but electrically active test elevator at Site-77 have failed in all three attempts to produce a manifestation, despite identical button timing confirmed via video review. The research team's leading hypothesis, unconfirmed, is that successful triggering requires the entering party to not know the significance of what they are doing, which would make deliberate Foundation study of the sequence's mechanism self-defeating by design.

SCP-4260.name: Standing Rain
SCP-4260.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4260 is not contained but monitored and operationally exploited under joint authority of the Foundation and [DATA EXPUNGED] as a Thaumiel-class asset. A dedicated detection network (Project SCION-RAIN), consisting of atmospheric pressure and particulate sensors deployed in 40 metropolitan areas, flags candidate manifestation sites for immediate dispatch of a welfare-check unit operating under the cover of municipal emergency services. Personnel are reminded that SCP-4260's utility depends on rapid response and that delayed dispatch has, in 6 documented cases, resulted in the manifestation dissipating before a welfare check could be completed (see Description).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4260 refers to a localized meteorological anomaly in which falling rain, within a radius of approximately 20-35 meters centered on a fixed point, decelerates gradually with increasing altitude below approximately 40 meters and comes to a complete stop, remaining suspended in place, retaining its shape as falling droplets rather than pooling or dispersing, for a duration ranging from 20 minutes to just under 9 hours before either resuming normal fall or evaporating in place. The phenomenon occurs exclusively during active rainfall (it has never been observed to independently generate precipitation) and exclusively, in all 214 documented instances since the Foundation began systematic tracking in 2016, within one hour and 500 meters of the death of a person who was alone and unattended at the time of death, indoors or outdoors, and whose body had not yet been discovered by another person as of the manifestation's onset.
The suspended droplet field is faintly visible to unaided observation as a shimmer or haze rather than a discrete cloud, and does not obstruct movement, sound, or normal visibility through it; personnel and members of the public have walked through active manifestations without apparent effect or, in interview, without apparent awareness that anything was unusual. The Foundation's operational use of SCP-4260, formalized in 2017, is as a passive location signal for otherwise-undiscovered deaths of isolated individuals: dispatched welfare-check units, treating the manifestation coordinates as an anonymous tip, have located 187 deceased individuals to date who would, per actuarial estimates for comparable isolated populations, likely otherwise have gone undiscovered for a median of 11 additional days.
The phenomenon does not manifest for all qualifying deaths; comparison against regional isolated-mortality statistics suggests a detection rate of approximately 30-40%, with no identified factor distinguishing manifestation from non-manifestation cases beyond active rainfall being locally present at the time, meaning the effect's operational value is bounded by weather and cannot be relied upon as a comprehensive detection method. The Foundation has taken no position on the mechanism connecting isolated death to localized rain suspension and has explicitly declined, per a 2019 Ethics Committee ruling, to investigate whether the phenomenon evidences any form of awareness, intent, or agency, citing operational and psychological risk to assigned personnel of framing the asset in those terms.

ADDENDUM 4260-1: A minority position paper, filed by a member of the assigned research team and not adopted as policy, argued that the consistent radius, duration range, and post-discovery dissipation behavior of SCP-4260 are difficult to reconcile with a purely mechanical or environmental cause, and recommended the object be re-evaluated for reclassification pending further study of what, if anything, the suspended rain is "waiting" to see happen. The recommendation remains unactioned.

SCP-4261.name: The Losing Table
SCP-4261.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Wednesday Rubber Club (Site designation: GoI-4261) is permitted to continue normal operation at St. Aldhan's Community Hall, [REDACTED], under passive observation by Agent embedded as member "Harriet Voss." Foundation does not intervene in match outcomes, seating arrangements, or membership changes except where a documented loss would result in loss of autonomic function (respiration, cardiac rhythm, swallowing reflex) in the losing player, in which case Agent Voss is authorized to forfeit her own hand to redirect the transfer.
Deck replacement has been attempted on three occasions (2019, 2021, 2023) using freshly sealed decks provided by Foundation logistics; anomalous transfer resumed within one hand of the new deck's first use in each case. Deck substitution is no longer considered a viable interruption method and further attempts require O5 authorization.
A rotating waiting list of prospective members exists; Foundation does not discourage new membership, as club attrition (via death or withdrawal) has historically been offset by recruitment at a rate sufficient to avoid public notice.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4261 is the recurring social behavior of an eleven-to-fourteen-member amateur bridge club, active in some form since at least 1974 under successive incarnations and venues. Play follows standard contract bridge rules with no observed deviation in procedure, scoring, or etiquette.
When a partnership loses a rubber (best two of three games), each losing player experiences the permanent, irreversible transfer of one discrete skill, memory, or physical capability to a member of the winning partnership, selected apparently at random between the two winners. Transferred items are typically procedural: the ability to parallel-park, recall of a deceased spouse's face, proficiency in a second language, continence. The recipient reports no discomfort and frequently does not notice the acquisition until directly tested.
Losses compound with repeated defeat. Long-term members who lose consistently exhibit a documented pattern of narrowing capability, beginning with minor motor skills and progressing, over years, toward loss of basic autonomic functions. Four deaths among club membership since 1974 have been attributed by Foundation pathology to this progression; local death certificates in all four cases list unrelated natural causes.
No club member has been observed to express distress at losing. Several have stated, when interviewed, some variation of the belief that they are "giving it up to someone who'll use it better," and decline offers of cessation or relocation. Members who win consistently do not appear to notice, express concern about, or discuss the accumulation of abilities that are not their own.
The origin of the anomaly has not been isolated to the deck, the venue, the scoring pads, or any individual member; substitution of all four has failed to halt the effect, suggesting the anomaly inheres in the game's completion as a social act rather than in any object used to play it.

ADDENDUM 4261-1: Agent Voss's most recent report notes that the club has begun, without apparent coordination, favoring pairings that separate the longest-standing members from the newest ones. Whether this reflects a deliberate strategy of protecting new members, or of directing losses toward those judged to have the least left to lose, has not been determined.

SCP-4262.name: First Response
SCP-4262.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Krug Hollow Volunteer Fire Department (GoI-4262), population-served approximately 340, is to remain operational under its existing roster and equipment. Foundation front company "Hollow Creek Mutual Insurance" underwrites all property in the department's service area to control claims documentation and prevent pattern recognition by outside adjusters.
Two members of Mobile Task Force Sigma-7 ("Firewatch") are embedded within the department under standard volunteer status. Embedded personnel are not authorized to prevent dispatch or discourage response under any circumstance; three prior attempts to delay or cancel a dispatch (2011, 2016, 2020) resulted in the fire manifesting at the firehouse itself, on two occasions with on-duty personnel inside.
Should the department disband, relocate, or otherwise cease to exist as a functioning unit, Site Director approval is required before any action is taken to prevent this, given uncertainty as to whether cessation would eliminate the anomaly's fire risk or simply displace it to an unmonitored population. Current standing order is non-interference with departmental continuity.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4262 denotes a consistent temporal anomaly associated with dispatch procedure at the Krug Hollow Volunteer Fire Department, a twelve-member all-volunteer brigade serving an unincorporated township. In 83% of documented incidents (n=61, 2003-present), department members have arrived at, or begun actively responding to, a structure fire between four and thirty-one minutes before any combustion is independently verifiable to have begun. In eleven incidents, firefighters were observed laying hose and breaking windows at a structure that subsequently, and only subsequently, ignited.
Statistical review by Foundation analysts indicates that fires within the department's service boundary occur if and only if the department mobilizes in response to them; no fire in the service area has been recorded without a corresponding, temporally-preceding dispatch. Conversely, department members report receiving dispatch information -- variously described as a radio tone, a "pull," or "just knowing" -- with no identifiable triggering call, alarm, or witness report. When questioned, dispatched members describe the sensation as unremarkable and comparable to legitimate emergency response, stating some variant of "you just go."
No member has expressed the belief that their response causes the fire. Several long-serving members, when this possibility was suggested during a cover-story interview, responded with mild irritation, characterizing the fires as inevitable and their role as strictly limited to arriving in time. Fire origin and cause determinations filed by County Fire Marshal (an unwitting party) are consistently unremarkable and attribute ignition to mundane sources -- wiring, unattended cooking, lightning -- appropriate to each structure.
Membership turnover has not altered the phenomenon; new recruits begin receiving dispatch "calls" within an average of six weeks of joining, regardless of prior volunteer firefighting experience.

ADDENDUM 4262-1: Foundation modeling has not resolved whether SCP-4262 represents the department causing fires through response, fires "selecting" responders in advance through unknown means, or a closed causal loop in which the question of origin is undefined. A 2022 proposal to test the hypothesis by covertly disbanding the department for one calendar year was rejected by the Ethics Committee on grounds that a null result would still leave 340 residents uninsured against the possibility that the fires would occur regardless, without response.

SCP-4263.name: Open House
SCP-4263.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation-affiliated agents maintain membership in the Tri-County Board of Realtors (GoI-4263) sufficient to monitor all listings flagged as concurrently represented by three or more member agents ("triple-listings"). Any triple-listing approaching a closing date is to be flagged to Site-77 Real Estate Monitoring Cell no less than 72 hours prior to scheduled closing.
Direct prevention of a triple-listing sale is not authorized except by unanimous Site Director and Ethics Committee approval, as four prior interventions (blocking financing, inducing seller withdrawal) resulted in the erasure event occurring regardless, applied to a substitute buyer not originally party to the listing. Current policy is to identify, wherever possible, which of the competing buyers is least socially embedded (fewest dependents, weakest community ties) prior to closing, in order to reduce downstream anomalous memory disruption among the erased individual's associates; this policy is under continued Ethics Committee review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4263 refers to a recurring anomalous event associated with residential property sales concluded through the Tri-County Board of Realtors, a standard-seeming regional professional association of approximately 140 licensed real estate agents. The anomaly manifests specifically, and only, when a single property is simultaneously represented in active buyer negotiations by three or more Board member agents on behalf of three or more prospective buyers ("triple-listing").
Upon closing of sale to one buyer, one of the unsuccessful bidding parties -- not necessarily the buyer who made the lowest offer, and with no consistent selection criterion yet identified -- undergoes retroactive removal from the transaction record. In 61% of confirmed cases, this removal extends beyond documentation: the individual is retroactively erased from existence, with no body, no forwarding trace, and no consistent memory of them retained by immediate family, coworkers, or, notably, the realtor who represented them. Remaining paperwork referencing the erased buyer is altered to show a withdrawal of offer in unremarkable, contemporaneous language ("buyer rescinded, financing").
Realtors themselves show no anomalous behavior, distress, or awareness; agents who have represented erased buyers on multiple occasions describe their work in ordinary professional terms and do not recall specific erased clients when the closed file is presented to them, though they recall the sale and the successful buyer without difficulty.
The Board has approximately doubled its membership since 2009, a period corresponding with a documented rise in regional triple-listing frequency, though no causal relationship between Board growth and listing volume beyond ordinary market forces has been established. It is not known whether growth is a cause, a consequence, or unrelated to the anomaly.

ADDENDUM 4263-1: Interview excerpt, Agent Delgado (embedded, seven years), on why she has not requested reassignment: "You stop being able to tell if you're the one who's going to close on something, or the one who's going to get closed on. I've started asking every client if they've got someone at home who'll notice."

SCP-4264.name: The Unlisted Employee
SCP-4264.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
No direct containment action is to be taken against the individual(s) associated with SCP-4264 pending further research. Foundation payroll-monitoring software has been installed, under standard corporate audit pretext, at Meridian Claims Processing LLC (GoI-4264 primary site) and eleven affiliated regional offices identified as exhibiting the same personnel anomaly.
Attempts to directly interview or physically detain an SCP-4264 individual are suspended following Incident 4264-3, in which a detained subject was successfully transported and held for six hours at a secure facility before all containing personnel, independently and without prior communication, lost the ability to recall the subject's presence, location, or the fact of the detainment itself; the subject was later found to have returned to their workstation with no gap in employment records. Current research is limited to indirect methods: payroll data analysis, output review, and analysis of the small number of physical objects (badges, coffee mugs, desk nameplates) associated with each SCP-4264 individual, which remain perceivable and legible to unaffected personnel.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4264 designates a recurring personnel anomaly identified across at least twelve unrelated corporate offices, most consistently within mid-sized claims-processing, data-entry, and back-office administrative environments. In each identified instance, exactly one employee is present on payroll, badge access logs, and building security footage, who cannot be seen, heard, described, or consciously recalled by any coworker at the site, including direct supervisors and Human Resources staff who process their employment paperwork.
The individual's desk, output, and effects are treated by coworkers as unremarkable fixtures of the office; requests to "ask [name] about it" are followed reflexively, without any apparent awareness that the employee referenced cannot be described afterward. Interviewed staff, when shown security footage of the individual, express mild confusion lasting several seconds before attention visibly redirects to unrelated matters, a pattern consistent across all subjects and offices tested.
Output attributed to SCP-4264 individuals is, without exception, error-free, and offices employing one report claims-processing accuracy rates significantly above regional average (mean +14.2%, office-level comparison). Removal or reassignment of an SCP-4264 individual has not been successfully tested; the sole documented attempt (Incident 4264-3, above) suggests active resistance to interruption of employment status, though whether this resistance originates from the individual or from some property of the office environment itself has not been determined.
It is not established whether the twelve identified individuals represent a single entity operating across sites, a class of functionally identical individuals, or an unrelated coincidence of independent anomalies. Applications to eleven of the twelve offices' Human Resources departments for the individual's personnel file have returned complete, unremarkable records -- including social security number, prior employment history, and next of kin -- none of which have been successfully cross-referenced to any other government or Foundation database.

ADDENDUM 4264-1: A twelfth office, added to the active monitoring list in 2025, was found already staffed with an SCP-4264 individual on the date its monitoring began, despite the office itself having opened only four months prior. Personnel records indicate the individual was hired in the office's second week of operation.

SCP-4265.name: The Fallow Plot
SCP-4265.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains observational access to Birchcombe Community Garden Cooperative (GoI-4265, 44 active plot-holders) via a cover identity ("regional soil conservation surveyor") permitting quarterly site visits. The Cooperative's internal rotation schedule for the "fallow plot" designation is not to be interfered with; two prior Foundation attempts to anonymously reassign the designation (2017, 2020) resulted in redistribution of the accumulated deficit across all 44 members simultaneously, producing minor concurrent injury or illness in the entire membership rather than concentration in a single individual, an outcome judged substantially worse than baseline.
Committee elections determining plot assignments are to be monitored but not influenced. Any plot-holder assigned the fallow designation for more than two consecutive seasons is to be flagged for welfare monitoring; three such individuals have died of causes clustering statistically outside regional baseline (cumulative unlikely-accident and sudden-illness rate) since observation began in 2015.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4265 refers to an anomalous distributive effect localized to the membership of the Birchcombe Community Garden Cooperative, a 44-plot allotment garden operating under an elected governing committee since 1988. One plot within the garden's boundary is designated each growing season as the "fallow plot" and is left formally unplanted per Cooperative bylaws, ostensibly for soil rest.
Statistical analysis of member health records, insurance claims, and self-reported incident logs (voluntarily submitted as part of ordinary Cooperative record-keeping) indicates that the remaining 43 plot-holders experience adverse events -- injury, illness, financial loss, property damage -- at a rate approximately 60% below regional baseline for a comparable population, while the individual assigned that season's fallow plot experiences adverse events at a rate approximately 26 times regional baseline, clustered within the growing season during which they hold the assignment.
The Cooperative's bylaws describing fallow-plot assignment make no reference to this effect and are consistent with ordinary agricultural rationale. However, interviews conducted under cover suggest broad tacit awareness among longtime members: the assignment is informally known as "keeping the ground quiet," is generally avoided through minor social maneuvering (arriving late to the assignment meeting, volunteering for other committee roles), and is disproportionately held, across the Cooperative's recorded history, by newer members, elderly members living alone, and members without immediate family in the area.
No member interviewed has explicitly acknowledged the fallow plot as harmful. Several, when the pattern was described to them under the cover pretext of "informal research into gardening superstitions," responded that the arrangement was "just tradition" or that the plot "needed the rest more than we do."

ADDENDUM 4265-1: The 2024 fallow assignment was accepted, without apparent lobbying or selection pressure by other members, by a plot-holder who had joined the Cooperative six weeks prior and had not yet been informed, by any other member, of the assignment's informal reputation.

SCP-4266.name: The Complete Line
SCP-4266.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Wexford County Genealogical Society (GoI-4266, approx. 90 members) is not to be dissolved, restricted, or denied access to public genealogical archives, as prior restriction attempts (2013) demonstrably accelerated independent completion of lineage research by motivated members using non-Society resources. Foundation maintains two embedded agents with Society research privileges, tasked with identifying member research projects nearing verified completion of an unbroken documented line.
When a member's research is assessed as within one generation of verifiable completion, Site-77 Anomalous Genealogy Cell is authorized to introduce a single fabricated documentary gap (a plausible period of missing parish, census, or immigration records) into relevant public or digitized archives accessible to the member, sufficient to prevent formal completion without triggering suspicion of interference. This measure has an estimated 40% long-term success rate, as some members successfully route around the fabricated gap using alternative sources within 18-36 months.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4266 is a genealogical research society whose stated mission -- tracing member family lines to a documented point of origin -- carries an anomalous consequence: a member who successfully compiles a complete, source-verified, unbroken line of descent from themselves to a documented originating ancestor, with no generational gap, undergoes retroactive removal from that lineage and, in all 6 confirmed cases, from existence generally.
The completed tree itself is not erased; Society archives retain the full documented line, with the terminal (living) entry either left blank, relabeled "descendant unknown," or, in two cases, populated with a plausible but fabricated name unconnected to any real individual, apparently substituting for the erased member without any Society member noticing the substitution. Immediate family of erased members retain fragmentary, degraded memories -- a sense of an absence, occasional confusion at family gatherings, photographs featuring unidentified figures matching the erased individual's likeness that family members cannot name.
Society culture treats "completing the circle" as the organization's highest, if rarely achieved, honor, and members who approach completion are met with encouragement rather than concern. Of the six confirmed completions since Society founding in 1961, interview data recovered from associates prior to erasure suggests at least four of the six were aware, in general terms, that completion carried some cost, and pursued it regardless; one left a note, recovered by an embedded agent before its own retroactive alteration into an unrelated grocery list, that read in part: "if the line closes, I close with it, and that's not the same as dying."

ADDENDUM 4266-1: It has not been established whether erasure constitutes destruction of the individual or removal to an undetermined state consistent with the "not the same as dying" framing recovered above. No post-erasure contact, of any kind, with an erased individual has been documented.

SCP-4267.name: Five Stars
SCP-4267.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The driver collective operating under the informal name "The Route" (GoI-4267, estimated 200-340 active members across a metropolitan rideshare/delivery market) is not to be formally contained or dissolved. A Foundation-controlled cell of 6 drivers ("Asset Group Meridian"), recruited from genuine former GoI-4267 members under standard incentive protocols, is maintained within the collective's operating radius and app ecosystem for approved Thaumiel-classified operations (see Addendum 4267-2).
Civilian members of GoI-4267 are not to be informed of the anomaly's mechanism. Foundation monitors the collective's private messaging channels for organized "protective" behavior (refusal to log off during disputes, buddy check-ins) and intervenes covertly only to prevent civilian fatality clusters, via anonymous tip-offs to app platform trust-and-safety teams resulting in review removal.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4267 denotes an anomalous mechanism affecting an informal mutual-aid network of rideshare and food-delivery drivers operating across a single metropolitan area, self-organized around a private messaging channel and referred to by members as "The Route." Membership is fluid and defined by participation in the channel rather than formal registration.
A negative ("1-star") review submitted against the in-app profile of any active GoI-4267 member results, within 4-40 minutes, in a physical injury manifesting on a member of the collective who is logged into the app as available at the time of submission -- not necessarily the reviewed individual. Injury severity correlates with the negativity and specificity of the review's written text rather than its numeric score alone; reviews containing specific hostile language ("should be fired," "ruined my night," "hope he crashes") produce measurably worse outcomes (fractures, lacerations) than terse low scores without comment (bruising, minor sprains).
Members have independently developed folk-protective practices without, in interviews, articulating an understanding of the underlying mechanism: never going offline during an active dispute with a passenger or customer, group check-ins after any reported confrontation, and informal blacklisting of accounts believed to leave harsh reviews. These behaviors measurably reduce injury frequency and severity, suggesting some degree of functional, if not conscious, comprehension among the collective.

ADDENDUM 4267-1: Origin of the mechanism is unknown. The review platforms involved (three major rideshare/delivery apps) show no shared code, ownership, or anomalous properties independent of GoI-4267 membership; drivers for the same platforms outside the collective's messaging channel do not exhibit the effect.

ADDENDUM 4267-2 [CLASSIFIED -- THAUMIEL DESIGNATION, O5 EYES ONLY]: Asset Group Meridian has been used, under authorization 4267-T-3 through -11, to submit coordinated hostile reviews against driver profiles fraudulently registered to identified hostile GoI personnel operating covertly as rideshare drivers in three prior field operations, resulting in confirmed incapacitating injury to two targets and one unconfirmed. Ethics Committee has noted, without formal objection sufficient to block continued use, that this application relies on the same civilian collective whose members the Foundation is separately obligated to protect from injury under standing containment policy, and that Asset Group Meridian's recruited drivers do not appear to have been informed that their own continued participation places them, statistically, within the pool of potential injury recipients on operations where multiple hostile reviews are submitted in close succession.

SCP-4268.name: Shared Watch
SCP-4268.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation monitors active membership rolls of the Ashgrove Meadows Neighborhood Watch (GoI-4268) via a compromised HOA management account and maintains a standing minimum-membership threshold alert. Current safe threshold is estimated at 31 active patrol-eligible members; membership has not fallen below 34 since monitoring began in 2018, but two near-threshold events (2019, 2023) were resolved only through Watch-organized recruitment drives conducted without Foundation involvement.
Should active membership approach the estimated threshold, Foundation is authorized to introduce anonymous prospective members (embedded personnel or induced genuine recruits via targeted local advertising) to restore buffer capacity. Direct disclosure of the mechanism to Watch leadership remains prohibited pending Ethics Committee review of standing recruitment practices (see Addendum 4268-1).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4268 is an anomalous mutual-redistribution effect affecting registered active members of the Ashgrove Meadows Neighborhood Watch, a suburban volunteer patrol organization of currently 38 members operating within a defined thirty-block residential boundary. Physical injury sustained by any active member while within the patrol boundary is not experienced solely, or even primarily, by that member; instead, the total physiological harm is calculated (mechanism unknown) and redistributed in approximately equal fractional shares across all currently active members, including those off-duty or asleep at the time.
At current membership levels, this redistribution renders most injuries -- including one documented vehicular collision and one dog attack -- perceptible only as brief, unattributed discomfort (a headache, a moment's dizziness) across the membership, with no member experiencing harm proportional to the original injury's severity. Membership decline sharply increases per-member share; retrospective analysis of a 2011 incident, when the Watch numbered 9 active members, indicates a single member's broken arm was redistributed as moderate, simultaneous bone fractures across all 9, two requiring hospitalization, with no member able to identify redistribution as the cause and all nine independently attributing their injuries to unrelated falls.
No member interviewed demonstrates awareness of the redistribution mechanism; the Watch's active and consistent recruitment culture is attributed by members to "just wanting more eyes on the street," and turnover is not unusually high, suggesting the required minimum buffer is being maintained through ordinary, non-anomalous social effort rather than any conscious understanding of its necessity.

ADDENDUM 4268-1: Foundation review of Watch recruitment materials identified a pattern of disproportionate outreach toward newly-arrived residents, recently widowed or divorced individuals, and households with no other local social ties -- a pattern consistent with, though not proven to be caused by, selection for members whose absence from the buffer pool (through death, relocation, or withdrawal) would be least likely to prompt external inquiry. Ethics Committee review of this pattern, and of whether continued non-disclosure constitutes complicity in it, remains open as of this filing.

SCP-4269.name: Continuous Watch
SCP-4269.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Millhaven Amateur Astronomers' Society (GoI-4269, 19 active members) is to be monitored but not disrupted. Foundation has quietly assumed indirect financial support of the Society's observatory (a converted grain silo on privately-owned land) through an anonymous "estate bequest" mechanism, ensuring equipment maintenance continues without requiring Society fundraising that might reduce available volunteer hours for shift coverage.
Three Foundation personnel maintain standing membership and participate in the rotation schedule under cover identities to provide contingency redundancy against unplanned shift gaps due to member illness, weather, or attrition. No gap exceeding four minutes has occurred since Foundation involvement began in 2016; the shortest gap prior to Foundation involvement with confirmed anomalous correlation was seven minutes (Incident 4269-2, 2009).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4269 refers to a bylaw-enforced practice of the Millhaven Amateur Astronomers' Society requiring continuous, unbroken overnight observation of the night sky above the town of Millhaven, maintained through rotating member shifts, without exception, since a date no current member or Society record can specify (Society founding documents reference the rule as already in place at incorporation, 1962).
Statistical review of Society shift logs against Millhaven town incident records (missing-persons reports, unexplained property damage, unattributed injury) identifies eleven historical incidents temporally correlated with gaps in observation coverage exceeding five minutes, all occurring prior to 2016. No incident with a comparable profile has occurred during any period of verified continuous coverage. The mechanism by which observation, specifically, prevents these incidents -- and the nature of what an incident represents or involves -- has not been determined; no anomalous entity, object, or process has been directly observed or recorded by Society equipment despite decades of continuous monitoring, including several nights during which recording equipment operated throughout a documented external incident elsewhere in town.
Society members enforce shift adherence with a rigor disproportionate to the organization's stated recreational purpose, including maintaining coverage through severe weather, using indoor infrared equipment when direct observation is obstructed by cloud cover, and immediate, unquestioned shift reassignment when a member reports incapacity. No member interviewed under cover pretext can articulate why unbroken coverage is considered essential; the standard response is a variation of "it's just what we do," delivered without apparent unease, alongside genuine inability to recall when or why the practice began.
Society membership recruitment specifically favors candidates capable of reliable overnight availability (retirees, night-shift workers, the chronically insomniac) and the Society has, without formal policy, never lapsed below eight active members since at least 1980.

ADDENDUM 4269-1: The most recent gap-correlated incident prior to Foundation involvement (Incident 4269-2, 2009, seven-minute gap due to member medical emergency) coincided with the disappearance of a Millhaven resident, recovered eleven days later approximately 40 km from town with no memory of the intervening period and non-standard frostbite injuries inconsistent with regional weather conditions for the date in question. The resident was not, and has never been, a Society member.

SCP-4270.name: One Table
SCP-4270.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Route 9 Cook-Off Circuit (GoI-4270, 26 active competing members across four county fair associations) requires no physical containment. Foundation maintains a dietary monitoring arrangement with a cover nutrition-research pretext ("Route 9 Longitudinal Health Study") under which members submit voluntary food diaries, permitting early detection of destabilizing dietary events.
Prospective new members joining or existing members withdrawing from the Circuit are associated with a documented 2-to-5-day period of collective metabolic disruption (see Description) and are to be flagged to Foundation medical liaison for monitoring of both the joining/departing individual and remaining Circuit members. No containment action beyond monitoring and, where consented to, post-transition nutritional support is currently authorized.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4270 refers to an anomalous shared physiological effect linking the 26 active members of the Route 9 Cook-Off Circuit, an informal regional competitive cooking and potluck association organized around participation in seasonal county fair cooking contests. Members' metabolic states -- caloric absorption, blood glucose regulation, subjective hunger and satiety, and measurable body weight -- are linked such that a significant deviation experienced by any one member (overeating, fasting, illness-related appetite loss) produces an inverse, compensating effect distributed across the remaining membership within approximately six hours, regardless of members' physical distance from one another.
In practice, this produces a stable collective equilibrium: individual members report weight and appetite fluctuations dramatically smaller than expected given their documented food intake, while the group's cooking competitions -- nominally judged on taste, presentation, and technique -- function, according to informal member consensus recovered through cover interviews, as an indirect and largely unspoken means of negotiating whose "turn" it is to carry a caloric surplus or deficit on behalf of the group, generally without members using this explicit language.
The mechanism responds measurably to membership changes. New members joining the Circuit are absorbed into the shared equilibrium gradually, with a 2-to-5-day adjustment period during which both the new member and 3-5 randomly affected existing members report acute, unexplained appetite disruption. Members attempting to leave the Circuit undergo a comparable, typically more severe disruption; one documented case (2021) involved a departing member requiring hospitalization for four days for what her discharge paperwork records as an unexplained metabolic event, before informally rejoining the Circuit, after which her symptoms resolved without further medical intervention within 36 hours.

ADDENDUM 4270-1: A current member, interviewed under the nutrition-study cover, has expressed a stated intention to relocate out of state in the coming year for employment reasons, which would constitute a permanent rather than temporary departure from the Circuit. No mechanism for permanent departure has yet been documented, as the sole prior attempt (above) ended in informal reintegration rather than confirmed exit. Foundation medical liaison has flagged this pending relocation for priority monitoring.

SCP-4271.name: Chapter and Verse
SCP-4271.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Millbrook Tuesday Book Club (GoI-4271, 7 current members) is to be maintained at its present reading pace under no circumstances faster than its current rate of approximately 1.5 pages per week. Foundation liaison, embedded as member "Carol Anders" since 2014, is tasked with actively discouraging any club proposal to increase reading pace, using standard social deflection (scheduling conflicts, requests for "more discussion time") rather than disclosed reasoning.
The book in circulation (a mass-market paperback, publication details withheld, currently on approximately page 267 of 312) is not to be destroyed, lost, or replaced with an alternate copy; two prior replacement attempts using textually identical reprinted copies (2016, 2019) both resulted in the club, without prompting, independently and correctly identifying the substitute as "not the same book" within one meeting and refusing to continue reading from it until the original was located and returned. The original copy shows physical degradation inconsistent with its handling history (a single reader's copy would not show this level of wear) but has not been permitted to leave club custody for forensic examination.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4271 refers to a synchronization effect linking the town of Millbrook (population 1,140) to the current reading position of the Millbrook Tuesday Book Club within a specific paperback novel, ostensibly an unremarkable mid-list literary work first published in 1987. Local conditions -- weather, minor civic events, the general texture of daily life described by residents in cover interviews as "normal" -- correspond, with a consistency verified across eleven years of Foundation observation, to events described in the chapter or chapters the Club is currently discussing.
Deviation from the Club's established pace produces measurable disruption. In the sole documented instance of accelerated reading (Incident 4271-4, 2017, in which the club read four chapters in a single week to accommodate a member's temporary absence), the town experienced a 72-hour period of subjective temporal distortion reported by numerous non-member residents as "the day that wouldn't end" or "losing an afternoon," corresponding to a chapter in which the novel's protagonist experiences a similarly extended, disorienting day. Slowing significantly below the established pace, conversely, produces stagnation effects (repeated identical days, described by residents as deja vu clusters) rather than distortion, leading the Club, apparently through trial rather than explicit understanding, to maintain a pace neither fast nor slow enough to produce disruption at scale.
The Club has read the same 312-page novel continuously since at least 1974 (earliest confirmed meeting minutes), a period during which, at current pace, it should have finished the book roughly six times over. Interview and archival research indicates the Club has never finished it, and no surviving member can recall having previously reached, or approached, its final pages until the current reading position -- the closest documented approach to the end in the group's known history.
Club members display no overt distress regarding their approach to the book's conclusion, though meeting frequency has, without formal decision, increased from monthly to weekly over the past eighteen months, and member "Carol Anders" (embedded) reports increasing tension and unusually long silences during discussion of the final chapters' content.

ADDENDUM 4271-1: Site Director review has authorized Agent Anders to introduce plausible delay tactics (health-related absences, disputes over discussion scheduling) sufficient to extend the Club's approach to the final page by an estimated minimum of eighteen months, pending further research into consequences of completion. No consensus exists among consulted researchers as to what "finishing" the book would produce, though all consulted agree that the question should not be tested experimentally while alternatives remain available.

SCP-4272.name: The Standby List
SCP-4272.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4272 designates a regional organ-transplant patient support group meeting biweekly at [REDACTED] Medical Center; membership is fluid, determined by ordinary enrollment on the region's transplant waiting list, and cannot be restricted by the Foundation without alerting hospital administration to Foundation interest. A Foundation-embedded medical social worker (cover: hospital-employed group facilitator) attends every session to informally monitor member sentiment and flag statements assessed as resentment or ill-wish directed at a specific higher-priority member (see Description). Flagged members are not to be removed from the group or the waiting list under any circumstances; Incident 4272-2 confirmed that involuntary removal does not prevent the correlated effect and may worsen it.

Transplant failure and rejection statistics for all group members are cross-referenced weekly against group attendance and session transcripts by an embedded biostatistician. No intervention beyond continued observation has been authorized pending Ethics Committee review of Addendum 4272-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4272 refers to a documented statistical anomaly among members of a specific, otherwise unremarkable organ-transplant patient support group of approximately 20-30 rotating members. Foundation involvement began after a hospital-internal audit, later obtained by an embedded asset, flagged an implausibly high correlation between transplant rejection or graft failure in one patient and a documented instance, within the preceding 72 hours, of a same-group member privately expressing resentment, envy, or a wish for ill fortune toward that patient — typically over relative position on the regional waiting list, a scarce and emotionally fraught resource.

Across 61 reviewed cases spanning four years of group membership, transplant failure or serious post-operative complication occurred in the resented member within 72 hours of a documented ill-wish in 44 instances (72%), a rate Foundation statisticians assess as categorically inconsistent with baseline transplant failure rates for the relevant procedures and patient risk profiles. The effect does not require the ill-wish to be spoken aloud, confronted, or even consciously acknowledged by the wishing member; 11 of the 44 confirmed instances were recovered only from private journals, therapy notes, or, in three cases, an embedded facilitator's own session observations of a member's unspoken but visibly hostile reaction to another's good news.

No mechanism has been identified. The wishing member reports no sense of causing or intending the outcome, and in every interviewed case has responded to being informed of the correlation (a disclosure the Foundation does not make, but which occurred once, see Addendum) with acute, apparently genuine distress rather than any satisfaction. The correlation holds only within the group itself; ill-wishes directed at non-members, and ill-wishes by non-members directed at group members, show no elevated correlation with negative outcomes.

ADDENDUM 4272-1: A minority position within the Ethics Committee has argued SCP-4272 should be reclassified Safe on grounds that no member has been shown to act with intent, and that continued covert observation without intervention constitutes the Foundation passively permitting harm it could plausibly investigate further. The majority position holds that any intervention (dissolving the group, informing members, isolating high-risk patients) has not been shown to reduce rather than redistribute the effect, and that Incident 4272-2 — in which one member's request for transfer to a different support group was followed by a transplant failure in a member of her *new* group within 72 hours, with no prior contact between the two women — suggests the anomaly may not be bound to this specific group's membership roster at all, but to something about the list itself. This finding remains under active review and has not been disclosed to any member.

SCP-4273.name: The Annotating Salve
SCP-4273.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 400 mL of SCP-4273 is stored in three sealed borosilicate jars within a standard chemical locker at Site-19, Wing C. Withdrawal for testing requires sign-off from two Level 3 personnel and a written justification limited to a single application per test. Application of SCP-4273 to Foundation personnel is currently suspended pending review of Incident 4273-7 (see Addendum). Any wound treated with SCP-4273 outside of sanctioned testing is to be photographed in full before the resulting scar tissue completes formation (72-96 hours post-application) and the subject debriefed by a psychologist cleared for anomalous-linguistic material.

Stock quantities are not to be allowed to fall below 150 mL. Synthesis of SCP-4273 has not been achieved; the substance's origin (a defunct wound-care clinic in Adapazarı, decommissioned 2003) has yielded no further samples on three separate site surveys.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4273 is a translucent, faintly amber gel with the viscosity and inert chemical profile of a standard petroleum-based wound dressing. It carries no anomalous properties under any standard assay (spectroscopy, chromatography, microbial culture) and does not react with skin, blood, or common antiseptics.

When applied to an open wound in humans, SCP-4273 accelerates closure to within 24-48 hours regardless of wound size, with no scarring contracture, no infection risk observed in 61 documented applications, and no anomalous effect on the subject's health otherwise. The anomaly appears exclusively in the resulting scar tissue, which does not form as expected (a raised or flattened mass of collagen) but as a continuous line of raised tissue resembling handwritten script, in a hand not belonging to the subject, arranged as though written across the wound site regardless of its shape or orientation.

The script is legible in roughly 40% of cases. Transcribed text has, to date, never been threatening, obscene, or grammatically incoherent. It is, instead, unnervingly mundane: shopping lists, half-remembered song lyrics, appointment times, single declarative sentences ("The kettle was already on the stove.", "She did not tell him about the letter."). Cross-referencing with subject interviews has connected roughly one in six transcriptions to a specific memory, document, or conversation the subject could identify - but in eleven cases, the connected event had not yet occurred at the time of application, and occurred within the following month.

No transcription has repeated across subjects. No subject has reported being able to consciously influence the resulting text.

ADDENDUM 4273-7: On [DATE REDACTED], Researcher Öztürk sustained a minor laceration during sample handling and was treated with SCP-4273 under standing protocol for accidental exposure. The resulting scar read, in full: "Tell them it was already lit before I opened the door." Site-19's evening shift experienced an electrical fire in Storage Wing C four days later, point of origin undetermined, extinguished without injury. Researcher Öztürk has been reassigned to non-handling duties pending further review. She has declined further debriefing on the incident.

SCP-4274.name: The Convergent Beverage
SCP-4274.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining 297 bottles of SCP-4274 are stored upright, unrefrigerated, in a humidity-controlled cabinet at Site-19, Storage Bay 4. Each bottle is individually logged by serial number on the base cap. Testing requires approval from the Site Ethics Committee and participation of no more than two subjects per trial, both volunteers or D-Class briefed on the procedure. SCP-4274 is not to be tested on minors under any circumstance. Empty bottles are to be retained rather than discarded, as preliminary analysis suggests the anomalous property may reside in trace residue rather than the liquid itself; three "empty" bottles have tested positive for the effect when refilled with inert water.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4274 refers to a specific bottling run (lot code MVS-0619, approximately 8,000 units) of an orange-flavored carbonated soft drink produced under the now-defunct regional brand "Maviş," last distributed in [REGION REDACTED] in 1998. Chemical analysis shows nothing distinguishing SCP-4274 from any other bottle of the same product; sugar content, carbonation, and flavoring are within expected commercial tolerances.

The anomalous effect manifests only when exactly two individuals each consume SCP-4274 from separate bottles of the affected lot within the same ten-minute window and within approximately three meters of one another. Beginning 40-90 seconds after the second subject's first swallow, both subjects report a period of between 90 and 180 seconds during which they perceive fragments of the other subject's immediate sensory input and short-term recall, overlaid on their own. Subjects consistently describe the experience as intrusive rather than communicative - neither party can direct or query the other's perceptions, and both report a lingering difficulty afterward in determining which memories from the window were originally their own.

The effect does not occur with one subject alone, does not scale beyond two subjects (a three-subject trial produced no anomalous effect in any participant), and has not been reproduced using bottles from any other lot, including lots produced at the same facility on adjacent dates.
