Partial retrograde amnesia is common following exposure; subjects reliably recall that an exchange occurred but struggle to articulate its content beyond vague sensory description ("cold," "someone else's headache," "the taste of a cigarette I never had"). No subject has reported lasting harm. Four subjects, unprompted, have described the experience as something they would seek out again.

ADDENDUM: SCP-4274 came to Foundation attention after two civilian minors in [REDACTED] shared a bottle each from a private collection inherited from a relative; one subject subsequently contacted local authorities with detailed, accurate knowledge of domestic abuse occurring in the other subject's household, information the first subject could not otherwise have possessed. Local intervention followed before Foundation agents secured the remaining stock. The relative who originally owned the collection is deceased and left no records explaining its acquisition or storage.

SCP-4275.name: Unworn Polish
SCP-4275.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 4 kg of SCP-4275 is stored as a sealed powder in a single lead-lined tin within Site-19's Secure Materials Vault. Personnel handling SCP-4275 must wear nitrile gloves and avoid any use of the substance on Foundation records, currency, or identifying materials of any kind; three requests for testing on redacted document paper have been denied on standing policy. All objects treated with SCP-4275 during testing are to be photographed, weighed, and cross-referenced against any existing database entries both before and no less than 72 hours after treatment, when secondary effects typically stabilize.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4275 is a fine, grey-white abrasive powder resembling commercial metal polish, odorless and chemically unremarkable under standard analysis (primarily calcium carbonate and an unidentified 6% mineral fraction). It was recovered from an estate sale in [REDACTED] alongside a restoration workshop's inventory, none of which have shown similar properties.

When applied to any solid object and buffed by hand for approximately three minutes, SCP-4275 removes surface wear, oxidation, and patina, restoring a "new" or "unworn" appearance regardless of the object's actual age or material. This aspect of the effect is consistent with its apparent intended use as a restoration compound and has no anomalous chemical signature.

The anomalous property lies in a secondary effect first identified in Test 4275-12. Any identifying mark removed by the polishing process - a serial number, an engraving, an owner's inscription, forensic tool marks, accumulated fingerprint residue - does not merely vanish from the object. Within 24 to 72 hours, external records referencing that mark (databases, paper files, photographs held in separate locations, in one case a museum's own printed catalogue) update to reflect the object's new, unmarked state, without any human intervention documented or admitted to by record custodians. The object's history, so far as any external record is concerned, comes to match its new physical condition. Interviews with custodians of altered records have found no anomaly in their own recollection of the update process; several insist the records were "always" as they now appear.

Foundation testing has confirmed this effect on library catalog cards, a hospital's patient equipment log, and - in a single sanctioned test - a firearm's ballistic registration, an experiment not repeated. The mechanism by which non-adjacent, non-networked records update in tandem remains unexplained.

ADDENDUM: A bronze sculpture, reported stolen from a private gallery in 2019, was recovered by Foundation agents in the possession of an individual who produced a complete, internally consistent provenance for the piece dating back three decades, none of which existed in any record prior to the theft. SCP-4275 residue was found on the sculpture's base. The individual has been released pending further investigation; no charges have been filed, as no record currently supports that a theft occurred.

SCP-4276.name: The Forgetting Weave
SCP-4276.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4276, a single bolt of woven cloth approximately 4.2 by 1.8 meters, is stored folded inside a sealed cedar chest in Site-19's Textile Containment Locker. The chest is not to be opened except for approved testing, and SCP-4276 is never to be left in contact with sleeping personnel outside of a monitored trial. Any Foundation-owned documents, photographs, or recordings referencing a test subject's family members are to be digitally backed up prior to testing and stored off-site, as physical copies retained on-site have shown degradation consistent with SCP-4276's secondary effect (see below).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4276 is a heavy, tightly woven blanket-sized cloth of a consistent grey-blue color, of unknown fiber composition; standard textile analysis returns results consistent with wool but the individual fibers do not burn, dissolve in acid, or respond to any dye. SCP-4276 maintains a constant surface temperature of approximately 21°C regardless of ambient conditions, a property that persists even when the cloth is submerged in liquid or held in a vacuum chamber.

Any individual who sleeps beneath SCP-4276 for a continuous period of six hours or more will, upon waking, have lost all conscious and autobiographical memory of one specific other living person, invariably a blood relative. The forgotten individual is never chosen by the sleeper; interviews conducted before and after exposure show sleepers cannot identify who has been "selected" from their family in advance, and several have initially denied having any relative matching the one they have in fact forgotten, until presented with prior interview transcripts.

The forgetting is total with respect to the sleeper's own recollection but does not extend to other people's memories of the same relative, nor does it erase the forgotten individual from Foundation records or non-physical (digital) documentation. It does, however, cause measurable degradation - fading ink, warping photographic paper, static-obscured audio - in any physical document held by the sleeper personally that references the forgotten relative, an effect that does not occur in documents held elsewhere, including duplicates.

Across three generations of the same family (see Addendum), repeated exposure to SCP-4276 by different members has resulted in the cumulative, family-wide forgetting of a single ancestor, a woman believed by genealogical record to have died in 1961, whose name no surviving family member can now produce despite her continued presence in municipal birth and death registries obtained independently by Foundation researchers.

ADDENDUM: SCP-4276 was surrendered to the Foundation by the Kayabaşı family of [LOCATION REDACTED], who described it as an "inherited blanket" used by the household's eldest member during periods of grief, understood within the family to "take the worst of it away." Three living family members, when shown the municipal record naming the forgotten ancestor, expressed no recognition and mild distress at being unable to feel anything about a name attached, per the record, to a woman who raised two of their parents.

SCP-4277.name: The Persistent Flavor Salt
SCP-4277.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The 900 g of SCP-4277 recovered to date is stored in a single airtight glass container within Site-19's Standard Chemical Storage, segregated from all consumable stock. Testing requires the subject to abstain from any food, drink, gum, or oral medication for a minimum of four hours prior, verified by observation. No more than 0.5 g of SCP-4277 is to be dissolved per test; higher concentrations have not been approved following Incident 4277-3.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4277 is a fine, white crystalline solid, chemically consistent with sodium chloride under mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction, and taste (by three willing researchers, prior to the substance's anomalous properties being identified). It was recovered from the kitchen of a closed restaurant in [LOCATION REDACTED], found in an unlabeled tin among ordinary pantry salt.

When dissolved in any potable liquid at a concentration of 0.05% or greater, SCP-4277 does not impart a salty or otherwise identifiable taste of its own. Instead, the liquid takes on the flavor most recently tasted by the person about to drink it, regardless of that flavor's relationship to the liquid's actual composition. A subject who has just eaten citrus will perceive plain water treated with SCP-4277 as citrus-flavored; a subject who has eaten nothing in the prior test window perceives no flavor override and reports the liquid's true taste.

The effect is entirely subjective to the drinker; multiple subjects drinking from the same treated glass in sequence, having eaten different things beforehand, report different and mutually exclusive flavors from an identical sample. The liquid's actual chemical composition, confirmed by lab analysis before and after each test, does not change.

The override does not fade with time in the ordinary sense; subjects report the imprinted flavor at full intensity regardless of how long ago they last ate, provided no further food or drink has been consumed. The effect resets only after actual consumption of a new food or beverage, at which point that new flavor becomes what the treated liquid reproduces on the next exposure.

Fourteen of thirty-one test subjects have, at some point, reported a flavor they could not attribute to any recent meal - most commonly described as "milk, but wrong," "something sweet I don't want," or, in four cases, independently and without prompting, "the inside of my mouth before I had teeth." No subject has been able to explain these reports further, and follow-up interviews have not reproduced them on demand. Subjects reporting this variant flavor have shown no measurable difference in bloodwork, recent diet, or psychological evaluation from those who have not.

ADDENDUM 4277-3: A test using 1.2 g of SCP-4277 (above the currently approved maximum) resulted in the subject reporting the imprinted flavor continuously for eleven days regardless of subsequent food intake, describing it throughout as "a taste I had before I could talk about tastes." The subject's diet and food preference did not change during this period. The flavor override resolved without intervention on the twelfth day. The subject has requested not to participate in further SCP-4277 testing.

SCP-4278.name: The Sequence-Breaking Gas
SCP-4278.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4278 originates from a fissure approximately 40 cm in width located at coordinates [REDACTED] beneath Sub-Site 4278, a purpose-built underground facility disguised as a seismological monitoring station. The fissure cannot be sealed; three attempts (concrete, expanding foam, welded steel plate) have each failed within 96 hours, the sealing material found breached from within without any mechanical evidence of the breach. Current procedure maintains a continuous negative-pressure ventilation system drawing SCP-4278 to a scrubbing unit before atmospheric release at a rate calculated to prevent ambient concentration in occupied areas from exceeding 0.02%. Personnel entering the fissure chamber must use closed-circuit breathing apparatus; unprotected exposure of any duration is to be logged as an incident.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4278 is a colorless, odorless gas, chemically indistinguishable from ambient atmospheric nitrogen under standard analysis. Its anomalous property manifests exclusively in humans (and, in limited testing, has not manifested in other language-using test subjects) who inhale it at concentrations above approximately 0.01%.

Affected individuals continue to speak in grammatically well-formed sentences of their native or preferred language, and continue to describe real events using accurate, verifiable content. What changes is the temporal placement of that content relative to when it is spoken. A subject at low exposure will, for instance, describe an object falling from a shelf between one and four seconds before it does so, in the same tone and with the same apparent spontaneity as an ordinary remark, then a moment later describe, as though it had only just happened, something that occurred several seconds prior. Subjects do not report any subjective sense of foreknowledge; they experience their own speech as commentary on the present, and are consistently startled or unsettled, upon review of recordings, to learn what they said and when.

The degree of temporal displacement scales with both concentration and duration of exposure. At the facility's ambient trace levels, displacement rarely exceeds five seconds in either direction. Subjects exposed directly at the fissure mouth for periods exceeding ninety seconds have described events hours in advance of their occurrence, with corresponding degradation in their ability to describe anything at all from their actual present - such subjects report a sensation of "talking into a delay" and, in two cases, have been unable to produce any speech synchronized with present events for over six hours post-exposure, communicating only in statements later confirmed to be accurate descriptions of moments still to come.

No subject has been able to consciously query or direct the temporal placement of their own speech, and no subject exposed at high concentration has described events more than approximately 11 hours in advance, a ceiling that has held across 22 trials without explanation.

ADDENDUM: Seismic monitoring of the fissure recorded a 3 mm widening over the past eighteen months, within instrument tolerance but trending consistently in one direction across all readings. No corresponding increase in gas output has been detected. The facility's actual seismological cover function has, on two occasions, produced data that later proved accurate for regional tremors not yet recorded by any external monitoring station at time of transmission.

SCP-4279.name: The Thirty-Year Developer
SCP-4279.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The 6 remaining bottles of SCP-4279 (total volume 1.4 L) are stored in a lightproof case within Site-19's photochemical stores, separate from standard developing chemicals to prevent accidental cross-use. Development using SCP-4279 requires authorization from a Level 3 researcher and is logged with the exact date and time of development, as this - rather than the date the photograph was taken - determines the resulting image's temporal reference point (see Description). Requests to use SCP-4279 to image any active Foundation site are subject to additional review, as three prior such tests remain unresolved (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4279 refers to a set of glass bottles of black-and-white photographic developing fluid, recovered from an abandoned studio in [LOCATION REDACTED] whose proprietor's whereabouts are unknown. The bottles are labeled by hand, in ink, with the single word "Geç" ("late," in the sense of delayed rather than deceased). Chemical composition is broadly consistent with a standard silver halide developer of a type commercially available prior to 1970, with an unidentified 2% additive.

When used to develop correctly exposed black-and-white film of any real-world location, SCP-4279 does not produce an image of the location as it appeared at the time of exposure. Instead, it produces an accurate photographic image of that same location as it will appear exactly thirty years after the date of development - not the date the photograph was taken. Redeveloping a duplicate negative from the same original exposure, on a different date, produces a different image, correctly offset thirty years from its own (later) development date. The same negative is not fixed to a single future; it is fixed to an interval from whenever SCP-4279 is used on it.

Resulting images have proven consistently accurate where independently verifiable: a 1994 test photograph of a since-demolished Ankara apartment building, developed in 1996, correctly depicted the parking structure that replaced it in 2026. No image produced by SCP-4279, across 40 documented tests, has ever contained a human figure, vehicle in motion, animal, or any other transient subject, even when the original exposure captured one prominently in frame. Foundation photo analysts have not identified any technical mechanism (double exposure, dodging, physical obstruction) that would account for this omission.

ADDENDUM: On [DATE REDACTED], a research team developed an SCP-4279 negative taken of Site-19's primary courtyard, intending only to confirm the substance's range was not limited to civilian locations. The resulting image depicted open, uncultivated grassland with no structures, roads, or fencing of any kind, under what analysts assess to be daylight conditions consistent with late spring. Geographic features matching the surrounding terrain (a distinctive ridge line, visible in both the original and developed image) confirm the location is correct. The photograph has been sealed pending review by O5 Command. No further tests targeting active Foundation sites have been approved.

SCP-4280.name: The Listening Alloy
SCP-4280.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All 34 recovered samples of SCP-4280 (totaling 11 kg, primarily as wire and sheet fragments) are stored in individual foam-lined cases in Site-19's Acoustics Lab, physically separated by a minimum of two meters to limit cross-sample interference during testing. A directional microphone array records continuously in the storage room at all times; playback events, which occur without external stimulus on an unpredictable schedule (see Description), are to be captured in full and transcribed by on-duty personnel regardless of shift hour.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4280 is a dull grey metallic alloy of unknown composition, recovered as electrical wiring fragments during the demolition of an apartment building in [LOCATION REDACTED] constructed in 1958. Standard assay identifies aluminum, copper, and an unidentified 9% fraction resistant to spectroscopic analysis. Despite its appearance and installation context, SCP-4280 does not conduct electrical current under any tested voltage.

SCP-4280 instead conducts and appears to indefinitely retain acoustic vibration, in a manner functionally analogous to analog sound recording, though no mechanism for this has been identified - the alloy shows no groove, magnetic domain, or other structure under electron microscopy that would account for stored information. At unpredictable intervals, averaging roughly once every 40 hours per sample but not observed to follow any pattern tied to time, temperature, humidity, or handling, a sample of SCP-4280 will audibly reproduce a sound event, typically 10 to 90 seconds in length, at a volume roughly equivalent to the original recorded sound.

Reproduced audio has never matched any sound Foundation staff are aware of having occurred near the sample during containment. Content ranges from mundane domestic noise (dishware, a radio program later confirmed to have aired the same year the building was constructed) to fragments of conversation in Turkish, and in nine cases, in a language Foundation linguists have been unable to identify or match to any known language, living or dead.

Critically, when two or more samples of SCP-4280 are stored in separate, acoustically isolated locations with no possibility of physical or electromagnetic contact, they have on eleven occasions produced the same audio event within the same 24-hour window, word-for-word identical where speech is involved. This has held true even for samples held at Foundation sites over 1,000 km apart. No explanation for this synchronization has been established, and it has not been possible to predict which sample will "select" a given recording or when.

ADDENDUM: A playback event on [DATE REDACTED], captured simultaneously by two samples held in separate secure storage rooms, reproduced a conversation in accented English discussing "the numbers Öztürk sent" and "keeping it out of the log until after the site review" - phrasing which two independent analysts flagged as consistent in structure and cadence with internal Foundation communications. No corresponding conversation has been located in any Foundation record, transcript, or personnel statement. The matter has been referred to Internal Security. Öztürk is a common Turkish surname; six Foundation personnel at Site-19 currently hold it.

SCP-4281.name: The Transferring Anesthetic
SCP-4281.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The 40 remaining ampoules of SCP-4281 (2 mL each) are stored under standard medical refrigeration in a locked case within Site-19's Medical Wing, accessible only to Level 4 medical staff with the personal authorization of the Site Director for each individual use. SCP-4281 is not to be administered to any patient except where conventional anesthesia is contraindicated and death or permanent injury is otherwise imminent. Every administration requires prior sign-off from at least one O5 Council member or their designated proxy, logged with patient identity, dosage, and medical justification. Use of SCP-4281 outside these conditions is grounds for immediate termination of clearance.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4281 is a clear, faintly viscous injectable liquid recovered from the dispensary of a shuttered private clinic in [LOCATION REDACTED], alongside patient records indicating its use in at least 60 documented procedures between 1988 and 1994 under the clinic's own name for it, "anestezi-D." No formal chemical patent or manufacturing record has been located.

When administered intravenously, SCP-4281 produces complete, immediate elimination of all physical pain in the recipient for a duration proportional to dosage (approximately 40 minutes per 2 mL ampoule), with no sedative, motor, or cognitive impairment - recipients remain fully alert and have undergone documented surgical procedures, including two amputations, reporting zero pain throughout.

The pain is not eliminated. Foundation monitoring, cross-referenced against hospital admission data in the surrounding region following each administration, has identified a statistically significant spike in unexplained acute pain presentations - chest pain, migraine-level headache, abdominal pain - among individuals with no connection to the treated patient, occurring within minutes of each SCP-4281 administration and lasting for a duration matching the treated patient's dose. These individuals report pain onset "for no reason," consistent in character and apparent severity with the procedure the treated patient underwent, without anesthesia of their own.

The Foundation has been unable to identify any pattern determining which individual receives the displaced pain - recipients identified after the fact share no geographic proximity to the treated patient, no medical history, no traceable connection. Recipients cannot be warned, selected against, or compensated, as they are identified only retroactively through hospital record correlation, and even then only in a minority of cases; the true total number of pain recipients per administration is unknown, and the Foundation currently assumes displacement is distributed among multiple unwitting recipients per dose rather than a single individual, though this has not been confirmed.

ADDENDUM: Three deaths in the [REGION REDACTED] area, each involving an individual with a pre-existing cardiac condition found collapsed with no external injury, have been statistically correlated (p < 0.01) with the timing of SCP-4281 administrations at Site-19, though no direct causal mechanism has been established and no connection between the deceased and any Foundation patient has been found. The O5 Council has not suspended SCP-4281's approved use.

SCP-4282.name: The Deepening Admixture
SCP-4282.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The remaining stock of SCP-4282, approximately 210 kg of grey powder additive, is stored in sealed drums at Site-19's Secure Materials Vault and is not to be mixed with any cement, mortar, or concrete under any circumstances outside of sanctioned, single-batch laboratory testing capped at 500 g per test. The one known standing structure built with SCP-4282-treated concrete, a four-story apartment block in [LOCATION REDACTED] acquired by the Foundation under civil pretext in 2019 and redesignated Containment Site-4282, is to be surveyed by laser interior mapping on a weekly basis, with results compared against the building's original 1974 architectural plans. Personnel entering rooms not present on the original plans must operate in pairs, maintain constant radio contact, and are not to proceed more than 15 meters from the last mapped doorway.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4282 is a fine grey powder, chemically similar to standard fly-ash concrete admixture, identified through purchasing records recovered from a defunct construction supply company that operated in [LOCATION REDACTED] between 1971 and 1979. Company records show SCP-4282 was sold as a proprietary "expansion-reducing" additive; its actual effect is the inverse.

Any concrete structure poured using SCP-4282-treated material will, beginning approximately 18 months after curing, develop additional interior floor area not reflected in the structure's exterior dimensions. Expansion is initially slow, on the order of 2-4 cm of additional interior depth per year in affected rooms, and is not consciously noticed by long-term occupants; interviews with residents of Containment Site-4282 prior to Foundation acquisition found near-universal difficulty recalling the layout of their own homes accurately, despite no reported disorientation in daily use.

Expansion accelerates over time and eventually manifests as entirely new rooms accessible from existing doorways, closets, or, in four documented cases, blank interior walls that were not previously understood to be doors. New rooms are structurally consistent with the building's existing materials and style. Approximately 60% are found empty. The remainder contain furnishings or objects that are near-exact but degraded duplicates of items in adjacent, "original" rooms - a duplicate armchair with the same upholstery pattern but represented as though decades older, a duplicate kitchen table set with place settings for a number of occupants exceeding the room's original household.

The rate of new room formation at Containment Site-4282 has increased in each of the past three years. Total mapped interior floor area, as of the most recent survey, exceeds the building's exterior footprint by a factor of approximately 6.4, with no corresponding increase in the building's exterior dimensions, weight (confirmed by foundation load-bearing analysis), or visible structural stress.

ADDENDUM: During a routine mapping survey on [DATE REDACTED], Site-4282 personnel discovered, in a previously unmapped room approximately 40 meters from the building's exterior wall by interior measurement, signs of recent human habitation - bedding, food waste less than a week old, and a set of six additional degraded duplicate rooms branching further inward. No individual has been located. Site-4282's exterior perimeter shows no breach. The Foundation has not determined how, or whether, anyone could have entered.

SCP-4283.name: The Remembered Afternoon
SCP-4283.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The approximately 3.1 kg of SCP-4283 held by the Foundation is stored in a single sealed ceramic jar within Site-19's Standard Chemical Storage. Consumption for testing requires Ethics Committee approval and is limited to volunteer or briefed D-Class subjects; no subject may be dosed more than twice, given evidence of cumulative effect (see Description). All subjects are to undergo a baseline autobiographical memory interview before dosing and follow-up interviews at 24 hours, one week, and one month post-exposure.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4283 is a dark amber, viscous, honey-like substance of plant or possibly apicultural origin, recovered in small quantities from three unrelated sources: a market stall in [LOCATION REDACTED] selling it as a folk remedy for "restlessness," a private apiary whose owner could not explain its presence among ordinary honeycomb, and, in one case, a sealed jar found buried beneath a home under demolition. Standard chemical analysis identifies primarily fructose and glucose consistent with honey, with an unidentified 4% organic fraction.

Ingestion of even a small quantity (1 mL or greater) of SCP-4283 reliably produces, within 10-20 minutes, a vivid and highly detailed autobiographical memory of a single specific afternoon: a lakeside gathering, weather described consistently as warm with intermittent cloud cover, attended by several unnamed others, centered on a red plaid thermos and the sound of someone's laughter carried across water. Subjects experience this as a genuine personal memory, indistinguishable in subjective quality from verified recollections, and consistently express surprise or distress upon being informed - accurately, and independently confirmed in all 44 documented cases - that no subject has ever actually attended such an event, and that the described afternoon does not correspond to any location, date, or gathering any subject can independently verify.

Cross-referencing subject accounts has confirmed the memory is identical in specific, granular detail across unrelated subjects with no contact with one another, down to incidental elements (the thermos's plaid pattern, the exact number of birds visible overhead) that should not be reproducible from a shared cultural memory or coincidence. No subject has been able to identify who else was present in the memory or produce a face for any of them.

Repeated dosing increases the memory's vividness and its resistance to subjects' conscious effort to disbelieve it; two subjects given a second dose have subsequently reported difficulty distinguishing the false afternoon from their genuine childhood memories in casual recall, though formal testing still allows them to correctly identify it as false when directly questioned.

ADDENDUM: Beginning with the most recent batch of test subjects, an element not previously reported by any subject in 31 prior trials has appeared independently and without prompting in five consecutive accounts: a figure standing at the tree line at the edge of the described lake, motionless, whose presence subjects describe as having "always" been part of the memory despite no such detail appearing in any interview transcript prior to this batch. Subjects have not been able to describe the figure beyond its position and stillness. Testing with SCP-4283 has been suspended pending review.

SCP-4284.name: The Process Suppressant
SCP-4284.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4284 is maintained as a designated Foundation emergency response asset rather than a contained anomaly. 212 pressurized canisters (each holding 6 L of liquefied SCP-4284) are installed in emergency dispersal units at 14 Foundation sites, integrated with fire suppression and containment-breach response systems. Deployment authorization below Site Director level requires confirmation that conventional suppression or amnesticization is inadequate to the situation. All personnel present during a dispersal event are to be pulled from active duty for no less than 72 hours afterward and evaluated for cognitive continuity (see Description). Non-Foundation civilians exposed during a dispersal event require standard Class-B amnestic administration following recovery, as SCP-4284 exposure alone does not remove existing long-term memory of the anomaly.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4284 is a colorless, faintly cold gas developed by Foundation chemical engineering following analysis of an unrelated anomalous sample (see Document 4284-A, restricted), currently synthesized and maintained under controlled Foundation production. When dispersed, SCP-4284 forms a stable, slow-dissipating cloud within which any ongoing physical, chemical, or biological process is measurably slowed or entirely halted for the cloud's duration, typically 8 to 20 minutes depending on dispersal volume and ambient airflow.

Within an active SCP-4284 cloud, combustion is extinguished and cannot be reignited by external ignition source; chemical reactions in progress (including several anomalous corrosive and reactive effects tested under containment) measurably slow or stop; biological growth and decay processes, including wound infection, tissue necrosis, and cellular division, pause without apparent harm to the organism, resuming at typical rates upon the cloud's dissipation.

In humans, exposure additionally produces a temporary, complete suspension of new long-term memory formation for the duration of exposure, functionally equivalent to profound anterograde amnesia, while leaving reflexes, existing memory, language comprehension, and the ability to follow simple verbal instruction intact. Exposed individuals can be directed to evacuate, assist, or otherwise act appropriately during an incident, but retain no memory of the event itself upon the cloud's dissipation and their cognition's return to baseline, typically within 90 seconds of clearing the affected area.

This property has made SCP-4284 a standard tool in incident response where conventional amnesticization would be impractical mid-event - the gas is dispersed at the point of an anomalous breach, personnel and bystanders act on instruction to contain or evacuate, and no witness retains memory of the anomalous elements observed during the response, without requiring post-incident chemical amnesticization for minor exposures.

Several anomalous objects and entities whose active properties depend on a continuous internal or environmental process (including at least two self-propagating memetic effects and one corrosive entity, cross-referenced under separate files) have been successfully arrested mid-event using SCP-4284, with the paused process resuming at the point it left off once the gas dissipated, rather than restarting or being permanently halted. This has proven useful for controlled re-initiation under laboratory conditions but has also meant SCP-4284 functions as a delay rather than a cure in all documented cases to date.

ADDENDUM: Personnel exposed to SCP-4284 on more than four occasions within a calendar year show, on standard cognitive assessment, a mild but consistent deficit in memory consolidation persisting outside of exposure events, not present in personnel exposed three or fewer times. The deficit has not progressed further with continued exposure in the six cases tracked longitudinally, but has also not reversed. Affected personnel remain cleared for active duty. The mechanism is not understood.

SCP-4285.name: Tomorrow's Other Weather
SCP-4285.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4285 is contained through the maintenance of Relay Post 4285, a shielded antenna array and staffed receiving station disguised as a defunct AM transmitter tower, located outside [REDACTED], which absorbs and records the nightly broadcast before it can propagate beyond a 4-kilometer radius. Site security confirms no unauthorized civilian receiver has entered this radius since containment began. Two on-duty researchers are assigned nightly to log the broadcast under standard transcription protocol 4285-B; personnel are rotated every 30 days to limit cumulative exposure to the forecasts' content (see Addendum). Individuals named in a broadcast who reside within the affected radius are to be monitored discreetly by field agents posing as community volunteers or social workers, but are not to be informed of the broadcast's existence or contents under any circumstance. Any recorded forecast concerning a Foundation staff member must be reported immediately to the Site Director, and the staff member reassigned off-duty for the predicted period.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4285 is a radio broadcast transmitted nightly at 22:50 local time for 3-5 minutes on 1030 kHz, a frequency without a licensed broadcaster in the region since 1987. The broadcast consists of a single male voice, identified through voiceprint analysis as consistent with radio announcer Warren W. Voss (1922-1989, deceased), delivering what is structured as a standard regional weather forecast but which describes interpersonal, emotional, or domestic events using meteorological terminology, e.g., "a low-pressure system of resentment is building over the Alcott residence on Birch Street; residents should expect scattered raised voices by Thursday evening, clearing by Friday." Broadcasts name between one and six individuals or households per night by full name and, in approximately 60% of cases, street address.

Cross-referencing of 1,340 archived forecasts against subsequent field verification, conducted without informing subjects, indicates the described event occurs, matching the forecast's severity and approximate timing, in 91.7% of cases where the named individual's routine was not otherwise disrupted. When a named individual's routine is altered by unrelated circumstance (illness, travel, unconnected police involvement, etc.), the forecast event fails to occur in 89% of these cases; however, a different adverse interpersonal event of comparable emotional severity occurs to the same individual within 96 hours in 71% of these cases. Foundation analysts refer to this substitute event informally as a "backdoor front." No method of preventing both the forecast event and its substitute has yet been identified.

ADDENDUM 4285-1: On [DATE], Researcher [REDACTED], while transcribing, heard her own name and address in the broadcast ("a sharp gust of an old apology, unsent, will finally reach Dr. [REDACTED] this Sunday"). Per protocol she was reassigned and confined to Site grounds through the following Monday. On Sunday, she received a phone call from her estranged father, who apologized for an incident in [REDACTED]. She reported the conversation as "correct in every particular I hadn't told anyone here." She has since submitted three requests for permanent reassignment away from SCP-4285 transcription duty; all have been denied pending further study of whether personnel exposure affects broadcast accuracy. No test has yet been approved to determine how SCP-4285 obtains information about individuals who have never been within its broadcast radius, as in Researcher [REDACTED]'s case, whose father resides 340 km away.

SCP-4286.name: The Inheritance Pattern
SCP-4286.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The original instance of SCP-4286, a hand-written pattern on a 10x15 cm index card, is stored in a standard document safe at Site-77. Fourteen confirmed transcribed copies, each independently capable of producing the anomalous effect, have been recovered from private knitting circles, online pattern-sharing forums, and secondhand pattern books between 1994 and the present; recovery is ongoing via automated scraping of craft forums for the phrase "the one that gives you dreams," a nickname the pattern has acquired independently among civilian knitters. All recovered copies are stored separately to prevent further hand-transcription. Personnel are prohibited from copying SCP-4286 by hand under any circumstance; mechanical reproduction (photocopying, scanning, photographing) reliably yields a blank or illegible image and is the approved method for study copies. Completed garments knitted from SCP-4286 are also to be contained and are not to be worn by personnel for longer than the 40-minute intervals required for testing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4286 is a knitting pattern of unremarkable design, adaptable to scarves, sweaters, blankets, and similar items depending on the knitter's chosen yarn and needle gauge; no specific finished shape is required for the anomalous property to manifest. Any garment completed by following the pattern, once worn by any person for a cumulative six hours (not necessarily by the original knitter, and not necessarily contiguous), causes the wearer to experience a single vivid dream during their next sleep cycle. The dream's content consistently reflects an emotional state, memory, or private thought the knitter was experiencing during the specific hours in which they worked on the garment, regardless of whether the knitter ever articulated or was consciously aware of that content. Wearers have reported dreams matching events later confirmed to have happened to the knitter but which the knitter stated they had never disclosed to anyone.

The effect requires no proximity or relationship between knitter and wearer; garments sold, gifted, or resold at thrift stores have transmitted dreams to strangers. Knitters interviewed after learning of the anomaly describe the sensation of working on SCP-4286 as "relaxing" or "like finally getting to think," with no awareness that the private content of that thinking was being recorded into the garment.

ADDENDUM 4286-1: Subject D-8112 knitted a scarf from SCP-4286 over eleven sessions while housed at Site-77, primarily during a period in which she expressed no distress to attending staff. The scarf was given, per standard testing protocol, to D-9027, who wore it for the required duration and reported a dream in which she "was underwater in a kitchen I didn't recognize, trying to find a phone number I already knew, and I already knew I wasn't going to reach anyone in time." D-8112, on debrief, stated she had spent those eleven sessions "thinking about a call I didn't make before my sister died," information she had not previously disclosed in eight months of prior debriefs. She has declined further questioning on the subject. The garment has been retained for further study; D-8112 has not been informed that the scarf was worn by another subject.

SCP-4287.name: Special of the Day
SCP-4287.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4287 (original laminated card plus 6 recovered reproductions) is stored in Site-77 document containment. Access requires Level 2 clearance and written research justification. Personnel are prohibited from reading SCP-4287's item descriptions aloud in the presence of non-cleared individuals. Because the anomalous property persists in any legible reproduction, including photographs, all digital images of SCP-4287 are stored on air-gapped media only; any suspected public upload is to be reported to the Web Crawler Taskforce for removal and amnesticization of the uploader if identified.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4287 is a single-page laminated restaurant menu bearing the letterhead of "Harlan's," a diner whose listed address in [REDACTED] currently corresponds to an undeveloped lot; no permit or business record for "Harlan's" has been located. The menu lists fourteen items with short descriptive text (e.g., "Our Tuesday meatloaf, the way your mother almost made it, with gravy she never got the recipe right for").

Any individual who reads an item's description experiences an immediate, fully convincing gustatory and olfactory hallucination of consuming that item, including sensations of chewing, swallowing, and satiety. The hallucination provides no caloric or nutritional benefit; subjects remain physiologically hungry despite reporting fullness. If the subject additionally states the item's name aloud with the stated or implied intention of ordering it (verified across 40 trials to require genuine intent, not mere recitation), the hallucination triggers as above, and the subject subsequently and permanently loses recall of one unrelated, genuine meal previously eaten in their life. The memory removed is selected by unknown criteria; subjects cannot identify which meal was lost, only that a gap exists (e.g., "I know I had dinner with her that week, I just can't picture where or what"). Repeated use compounds this loss; D-class subjects administered five or more "orders" over a testing period showed measurable difficulty recalling any specific meal shared with a named companion, though memory of the companion in non-dining contexts remained intact.

The menu's physical description text has been observed to change between readings by different individuals — no two researchers have independently transcribed the same fourteen items in the same order, and follow-up review of prior transcriptions shows items present in earlier logs absent from the current physical card. The mechanism for this substitution, and its relationship, if any, to the memories removed from subjects, is unconfirmed.

ADDENDUM 4287-1: D-9114 was administered eight orders over four days as part of a memory-mapping study. On the fifth day, D-9114 failed to recognize her own assigned cellmate of three years, later clarifying: "I know who she is. I just can't remember eating with her. I don't think we ever did, but I think we did every day." D-9114 was withdrawn from further testing. The item she had most recently "ordered" — listed at the time as "the soup you had the night you decided to stay" — no longer appears on the card.

SCP-4288.name: The Extra Stop
SCP-4288.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation maintains embedded access to the automated announcement server of Transit Line [REDACTED] under Foundation front company [REDACTED] Municipal Systems Maintenance. A minimum of two field agents ride the affected line at all times in rotating eight-hour shifts, equipped with covert audio recorders and standard Class-A amnesticide reserves. Any civilian reporting having heard an announcement naming a station not on the official line map to transit staff is to be intercepted and administered amnestics before local reports are filed. Passengers confirmed to have shared a car during a recorded instance of SCP-4288 are to be tracked via ticketing/fare-card data for 30 days following exposure; disappearances are logged under Incident Class Delta and reported to O5 command.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4288 refers to a recurring anomalous event affecting the automated public-address system of Transit Line [REDACTED], occurring at an estimated rate of once per 4,000 single-car journeys. During an affected journey, the automated announcement voice — otherwise identical in tone, pacing, and diction to the standard system recording — includes, at the position where the next real station name would be announced, the name of a station that does not appear on any official map, ticketing system, or construction record for the line, and has never existed under that name at any point in the line's documented history (names recorded to date: "Aubergene Street," "Founder's Crossing," "St. Mira's Landing," and eleven others).

All passengers present in the specific car during the announcement — and only those passengers, confirmed via interview of adjacent cars showing no effect — subsequently possess a shared, mutually consistent false memory of having previously visited the named station: shopping there, changing trains there, or living near it. These memories integrate retroactively and do not present as recent or unusual to the subject; subjects volunteer the memories unprompted in casual conversation rather than under questioning. Independent interviews of passengers from the same car, conducted separately, produce matching descriptions of the nonexistent station's platform layout, signage color, and adjacent street-level businesses, a degree of cross-subject consistency not otherwise observed in Foundation-documented false-memory phenomena.

Three subjects to date, upon growing preoccupied with locating the named station, have boarded the line specifically to search for it and have not been recovered. Station camera archives show each subject boarding normally; none appear on exit or platform cameras at the subsequent real stop. The train itself shows no anomaly in transit time, and no other passengers in the same car report anything unusual about the missing subjects' departure — several, when asked, insist the subject got off "at the stop before this one," which does not match camera timestamps.

Attempts to remove the anomalous announcement segment from the transit authority's server source code succeed only until the next scheduled software update, at which point the segment reappears unprompted, including in test environments physically isolated from the network. A 2024 audit found announcement software of the same manufacturer, running on four other unrelated transit systems, contains no anomalous segment at present; this is not considered reassurance.

SCP-4289.name: Nobody's Laughing Alone
SCP-4289.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The master recording of SCP-4289, a 58-minute digital video file originally broadcast on public access cable television in [REDACTED] in 1997 under the title "Live at the Wagon Wheel," is stored on air-gapped Foundation servers. Viewing is restricted to authorized research groups of no fewer than three and no more than eight individuals, all fitted with cardiac monitors, in a room with immediate medical support on standby. Group viewings by fewer than three individuals are prohibited pending further study (see Addendum). Any recovered public copies or re-uploads are to be purchased or DMCA-removed and the uploader interviewed.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4289 is a recording of a stand-up comedy performance by a performer credited only as "Big Gene," whose material consists of unremarkable observational comedy of the era. The recording is not anomalous to a solitary viewer, who reports finding the material "mildly funny" at most and experiences no unusual physiological effects.

When viewed simultaneously by two or more individuals in the same physical space, SCP-4289 induces, beginning approximately four minutes into the recording, involuntary laughter among all viewers synchronized to within 200 milliseconds of one another, regardless of whether individual viewers find a given joke humorous. Laughter continues for the duration of the recording and does not correspond in frequency or intensity to the actual comedic content, occurring, for instance, with equal force during a joke and during the unscripted pause immediately following it. Cardiac monitoring of test groups shows heart rates of all viewers converging toward a single shared rate, the median of the group's individual resting rates, within the first six minutes and remaining synchronized within 3 BPM of one another for the recording's duration, a physiological effect with no established mechanism.

Groups of five or more show the most severe convergence, with two trials, Group Sizes 6 and 8, producing sustained heart rates in excess of 160 BPM in all members simultaneously despite no corresponding physical exertion; both trials were halted by monitoring staff before injury occurred. No instance to date has produced lasting cardiac harm, though Ethics Committee review has restricted further large-group testing pending cardiology consultation.

Subjects uniformly report the experience as pleasant, describing it afterward as "the hardest I've laughed in years" regardless of whether they recall finding any specific joke funny, and several D-class subjects have requested repeat viewing, a response inconsistent with Foundation experience regarding compulsion-adjacent anomalies, which are more typically reported as intrusive or unwelcome.

ADDENDUM 4289-1: Performer credited as "Big Gene" has not been identified. The venue named in the recording's title card, the Wagon Wheel, operated at the listed address from 1994 to 1997 and closed following an unrecorded incident; former staff, when located, decline to discuss the closure.

SCP-4290.name: Instructions Included
SCP-4290.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4290 is retained at Site-77 under Thaumiel-classification authorization 4290-T, issued jointly by the Department of Applied Reality Engineering and Site Ethics Committee. Use is restricted to Foundation containment-furniture fabrication requests approved by a Level 3 supervisor. Each use must be logged, including the identity of the assembling individual and a post-assembly psychological screening (see Description). SCP-4290 is not to be used to fabricate furniture for personnel without informed consent and completion of Form 4290-C.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4290 is a 40-page furniture assembly instruction booklet, written in the stilted, translation-adjacent English and pictogram style typical of flat-pack furniture manuals, recovered from a warehouse fire in [REDACTED] in 2003 alongside 200 identical, non-anomalous printed copies, all of which have been confirmed inert and returned to circulation. The recovered instance, distinguishable only by a faint discoloration on its cover, produces an anomalous effect when followed to completion by a single individual assembling any piece of furniture using the diagrams as a general template, regardless of the furniture's actual source components.

The completed furniture item, while retaining its ordinary function and appearance, possesses one additional structural property directly related to an anxiety, regret, or unresolved tension held by the assembler during construction, expressed as a physically useful containment or engineering property. Documented examples include: a bookshelf assembled by a researcher preoccupied with a subject's tendency to relocate objects unnoticed, which subsequently proved immune to all forms of object displacement observed in three unrelated anomalies; a filing cabinet assembled by an agent anxious about information leaks, whose drawers cannot be opened by any individual other than the assembler or those the assembler has explicitly authorized aloud; and a chair, assembled by a D-Class technician anxious about his own physical restraint history, capable of holding Keter-class humanoid SCP-4118 without triggering its escape-trigger conditions, a property no purpose-built containment chair had achieved in eleven prior attempts.

The specific property generated cannot be selected or directed by the assembler; it correlates with their psychological state but is not consciously controllable, and 60% of assembly attempts to date have produced furniture with no discernible anomalous property at all, believed to correlate with assemblers who report neutral emotional states during construction. Personnel selected for SCP-4290 fabrication tasks are therefore assigned based on documented, relevant, pre-existing anxieties matched to desired containment properties, a practice formally approved under Ethics Committee Ruling 4290-1 but revisited annually.

ADDENDUM 4290-1: Following the chair incident, Site Ethics Committee raised the question of whether repeated assignment of personnel to SCP-4290 tasks based on their documented anxieties constitutes an inappropriate use of psychological profiling for institutional gain. The practice remains authorized. The technician who assembled the SCP-4118 restraint chair has since been reassigned to unrelated duties at his own request and has not been asked to use SCP-4290 again.

SCP-4291.name: Missed Call From
SCP-4291.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The master audio file of SCP-4291, 3.2 seconds in length and in .m4r format, is stored on a single air-gapped device inside a Faraday-shielded document locker at Site-77. Personnel are prohibited from setting SCP-4291 as an active ringtone on any personal or Foundation device. Testing occurs only on quarantined Foundation-issue phones with no active SIM card or account associated with any living relative of test personnel; D-class subjects are the preferred test population for this reason. Any Foundation phone confirmed to have SCP-4291 installed outside of an approved test is to be factory-reset and the assigning individual interviewed.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4291 is a short audio file, consistent in format and metadata with a standard third-party smartphone ringtone, obtained from a discontinued ringtone marketplace app in 2019 by Agent [REDACTED] during a routine sweep. Under normal use, once set as a device's ringtone, the phone will, at unpredictable intervals averaging one incidence per 11 days of active use, display an incoming call from a contact saved in the phone's address book as a deceased relative of the device's owner, with a caller ID name and, where applicable, photograph matching Foundation and public records for that individual.

If the call is answered, the subject reports hearing the voice of the deceased relative, judged consistent with archival recordings in 100% of cases tested (n=14), speaking in a manner consistent with an ordinary phone conversation, typically inquiring about mundane current events in the subject's life. In 4 of 14 trials, the caller volunteered information about the subject's future within the following 30 days; in all 4 cases the information proved accurate. In 2 of 14 trials, when the subject asked the caller a direct question about their own death, the caller answered with information later confirmed accurate by medical records the subject had not previously reviewed, including in one case a detail contradicting the subject's prior understanding of the death — the caller's stated cause of death did not match the death certificate on file, but matched an amended certificate filed eleven days later, which the subject could not have known existed.

The call terminates after a duration of exactly six minutes regardless of conversation content, cannot be recorded through any tested method (all recording attempts, digital and analog, yield only line noise), and does not appear in the device's call log after termination. Subjects uniformly wish to receive further calls and, when the device is confiscated per protocol, request its return; this request is denied.

ADDENDUM 4291-1: The identity of the ringtone's original composer or distributor could not be determined; the marketplace app that hosted it shut down in 2020, and its listed developer entity does not correspond to any registered business. The file's metadata lists a creation date nine days prior to the death of the first D-Class subject's mother, who is not the individual who called him.

SCP-4292.name: The Starter Deck
SCP-4292.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All recovered packs and loose cards of SCP-4292, currently 214 individual cards believed to represent an incomplete set, are stored in individual static-shielded sleeves at Site-77 Low-Prevalence Object Storage. Foundation front organization [REDACTED] Hobby Distribution has purchased manufacturing rights to the card line's parent game to prevent further legitimate print runs; however, SCP-4292 cards continue to appear in sealed packs of the game sourced from at least six confirmed unauthorized printing operations, origin unknown. Civilian trading card communities and online marketplaces are monitored by Task Force Pi-1 ("Card Sharks") for the specific card backs and border pattern associated with SCP-4292; recovered cards are purchased anonymously and never through direct confiscation, to avoid drawing attention to the set's anomalous status.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4292 refers to a subset of cards belonging to an otherwise unremarkable, mass-produced collectible card game aimed at children aged 8-14, themed around fictional creatures with numerical statistics. Each SCP-4292 card is visually near-identical to its non-anomalous counterparts in the same set, differing only in that the numerical statistics printed on the card, a combination of "Power," "Speed," and "Luck" values, correspond, when decoded via a substitution method independently discovered by three separate unconnected civilian collector communities, to the accurate date, outcome, and margin of a real-world future event — predominantly sporting fixtures, but also including, in 12 confirmed cases, elections, and in 2 confirmed cases, natural disasters, decoded on average 40 days prior to the event's occurrence.

The decoding method requires no specialized knowledge; it has been independently reconstructed by hobbyist forums who refer to the cards colloquially as "the real ones" and treat their predictive accuracy as an open secret within relevant communities, complicating containment. Foundation review of forum archives indicates general public belief in the cards' predictive nature is increasing rather than being dismissed as coincidence, a shift attributed to the set's 100% prediction accuracy across 340 decoded and subsequently verified cards to date.

Civilian betting activity tied to decoded SCP-4292 predictions has been detected in [REDACTED] amounts across eleven jurisdictions; the Foundation classifies this economic entanglement, combined with the set's active, uncontained reproduction and the impossibility of decoding cards not yet printed, as the basis for Keter designation. Of specific concern: two decoded cards to date have described events involving named Foundation personnel by initials and position title rather than full name, a specificity not observed in any other decoded card and not explainable by the substitution method used for sporting predictions, which requires only numerical inputs.

ADDENDUM 4292-1: Card #4292-190, decoded per standard method, translates to: "[REDACTED initials], Site-77, will not report for the next scheduled shift." The card was decoded four days before Dr. [REDACTED, initials matching] failed to report for a scheduled shift due to a family emergency unconnected to any known anomaly. The card has not decoded further information since.

SCP-4293.name: Closed Captioning
SCP-4293.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4293 refers to an anomalous subtitle and closed-caption track, not a physical object, currently confirmed present on 31 unrelated films spanning multiple decades, countries of origin, and distribution formats (VHS, DVD, digital streaming). No common source file, encoding standard, or distributor connects the confirmed instances. Foundation Web Crawler Taskforce monitors streaming platforms and physical media marketplaces for viewer complaints matching SCP-4293's signature (see Description) and acquires flagged copies for study. Because the anomaly activates only when captions are enabled by a viewer's deliberate choice, no active containment of source files is presently feasible; public advisory has not been issued, as awareness campaigns are assessed to increase, not decrease, caption usage among the target demographic.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4293 manifests when an individual enables subtitles or closed captioning, in any language, while viewing one of the confirmed affected films. The displayed caption text periodically diverges from the film's actual audio dialogue, inserting instead a grammatically ordinary sentence pertaining directly to a private fact about the viewer that could not have been known to the film's original captioner: a name, a location, an unresolved personal matter, or, in nine documented cases, information the viewer states they did not consciously know themselves prior to reading it, such as the actual whereabouts of a lost object, later verified correct.

Divergent captions appear for an average of 2.4 seconds before the caption track resumes standard transcription, are visually and stylistically identical to the surrounding captions in font, timing, and positioning, and are not present in the same film's caption file when reviewed by a second viewer simultaneously or when the same viewer re-watches the identical scene; the inserted line is never repeated. Audio analysis confirms the film's actual spoken dialogue during the divergent interval matches the official script and is unrelated to the displayed caption. Viewers without captions enabled experience no anomaly regardless of exposure duration.

The insertions are not reliably distressing; a slight majority of interviewed viewers (58%) report the experience as "eerie but not upsetting," while 12% report significant distress requiring Foundation follow-up, typically among viewers for whom the inserted information concerned a deceased person or unresolved grief. The remainder report not noticing the divergence at all despite eye-tracking confirmation that they read the altered text, an inconsistency not yet explained.

ADDENDUM 4293-1: Researcher [REDACTED] viewed SCP-4293-affected film "Harbor Light" (1961) with captions enabled as part of a standard cataloguing pass. At 00:41:12, the caption read: "the numbers she wrote on the fridge were never a phone number." Researcher [REDACTED] confirmed in her personal notes, unprompted and prior to consulting any record, that her mother kept a string of digits taped to the refrigerator throughout the researcher's childhood, which she had always assumed was an old phone number and had never questioned. Foundation records show no automated method by which this detail could have been known to any party with access to SCP-4293's source files. No further caption addressed to Researcher [REDACTED] has appeared in any subsequent screening.

SCP-4294.name: Exhibit Not Shown
SCP-4294.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The 11 recovered handheld audio guide units constituting SCP-4294, along with their docking cradle and charging unit, are stored at Site-77 in a lead-lined cabinet when not in active testing. The units function only when paired with their original cradle; separated from it for longer than 72 hours, a unit's battery cannot be recharged by any method and the unit becomes permanently inert (7 units have been lost to this process and are retained as inert controls). Testing requires a controlled gallery-like environment, Site-77 Room C-4, furnished with placeholder museum signage; personnel are prohibited from conducting tests in any real public museum or gallery space.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4294 units are audio guide devices of a make and model matching standard commercial museum rental equipment circa 2005, recovered from an estate sale following the closure of [REDACTED] Regional Museum in 2018, a real, non-anomalous institution; no connection between the museum's closure and SCP-4294 has been established. When operated in any room containing at least one genuine museum-quality display case, cabinet, or plinth, regardless of whether the case contains an actual object, SCP-4294 will, when its numbered keypad is used to "select" an exhibit number not corresponding to any real placard in the room, play a detailed, professionally narrated 90-second to 4-minute description of an object that is not present.

Descriptions are specific and internally consistent (provenance, material, dimensions, prior ownership history) but do not correspond to any catalogued object in any museum collection searched to date by Foundation archivists. In 6 of 40 documented test instances, an object matching the played description, including material and approximate dimensions, was subsequently located by Foundation acquisition teams in unrelated private collections, storage facilities, or, in one case, a landfill, within the following 18 months, and recovered. The object's actual history did not match the details in the corresponding SCP-4294 description in any of the 6 recovered cases; testers describe the discrepancy as the description having described "what the object should have been," rather than what it was.

SCP-4294 does not appear to select object descriptions in response to keypad input in any discernible pattern; the same number entered twice in the same room produces different descriptions in 90% of trials, and no description has repeated in 40 documented tests. The mechanism by which SCP-4294 subsequently guides Foundation teams to matching physical objects, when this occurs, is not understood, and Department of Analysis has declined to classify this as intentional on the device's part pending further data.

ADDENDUM 4294-1: Test 4294-19 produced a description of "a child's shoe, left foot only, recovered from the Kesler house fire, donated 1962 by a surviving relative who wished to remain unnamed." No Kesler house fire is on record in any jurisdiction searched. Acquisitions has not located a matching object as of this filing. The description remains under standing search flag.

SCP-4295.name: Find These Words
SCP-4295.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4295, a mass-market paperback puzzle book of 96 pages with publisher information absent from the copyright page, is stored in standard document containment at Site-77. Personnel are prohibited from completing any puzzle within SCP-4295 without prior approval, as completion of a puzzle is irreversible (see Description). 71 of the book's 80 puzzles have been completed by prior Foundation testing and are no longer usable for further study; the remaining 9 are reserved for controlled testing only under Level 2 authorization.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4295 outwardly resembles a standard word-search puzzle book of the type sold in pharmacies and gas stations, containing 80 grids of letters with an associated word list per puzzle. Puzzles are not anomalous until a subject locates and circles all words on a given puzzle's list, at which point the subject permanently loses the ability to recognize those specific words, in any language they know that shares a cognate, as vocabulary — they retain full comprehension of the underlying concept but can no longer read, write, speak, or recognize the specific word form used to describe it, describing the sensation as the word "looking wrong" or "like a word from a language I don't speak." Subjects compensate by using synonyms or circumlocution, often without noticing they have stopped using the original term.

Word lists are thematically ordinary (e.g., "Kitchen," "Weather," "Family") and the removed vocabulary is correspondingly mundane, which Foundation psychological staff assess as a significant containment risk: subjects who complete a puzzle involving common words, documented cases include "mother," "tomorrow," and "enough," experience measurable communication difficulty and are frequently unaware of the specific cause, instead attributing the resulting circumlocution to stress, fatigue, or unrelated cognitive concerns. Removal is not reversible by any tested method, including hypnotic regression, and does not extend to the underlying concept, memory, or emotional association, only to the specific linguistic label.

Subjects who complete multiple puzzles do not report cumulative distress proportional to vocabulary loss; several D-class subjects who completed six or more puzzles described the experience afterward as "peaceful" or "less cluttered," a response the Ethics Committee has flagged as inconsistent with the objective severity of induced expressive aphasia and worth further study rather than reassurance.

ADDENDUM 4295-1: D-9273 completed the puzzle themed "Family," which included the word list: mother, father, sister, brother, cousin, aunt, uncle, grandmother, grandfather, twin. Post-test interview transcript records D-9273 repeatedly referring to "the woman who had me" and "the man she was married to" without apparent distress or awareness of the substitution, and stating, when asked directly whether anything felt different: "No. Should it?"

SCP-4296.name: Second Cast
SCP-4296.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The complete script of SCP-4296, a three-act stage play titled "Harvest Recess," author credited as "Anonymous" on all 4 recovered printings, is stored in Site-77 restricted archive. Foundation policy prohibits any full read-through of the script by three or more individuals in the same physical space under any circumstance. Two known amateur theater companies have staged unauthorized productions of SCP-4296 obtained through public-domain script archives, as the script's copyright status is unclear and cannot currently be legally challenged; both productions are the subject of ongoing Foundation intervention (see Addendum). Foundation monitoring of script-licensing databases and community theater listings continues under Task Force Rho-6 ("Stage Managers").

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4296 is a play script of ordinary format and unremarkable dramatic content, a domestic drama concerning three siblings dividing a deceased parent's estate. The script becomes anomalous only during live performance before an audience, requiring a minimum cast of four actors and a minimum audience of one. At an unpredictable point during Act II, one performer on stage will, without deviation from blocking or vocal performance suggesting awareness, begin speaking lines that do not appear in any known printing of the script, in a manner seamlessly continuous with the surrounding dialogue such that audiences reliably fail to notice a change has occurred.

Following this point, the performer delivering the altered dialogue gradually exchanges identity with a randomly selected audience member: the performer's memories, personality markers, and physical mannerisms measurably transfer to the audience member over the remainder of the performance, while the original performer exhibits corresponding onset of the audience member's memories and personality. By the play's end, average performance length 100 minutes, the exchange is complete; the former performer exits with the rest of the audience, generally unaware anything has occurred, and the former audience member remains onstage to take a curtain call they have no memory of preparing for.

Both individuals retain their original physical bodies; the exchange is one of memory, personality, and skill (former audience members have been observed to competently perform blocking and lines for scenes they have no memory of rehearsing). The exchange is not reported as distressing by either party in 60% of cases, who instead describe a vague, growing unfamiliarity with their own life that they attribute to unrelated causes over the following weeks. In the remaining 40%, subjects present with acute identity distress requiring intervention. No case of reversal, spontaneous or induced, has been documented. The Foundation's Keter designation reflects both the play's uncontained public performance history and the absence of any identified method to predict which cast member or audience member will be selected, or to prevent the exchange once a performance has begun.

ADDENDUM 4296-1: The [REDACTED] Community Playhouse production, halted by Foundation intervention disguised as a fire code violation during intermission of its second performance, had already completed one full undetected exchange during its opening night. The affected audience member, a 34-year-old accountant with no theatrical background, has since joined the cast of the playhouse's next production and reports "always having wanted to try this." He has not been informed of SCP-4296's nature. Foundation is presently divided on whether disclosure would constitute a containment improvement or an unnecessary escalation.

SCP-4297.name: You've Reached
SCP-4297.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4297 refers to an anomalous property affecting a single physical answering machine unit, a cassette-based model of a manufacturer now defunct, currently stored powered-off in Site-77 Low-Risk Storage. The unit is not to be connected to any active phone line, cellular relay, or VoIP system. Prior connection to Foundation testing lines has been discontinued following Incident 4297-3 (see Addendum). Any recovered secondary units confirmed to exhibit the same effect, currently none identified, are to be reported immediately to the Site Director.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4297 causes an outgoing voicemail or answering-machine greeting recorded by its owner using the affected unit to change, without the owner's re-recording or knowledge, between the time it is recorded and the time it is next heard by a caller. The change is not visible or audible to the greeting's owner upon internal playback checks and is detected only by external callers. The altered greeting always begins with the standard recorded phrase in the owner's own voice but concludes with an additional sentence, also rendered in a convincing reproduction of the owner's voice, describing a specific, currently accurate fact about the owner's life unknown to the general public — location, activity, or emotional state at the moment the caller places the call, rather than at the moment of recording.

Callers uniformly report the additional sentence as unsettling specifically because of its present tense and accuracy (e.g., a greeting recorded months prior concluding, for one specific caller, "—sorry I can't answer, I'm standing in the kitchen right now deciding whether to call you back"). The appended sentence differs between callers who reach the same greeting at different times, each tailored to information seemingly relevant to that specific caller's relationship with the owner, and is never heard by the owner regardless of how many times they call their own number. No caller has reported the appended sentence being incorrect.

The unit's origin is unknown; recovered alongside a residential estate sale, its prior owner, name on record, deceased of natural causes, left no explanation of its acquisition. Testing has confirmed the effect persists regardless of which individual's voice is used to record the outgoing greeting, indicating the anomaly resides in the machine rather than any recorded voice.

ADDENDUM 4297-1 (Incident 4297-3): During an authorized test, Researcher [REDACTED] recorded a standard greeting on SCP-4297 and Agent [REDACTED] called the line from an external number. The recorded greeting concluded, in Researcher [REDACTED]'s voice: "—I'm not going to tell you I'm fine, because you'll know I'm lying, the way you always do." Researcher [REDACTED], when informed of the appended content, requested to end her shift early, citing an unrelated personal matter she declined to specify. The unit has not been connected to any line since.

SCP-4298.name: Choose Your Next Move
SCP-4298.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known physical media containing SCP-4298, currently 3 5.25-inch floppy disks and 6 confirmed digital ISO copies circulating on abandonware archival sites, are logged under Task Force Pi-1 ("Card Sharks," secondary assignment) monitoring. Physical disks are stored in a Faraday-shielded evidence locker at Site-77; digital copies cannot be reliably removed from public archival sites without drawing unwanted attention, and Foundation policy currently favors covert monitoring over takedown requests. Personnel are prohibited from running SCP-4298 on any device connected to a network or possessing any form of remote connectivity. All test sessions must be logged in full, including verbatim transcription of all player input and game output.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4298 is a text-based interactive fiction game titled "GREY HOUSE" running on period-appropriate 1980s home computer architecture, presenting the player with descriptive text and accepting short natural-language commands ("go north," "take key," "ask about the letter"). The game's narrative, superficially a haunted-house mystery, is not anomalous in content.
