The anomalous property manifests in the relationship between the player's in-game choices and their subsequent real-world behavior: choices made by a player within SCP-4298 correspond, with a confirmed rate of 88% across 60 documented sessions, to choices that same player subsequently makes in unrelated real-world circumstances within the following 24 hours, matching in underlying structure — a player who chooses to "trust the stranger" in-game subsequently extends unwarranted trust to an unrelated real person; a player who chooses violence toward an in-game antagonist reports a disproportionate real-world confrontation with an unrelated party.

The correspondence is not merely thematic; specific quantities and outcomes described in-game have, in 14 documented cases, matched real-world outcomes with a precision inconsistent with coincidence — a player who is told in-game they have "three days" before an in-game consequence occurs experiences an unrelated real-world deadline of exactly three days following the session. The game does not appear to predict outcomes independent of player choice; rather, the act of choosing within the game appears to constrain or determine the player's subsequent real behavior, a causality Foundation researchers have been unable to establish direction for, whether the game reflects a choice the player was already going to make, or produces it.

Sessions terminated before reaching an ending produce no observed effect; the correspondence manifests only for players who complete the game to one of its four documented endings. No method to prevent a test session from reaching completion, short of destroying the hardware mid-session, which has produced hardware failure without preventing the anomalous correspondence in 2 of 3 attempts, has proven reliable. Keter designation reflects the anomaly's active circulation on public abandonware archives, its confirmed functionality on modern emulator software, removing the hardware barrier to exposure, and the absence of any consent mechanism preventing casual players from experiencing life-altering correspondence without warning.

ADDENDUM 4298-1: D-8846 reached the game's "Ending C" ("You leave the house and do not look back") during a monitored session. Within the following 24 hours, D-8846 requested and was granted voluntary termination from further Foundation testing duty, a request he had not previously made in fourteen months of service and did not explain beyond stating "I already decided this before you asked."

SCP-4299.name: Not Quite Grown
SCP-4299.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4299, a 7-inch vinyl single pressed on unmarked black vinyl, a common commercial format circa 1970s-1980s with no visible label or manufacturer markings, is stored in standard object containment at Site-77 and is not to be played under any circumstance without Level 2 authorization and Ethics Committee sign-off, per policy established after Incident 4299-1 (see Addendum). Testing requires the presence of a licensed pediatric physician when infant subjects are involved.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4299 outwardly resembles a standard 7-inch vinyl single played at 45 RPM, playing an unremarkable 32-second lullaby melody on a single locked, non-repeating groove, tentatively identified by Foundation musicologists as a variant of a public-domain folk tune though no exact match has been located, for approximately 90 seconds before the needle must be manually lifted. When played within audible range, approximately 5 meters, of a human infant under 12 months of age, SCP-4299 measurably slows the subject's rate of physical growth and developmental progression for a period directly proportional to the duration of exposure, at an observed rate of approximately 11 days of developmental delay per minute of exposure. The effect is cumulative across multiple exposures and does not reverse spontaneously; affected infants eventually resume typical developmental progression from the point at which it was slowed, rather than catching up to chronological age.

The effect is specific to infants; no comparable slowing has been observed in subjects over 12 months, and adults exposed to SCP-4299 report only that the melody is "hard to place" and mildly soothing. Parents and caregivers of affected infants, across all 6 documented pre-Foundation cases recovered through hospital pediatric-delay records cross-referenced with the record's known ownership chain, uniformly report finding the slowed development reassuring rather than alarming at the time, several independently describing a wish for their child to "stay little a while longer" prior to identifying the cause. This correlation between caregiver sentiment and the anomaly's function has not been explained and may be coincidental; Department of Analysis notes the record's known ownership chain shows it was retained across three generations of the same family despite the effect being informally recognized within the family by the second generation, who nonetheless chose not to discontinue its use.

ADDENDUM 4299-1: Following acquisition, SCP-4299 was played during a standard cataloguing procedure within audible range of Researcher [REDACTED]'s infant daughter, present on-site due to a childcare scheduling conflict, for an estimated 40 seconds before being noticed and stopped. Subsequent pediatric assessment confirmed developmental delay consistent with approximately 7 days of slowed progression. Researcher [REDACTED] was not disciplined, as the incident was assessed as an administrative failure in transport protocol rather than personnel negligence; she has since requested and been granted reassignment away from any future contact with SCP-4299. Her daughter's development has since resumed typical progression. Researcher [REDACTED]'s current whereabouts within the Foundation are not relevant to this file, and she has declined to provide further comment for the record.

SCP-4300.name: Items For Sale
SCP-4300.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4300 refers to the classified advertisement section of a specific, otherwise unremarkable weekly community newspaper, [REDACTED] Pennysaver, currently produced under full Foundation editorial and printing control via front company [REDACTED] Regional Publishing, acquired in 2011 following identification of the anomaly. Foundation-approved use of SCP-4300 for controlled item disposal (see Description) requires Level 3 authorization and completion of Form 4300-D per targeted item. Public circulation of the Pennysaver continues at reduced print volume to preserve the anomaly's functional conditions; subscriber lists are monitored, and the paper is not available for digital subscription or online archive to limit uncontrolled exposure.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4300 causes items listed for sale in the classified section of the affected newspaper issue to correspond, in a majority of printings, to an item genuinely owned by a specific reader of that issue, described with sufficient specificity — approximate condition, distinguishing marks, general location — that the reader recognizes the listing as referring to their own possession, despite the reader never having placed or authorized such a listing. If the reader responds to the listing using the listed contact method, historically a P.O. box, currently a Foundation-monitored phone line, and completes a purchase, paying the listed price, always modest, to the listed party, the described item vanishes from the reader's actual possession at the moment of transaction completion, regardless of the item's physical location at that time, and does not reappear. The reader receives no physical exchange; the transaction consists solely of payment.

Foundation testing under Thaumiel authorization has established SCP-4300 as a reliable method for the discreet, non-violent, non-traumatic removal of hazardous or anomalous objects from civilian possession when an object's Foundation-standard retrieval would risk public exposure or requires a level of force disproportionate to the object's actual danger. To date, 34 minor anomalous objects, average Object Class equivalent Safe, have been successfully removed from uncontained civilian possession via engineered SCP-4300 listings, at total Foundation expenditure of $[REDACTED] in listed purchase prices, a substantially lower operational cost than comparable field retrieval operations. The mechanism by which the Foundation "places" a desired listing rather than merely observing naturally occurring ones remains only partially understood; current practice involves editorial staff, all Foundation personnel, submitting a listing through the paper's normal internal process, which the anomaly incorporates into the printed edition at a rate correlating with, but not identical to, submission specificity, and is treated as a functioning if imperfectly characterized interface rather than a fully reverse-engineered mechanism.

ADDENDUM 4300-1: Editorial staff have observed that listings placed through normal channels occasionally print with alterations not present in the submitted text — most commonly, a lower price than submitted, and in 3 cases, a different listed seller name than the Foundation front submitted, corresponding in each case to the actual first name of the object's original civilian owner, information not included in any submission. The Department of Analysis has not yet determined how SCP-4300 obtains this information and has recommended, thus far without approval, that all future submissions be reviewed for the possibility that the newspaper is not merely executing Foundation requests but independently verifying them against its own criteria.

SCP-4301.name: The Cross-Reference Drawer
SCP-4301.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4301 is stored in Records Annex 3 of Site-73, integrated into a bank of forty-one visually identical oak card-catalog cabinets so that its physical location is not obvious to unauthorized personnel. The drawer itself is not to be relocated, refinished, or replaced; attempts to duplicate its housing have not reproduced the anomaly.

Access to SCP-4301 is restricted to archival staff holding Level 3 clearance or higher, and all access must be logged under the two-person integrity rule: no individual may open the drawer or remove a card while alone. No more than one card may be withdrawn from the drawer per audit cycle (28 days) without director-level authorization. Any card removed for review must be photographed in full, front and back, before and after handling, and returned to its original position within four hours.

Personnel who discover that a card bearing their own name has been generated are to report to the Site-73 psychologist within one business day, whether or not they have noticed any subjective change. Cards are not to be destroyed under any circumstances; two prior incidents of accidental card destruction are documented in Addendum 4301-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4301 is a single drawer belonging to a card-catalog cabinet manufactured circa 1958, presently seated in a cabinet at Site-73's Records Annex. The drawer contains index cards, each corresponding to one living or deceased Foundation staff member who has, at any point, read a document classified Level 4 or above from Site-73's holdings. A new card generates inside the drawer within 6 to 30 hours of a qualifying individual's first reading of such a document; the mechanism of generation has not been observed directly, as the drawer has never been found open during the interval.

Each card lists the subject's full name, position, and a single typed sentence beginning "Now knows that—" followed by a paraphrase, never a verbatim quotation, of the classified content read. The sentence is accurate but incomplete, omitting details a reader would consider essential.

If a card is physically removed from the drawer, the corresponding individual's retention of the specific content described on the card degrades over the following 48 hours, without their conscious awareness of the loss. They will continue to believe they possess the knowledge in question and will speak and act accordingly until confronted with direct evidence of its absence, at which point they experience the gap as a memory of having "always meant to look that up." Reinserting the card restores retention in approximately 60% of cases; the remaining 40% show no improvement even after extended reinsertion.

ADDENDUM 4301-1: Twelve cards currently in the drawer correspond to personnel who are deceased. These cards continue to be periodically re-typed, with the descriptive sentence updated to reflect content the deceased individual could not, by any known means, have newly encountered. The source of these updates is unidentified.

ADDENDUM 4301-2: On two occasions, cards were destroyed by fire or shredding. In both cases, the corresponding individual's knowledge of the associated content did not merely degrade but became, per interview transcripts, knowledge they insist they "never had reason to learn," accompanied by mild hostility toward colleagues who reference it in conversation. Whether this represents replacement of the missing knowledge with a false negative belief, or something else, remains unresolved.

SCP-4302.name: The Franking Machine
SCP-4302.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4302 is secured in a locked mail-processing closet in the sub-basement of Site-19, disconnected from the site's internal mail circuit and denied a working power cable; the unit does not require electrical power to operate, and this measure serves only to discourage casual use. The room housing SCP-4302 is under camera observation at all times, and the camera feed is not to be reviewed by on-duty personnel except for containment-breach verification, per Protocol 4302-Silence (see Description).

Use of SCP-4302 for any purpose is prohibited without written authorization from the Site-19 Director and concurrent sign-off from the Ethics Committee. Any item found to have been processed through SCP-4302 without authorization is to be intercepted before delivery wherever logistically possible, quarantined for no less than thirty days, and its contents read only by personnel not named as sender or recipient.

Personnel are reminded that SCP-4302 cannot be reasoned with, warned, or fed false addresses as a containment strategy; two attempts to do so are recorded in Incident 4302-A and 4302-C, respectively, both unsuccessful.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4302 is a manual postage-franking machine of a style commercially discontinued in approximately 1974, bearing no manufacturer's mark. Any letter, package, or document fed through its roller receives a postmark and is, from that point, guaranteed physical delivery to the address written upon it, by means not observed and not preventable through interception of standard postal or courier systems—items have been recovered already delivered despite confirmed containment of all conventional transit.

The anomalous property is not the guarantee of delivery but its relationship to time. An item processed by SCP-4302 arrives at its destination at whatever point the contents are "true," rather than at a point following its dispatch. A letter describing an event will arrive once that event has occurred, regardless of when it was written or mailed—including arriving before it was written, from the recipient's frame of reference, if the described event will have already taken place by then.

This has been exploited twice by Foundation personnel attempting to warn colleagues of impending incidents. In both cases, delivery of the warning prevented the incident, which in turn meant the warning's contents were never true, which in turn appears to have prevented the letter from ever having been written—yet both recipients retain clear memory of reading it, and the letters themselves remain in evidence lockers, their described incidents never having occurred. Site-19's philosophical staff refer to this category of object informally as "settled," meaning its causal status is stable but not resolved into a single consistent history; formal designation is pending review.

Protocol 4302-Silence prohibits documentation staff from discussing the specific contents of any letter processed through SCP-4302 in the presence of anyone who might plausibly become its sender, on the theory—unconfirmed—that awareness of a letter's future content could suppress the actions that would otherwise have made it true, with unknown consequences for the letter's already-established delivery.

ADDENDUM: A third letter, addressee redacted, was recovered from SCP-4302's output tray on ██/██/2023, already postmarked, already delivered per tracking, and already read by its recipient according to their own testimony—except that no member of Foundation personnel has yet fed anything into the machine that day, and the security footage for the relevant hour has not yet been reviewed, per standing protocol, by anyone who is not already its recipient.

SCP-4303.name: The Nested Specimen Jars
SCP-4303.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4303 consists of six borosilicate glass jars nested within one another and is stored, fully assembled, in a padded case in the Site-45 biological containment locker. The jars are not to be separated except during scheduled observation, conducted no more than once per month, as separation and reassembly appear to reset the developmental offset described below (see Description) and destroy several weeks of comparative data each time. Handling requires two researchers: one to record, one to open.

Under no circumstances is the innermost jar to be opened without the five outer jars first being opened and logged in sequence. Researchers who have attempted to bypass jars to reach the innermost directly report acute anxiety and, in one case, brief unresponsiveness; the specimen itself has shown no corresponding reaction, and the cause of researcher distress has not been established as anomalous in nature, though it is treated as such pending further study.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4303 is a set of six nested glass jars, graduated in size such that each fits inside the next, in the manner of a matryoshka doll rendered in laboratory glassware. The outermost jar is empty. Each jar inward contains a single specimen of Tenebrio molitor (mealworm beetle, or a preceding larval stage thereof), apparently the same individual organism at successively earlier points in its life cycle, despite the jars having been sealed, per Foundation testing, for no less than four years.

The specimen in Jar 2 (second from outside) is an adult beetle showing wear and pigment loss consistent with advanced age. The specimen in Jar 3 is a younger adult. Jar 4 contains a pupa. Jar 5 contains a late-instar larva. Jar 6, the innermost, contains a larva small enough to have hatched, by external estimate, within the past several days—an estimate that has not changed across seventy-one monthly observations spanning just under six years.

The specimens do not develop forward in real time relative to one another; the beetle in Jar 2 does not die, and the larva in Jar 6 does not visibly age, across any observation period yet recorded. Standard entomological practice would place the total elapsed developmental time represented across all six jars at approximately four to five months; the jars have been in Foundation custody for sixty-nine months as of this writing, and in an unknown private collection for an undetermined period before recovery.

No mechanism has been identified by which the jars maintain this staged arrangement, nor by which the innermost specimen fails to progress. Foundation entomologists have declined, formally and in writing, to hypothesize what would be found if a seventh jar existed inside the sixth, and researchers are discouraged from raising the question informally, per a Site-45 department memo dated after the incident described in the addendum below.

ADDENDUM 4303-1: During the sixty-third observation, Researcher Ohno, working alone in violation of protocol, reported that the innermost jar "felt like it was still being packed," and requested reassignment the following day. Her file notes no prior history of anxiety related to fieldwork. She has since declined to discuss SCP-4303 further, including for the purposes of this addendum, and no replacement testimony has been solicited.

SCP-4304.name: The Conductor's Baton
SCP-4304.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4304 is stored in a velvet-lined case inside a Faraday-shielded locker at Site-64, itself situated within a windowless interior room to eliminate lines of sight through any window or reflective surface. The case may only be opened by personnel with Level 3 clearance and specific authorization from the Performing Anomalies Subcommittee.

Testing involving SCP-4304 requires a minimum fifteen-meter buffer of unoccupied space in all directions from the wielder, verified by motion sensors, and no test may exceed ninety seconds of active conducting. All personnel not directly involved in a test are to remain outside line of sight of the wielder for its duration; this includes closed-circuit monitoring, which must be conducted via audio feed only during live tests.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4304 is a conductor's baton of unremarkable manufacture, wooden shaft and cork grip, recovered from the estate of a regional orchestra conductor following his sudden retirement in 1991. When held by any individual who performs conducting gestures with it—establishing a visible, repeating beat—every person within direct line of sight of the gestures involuntarily synchronizes their heart rate and respiration to the indicated tempo within approximately eight beats, regardless of distance, obstruction by transparent material, or the observer's awareness of the object's nature.

The effect does not extend to persons who cannot see the gestures, including those relying on peripheral vision alone at extreme angles, nor does it compel any gross motor action; affected individuals do not move, march, or dance in time. The synchronization is entirely internal—cardiac and respiratory—and subjectively unnoticed by most subjects unless the indicated tempo falls well outside a safe resting range, at which point subjects report the sudden, involuntary awareness of their own pulse as "someone else's hand on it."

Tempos maintained below 100 beats per minute produce no adverse effects and have been used, under controlled conditions, in three sanctioned trials to calm agitated crowds during minor site evacuations (see Addendum). Tempos sustained above 160 beats per minute for longer than thirty seconds have produced tachycardia, one instance of atrial fibrillation in a subject with a pre-existing condition undisclosed at the time of testing, and, in a single unauthorized field use described below, one fatality.

The wielder's own heart rate is not affected by the baton's use.

ADDENDUM 4304-1: SCP-4304 was deployed without full authorization during the Site-64 partial evacuation of ██/██/20██, by a researcher acting on standing verbal guidance she later stated she believed covered the situation. The baton successfully regulated the breathing and pulse of approximately forty evacuating personnel over a six-minute corridor transit, preventing what evacuation modeling suggests would likely have been a crush injury. One bystander outside the evacuation route, a contractor with no Foundation affiliation and an undisclosed cardiac condition, was within line of sight for eleven seconds during a tempo adjustment and died of cardiac arrest approximately ninety minutes later. The Performing Anomalies Subcommittee has not yet ruled on whether this constitutes grounds for reclassification, formal restriction to Thaumiel-adjacent use under stricter review, or indefinite suspension of all testing pending a use-of-force determination that, three years on, remains open.

SCP-4305.name: The Intercom Panel
SCP-4305.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4305 remains installed in its original location, the third-floor administrative corridor of a decommissioned regional office now designated Site-88, as removal attempts in 2019 resulted in the wall-mounted unit reappearing, functionally identical, in the same location within eleven days despite complete demolition of the surrounding wall section. The corridor is sealed behind a keypad-locked door, and the intercom's speaker grille has been covered with acoustic dampening foam, reducing but not eliminating audibility of incoming transmissions.

Personnel are prohibited from pressing any of SCP-4305's twelve numbered call buttons under any circumstance without a filed research request and the presence of a second witness equipped with an independent audio recorder. Any transmission received is to be treated as classified at Level 4 pending review, regardless of apparent content, and is not to be discussed with anyone whose extension number matches one referenced in the transmission.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4305 is a wall-mounted intercom panel of institutional manufacture, consistent with equipment installed in mid-20th-century office buildings, bearing twelve numbered call buttons corresponding to a numbering scheme that does not match any extension list on record for the building's former occupant, a paper-goods distributor that vacated the premises in 1988.

Pressing a button initiates a connection, audible through the grille as a faint two-tone ring followed by a response, to whichever individual "holds" the position designated by that number within some referential scheme the Foundation has not fully reconstructed. In approximately 30% of documented calls, the respondent identifies themselves by a name and title matching current or former Foundation personnel, including eleven individuals confirmed deceased at the time of the call and four whose personnel files show no history of assignment to any facility with an extension numbering system resembling SCP-4305's. In the remaining calls, the respondent identifies a title with no corresponding position in any Foundation department, e.g., "Third Compliance," "Night Archivist," or "the one who checks," and either declines to elaborate or answers questions with responses later found to be accurate regarding classified matters the respondent should have had no means of knowing.

Respondents are, without exception, aware that they are speaking to someone outside their own context and do not express confusion about the call; several have asked the Foundation caller, by name, why it took so long to call back, despite no prior documented contact.

SCP-4305 cannot be used to reach any specific individual on request; the position reached for a given button number is not fixed and has changed between successive calls to the same button in at least six documented instances, with no correlation yet established to time of day, caller identity, or button-press interval.

ADDENDUM 4305-1: On ██/██/20██, a call to button 7 was answered by an individual identifying themselves as the current occupant of the auditor position within the Site-88 Records Office—a position that, per current organizational charts, does not exist and has never existed at that site. The respondent correctly stated the badge number of the calling researcher, who has since been reassigned at their own request. Site-88 administration maintains, for internal purposes, that button 7 is to be considered permanently out of service.

SCP-4306.name: The Fountain Pen
SCP-4306.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4306 is designated Thaumiel and is maintained under the direct authority of the O5 Command, stored in a dedicated vault at Site-01 accessible only by two-key authorization requiring one O5 Council signature and one signature from the Director of Temporal/Causal Affairs. SCP-4306 may be deployed only against a written, O5-approved Statement of Correction specifying the exact sentence to be inscribed, the intended factual outcome, and an accounting of anticipated cost (see Description).

No sentence may be inscribed using SCP-4306 without a completed Cost Assessment from the Site-01 Archive Actuarial Unit. Emergency deployment without a completed assessment has occurred twice in the object's containment history and is grounds for immediate O5 review regardless of outcome.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4306 is a black lacquer fountain pen of no identifiable manufacture, recovered in 1987 from the personal effects of a Foundation records clerk who had, per her final entries, used it to correct "small things" in her own department's files for approximately six years without apparent incident or oversight.

A grammatically complete, present-tense declarative sentence, written by hand with SCP-4306 and allowed to dry undisturbed, becomes true. This applies exclusively to statements of documentary or historical fact concerning matters the Foundation is positioned to verify or falsify through its own records—personnel status, incident classification, containment history, the prior existence or non-existence of a document—and does not extend to statements describing present physical states, natural law, or the direct outcome of ongoing events. The sentence "Incident 4306-9 did not occur" has been used successfully; the sentence "Subject is not currently on fire" has not been tested, and is prohibited from testing by standing order.

Once dry, the written sentence updates not only the physical page but every corresponding record the Foundation holds, including digital copies, with no discernible mechanism of transmission and no interval of delay yet measured above four seconds. Personnel memory of the prior, now-false state is not reliably altered; most personnel who directly participated in an erased event retain fragmentary recollection of it as something they "can't quite place," a discrepancy the Foundation currently manages through routine, non-anomalous reassignment and, where necessary, standard amnesticization.

Every inscription draws a cost, paid not by the writer but by removal of one true, verifiable, and independently corroborated fact from the world at large—a fact unrelated in content to the inscription, selected by a process the Foundation has not identified, and discovered only after the fact through its absence. Three such losses are confirmed: the complete architectural records of a since-demolished 19th-century building, the paternity of a Foundation researcher's grandfather (now recorded, and believed by all living relatives, to be a different man, with no discrepancy in any document), and the original recipe for a defunct regional food product, mourned by no one who now remembers it existing.

ADDENDUM 4306-1: SCP-4306 has been used, under full authorization, on four occasions to correct catastrophic containment-breach documentation likely to cause mass-casualty disclosure events. The Archive Actuarial Unit's central unresolved finding is that the magnitude of each cost has, so far, borne no measurable proportion to the magnitude of what was corrected—the erasure of a citywide incident and the erasure of a single clerical typo have each, on record, cost the world exactly one fact. Whether this indicates a fixed price per use, or a debt not yet fully called, has not been determined.

SCP-4307.name: The Transport Wheelchair
SCP-4307.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4307 is stored unoccupied in Medical Bay 3 of Site-27 and may be used only for approved testing, never for routine patient transport, per standing medical directive following Incident 4307-3. When not in active use, SCP-4307's wheels are to be locked and the chair covered with an opaque cloth; anecdotal reports that an uncovered SCP-4307 is more likely to be "requested" by patients unprompted have not been substantiated but are treated as sufficient grounds for the covering requirement.

Any individual who has previously received medical treatment, of any kind, at any facility, may not be transported in SCP-4307 without Medical Director approval and the presence of a second staff member walking alongside at all times, in physical contact with the occupant's shoulder or hand for the duration of transport.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4307 is a manual wheelchair of standard mid-range medical manufacture, distinguishable from non-anomalous stock only by a small brass plate riveted beneath the seat, engraved with a serial number that does not match the manufacturer's records and that several other, non-anomalous wheelchairs from the same production run have also been found, on inspection, to lack entirely, as though the plate belongs to no fixed unit.

When an individual with any prior history of medical treatment is seated in SCP-4307 and moved—by another person pushing it; self-propulsion does not trigger the effect—the route traveled will, at some point within the first ninety seconds of movement, pass through a corridor, room, or ward that does not correspond to the actual floor plan of the building in which the transport is occurring. This space is, per all available instrumentation, physically present for the duration of the transport: it registers on cameras, its temperature and air pressure are measurable, and it does not appear to be a hallucination shared only by the occupant.

The space encountered corresponds to a location from the occupant's own prior medical history—a childhood hospital ward, a since-demolished clinic, a room from a procedure the occupant may not consciously recall—populated by no additional persons in the overwhelming majority of cases, though four instances have involved the transient appearance of a figure in period-appropriate medical dress who does not respond to speech and cannot be touched. The transport always concludes at the correct, intended destination, with elapsed real time matching the distance traveled; the anomalous corridor does not appear to extend the journey's duration, only its content.

Occupants' reactions vary from no acknowledgment (most common in occupants transported while unconscious or heavily sedated) to acute distress. Two occupants have reported the experience as comforting, one specifically describing the remembered ward as "the only room that was ever quiet." Post-transport interviews show no consistent pattern in which patients recognize the anomalous detour at all; many recall only the intended route.

ADDENDUM 4307-1 (Incident 4307-3): A researcher being transported for an unrelated minor procedure was routed through what her prior medical records confirm to be a pediatric oncology ward matching her own childhood treatment facility, demolished in 1994. She experienced no distress during transport but returned to the ward, unprompted and alone, twice more during her recovery period using SCP-4307 without authorization before the covering-and-locking requirement above was instituted. She has since been reassigned off-site at her own request and has not commented further on what drew her back.

SCP-4308.name: The Hearing Aid
SCP-4308.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4308 is stored in a standard evidence locker at Site-27 when not in authorized use and is issued only for specific investigative purposes approved by a Level 3 case supervisor. Use of SCP-4308 requires the operator to complete a mandatory debrief with Site-27 psychological staff within 24 hours of any session exceeding ten minutes of continuous wear, regardless of reported content.

SCP-4308 is not to be worn continuously by any individual for longer than sixty minutes in a single 24-hour period. This limit was established following Incident 4308-1 (see Addendum) and is enforced by an internal timer built into current issue protocol rather than any known property of the device itself.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4308 is a beige, behind-the-ear hearing aid of a make discontinued in the early 1990s, recovered in 2003 from the personal effects of a deceased hospice volunteer. It functions as a conventional, non-anomalous hearing aid for ambient sound in real time. Its anomalous property activates only when the wearer is within approximately four meters of the remains, place of death, or a long-held personal possession of a deceased individual, at which point the device additionally, faintly, reproduces audio corresponding to that individual's final spoken words prior to death.

The recording is not a memory or hallucination internal to the wearer; the sound is audible, at low volume, to any person present, and has been captured on standard recording equipment carried by the wearer in seventeen of nineteen documented trials. Audio quality is consistent with the acoustic environment of the death itself—a hospital room recording sounds like a hospital room, regardless of the wearer's actual present environment—suggesting the device is reproducing an actual historical sound rather than generating one.

The words reproduced are, in the significant majority of cases (roughly 80% across current trials), not any words witnesses at the time recall the deceased actually saying, nor words consistent with the deceased's documented final moments. Interviews with witnesses to the original deaths, where available, frequently describe the actual final words as unremarkable, incomplete, or entirely absent due to unconsciousness—while SCP-4308 reproduces a complete, coherent sentence in every trial to date, delivered in a clear voice matching other available recordings of the deceased.

The Foundation's working hypothesis, unconfirmed, is that SCP-4308 does not reproduce what was said, but what very nearly was said and was not, in the final seconds available to say it. This has not been tested against a case with a verified, complete, and witnessed final utterance, as no such case has yet met the device's four-meter proximity requirement during authorized testing.

ADDENDUM 4308-1: During an unauthorized extended session (approximately three hours) at the site of a multi-fatality incident, wearer Dr. Imamura reported that the device's output had, by the second hour, stopped resembling any of the incident's confirmed casualties and had instead begun producing a single repeating sentence in a voice she did not recognize and could not later describe, which she declined to transcribe in her incident report. She has requested, and been granted, permanent reassignment away from further contact with SCP-4308.

SCP-4309.name: The Vending Machine
SCP-4309.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4309 is housed in a dedicated break room at Site-64, electrically powered but disconnected from the site's central inventory-restocking system; its internal stock is manually replenished by two assigned logistics staff on a weekly schedule and its coin/card mechanism has been rewired to accept only Foundation-issued site tokens, limiting use to authorized personnel. A sign-out log is maintained for every purchase.

Personnel are permitted to use SCP-4309 during normal operations without special authorization, as restricting access has, in three separate trial periods, correlated with an increase in unrelated minor injuries among Site-64 staff (see Addendum 4309-2); the current standing policy is to leave the machine in normal circulation and monitor its output rather than restrict it. Any item dispensed by SCP-4309 that does not match the button pressed is to be retained by the purchaser, logged with time and location, and not discarded or consumed/used for its apparent snack purpose before consulting the daily anomaly digest.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4309 is a refrigerated vending machine of standard commercial make, stocked with ordinary snack and beverage items purchased through normal Foundation procurement. In approximately 4% of transactions, the item dispensed does not match the button selected, nor does it match any item loaded into that column by restocking staff; instead, the machine produces a small object, packaged in snack-appropriate wrapping, that in seventeen of nineteen documented cases proved directly useful to the purchaser in responding to an unplanned hazardous event occurring within the following ninety minutes.

Recorded substitutions include: a foil-wrapped item resembling a granola bar that was, on opening, a folded square of fire-resistant cloth, dispensed to a researcher who suffered a lab fire eleven minutes later; a bottled water substituted with an identical bottle containing a chelating compound later confirmed to counteract a chemical exposure the purchaser sustained that afternoon; and, on one occasion, a candy bar that was, in fact, a candy bar, given to a staff member who experienced no incident of any kind for the following six months, the longest injury-free stretch on her record.

The mechanism by which SCP-4309 anticipates a purchaser's near-future need for a specific item has not been identified. The machine has no network connectivity, and its internal components, examined during two authorized partial disassemblies, do not differ from standard stock for its model beyond the presence of a sealed compartment behind the primary stock columns that current tools have been unable to open without risking damage to the mechanism.

The Foundation has not established whether SCP-4309 predicts hazardous events that would occur regardless of its intervention, or whether use of the machine itself increases the local probability of a hazardous event occurring, as a precondition for the substitution to be "necessary." Site-64's safety office notes, without drawing a formal conclusion, that the rate of minor incidents among frequent SCP-4309 users is measurably higher than among staff who rarely use the machine, while the severity of those incidents, once they occur, is measurably lower.

ADDENDUM 4309-1: SCP-4309 has never dispensed a substitute item to any individual who was not, at the time of purchase, a Foundation employee with an active incident-response role, despite regular use by contracted janitorial and food-service staff.

ADDENDUM 4309-2: Restriction trials (20██, 20██, 20██) each reduced overall SCP-4309 usage by more than 90% and were each followed, within the subsequent month, by a statistically significant rise in unrelated minor injuries among Site-64 personnel, relative to baseline. No causal mechanism has been proposed that the Ethics Committee considers satisfactory.

SCP-4310.name: The Overpacked Suitcase
SCP-4310.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4310 is stored empty and closed in a standard storage unit at Site-45, with its interior capacity measured monthly using the standard packing protocol described below and logged against a current relationship inventory of its most recent handler, maintained by Foundation psychological staff with that individual's informed consent. SCP-4310 is not to be issued to personnel for personal use, following the events described in Addendum 4310-1.

Any researcher assigned to interact with SCP-4310 must complete a Relationship Inventory Disclosure prior to and following each testing session, administered by a psychologist not otherwise involved in the object's study. Test sessions are limited to one per researcher per month.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4310 is a brown leather suitcase of a style commercially available through the 1970s, exterior dimensions 71 cm × 46 cm × 23 cm, presenting no anomalous properties to external measurement or handling. Its interior capacity, however, does not correspond to its exterior volume and has been observed to vary between approximately 60 liters and, in its largest recorded state, just under 2,900 liters—more than forty times its apparent physical capacity—without any corresponding change to its outward dimensions or weight when empty.

Standard packing protocol establishes interior capacity by filling SCP-4310 with uniform 10 cm foam cubes until closure becomes impossible, then calculating volume from the count retrieved. Capacity measured this way correlates, with a strength Foundation statisticians describe as "uncomfortably clean," to an inverse relationship with the number of sustained, mutually-acknowledged personal relationships—family, romantic, platonic, but not strictly professional—maintained by whichever individual most recently handled the case with intent to use it for its designed purpose (i.e., packing it for personal travel, not for testing).

SCP-4310's provenance traces to the estate of a man who died alone in 2011 after several decades of increasing social withdrawal; neighbors reported he traveled several times a year despite, in his final decade, having no known contact with any living relative or documented friend. The suitcase recovered from his flat measured at capacity in the testing range, holding, per the standard protocol, 2,847 liters of foam cubes.

Interior capacity responds to changes in the handler's relational status within a period of roughly two to six weeks following a qualifying change—an estrangement, a death, a reconciliation—rather than instantaneously, and the mechanism by which the object identifies a "relationship" as sustained and mutually acknowledged, as opposed to one-sided or lapsed, has not been reproduced by any interview protocol devised by Foundation psychology staff; the object appears to track something closer to the actual state of the relationship than to either party's self-report of it.

No handler has been observed capable of consciously altering SCP-4310's capacity through deliberate manipulation of their own relationships for that purpose; three attempts to do so, undertaken by researchers aware of the correlation, produced no measurable capacity change, which the current research lead attributes, without further elaboration, to the object "not being fooled."

ADDENDUM 4310-1: Following six months of monthly testing, one assigned researcher's personal capacity measurement rose from 340 liters to 2,100 liters. Her Relationship Inventory Disclosures over the same period show a documented decline from eleven acknowledged sustained relationships to one. She has stated in debrief that she does not believe SCP-4310 caused this decline, and Foundation psychological staff have, to date, found no basis to dispute her assessment, though the object's testing schedule for her case has been suspended pending further review.

SCP-4311.name: The Household Barometer
SCP-4311.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4311 is mounted on an interior wall of a dedicated, unoccupied testing room at Site-19, isolated from exterior weather exposure by a sealed, climate-controlled anteroom to rule out mundane atmospheric influence on its readings. The room is monitored continuously by camera with audio, and its reading is logged by a technician stationed outside the room via remote optical viewer at intervals of no less than four hours.

No individual is to remain alone in the same room as SCP-4311 for longer than fifteen minutes. If SCP-4311's needle enters the region marked "STORM" on its face (see Description), the room is to be evacuated immediately and Site-19's on-duty medical and security personnel notified as though responding to an active internal threat, regardless of whether one has yet been identified.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4311 is a wall-mounted aneroid barometer of conventional 1930s domestic manufacture, brass-cased, with a printed dial marked in the standard range from "STORMY" through "FAIR" to "VERY DRY." It was recovered in 1976 from a private residence in which six occupants, across four unrelated families residing there in succession between 1938 and 1975, died by violence—homicide in four cases, suicide in two—with SCP-4311 present and mounted in the front hallway throughout.

SCP-4311 does not respond to atmospheric pressure. Its needle position correlates, in retrospective analysis of the original residence's incident history and in one hundred and four subsequent Foundation trials, with the near-term probability of a violent death occurring to a specific, identifiable individual within line of sight of the instrument at the time of reading—not to any general population risk, but to one person, who the device does not otherwise indicate. When the needle rests in "FAIR" or drier, no correlation with elevated risk to anyone present has been established. When the needle enters the "CHANGE" region, Foundation trials have shown a measurable, elevated rate of minor accidents and interpersonal conflict among observers within the following six hours. When the needle reaches "STORMY," in eleven of eleven controlled trials to date, one observer present at the reading suffered a violent death, by widely varying means, within the following seventy-two hours, despite full awareness of the prediction and active Foundation intervention in nine of the eleven cases.

The two exceptions—both intervention attempts—were prevented from resulting in death only through measures the review board has since classified as extraordinary and non-repeatable: in one case, a would-be assailant's own sudden, unrelated fatal medical event; in the other, an equipment failure that the responsible researcher has since stated she does not believe was coincidental, without further elaboration.

SCP-4311 does not identify which observer is at risk, nor the manner or cause of the death it predicts. The Ethics Committee's central unresolved question, restated in each annual review since 1979 without resolution, is whether SCP-4311 forecasts violence that would occur regardless of its presence, or whether its reading is itself among the causes—whether, in some fashion not yet demonstrated but not yet excluded, the instrument does not merely watch the storm.

ADDENDUM 4311-1: SCP-4311 has, on three occasions since acquisition, been found relocated to a different wall within its containment room overnight, despite no indication of unauthorized entry and mounting hardware showing no sign of tool use. In each instance, the direction of relocation placed the instrument facing a different door than before. No pattern in the choice of door has yet been established.

SCP-4312.name: The Brass Handbell
SCP-4312.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4312 is classified Thaumiel and is held at Site-01 under direct O5 authority, stored unrung in a lead-lined case requiring simultaneous authorization from two O5 Council members for removal. Use of SCP-4312 constitutes an irreversible administrative action and may be authorized only for the express purpose of severing a named individual's documentary existence within Foundation and, where achievable, external records, as a measure of absolute last resort against information hazards, compromised personnel with hostile knowledge, or entities whose continued documentary existence poses unacceptable risk.

Every authorized use requires a completed Redaction Justification signed by both authorizing Council members and reviewed post-use by the Ethics Committee, which retains no power to reverse an application already made but may recommend disciplinary action against authorizing personnel. SCP-4312 has been used, per available records, on nine occasions since its acquisition by the Foundation in 1962.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4312 is a brass handbell of plain, undecorated manufacture, approximately 14 centimeters in height, bearing no maker's mark, foundry stamp, or inscription. Its origin prior to Foundation acquisition is undocumented; the site of its recovery is itself among the nine applications on record (see Addendum).

When rung within audible range of a specific named individual, with that individual's full legal name spoken aloud by the ringer at the moment of ringing, that individual's name and identifying documentary trace is removed, within an observed window of under one hour, from every physical and digital record accessible to the Foundation, and, per limited external verification conducted in three of the nine cases, from records held outside the Foundation as well, including government identification systems, in a manner the Foundation has not been able to replicate through any of its own information-access capabilities.

The affected individual is not killed, does not disappear physically, and retains full first-person memory of their own life and identity. However, every other person's documentary and administrative relationship to them is severed: colleagues' personnel files no longer list them, past correspondence no longer bears their name, and institutions the individual has dealt with—banks, employers, medical providers—cease to hold any record of their existence, typically within days, through processes (account closures, employment terminations, record consolidations) that appear mundane individually but which the Foundation has confirmed, in seven of nine cases, would not have occurred absent SCP-4312's use.

Personal, non-documentary memory in other individuals is not affected by SCP-4312: people who knew the affected individual personally, rather than through records, generally continue to remember them, though several report the memory becoming, over subsequent months, difficult to corroborate or discuss, "like describing someone you can't prove you met." Whether this represents ordinary memory decay or a secondary effect of SCP-4312 has not been established.

The nine known subjects of SCP-4312's use have not been definitively located for follow-up in any case; the Foundation's own tracking capability, which relies substantially on the documentary systems SCP-4312 removes its subjects from, is not effective against them by design.

ADDENDUM 4312-1: The most recent authorized use, in 20██, targeted a senior records archivist found to have independently reconstructed portions of a redacted historical incident through cross-referencing unrelated low-clearance documents over several years of unsupervised access—a capability the authorizing Council members' justification memo describes only as "a research method this Foundation cannot permit to become general practice." The archivist's current status, five years on, is unknown. Her name does not appear in this document.

SCP-4313.name: The Substitute Print
SCP-4313.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

SCP-4313 specimens (currently 14) are housed in a segmented, humidity-controlled aquarium (Containment Unit 4313-Delta) at Site-77, water changed weekly, substrate of sterilized sand and driftwood; feeding only with keratin pellets (do not permit incidental human contact). Any drain, pipe, or damp maintenance area within 500 meters of confirmed specimen presence is to be fitted with 0.5mm mesh filtration and inspected monthly by Containment personnel with training in molt-print identification. Any object bearing a fingerprint of unknown provenance recovered from a site with documented SCP-4313 activity is to be forwarded to Task Force Iota-9 ("Fingermen") for verification before use in any Foundation or civilian judicial, security, or identification process. Local law enforcement agencies operating within the contamination radius are not to be informed of SCP-4313's existence; Foundation liaisons are instead to monitor open criminal case files for anomalous print matches and arrange discreet suppression or reclassification of resulting evidence through established cover channels. Termination of specimens is prohibited pending completion of ongoing research into the biometric duplication mechanism (see Addendum 4313-2).

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4313 is a previously uncatalogued species of small (2-4cm carapace width) freshwater arthropod resembling Potamidae (freshwater crabs) but possessing an additional pair of specialized mouth-adjacent glands that secrete a keratin analogue. When an SCP-4313 specimen makes sustained tactile contact with human skin — typically during nocturnal foraging on sleeping or immobile subjects — it does not feed, but instead appears to record the ridge pattern of the contacted skin. Within 6-30 hours, the specimen deposits a thin, translucent secretion on a nearby hard surface (tile, glass, metal) that hardens into a raised, tactile, and optically indistinguishable reproduction of the recorded fingerprint. The mechanism by which the pattern is stored and reproduced is not understood; specimens possess no observable neurological structure capable of pattern retention exceeding several seconds.

Deposited prints (designated "molt-prints") pass standard forensic verification, including ridge-detail comparison, sweat-pore analysis, and most biometric scanner hardware, with a false-negative rate under laboratory testing of 0.3%. Molt-prints degrade and become undetectably brittle after approximately 90 days, after which they flake away, leaving no residue. SCP-4313 shows no preference for the identity or legal status of the individual whose print it reproduces; recovered molt-prints have matched subjects who were, at time of deposition, incarcerated, deceased, or otherwise demonstrably absent from the deposition location.

ADDENDUM 4313-1:

SCP-4313 was first identified after ███████ County Sheriff's Department submitted a print recovered from a residential burglary scene that matched a homeowner who had been deceased for eleven months. Foundation intervention prevented the case from proceeding to an exhumation order. Six additional convergent incidents across three states were later confirmed as SCP-4313 in origin.

ADDENDUM 4313-2:

Ongoing behavioral study seeks to determine whether SCP-4313 selects surfaces for molt-print deposition at random or according to some undetermined criterion; a working hypothesis, currently unconfirmed, holds that specimens preferentially deposit prints in locations where the reproduced individual will derive maximum consequence from the identification.

SCP-4314.name: The Simultaneous Bloom
SCP-4314.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Because SCP-4314 cannot be contained in the conventional sense (see Description), containment efforts are directed at documentation, sample collection, and information control rather than physical restraint. All Foundation sites housing more than 50 personnel are required to maintain a Bloom Response Team on 24-hour standby, equipped with sterile collection vessels, digital timestamping equipment, and NDA-briefed medical observers. Upon any confirmed SCP-4314 manifestation, the affected liquid body is not to be disturbed, drained, or covered for a minimum of eleven minutes, after which the specimen will have completed dissolution without intervention. Any specimen that fails to dissolve within fifteen minutes of first observation, or that is observed forming outside the context of a corresponding human death, is to be reported immediately to O5 Command as a Code Cerulean event, and the affected area placed under lockdown pending Level 5 authorization. Public and internal Foundation awareness of SCP-4314's correlation with mortality events is restricted to personnel holding 4314-specific clearance. Facility potable water systems, medical IV reservoirs, and standing water features are subject to unannounced Bloom Response drills no less than quarterly.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4314 is the designation given to a translucent, radially symmetric organism approximately 4-9 cm in diameter, morphologically consistent with Class Scyphozoa (true jellyfish) despite being observed exclusively outside marine environments. SCP-4314 does not swim, feed, or otherwise behave as a discrete organism prior to manifestation; rather, at the moment of a human subject's clinical death — defined as irreversible cessation of cardiac and respiratory function — one or more fully-formed SCP-4314 specimens appear, without transitional state, in every body of standing liquid exceeding 200mL located within an area that has varied across recorded incidents from 4 to 340 meters of the deceased. Manifestation is simultaneous across all qualifying liquid bodies to a precision better than can be measured with Foundation chronometric equipment (<0.01 seconds).

Specimens exhibit no response to physical stimuli, produce no detectable biochemical byproducts distinguishable from the medium they occupy, and dissolve without residue approximately 10-14 minutes after manifestation regardless of the liquid's temperature, salinity, or containment. No specimen has been successfully preserved, frozen, or removed from its medium of appearance; all such attempts result in immediate and complete dissolution. Tissue sampling performed within the window has recovered cellular material inconsistent with any known phylum, exhibiting protein structures that denature at standard laboratory temperature within seconds of extraction.

SCP-4314 was first identified in 2004 following simultaneous reports from three separate hospital wards in the same city, each describing a jellyfish-like organism appearing in a water pitcher, an aquarium, and a mop bucket respectively, within the same minute a patient died in a fourth, unconnected ward. Subsequent retrospective analysis of hospital and mortuary incident logs suggests SCP-4314 manifestations have been occurring, unrecognized, for a documented minimum of forty years prior to identification.

ADDENDUM 4314-1:

Because SCP-4314's manifestation is a reliable, if imprecisely bounded, indicator that a death has just occurred nearby, seventeen Foundation sites have incorporated unofficial Bloom monitoring into internal emergency response, using standing water features as passive mortality sensors. This practice has not been formally authorized by the Ethics Committee and remains a standing point of dispute; a 2021 review found that four sites had begun stationing observers near water features specifically to await manifestations, a practice the review characterized as "incompatible with the Foundation's stated relationship to human death" without recommending disciplinary action.

ADDENDUM 4314-2:

On one occasion, an SCP-4314 specimen was documented failing to dissolve on schedule; observers reported it remained motionless in a laboratory basin for six days before being examined further, at which point staff discovered the associated death had been misrecorded and the subject was, in fact, still alive in a persistent vegetative state at a facility 60km away. The subject died four hours after the specimen was first disturbed. This incident has not been repeated and remains unexplained.

SCP-4315.name: The Shared Nerve
SCP-4315.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The 214 known specimens of SCP-4315 are maintained as a single undivided colony in a 1,200-liter freshwater tank at Site-77, Containment Wing C. The colony is not to be divided, and no individual specimen is to be removed from the tank for any purpose without prior authorization from the Site Director, as removal beyond a distance of approximately 30 meters has been observed to induce measurable distress across the remaining colony (see Description). Personnel assigned to SCP-4315 husbandry duties for a cumulative period exceeding 40 hours are to be rotated out of the assignment and flagged in personnel records as "4315-Bonded"; such personnel are barred from participation in any Foundation procedure involving the deliberate infliction of pain or distress on detained or interviewed subjects, per Ethics Committee Ruling 4315-A.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4315 is a colony of small freshwater shrimp, individually unremarkable and consistent with known Atyidae morphology, which was first flagged for anomalous properties after Site-77 aquarium staff reported that injury to a single specimen — during routine tank maintenance — produced simultaneous guarding, withdrawal, and stress-hormone elevation across the entire colony, including specimens with no direct sensory access to the injured individual (opaque partition, separate water source). Subsequent testing confirmed that the colony functions, for purposes of nociception, as a single distributed organism: pain inflicted on any one specimen is registered, to a diminishing but measurable degree, by every other specimen in the colony regardless of physical separation, up to the current tested maximum of 4.1 kilometers.

The anomaly extends to human beings who maintain sustained physical or caretaking proximity to the colony. Personnel who have spent more than approximately 40 cumulative hours in direct contact with SCP-4315 (feeding, tank maintenance, handling) develop a measurable, though subclinical, physiological response when a colony specimen is injured — elevated heart rate, galvanic skin response, and in six documented cases, reported phantom pain in a limb corresponding to the injured specimen's damaged appendage. This "bonding" effect does not reverse with subsequent separation from the colony; three former Site-77 staff members transferred to other facilities in 2019 continued to register bonded responses during scheduled testing as of the most recent review.

The mechanism is unknown. SCP-4315 shrimp possess no observable shared neural tissue, electromagnetic signaling organ, or other structure that would account for either the intra-colony effect or its extension to bonded humans. Genetic sequencing shows no anomaly relative to baseline Atyidae.

ADDENDUM 4315-1:

SCP-4315's bonding effect was proposed by Dr. ██████ in 2018 as a potential interrogation-ethics safeguard: rotating bonded personnel through supervisory roles in high-duress interview procedures, on the theory that a bonded supervisor would register subclinical distress if an interview crossed into what the colony's aggregate nervous system would register as injurious. A twelve-month pilot produced inconsistent results and was suspended following an incident in which a bonded supervisor collapsed during an unrelated containment breach after a struck specimen was crushed during an evacuation; the correlation between these events was not proven, and the pilot has not been resumed pending further review.

ADDENDUM 4315-2:

The origin of the colony's first, founding specimens remains undocumented; site acquisition records from 1994 list them only as "biological samples, misc., aquarium stock," with no supplier of record.

SCP-4316.name: The Classification Spore
SCP-4316.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Cultivation of SCP-4316 is restricted to a single climate-controlled growth chamber (Mycology Wing, Site-19), maintained by personnel with Level 3/4316 clearance under Department of Applied Occult Biology oversight. Spore harvesting occurs on a fixed six-week cycle; harvested spore capsules are stored in nitrogen-sealed containers and issued only against a signed Field Exposure Authorization, individually numbered and tracked by the Office of the Director of Mobile Task Force Operations. Personnel administered SCP-4316 exposure ("Spored" personnel) are subject to mandatory quarterly neurological and psychological evaluation for the duration of their active service and for no fewer than five years following their final exposure. Unauthorized cultivation, spore theft, or off-protocol exposure is to be treated as a Class-2 security violation.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4316 is a fungal species of the order Agaricales, macroscopically resembling a pale bracket fungus, first recovered from the wall of a partially collapsed Cold War-era Foundation records annex in 1987. When its spores are inhaled by a human subject, they induce, within 20-40 minutes, a persistent cross-sensory condition in which the subject visually perceives a translucent overlay of text and color associated with any person, object, or location the subject observes that the Foundation has formally classified — object class, threat designation, containment status, or, in the case of personnel, security clearance level. The overlay is not read in any ordinary sense; subjects uniformly report it as an immediate, wordless apprehension that resolves, when attended to, into legible text in the subject's native language.

The mechanism producing this effect is unknown and has resisted all attempts at biochemical isolation; the active compound, tentatively designated 4316-A, has not been synthesized, and specimens grown from spores collected off-site (in one documented case, a fragment sent to an unwitting external contract laboratory) produce no such effect, suggesting the anomaly is not solely biochemical but somehow contingent on the fungus's continuity with Foundation documentation systems, a property the Department of Applied Occult Biology has termed "administrative entanglement" without further elaboration.

Exposure is not without cost. Approximately one in six Spored subjects report the overlay persisting indefinitely rather than the intended 72-96 hour window, with some cases exceeding four years at time of writing. Long-duration exposure correlates with a documented tendency for subjects to perceive classification overlays on objects, locations, and individuals the Foundation has never formally reviewed — the fungus appears, in these cases, to generate a classification rather than report one, and in at least three instances a subject's spontaneous "reading" of an unreviewed anomaly was later confirmed accurate by formal Foundation assessment conducted independently and after the fact.

ADDENDUM 4316-1:

SCP-4316 is currently issued to designated field agents ahead of high-risk site surveys as a supplement to standard anomaly-detection equipment, under the internal designation "Spore Protocol." Its Thaumiel classification reflects its sustained operational value; four site-collapse incidents between 2015 and 2023 are formally credited to early identification made possible by Spored personnel.

ADDENDUM 4316-2:

Dr. ██████, the researcher who has undergone the most cumulative SCP-4316 exposures (eleven), has in recent evaluations reported perceiving a classification overlay on herself. She has declined to disclose its content to evaluators, citing, per session transcript, "no clearance requirement that covers telling you." She remains on active duty pending psychological review.

SCP-4317.name: The False Chime
SCP-4317.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

All Foundation facilities in regions with confirmed SCP-4317 populations (currently limited to five temperate-zone site clusters) are required to install dual-authentication alarm hardware in which any fire, evacuation, or containment-breach alarm must be independently triggered from two physically separated control points before facility-wide broadcast occurs. Ventilation intakes and external wall penetrations are to be fitted with acoustic-dampening mesh rated to attenuate frequencies between 2-6 kHz, the band in which SCP-4317 mimicry is most accurate. Personnel are trained to verify any alarm event against the facility's digital incident log before initiating evacuation procedures; alarms not corroborated by a logged trigger event are to be treated as suspected SCP-4317 activity and reported to site Entomology Liaison staff rather than acted upon. Specimen capture is authorized using standard UV-lure traps outside facility perimeters; captured specimens are to be transferred live to Site-77 for study.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4317 is a species of large-bodied moth (forewing span 9-14 cm) externally similar to Saturniidae but distinguished by an enlarged, internally ridged thoracic structure capable of producing complex, sustained tonal sequences through rapid wing-case vibration. Structurally, this apparatus resembles known stridulatory organs in other Lepidoptera, but SCP-4317's version is capable of an unusual degree of acoustic precision and range.

SCP-4317's anomalous property is behavioral rather than physiological: specimens have been repeatedly observed and recorded reproducing, with waveform fidelity exceeding 98% match to source recordings, the standardized fire alarm tones, PA chime sequences, and synthesized evacuation announcements used by a range of institutional facilities, including — disproportionately relative to the moth's apparent global range — Foundation sites. No population of SCP-4317 has been observed mimicking any sound not associated with a building evacuation or emergency broadcast protocol; control recordings of ambient traffic noise, animal calls, and non-emergency human speech have never been reproduced by any captured specimen under laboratory conditions, despite specimens' evident capacity to do so mechanically.

Mimicry is typically performed at night, from concealment near building ventilation systems, and continues for the duration of a human evacuation response, ceasing abruptly once evacuated personnel are outdoors and dispersed — the point in a genuine evacuation at which personnel density in unlit or unmonitored areas is highest. Foundation entomology staff have not identified a feeding, mating, or predatory behavior directly following mimicry events, though three incidents of unexplained minor lacerations and one fatality attributed to a crowd-crush injury during an unverified SCP-4317-triggered evacuation at an external commercial facility remain under review for possible indirect correlation.

ADDENDUM 4317-1:

Genetic analysis places SCP-4317 as most closely related to moth populations first documented in the 1930s, predating the standardization of electronic fire alarm tones by several decades, raising an unresolved question as to how or when the species' mimicry repertoire came to include sounds that did not exist at the time of its apparent divergence from known Saturniidae lineages.

SCP-4318.name: The Ear Orchard
SCP-4318.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

All confirmed SCP-4318 seed-bearing plant matter is to be incinerated at the site of discovery; no viable seed is to be transported for storage or study under any circumstances (see Incident 4318-Kilo). Personnel operating in regions with confirmed SCP-4318 presence, currently seven sites across two temperate river-valley ecosystems, are required to wear sealed in-ear protection rated to exclude particulate matter below 40 microns at all times when outside sealed vehicles or structures. Any individual reporting sudden, localized hearing improvement, unexplained tinnitus, or auditory perception of sound sources later confirmed to be beyond normal hearing range is to be quarantined immediately and referred for Level 3 medical evaluation under Protocol 4318-Extraction. Extraction of germinated specimens from a host ear canal is to be performed only by Site-77 surgical staff; field extraction is prohibited following the fatality recorded in Incident 4318-Kilo.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4318 is a flowering plant of unknown taxonomic family, superficially resembling dodder (Cuscuta spp.) in its parasitic, leafless growth habit. SCP-4318 seeds are viable only within the human ear canal; germination has not been observed on any other substrate, living or inert, despite extensive testing. Seeds enter the ear canal through normal environmental contact — wind-borne dispersal has been documented at distances exceeding 800 meters from the nearest known parent plant — and germinate within 48-72 hours given sufficient ambient humidity, producing a fine, pale root structure that anchors in the auditory canal without perforating the tympanic membrane in the majority of documented cases.

Over a subsequent period of 10-16 days, the germinated specimen develops a secondary structure Foundation biologists have termed an "auxiliary array": a cluster of thread-fine filaments that extend along the ear canal and, in seventeen documented cases, into the middle ear via the Eustachian tube, without triggering conventional infection response or reported pain. Hosts uniformly report a period of enhanced auditory acuity during array development, followed by a distinct secondary phase in which they report perceiving sounds inconsistent with their physical environment — voices, ambient noise, and in nine cases, fragments of speech that hosts identified, upon later investigation, as originating from other confirmed SCP-4318 hosts at the time, at distances the host could not otherwise perceive by any known means.

The plant reaches reproductive maturity 25-30 days post-germination, at which point a small flowering structure emerges from the host's ear canal, remaining for approximately four days before releasing a new generation of airborne seed and withering. Extraction prior to flowering is survivable in the large majority of cases; extraction after flowering has begun has, in all six attempted cases, resulted in immediate profound hearing loss in the affected ear, in three cases bilateral.

ADDENDUM 4318-Kilo:

A field extraction attempted by unauthorized personnel at ██████ resulted in the host's death, apparently from cardiac arrest, at the moment of extraction; a second SCP-4318 host present at the same site, located 340 meters away with no line of sight or conventional audible range to the first, was independently observed to collapse at the same instant, sustaining no extraction-related injury of her own. She survived and, upon recovery, stated only that "it stopped, and then it was very quiet," declining to elaborate further despite repeated interview attempts.

SCP-4319.name: The Inverted Wood
SCP-4319.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The current extent of SCP-4319 (approximately 340 hectares of mixed temperate forest designated Site-77-Annex) is enclosed by a double perimeter fence, an outer conventional barrier and an inner electrified line calibrated to non-lethal thresholds for animals up to 25kg, monitored by thermal camera coverage with no gaps exceeding 15 meters. Foundation-owned land bordering the affected area is not to be logged, cleared, or otherwise disturbed in a manner that might create new lichen dispersal vectors. Any animal, of any size, observed exiting the containment perimeter is to be captured alive where feasible and held in isolated veterinary quarantine for no fewer than 30 days before release or further disposition, owing to the extended latency period documented for behavioral effects (see Description). Entry to SCP-4319's interior requires Hazard Team escort and is restricted to personnel briefed on the Standing Prey Protocol, under which the smallest organism in any observed interaction is to be treated as the more dangerous party regardless of species or apparent size differential.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4319 is a crustose lichen species, likely a fungal-algal symbiosis within the order Lecanorales, found growing on the bark of an expanding stand of oak, birch, and pine trees. Trees colonized by SCP-4319 show no distinguishing external symptoms beyond the lichen's grey-green growth pattern and a documented, unexplained 12-18% increase in canopy density relative to uncolonized trees of comparable age nearby.

Fauna resident within an SCP-4319-colonized area for a sustained period — current data suggests a minimum exposure threshold of approximately three weeks — undergo a durable reversal of predator-avoidance and predatory behavior relative to their position in the local trophic hierarchy. Small mammals, ground-nesting birds, and invertebrates that would ordinarily constitute prey species have been repeatedly documented initiating and completing successful predatory attacks on animals many times their mass, including foxes, domestic dogs, and, in one instance, a white-tailed deer killed over eleven hours by a coordinated group of eastern chipmunks. Conversely, larger animals within the affected zone display avoidance behavior toward smaller fauna disproportionate to any conventional threat those smaller animals pose, including documented cases of adult red foxes fleeing single field mice.

The mechanism is not fully understood.
