SCP-4319 spores, recovered from air samples within the affected zone, contain a novel alkaloid compound (tentatively 4319-A) that, when administered to control animals in laboratory conditions, produces measurable but temporary reductions in threat-response latency; however, laboratory-dosed animals have not replicated the sustained, apparently durable behavioral reversal observed in the field, and no laboratory subject has successfully preyed upon an animal larger than itself. Researchers have not ruled out an additional, uncharacterized component of the effect contingent on continued proximity to living SCP-4319 growth, structural terrain features, or an as-yet unidentified variable.

ADDENDUM 4319-1:

Satellite and ground survey data indicate the SCP-4319-colonized area has expanded at a rate of approximately 4% per year since its 2009 identification, a rate that does not correlate with any measured rate of lichen spore dispersal recorded in comparable non-anomalous Lecanorales species, and which current containment measures have not meaningfully slowed.

SCP-4320.name: The Static Colony
SCP-4320.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Because SCP-4320 individuals cannot be reliably identified via any camera or recording device (see Description), containment relies on physical trapping and direct human observation rather than surveillance. All confirmed SCP-4320 burrow sites are to be fitted with pressure-sensitive floor plating and infrared motion sensors (non-visual sensor types remain unaffected by the anomaly) connected directly to an audible on-site alarm; camera coverage of these areas should be maintained for standard purposes but is not to be relied upon as evidence of specimen presence or absence in incident reports. Personnel filing incident reports involving suspected SCP-4320 activity are not required to produce corroborating footage, per Directive 4320-Administrative, and are to have such reports accepted on the basis of direct testimony alone, cross-referenced where possible against the physical sensor log. Specimens captured in live traps are to be transferred to Site-77 Bioacoustics Lab for study; euthanasia is not authorized without Level 4 approval.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4320 is a colony of subterranean rodents, approximately 22cm in body length, sharing morphological characteristics with both Heterocephalus glaber (naked mole-rat) and larger fossorial rodent species, distinguished by dense, short fur exhibiting a fine, high-contrast mottled pattern. To unaided human vision, SCP-4320 specimens are entirely unremarkable and visible under normal conditions; the anomaly manifests exclusively in any photographic, video, or other optical recording medium, in which SCP-4320 specimens do not appear as themselves but are instead replaced, in the recorded image, by a localized region of visual noise closely resembling analog signal interference or digital compression artifacting, regardless of recording technology, resolution, or lighting conditions.

The obscuring effect applies only to the specimen's body; objects the specimen is in contact with, disturbed matter, and any other animal or object do not display equivalent artifacting. The effect has been confirmed across thirty-one distinct camera and recording technologies tested by Foundation researchers, including devices with no shared manufacturer, sensor type, or processing pipeline, and has resisted every attempted correction in post-processing; forensic imaging staff have been unable to identify any consistent digital signature explaining the artifact's generation, and the affected image region cannot be reconstructed from surrounding frame data by any method tested.

SCP-4320's practical containment difficulty stems primarily from institutional friction rather than physical escape: personnel reporting specimen sightings, property damage, or minor bite injuries have, on eleven documented occasions prior to Directive 4320-Administrative, had incident reports rejected or downgraded by reviewing staff on the stated grounds that available camera footage did not substantiate the claim, despite the footage in each case showing the now-recognized static artifact at the reported time and location.

ADDENDUM 4320-1:

Following the introduction of infrared and pressure-sensor corroboration, colony population at the primary containment site has been estimated at 40-70 individuals, though no visual count has ever been possible, and Foundation researchers acknowledge the population estimate cannot be independently confirmed by any recorded means.

SCP-4321.name: The Foretelling Shell
SCP-4321.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The seven known living SCP-4321 specimens are held in individual climate-controlled enclosures at Site-19, Biological Containment Wing E, isolated from one another and from all non-essential staff. Non-lethal shell imaging (see Addendum 4321-1) is the only authorized method of examining growth-ring content; lethal biopsy or shell sectioning of a living specimen requires unanimous O5 Council authorization and has been granted only twice. All imaging data derived from SCP-4321 shells is classified at a minimum of Level 4 and is to be reviewed exclusively by the standing Foretelling Review Committee, whose members are subject to mandatory rotation every eighteen months and post-service psychological monitoring for a minimum of three years. Under no circumstances is imaging data to be cross-referenced against ongoing Foundation operations by personnel with operational authority over those operations, per Ethics Committee Ruling 4321-C ("the Committee finds no configuration of this practice compatible with sound decision-making").

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4321 is a species of freshwater turtle, morphologically similar to Chrysemys picta (painted turtle) but reaching a documented maximum size of 68cm carapace length, well in excess of any known related species. Like ordinary chelonians, SCP-4321 shells develop concentric growth rings (scutes) over the animal's lifespan; unlike ordinary chelonians, cross-sectional and high-resolution surface imaging of these rings reveals embedded, non-biological patterning consisting of discrete pictographic and, in several cases, alphanumeric content.

Content recovered from SCP-4321 growth rings has, in eighteen of twenty-two cases subjected to long-term follow-up, subsequently corresponded — with an average lead time of 4.7 years — to real-world events occurring at a location associated with the specimen's origin or holding site, including two localized natural disasters, one industrial accident, and, in a single widely-discussed internal case, the layout of a Foundation site breach that occurred six years after the corresponding ring was formed and photographed. The mechanism by which the shell generates this content, and its relationship (if any) to genuine precognition as opposed to sophisticated coincidence or self-fulfilling interpretation, remains formally unresolved; the Foretelling Review Committee has explicitly declined to characterize confirmed matches as "predictions" in any official documentation, citing the impossibility of ruling out interpretive bias applied retroactively to ambiguous imagery.

New growth rings form on an irregular schedule averaging one every 14-20 months, are only legible via specialized imaging performed by trained personnel, and cannot be induced, accelerated, or their content influenced by any tested intervention, including controlled environmental stress, dietary manipulation, or direct handling. Rings are permanently legible from the moment of formation; there is no evidence the content changes or updates once recorded.

ADDENDUM 4321-1:

A non-lethal ultrasonic cross-sectional imaging technique was developed in 2017, reducing reliance on lethal biopsy; two specimens sacrificed prior to this development remain the only complete internal shell records obtained, and their full ring content, preserved on file, has not been fully reviewed for lead-time correspondence given the volume of ambiguous imagery involved.

ADDENDUM 4321-2:

Specimen 4321-4 developed a ring in 2022 that the Review Committee, after extended deliberation, formally declined to open for General Staff review, on grounds stated in the closed session record only as "premature." The ring's content remains sealed pending further O5 review.

SCP-4322.name: The Containing Hive
SCP-4322.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The SCP-4322 apiary (currently 40 hives, approx. 2.1 million individuals) is maintained at Site-64, a facility purpose-built around a rotating collection of low-risk Safe- and Euclid-class anomalous objects held specifically to sustain hive productivity (see Description). Hive placement relative to housed anomalies is managed by Apiary Staff in consultation with the Department of Applied Occult Biology according to a standing rotation schedule; no single anomaly is to remain in proximity to the same hive subset for longer than 90 days, a limit informally adopted after Incident 4322-Bravo. Harvested SCP-4322 wax ("suppressant wax") is stored under standard cold-chain protocol and is issued to Task Forces and Containment Teams Foundation-wide for temporary field suppression of qualifying anomalous properties, subject to the limitations described in Addendum 4322-1. Any hive subset observed constructing comb oriented toward a specific compass bearing for more than 72 continuous hours is to be reported to Apiary Staff, as this behavior has preceded three of the four confirmed instances of unassisted anomaly discovery by SCP-4322 (see Addendum 4322-2).

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4322 is a eusocial bee species outwardly consistent with Apis mellifera (Western honey bee) in size, morphology, and colony structure, first identified after an independent apiarist reported that honey harvested from a hive situated near an undisclosed anomalous rock formation temporarily and partially suppressed the formation's minor reality-bending properties when applied directly to its surface. SCP-4322 colonies require regular proximity — within approximately 15 meters, with diminishing effect beyond — to an active anomalous object or entity in order to produce viable suppressant wax; colonies denied such proximity for longer than approximately six weeks cease wax production entirely and revert to producing ordinary, non-anomalous honey and wax, though colony health is not otherwise affected.

Suppressant wax, when applied directly to an anomalous object's surface or, in the case of biological anomalies, to skin or analogous tissue, produces a temporary (typically 6-30 hours, varying by anomaly) reduction in the potency or activity of a subset of anomalous properties, most reliably those involving matter transformation, low-level cognitive influence, and localized reality alteration; wax has shown negligible or no effect on anomalies involving temporal manipulation, extradimensional properties, or Keter-class self-sustaining processes. The compound responsible has not been isolated; standard chemical analysis of suppressant wax shows no meaningful difference from ordinary beeswax.

SCP-4322 colonies have, on four documented occasions, been observed altering foraging patterns and comb orientation in ways later found to correlate with the presence of a previously uncatalogued anomalous object within their foraging range, in each case preceding Foundation identification of the object by conventional means by between nine and thirty-one days. The mechanism by which colonies detect anomalous properties at a distance is unknown.

ADDENDUM 4322-1:

Suppressant wax's dependency on ambient anomalous exposure for both production and, per emerging research, potency, has prevented full synthetic replication; three attempts to reproduce the compound using isolated 4322 genetic material outside an active apiary environment have failed to produce wax with any suppressant property.

ADDENDUM 4322-2 (Incident 4322-Bravo):

In 2019, a hive subset maintained near SCP-████ for 140 consecutive days, exceeding the since-adopted 90-day limit, began producing wax with suppressant properties inverted — that is, wax that measurably intensified rather than suppressed the treated anomaly's properties. The affected hive subset was destroyed. The 90-day rotation limit was adopted following this incident and has not since been exceeded.

SCP-4323.name: The Autopsy Culture
SCP-4323.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

The remaining sample of SCP-4323 culture medium (currently 1.4 liters, Site-77 Cold Storage, Sub-Level 3) is stored in triple-sealed cryogenic containment at -80°C. Access requires joint authorization from the Site Director and the Department of Pathology and is logged individually per use; no single withdrawal in excess of 4mL is permitted without Level 4 review. Any deceased tissue exposed to SCP-4323, whether intentionally in an authorized procedure or accidentally, is to be treated as active for the full duration of the subsequent procedure and is not to be left unattended or unmonitored at any point between exposure and the procedure's formal conclusion. All personnel present during an SCP-4323-assisted procedure are required to undergo post-procedure psychological debriefing; six of the eleven personnel who have participated in such procedures have subsequently declined further assignment involving SCP-4323 without disciplinary consequence.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4323 is a culture of an undetermined bacterial species recovered in 1991 from a mislabeled specimen jar in a decommissioned Foundation mortuary freezer at a since-closed facility; the jar's accompanying documentation, largely illegible, appears to date from no later than 1962. Culture medium, when applied topically to human tissue that has been deceased for no more than approximately six hours, induces a localized and temporary reanimation effect in the treated tissue and any anatomically connected musculature, restricted almost entirely to passive, cooperative movement — limb repositioning under manual guidance, relaxation of rigor-affected muscle groups, and, in a minority of cases, simple reflex-consistent responses to direct stimulus.

The defining anomalous property of SCP-4323 is not the reanimation itself, which Foundation researchers consider broadly consistent, if far exceeding typical duration and control, with known post-mortem muscular phenomena, but its temporal precision: treated tissue reliably ceases all responsive activity at the exact moment a procedure being performed upon it — surgical, forensic, or, in the majority of documented applications, an autopsy — is declared complete by the presiding examiner, regardless of the procedure's actual planned or expected duration, and regardless of whether the cessation point was communicated aloud, recorded only in the examiner's notes, or, in four controlled trials, decided upon but not yet documented in any form. No treated specimen has ceased activity prior to a procedure's declared conclusion, and no treated specimen has continued activity for a measurable interval beyond it; the observed margin in seventy-nine trials has not exceeded four seconds in either direction.

SCP-4323 shows no capacity for movement, response, or reanimation effect outside the context of an ongoing, formally recognized examination or procedure; tissue treated and then left without any procedure being performed upon it exhibits no reanimation whatsoever, behaving as ordinary deceased tissue.

ADDENDUM 4323-1:

In trial 4323-52, the presiding examiner privately decided, without recording or verbalizing the decision, to extend a scheduled autopsy by an additional unplanned procedure after noting an anomaly in the specimen's tissue; the treated remains ceased activity at the originally scheduled, unextended conclusion time, three minutes before the examiner's unspoken revision would have taken effect. The examiner has since requested reassignment away from further SCP-4323 trials.

ADDENDUM 4323-2:

The original source of the bacterial culture, and the identity of the 1962-era researcher or researchers responsible for its collection, has not been established. No further specimens of SCP-4323 have been located despite repeated search of the originating facility's remaining archived holdings.

SCP-4324.name: The Filing Spider
SCP-4324.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

All Foundation records facilities are to conduct quarterly inspection of any physical storage container previously or currently holding personnel termination documentation (voluntary separation, involuntary dismissal, or documentation using the Foundation's operational-termination euphemism, hereafter "Class-T records") for SCP-4324 web presence. Confirmed webs are not to be removed, cleaned, or disturbed except by Archives staff holding 4324-specific training; web strands recovered during authorized document destruction procedures are to be preserved separately and forwarded to Site-77 Archives for cataloguing rather than destroyed alongside the source documents. Standard document destruction procedures (shredding, incineration) for Class-T records are not altered by SCP-4324's presence and remain otherwise mandatory per existing retention schedules; Archives staff are reminded that SCP-4324 web recovery does not constitute an exception to those schedules and is not to be cited as a reason to delay or forgo required destruction.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-4324 is a species of small (leg span 1.5-3cm), pale, unpigmented spider of uncertain family, distinguished by an exclusive and highly specific web-site preference: SCP-4324 individuals build webs only within enclosed physical storage containing what the Foundation designates Class-T personnel records, and have never been observed nesting in any other document type, container type, or non-document environment, despite extensive relocation testing.

SCP-4324 silk possesses two anomalous properties. First, it exhibits tensile strength exceeding any known natural or synthetic fiber by a factor of approximately 40, resisting cutting, burning below 900°C, and dissolution by all tested solvents; strands recovered from decommissioned cabinets have survived building fires that destroyed the surrounding structure. Second, and more significantly, microscopic examination of SCP-4324 silk recovered from a container holding Class-T records reveals a fine internal structural patterning that, when magnified and processed through standard document-imaging software, resolves into legible reproductions of the specific document text the silk's supporting web was spun in proximity to — including documents subsequently shredded, incinerated, or otherwise formally destroyed under standard retention-expiry procedures.

This property was first identified in 2013 during an internal audit that recovered the presumed-destroyed termination order for a Foundation researcher dismissed in 1988 for unspecified cause, reconstructed in full from silk recovered from the researcher's original personnel cabinet decades after the physical document had been shredded per standard retention policy. Subsequent deliberate testing has confirmed the effect is consistent and reproducible: SCP-4324 webs constructed in proximity to Class-T documents reliably preserve legible text content independent of the physical document's subsequent fate, with no observed exception across forty-one controlled trials.

SCP-4324 shows no anomalous properties in any other respect; specimens feed on ordinary insects, reproduce at typical arachnid rates, and show no unusual longevity, size, or aggression. The species has been observed at Foundation records facilities on four continents, with no established means of transmission or introduction between sites, and no specimen has been observed at any facility prior to that facility's first stored Class-T record.

ADDENDUM 4324-1:

The Office of Internal Compliance has, following the 2013 discovery, incorporated authorized SCP-4324 silk recovery into three separate internal misconduct investigations where the underlying Class-T documentation had been improperly or prematurely destroyed. This practice remains formally unacknowledged in Archives policy, and no directive currently requires Class-T record custodians to disclose the presence of confirmed SCP-4324 webs prior to requesting document destruction.

SCP-4325.name: The Average Man
SCP-4325.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4325 is housed in a standard single-occupancy unit at Site-77 under the cover identity of a long-term voluntary research participant. A live data feed from the national statistics institute, the ministry of health's actuarial office, and three anonymized insurance-industry datasets is to be maintained at all times; any interruption longer than six hours requires immediate medical standby, as SCP-4325's biometric readings destabilize without a reference population to track.
The reference population SCP-4325 is anchored to must be selected and documented in writing by the Site Director, and changed only with O5 authorization. Anchoring SCP-4325 to the general national population is Foundation default policy, as it produces the least volatile fluctuations. Anchoring him to smaller or more specialized populations (e.g., Foundation personnel) is prohibited outside of sanctioned research detailed in Addendum 4325-1.
SCP-4325's identification documents are to be reissued quarterly, as his legal name, birth date, and listed occupation drift toward whatever values are most statistically common within his anchor population that quarter. Staff are instructed to address him by his current legal name only; use of prior names has been observed to cause disorientation lasting several hours.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4325 is a human male, apparent age 35–45, first identified in 2015 when a routine hospital admission flagged his bloodwork as matching six national health averages to a degree of precision statistically impossible for an individual (p < 10^-11 across independent measures). Subsequent monitoring confirmed that SCP-4325's vital signs, body mass, cholesterol and glucose levels, household income bracket, marital status, and even his statistically likely cause of death continuously converge on the current mean values for his anchor population, updating within hours of any shift in the underlying data.
The effect extends beyond biology. SCP-4325's employment history, educational attainment, and consumer habits reorganize to track the modal values reported in labor and retail statistics. His body has been documented to acquire and lose scars, surgical histories, and even minor old injuries consistent with population-wide incidence rates, seemingly retroactively — hospital and school records external to Foundation custody have on three occasions been found to already reflect these changes, suggesting the anomaly edits documentation it did not create.
SCP-4325 retains awareness of these changes but experiences them as a form of memory drift rather than sudden replacement; he reports "remembering" a childhood, a job, a marriage that he knows intellectually did not happen to him, with a persistent, low-grade sense that his memories belong to someone else on loan. He has not been able to independently verify what, if anything, was true about him before Foundation acquisition.

ADDENDUM 4325-1:
In 2019, researchers confirmed that briefly re-anchoring SCP-4325 to the Foundation's own personnel population caused his vitals to shift in ways that correlated with concealed data — elevated population-wide markers for stress-related illness preceded, by roughly eleven days, an unreported containment breach at a separate site. This use has since been repeated four times as an unofficial early-warning instrument, a practice the Ethics Committee has formally objected to twice without success.
SCP-4325 has asked, on file, to be told what population he would revert to if left completely unanchored. Per the results of a single unauthorized 2021 test, terminated after nine hours when his vitals approached the population's mean age at death, this question remains formally unanswered.

SCP-4326.name: The Inherited Death
SCP-4326.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known carriers of SCP-4326 are to be registered under the Lineage Watch program and monitored via biannual welfare checks rather than physical containment, as the anomaly poses no direct threat to personnel and involuntary confinement has been shown to accelerate onset. Carriers are first-born daughters of a woman who died as a result of SCP-4326; approximately 340 individuals across six documented family lines are currently under observation.
Field agents assigned to Lineage Watch are prohibited from disclosing the mechanism of SCP-4326 to carriers under the age of twenty-five except with Ethics Committee approval, following the 1998 Adana incident in which early disclosure was assessed to have contributed to onset by way of anticipatory anxiety. Carriers who request full disclosure after their twenty-fifth birthday are to receive it, along with a standing offer of relocation, occupational reassignment away from any circumstance resembling their mother's death, and continuous psychological support. Fourteen carriers to date have accepted long-term relocation; none who accepted before onset have yet died of SCP-4326.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4326 is a hereditary anomaly affecting the first-born daughter in certain maternal lines, causing the carrier to die by a method closely resembling — in physical mechanism, location type, and often approximate age — the death of her mother, in cases where the mother's death is itself attributable to SCP-4326. The pattern has been traced back at least five generations in its oldest documented line, with no identified originating incident.
Carriers do not appear to be forced toward their deaths by any detectable external force; instead, affected individuals report a gradual narrowing of ordinary decision-making in the months and, in acute cases, hours before death, describing plausible, mundane reasons for choices that happen to reconstruct their mother's final circumstances — changing a commute, revisiting a closed relationship, delaying a medical appointment. Interviewed carriers who survived near-miss incidents describe the sensation as indistinguishable from ordinary free will at the time, becoming legible only in retrospect.
SCP-4326 does not activate in daughters whose mothers died of unrelated causes, nor does interrupting one occurrence prevent the anomaly from later affecting that carrier's own first-born daughter through a different but structurally similar death. Three documented interventions successfully prevented an individual death; in each case, the carrier survived to old age, but her daughter later died in a manner Foundation analysts assessed as thematically, though not mechanically, consistent with the grandmother's original death — suggesting SCP-4326 tracks a symbolic rather than literal template.

ADDENDUM:
A 2022 proposal to attempt full lineage termination through voluntary non-reproduction counseling was tabled after Ethics Committee review concluded the Foundation could not ethically direct reproductive decisions, however framed as advisory. The proposal remains formally unresolved. Several carriers under long-term relocation have independently asked whether choosing not to have a daughter would end the pattern for their line. No carrier has yet been given a confirmed answer, as the Foundation has not observed a lineage terminate this way and cannot rule out other transmission mechanisms.

SCP-4327.name: The Unlived Backup
SCP-4327.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4327-B, the dormant secondary consciousness residing within SCP-4327-A's nervous system, is to remain unactivated under all circumstances except a Level 4-authorized declaration of SCP-4327-A's imminent, unpreventable death. SCP-4327-A resides in a standard personnel apartment at Site-77 under a voluntary consultancy contract and is free to leave the site, subject to standard tracking for anomalous individuals of unclear origin.
The activation procedure, which requires a specific combination of controlled cardiac arrest and electrical stimulus documented in Document 4327-A-1, is to be known only to the assigned on-call physician and the Site Director. SCP-4327-A has formally requested, and been denied, the right to know this procedure himself, on the grounds that foreknowledge could allow self-activation, an outcome assessed as constituting the effective death of SCP-4327-A's current personality.
SCP-4327-B is not to be activated for research, testing, or any purpose other than genuine life preservation. This restriction has been violated once (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4327-A is a human male, age 41, who presented to a Foundation-affiliated hospital in 2020 for an unrelated injury. Imaging incidentally revealed a second, fully formed set of neural structures overlaid on his own, inactive but showing baseline metabolic activity inconsistent with dead or vestigial tissue. Subsequent non-invasive testing identified this structure, designated SCP-4327-B, as a complete secondary personality matrix: a full set of memories, skills, and dispositional traits belonging to a person who has never been conscious and has no personal history, having apparently existed in this dormant state since SCP-4327-A's early childhood.
Limited diagnostic communication with SCP-4327-B (achieved through partial, temporary activation under strict protocol, see Addendum) indicates it possesses awareness of itself as separate from SCP-4327-A, describes itself using a different name of its own choosing, and is cognizant that its only path to sustained consciousness runs through SCP-4327-A's death. SCP-4327-B has expressed neither impatience nor distress at this arrangement in the two sessions conducted to date, a response staff psychologists have been unable to characterize as either healthy acceptance or profound repression, given the impossibility of applying ordinary developmental frameworks to an entity that has never lived.
SCP-4327-A is aware of SCP-4327-B's existence and has described the knowledge as "living next to my own replacement," but has not requested removal or destruction of the secondary structure, citing uncertainty over whether doing so would constitute killing something.

ADDENDUM:
In 2021, a since-terminated researcher conducted an unauthorized full activation of SCP-4327-B lasting four minutes, during which SCP-4327-A's own consciousness was suppressed. SCP-4327-B, questioned briefly before re-suppression, asked only where SCP-4327-A currently was and whether the activation was permanent. On being informed it was not, SCP-4327-B did not resist deactivation. SCP-4327-A retains no memory of the four minutes and has not been informed that the incident occurred beyond a formal, mandatory disclosure filed to comply with Foundation informed-consent policy for anomalous test subjects. He has not asked follow-up questions.

SCP-4328.name: The Deeded Man
SCP-4328.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4328 is held at Site-77 in a reinforced residential unit whose boundary is marked, on all sides, by a physical property line surveyed and registered with a cover municipal land registry as belonging to a Foundation shell entity, "Anadolu Miras Holding." This registration is not cosmetic: testing has confirmed SCP-4328's anomalous transportation effect (see Description) responds specifically to registered legal ownership of the parcel he occupies, and any lapse, dispute, or transfer of this registration carries an extreme risk of immediate, uncontrolled relocation.
The Foundation's ownership documentation must be renewed no fewer than sixty days before any expiration date, verified independently by Legal and Records divisions, and never allowed to overlap with a rival claim, however spurious. Three historical claimants to the original 1867 deed underlying SCP-4328's anomaly have been identified; all current descendants are under discreet Foundation monitoring, and any legal action they initiate regarding the original property is to be intercepted and neutralized through civil proceedings before reaching public record.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4328 is a human male, apparent age 50, who is the current living subject of an Ottoman-era property deed (Document 4328-Deed, translated and archived) transferring ownership not of land, but of a named individual, to a specified family line, dated 1867 and never formally annulled under subsequent legal regimes. Foundation legal analysis has been unable to determine the deed's origin or the identity of the original grantor.
SCP-4328's anomalous property is total and literal enforcement of this deed regardless of its legal unenforceability under any modern jurisdiction: whichever party holds documented legal title to the deed — or, functionally, to any parcel of land the Foundation has caused to be legally associated with the original deed's registry entry — SCP-4328 will relocate to, instantaneously and without regard for intervening distance or physical barriers, should that title change hands. This has occurred four times since Foundation contact in 1994, each following a change in registered ownership of the anchor parcel, including one incident in which a records clerk's clerical error transferred SCP-4328 to a private citizen's unrelated grocery store for eleven hours before the Foundation reasserted title.
SCP-4328 has aged apparently normally and shows no injury from these transfers, but has described the process as "belonging to paper." He retains full cognitive function and personal memory, is cooperative with Foundation staff, and has on multiple occasions asked whether the original deed could be destroyed. Foundation legal counsel has assessed that destruction of the physical document does not appear to affect the anomaly, as a certified 1962 photographic copy has been shown to retain identical enforcement capability.

ADDENDUM:
SCP-4328 was legally born free; Foundation historical research has found no record of the original 1867 transaction's terms, consideration paid, or whether the individual originally deeded gave any form of consent. SCP-4328's own family history was lost prior to Foundation contact, and he does not know if he is a direct descendant of that individual or an unrelated person onto whom the deed's effect has, at some point, transferred. This question remains under passive historical investigation, without result.

SCP-4329.name: The Man Who Undoes Small Things
SCP-4329.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4329 resides in a modified apartment at Site-77 containing no fragile, perishable, or single-use items of significant research or sentimental value, as objects within an approximately four-meter radius of SCP-4329 are subject to intermittent local temporal reversal (see Description). Staff entering this radius should expect minor, harmless reversals of recent actions — a poured drink returning to its container, a closed door reopening — and are advised these effects are not dangerous but may be disorienting; new personnel receive a mandatory orientation briefing before first contact.
SCP-4329 is permitted standard personal effects and a research stipend. Because the reversal effect does not extend to living tissue or to events older than approximately ninety seconds, no special medical containment is required. SCP-4329 has voluntarily agreed to wear a wrist-mounted event logger to assist ongoing study of the anomaly's triggering conditions, which remain only partially understood.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4329 is a human male, age 29, around whom minor physical events — those involving small objects, short timeframes, and low energy — spontaneously reverse in a localized region of space, restoring the object or event to its state roughly sixty to ninety seconds prior. Reversed events include, among hundreds logged: a dropped cup reassembling and returning to a table edge; a struck match re-igniting and un-burning; a torn piece of paper rejoining; a spilled coffee ring receding into a mug already refilled to its pre-pour level.
The effect appears to trigger unpredictably, at a mean rate of 2.3 times per day, and does not respond to conscious control by SCP-4329, who reports the events as no more noticeable to him than a hiccup, and has described living with them since early childhood as "the world stuttering near me." No correlation has been established between SCP-4329's emotional state and the frequency or scale of reversals, though a slight increase in frequency (unconfirmed, n=1 subject) was logged during a period of documented insomnia in 2021.
The reversal never affects objects or events beyond the local radius, never reverses an action taken by SCP-4329 himself with apparent intent (he cannot, for instance, use the effect to un-drop something on purpose), and has never been observed to reverse an event involving injury, however minor — a paper cut sustained by a researcher in 2020 did not heal or un-happen despite occurring well within range and timeframe, a discrepancy that remains unexplained.

ADDENDUM:
SCP-4329 has requested clarification on why the anomaly appears to protect small objects from minor accidents but never protects people from harm, including, on one occasion, himself — a 2022 incident in which he cut his hand on broken glass produced by a reversal-affected object went unreversed, despite the glass itself un-breaking around the wound seconds later. He was informed that Foundation researchers do not currently have an answer. He has not raised the question again.

SCP-4330.name: The Convenient World
SCP-4330.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4330 is housed in a dedicated isolation wing at Site-77, physically separated from unshielded infrastructure by no less than 200 meters in all directions. All personnel entering the wing must complete a full inventory of relevant personal and environmental facts (route taken, objects carried, appointments scheduled) before and after contact, to allow detection of SCP-4330-induced discrepancies. This procedure has flagged discrepancies in 31% of logged contacts.
SCP-4330 must never be informed, directly or through inference, that his environment has been altered on his behalf, as confirmed awareness has twice preceded a measurable increase in alteration severity (see Incident 4330-3). Staff are trained to respond naturally to any environmental inconsistency SCP-4330 does not himself remark upon, and to avoid displaying confusion in his presence.
Due to the risk of large-scale historical alteration, SCP-4330 is barred from unsupervised access to news media, correspondence with family, or any activity through which he might learn of an event he would find distressing enough to unconsciously prefer altered.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4330 is a human male, age 53, a former municipal clerk first flagged in 2017 after Foundation analysts investigating an unrelated anomaly noticed that three independent historical records disagreed about a minor local event in ways that consistently favored a version SCP-4330 would have found less upsetting to learn about. Subsequent investigation determined that reality reshapes itself, retroactively and without apparent limit on scale, to preserve SCP-4330's comfort, self-image, and personal narrative, whenever he is at risk of learning something that would meaningfully disturb his sense of the world.
The scope of documented alterations ranges from trivial (a rude remark made to him by a shopkeeper in 2019 was, within days, absent from the shopkeeper's own memory and receipts) to severe: a 2021 workplace restructuring that would have resulted in SCP-4330's dismissal instead resulted, across all available records, in the restructuring never having occurred, with eleven affected employees' documented histories altered to match. None of the affected employees have shown awareness that their circumstances changed.
SCP-4330 himself is unaware of his anomalous nature and believes himself to be an ordinary, if occasionally fortunate, man. He has expressed mild guilt at what he perceives as an unusually easy life, a sentiment analysts believe reality may already be quietly working to erode, given two documented cases in which SCP-4330's stated feelings of guilt were followed within a week by an alteration reducing the objective scale of the underlying good fortune, seemingly to make it feel less remarkable.

ADDENDUM 4330-3:
In 2023, a researcher informed SCP-4330, during an unauthorized off-protocol interview, that his coworker's 2021 job loss had in fact occurred and been erased. Within four hours, all Foundation records of the interview itself, including the researcher's own testimony, began exhibiting the same alteration pattern documented elsewhere. The interview is confirmed to have happened only because it was recorded on backup media stored outside SCP-4330's usual radius of effect; the researcher, when re-interviewed, recalled a different, uneventful conversation.

SCP-4331.name: The Assigned Listener
SCP-4331.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4331 resides in standard housing at Site-77. Because SCP-4331's anomaly determines which single individual, at any given time, is capable of perceiving her as a distinct, memorable person, she must be accompanied at all times by a staff member confirmed to currently hold this status, designated her Anchor. Handoff between Anchors is to be conducted according to Protocol 4331-Continuity, and any lapse in Anchor coverage exceeding fifteen minutes requires Site Director notification.
When the current Anchor status transfers to a new individual — an event that occurs unpredictably, at a mean interval of 9 days, and cannot be predicted or controlled by either SCP-4331 or the Foundation — all personnel who previously held the role immediately lose the ability to specifically recall SCP-4331 as a distinct individual, retaining only a generalized, unplaceable sense of familiarity. Staff who have served as Anchors are not to be reassigned away from Site-77 without a debrief interview, several of which have proven difficult to conduct meaningfully given the subjects' inability to recall the relevant events in specific detail.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4331 is a human female, age 33, whose anomalous property is that, at any given moment, precisely one living person is capable of perceiving, recognizing, and retaining specific memories of her as a distinct individual. All other people who interact with SCP-4331 during this period perceive her physically without issue but form no lasting specific memory of the interaction, instead retaining only a vague, generalized impression comparable to recalling a stranger glimpsed once in a crowd.
The identity of the current Anchor changes without apparent pattern related to proximity, relationship, or duration of prior contact; strangers have been assigned Anchor status ahead of family members, and the role has, on four documented occasions, briefly rested with SCP-4331 herself being unable to recall her own recent actions during a period in which the anomaly is hypothesized to have targeted no external subject.
SCP-4331 describes the experience as a lifelong pattern beginning in early childhood, recounting a succession of friendships, a marriage, and one prior pregnancy (outcome unconfirmed; records inconsistent) that ended, from her perspective, not through conflict but through the other party's apparently sincere inability to recall who she was. She has described the condition as "never being left, exactly — just unremembered, one at a time." Foundation psychological staff assess her as functioning but chronically isolated, given that sustained relationships of any kind require either impossibly long Anchor tenure or her partner's willingness to be reintroduced to her, repeatedly, as a stranger.

ADDENDUM:
SCP-4331 has asked whether Foundation research might identify what determines Anchor selection, expressing hope that a discoverable pattern would at least make the unpredictability feel less arbitrary. No pattern has been found across six years of data. She has stopped asking whether one exists.

SCP-4332.name: The Translator of the Dead
SCP-4332.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4332 is housed at Site-77 and is deployed for authorized interviews with the recently deceased only upon written approval of a Level 3 supervisor and attending Ethics Committee liaison. Sessions are limited to one per week and a maximum duration of eleven minutes, corresponding to the observed window in which SCP-4332's translation ability remains functional relative to a given decedent's time of death (see Description); sessions are to be terminated immediately at the eleven-minute mark regardless of content, as extension attempts in early testing produced escalating physiological distress in SCP-4332.
SCP-4332 retains full right of refusal for any requested session and has exercised this right nineteen times to date, most frequently for cases involving the deaths of minors. No disciplinary or administrative consequence may attach to a refusal. A standing post-session psychological support arrangement is mandatory and non-waivable.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4332 is a human female, age 47, capable of perceiving and communicating with the consciousness of a recently deceased individual for a period beginning roughly twenty minutes after clinical death and ending, without exception observed to date, precisely eleven minutes and four seconds later. The mechanism of perception is unclear; SCP-4332 describes it as similar to being in a room with someone on a delayed phone connection, and reports that the deceased individual is typically, though not always, aware of their own death and able to converse coherently within the window.
SCP-4332's ability requires physical proximity to the body or, in a minority of tested cases, to an object of significant personal association with the deceased. Information obtained through SCP-4332 has been independently verified as accurate in 61 of 74 documented sessions where verification was possible, including two cases providing actionable intelligence on unrelated anomalous phenomena the decedent had encountered before death. The remaining sessions produced information later assessed as unverifiable rather than false, and no confirmed instance of SCP-4332 relaying deliberately false information has been recorded.
SCP-4332 has described the work as "the only apology most of these people ever get to give or receive," and has stated that she experiences a distinct, cumulative fatigue after each session unrelated to physical exertion, which she is unable to further characterize. Long-term health monitoring has not identified a physiological cause for this fatigue, though session frequency has been informally correlated with a mild, gradual decline in SCP-4332's own measures of affective range over eight years of Foundation contact.

ADDENDUM:
In a 2023 session, SCP-4332 relayed a message from a deceased Foundation researcher directly addressed to a colleague present in the room, containing information about the researcher's death that contradicted the official incident report. The discrepancy was substantiated by subsequent investigation and the report corrected. SCP-4332 was not disciplined for the deviation from session protocol that allowed this exchange, but has since been formally barred from sessions involving decedents she had a prior personal or professional relationship with, a restriction she did not contest.

SCP-4333.name: Borrowed Health
SCP-4333.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4333 resides at Site-77 under a standard care arrangement. Because SCP-4333's healing ability functions by drawing forward from his own future physiological condition rather than generating new biological material (see Description), any use of the ability, whether voluntary or triggered involuntarily, must be logged and reported to the attending physician, who maintains a running estimate of SCP-4333's accrued physiological debt.
SCP-4333 is not to be used for routine medical treatment of Foundation personnel except in life-threatening emergencies with no other available intervention, and only with SCP-4333's informed, session-specific consent; standing consent is not considered valid under current Ethics Committee guidance. All such uses require post-hoc Ethics Committee review within 72 hours.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4333 is a human male, age 26, capable of healing injuries — his own or, through direct touch, another person's — at a rate far exceeding normal biological limits, up to and including regeneration of significant tissue loss within minutes. The mechanism, determined through longitudinal imaging comparison, is not generative: SCP-4333's body does not produce new material so much as it appears to retrieve tissue condition from a point later in his own physical timeline, healing a present wound by, in effect, borrowing against a future state in which the wound has already closed naturally.
This borrowing carries a corresponding physiological cost. Extensive use of the ability accelerates markers consistent with aging and cumulative wear — bone density loss, cardiovascular strain, and cellular senescence markers — at a rate proportional to the severity of injury healed, effectively spending future years of ordinary health to resolve present injury. SCP-4333's own longitudinal health data indicates a biological age currently outpacing his chronological age by approximately six years, attributed almost entirely to voluntary and involuntary use of the ability since its onset at age 19.
The ability activates involuntarily whenever SCP-4333 or a person in direct contact with him sustains sufficiently severe injury, regardless of his own wishes, a feature that has on two occasions healed injuries SCP-4333 stated afterward he would have preferred to keep, citing the medical leave, sympathy, or occupational reassignment the injury would otherwise have afforded him. He has described the involuntary trigger as "a kindness I can't turn down even when I want to," and has requested, without success to date, a means of consciously suppressing it.

ADDENDUM:
SCP-4333 has asked Foundation medical staff directly how many years of accrued debt would be required before the ability could no longer heal a given injury, effectively asking how much of his life remains available to spend. He has been informed that current models cannot answer this with confidence, as the relationship between accrued debt and remaining capacity has not been observed to be linear. He continues to use the ability on colleagues who ask.

SCP-4334.name: The Edited Remainder
SCP-4334.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4334 is contained at Site-77 in a cognitohazard-rated observation suite. Because SCP-4334 is believed to consist of accreted content removed from the memory of a single Foundation researcher (see Description) across a documented sequence of forty-one separate amnesticization procedures, all personnel who have administered or authorized amnesticization of the original researcher (Dr. ████, hereafter Subject-0) are barred from unsupervised contact with SCP-4334.
SCP-4334 does not require physical restraint, as it has never displayed hostile behavior or attempted departure, but is to be monitored continuously for any indication that it is accumulating further content, which would suggest ongoing, undetected memory-alteration activity targeting Subject-0 outside of logged procedures. Two such indications have been recorded (see Addendum).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4334 is a humanoid entity, physically resembling Subject-0 at a composite of ages spanning roughly fifteen years of his service record, first observed in 2019 occupying a supply closet adjacent to Subject-0's former office at Site-77. Interviews and cross-referencing against amnesticization logs indicate that SCP-4334's memories, mannerisms, and apparent personality consist entirely of material excised from Subject-0's mind across forty-one separate memory-alteration procedures conducted between 2004 and 2019, primarily following Subject-0's repeated exposure to classified information above his clearance or to psychologically damaging incident scenes.
SCP-4334 does not consider itself a copy or remnant of Subject-0, but rather describes itself, consistently across interviews, as "what Site-77 decided he didn't need to be." It possesses full, coherent recall of every incident redacted from Subject-0's memory, information Foundation Records has independently verified as accurate against original incident files in one hundred percent of the forty cases checked. SCP-4334 has never attempted to contact Subject-0 directly, stating that it does not believe Subject-0 would recognize it, or would want to.
Subject-0 remains an active Foundation researcher, unaware of SCP-4334's existence per standing Ethics Committee order, on the assessment that disclosure would constitute a severe and unnecessary psychological harm given that the amnesticizations in question were themselves conducted under valid Foundation policy. This order has been the subject of two internal appeals by staff who argue Subject-0 retains a right to know, both denied.

ADDENDUM:
In 2022, SCP-4334 was found to possess memory of an incident dated after its initial 2019 emergence, corresponding to an unlogged amnesticization event later confirmed to have been administered to Subject-0 without proper documentation by a since-reprimanded field team. This confirms SCP-4334 continues to accrue new content in real time from ongoing edits to Subject-0's memory, and that its size and complexity will likely continue increasing for as long as Subject-0 remains in active field service. SCP-4334 has not commented on this development beyond noting, when informed, that it "felt heavier that week."

SCP-4335.name: The Compelled Truth
SCP-4335.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4335 resides at Site-77 and wears mandatory full-coverage gloves at all times outside of authorized sessions, as her anomalous effect triggers on direct skin contact with another person's bare skin. Authorized interrogation sessions require Level 3 approval, a documented investigative necessity, and presence of a staff psychologist, due to the effect's documented impact on both subject and interviewee (see Description).
SCP-4335 is not to be used more than twice per month absent a critical operational need, per Ethics Committee restriction imposed in 2020 after longitudinal evidence indicated cumulative harm to SCP-4335 from repeated use (see Addendum). She retains standing authority to end any session immediately without providing justification.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4335 is a human female, age 38, whose bare touch compels the touched individual to answer any question posed during the contact with full, involuntary truthfulness, for a duration lasting as long as contact is maintained and up to approximately thirty seconds afterward. The compulsion affects only verbal or written response to direct questioning; it does not extend to unprompted disclosure, and subjects retain full awareness of the compulsion and, in the majority of cases, considerable distress at their inability to resist it.
The effect has proven reliable across two hundred and eleven documented sessions and has never been observed to compel a statement independently verified as false, though subjects have on several occasions provided sincerely believed answers later shown to be factually inaccurate, indicating the compulsion enforces subjective honesty rather than objective truth. The Foundation has used SCP-4335 to resolve eleven cases involving deceptive GoI operatives, at a rate of success no interrogation method in standard use approaches.
SCP-4335 has reported a specific, cumulative cost to repeated use: following each session, she experiences a period, lasting from hours to several days, of being unable to reliably distinguish her own genuine beliefs and memories from things she suspects she may have only said because they were, at the time, simply and inarguably true. She has described this as "losing the edges of what's actually mine," and staff psychologists have documented a measurable decline, correlated with session frequency, in her performance on standard tests of autobiographical memory confidence.

ADDENDUM:
In 2020, following a nine-session period supporting an urgent investigation, SCP-4335 reported a three-week episode during which she was unable to state her own name with confidence, despite it not being in factual dispute, describing the sensation as no longer being sure whether she "actually believed it or just couldn't tell the difference anymore." The Ethics Committee restriction followed directly from this incident. SCP-4335 has continued to volunteer for sessions exceeding the monthly limit when informed the operational need is severe, a pattern the Committee has discussed but not yet acted to prevent.

SCP-4336.name: The Living Safety Valve
SCP-4336.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4336 is maintained as a strategic asset under the joint authority of the Site-77 Director and the O5 Council liaison for infrastructural risk. SCP-4336 resides in rotating deployment at facilities and population centers assessed as high-risk for large-scale industrial, structural, or transit disaster, relocated on a schedule determined by Foundation predictive-risk modeling and reviewed monthly.
SCP-4336's deployment locations and duration limits are governed by Protocol 4336-Rotation, which caps continuous deployment at any single site to ninety days, following documented evidence that prolonged deployment produces escalating psychological strain (see Description). SCP-4336 holds standing authority to request early rotation, which has been granted in all nine cases to date where requested. Deployment locations remain classified even from most on-site Foundation liaison staff, who are briefed only that a protective asset is present.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4336 is a human male, age 44, around whom specific categories of large-scale accidental disaster — structural collapse, transit derailment, industrial explosion, and comparable mass-casualty accidental events — fail to occur within an effective radius of approximately twelve kilometers, for reasons that do not appear to involve any conventional causal intervention; near-miss investigations at prior deployment sites have documented mechanical failures, human errors, and structural faults consistent with historical disaster precursors that simply did not progress to failure, with no identifiable point at which the causal chain was interrupted.
The effect is not absolute: smaller-scale accidents, individual injuries, and deliberate (non-accidental) incidents are unaffected, and SCP-4336's radius has, on two occasions, failed to prevent an incident later attributed to insufficient advance deployment time. Foundation risk modeling estimates SCP-4336's presence has prevented, conservatively, four incidents that would each have resulted in over one hundred casualties, based on comparison to statistically matched control sites without deployment.
SCP-4336 reports no subjective sensation of exerting any active effort and states he was unaware of his own anomalous nature until Foundation contact in 2016, at which point local disaster-rate anomalies across his life history were retroactively identified. He has described the role assigned to him since as "being furniture that happens to save lives," and has, on multiple documented occasions, expressed ambivalence about a role he did not choose and cannot decline without, by Foundation estimate, allowing predictable mass casualties to occur.
Extended deployment has been associated with a documented decline in SCP-4336's affect and sleep quality, worsening with deployment duration and correlated, though not confirmed causally, with proximity to populations he is aware he is protecting without their knowledge or consent. He has stated he finds this awareness "heavier than the job itself."

ADDENDUM:
A 2023 proposal to inform affected local populations, in general terms, that protective measures were in place was rejected by the O5 Council on operational security grounds. SCP-4336 was consulted on this decision as a matter of internal policy rather than formal authority, and recorded his objection, which is noted in the file without further action.

SCP-4337.name: The Declaration Lane
SCP-4337.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Lane 6 of the customs hall at [REDACTED] International Airport, hereafter the Declaration Lane, is maintained under continuous Foundation oversight disguised as a routine secondary-inspection station. Two Foundation personnel are permanently embedded as customs officers on rotating eight-hour shifts. All travelers directed to Lane 6 by embedded personnel are considered voluntarily exposed and are not to be redirected; travelers who approach Lane 6 unprompted are to be diverted to Lane 5 or Lane 7 without explanation.

The anomalous effect is triggered exclusively by the verbal phrase "nothing to declare" spoken in response to a direct question from lane personnel. Travelers who instead present a declaration, however minor, do not trigger the effect regardless of the accuracy of that declaration. Foundation officers stationed at Lane 6 are trained to ask the standard declaration question of any subject scheduled for exposure and to accept non-answers, gestures, or written declarations as valid alternatives when exposure is not desired.

Subjects who trigger SCP-4337 are to be monitored via the standard missing-persons protocol at the destination airport; recovery teams are pre-positioned at the seventeen confirmed alternate destinations (see Addendum 4337-1). Recovered subjects are to be administered Class B amnestics and returned to their point of origin with fabricated travel documentation.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4337 is an anomalous effect localized to customs inspection Lane 6. When a traveler at the lane responds to an officer's declaration inquiry with the specific phrase "nothing to declare," the traveler does not proceed to the arrivals hall of the airport in which Lane 6 is physically located. Instead, closed-circuit footage shows the traveler's queue position becoming vacant within one to three seconds of the utterance, with no visible transition, teleportation effect, or gap in the footage consistent with a cut.

The traveler subsequently appears at customs in a different airport, in a country that is, in the majority of recorded cases (61 of 74), not the traveler's stated destination and not any country the traveler has visited before. Passport and entry records at the receiving airport show a routine, unremarkable entry stamped at a time consistent with a normal flight arrival; boarding records, airline manifests, and CCTV at the originating airport show the traveler as having simply never checked in for their original flight. No institutional memory of Lane 6 having processed the traveler persists outside Foundation records.

Interviews with 41 recovered subjects indicate no subjective experience of transit. All believed, until informed otherwise, that they had arrived at their intended destination; several had already begun ordinary post-arrival activity (hailing transport, contacting relatives) before recovery.

ADDENDUM 4337-1: Of the seventeen confirmed destination countries, four do not appear on any current geopolitical registry recognized by Foundation Records and Information Security. Diplomatic and cartographic assets have been unable to independently verify the existence of these four countries by any means other than subject testimony and the entry stamps themselves. This matter remains open.

SCP-4338.name: The Last Verse
SCP-4338.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Karaoke Room 7 of [REDACTED] Entertainment Lounge has been leased in full by Foundation front company Aldergate Holdings and is closed to public access. Access requires Level 2 clearance and completion of the Verbal Capacity Waiver briefing. No more than one Foundation researcher may perform in the room per calendar month; performances by embedded assets are logged under Project VERSE and reviewed by the on-site Ethics Committee liaison prior to approval, given the permanent nature of the effect's cost.

The room's karaoke machine and song catalogue are not to be removed, repaired, or replaced; three prior attempts at relocating the machine to Site-88 resulted in the anomaly failing to manifest at the new location and manifesting instead in the nearest karaoke-capable room to the original address, requiring re-acquisition of an entire adjacent business.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4338 is an anomalous effect affecting any individual ("the performer") who sings a complete song using the karaoke machine housed in Room 7. If the performer completes the song with full lyrical accuracy, the machine's speakers will, for a duration of between four and eleven seconds after the track ends, reproduce the voice of the song's original recording artist speaking a short, grammatically complete sentence in a register distinct from the recorded song. Content of these statements varies and has not been reliably correlated with performer identity, song content, or session history; Foundation linguists categorize approximately 40% of recovered statements as mundane, 35% as ambiguous, and 25% as apparently directed at Foundation containment efforts specifically, despite no plausible information channel to the original artists.

If the performer instead sings the song with any lyrical inaccuracy — a skipped, misremembered, or substituted word — the performer permanently loses fluent use of that specific word in ordinary speech and writing following the performance. Affected individuals retain full comprehension of the word when encountering it in others' speech or text, and can typically produce a synonym or circumlocution without apparent distress, but are physically unable to voice or write the specific lexical item; attempts result in a brief but consistent stutter-substitution with a phonetically unrelated placeholder sound. The effect has proven permanent in all 19 documented cases and has resisted memory-adjacent and language-center-targeted treatment.

Word loss has ranged from common function words to proper nouns; one Foundation asset (D-88214) lost use of their own first name after misremembering a single syllable during an authorized test performance, and has since been reassigned under a service alias.

ADDENDUM: Committee review of Project VERSE (2021) recommended discontinuing live testing following a controlled session in which a subject lost fluent use of the word "stop" mid-performance and was unable to verbally halt an unrelated safety drill in progress in an adjacent corridor for approximately ninety seconds. No further live testing has been authorized as of this record's filing.

SCP-4339.name: The Displaced Tide Pool
SCP-4339.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: A tide pool located at coordinates [REDACTED] on a rock shelf accessible only at low tide has been designated SCP-4339 and is enclosed by a low observation fence disguised as coastal erosion signage. Public beach access to the shelf is restricted during low-tide windows via a standing "unstable rock" advisory maintained with the cooperation of local coast guard authorities. A two-person Foundation observation team monitors the pool during each low-tide window using tide charts to predict access times, which vary independently of the actual regional tide schedule by an offset that has ranged from eleven days behind to nine days ahead of observed conditions.

No object, organism, or Foundation personnel are to be placed in or otherwise introduced into SCP-4339 without prior authorization from the assigned researcher, given the confirmed risk of unrecoverable aging or de-aging. Any object retrieved from the pool is to be assumed to originate from an offset date and cross-referenced against the Displacement Log (Addendum 4339-1) before release from containment.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4339 is a tide pool measuring approximately 2.1 by 1.4 meters, unremarkable in composition, salinity, and marine life under direct testing. Its anomalous property is that the surface of the pool, when viewed from directly above, reflects the sky not as it currently appears above the pool but as it appeared or will appear at the same location on a different date, hereafter the "offset date." The offset is not constant; it has been observed to range from 34 days in the past to 12 days in the future relative to the date of observation, and cannot be predicted from prior offsets.

Small objects or organisms placed into the pool disappear from the pool within a period of several seconds to two minutes and are not recoverable from the pool itself. In 22 of 26 documented cases, objects of matching description were subsequently recovered from naturally occurring tide pools elsewhere along the same coastline, at a location and date consistent with the offset reflected at the time of introduction. Organisms recovered in this manner show physical development consistent with the elapsed offset period rather than the actual elapsed time; a shore crab introduced into SCP-4339 and recovered nine days later by real-time clock had molted and grown to a size consistent with approximately five weeks of natural development, matching the pool's offset at time of introduction.

No object or organism has been successfully retrieved with a negative net offset (i.e., recovered "younger" than introduced), though this remains mathematically possible under current offset models and is treated as an open containment concern.

ADDENDUM 4339-1: A waterproof placard was introduced into SCP-4339 on 03/2019 bearing a written request that it be returned to the introduction point rather than left on the shoreline. It has not yet been recovered. Current offset models place its expected surfacing date beyond the observation window of this Foundation's current low-tide access agreement, which expires in 2031.

SCP-4340.name: Box Without an Owner
SCP-4340.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Vault Room 3B of [REDACTED] Trust Bank, designated SCP-4340, has been placed under Foundation financial oversight through majority acquisition of the bank's holding company. Two embedded Foundation personnel are maintained on-site under vault-management cover at all times the vault is accessible. Any safe deposit box observed to bear a number not present on the bank's official box registry is to be treated as an active instance of SCP-4340-1 and reported immediately; such boxes are not to be opened by non-Foundation personnel under any circumstance.

Boxes confirmed as SCP-4340-1 instances are to be photographed, sealed, and left undisturbed pending review by the assigned temporal liaison. Contents are not to be removed from a 4340-1 instance except under Level 4 authorization and only after the enclosed date slip (see Description) has been logged and cross-referenced against the named future depositor's current known status. Removal of contents prior to their documented deposit date is strictly prohibited outside of sanctioned intervention scenarios per Addendum 4340-2.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4340 refers to the recurring appearance of safe deposit boxes within Vault Room 3B that do not correspond to any box leased by a current or former client of the bank. These boxes, designated SCP-4340-1 instances, appear at a rate of approximately one per six weeks, occupying physical space within the vault wall that Foundation measurement confirms was solid immediately prior to appearance, without any corresponding structural gap elsewhere in the wall.

Each 4340-1 instance is locked and contains, upon authorized opening, a quantity of items consistent with ordinary safe deposit contents (documents, jewelry, currency, small heirlooms) along with a single paper slip bearing a full legal name, a future date, and a signature. In all 61 documented cases to date, the named individual has subsequently opened a legitimate box at the same bank on or near the stated future date and deposited items matching those found in the corresponding 4340-1 instance, with no apparent memory of the items having previously existed within Foundation custody.

In four cases where Foundation personnel removed an item from a 4340-1 instance prior to the stated deposit date, the named future depositor was subsequently found, upon investigation, to have no record of ever having acquired the removed item — family photographs, correspondence, and in one case the item's manufacturer records, all consistent with an item and its provenance never having existed. The affected individuals showed no awareness of any discrepancy or loss.

ADDENDUM 4340-2: Following Incident 4340-4, in which an item removed early was later matched to a piece of evidence relevant to an unrelated ongoing criminal investigation, a standing exception protocol permits Level 4 authorization for early removal in cases where retention of the item is assessed to pose a documented threat to Foundation secrecy or operational security. Seven such removals have been authorized to date. The long-term effect of these removals on the four affected timelines remains unassessed.

SCP-4341.name: The Waking Bench
SCP-4341.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The third bench from the rail in the public gallery of Courtroom 2, [REDACTED] County Courthouse, is designated SCP-4341 and is maintained under permanent "reserved for court personnel" signage. A Foundation-embedded bailiff is present during all sessions held in Courtroom 2 and is responsible for ensuring no unauthorized member of the public occupies the bench for longer than fifteen consecutive minutes without direct observation. Visibly drowsy occupants are to be roused immediately by embedded personnel under the pretext of standard courtroom decorum enforcement.

In the event SCP-4341 activates despite preventive measures, embedded personnel are to allow the resulting proceeding to continue uninterrupted and are to discreetly document all case details for retroactive cross-referencing. Amnestic administration to displaced individuals is deprioritized in favor of continuous monitoring, as displaced individuals have shown no distress markers and administering amnestics prior to case resolution has twice resulted in incomplete legal outcomes for the original defendant.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4341 is an anomalous property of a specific bench in the public gallery of Courtroom 2. Any individual who falls fully asleep while seated on the bench during an active court session will, upon the next recorded procedural moment (an objection, a verdict, a recess call, or similar), be found seated in the defendant's chair, dressed in attire consistent with a defendant appearing for that day's docketed case, while the individual previously occupying the defendant's chair — the case's actual charged party — is found asleep in the gallery bench in the newly displaced individual's original seat and clothing.

Court staff, opposing counsel, and courtroom recording systems treat the substitution as though it had always been the case; transcripts, exhibit labels, and the day's docket reflect the displaced individual's name in place of the original defendant's from the moment of substitution onward, with no institutional memory among staff of any change. The original defendant, now in the gallery, wakes with no memory of the substitution and no apparent awareness that they are not the individual named in that day's proceedings, typically departing the courthouse without incident once the session concludes.

Foundation review of 11 documented substitutions found no correlation between the displaced individual's real-world legal history and the docketed case they were substituted into; verdicts rendered under SCP-4341's effect have ranged from acquittal to custodial sentencing, all of which the substituted individual subsequently serves, appeals, or otherwise experiences as though it were their own legitimate case, with correspondingly altered public and institutional records persisting indefinitely.

ADDENDUM: No mechanism has been identified by which the original defendant's case is resolved, closed, or otherwise accounted for following a substitution. Foundation legal liaisons have been unable to determine whether the original charges are considered administratively closed, transferred, or simply unrecorded. This matter remains open.

SCP-4342.name: The Shadow Garden
SCP-4342.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The orchid conservatory at [REDACTED] Botanical Gardens, designated SCP-4342, has been closed to public access under the pretext of a multi-year restoration project. A Foundation horticultural team maintains the conservatory's plant collection to preserve its function as camouflage. All visitors requiring exposure for research purposes must sign the Standard Reflective Loss Waiver prior to entry.

The conservatory floor and lower wall surfaces, where accumulated shadow instances (designated SCP-4342-1) are visible, are not to be cleaned, repainted, or otherwise disturbed. Personnel are prohibited from stepping on, scraping, or applying any abrasive or chemical treatment to a 4342-1 instance. Any 4342-1 instance inadvertently damaged is to be reported immediately; the individual to whom the instance corresponds is to be located and monitored for the duration outlined in Protocol 4342-Mirror.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4342 refers to the conservatory building itself and the anomalous effect experienced by individuals who enter, remain within, and subsequently exit it. Upon exiting the conservatory's single functional doorway, an individual's shadow, as cast by the conservatory's interior lighting at their final position before exit, remains fixed to the floor or lower wall surface in that position rather than departing with the individual. The individual, upon exiting, casts no anomalous absence and appears outwardly unaffected; the loss becomes apparent only when the individual is subsequently observed in any environment containing a light source of sufficient strength to normally cast a shadow, at which point no shadow is produced.

The 4342-1 instances accumulated within the conservatory are visually consistent with ordinary cast shadows in shape and density but do not move, lengthen, or shorten in response to changes in the conservatory's lighting, and do not fade over time; the oldest confirmed instance, dated by conservatory renovation records, has persisted for at least the 34 years the building has stood at its current location, predating Foundation awareness of the anomaly.

Individuals who have lost their shadow to SCP-4342 report no physical discomfort and, when unprompted, do not independently notice the absence; the condition is typically identified by acquaintances or, in three documented cases, by the individual's own photographs. No case of shadow loss has been reversed by any tested method, including removal or destruction of the corresponding 4342-1 instance, which instead results in the affected individual's inability to appear in any photographic or video medium going forward, rather than restoration of the shadow.
