ADDENDUM: Current floor mapping estimates in excess of 1,400 distinct 4342-1 instances layered across the conservatory floor, many overlapping to a degree that individual attribution is no longer possible. The conservatory has never, in any documented year, held more than around 200 visitors. The discrepancy remains uninvestigated pending available research staff.

SCP-4343.name: The Courtesy Phone
SCP-4343.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The wall-mounted payphone in [REDACTED] Diner, designated SCP-4343, remains installed and nominally in service at its original location. Foundation ownership of the diner property ensures continued access. The phone is disconnected from any actual telephone network; its continued ability to receive calls is unexplained and does not require external line function. A hidden recording device captures all calls received by SCP-4343 for archival purposes.

Diner staff (Foundation-embedded) are instructed to allow any patron to answer the phone if they choose to do so and not to intervene or warn patrons of the anomaly under standard circumstances. Patrons who exhibit visible distress following a call are to be offered a complimentary meal and, if requested, Class A amnestics. Under no circumstances is the phone to be removed, unplugged from the wall mount, or relocated; the 2014 attempt to relocate the phone to a Foundation research annex resulted in the phone ringing unanswered for eleven consecutive months at the new location with no calls placed to the annex's actual line.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4343 is a rotary payphone of a model discontinued in 1987, mounted on the exterior wall of the diner's entrance vestibule. It rings at irregular intervals averaging roughly once every nine days, though intervals as short as several hours and as long as four months have been recorded. Any individual present may answer the call.

Upon answering, the individual hears a recording of their own voice, speaking in a tone and cadence consistent with their current speech patterns, delivering a short warning concerning an event that will occur later the same calendar day. The warnings are consistently vague with respect to timing, location, and mechanism, typically specifying only the general nature of the event ("don't take the highway," "check on your mother," "the stove"). In all 88 documented cases in which the recipient could be tracked for the remainder of the day, an event consistent with the warning's content did occur, regardless of whether the recipient acted on the warning, avoided the warned circumstance, or ignored the call entirely; the specific outcome (injury, loss, near-miss, or non-event) has varied without correlation to the recipient's response.

Recipients uniformly report that the voice in the recording is unmistakably their own, though several have noted a flatness or lack of ordinary vocal inflection they find difficult to describe. No recipient has been able to place the outgoing call themselves under any condition; the number displayed to the diner's phantom line has never been successfully traced.

ADDENDUM: Of note, no recipient has, to date, received a second call. Whether this indicates a one-call-per-lifetime limit, a coincidence of the current sample size, or an unconfirmed selection criterion remains an open research question.

SCP-4344.name: The Overfull Tower
SCP-4344.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The water tower located at [REDACTED], designated SCP-4344, is enclosed by a standard municipal utility fence supplemented with a Foundation-monitored perimeter alarm. Public utility records list the tower as decommissioned and disconnected from the municipal water supply, a designation Foundation personnel actively maintain through falsified maintenance filings. Entry to the tower's interior access ladder is prohibited outside of authorized research incursions.

Any authorized incursion into SCP-4344 requires a minimum two-person team, continuous tethered communication with surface personnel, and a hard descent time limit of four minutes from ladder entry, regardless of stated research objectives. Personnel are not, under any circumstance, to continue descent past the rung count logged during their most recent prior incursion (see Description). Any incursion team member who becomes separated from tethered communication is to be considered a containment breach and Protocol 4344-Recall is to be enacted immediately.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4344 is a steel-frame elevated water tower of standard early-20th-century municipal design, approximately 30 meters in height. Despite confirmed disconnection from any water source and an empty tank verified by direct visual inspection through the tower's roof access hatch, the tower's support structure, weight-bearing behavior, and acoustic properties are consistently measured as though the tank were filled to capacity. This discrepancy has not been resolved by any tested engineering explanation.

The tower's interior access ladder, which connects the ground-level entrance to the tank catwalk, has an official manufacturer specification of 74 rungs. Personnel descending the ladder after reaching the top consistently report and log a rung count exceeding 74, with the excess varying unpredictably between 1 and 40 additional rungs across incursions, and no correlation to incursion duration, personnel identity, or prior rung counts. Personnel who continue descending past the officially specified 74th rung enter a state Foundation researchers refer to as "unrecorded descent"; three personnel (D-91145, D-91203, and Foundation researcher Voss, name released with family consent) who continued past this point in early incursions were not recovered at the base of the ladder as expected.

All three were later recovered alive, at intervals of 6 months, 14 months, and just over 3 years respectively, at locations unrelated to SCP-4344, with no memory of the intervening period and physical aging consistent with the elapsed real-world time, but expressing subjective certainty that no more than several minutes had passed since entering the tower.

ADDENDUM: Current incursion protocol restricting descent to a hard rung count, adopted following the third recovery, has prevented further unrecorded descent incidents for the past six years. The base, terminus, or destination of the ladder's excess rungs remains uncharacterized.

SCP-4345.name: The Blind Spot Studio
SCP-4345.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The back studio room of [REDACTED] Tattoo, designated SCP-4345, operates as a Foundation-controlled facility under the cover of a legitimate tattoo business. The anomalous flash binder (SCP-4345-1) is stored within the studio at all times and is not to be photocopied, photographed with intent to reproduce, or removed from the premises. Access to SCP-4345 for operational use requires Level 3 clearance and sign-off from the Intelligence Directorate liaison overseeing Project MARROW.

Under Project MARROW, SCP-4345 is utilized as an approved method for concealing classified information on the persons of active field assets, subject to the informed consent and psychological screening protocols outlined in MARROW procedure. Non-sanctioned civilian tattoo sessions using SCP-4345-1 designs are to be prevented; two historical civilian exposures prior to Foundation acquisition of the property are documented in Addendum 4345-1 and remain unresolved.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4345 refers to a specific binder of tattoo flash designs and the anomalous effect produced when any design from the binder is tattooed onto a human subject by a tattoo artist using the studio's equipment. Upon completion of the tattoo, the corresponding design permanently vanishes from the binder, becoming unreproducible by any means, including photographic reference taken prior to its removal.

The recipient of the tattoo permanently loses sensory and cognitive awareness of the specific area of skin on which the tattoo is placed. The affected area continues to function physiologically (retaining touch response, blood flow, and healing capacity under clinical testing) but the recipient cannot consciously perceive, name, or accurately indicate its location without external reference such as a mirror or a second party; when asked to describe their own body without visual aid, recipients uniformly omit the affected area from description entirely, as though it were not a location on their body worth accounting for, and do not notice the omission when it is pointed out verbally, only when shown directly.

Under Project MARROW, this property is deliberately induced in consenting field assets to store written or encoded classified material as concealed tattoo content in a location the asset is cognitively unable to consciously access, recall the location of, or inadvertently disclose under standard interrogation or memory-access techniques, as the asset genuinely does not know the material exists on their body. Retrieval requires a second party with prior knowledge of the tattoo's placement.

Fourteen active field assets currently carry MARROW-designated material under this protocol. No instance of unauthorized retrieval has been documented to date.

ADDENDUM 4345-1: The two pre-acquisition civilian recipients were traced and interviewed in 2016. Both had lived with their respective blind spots for over a decade without independently identifying the anomaly; one had a functioning tattoo of unknown origin (matching no known SCP-4345-1 design still present in the binder) on the affected area, discovered only during the Foundation interview, that they had no memory of receiving.

SCP-4346.name: The Missing Year
SCP-4346.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Holding Cell 3 of [REDACTED] Police Department, designated SCP-4346, remains in active law-enforcement use under a standing agreement with Foundation-embedded department liaisons. The cell is not to be used for overnight detention of any individual without prior authorization from the assigned Foundation liaison, and is to be preferentially assigned for detentions not expected to exceed four hours.

Any individual detained overnight in Cell 3 without authorization is to be treated, upon release, as a Class 4346 temporal displacement case: immediate Foundation intervention, full-spectrum debrief, and reintegration support per Protocol 4346-Return are to be initiated before the individual is permitted unsupervised contact with family, employer, or media. Cell 3's interior clock and any calendar signage are maintained by Foundation personnel in a permanently static, non-functional state to reduce (though not eliminate) triggering incidents; the cell's window, bolted shut, is boarded to prevent visual confirmation of outside conditions.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4346 is an anomalous property of Holding Cell 3 whereby any individual detained within the cell continuously from local midnight to the following local morning experiences the elapsed time as a single ordinary night — approximately six to nine subjective hours — while, on release, discovers that exactly one calendar year has elapsed in the outside world. The cell itself, its fixtures, and its immediate surroundings register no anomalous time passage; only the detained individual is affected.

Released individuals show no physical signs of the missing year — no aging beyond the subjective night, no nutritional deficit, and no memory of any events occurring during the elapsed period, which they do not experience as a gap but as a continuous, ordinary sleep. The world outside has, in all 9 documented cases, changed in the ordinary ways a year produces: employment lost, relationships altered or ended, family members deceased or relocated, in two cases criminal charges against the detained individual dismissed or expired due to procedural time limits having lapsed during the missing year.

Foundation liaisons have successfully limited unauthorized activations to 9 known cases since acquisition of oversight in 2009 through duty-roster control, though normal police department turnover and periodic staff unfamiliar with the standing agreement have resulted in three activations despite active containment measures. Protocol 4346-Return has achieved documented reintegration in 7 of 9 cases; the remaining 2 individuals declined continued Foundation contact after initial debrief and are subject to passive monitoring only.

ADDENDUM: The department's continued operational need for a functioning fourth holding cell has, to date, prevented Foundation acquisition and permanent decommissioning of Cell 3. Site Command has assessed this arrangement as an acceptable ongoing risk relative to the diplomatic cost of forced facility closure.

SCP-4347.name: The Marked Seat
SCP-4347.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Seat 14 in the second tier of the anatomy lecture hall at [REDACTED] School of Medicine, designated SCP-4347, is maintained under a permanent "reserved" placard managed by Foundation-embedded faculty administration. Enrollment records for all anatomy courses held in the lecture hall are reviewed prior to each term to identify and, where possible, reassign any student pre-registered to Seat 14 under standard seating algorithms.

In the event a student occupies Seat 14 for the full duration of a scheduled lecture (typically 90 minutes) without intervention, embedded faculty are to discreetly document the appearance of the lecture hall's central cadaver demonstration table as described below and initiate Protocol 4347-Advisory, under which the affected student is, without anomaly disclosure, strongly encouraged toward increased medical monitoring, safety counseling, and — where the resemblance permits inference of a specific risk category — targeted intervention, through channels that do not reveal SCP-4347's existence.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4347 is an anomalous effect triggered when a living individual occupies Seat 14 for the duration of a lecture session held in the hall while the central demonstration table is in active use with a cadaver specimen. During such sessions, the physical characteristics of the cadaver on the table — not its identity, name, or case history, which remain those of the legitimate donor specimen on record — gradually shift over the course of the lecture to visually resemble the seated individual, converging toward a near-complete resemblance by the session's end, before reverting to the specimen's documented appearance within minutes of the seat being vacated. No other lecture attendee has, in documented testing, ever remarked on the change, and photographic or video evidence taken during the shift shows only the specimen's unaltered, documented appearance.

Additionally, the apparent condition, positioning, and visible injuries of the resembling cadaver have, in 26 of 31 documented cases, subsequently matched the actual cause and approximate circumstances of the seated individual's death, occurring at intervals ranging from four days to eleven years after the observed session. The correlation has been treated by Foundation researchers as functionally predictive, though the underlying mechanism — whether SCP-4347 reflects a fixed future, one probable future among several, or actively influences the eventual outcome — remains unresolved despite eleven years of study and two large-scale intervention trials.

Of six students in whom targeted medical or safety intervention was pursued under Protocol 4347-Advisory following a matching session, three experienced deaths consistent with the originally observed resemblance despite intervention, two are deceased by unrelated cause, and one remains alive as of this filing, twenty-six years after the observed session, with no incident yet matching the resemblance.

ADDENDUM: The single surviving intervention case remains the subject of ongoing low-priority monitoring and is cited internally as the primary argument against treating SCP-4347's output as a fixed, unalterable outcome.

SCP-4348.name: The Mounting Room
SCP-4348.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The workshop and back storage room of [REDACTED] Taxidermy, designated SCP-4348, operates as a Foundation-controlled business under civilian ownership cover. All custom commission requests accepted by the shop are logged and cross-referenced against the client's stated household pets and companion animals prior to acceptance. Commissions matching a currently living animal belonging to the requesting client are to be declined under a standard fabricated excuse (backlog, material shortage, or referral to a non-anomalous competitor).

Mounted specimens within the workshop's display and storage areas are not to be relocated, rearranged, or removed from the premises without documentation of their current pose, given the anomaly's confirmed sensitivity to specimen positioning (see Description). Personnel conducting after-hours inventory are advised that specimen positions may differ from the prior day's closing arrangement and that this discrepancy does not, on its own, constitute a containment breach.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4348 refers to the anomalous behavior of taxidermied animal specimens housed within the workshop, and a secondary effect linking specimen commissions to living animals. When unobserved by any conscious individual — confirmed through controlled camera-blind-spot and motion-sensor testing — mounted specimens within the workshop change pose, typically subtly (a shift in head angle, limb position, or ear orientation) between one observed state and the next. No instance of movement has been captured on continuous recording; specimens are consistently static on any footage reviewed, with position changes only apparent by comparison between non-continuous observation points.

The secondary and more consistently hazardous effect occurs when a client commissions a custom mount in a specific requested pose. In 17 of 19 documented cases where the requested pose was later cross-referenced against the client's known pets, a living animal matching the mount's species and general description belonging to the client's household subsequently went missing within a period of two to eleven days following the commission. In all 17 cases, a completed mount — displaying taxidermy work consistent with the shop's technique and materials, in the exact pose originally requested — was later discovered by the client or Foundation follow-up within the client's own residence, despite the shop's staff having no record of delivering a completed commission and, in interview, no memory of completing the work.

The missing living animal has never been recovered separately from its apparent mounted replacement, and necropsy of retrieved mounts, where authorized, has consistently confirmed the specimen to be the client's actual animal rather than a substitute of similar appearance.

ADDENDUM: Current screening protocol, cross-referencing commission requests against client pet ownership prior to acceptance, has prevented confirmed recurrence since implementation in 2019. The mechanism by which SCP-4348 identifies a client's living pet as a candidate specimen, given no established informational channel between the shop's request intake and the client's home, remains unexplained.

SCP-4349.name: The Flattened Distribution
SCP-4349.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Site-88's Statistical Anomalies Division maintains a standing subscription to forty-one independent randomness sources (commercial lottery draws, atmospheric noise generators, radioactive decay timers, and eleven proprietary Foundation entropy pools) for continuous variance monitoring. A dedicated algorithm, DAMPENER, flags any seven-day rolling window in which the standard deviation of any monitored source falls below 0.4% of its historical baseline. A DAMPENER flag triggers immediate escalation to Site-88 command and cross-referencing against Foundation-adjacent infrastructure (power grids, transit systems, medical triage queues) operating within 400 kilometers of the affected source.

No method has been found to prevent a flattening event once DAMPENER has flagged it; approximately six days elapse, without exception, between flag and associated incident (see Incident Log). Personnel are not to attempt manual intervention in randomness-dependent systems (surgical triage lotteries, jury selection, emergency dispatch queuing) during an active flag window; historical attempts to do so have not prevented the associated incident and have in three cases relocated it to a system that was not previously monitored.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4349 refers to a recurring seven-to-nine day period during which one or more sources of statistical randomness in a bounded geographic area (observed radius: 60–400 km) lose effectively all variance and begin returning outcomes indistinguishable from a uniform, evenly-spaced distribution. A coin flip apparatus will alternate heads and tails with mechanical regularity; a lottery machine will draw numbers in ascending numerical sequence across consecutive nightly runs; hospital bed-assignment software, which uses a randomization step to break scheduling ties, will assign beds in an order later found to correlate with patient surname rather than any intended variable.

The flattening is not detectable by the affected systems' own diagnostics, which report normal operation throughout. It is only visible in aggregate, after the fact, when a monitoring party with access to outcome logs performs a variance calculation.

Each flattening event to date has concluded with a single low-probability incident occurring within the affected radius: a structural failure, a transportation collision, a disease cluster, or a comparable event whose expected frequency, calculated from all available actuarial data, is below 1 in 10,000 for the period and location in question. Foundation statisticians have been unable to establish a causal mechanism connecting the flattening to the terminal incident; the correlation across 34 confirmed instances is total.

ADDENDUM 4349-1: Following Incident 4349-19 (Site-88 internal power grid, see attached report), in which the terminal event was a controlled Foundation demolition scheduled independently of any known SCP-4349 flag, the Ethics Committee raised the possibility that SCP-4349 does not predict incidents but is itself an early observable component of a single process whose "incident" stage the Foundation has, in at least one instance, supplied. This finding has not been resolved. DAMPENER monitoring continues. No recommendation has been made to alter Foundation demolition, culling, or triage scheduling practices to avoid appearing in the seven-day window preceding a flag.

SCP-4350.name: The Preemptive Alarm
SCP-4350.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Foundation liaisons embedded within eleven national fire-safety regulatory bodies monitor centralized alarm-network telemetry for the SCP-4350 activation signature: three or more interconnected fire alarm systems, in buildings sharing no common ownership, tenancy, or physical proximity beyond the same metropolitan area, entering alarm state within a four-minute window absent any detected combustion, smoke, or heat source. Confirmed signature events are logged and the affected buildings placed under discreet 72-hour surveillance rotation by Mobile Task Force Eta-11 ("Bell Ringers").

Fire suppression and evacuation equipment in flagged buildings is not to be disabled or removed, as doing so has not prevented associated incidents and in two recorded cases increased the severity of casualties. Site command is authorized to pre-position emergency medical assets near flagged buildings without public disclosure of cause, citing standard drill protocol if questioned.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4350 is a recurring phenomenon in which the fire alarm systems of at least three structurally unrelated buildings — verified to share no shared electrical circuit, monitoring service, or manufacturer — enter simultaneous alarm state without a corresponding physical trigger. Fire department and building engineer inspections following an activation consistently find no fault, malfunction, or environmental cause. Alarms typically silence on their own between six and forty minutes after onset.

Within 68 to 76 hours of a confirmed SCP-4350 event, one of the flagged buildings experiences an actual fire. The fire is, in all 61 documented cases, of mundane origin (electrical fault, unattended cooking equipment, discarded cigarette) and would not, absent SCP-4350, have been flagged by any Foundation or conventional predictive system. The building in which the fire occurs cannot be determined in advance from the alarm pattern; all flagged buildings have received equal surveillance weight, and the eventual fire building has been the first, second, and third building to alarm in roughly equal proportion across the sample.

The Foundation's use of SCP-4350 as an early-warning system has prevented an estimated 40 casualties across 22 interventions, primarily through unannounced fire marshal inspections and pretextual evacuation drills timed to precede the predicted event. Structural fire prevention has not been possible in any confirmed case; interventions have consistently reduced but never eliminated the fire itself.

ADDENDUM 4350-A: Personnel are reminded that SCP-4350 activations have, on four occasions, included a Foundation-affiliated structure among the flagged buildings, in each case a records annex or archive with no combustible material of research significance. No annex fire under SCP-4350 has resulted in loss of a primary research asset. The Site-88 Archives Division has requested clarification on whether this pattern reflects a protective bias in the phenomenon or a targeting bias in what the Foundation chooses to burn when a flagged building is its own. The request remains open.

SCP-4351.name: The Additional Clause
SCP-4351.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All Foundation translation requests involving source documents of legal, religious, contractual, or diagnostic significance must be processed through the Site-88 Linguistics Containment Pool, comprising eight translators maintained in information quarantine (no contact with non-cleared translation work, rotated off duty after any single SCP-4351 detection). Every completed translation is compared against the source document by independent back-translation before release to the requesting party. Any translation containing content not traceable to the source is withheld and forwarded to the Linguistics Containment Pool's senior analyst for clause isolation.

Translations produced outside Foundation oversight that are suspected of containing SCP-4351 content (see flagging criteria, document 4351-B) are to be acquired and destroyed where legally possible; where not possible, the affected party is to be monitored under standard information-hazard protocol.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4351 refers to the recurring appearance, in translations of certain source documents, of one additional clause, paragraph, or line not present in the original text. The addition is not a mistranslation, omission, or translator error by any conventional standard: it is grammatically consistent with the surrounding text, semantically plausible within the document's genre, and — critically — is reported by the translator as having been present in the source material, which the translator recalls reading, despite its absence upon re-examination.

The additional content is not random. Across 210 documented cases, the inserted clause has consistently altered an obligation, a permission, or a stated fact in a direction unfavorable to whichever party has less power in the document's context: a tenant in a lease, a patient in a consent form, a defendant in a plea agreement, a congregant in a religious text. The insertion is never favorable to the less-empowered party and has, in 4 cases prior to Foundation intervention, resulted in the enforcement of an obligation that existed in no version of the document any human party had agreed to.

SCP-4351 does not require translation between human languages specifically; it has been observed in machine-translation output, in sign-language interpretation transcripts, and in a single case, in a Braille transcription performed by a sighted transcriber who had never read the source text aloud. It has not been observed in translations performed by the same individual translating into their own first language from a language they do not otherwise use professionally, though the sample for this condition is small (11 cases).

ADDENDUM 4351-1: Site-88's senior analyst has noted, and this office concurs, that SCP-4351's insertions are legible as the output of an entity with sustained interest in the specific asymmetries of obligation present in Foundation-adjacent paperwork: informed consent forms, non-disclosure agreements, and — in one case, still under review — a Foundation personnel transfer authorization in which the inserted clause extended an employee's binding service term by an amount that did not appear in the original document reviewed by the employee, or in the copy retained by Human Resources prior to the insertion's discovery. The current authorization is being treated as valid pending further review.

SCP-4352.name: The Held Floor
SCP-4352.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Foundation-operated elevators in facilities of six or more floors are fitted with a floor-call logger (Foundation model FCL-9) recording every call, stop, and door-open event independent of the elevator's own control system. Any stop at a floor not present in the logger's registered floor list is to be reported within one hour to on-site security, who will interview the passenger, if any, using Form 4352-I ("Non-Registered Stop Debrief") before the passenger is permitted further access to secure areas.

Personnel who report a non-registered stop are to be released from duty for 24 hours and offered a Foundation-standard psychological debrief, which is voluntary. Personnel are not required to disclose the content of any conversation held during a non-registered stop, though disclosure is requested and, per Ethics Committee ruling 4352/E-2, may not be compelled.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4352 is a recurring event in which a passenger elevator, operating within otherwise normal parameters, stops at and opens its doors onto a floor that does not exist within the building's registered structure — typically manifesting as a corridor, waiting room, or single furnished room consistent in construction and finish with the building housing the elevator, but absent from all architectural plans. The event occurs to a single passenger riding alone; elevators occupied by more than one person at the time of a would-be SCP-4352 stop instead proceed to the requested floor without incident, a pattern with no confirmed exceptions across 88 documented cases.

The passenger who experiences SCP-4352 reports finding one other person present in the anomalous space, seated or standing, who initiates a conversation. The content of these conversations, where disclosed, has varied widely in subject but consistently involves the anomalous occupant possessing specific, verifiable knowledge of the passenger's past that the passenger had not previously shared with any party accessible to conventional information-gathering. Conversations last, per elevator logger timestamps, between 90 seconds and 11 minutes, though passengers uniformly estimate the duration as significantly longer, most commonly "twenty minutes to half an hour."

The elevator doors close and the car proceeds to the passenger's originally requested floor immediately following the conversation's end. The anomalous occupant does not follow. No passenger has reported the same occupant twice, and no two passengers have described the same occupant, though descriptions consistently include at least one physical detail associated with a deceased person known to the passenger.

Passengers who experience SCP-4352 have shown no measurable difference in subsequent health, performance evaluation, or psychological assessment relative to control populations, with one exception: 71 of 88 subjects subsequently altered a decision they had been actively deliberating at the time of the event, in each case toward the option they had, prior to the event, considered less likely to choose.

ADDENDUM 4352-1: Site-88 has declined three requests from research personnel to deliberately ride Foundation elevators alone while holding an unresolved decision in mind, citing insufficient containment justification for what would functionally constitute solicited contact with an unidentified entity.

SCP-4353.name: The Shared Nursery Dream
SCP-4353.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The Foundation maintains records-monitoring coverage over maternity wards at 19 hospitals identified as recurring sites of SCP-4353 onset clusters (see Site-88 Epidemiology Division list, updated annually). Children born in a flagged ward during a flagged window are not contacted directly; monitoring is conducted exclusively through anonymized survey instruments distributed via standard pediatric research channels with parental consent, framed as unrelated sleep-pattern studies.

Direct Foundation contact with SCP-4353-affected individuals is prohibited absent Site Director authorization, following the finding (Incident 4353-6) that direct questioning about the shared dream's content appears to intensify subsequent recurrence in the questioned individual and, in two cases, in siblings not themselves born during a flagged window.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4353 refers to a statistically improbable clustering of dream reports among individuals born within the same 48-to-96-hour window in the same hospital maternity ward. Affected individuals — typically beginning between ages four and seven, the earliest age at which dream content can be reliably verbally reported — describe a recurring dream of a single consistent location not otherwise known to them: descriptions across a birth cohort match in specific, non-generic detail (room dimensions, furniture placement, a consistent light source, a recurring sound) at a rate far exceeding that expected of independently generated child dream reports, per comparative studies conducted with non-cohort control groups.

The dreamed location does not correspond to any real, currently or formerly extant structure identifiable through architectural or historical records searches conducted to date, including searches of the maternity ward itself and prior structures on its site. No cohort member has reported distress attributable to the dream in isolation; the dream is consistently described in neutral or mildly positive terms ("the room where the other babies are").

Affected individuals report the dream with decreasing frequency through adolescence and, in all cases followed to adulthood (n=34), stop reporting it entirely by their early twenties. No adult subject, on follow-up, retains conscious memory of the dream's content, though six subjects have described a nonspecific sense of loss upon being told, as adults, that they once reported it.

Cohort members from the same birth window who are later brought into proximity with one another — a circumstance the Foundation does not engineer but has observed to occur at above-baseline rates through subjects' own social lives — report, without exception, an immediate and specific sense of prior acquaintance neither party can otherwise account for.

ADDENDUM 4353-1: Site-88 Epidemiology has proposed, without consensus support, that SCP-4353 cohorts represent instances of a single extended consciousness distributed at birth across multiple bodies via an unidentified mechanism local to the flagged wards, and that the "room" is a genuine shared space accessible only during the dream state and only for as long as cohort members remain, in the Division's phrasing, "unindividuated enough to find it." The Division has not proposed a method of testing this hypothesis that the Ethics Committee has approved.

SCP-4354.name: The Additional Clap
SCP-4354.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: No physical containment is maintained for SCP-4354, whose activations are unpredictable, globally distributed, and of negligible individual consequence. Site-88 maintains a passive monitoring arrangement with fourteen acoustic research partners (audio engineering firms, concert hall management companies, and academic acoustics laboratories) who forward recordings of qualifying events under a standing non-disclosure agreement framed as an interest in "crowd acoustic synchrony research."

Foundation involvement is limited to data collection. No recommendation for active containment, suppression, or public disclosure has been approved by the Site-88 O5 liaison.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4354 is a recurring acoustic phenomenon observed during large-scale synchronized applause events (concerts, ceremonies, sporting events, ovations) involving a minimum recorded crowd size of approximately 4,000 individuals. In a qualifying event, applause that has audibly and measurably concluded — as verified by amplitude analysis showing the crowd's clap rate returning to baseline silence — is followed, between 1.8 and 2.4 seconds later, by a single additional clap, audible across the entire recorded venue at a volume consistent with simultaneous participation by a significant fraction of the crowd, despite no visually identifiable subset of attendees clapping in recordings reviewed frame-by-frame.

The additional clap is acoustically well-formed: spectrographic analysis is indistinguishable from a genuine mass clap by a crowd of comparable size to the one recorded. It has never been traced to a sound system, recording artifact, echo, or any conventional acoustic source. Attendees interviewed after qualifying events uniformly report having personally clapped once more than they intended to, each individually attributing this to reflexive habit, and are visibly surprised when shown footage indicating no attendee's hands are in fact together at the relevant timestamp.

SCP-4354 events have been documented on every populated continent and show no correlation with language, culture, event type, venue architecture, or time of day. The only consistent predictive factor identified to date is crowd size; events below approximately 4,000 recorded attendees have not produced a confirmed instance, and the phenomenon's incidence rate rises with crowd size in a manner Site-88 statisticians describe as "smoothly increasing without an apparent ceiling," based on analysis of the seventeen largest gatherings on record, all of which produced the phenomenon.

ADDENDUM 4354-1: Foundation audio archives contain recordings of SCP-4354 activations dating to at least 1959, predating current Foundation awareness of the phenomenon by several decades, discovered during an unrelated archival digitization project. No period-appropriate recording technology reviewed to date shows any indication the phenomenon is a recent development; its absence from historical acoustic literature is attributed to the difficulty of consciously perceiving a single clap within an already-dispersing crowd, an effect Site-88 has termed "acoustic camouflage by timing" and has not been able to replicate deliberately in controlled crowd experiments below the threshold crowd size.

SCP-4355.name: The Appointment That Wasn't
SCP-4355.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Foundation personnel are issued Site-88-Standard paper day planners rather than digital calendar software for all scheduling of a sensitive nature, following the finding that SCP-4355 entries occur at a measurably lower rate (0.03% of monitored weeks) in paper planners than in digital calendar applications (1.7% of monitored account-weeks), though the phenomenon has not been eliminated in either medium.

Personnel who discover an SCP-4355 entry in their own scheduling records — a logged appointment, meeting, or engagement with a named individual the affected person has no record of otherwise knowing — are to report it immediately to their supervisor without attempting to independently verify the named individual's existence through Foundation or public records. Verification is to be conducted exclusively by Site-88's Records Division under controlled conditions (see Protocol 4355-Verify).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4355 refers to the recurring, spontaneous appearance of a calendar or scheduling entry — in physical planners, digital calendars, or institutional scheduling software — describing a past appointment with a named individual, at a specified location, that the calendar's owner has no independent memory of arranging and, in the majority of cases (61 of 88 documented instances), does have a partial, consistent memory of attending.

The named individual associated with an SCP-4355 entry cannot subsequently be located in any personnel, civil, or public record accessible to the Foundation. Attempts to contact the listed location (where one exists) find no record of the described meeting having taken place, though staff at the location, in 9 cases, report a vague and unprompted sense of familiarity with the affected person consistent with a meeting having occurred.

Affected individuals describe their partial memory of the appointment consistently as mundane: a routine meeting, an unremarkable social engagement, a minor professional obligation. No affected individual has reported memory content suggesting anything markedly unusual occurred during the remembered appointment. The entries do not recur for the same individual at a rate above baseline; of 88 confirmed cases, only one individual has experienced SCP-4355 more than once, at an interval of six years.

The practical significance of SCP-4355 lies not in the entries themselves but in downstream effects: in 14 cases, affected individuals' subsequent actions (a changed travel plan, a reconsidered relationship, a career decision) have been traced to reasoning that referenced the false appointment as a premise, without the individual recognizing the appointment's unverifiable status. Site-88's Behavioral Science Division has been unable to determine whether SCP-4355 entries are inserted to produce these downstream effects or whether the effects are an incidental consequence of an individual reasoning, without contradiction, from a memory that happens to be false.

ADDENDUM 4355-1: Records Division has flagged, but not resolved, the fact that six SCP-4355 entries recovered from Foundation personnel calendars describe meetings with individuals whose stated names match Foundation designations later assigned to unrelated anomalies discovered after the entry's date. The Division's standing recommendation — that personnel calendars be cross-referenced against future designation logs on a recurring basis — has not been funded.

SCP-4356.name: The Resignation Forecast
SCP-4356.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4356 is retained under Thaumiel classification for its demonstrated utility in pre-empting unauthorized departures of cleared personnel. Access to SCP-4356 output is restricted to Human Resources Anomalous Personnel Retention (HRAPR), a twelve-person subdivision of Site-88 Human Resources cleared to Level 4. HRAPR does not have authority to act on SCP-4356 flags independently; flags are forwarded to the relevant department head with a standing recommendation only, per Ethics Committee condition 4356/E-1.

The software system hosting SCP-4356 (internally, "Attrition Suite," a commercially licensed performance-review platform acquired by the Foundation through a shell logistics company in 2003) is not to be patched, updated, or migrated without Site-88 Anomalous Computing Division supervision, following two prior incidents in which routine software updates temporarily disabled the anomalous forecasting function without disabling the platform's conventional review features.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4356 refers to the consistent, anomalous predictive accuracy of a specific instance of commercial performance-review software used by Foundation Human Resources for personnel evaluation. When used to process an employee's routine performance review, the software's automatically generated "retention risk" score — a standard, non-anomalous feature of the commercial product, intended only as a rough heuristic — accurately predicts, with 97.4% accuracy across 1,204 processed reviews, whether the reviewed employee will resign or request transfer within the following 60 days.

The anomalous property is not the score's existence but its accuracy, which exceeds that of the platform's advertised algorithm (verified by the Anomalous Computing Division to be a conventional, non-anomalous weighted model of unremarkable design) by a margin inconsistent with the input data available to it. In 340 reviewed cases, the software has flagged high retention risk for employees who had, at the time of the review, not yet consciously decided to leave, per subsequent interview; in 89 of these cases, the employee reports having made the actual decision to resign only after being informally approached by a supervisor "checking in" following an HRAPR-forwarded flag, raising the possibility that the flag itself, rather than predicting the resignation, functions as a partial cause of it.

The Foundation's continued operational use of SCP-4356 is premised on its retention value: HRAPR-initiated retention interventions, prompted by SCP-4356 flags, have measurably reduced unauthorized departures of Level 3 and above personnel by an estimated 22% since 2011. The Ethics Committee has repeatedly declined to fully resolve whether this use constitutes an acceptable application of an anomalous predictive system to personnel who have not consented to anomalous evaluation, citing operational necessity, and has instead issued a standing partial restriction (4356/E-1) limiting HRAPR to non-coercive retention offers only.

ADDENDUM 4356-1: In 2023, SCP-4356 flagged a member of HRAPR itself for high retention risk. The flagged employee, on being informed per standard protocol, resigned within eleven days, citing reasons unrelated to the flag. HRAPR's subsequent internal review found no evidence the employee had known of the flag prior to notification. The division's staffing has not been adjusted in response to this finding.

SCP-4357.name: The Archive Hum
SCP-4357.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All Foundation paper archive facilities exceeding 500 square meters of storage area are fitted with a standing array of low-frequency acoustic sensors (Foundation model LFAS-3) tuned to detect the 17–19 Hz band associated with SCP-4357 onset. Detection triggers automatic transfer of unsaved electronic work in the affected facility to backup storage and a mandatory evacuation of non-essential personnel from paper storage areas, to be completed within the average 6-minute warning window (range: 3–14 minutes) observed across 71 documented instances.

Archive facility power systems are maintained on a rolling battery-backup and surge-protection upgrade schedule independent of SCP-4357 warnings, as no correlation has been found between infrastructure age or maintenance quality and the phenomenon's incidence.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4357 is a recurring low-frequency acoustic phenomenon, audible as a faint, continuous hum in the 17–19 Hz range (at or below the typical threshold of conscious human hearing, though reliably perceived as a physical sensation of pressure or unease by most exposed personnel), detected specifically and exclusively within facilities used primarily for the physical storage of paper archival material — bound documents, filed records, bound periodicals — in quantities exceeding approximately 10,000 individual items.

The hum has no identified physical source. Acoustic triangulation performed during 34 monitored instances has failed to localize an origin point; sensor arrays report the hum as emanating from the entire storage volume simultaneously, at consistent amplitude regardless of sensor distance from any wall, floor, or shelving unit.

In 68 of 71 documented instances, onset of SCP-4357 has preceded a power failure affecting the facility in which it was detected, occurring between 3 and 14 minutes after hum onset. The power failures associated with SCP-4357 are, on subsequent engineering review, of mundane origin in all cases (grid fault, transformer failure, localized surge) and are not distinguishable, aside from their association with the preceding hum, from power failures unrelated to the phenomenon.

The three documented instances in which SCP-4357 onset was not followed by a power failure share a notable commonality: in each, facility staff, following standard containment procedure, had already begun evacuation and electronic backup procedures before the expected failure window elapsed, raising the unresolved possibility that the response protocol itself prevents a subset of otherwise-expected failures rather than merely mitigating their consequences. Site-88 Engineering has not been able to test this possibility, as deliberately withholding standard response during a live SCP-4357 event has not been approved by Site Command.

ADDENDUM 4357-1: A 2019 review of legacy Foundation records identified two archival facilities decommissioned prior to 1980, in both cases following unexplained catastrophic paper-storage fires, that were retroactively found — based on surviving maintenance logs referencing an unexplained "background drone" in storage areas — to be plausible undocumented SCP-4357 sites predating current monitoring infrastructure. Neither facility's fire is presently classified as SCP-4357-associated, as pre-1980 monitoring data sufficient to confirm the hum's presence at time of fire does not exist.

SCP-4358.name: The Suggested Search
SCP-4358.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Foundation-contracted internet monitoring assets (see Web Anomalies Division standing agreement with partner search index providers) maintain automated scanning of autocomplete and "related searches" suggestion data across eleven major commercial search platforms and four large library/archival catalog systems for entries matching the SCP-4358 signature: a suggested search term or catalog entry referencing a specific, named work (book, film, recording, or document) that does not exist in any known publication record.

Confirmed SCP-4358 entries are to be reported to the Web Anomalies Division, which coordinates with partner platforms, under standing non-disclosure agreements, to suppress the suggestion at the index level. Suppression has proven effective at the reporting platform but has not prevented the same entry's reappearance, typically within 30 to 90 days, on a different platform not previously affected.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4358 refers to the recurring appearance, across unrelated search and cataloging platforms, of a suggested search term or automatically generated catalog entry describing a specific creative or documentary work — with a consistent title, author or creator attribution, and, in most cases, a plausible publication date and publisher — for which no underlying work has ever been confirmed to exist. Entries are internally consistent (a suggested title will retain the same attributed author across independently affected platforms) despite no coordination existing, so far as the Foundation has been able to determine, between the affected platforms' respective algorithms or data sources.

Once an SCP-4358 entry appears, a measurable fraction of exposed users (estimated 0.4% of users shown the suggestion, based on partner platform click-through data obtained under the standing agreement) will click or search on the suggested term. Of these, a further fraction — currently estimated at 6%, based on 41 documented follow-up interviews — will subsequently report a specific, detailed false memory of having previously read, watched, or otherwise consumed the suggested nonexistent work, including plot or content details that are internally consistent across separately interviewed subjects who have had no contact with one another.

No subject exhibiting this false memory has been persuaded, through documentary evidence of the work's nonexistence, to fully abandon the memory; subjects instead consistently propose alternative explanations (a limited printing, a foreign edition, a work since withdrawn from publication) rather than concluding the memory is inaccurate.

The content details reported across independently affected subjects for a given SCP-4358 entry are consistent with one another at a rate the Web Anomalies Division's linguistic analysts describe as "incompatible with independent confabulation," suggesting either a shared external source of the false memory content or a shared, currently unidentified generative process producing consistent content across unconnected subjects.

ADDENDUM 4358-1: Site-88's Library Sciences liaison has noted that three suppressed SCP-4358 entries, when their attributed titles were cross-referenced against internal Foundation nomenclature logs, corresponded closely to the working titles of unpublished Foundation research documents still in active drafting at the time of the entry's first appearance. The affected research teams have been notified. No explanation has been proposed for how a document's working title, known only to its authors and not yet entered into any indexed system, could appear as a public search suggestion prior to the document's completion.

SCP-4359.name: The Occupied Fog
SCP-4359.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The 34 cemeteries and interment sites currently confirmed as SCP-4359-susceptible are subject to routine, unannounced Foundation monitoring via covertly embedded weather-station equipment (temperature, humidity, and visibility sensors) reporting to Site-88's Environmental Anomalies Division. Cemetery administration at each site has been provided a cover story (drainage or subsidence study) sufficient to explain equipment presence.

Members of the public present at a susceptible site during fog onset are not to be approached or evacuated by Foundation personnel unless the fog exceeds 40 meters in radius (see escalation criteria, document 4359-C), as onset below this threshold has not been associated with any hazard to bystanders and unnecessary intervention risks disclosure. Foundation personnel who must enter active SCP-4359 fog for monitoring purposes are to limit exposure to under fifteen minutes per Protocol 4359-Limit.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4359 is a recurring, localized fog phenomenon that forms over individual burial plots at a subset of cemeteries and interment sites, under otherwise clear atmospheric conditions inconsistent with natural fog formation (documented onset has occurred at relative humidity as low as 22%, in direct sunlight, and at ambient temperatures up to 34°C). The fog forms over a single grave or interment marker at a time, extends to a radius of between 2 and 60 meters depending on instance, and dissipates without residue within one to four hours.

Onset of SCP-4359 correlates, in 94% of 190 documented instances, with an identifiable act of active research or inquiry into the identity or biography of the interred individual occurring elsewhere, not necessarily near the grave site — a genealogical records request, a journalist's inquiry, a descendant's first successful identification of the grave through archival research, or, in 6 instances, Foundation personnel researching the individual for unrelated case purposes. The correlation holds regardless of the researching party's location, which has in confirmed instances been on a different continent from the affected grave, with fog onset occurring within an average of 40 minutes of the research act (range: 8 minutes to 6 hours).

Personnel or bystanders who enter SCP-4359 fog report no injury but consistently describe an acute, specific sense of being "looked at with recognition," and in 22 cases have independently and correctly stated a fact about the interred individual's life that the reporting person had no prior access to and that was, in each case, subsequently verified against historical records.

The mechanism connecting an act of biographical research to fog formation at a physically remote, unmonitored grave site remains unidentified. No sensor equipment deployed to date has detected any signal, transmission, or energy anomaly at either the research location or the grave site that would account for the apparent correlation.

ADDENDUM 4359-1: Site-88 has restricted access to SCP-4359's case file to personnel not currently conducting genealogical or biographical research into any deceased individual for personal (non-case-related) reasons, following an internal incident in which a researcher's private genealogical inquiry into an unrelated family matter is believed to have triggered fog onset at a grave with no prior SCP-4359 history, 900 kilometers from the researcher's location.

SCP-4360.name: The Final Signature
SCP-4360.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4360 is maintained under Thaumiel classification and restricted procedural control by the Site-88 Office of Internal Ratification, the only body authorized to invoke the phenomenon deliberately. Deliberate invocation is limited to the closure of Foundation containment procedures for anomalies assessed as unstable, incompletely understood, or resistant to conventional procedural revision, and requires joint authorization from a Site Director and one Ethics Committee representative per Protocol 4360-Invoke.

Documents bearing a completed SCP-4360 signature are to be stored in Site-88's Sealed Ratifications vault and are not to be reopened, amended, or re-signed under any circumstance; two attempted re-signings on record have each resulted in the immediate, unexplained failure of the containment procedures the original signature had stabilized (see Incident 4360-3).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4360 refers to an anomalous effect observed when a specific, ritualized signing procedure — developed independently within Foundation administrative practice over approximately three decades and only later recognized as anomalous rather than merely traditional — is performed on a finalized containment procedure document by an authorized signatory. The procedure requires the signatory to sign the document three times in the same ink, in the same physical location, without the document leaving line of sight between signatures, and to read a specified closing formula aloud before the third signature is applied.

Containment procedures ratified through SCP-4360 exhibit a measurable and reproducible stabilizing effect on the anomaly they govern: post-ratification incident rates for anomalies under SCP-4360-ratified procedures are, across 61 tracked cases, an average of 71% lower than pre-ratification incident rates for the same anomaly under the same (textually unchanged) procedure. The effect is not attributable to any change in procedural content, as the ratified document is, deliberately, textually identical to its pre-ratification draft; only the signing act differs.

The mechanism is not understood. Site-88's Thaumaturgy Liaison Office has proposed, without full consensus, that SCP-4360 functions as a genuine binding ritual, operating on some property of institutional commitment or collective belief rather than on the anomaly directly — a hypothesis partially supported by the finding that SCP-4360's stabilizing effect is measurably weaker (approximately 40% reduction rather than 71%) when the signing procedure is performed by a signatory who privately, per post-signing interview, did not believe the procedure would have any effect.

The Foundation's reliance on SCP-4360 for procedural stabilization is now sufficiently extensive — 61 ratified anomalies as of the most recent audit, several assessed as Keter-class prior to ratification — that the Office of Internal Ratification has flagged, in an internal memo now under Ethics Committee review, the Foundation's growing operational dependency on a ritual its own specialists cannot fully explain, cannot verify will continue to function, and cannot identify a substitute for.

ADDENDUM 4360-1: The original SCP-4360 signing procedure's origin has not been traced to any single directive, training document, or founding text. The earliest confirmed instance, recovered from Site-19 archival records, is a 1962 containment procedure bearing a triple signature and closing formula matching the current standard, filed by a signatory whose personnel record contains no documented training in, or awareness of, any such procedure at the time.

SCP-4361.name: The Apprenticeship Ledger
SCP-4361.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation containment of the phenomenon associated with the informal international trade fellowship known internally as "the Ledger" is observational and advisory rather than physical. A standing team of four handlers, rotated annually, maintains contact with retiring master tradespeople identified through guild registries, insurance filings, and probate records showing unusually rapid, well-documented decline of skilled tradespeople within twelve months of formally certifying an apprentice. Handlers are trained in the relevant trades (locksmithing, lutherie, glazing, clockmaking, bespoke tailoring) sufficiently to conduct plausible cover interviews.

No attempt is made to prevent the transfer of skill or the associated mortality; three prior interventions (Incidents 4361-1 through -3) attempting to medically sustain a master past the transfer window resulted in either transfer failure (the apprentice's acquired skill degraded to baseline within days) or the master's death occurring regardless, on schedule, by means the intervening physicians could not adequately explain. Current policy is to identify masters nearing transfer, offer counseling and end-of-life support framed as an unrelated community health outreach program, and debrief apprentices afterward under a cover story concerning "occupational trauma."

The physical ledger itself — a bound volume, its current custodian unknown to the Foundation, that is somehow updated with each qualifying transfer regardless of Foundation surveillance of candidate masters — has never been recovered or directly observed by Foundation personnel.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4361 refers to a documented pattern among master tradespeople across at least eleven countries and, per genealogical tracing, at least six generations. When a master formally accepts an apprentice and, over a period Foundation data suggests averages fourteen months, deliberately transmits the entirety of their accumulated craft knowledge without withholding any technique, secret, or trade refinement, the master's health begins an otherwise unremarkable decline — commonly diagnosed as an ordinary age-related condition — culminating in death within approximately eleven to thirteen months of the final lesson.

At the moment of the master's death, the apprentice's hands (documented via interview, video, and in six cases direct observation) demonstrate immediate, complete proficiency at the transferred craft equal to or exceeding the master's own peak skill, without further practice. This includes techniques never explicitly demonstrated to the apprentice, suggesting the transfer exceeds ordinary instruction.

Masters within the affected trades are, per interview, broadly aware of this pattern, though rarely willing to discuss it directly even with trusted apprentices. A significant number — Foundation estimates place it above sixty percent of contacted masters — respond to this awareness by unconsciously or deliberately withholding at least one meaningful technique from every apprentice they train, thereby surviving the transfer window at the cost of that technique effectively vanishing from the trade line, since the apprentice will, in turn, also never know to teach it forward. Interviews suggest this withholding is rarely a conscious choice at the time; masters describe "forgetting" to mention a specific step, or "meaning to get to it" indefinitely.

Genealogical trade analysis conducted by Foundation researchers indicates several formerly documented techniques (a specific tempering method in a now-extinct line of Bavarian locksmiths; a lacquer formulation among third-generation Kyoto lute-makers) have measurably vanished from all living practitioners over the past four decades, coinciding with confirmed SCP-4361 transfer events in those lines.

ADDENDUM 4361-A: Interview excerpt, Master Clockmaker Henrik Aalders, eleven days prior to death, conducted under cover of an occupational health survey.

Aalders: You already know. I can see it in how you're asking.
Interviewer: We're just following up on a few—
Aalders: I taught Marta everything. Everything I know how to do with my hands, she can do now, better probably, she's younger. I felt it change last week. Like handing over a key and the lock changing shape behind you.
Interviewer: Is there anything you didn't teach her?
Aalders: [pause, 22 seconds] The regulator escapement my father showed me. The old method, not the one in the books. I keep meaning to write it down for her. I have time.
Interviewer: Do you?
Aalders: [no response logged]

Aalders died nine days later. A post-transfer interview with apprentice Marta Ohler confirmed complete mastery of Aalders' documented repertoire, excluding the escapement technique referenced above, which she reports never having been shown.

SCP-4362.name: The Unheard Frequency
SCP-4362.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation Radio Monitoring Unit 12 maintains continuous, automated recording of all frequencies historically associated with SCP-4362 transmissions, sourced from the volunteer emergency communications network operating under the public designation Regional Auxiliary Relay Corps (RARC). Recording equipment is installed at all seventeen known RARC relay stations under cover of routine equipment maintenance contracts with the two civilian organizations that jointly administer RARC. Personnel embedded within RARC as ordinary volunteer operators (currently four, callsigns withheld) report any transmission matching historical SCP-4362 patterns — specifically, warnings of an impending localized disaster delivered in the transmitting operator's own voice and callsign but outside any scheduled net session — within one hour of occurrence, to permit rapid dispatch of Foundation or front-organization emergency response ahead of the predicted event.

Operators later found to have relayed an SCP-4362 transmission are not detained or informed of Foundation involvement; standard debrief consists of an unrelated volunteer satisfaction survey used to document the operator's memory gap without alerting them to its cause.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4362 designates a recurring anomalous phenomenon within RARC, a legitimate amateur radio emergency-auxiliary network spanning a four-state region, active since 1979. Approximately six to nine times per year, under high-frequency "skip" propagation conditions that allow signals to travel unusually long distances via atmospheric reflection, a RARC relay station receives and forwards a voice transmission warning of a specific, imminent local disaster — structural collapse, wildfire, flash flood, or similar — including exact location and a time window generally between forty minutes and six hours out. Cross-referenced against subsequent events, these warnings have proven accurate in 91.7% of the 118 cases logged by the Foundation to date, with the remainder unconfirmed rather than falsified.

Station logs, and in eleven cases contemporaneous audio recordings, confirm the transmission occurred and was relayed by an identifiable operator using that operator's registered callsign and, per voice analysis, that operator's own voice. In one hundred percent of interviewed cases (n=64), the operator has no memory whatsoever of receiving, speaking, or transcribing the message, despite otherwise intact memory of the surrounding shift. This gap has resisted hypnotic recall, and in nine Foundation-supervised cases, resisted class-A amnestic-reversal protocols, which typically restore even chemically suppressed memory; investigators consider this notable, as it implies the memory was never encoded rather than merely suppressed.

No transmission has been traced to a source outside the RARC network itself — the signal does not originate externally and get relayed, but appears to originate at the reporting station, from the reporting operator, with no detectable point of insertion.

The identity or nature of whatever composes and delivers these warnings through unknowing operators remains undetermined. RARC's founding documents, examined by Foundation historians, predate the earliest confirmed SCP-4362 transmission (1984) by five years, suggesting either a dormant period or an unrelated founding purpose later co-opted.

ADDENDUM 4362-A: Operator interview, callsign redacted, following a confirmed transmission that preceded a grain silo collapse by ninety minutes with three residents evacuated in time.

"I remember checking in at nine, and then I remember the phone ringing at ten forty telling me my callsign went out with a collapse warning. I have nothing in between. I didn't even know silos could do that. I looked it up after, just to understand what I'd apparently said."

The operator declined further sessions. Monitoring continues.

SCP-4363.name: The Understudy Registry
SCP-4363.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The database associated with SCP-4363, publicly known as the Cross-Company Understudy Exchange (CCUE), remains operational and unaltered; deletion or modification attempts (Trials 4363-7 through -9) produced no measurable change in the anomaly's frequency and are suspected to have no effect on a property that is not stored in the database's technical infrastructure. Foundation-affiliated theatrical placement agency Redline Casting Associates maintains a controlling administrative stake in CCUE sufficient to monitor registrations and interview flagged members without alerting member companies to Foundation involvement.

Any registered understudy who has fully memorized a role and remains registered without having performed it for longer than ninety consecutive days is flagged for a discreet follow-up interview, conducted by an embedded caseworker posing as a CCUE wellness liaison, to document the content of SCP-4363-associated false memories (see Description) before natural attrition or cross-contamination with genuine performance memories degrades the account's reliability as data.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4363 is a memory anomaly affecting registered understudies in CCUE's member network who have fully memorized an assigned role and remain registered, without ever going on stage in that role, for more than ninety consecutive days. Affected understudies begin to report detailed, sincerely held episodic memories of having performed the role: a specific night, an audience's reaction, a line fumbled and recovered, the texture of a particular costume. These memories are subjectively indistinguishable from genuine memory, pass standard interview-based deception screening, and in 61 of 203 documented cases have been maintained by the subject even after being shown video evidence of the actual lead performing on the claimed date.

Cross-referencing of these false-memory accounts across geographically and administratively unconnected CCUE productions of the same script has established that understudies who never met, performed in different cities in different years, and in 9 cases were registered under productions using different translations of the source text, independently report performance memories agreeing on invented, non-scripted details not present in any published version of the play — a specific ad-libbed line, a specific technical mishap, a specific unscripted audience interaction — with a rate of cross-subject agreement Foundation statisticians assess as incompatible with coincidence or shared source material.

No mechanism has been identified by which unconnected individuals converge on identical invented content. The false memories do not correspond to any actual performance, by any performer, on record; the 'phantom performance' they describe appears to exist only as a memory, shared and consistent, held by people who did not attend it.

SCP-4363 does not resolve when the understudy is later cast and genuinely performs the role; genuine and phantom performance memories then coexist, and 34 interviewed subjects in this category report difficulty determining, without external verification, which of several remembered performances actually occurred.

ADDENDUM 4363-A: Case file summary. Subject remained registered as understudy for a regional production for eleven months without performing, developed a detailed phantom memory of a performance including a specific mistimed entrance during Act 2, and upon later obtaining video footage of the actual lead's full run, confirmed no such mistimed entrance occurred in any recorded performance. Subject has since requested, and been granted, indefinite leave from further CCUE registration, citing an inability to 'keep track of what I actually did.'

SCP-4364.name: The Rare-Type Registry
SCP-4364.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The registry associated with SCP-4364, operating publicly as a boutique private blood-matching concierge service under the name Meridian Compatibility Partners, is permitted to continue operations under Foundation financial control, exercised through a shell holding company that acquired majority ownership in 2009. Foundation medical liaisons review all match requests before fulfillment, prioritizing genuine medical need and declining requests assessed as recreational, cosmetic (a documented minority of wealthy clients have sought transfusions for purported longevity or vitality effects unsupported by any Foundation-confirmed benefit beyond ordinary transfusion), or otherwise inconsistent with donor welfare.

All 214 known SCP-4364 donors are enrolled in a long-term health monitoring program, framed to donors as a standard rare-blood-type research cohort, which tracks the accelerated senescence associated with donation and provides medical and psychological support. Donors are not informed of the precise mechanism, though several have independently arrived at an accurate understanding.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4364 designates a blood phenotype, currently unclassified within any recognized blood group system, carried by 214 identified individuals with no established familial, geographic, or ethnic pattern connecting them. The phenotype cross-matches as compatible with all recipients regardless of the recipient's own type (functioning as a universal donor) and additionally confers, upon transfusion, resistance to organ transplant rejection, resolution of otherwise treatment-resistant clotting disorders, and, in nine documented cases, apparent remission of conditions with no established transfusion-based treatment, at rates well beyond any documented placebo or coincidental recovery baseline.

Each unit donated by an SCP-4364 carrier accelerates that donor's biological aging, measured via independent cellular and epigenetic markers, by approximately eleven months per standard donation unit, an effect with no observed variance based on donor health, age, or recovery time between donations. This aging is permanent and cumulative; it does not slow, reverse, or plateau with repeated donation, and carriers who donate at the medically recommended maximum frequency show biological ages ten to twenty years beyond chronological age within a decade of their first donation.

All 214 donors report, independent of contact with one another, an unusually strong compulsion to respond when contacted for a compatible match, describing it as difficult or impossible to decline despite conscious awareness of the personal cost, several using language resembling reported descriptions of blood-donation urges in ordinary donors but substantially more intense. No carrier has been identified who was aware of their phenotype prior to a first donation revealing it through routine cross-match testing; the discovery is, in every case, accidental.

Object class Safe reflects the phenomenon's containment stability and the absence of any need for physical restriction; the primary containment concern is the registry's coordination and donor welfare rather than the phenotype itself, which cannot be induced, transferred, or suppressed by any tested means.

ADDENDUM 4364-A: Donor 097, age 34 (biological age assessed at 51), on continuing to donate despite awareness of the cost: "I've done the math. I know what it takes off the other end. I still can't say no when they call. It doesn't feel like choosing not to. It feels like the choice was never really offered."

SCP-4365.name: The Obituary Desk
SCP-4365.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Foundation maintains covert editorial oversight of the Ashford County Clarion, a weekly regional newspaper of legitimate circulation (approx. 4,100), through a controlling stake held by a Foundation front media holding company since 1998. The obituary desk, currently staffed by two writers, operates under a standing internal policy — instituted at the paper prior to Foundation acquisition and preserved without alteration — requiring written, funeral-home-confirmed notice of death before any obituary draft is begun. This policy is treated by Foundation liaisons as a critical safeguard rather than routine editorial practice and is never relaxed for deadline pressure.

Any draft obituary begun, in whole or part, for a person not subsequently confirmed dead within seventy-two hours is to be immediately reported to the embedded Foundation liaison (currently posing as the paper's managing editor), who initiates Protocol Ashford-Black: identification and continuous monitoring of the named individual, restriction of the draft's further circulation, and, where the subject's death appears imminent and consistent with an accidental draft's content, preparation for standard amnesiac and evidence suppression response.

Personnel are prohibited from testing SCP-4365's properties under any circumstances. Two prior unauthorized tests by since-terminated Foundation researchers (see Incident 4365-2) are addressed below.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4365 refers to an anomalous property of obituaries completed by the obituary desk of the Ashford County Clarion, first identified in 1961 and confirmed to predate Foundation acquisition of the paper. A completed obituary — one written to the desk's normal editorial standard and set for publication — retroactively and prospectively fixes the described death as factually true in every detail, including details fabricated, guessed, or erroneous relative to the deceased's actual circumstances, provided the piece was begun only after the desk received confirmation of death from a licensed funeral home.

The mechanism does not require publication; an obituary shredded, deleted, or never printed still "fixes" the described details, which subsequently match forensic and medical records regardless of whether those records were available to the writer at time of composition.
