Writers have, in eleven documented cases, invented specific but plausible causes of death (a rare cardiac condition, a specific accident mechanism) that later matched autopsy findings exactly, despite the writer having no access to medical information at time of writing.

SCP-4365 becomes acutely dangerous when a draft is mistakenly begun for a living person, typically through a funeral home clerical error, a shared name, or premature notification. In four documented such cases (the earliest, 1974, predates Foundation involvement and was reconstructed from archive review), the named living individual subsequently died within days to weeks, by means consistent with the erroneous draft's content, despite the draft never being completed or published. Object class Keter reflects the demonstrated potential for the desk, or a comparable mechanism, to be deliberately weaponized against a specific living target by anyone able to manufacture a false funeral home confirmation — a vulnerability confirmed by Incident 4365-2, in which a terminated researcher successfully produced a false confirmation for a test subject, who died of the drafted cause six days later before the draft could be intercepted.

ADDENDUM 4365-B: Current obituary desk writer Diane Kowalczyk, employed 1988–present, on the policy: "I don't write about the living. I don't write about the almost-dead. I wait for the call from the home. It sounds superstitious until you're the one holding the pen."

SCP-4366.name: The Night Janitorial Pool
SCP-4366.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation control of SCP-4366 is exercised through majority ownership of Cresthill Facility Staffing, a legitimate regional contract-janitorial agency supplying night-shift cleaning personnel to approximately 340 corporate office buildings across a metropolitan area. Ownership was acquired in 2011 following identification of the anomaly. No changes have been made to Cresthill's assignment algorithm, which randomly rotates janitorial staff across client buildings on a rolling basis and predates Foundation acquisition; attempts to analyze or predict its assignment logic (see Addendum 4366-A) have not identified a conventional mechanism.

All Cresthill employees who report unusual cleaning tasks (described by staff, without prompting, in mundane terms such as "the big coffee spill" or "the glass thing in 14B") are logged by shift supervisors, themselves Foundation-aware Cresthill managers, without alerting the reporting employee. Buildings with a logged incident are cross-checked against employee attendance, security footage, and after-hours entry logs for that building; in a review of 89 such incidents, no supporting evidence has been found that the described event (assessed via residue as consistent with violence, acute psychological crisis, or property destruction) occurred, was reported, or is known to any building occupant.

No intervention is made in Cresthill's operations. Personnel are not informed of the anomaly and are not tested, screened, or specially selected; ordinary hiring and rotation continues.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4366 designates an anomalous correlation between Cresthill Facility Staffing's night-shift janitorial pool and the appearance, in seemingly random client office buildings, of physical residue consistent with violent or severely disruptive incidents — bloodstains, broken glass, overturned furniture, scorch marks — for which no corroborating record exists in security footage, badge-access logs, incident reports, insurance claims, or subsequent interviews with building occupants and management.

Individually, no Cresthill employee perceives the residue as anomalous. Interviewed staff (n=41) describe cleaning ordinary messes — spilled liquid, broken glassware, disarranged furniture from a supposed after-hours event — using mundane, consistent, but incorrect terminology, even when the residue tests positive for human blood, accelerant, or other materials inconsistent with the stated description. No tested method (direct questioning, hypnosis, chemical memory enhancement) has produced an accurate description from an employee of what they cleaned; the category of information appears categorically inaccessible to them rather than suppressed, as employees show no distress, hesitation, or physiological deception markers when giving the inaccurate description.

Foundation analysis of building assignment patterns suggests, without statistical certainty, that buildings receiving a residue-cleaning assignment are more likely than baseline to have hosted an anomalous or violent event per other, unrelated Foundation and non-Foundation incident data for that address — though the "event" in question is typically otherwise undocumented and unwitnessed, suggesting the janitorial dispatch may be the sole surviving evidence that anything occurred at all.

Object class Safe reflects the passive, self-resolving nature of the phenomenon; the acute concern is epistemic rather than physical — the pool appears to be functioning as an unwitting, unexplained cleanup and containment layer for incidents the Foundation itself has no other record of, implying the existence of an external allocating agency whose scope and purpose remain unknown.

ADDENDUM 4366-A: Statement, Cresthill employee, routine post-shift check-in, unprompted: "Someone really went to town on that conference room. Red cleaning solution everywhere, like they knocked over ten bottles of it. Chair was broken clean in half. Whole building was locked up tight when I got there, though. Nobody signed in all night." No incident of any kind was logged for that building or floor by any other source.

SCP-4367.name: The Standing Coverage Pool
SCP-4367.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation Medical Oversight Group maintains covert administrative access to the shared digital on-call scheduling system used by Meridian Rural Health Partnership (MRHP), a consortium of eleven underserved emergency departments spanning a three-state rural region, through a placed systems-administration contractor. Physicians whose names appear on the MRHP roster, regardless of actual shift status, are cataloged; any physician exhibiting the compulsive travel response defined below is flagged and, upon confirmed onset, discreetly escorted rather than obstructed, as physical restraint has in two documented cases (Incidents 4367-3, 4367-6) resulted in the physician sustaining injury while attempting to continue toward the hospital regardless.

Patients meeting the qualifying trauma profile (clinical death on arrival with continuing, non-standard vital signs) are, upon identification, to be isolated to a single treatment bay pending arrival of the responding physician; Foundation medical personnel do not attempt treatment themselves, as all seven attempts to substitute non-roster physicians for the responding SCP-4367 physician have resulted in patient death within the hour, whereas roster-physician-attended cases show a 74% durable survival rate at 30 days.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4367 designates an anomalous compulsion affecting physicians listed on the MRHP shared on-call roster, triggered specifically by the admission, at any of the eleven affiliated emergency departments, of a patient presenting clinically dead on arrival (no cardiac or respiratory activity, fixed pupils, consistent with death by standard diagnostic criteria) whose vital signs nonetheless continue to register, intermittently and without medical explanation, on standard monitoring equipment.

Upon such admission, every physician currently listed on the shared roster — including physicians off duty, on leave, geographically distant, or not legally scheduled for that facility — experiences an overwhelming, physically compulsive need to travel immediately to the admitting facility, described uniformly by affected physicians as categorically different from professional obligation or concern, closer to an involuntary physical drive comparable to a reflex. In documented cases, physicians have left family events, medical conferences on other continents, and in one case a personal hospitalization, arriving at the qualifying facility between eleven minutes and (in the continental case) nineteen hours after onset, all cases resulting in arrival before the patient's status resolved one way or the other.

Upon arrival, the compelled physician performs interventions on the qualifying patient that Foundation medical review has assessed as either medically inappropriate to the presented condition or, in four cases, procedurally impossible given the equipment and time available, resulting in the patient's survival and eventual return to a stable, ordinary physiological state. The treating physician subsequently has no memory of traveling to the facility or of the intervention performed, though memory of the compulsion's onset (the initial, overwhelming urge) is retained.

The relationship between roster inclusion and the compulsion is confirmed: physicians removed from the shared digital roster, even while continuing to practice at an affiliated facility under a separate scheduling system, do not experience the compulsion in subsequent qualifying admissions.

ADDENDUM 4367-A: Dr. Priya Nakamura, on a compelled response from an academic conference 1,900 miles away: "I stood up in the middle of a session. I don't remember deciding to leave, I remember being in a cab. I don't remember any of the flight. I remember standing over a patient with my hands already moving and not remembering the last four hours of my own life."

SCP-4368.name: The Lighthouse Log
SCP-4368.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Foundation maintains SCP-4368 through indirect financial and administrative support of the Keeper's Fellowship, an informal international association of individuals — currently 61 confirmed — who maintain daily handwritten logbook entries at fully automated lighthouses no longer requiring staffed operation. Support is delivered through a maritime heritage preservation nonprofit funding small stipends and housing allowances to Fellowship members, most of whom hold no official employment relationship with the lighthouses they log.

Any lighthouse under Fellowship coverage found to have gone more than eighteen hours without a fresh entry is escalated to Foundation regional liaisons, who dispatch a Fellowship member (preferentially the assigned keeper, or a trained backup from a roster of 40 additional individuals) to restore logging before the thirty-hour threshold associated with measurable coastal instability is reached. Fourteen coastal sites currently lack a reliable local keeper; these are prioritized for Fellowship recruitment, complicated by the requirement, established through trial and error, that effective keepers must maintain long-term, largely uninterrupted residence near the assigned lighthouse.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4368 designates a confirmed causal relationship between sustained handwritten logbook entry at any of at least 74 identified coastal lighthouse sites and the short-term geological and tidal stability of the surrounding coastline. Entries must be handwritten (typed, dictated, or digitally logged entries do not produce the effect), made by a specific individual associated with that site over time (a substitute's entry is effective but less so, with instability accumulating faster during substitute coverage), and need not be substantive — repeated, near-identical entries recording routine, unremarkable conditions are as effective as detailed ones.

When a covered lighthouse goes without a fresh entry for approximately eighteen to thirty hours, the adjacent coastline (typically a radius of 1.5 to 4 kilometers) begins exhibiting measurable anomalies: erosion rates increase by a factor of four to nine relative to baseline for that coastline type, tidal timing drifts from astronomical prediction by up to several hours, and in nine documented cases, charted rocks, shoals, or sandbars have measurably shifted position by tens of meters within a single missed-logging period. A resumed entry halts further drift within hours and reverses accumulated instability over a period roughly proportional to the length of the lapse, typically days to weeks.

Fellowship members, largely unaware of the precise mechanism (most believe their logging to be a meaningful but non-anomalous maritime tradition, and Foundation policy is to preserve this belief where possible), uniformly describe the obligation using language closer to vocation or inherited duty than employment; several current keepers inherited the role informally from a parent or mentor with no other channel of transmission, and Foundation attempts to recruit and train keepers with no prior connection to a site have a substantially lower success rate (44%) than informal succession within existing keeper families or communities (91%).

Object class Safe reflects long-term containment stability, though the Foundation notes with concern that the total number of active Fellowship keepers has declined by approximately 30% over the past twenty years as the tradition's informal, largely undocumented transmission fails to keep pace with keeper retirement and death.

ADDENDUM 4368-A: Fellowship keeper Rosalind Auer, third-generation keeper at Cape Ferrant Light, on why she continues a role with no formal pay or recognition: "My mother used to say the light doesn't need us anymore but the water still does. I didn't understand that until I missed a week once, when my mother was dying. You could see the shoreline different when I came back. Nobody else noticed. I did."

SCP-4369.name: The Correspondence Match
SCP-4369.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation monitoring of SCP-4369 is conducted through an embedded membership secretary position within the Continental Postal Chess Circle (CPCC), a legitimate correspondence chess organization founded in 1951 and currently maintaining active correspondence for approximately 1,900 games worldwide. The secretary position, held continuously by Foundation personnel since 1988, provides access to full game records, member rosters, and — critically — succession notifications, filed when a member intends to pass an in-progress game to a family member or household associate following incapacitation or death.

Foundation personnel do not intervene to force resignations or otherwise alter game outcomes. Attempts to do so (Incident 4369-4, in which a Foundation liaison resigned a stalled 1962 game on behalf of an incapacitated player without consulting the family) resulted in immediate, severe injury to the player's household, confirming that the misfortune effect described below applies regardless of whether the resigning party is the original registered player.

Games identified as approaching 40+ years' duration are flagged for close monitoring, as historical data indicates lopsided long-duration games carry markedly higher associated misfortune upon eventual resignation or the games' rare natural conclusion.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4369 designates an anomalous consequence attached to resignation in postal (mail-based) correspondence chess games registered with CPCC. When a player formally resigns a game, or a game is otherwise terminated by abandonment (no move submitted within the club's forfeiture window), the resigning or forfeiting player experiences a misfortune — ranging from minor bad luck to serious injury or property loss, per case review of 112 documented resignations — within days of the resignation being logged. Severity correlates strongly (r=0.81) with the player's material and positional deficit at the point of resignation: resigning a nearly-lost game produces comparatively minor misfortune, while resigning a game abandoned decades earlier at a severe disadvantage has produced outcomes including three documented deaths.

Games are not resolved by ordinary means such as time control, as CPCC correspondence rules impose no strict time limit provided some engagement with the game continues; as a direct consequence, a substantial number of CPCC members are, per club records, playing out games that reached decisive, effectively lost positions decades earlier, making one or two moves per year to sustain "ongoing" status and avoid triggering resignation.

When an original player dies or becomes incapacitated mid-game, a household member (commonly, though not exclusively, a descendant) frequently reports a strong compulsion to inherit the correspondence, adopting the deceased player's handwriting style, address, and playing habits closely enough that most opposing players either do not notice the substitution or decline to acknowledge it. CPCC records show 34 games currently being played, unbroken, by a third or later generation of substitutes for the original registered player, the oldest dating to 1954.

A documented but informally observed practice holds that a game formally and properly inherited by a willing heir, following correct procedure, partially resets the accumulated positional deficit's associated risk — the mechanism for this reduction is not understood, and CPCC's own written rules make no reference to it.

ADDENDUM 4369-A: Member correspondence excerpt, 2019, discussing a game begun by the writer's grandfather in 1958 and inherited by the writer in 2003: "I am down a rook and two pawns in a position my grandfather described in his own notes as 'unsalvageable.' I have made one move a year for sixteen years. I am aware how this looks. I am not stopping."

SCP-4370.name: The Process Servers Fraternity
SCP-4370.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation Legal Anomalies Division maintains a monitored liaison relationship with the Old Bailiff Fraternity (OBF), an insular trade fraternity of licensed process servers operating primarily across a six-state region, through two embedded members (currently journeyman rank, insufficient for access to senior ritual procedure). Full OBF membership rolls, ritual procedure documentation, and client intake records remain inaccessible to the Foundation; current understanding of SCP-4370 is assembled from embedded-member reporting, intercepted correspondence, and post-incident interview.

Individuals or organizations believed to be seeking OBF services against a Foundation-relevant entity (current or former Foundation personnel, contained anomalous individuals with recognized legal personhood, or Foundation front organizations) are to be identified and, where operationally feasible, the service prevented through conventional legal or administrative means before ritual conditions can be completed; OBF ritual practice appears strictly bound by preparation and completion conditions and cannot, per current understanding, be rushed or improvised.

Members who complete an unusual service are not detained. OBF's internal enforcement of consequences for incomplete or improperly performed service (see Description) has proven, in three observed cases, sufficient deterrent that Foundation intervention against individual servers is considered low priority relative to intercepting client intake.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4370 designates a body of ritual practice maintained within OBF enabling legally and metaphysically binding service of process upon recipients not ordinarily servable through conventional means, including specific classes of corporate shell entities, certain categories of deceased persons' estates under specific unresolved-obligation circumstances, and — per seven confirmed OBF service actions reviewed by the Foundation — no fewer than four distinct non-human or conceptual entities demonstrated to hold contractual or legal obligations recognized under civil court rulings exploiting jurisdictional definitions of "legal person."

Ritual service requires precise, non-negotiable conditions specific to the recipient category: documented requirements include exact phrasing recited from memory rather than read, service performed at specific astronomically or calendrically defined times, and, in all reviewed cases, the serving member's deliberate avoidance of direct eye contact with the recipient or its representative throughout the encounter. Deviation from required conditions, per OBF internal doctrine, results in "failed" service that does not bind the recipient and instead transfers the recipient's legal or metaphysical obligation directly onto the serving member.

Successfully completed unusual service extracts a cost from the serving member: a contiguous period of the member's own remembered personal history — chosen by a mechanism OBF members describe as involuntary rather than selected — becomes permanently and irrecoverably lost to them, confirmed by family interview and, in nine cases, documented gaps in personal records the member has no memory of having created. Cost duration correlates with the scale or danger classification of the entity or estate served, ranging from several hours (minor shell-entity service) to, in one documented case, approximately six years.

OBF members accept this cost as an occupational condition; unusual services command fees the Foundation assesses as 40 to 200 times standard process-serving rates, and members report the fraternity's internal culture treats memory loss similarly to how conventional hazardous trades treat physical risk — acknowledged, insured against informally through mutual aid, but not treated as disqualifying.

Object class Keter reflects both the entities confirmed servable through this mechanism and the fraternity's demonstrated willingness to accept contracts from outside parties, including, per intercepted correspondence, inquiries the Foundation assesses as originating from other anomalous or criminal organizations seeking to bind dangerous entities to obligations for their own purposes.

ADDENDUM 4370-A: Intercepted internal OBF correspondence, senior member to journeyman, redacted: "You'll lose the six weeks either way, might as well be six weeks you don't want back. Don't look at it. Say it like you mean it even when you don't understand a word. And don't ask what happens if you get the wording wrong, because you already know, you watched Bellamy find out."

SCP-4371.name: The Storm Spotters Net
SCP-4371.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4371 is maintained as an active Foundation asset under joint administration of the Foundation's Meteorological Applications Office and a cover organization operating as a regional SKYWARN-affiliated volunteer weather-spotter network, publicly known as the Tri-State Spotter Alliance (TSSA), with approximately 2,200 registered volunteer members. Foundation control is exercised through the TSSA's report-relay hub, staffed entirely by Foundation personnel posing as National Weather Service liaison volunteers, which determines which of the many incoming spotter reports are relayed onward as "confirmed" sightings versus logged without relay.

Deliberate use of SCP-4371 for severe weather suppression or redirection (Protocol Fairwind) requires authorization from the Meteorological Applications Office director and is limited to scenarios where naturally forming severe weather (tracked via conventional meteorology, independent of SCP-4371) threatens a population center of 10,000 or more. Execution involves selectively relaying matching reports from Foundation-placed "trusted" spotters (67 individuals recruited into TSSA specifically for this purpose, unaware of the mechanism, believing themselves ordinary highly-engaged volunteers) describing a competing formation over a pre-selected unpopulated target zone, until relay volume reaches the empirically established activation threshold.

Use of Protocol Fairwind for purposes beyond population protection, including the agricultural rainfall trials referenced in Addendum 4371-B, requires O5 authorization.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4371 designates an anomalous causal relationship between aggregated volunteer storm-spotter reports relayed through TSSA's hub and the actual subsequent formation of the reported severe weather event at the reported location. When a threshold number (empirically established at eleven to fourteen, varying by season and region) of independent TSSA-registered spotters relay matching, unprompted reports of a specific developing severe weather formation (wall cloud, funnel cloud, particular hail signature) not yet corroborated by radar or satellite data, that formation subsequently develops at the reported location within an average of 51 minutes, regardless of prior atmospheric conditions or forecast models, which show no basis for the eventual formation prior to the reports.

The effect requires genuine, independently arrived-at spotter belief; reports made with conscious intent to trigger formation, or coordinated in advance among spotters, consistently fail to produce the effect (23 controlled tests by Foundation researchers attempting deliberate triggering without genuine spotter belief have a 0% success rate), indicating the mechanism responds specifically to a threshold of good-faith, independently formed perception rather than to the report content or volume alone.

Reports below threshold do not trigger formation and appear to function as ordinary, non-anomalous spotting activity; TSSA's public-facing operations and vast majority of its volunteer base show no indication of anomalous character and the organization performs a genuine, valuable severe-weather-reporting public service independent of Foundation exploitation of the underlying mechanism.

Since Protocol Fairwind's authorization in 2016, the Foundation has executed 31 confirmed storm redirections, preventing an estimated combined direct-strike exposure to approximately 340,000 residents across affected population centers, with no documented instance of the redirected formation causing harm at its induced location, all 31 having been directed to unpopulated agricultural or wilderness zones pre-cleared by Foundation front-organization land acquisition.

ADDENDUM 4371-B: Per Site Director approval, a limited trial series (Trials Fairwind-Ag-1 through -6) tested whether sub-severe threshold spotter reports could induce beneficial, non-severe precipitation events in drought-affected agricultural zones using the same mechanism at lower report thresholds. Results were inconsistent (2 of 6 trials produced measurable beneficial rainfall; the remainder produced no effect or, in one case, induced hail damage inconsistent with drought-relief goals). Further trials are pending refinement of the threshold model and remain classified above Site Director review.

SCP-4372.name: The Foster Line
SCP-4372.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The network associated with SCP-4372, internally referred to by its own members as "the Line," operates entirely outside state child welfare systems and has, despite sustained effort since its 1994 discovery, resisted full Foundation infiltration; current oversight consists of six confirmed embedded contacts at varying trust levels within an estimated total network size of 140 to 190 households across a wide, non-contiguous geographic distribution.

The Foundation does not attempt to dismantle the Line or remove children from it. Two prior removal attempts (Incidents 4372-2 and 4372-5) resulted in mass-casualty entity awakening events, addressed under separate incident documentation, confirming removal risk exceeds the Line's own documented internal relocation practice. Current Foundation policy is passive monitoring, identification of Line households for demographic and risk-pattern tracking, and quiet diversion of state child-welfare inquiries away from confirmed Line placements where doing so does not itself compromise the child's safety.

Any child independently identified by Foundation personnel as bearing the physical or behavioral markers associated with SCP-4372 host status, but not already known to the Line, is not to be placed with the Line nor removed from standard channels without O5 authorization, given unresolved uncertainty regarding whether Line-specific rearing practices are necessary preconditions for successful dormancy or merely correlated with it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4372 designates a self-organized, informally hereditary network of foster households that identifies and takes in infants and young children who are, per Foundation biological and metaphysical assessment, hosts to a dormant parasitic entity of unconfirmed origin and classification, provisionally designated SCP-4372-A. Identification of host children by Line members occurs through means the network's own members cannot fully articulate — commonly described as recognizing a specific cry pattern, an atypical birthmark configuration, or simply an immediate, strong certainty upon contact — and has, in all 61 cases reviewed by the Foundation, correctly identified genuine SCP-4372-A hosts with no documented false positive.

Children raised within the Line's specific, only partially documented rearing practices remain in stable, apparently permanent dormancy through adulthood, at which point they typically leave the network and, per available follow-up, lead ordinary lives with no further host-related incident. Practices confirmed by Foundation observation include systematic withholding of the child's given birth name in favor of a network-internal name until approximately age twelve, and mandatory relocation to a different Line household every three to five years regardless of the child's attachment to a current placement or caregiver's willingness to continue.

Children removed from the Line prematurely, or raised past documented attachment thresholds without relocation, show markedly elevated risk of SCP-4372-A activation; four documented activation incidents (three from premature removal, one from a Line caregiver's refusal to relocate a child past the five-year threshold) produced localized mass-casualty events before Foundation or Line containment response, with a combined confirmed death toll of 61.

The mandated relocation practice imposes severe, repeated emotional cost on Line caregivers, who form and then are required to dissolve a parental bond with each child roughly every three to five years, permanently and without the recognition, support, or institutional structure available to conventional foster systems; interviewed former Line caregivers uniformly describe the relationship's end as comparable to bereavement, repeated across a caregiving career that may span twenty or more children over several decades.

The Line's total absence of external accountability, its correct but unexplained identification method, and the confirmed catastrophic risk of any interruption together justify Keter classification; the entity or process the Line exists to contain remains, itself, largely unstudied, as the Foundation's priority has necessarily remained the network's stability rather than SCP-4372-A's direct investigation.

ADDENDUM 4372-A: Embedded contact report, former Line caregiver of eleven children across twenty-six years, on why she has not left the network despite the repeated cost: "You ask me how I do it again and again. I don't do it again. I do it once, differently, eleven times. Nobody trains you for the leaving. You just find out you can survive it, and then you find out you can survive it again."

SCP-4373.name: The Rightful-Recipient Powder
SCP-4373.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Approximately 38 kilograms of SCP-4373 are stored in three sealed steel tins within the Records Annex of Site-77, held at 40-50% relative humidity to prevent clumping. Access requires sign-off from two Level 4 personnel and a written statement of intended recipient, which is filed regardless of whether the request is approved. Foundation mail-handling personnel are instructed to inspect incoming and outgoing packages for a fine grey-black residue matching SCP-4373's signature; any item found pre-treated is to be quarantined in a lead-lined container and its stated destination logged with the Site-77 Records Division before it is opened by anyone. Under no circumstances is SCP-4373 to be applied to material addressed to, or originating from, O5 Command without prior authorization from at least two Council members, following the events described in Addendum 4373-2. Personnel who discover they have received an item bearing SCP-4373 residue are to report to the nearest Ethics Committee liaison before opening it.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4373 is a fine, grey-black powder, chemically resembling powdered graphite with an unidentified crystalline additive comprising roughly 4% of its mass by volume. When a quantity of SCP-4373 equivalent to a light dusting (approximately 0.2 g per square meter of surface) is applied to the exterior of a sealed envelope, parcel, or similar container prior to transit through any postal or courier system, the item will arrive not at the address written upon it, but at whatever destination SCP-4373 determines to be the "correct" one. This determination does not appear to follow the address, the sender's intent, or any legible instruction; it instead appears to track some combination of who most needs, is most owed, or most closely matches a description of the item's contents, without regard for whether that party currently exists, is aware the item is coming, or occupies an address reachable by conventional means.

Deliveries verified under controlled testing have reached: a Foundation researcher eleven years before her recruitment, at an address she had not yet moved to; the estate of a recipient deceased six weeks prior, care of a probate attorney who had not yet been assigned the case; and, in one instance, a job title rather than a named individual, resulting in delivery to whichever Site-77 employee held that title at the time the item happened to arrive, regardless of turnover. SCP-4373 was recovered in 1994 from an unmarked pallet in the Site-77 receiving dock after three items addressed to external parties were instead delivered, correctly sealed and postmarked, to Foundation personnel with no listed connection to the senders.

ADDENDUM 4373-1: Of eighteen controlled test deliveries conducted between 1995 and 2003, eleven reached a verifiable, appropriate destination not written on the parcel. Four reached destinations that could not subsequently be verified to exist. Three have not been accounted for.

ADDENDUM 4373-2: In 2011, Site-77 Director Okur applied SCP-4373 to a personal letter of resignation, intending it to reach "whoever should read it." The letter was later found, unopened, filed in the O5 Command physical archive under a classification code that did not exist prior to the letter's arrival. The code has since been used four more times, by four different authors, none of whom applied SCP-4373 to their correspondence. Testing on this phenomenon has been suspended pending Ethics Committee review.

SCP-4374.name: The Unbroken Varnish
SCP-4374.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Remaining stock of SCP-4374 (approx. 11 liters) is stored in its original sealed containers in a standard chemical locker at Site-19, Storage Wing C. Use requires a Level 3 work order specifying the object to be treated and confirmation that the treatment site is at least 4 meters from any occupied workstation. Furniture, containers, or equipment treated with SCP-4374 prior to the 2009 moratorium remain in circulation across nine sites and are not being recalled, as removal has been assessed as higher-risk than continued use; a running inventory is maintained by Site Logistics. Personnel working near SCP-4374-treated objects are advised, not required, to maintain a minimum 2-meter clearance during periods of physical strain on the object (heavy loading, impact, structural stress).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4374 is an amber, faintly resinous varnish, originally manufactured under a commercial furniture-finishing brand discontinued in 1987. When applied to a solid, load-bearing object -- wood, most metals, and glass have tested positive; textiles and unfired ceramics have not -- the object becomes highly resistant to fracture, splintering, shattering, or structural failure under conditions that would otherwise cause it, up to and including direct impact from vehicles and small-caliber firearms. The treated object does not become invulnerable; rather, it does not appear to absorb the destructive energy directed at it. That energy is instead measurably transferred to the nearest living organism above 2 kilograms of body mass, manifesting as blunt trauma, fracture, or (in five recorded cases) full-body impact injury consistent with the force the object itself would otherwise have sustained, regardless of that organism's distance, orientation, or awareness of the event. The transfer is near-instantaneous and does not appear to be blockable by intervening solid matter; a subject in an adjacent, sealed room has been injured by force directed at an SCP-4374-treated door.

SCP-4374 came to Foundation attention in 1988 following an insurance claim regarding a filing cabinet that survived a warehouse collapse undamaged; the sole employee on the premises sustained injuries consistent with having been struck by a falling structure, despite being found standing, uninjured by any physical contact, twelve meters from the cabinet.

ADDENDUM:
A 2009 containment review recommended immediate recall of all SCP-4374-treated furniture following an incident in which a treated conference table absorbed the structural collapse of a partial ceiling failure at Site-19; the transferred force was distributed across seven personnel present in the room, none of whom were touching the table, resulting in two fatalities. The recall was not implemented. Current object class remains Safe on the basis that SCP-4374 itself, unapplied, presents no risk; the Ethics Committee has requested this classification be revisited.

SCP-4375.name: The Waking Draught
SCP-4375.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Production of SCP-4375 is restricted to a single approved urn at each of Site-19, Site-45, and Site-77, operated only by kitchen staff holding Level 2 clearance or higher who have signed briefing document 4375-K. The urns are refilled from a 200-liter concentrate reserve held in Refrigerated Storage, access to which requires Level 4 authorization logged individually per withdrawal. SCP-4375 is to be served only during shifts designated "night watch" or equivalent by site scheduling and only to personnel who have signed the standing consent form referenced in Addendum 4375-3. Any personnel who report drinking SCP-4375 outside an authorized shift are to be interviewed by the Memetics Division before returning to duty.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4375 outwardly resembles strong black coffee and was, until 2016, believed by most consuming personnel to simply be strong black coffee; current site instant-coffee stock is in fact SCP-4375 concentrate, diluted at standard ratio. Personnel who consume SCP-4375 during an overnight shift experience the expected effects of caffeine -- alertness, reduced perceived fatigue -- but retain no accurate memory of the shift's events afterward. In place of accurate memory, subjects report a coherent, internally consistent recollection of an uneventful shift: routine checks completed, nothing anomalous observed, no incidents to report. This substitute memory is indistinguishable, from the subject's own perspective, from an ordinary memory, and subjects who are shown documentary evidence contradicting it (security footage, incident reports in their own handwriting) initially respond with confusion or mild irritation before accepting the evidence, at which point the original substitute memory is not restored to accuracy but is instead updated to incorporate the new information as something they "must have forgotten to mention."

SCP-4375 was not discovered; it was identified. In 2016, a routine audit of overnight incident logs found a twenty-two-year discrepancy between the number of overnight anomalous events recorded by automated monitoring systems and the number described in personnel debriefs, across every site where the current coffee stock had been distributed. No record has been found of SCP-4375's introduction, procurement order, or original formulation. The concentrate reserve was already in place when Refrigerated Storage was inventoried under the current cataloguing system in 1994.

ADDENDUM 4375-1: Interviews with senior logistics staff active before 1994 have not identified who authorized the initial order. Three former staff independently described the coffee as having "always been the good stuff we got for nights," suggesting the substitution predates available records.

ADDENDUM 4375-2: A 2019 proposal to discontinue SCP-4375 and replace it with standard coffee was rejected by site administration at two of three sites, on the stated grounds that "removing it now would tell the night shift immediately what they haven't been told for twenty years," and that current personnel wellbeing metrics for night-shift staff, while based on false memories, are measurably better than those recorded for equivalent day-shift personnel.

ADDENDUM 4375-3: The "standing consent form" referenced above is itself served alongside a first cup of SCP-4375 during onboarding, and signing it is, per current administrative policy, retroactively treated as informed consent regardless of whether the signee recalls having read it.

SCP-4376.name: The Second Uniform
SCP-4376.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Standard-issue field uniforms manufactured from SCP-4376-affected fabric (currently nine confirmed sets, designated SCP-4376-1 through -9) are stored in individually sealed garment bags in a climate-controlled locker at Site-64, distinct from the general uniform supply chain following the 2017 reclassification. No SCP-4376 garment is to be issued for active field use; all nine are retained solely for study. The Foundation's uniform manufacturing contract has been quietly redirected to a different supplier at all sites where SCP-4376 stock originated, though the original supplier's identity and current status remain unconfirmed. Any newly manufactured uniform found to exhibit SCP-4376 properties during routine post-incident laundering is to be pulled from circulation and forwarded to Site-64 with full wear history.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4376 refers to a recurring anomalous property observed in a specific weave of standard-issue Foundation field uniform fabric, sourced from at least one now-unidentifiable manufacturing batch mixed into otherwise ordinary supply shipments between approximately 2004 and 2017. Garments made from SCP-4376 fabric are visually and texturally indistinguishable from unaffected uniforms and do not test anomalous by any material analysis performed to date. The property manifests only when the wearer sustains a fatal or near-fatal injury while wearing the garment: the fabric itself sustains no visible damage or staining regardless of the nature of the injury, including injuries that would be expected to perforate, tear, or saturate the fabric. Blood, tissue damage, and wear consistent with the injury instead appear, within 6 to 30 hours, on the skin of the next living individual to wear a garment cut from the same original bolt of fabric -- regardless of whether that individual is issued the same physical garment or a different one, so long as both derive from the same source batch. The transferred marking is not itself an open wound; it does not bleed, and subjects describe it as painless, but it is visually and dermatologically identical to the original injury, including bruising patterns and, in four cases, entry wounds matching a caliber the second wearer had no exposure to.

The marking fades over a period of roughly three weeks, at which point the garment can again transfer a new marking if its previous wearer is subsequently injured. Nine currently identified SCP-4376 garments have collectively transferred markings on thirty-one occasions since the earliest confirmed case in 2009, involving personnel across four sites who in most cases had no operational connection to one another beyond drawing from the same supply requisition.

ADDENDUM:
Personnel Records has declined to notify individual current holders of SCP-4376-derived uniforms of their garments' provenance, citing a 2018 psychological assessment concluding that awareness of the property correlates with a measurable increase in reported injuries among wearers, a correlation the assessment was unable to further explain.

SCP-4377.name: Perimeter Chalk
SCP-4377.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
14 kilograms of SCP-4377 are held at Site-64 Security Division in standard chalk-line dispensers, refilled only by Security personnel with Level 3 clearance. SCP-4377 is authorized for use marking internal perimeter boundaries within Foundation sites only, at the discretion of Site Security, and its use must be logged with exact boundary coordinates and duration. Boundaries marked with SCP-4377 are to be clearly signed on the side facing authorized personnel, though this has not been found necessary for the anomaly to remain effective. Personnel who cross an SCP-4377 line without documented authorization are to be interviewed regardless of apparent behavior, as affected individuals typically do not recognize they have forgotten anything.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4377 is a compressed chalk pigment, pale blue-white, dispensed identically to standard security marking chalk and used to mark temporary or permanent boundary lines on floors, pavement, and similar surfaces. A line drawn with SCP-4377 produces no visible or sensory effect on approach. An individual who physically crosses a completed SCP-4377 line while holding a specific, articulable reason for doing so -- as opposed to crossing incidentally, in the course of unrelated movement -- will, within roughly four seconds of crossing, lose accurate recall of that specific reason. General purpose and context are retained: a subject crossing to retrieve a dropped item will recall having crossed to retrieve something, and may still complete the action, but will be unable to state why the item mattered enough to cross for, why they were carrying it, or in several tested cases, what the item actually was, even while holding it.

The effect does not extend to memories formed prior to approaching the line, nor does it impair reasoning, planning, or subsequent memory formation; it isolates only the specific motive held at the moment of crossing. Foundation Security has used SCP-4377 operationally since 2013 to mark restricted internal boundaries specifically because personnel who cross for unauthorized reasons cannot subsequently be interrogated about those reasons, which Security leadership has assessed as an acceptable trade-off against the loss of interrogation value, given that the crossing itself is still logged and visible on camera.

ADDENDUM:
In 2021, a Site-64 researcher under active internal investigation for unauthorized removal of documents crossed an SCP-4377 boundary while carrying the documents in question. Camera footage confirms the crossing and the documents' presence; the researcher, on being stopped, provided a coherent, calmly delivered account of routine document transfer that did not match any authorized transfer order and that the researcher, on later re-interview without having recrossed the line, was unable to either confirm or contradict. The documents were recovered. Their intended destination was not. The Ethics Committee has noted, without further comment on record, that SCP-4377 may now be functioning as much to protect certain actions from explanation as to prevent them.

SCP-4378.name: The Disclosure Alloy
SCP-4378.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4378 is manufactured under contract by Foundation Materials Division exclusively for use in document-security hardware -- filing cabinet locks, secure courier case latches, and archive drawer pulls -- at facilities holding classified physical records. No raw, unformed SCP-4378 stock is to be held outside Materials Division's foundry. Hardware manufactured from SCP-4378 is not distinguished by appearance or markings from ordinary security-grade alloy and is issued through standard procurement channels; a registry cross-referencing each installed unit to the classified fact it is currently bonded to is maintained solely by the Materials Division director and is not itself stored in SCP-4378-adjacent hardware, for reasons that should be self-evident.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4378 is a copper-nickel alloy, formulated by the Foundation in 1988 for internal security applications, whose hardness, electrical resistance, and thermal expansion coefficient vary measurably and reproducibly according to the number of individuals who possess accurate, current knowledge of a single specific classified fact designated to that alloy sample at the time of its casting. A freshly cast SCP-4378 component, bonded during casting to a fact known at that time to exactly three people, will register baseline hardness and resistance values consistent with the alloy's stated specification. As additional individuals independently come to know the same fact -- whether through authorized briefing, investigation, inference, or leak -- the component's hardness decreases and its electrical resistance rises in a near-linear relationship with the growing count, becoming measurably brittle once the number of aware individuals exceeds approximately fifteen, and structurally failing (fracturing under normal handling load) at counts generally between forty and sixty, varying by the nature of the underlying fact.

SCP-4378 does not identify which individuals know the fact, only how many; the mechanism by which it counts "knowledge" rather than mere physical proximity or database access has not been determined, and it does correctly distinguish between an individual who has read a summary without retaining it and one who genuinely understands and recalls the underlying fact, a distinction the Foundation's own personnel-tracking systems cannot reliably make.

Since 1991, SCP-4378 has been deployed as a passive internal leak-detection system: lock hardware bonded to a given classified fact is checked on a rolling schedule, and unexpected changes in measured hardness trigger an automatic security review without requiring investigators to know in advance who might be responsible. This use is officially sanctioned and is the basis for SCP-4378's Thaumiel classification.

ADDENDUM:
In 2020, a batch of forty-one SCP-4378 locks bonded to unrelated, individually low-sensitivity facts fractured within the same eleven-day period across six sites. No single leak sufficient to explain the failures, individually or in aggregate, has been identified. The Materials Division's working hypothesis, not yet confirmed, is that the forty-one facts are not actually unrelated, and that some number of Foundation personnel currently know something connecting them that has not yet been reported to anyone the alloy would recognize as authorized to receive it.

SCP-4379.name: Redaction Vapor
SCP-4379.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Incinerator Unit 12-B at Site-77 Records Disposal, the sole confirmed source of SCP-4379, is fitted with a sealed extraction hood and dedicated filtration line; personnel operating the unit are required to wear self-contained breathing apparatus for the duration of any burn cycle and for fifteen minutes following, regardless of visible smoke clearance. Documents scheduled for incineration under standard disposal protocol are not screened for which specific SCP-4379 emissions they may produce, as no reliable predictive method exists; disposal logs record only that a burn occurred, not its contents, which is itself a standing point of institutional concern noted in Addendum 4379-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4379 is a colorless, faintly acrid vapor produced as an inconsistent byproduct when classified paper records are incinerated in Unit 12-B, appearing in roughly one burn cycle in twenty and in no predictable relation to the volume, age, or classification level of the material destroyed. Personnel who inhale SCP-4379, even in trace concentration, lose all specific memory of exactly one file, case, or record they have previously read or handled during the course of Foundation employment. The selection is not random with respect to the individual: subjects consistently lose the memory of the single file whose destruction, loss, or continued existence they have the strongest unacknowledged emotional relationship to, a determination made by SCP-4379 rather than by the subject's own stated priorities, which frequently do not match. Subjects do not experience this as a gap; the forgotten file's existence is removed from recall entirely, including the fact that they were ever assigned to it, and cross-referenced administrative records (assignment logs, sign-off sheets bearing the subject's own signature) are, on review, accepted by the subject as clerical records of someone else's work, or as their own work on a case they now recall differently.

Because Unit 12-B is the Foundation's primary disposal point for decommissioned or superseded SCP documentation at Site-77, and because incineration of such material is routine and continuous, SCP-4379 exposure among Records Division personnel is common and, prior to 2018, was not tracked as an anomalous effect at all; symptomatic memory loss was attributed to ordinary occupational turnover and stress.

ADDENDUM 4379-1: A 2018 retrospective study comparing personnel file-assignment records against personnel-reported recall found that 71% of Records Division staff with more than five years of tenure near Unit 12-B could not accurately recall at least one file to which departmental records confirmed their direct, extensive involvement.

ADDENDUM 4379-2: The Ethics Committee has formally objected to continued operation of Unit 12-B without a burn-content log, on the grounds that the Foundation currently has no way of determining, in aggregate, what its own personnel have collectively forgotten, or whether the same file has been forgotten by multiple people independently, which would suggest SCP-4379 is not selecting a memory at random from each individual's personal significance, but converging on specific files for reasons the Foundation cannot currently investigate without personnel capable of recalling them.

SCP-4380.name: The Compliance Solvent
SCP-4380.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
6 liters of SCP-4380 are stored at Site-45 Interrogation Support in a ventilated cabinet requiring dual Level 4 authorization to access. Use of SCP-4380 for interrogation purposes requires prior written approval from both the presiding site director and an Ethics Committee liaison, logged as a distinct interrogation method separate from standard protocol; as of 2022, no such approval has been granted following the incident described in Addendum 4380-1, though the substance has not been formally decommissioned. Any surface or object cleaned with SCP-4380 must be documented prior to cleaning, including full transcription of any legible written content present.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4380 is a clear, low-viscosity cleaning solvent, functionally effective as an ink and light-adhesive remover, chemically unremarkable except for a trace organic compound of unknown origin. When SCP-4380 is used to remove legible writing -- ink, pencil, marker, or similar -- from a surface, the individual who physically performs the removal (not merely one present in the room) experiences, within minutes of completing the task, a strong and specific compulsion to enact the content of what was written, provided that content described or instructed an action the individual is physically capable of performing. This applies regardless of whether the individual read the text before or during its removal, or was even literate in the language it was written in; illiterate and non-native-reading test subjects have successfully enacted written instructions they could not have consciously understood.

The compulsion resolves upon completion of the described action, or, if the action is impossible, prevented, or indefinitely delayed, fades gradually over approximately 40 hours. In either case, the subject retains no memory of having felt the compulsion, of the instruction's content, or, frequently, of having cleaned the surface at all, though they typically retain accurate memory of the compulsion's outcome -- the completed action -- without connecting it to a cause.

SCP-4380 was developed under a since-terminated Foundation research contract exploring compliance-inducing agents for use at Site-45's detention wing, where it was used experimentally between 2014 and 2019 to extract compelled confessions by having detainees write a confession and then clean it away themselves, producing an enacted "confirmation" in the form of a subsequent, compelled truthful statement the detainee could not recall the origin of.

ADDENDUM 4380-1: In 2019, an interrogator assigned to administer SCP-4380 protocol was instructed to have a detainee write a false confession intended only to test the solvent's action on fabricated content. The detainee wrote a true statement instead, unprompted, implicating the interrogator's supervisor in an unrelated matter, and then cleaned it away under standard procedure. The supervisor was later found to have acted exactly as compelled-enacted, three weeks after the cleaning, in a manner consistent with the written statement, despite having never read it and having no known access to the detainee. The supervisor has no memory of the written statement's content and denies any compulsion. Programmatic use of SCP-4380 has been suspended since.

SCP-4381.name: The Rehearsal Sedative
SCP-4381.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Remaining stock of SCP-4381 (4.2 liters) is held at Site-45 Medical under standard controlled-substance protocol with an additional Ethics Committee seal requiring co-signature for withdrawal. Administration of SCP-4381 to any subject, detained or Foundation personnel, requires the same dual authorization specified for SCP-4380 use under Site-45 protocol (see SCP-4380 documentation) and is currently limited to a standing research exemption for follow-up study of previously administered subjects. No new administrations have been authorized since 2020.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4381 is a clear injectable sedative, chemically similar to standard pre-operative anesthetics with an additional unidentified compound making up less than 0.5% of solution by volume. A subject administered a standard dose of SCP-4381 loses consciousness within the expected timeframe for a sedative of its apparent class (60-90 seconds) and remains sedated for a duration consistent with dosage, showing no unusual vital signs throughout. Upon waking, subjects uniformly report having subjectively experienced their own death during the sedated interval -- not a dream or hallucination of dying, which subjects are generally able to distinguish and describe as such, but an experience they describe with high internal consistency across unrelated subjects as feeling complete, ordinary, and final, frequently including physical sensations (cessation of breath, cooling) that did not occur in the subject's actual, monitored physiological state.

Subjects do not retain narrative memory of the experience beyond the fact that it occurred and that it felt real; questioning subjects further on content produces only the repeated statement, phrased near-identically across subjects with no contact with one another, that "there wasn't anything after, and that was the whole point of it." Subjects administered SCP-4381 show no psychological harm directly attributable to the experience on standard assessment, but longitudinal follow-up (currently 34 subjects tracked over periods up to seven years) shows a statistically significant reduction in self-reported fear response to genuine mortal danger in field or custodial settings, alongside an equally significant increase in self-reported difficulty distinguishing, in retrospect, which of their memories of "dying" belong to the SCP-4381 experience versus an unrelated near-death event, in the nine subjects who have since had one.

SCP-4381 was developed at Site-45 for use as a non-lethal interrogation deterrent -- administered to detainees under the (accurate) representation that it was a sedative, its actual effect was not disclosed to subjects, and its use in this capacity was justified internally on the grounds that no physical harm results.

ADDENDUM:
The 2020 suspension followed a request from a former detainee, released without charge, for continued Foundation medical monitoring on the stated grounds that they "need to know when the real one happens, because I already know what it's supposed to feel like and I don't trust it anymore." The request was granted under a standing research exemption. The subject remains under quarterly review.

SCP-4382.name: Retroactive Filing Dust
SCP-4382.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known stock of SCP-4382 (2.1 kilograms) is sealed in a single container at Site-77 Records Division high-security vault, accessible only by direct written order from the Records Division director or an O5 Council member. No further quantity of SCP-4382 has been synthesized since its properties were understood, and current research is limited to non-destructive analysis of the existing stock. Any document suspected of SCP-4382 exposure -- indicated by discrepancies between a document's claimed filing date and its physical or digital paper trail -- is to be forwarded to Records Division for the retroactive-consistency audit described in Addendum 4382-1, not destroyed, per standing Ethics Committee order.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4382 is a fine, near-colorless dust, chemically consistent with common paper-conservation talc apart from an unidentified mineral trace. When applied to a physical document -- Foundation-format incident reports, memoranda, and similar records have all tested positive -- the document does not change in visible content, but becomes, within an average of nine days, fully integrated into the Foundation's institutional record as though it had existed and been properly filed since the date written or implied on the document itself, regardless of whether it in fact did. This integration is not limited to the document's own filing record: cross-referenced entries (personnel logs noting its receipt, prior citations of it in other documents, physical wear consistent with the claimed handling history) generate or update themselves accordingly, without any identified mechanism by which SCP-4382 could act on records physically or digitally separate from the treated document itself.

SCP-4382 does not appear to require the treated document's content to be truthful, only for it to be plausible within the format and context it claims. A test document -- a wholly fabricated 1970s incident report for a site that did not exist at the time -- was successfully integrated in 2016, producing three cross-referencing entries in unrelated existing files that had to be manually identified and flagged before removal, a process complicated by the fact that removing them left the citing documents internally inconsistent in ways that were themselves difficult to distinguish from ordinary clerical error accumulated over decades.

SCP-4382 was recovered in 2003 from an unrelated administrative dispute in which two departments produced contradictory but individually well-supported paper trails for the same incident; investigation found a shared source: a since-retired records clerk who could not explain possession of the substance and who, per contemporaneous interview transcripts, appeared to genuinely believe both versions of the incident had occurred.

ADDENDUM 4382-1: The retroactive-consistency audit, established in 2017, has to date reviewed 340 flagged documents. Sixty-one showed integration patterns consistent with SCP-4382 exposure. Of these, Records Division has been able to determine an original, untreated version of the record for eleven. The remainder are currently treated, per standing policy, as accurate.

SCP-4383.name: The Tempering Rain
SCP-4383.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The collection point for SCP-4383 -- a section of roof guttering on the original 1971 wing of Site-19 -- is fitted with a diversion channel routing all runoff to a sealed 900-liter cistern rather than the standard site water reclamation system. Access to cistern contents requires Level 3 authorization and is currently restricted to the ongoing longitudinal study described below. Personnel are prohibited from collecting or consuming rainwater from this section of roof by any unauthorized means; the guttering is visually unremarkable and has required physical signage since 1998 to prevent incidental collection by maintenance staff.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4383 is rainwater collected specifically from drainage across a roughly 40-square-meter section of Site-19's original architecture; water from any other section of the same roof, or reproduced in laboratory conditions using matched local rainfall and matched roofing material, does not exhibit the effect. Regular consumption of SCP-4383 (documented minimum: roughly 200mL, three times weekly, sustained over at least six months) produces a gradual, measurable reduction in the subject's physiological and behavioral fear response to genuinely dangerous stimuli -- elevated heart rate, startle reflex, and self-reported dread all decrease under controlled exposure to validated fear-inducing conditions, without a corresponding decrease in the subject's accurate risk assessment or judgment; subjects remain able to correctly identify danger, they simply do not feel afraid of it to the same degree.

The effect is not confined to the consuming individual. Biological offspring of long-term SCP-4383 consumers, even where the offspring has never personally consumed SCP-4383, show a statistically significant portion of the same fear-response reduction, diminishing but still measurable through at least two subsequent generations in tracked family lines, with no identified mechanism of transmission; the effect does not correlate with any tested genetic marker and has been observed in adopted children of consumers raised without knowledge of the consumer's habits, ruling out purely behavioral or environmental explanation in at least four documented cases.

SCP-4383 has been informally consumed by Site-19 personnel with roof access since at least the 1970s, predating its formal identification in 2005 following an unrelated study of fear-response outliers among long-tenured maintenance staff.

ADDENDUM:
The Ethics Committee has raised sustained objection to the absence of any recall or public-health notice regarding second- and third-generation effects in family members who were never Foundation personnel and never consented to any study. Site Administration's current position, unchanged since 2011, is that reduced fear response in descendants has not been shown to constitute harm, and that formally notifying affected families would require disclosing the existence of SCP-4383 and, by extension, the site itself.

SCP-4384.name: The Dampening Foam
SCP-4384.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4384 is installed as standard wall and ceiling insulation in seven designated high-stress interview and debriefing rooms across four sites, under a program administered jointly by Site Security and the Department of Psychological Services. Installation, removal, or modification of SCP-4384 in any room requires joint sign-off from both departments. Rooms containing SCP-4384 are marked on internal floor plans with a designation ("Type-D Room") that does not indicate the material's anomalous nature to staff without a documented need to know. No SCP-4384 stock is to be installed outside currently approved rooms pending the review requested in Addendum 4384-2.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4384 is a synthetic acoustic insulation batting, manufactured to standard specification by a contracted supplier and indistinguishable by material analysis from ordinary sound-dampening foam used throughout Foundation facilities. When installed within the walls or ceiling of an enclosed room in sufficient quantity (a minimum coverage threshold of approximately 70% of interior surface area has been established through testing), the room exhibits a secondary property beyond its intended acoustic dampening: personnel who experience a high-intensity emotional event within the room -- documented cases include interrogation, termination notification, and critical debriefing -- retain accurate factual memory of the event afterward but experience a measurable, persistent dampening of the event's associated emotional intensity on recall, compared against control subjects experiencing equivalent events in untreated rooms. Subjects can accurately describe what occurred, including their own reported feelings at the time, but do not re-experience or display the physiological markers of that emotional state when recalling it, even under conditions (guided recall, confrontation with contradicting parties) that reliably trigger such markers in control subjects.

The effect does not extend to events occurring outside the room, does not fade with subsequent exposure or time, and has no identified mechanism connecting the batting's acoustic dampening properties to its effect on recalled affect; material analysis has found no anomalous chemical or structural property distinguishing SCP-4384 from ordinary batting produced by the same supplier in the same period, and attempts to reproduce the effect using verified-ordinary insulation of identical specification have failed in all fourteen controlled trials.

SCP-4384 was identified in 2015 following an unusually low rate of reported psychological injury claims among interrogation personnel assigned to one specific room at Site-64, traced to a 2011 renovation using stock from a supplier batch later found to correspond with the seven currently installed rooms.

ADDENDUM 4384-1: The Department of Psychological Services formally endorsed continued and expanded use of SCP-4384 in 2016, citing measurable reduction in occupational PTSD indicators among personnel regularly conducting high-intensity interviews in treated rooms.

ADDENDUM 4384-2: A 2023 internal review noted that personnel assigned long-term to SCP-4384-treated rooms show no corresponding reduction in reported empathy or behavioral warmth outside those rooms, but do show a measurable increase in describing distressing events involving others -- including subjects' injuries and deaths occurring in treated rooms -- in flatter, more procedural language than personnel without such assignments, a pattern the review characterized as "worth continued observation" without further recommendation.

SCP-4385.name: The Third Season
SCP-4385.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All episodes, promotional materials, and hosting infrastructure associated with the podcast "██████ Cold" are to be monitored by Foundation-owned shell accounts subscribed to its distribution feed. Foundation Web Crawler Unit 12 scans all major podcast platforms weekly for any listing of a "Season 3" under this title or its aliases; any such listing is to be flagged, archived, and the associated account suspended through cooperating platform partners within four hours.

Individuals who report having listened to a nonexistent third season are to be located and interviewed under the pretext of an audience research survey. Interviewees exhibiting the described belief-implantation symptoms are to be administered a Class A amnesticization only after a full transcript of their claimed episode content has been recorded for archival comparison, as recurring structural details across interviews have proven useful in tracking the anomaly's underlying logic.

No Foundation researcher is to listen to any purported Season 3 audio file recovered from a subject's device. Recovered files are to be transferred to Data Containment for storage without playback, pending approval from at least two Level 4 personnel and a documented containment justification.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4385 refers to a recurring phenomenon associated with "██████ Cold," a two-season, independently produced true-crime podcast concerning the unsolved 2009 disappearance of a resident of ██████, Ohio. Beginning in early 2018, listeners across unconnected platforms began independently reporting having heard a twelve-episode third season of the podcast, despite the show's creators confirming no such season was ever recorded, scripted, or released.

Interviews with affected individuals reveal a striking consistency: episode numbers, guest names, and even specific sound design choices are described identically by listeners with no contact with one another. No audio file matching these descriptions has ever been recovered from any server, cache, or hosting provider under Foundation observation. Forensic analysis of affected devices indicates the audio was generated locally, on-device, without any corresponding network request, using processing resources consistent with standard media playback rather than synthesis — the mechanism of generation remains unidentified.

The content of the fabricated season consistently concerns the same real, unsolved disappearance covered in the podcast's first season. Affected listeners describe the season as "solving" the case, providing named suspects, locations, and forensic details not present in any public record. Critically, this information is false in every instance verified by Foundation investigators — yet listeners report near-total confidence in its accuracy, sufficient to prompt at least eleven documented cases of individuals contacting the ██████ Police Department, publishing the fabricated leads online, or, in one case, confronting a named individual directly.

The fabricated leads are neither random nor arbitrary. Comparative analysis suggests SCP-4385 constructs its narrative content from the listener's own private anxieties and unresolved suspicions regarding people known to them, repackaged as details of the unrelated cold case. No listener has yet recognized this substitution independently.

ADDENDUM 4385-1: Following the confrontation incident (Interviewee ████-9), the named individual — who had no verifiable connection to the original disappearance — required relocation and memory alteration after sustained harassment. The Foundation has since classified unsolicited "solved case" claims sourced from podcast audiences as a standing investigative trigger under Protocol Silent-Archive-██.

SCP-4386.name: The Case Study
SCP-4386.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation front organization Halveth Behavioral Research maintains editorial monitoring positions at eleven peer-reviewed psychology and psychiatry journals of moderate circulation. Any submitted manuscript matching the structural pattern of SCP-4386 — a single-patient case study using the designation "Patient ██" or a close variant, presenting biographical details in a manner Foundation linguistic analysis flags as excessively generalized while remaining internally specific — is to be intercepted prior to peer review and forwarded unopened to Site-77 Textual Anomalies Division.

Journal issues already in circulation that are confirmed to contain an instance of SCP-4386 are to be recalled under standard product-defect pretexts (misprint, citation error) where the publisher can be co-opted, or purchased in bulk through intermediary buyers where it cannot. Digital versions require coordinated takedown requests citing fabricated copyright violations.

Personnel with graduate-level psychology training are barred from reading recovered instances of SCP-4386 due to elevated susceptibility, per Incident 4386-3. Analysis is to be conducted only by personnel without formal clinical psychology background, under two-week rotation to limit cumulative exposure.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4386 designates a recurring case-study article appearing, without prior submission record, within the peer-reviewed literature of clinical and abnormal psychology. Each instance is formatted identically to legitimate scholarship: an abstract, a literature review, a methodology section, and a detailed case history of a single anonymized patient, followed by discussion of diagnostic implications. No author, institution, or IRB approval number associated with any instance has been verified to exist.

The anomalous property of SCP-4386 lies in its biographical section. The patient's described childhood, family structure, formative incidents, and stated occupation are phrased with sufficient generality to plausibly describe a wide readership, while containing three to five specific, unusual details (a scar's exact location, a childhood pet's uncommon name, the precise wording of a remembered argument) that, per subject testimony, match the reader's own undisclosed history exactly. No two readers of the same physical printing have reported identical specific details; the article appears to reformat this section per reader, though the mechanism and trigger for this substitution have not been isolated, and copies read by multiple people show only the most recently read version upon later inspection.

Readers who complete the case history section — full readers of the discussion section are not required for onset — begin exhibiting the diagnostic symptoms attributed to "Patient ██" within three to ten days, typically an escalating and specific behavioral or perceptual disturbance not present prior to reading. Symptom severity has ranged from mild (a persistent, false certainty of having misplaced an object that is later found undisturbed) to severe (Subject 4386-11 developed a delusion, matching the article's described case exactly, that a specific deceased family member remained alive and estranged, resisting correction for four months under standard care).

The Foundation has not determined whether SCP-4386 selects its readers, its biographical content, or both, nor whether instances are causally connected or independently arising. No instance has been observed to affect the same individual twice.

ADDENDUM 4386-1: Incident 4386-3 involved a contracted clinical consultant who, in the course of analysis, recognized diagnostic language from her own unpublished doctoral thesis embedded in an instance's discussion section, verbatim in three places. She has since been reassigned and is under long-term monitoring.

SCP-4387.name: Open File
SCP-4387.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known copies of the podcast episode "Episode 14: The Girl on Route 9" (produced by [DATA EXPUNGED] Media under the series "Cold Case Confidential") are to be stored on air-gapped media at Site-77. The Foundation maintains automated scraping of podcast platforms, torrent trackers, and file-sharing forums for the episode's audio fingerprint; any detected upload is to be flagged to Web Crawler unit Chi-9 for a takedown request under copyright pretext within four hours of indexing.
