Members of the public who report having "remembered" involvement in the disappearance of Ellen Marsh (the subject of Episode 14) to law enforcement, the original podcast's tip line, or online forums are to be identified via the Foundation's media-monitoring contract with [REDACTED] and administered a standard Class A amnestic by an embedded agent posing as a grief counselor or victim advocate, provided the report has not already been entered into a permanent record (police report, court filing, television broadcast). If the report has entered a permanent record, escalate to the Cold Case Task Force for a memetic scrub of associated documents and administer Class B amnestics to all personnel who handled the record.

Foundation-operated podcast analytics indicate the episode is currently held by an estimated 40,000-65,000 listeners across at least eleven platforms. Full recall is not considered feasible. Priority is suppression of aggregate listener contact with law enforcement.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4387 is a 58-minute audio episode of the podcast Cold Case Confidential, first uploaded to podcast platforms in March 2018, concerning the unsolved 1991 disappearance of 19-year-old Ellen Marsh from Route 9 outside Lassen, ██████. The episode is journalistically unremarkable: an amateur host narrates timeline, interviews two retired detectives, and closes without resolution, in a format typical of the genre.

Approximately six weeks after a listener has consumed the full episode without interruption, that listener will begin to report, first as an intrusive thought and later as a settled memory, having personally witnessed some portion of the events described. The recalled detail is never a full account. Instead it is a single, forensically plausible fragment: a car color not mentioned in the episode, a partial license plate, a fragment of overheard conversation, a physical description of a third party never named. No two listeners recall the same fragment.

When these fragments are collected in aggregate, as they have been, three times, by amateur "web sleuth" communities cross-referencing tip line submissions, they compose an increasingly coherent secondary account of the disappearance, one that names a suspect, provides a plausible motive, and describes a location for Marsh's remains. This secondary account has never once matched the real, Foundation-verified circumstances of the case, which remain unknown. Marsh's actual fate is not established as anomalous; the fabricated composite account is the anomaly.

Each of the three community-driven convergences has independently arrived at a different suspect, motive, and burial location, all internally consistent and none corroborated by physical evidence when investigated by Foundation-embedded liaisons. The mechanism producing the fragments is unknown. The episode's audio, at the waveform level, contains no anomalous data on any analysis performed by Site-77's Audiological Division; the effect appears to require the listener's completed act of listening, not any property extractable from the file alone.

ADDENDUM 4387-1: On four occasions, individuals administered amnestics for SCP-4387-related recall have, within eighteen months, independently relistened to the episode, with no memory of prior exposure or Foundation contact, and begun generating new fragments inconsistent with their prior ones. The Foundation has not determined why these individuals are disproportionately likely to re-encounter the file.

SCP-4388.name: Anomalous Frame
SCP-4388.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The image file constituting SCP-4388 (designated GOES-14_2011-273-1847.tif in its original archival metadata) is stored on a single non-networked workstation in Archive Wing 4 of Site-77, inside a lightless enclosure. The workstation's monitor is fitted with a physical shutter that must be manually opened by two authorized personnel before the file may be viewed. Viewing sessions are limited to one researcher at a time, twenty minutes maximum, with a mandatory forty-eight-hour interval between sessions for that researcher.

Personnel exhibiting SCP-4388-related effects (see Description) during or after an authorized viewing are to remain under Site-77 observation until the effect concludes naturally; sedation has been found to extend rather than shorten effect duration and is no longer authorized. All other copies of the file, including those retrieved from the National Oceanic archive from which it was originally sourced, have been located and destroyed; the archive's public database now redirects requests for the file to a substituted, non-anomalous frame from an adjacent timestamp.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4388 is a single infrared satellite image, apparently captured by the GOES-14 weather satellite on the date encoded in its metadata, depicting a stationary, closed-eye cyclonic cloud formation over open ocean at coordinates that correspond to no charted storm system in that satellite's mission records, nor in the records of any other satellite that photographed the same region at the same time.

A person who views SCP-4388 for longer than approximately four seconds will, for a duration equal to the length of their viewing session, perceive the same cyclonic formation superimposed on the actual sky above their present location, regardless of true weather conditions, cloud cover, or whether they are indoors. The formation is visually convincing: subjects report correct parallax as they move their head, and the illusion persists through eye closure and reopening. It does not appear in photographs taken by the subject during the episode, nor is it visible to bystanders unless those bystanders have also viewed SCP-4388 within the preceding six hours, in which case they perceive the same formation, from their own relative position, simultaneously with the original viewer.

The illusory formation produces no physical effects, no wind, no precipitation, no temperature change, and dissipates abruptly at the end of the viewing-length window rather than fading. Subjects uniformly describe the experience as one of dread disproportionate to what they are seeing, which several researchers have compared to the anticipatory unease preceding a real storm rather than fear of the image itself.

ADDENDUM 4388-1: Analysis of the image's compression artifacts confirms it was generated by GOES-14's actual imaging hardware and transmitted through the actual satellite downlink used at the time; it is not a fabrication inserted after the fact. No formation matching SCP-4388 has been observed by any weather satellite before or since. The Meteorological Analysis Task Force has not proposed a mechanism by which the satellite could have imaged a storm that existed nowhere in the atmosphere it was pointed at.

SCP-4389.name: Sampler Pattern 12
SCP-4389.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The master pattern sheet and all forty-one known printed copies of "Cross-Stitch Sampler Pattern No. 12: Home Sweet Home," originally distributed by ██████ Needlecraft Co. in a 1987 mail-order catalog, are held in Site-77's Textile Anomalies vault. Personnel are prohibited from stitching any portion of SCP-4389 beyond the testing allowances granted under Experiment Log 4389.

Any completed SCP-4389 sampler recovered in the field (see Description) is to be photographed, bagged in an opaque, light-blocking sleeve, and transported to Site-77 without being unwrapped by transporting personnel. Recovery teams are instructed not to ask the owning household whether they wish to keep the piece; consent is not solicited, as prior attempts to do so have resulted in the household's proxy insistence that Foundation personnel are "already family" and need not take anything.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4389 is a printed embroidery pattern for a decorative sampler, sold as an ordinary hobbyist product through legitimate retail channels between 1987 and 1991, when the supplying company ceased operations for reasons unrelated to any known anomaly. The pattern, when followed without deviation using the thread colors and stitch counts specified, produces a rectangular sampler reading HOME SWEET HOME above a stitched illustration of a house, framed by stitched flowers and a border.

A stitcher who deviates from the pattern's instructions, using a substitute thread color, an incorrect stitch, or stopping before completion, experiences an escalating compulsion to correct the deviation, described by test subjects as resembling an unresolved itch located "behind the sternum," which does not abate until the piece matches the pattern exactly. Subjects have continued stitching through pain, fatigue, and in three documented cases, past the point of medical advisability, without expressing distress about doing so.

A sampler completed to specification and displayed in a household (hung on a wall, typically, though placement does not appear to be a requirement) produces a gradual attachment effect in residents of that household, who report increasing reluctance to remove, sell, or relocate the piece, framed in each case as ordinary sentimentality rather than compulsion, even when directly informed of the object's anomalous status. Residents of households harboring a completed SCP-4389 for longer than approximately eight months have, in eleven documented cases, described brief periods, minutes to an hour, during which they "became," in their own words, an idealized version of a family member, behaving with uncharacteristic warmth or domesticity before returning to baseline with no memory of the interval.

The pattern does not specify a source designer; the ██████ Needlecraft catalog credits it to a contributor identified only by the initials "M.H.," who cannot be traced in company records or any external database.

ADDENDUM 4389-1: No completed SCP-4389 sampler has ever been found damaged, faded, or disposed of by its household of origin. All forty-one recovered instances were retrieved only after every resident of the household in question had died of unrelated causes.

SCP-4390.name: Day One
SCP-4390.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation front company Halbrook Logistics Solutions maintains cover ownership of the original production masters of SCP-4390 under the pretext of corporate archival services. All identified affected personnel (current or former employees of companies confirmed to have screened SCP-4390 or a related instance) are to be enrolled in the Foundation's long-term Occupational Memory Monitoring Program without their knowledge, disguised as a standard benefits/HR data service contracted to their employer.

Given confirmed evidence that SCP-4390 is one of at least nineteen structurally identical training videos produced under different company names by production entities that cannot be traced to a common owner (see Addendum 4390-2), full recovery is not considered achievable. Current containment priority is identification of the producing organization, designated GoI-4390-ARCHIVE ("The Onboarders") pending further data, and interception of newly commissioned instances before distribution.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4390 is an 11-minute human-resources orientation video, titled "Welcome to the Halbrook Family: Your First Day," produced for internal use at Halbrook Distribution Partners, a mid-size logistics firm headquartered in ██████, Ohio, prior to Foundation acquisition of the company as a monitoring front. The video follows the standard structure of a corporate onboarding presentation: a narrated company history, a benefits overview, and testimonials from employees identified only by first name and department.

Employees who view SCP-4390 as part of a genuine onboarding process begin, within one to three months, to report autobiographical memories consistent with a substantially longer tenure at the company than their actual hire date, memories of company events, coworkers, and internal milestones that predate their employment, in several cases predating the company's actual founding. These false memories do not overwrite or conflict with the employee's genuine personal history; they are additive, coexisting without apparent cognitive dissonance, and employees do not identify them as false unless directly confronted with employment records.

The effect is cumulative and non-exclusive: employees who separately view other SCP-4390-pattern videos (see Addendum) after leaving Halbrook's employ acquire additional false tenure at the corresponding companies, with no evident ceiling. One subject, a former Halbrook warehouse associate later employed by an unrelated firm that screened a structurally identical video (SCP-4390-2, at Meridian Fulfillment Group), reported clear, detailed memories of an employment history at both companies totaling fourteen years, against an actual combined employment period of nineteen months.

ADDENDUM 4390-1: The Foundation initially classified SCP-4390 as an isolated corporate curiosity. Reclassification to Keter followed the discovery of eighteen additional structurally identical videos (same shot composition, same narrator cadence, differing only in company branding and testimonial names) at logistics, warehousing, and call-center companies across four countries, none of which share a production vendor, ad agency, or corporate parent traceable through conventional investigation.

ADDENDUM 4390-2: The purpose of the false-tenure effect remains undetermined. No financial, legal, or operational benefit to the affected companies has been identified. The Foundation's working hypothesis, that GoI-4390-ARCHIVE is constructing fabricated, distributed employment histories for an unknown population, for an unknown purpose, is presently unconfirmed.

SCP-4391.name: Line Eleven
SCP-4391.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4391 is stored disassembled in Site-77's Optical Instruments locker, its eleven printed lines separated into individually sealed envelopes to prevent inadvertent reassembly and viewing. Reassembly for testing requires authorization from the Site Director and the presence of a staff ophthalmologist.

Personnel who have read SCP-4391's eleventh line aloud during an authorized test are to be flagged in personnel records for mandatory annual vision screening and are not to be assigned to field duties requiring corrected visual acuity below the threshold established at their most recent screening, regardless of self-reported vision quality. Subjects are not to be informed of the content of their own eleventh-line reading unless the subject is Foundation personnel with Level 3 clearance or higher who explicitly requests disclosure in writing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4391 is a Snellen-pattern visual acuity chart, functionally identical in printing and construction to charts manufactured for legitimate ophthalmic use, recovered from an optometry practice in ██████, following the practice's closure after its sole practitioner's disappearance. The chart's first ten lines are unremarkable, presenting the standard descending sequence of letters used to test acuity from 20/200 to 20/20.

An eleventh line, not present on any commercially manufactured Snellen chart, appears below the tenth only to a subject whose corrected or uncorrected visual acuity is sufficient to resolve it, typically requiring acuity better than 20/15. The eleventh line does not consist of the standard optotype letters (C, D, E, F, L, O, P, T, Z) but of smaller Latin letters forming a grammatically complete sentence in the subject's native language, regardless of what language the subject was tested in previously. When read aloud, as is standard acuity-test procedure, the sentence invariably states a specific calendar date, phrased as a statement of fact concerning the subject's own eyesight, for example, "your vision will fail completely by the fourteenth of November."

No subject has, to date, retained clear memory of having read the sentence; subjects recall completing a normal eye exam and report the reading of line eleven as a brief gap, comparable to a lapse in attention. The stated date is recoverable only from audio or video recordings of the test session. Of the eight instances in which a stated date has since elapsed, seven subjects experienced a genuine, medically unremarkable and irreversible loss of visual acuity consistent with the stated prediction, occurring within 72 hours of the date given, with no identified causal mechanism connecting the reading to the outcome. The eighth subject is Foundation personnel currently under long-term observation; the stated date for that subject has not yet elapsed.

ADDENDUM 4391-1: No two subjects presented with SCP-4391 have received the same eleventh line, either in content or in stated date. The chart's mechanism for generating a line specific to each reader, given that the physical printing does not change between tests, remains unexplained by Site-77's Optical Instruments Division.

SCP-4392.name: Recalculating
SCP-4392.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The navigation voice pack constituting SCP-4392 (internally designated "Voice: Clara, US English" by its distributing application, a consumer GPS navigation app with approximately 40 million active installations) cannot be removed from public distribution without alerting the parent company to Foundation involvement; current containment is limited to passive monitoring.

The Foundation maintains a standing data-sharing arrangement with the app's developer, disguised as a traffic-analytics research partnership, permitting Foundation analysts to flag anomalous routing instructions in near-real time. Drivers who report having followed a route toward a nonexistent destination are to be contacted within twelve hours by an embedded agent posing as roadside assistance or app-support staff and administered a Class A amnestic if the resulting incident has not generated a police report, insurance claim, or news coverage; escalate to Field Agent Team Delta-9 for document suppression if it has.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4392 refers to anomalous instructions periodically issued by the "Clara" voice option within a widely used consumer navigation application. Under normal operation, the voice functions identically to the application's other voice options, providing standard turn-by-turn directions generated by the application's routing algorithm.

Approximately once per 400,000 active navigation sessions (Foundation estimate, based on incident sampling), the Clara voice will, without deviation from its normal vocal cadence or the application's standard phrasing conventions, direct the driver toward a road, exit, or address that does not exist at the time of the instruction. In 61% of sampled incidents in which the driver disregarded the instruction, no anomaly was subsequently observed. In the remaining 39%, the indicated road, exit, or structure was independently confirmed to be constructed, opened, or officially addressed within a period ranging from eleven days to four years after the instruction was given, at the precise location the voice had indicated.

Drivers who follow an SCP-4392 instruction before the indicated location exists report no subjective sense that anything is wrong; several describe an unusual, retrospectively-recognized confidence in the app's accuracy despite visible evidence to the contrary, such as driving across an open field or into standing water while believing themselves to be on a paved road. Nine such incidents have resulted in vehicular accidents; three have resulted in fatalities. Foundation analysis has identified a behavioral pattern in which drivers who have previously received an accurate SCP-4392 instruction (one preceding a road that was later built) exhibit markedly increased compliance with subsequent instructions from the same voice, including instructions given under normal, non-anomalous circumstances that would ordinarily prompt driver skepticism, such as directions through evident dead ends.

ADDENDUM 4392-1: The application's routing algorithm, per cooperating engineers at the developer, does not have access to any construction-planning, zoning, or municipal-permit database that could account for SCP-4392's accuracy regarding future roads. The mechanism by which the Clara voice generates these instructions remains unidentified.

SCP-4393.name: The Quiet House
SCP-4393.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All 3,400 printed copies of the children's picture book The Quiet House (author credited as "R. Aldous," ISBN [DATA EXPUNGED], first printing 1996) that have been recovered are held in Site-77's Print Media vault. Foundation front company Aldous Family Press retains ostensible publishing rights and has not authorized a reprint since acquisition. An estimated 900-1,200 copies remain unrecovered in private ownership, library systems, and secondhand markets.

Households in possession of an unrecovered copy are to be identified through library circulation records and secondhand retailer purchase data where legally accessible, and visited under the pretext of a public library book-recall or product-safety-recall program. Households that report a child in the residence has "seen someone" in the house matching descriptions consistent with SCP-4393-1 (see below) are escalated immediately to the Child Anomalous Exposure Unit.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4393 is a 32-page children's picture book depicting, in text and illustration, a single evening in an unremarkable two-story house, narrated from the perspective of a child preparing for bed. The book's illustrations, examined against the original printing plates, are identical across all recovered copies at time of manufacture.

When SCP-4393 is read aloud to a child by a consistent caregiver on at least five occasions within a single household, the illustrations' background details, wallpaper pattern, furniture placement, framed photographs on illustrated walls, begin to diverge between copies, gradually coming to match corresponding details of the household in which the book is being read, despite no physical alteration being detectable in the paper or ink through any analysis performed by Site-77. The convergence is not immediate and is not reported by the reading adult, who does not perceive the change; it is consistently first noticed by the child being read to.

After the convergence is complete (typically 15-40 readings), a human figure, rendered in the same illustrative style as the book's other artwork, begins to appear in the illustrated house's windows and doorways across successive readings, positioned differently each time, generally closer to the illustrated child's bedroom door with each appearance. This figure, designated SCP-4393-1, is never described consistently by different children exposed to it, but individual children describe it consistently across sessions. In fourteen of nineteen documented cases, the child independently reported, to a parent, unprompted and outside the context of the book, having seen "the person from the book" standing in the actual house, most often in a doorway or hallway, at night.

No injury, disappearance, or physical evidence of intrusion has been associated with any SCP-4393-1 sighting. The book, when reading stops, does not revert; the converged illustrations remain converged, and SCP-4393-1 has in four cases continued to be reported by the child for periods exceeding one year after the book was removed from the home.

ADDENDUM 4393-1: The identity and motive of "R. Aldous" remain unestablished. The publisher of record dissolved in 1997; no additional works under this byline have been located.

SCP-4394.name: Exhibit A-19
SCP-4394.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The physical stenographic transcript constituting SCP-4394, originally entered as Exhibit A-19 in the sealed 1974 civil proceeding Marrow v. Combined Fidelity Trust, is held in a sealed records safe in Site-77's Legal Anomalies archive. Access requires Level 4 clearance and sign-off from both the Site Legal Liaison and a Foundation ethicist, logged separately.

Foundation legal-monitoring assets embedded within [REDACTED] regional court systems are tasked with identifying any court filing that quotes, paraphrases, or attaches a document matching SCP-4394's linguistic fingerprint (see Description), and flagging the presiding case for review by the Foundation's Judicial Outcomes task force. Where an SCP-4394-influenced filing has already produced a verdict, the Foundation does not currently intervene to overturn the verdict, per Ethics Committee ruling EC-4394-1, but monitors affected parties for long-term psychological effects.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4394 is a 340-page bound stenographic transcript, physically consistent with legitimate court reporting equipment and conventions of the period, purporting to document testimony given in a sealed 1974 civil trial. The transcript's cover page, case caption, and court seal are consistent with genuine county court records of the period; no corresponding case file exists in the county's physical or digital archives, sealed or otherwise.

The transcript's anomalous property is not contained in any fixed text. Multiple readers given SCP-4394 to review independently, under controlled conditions, produce entirely consistent summaries of the transcript's factual content, dates, names, and sequence of events do not vary between readers, but reach categorically opposed conclusions regarding the guilt or liability of the transcript's central figure, an unnamed defendant referred to throughout only as "the respondent." Each reader reports total confidence that their conclusion is the only one a reasonable interpretation of the text supports, and each reader, when shown a transcript excerpt annotated by a reader who reached the opposite conclusion, initially insists the annotation must be describing a different document.

Foundation testing (Experiment Log 4394-7) confirmed that excerpts of SCP-4394's text, when introduced into unrelated, non-anomalous legal proceedings as supporting argument (via Foundation-affiliated legal counsel under sanctioned test conditions, using civil small-claims matters selected for minimal real-world consequence), produced juror or arbitrator agreement with the introducing party's position at a rate of 100% across eleven trials, regardless of which side introduced the excerpt or the excerpt's ostensible relevance to the matter at hand. This testing was suspended following EC-4394-1 over concerns regarding due process and has not resumed.

ADDENDUM 4394-1: The Foundation has confirmed that at least one unaffiliated law firm, Grieve & Talbot LLP, has possessed and used excerpts of SCP-4394 or a functionally identical document in real litigation on at least four occasions between 1989 and 2009, achieving favorable outcomes in all four. The firm's source for the document has not been identified. Grieve & Talbot LLP dissolved in 2011; its surviving partners have not been located.

SCP-4395.name: The Lighthouse Keeper's Hour
SCP-4395.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4395 is broadcast on AM frequency ███ kHz at irregular intervals averaging one episode every eleven days, from a transmission source that Foundation radio-direction-finding teams have narrowed to a 40-kilometer radius in [REDACTED] but have not located precisely. A rotating team of three Foundation-monitored amateur radio operators, embedded within legitimate DXing communities in the affected region, maintains continuous logging of the frequency.

Upon detection of a new SCP-4395 broadcast, the responsible monitoring team transcribes the episode's plot content in full and forwards it to the Narrative Forecasting Unit, which cross-references named or implied locations against the broadcast's estimated reception radius (approximately 200 kilometers under standard nighttime AM propagation) to identify the likely-affected town. Foundation field teams are pre-positioned in the three towns historically most affected by SCP-4395 (████, ████, and Corbin Falls) to intervene in events matching the broadcast's plot beats where those events pose injury risk.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4395 is a serialized radio drama broadcast in the style and production quality of 1940s American radio theater, despite use of a transmission frequency and modulation standard not introduced until decades after that era's conclusion. Episodes run 22-30 minutes, feature a consistent cast of voice actors (unidentified, and consistent in vocal characteristics across all 61 logged episodes since discovery in 2003), and follow the fictional town of Corbin Falls through an ongoing narrative centered on its lighthouse keeper, Elias Whit.

Within seven days of a given episode's broadcast, some town within the broadcast's reception radius reliably experiences a real event matching that episode's central plot beat in structure, though never in named specifics, a fictional dispute between two characters over a boundary fence precedes a real, unrelated property dispute between actual neighbors; a fictional town meeting addressing a water shortage precedes a real municipal water advisory. The correspondence is structural rather than literal: names, exact circumstances, and outcomes differ between the broadcast and the real event, but the shape of the event, its participants' roles, its resolution, its emotional register, consistently matches.

The town affected by a given episode is not fixed; Corbin Falls, the broadcast's fictional setting, has no confirmed real-world counterpart, and the real towns affected vary by broadcast, correlating only with the physical reception radius calculated for that night's atmospheric conditions. No town has been affected by more than four episodes to date. Residents of affected towns show no awareness of the correspondence and, when interviewed by Foundation liaisons under pretext, do not recognize the broadcast's plot elements as familiar.

ADDENDUM 4395-1: Licensing and engineering records for the frequency used by SCP-4395 do not exist in any national telecommunications registry, past or present. The Foundation has not determined whether the broadcast causes the events it precedes, predicts them, or whether both broadcast and event are produced by a shared, unidentified upstream cause.

SCP-4396.name: Pick Up
SCP-4396.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The audio file constituting SCP-4396 (a 4-second MP3, file hash on record with the Digital Anomalies Division) is blocklisted at the hash level across cooperating cloud storage and messaging platforms under the Foundation's standing content-moderation partnership. Personnel are prohibited from setting SCP-4396 as a ringtone, notification sound, or contact-specific alert tone on any device, Foundation-issued or personal.

Individuals confirmed to have assigned SCP-4396 to a contact are to be approached by an embedded agent under a mobile-carrier customer service pretext and informed of a "device conflict" requiring the tone's removal; the assigned contact does not require separate notification or amnestic treatment, as the effect (see Description) does not appear to alter the contact's baseline memory or behavior outside of call-response instances.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4396 is a short, non-anomalous-sounding electronic chime, structurally similar to a default smartphone ringtone, that circulates as a shared audio file through messaging applications and file-sharing services. Standard audio analysis finds nothing distinguishing SCP-4396 from a conventional four-second synthesized tone.

When a subject (designated the "caller") assigns SCP-4396 as the specific ringtone associated with a single contact in their phone's contact list, that contact (the "recipient") will subsequently answer any call from the caller within one ring, regardless of the recipient's prior activity, location, device state (including devices powered off, in airplane mode, or physically distant from the recipient at the time of the call), or explicit prior intention not to answer. Recipients report no memory of the seconds immediately preceding the act of answering; the most recent continuous memory before answering is typically several minutes old, with the gap experienced as an ordinary lapse in attention rather than a loss of time.

The caller experiences a separate effect: a gradually intensifying urge to place additional calls to the recipient, unrelated to genuine communicative need, which test subjects describe as resembling boredom or idle habit rather than compulsion, despite call frequency increasing in documented cases from a baseline of 1-3 weekly calls to over 40 daily calls within three weeks of assigning the tone. Callers who have their access to the recipient's number removed (SIM confiscation, number change) redirect the same escalating call frequency toward other, non-SCP-4396-assigned contacts, though these calls are answered normally, at the recipient's discretion.

The Foundation has not identified a case in which SCP-4396 caused physical harm, but flags the object as a persistent risk to caller occupational and social functioning, and has recorded two cases of caller job termination attributable to call frequency during working hours.

ADDENDUM 4396-1: Removing SCP-4396 as a contact's assigned ringtone reliably ends both effects within 24 hours. The tone's original source or creator has not been identified; its earliest confirmed circulation dates to a 2015 file-sharing forum post with no retrievable uploader information.

SCP-4397.name: Brace For Impact
SCP-4397.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The master recording of SCP-4397, an in-flight safety briefing video produced for the defunct regional carrier Windham Air (operations ceased 1998), is held at Site-77. Digitized bootleg copies circulating among aviation-history enthusiast communities and CRT-media collector forums are monitored by Foundation web-crawler assets; identified upload sources are approached under an aviation-archival-rights pretext to arrange removal.

Foundation Aerospace Liaison Division maintains discreet awareness of any commercial or private flight known to have screened SCP-4397 or a bootleg derivative to passengers (documented in eleven cases, generally aviation-enthusiast charter flights screening it as a novelty). Flights confirmed to have screened SCP-4397 are not to be grounded or delayed on that basis alone; the Foundation's current ethical guidance (EC-4397-2) holds that the object's protective effect outweighs the containment value of denying passengers exposure, pending further review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4397 is an 8-minute in-flight safety video, produced in-house by Windham Air for mandatory pre-departure screening on its aircraft, covering standard content: seatbelt use, oxygen mask deployment, brace position, and emergency exit location. The video's production values, pacing, and on-camera flight attendant are unremarkable and consistent with the genre and period.

Passengers who have viewed SCP-4397 in full, when subsequently involved in a genuine airborne emergency (turbulence, decompression, or forced landing, documented in nine separate real-world incidents involving former Windham Air flights or later charter screenings), perform brace position, oxygen mask procedures, and evacuation behaviors with a precision and physical coordination exceeding what would be expected from a single safety demonstration, including in passengers who had not consciously recalled the video's content beforehand. In six of the nine documented incidents, exposed passengers moved into brace position in unison, within the same one-to-two-second window, without verbal cue from crew, including passengers seated apart from one another and unable to see each other's actions.

Statistical review of the nine incidents shows a survival and injury-avoidance rate among SCP-4397-exposed passengers exceeding the FAA baseline for comparable incident types by a margin the Foundation's Aerospace Liaison Division considers unlikely to be coincidental. However, exposed passengers interviewed after each incident describe the experience of the emergency itself with notable emotional flatness, several using near-identical phrasing ("I just did what I was supposed to do") regardless of the incident's severity, and report the felt sense of having limited independent control over their own movements during the emergency window, a sensation none found distressing at the time, though several found it retrospectively troubling once described back to them.

ADDENDUM 4397-1: Windham Air's safety-training vendor of record could not be located during Foundation historical research; the company that commissioned the video's production, listed on internal Windham Air documentation only as "Praxis Media Services," has no other identified body of work.

SCP-4398.name: Gallery Twelve
SCP-4398.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The Sennett Museum of Regional History in ██████ operates under sustained Foundation financial control through front foundation Anders Cultural Trust, which holds sufficient board influence to restrict the museum's audio-guide device inventory to Foundation-vetted units. All SCP-4398-affected devices (audio guide handsets numbered 1 through 40 in the museum's original 1988 acquisition, distinguishable from later replacement units only by internal serial number) are held in a monitored storage case and are not issued to visitors; the museum's current public-facing audio tour uses non-anomalous replacement hardware.

Visitors who have, prior to Foundation control of the site, followed SCP-4398's narrated directions to areas of the museum not present in its current floor plan (12 confirmed cases, 1988-2004) and not been located are classified MIA-4398 and remain open cases with the Missing Persons Liaison desk. Any individual matching an MIA-4398 description who is later identified in public records is to be flagged for immediate, cautious approach by a Foundation psychological support team, given documented reports (see Description) of profound temporal disorientation in the one confirmed recovery.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4398 designates an anomalous property of forty handheld audio-guide devices originally issued to visitors of the Sennett Museum of Regional History between 1988 and the Foundation's 2004 acquisition of site financial control. The devices, superficially standard cassette-based museum audio tours, narrate a guided route through the museum's exhibit halls in a calm, professionally recorded voice.

At an unpredictable point during playback, most commonly, though not exclusively, during the segment nominally covering the museum's second-floor regional-industry exhibit, the narration begins describing additional galleries, wings, and exhibits not present in the museum's actual architecture, in detail consistent enough (accurate ambient acoustics, plausible period-appropriate exhibit content, coherent wayfinding instructions referencing real, existing corridors as starting points) that visitors following the directions on foot have, in twelve documented cases between 1988 and 2004, walked out of Foundation-verifiable observation and not been located on-site or via any subsequent public record for a period of years, in one case, twenty-two.

The single confirmed recovery (2009, an individual matching the description and clothing of a visitor who followed SCP-4398 in 1991) was located working an unrelated retail job under her own legal name in a town 40 kilometers from the museum, expressing, on contact, the subjective conviction that only "twenty minutes or so" had passed since she left the museum gallery, and exhibiting no injuries, malnourishment, or other indication of eighteen years' unaccounted time. She has since declined further Foundation contact.

Foundation architectural surveys of the museum building, including ground-penetrating radar of adjoining walls and subfloor spaces, have found no physical space corresponding to the narrated additional galleries.

ADDENDUM 4398-1: Interviews with surviving original museum staff (pre-Foundation acquisition) indicate the audio-guide devices were sourced from a now-dissolved regional exhibit-design firm alongside several other, non-anomalous devices in the same purchase order; no design firm records distinguishing SCP-4398 from its non-anomalous siblings in that order have been recovered.

SCP-4399.name: The Dinner Table
SCP-4399.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation Group MC&E ("Marketing, Cover, and Engagement") holds effective creative-licensing control over SCP-4399 through shell advertising agency Correlate Creative, which has acquired exclusive re-licensing rights to the image from its original stock photography vendor. This arrangement allows the Foundation to regulate which brands and campaigns are permitted to license SCP-4399 and at what frequency, rather than removing the image from circulation.

SCP-4399 is deliberately licensed at a controlled cadence (target: no fewer than 800, no more than 1,400 confirmed placements annually across print, broadcast, and digital advertising within Foundation-monitored markets) sufficient to maintain population-level cumulative exposure within the range associated with the effect described below, under authorization of Directive MC&E-19 ("Managed Familiarity Assets"). Any organization outside Foundation control that acquires independent rights to republish or heavily feature SCP-4399 is to be approached by Correlate Creative representatives with above-market licensing buyout offers.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4399 is a stock photograph, catalog title "Family Dinner, Golden Hour" (photographer credited as J. Renner, shot 1994, originally licensed through a now-defunct stock agency later absorbed into a larger commercial photography library), depicting four unidentified models posed as a family of two adults and two children at a set dinner table. The image is not remarkable in composition or technical quality and has been licensed for use in advertising, editorial, and template contexts an estimated several hundred thousand times since its original sale.

Individuals whose cumulative visual exposure to SCP-4399, across unrelated advertisements, product packaging, stock template designs, and incidental media appearances, none of which need to be consciously noticed at time of viewing, exceeds an estimated threshold (Foundation modeling suggests roughly 40-60 exposures, though this varies by individual) begin to experience the models depicted in SCP-4399 as familiar, typically recontextualized as a remembered relative, family friend, or acquaintance from an unspecified earlier period of the subject's life, despite no such person existing in the subject's verifiable personal history.

This false familiarity does not generalize to a full false memory (subjects cannot typically recall specific shared events) but manifests as persistent affective association: subjects report SCP-4399 or products/advertisements featuring it evoke unearned nostalgia, trust, and emotional warmth disproportionate to the actual content being advertised. Controlled Foundation testing (Experiment Log 4399-3, conducted through Correlate Creative campaigns for non-Foundation consumer products under Ethics Committee sanction) confirmed that advertising campaigns using SCP-4399 produce measurably elevated brand trust and purchase-intent metrics compared to matched control campaigns using demographically similar, non-anomalous stock imagery, at a margin consistent across eleven independent campaign tests.

ADDENDUM 4399-1: MC&E's continued licensing of SCP-4399 for Foundation-commissioned campaigns (currently limited to recruitment materials for a Foundation-linked charitable front and three public-messaging campaigns related to disaster-preparedness compliance) has been approved under Directive MC&E-19 on the basis that the resulting trust effect measurably improves compliance outcomes. This use has not been reviewed by the Ethics Committee's standing membership, per an exemption whose original authorization the Committee's current members have been unable to locate.

SCP-4400.name: Exactly Where You Need To Be
SCP-4400.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The master audio recording of SCP-4400, a self-help audiobook of unconfirmed authorship, is held at Site-77 under joint custody of the Site Director and the Foundation's Behavioral Compliance Division, which retains standing authorization to deploy controlled excerpts under Directive BCD-11 ("Terminal Scenario Resourcing"). Full playback of SCP-4400 outside of sanctioned Behavioral Compliance operations requires Level 4 clearance and O5-tier notification.

Public distribution of SCP-4400 is limited to a small number of copies sold through legitimate self-help publishing channels prior to Foundation acquisition of the rights (approximately 6,000 copies estimated in circulation as audio CDs and digital purchases); recall is not attempted, as public-facing containment priority is limited to monitoring rather than suppression, given the object's comparatively low physical risk profile to unaffiliated listeners (see Description).

Sanctioned uses of SCP-4400 excerpts by Behavioral Compliance personnel require sign-off from a Foundation ethicist for each deployment and are logged permanently in the Terminal Scenario Resourcing register, which is reviewed annually by the Ethics Committee.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4400 is a 3-hour-40-minute self-help audiobook, titled You Are Exactly Where You Need to Be, narrated by an unidentified male speaker in a calm, unhurried cadence typical of the genre, structured as eleven chapters addressing common sources of life dissatisfaction (career, relationships, health, aging, regret) with conventional-sounding affirmational content.

A listener who completes SCP-4400 in full develops a stable, durable increase in subjective satisfaction with their current life circumstances that does not correlate with any objective change in those circumstances and does not diminish over the eighteen-month maximum follow-up period studied to date. Critically, this contentment effect operates independently of the listener's actual risk exposure or the objective severity of their circumstances: subjects have exhibited the effect while in situations conventionally understood as urgent, dangerous, or in need of remedy (documented subjects include individuals in untreated medical crises, active financial collapse, and one subject in physical restraint during a Foundation containment breach event), without the contentment reducing their capacity to follow direct instructions or perform physical tasks, only their subjective distress about, and motivation to independently alter, their circumstances.

Because this profile, the reduction of anxiety and resistance without corresponding reduction in task compliance, is operationally useful in scenarios where the Foundation requires compliant, non-panicking behavior from an individual whose situation cannot be improved (terminal containment breaches, incurable Foundation-related injuries, certain classes of sanctioned termination), Behavioral Compliance Division has, since 2011, deployed controlled excerpts of SCP-4400 under Directive BCD-11 to Class-D personnel and, in four documented cases, to Foundation staff in unsurvivable containment scenarios, in place of standard sedation, citing improved subject cooperation and reduced psychological distress during the intervention's final stage.

ADDENDUM 4400-1: The Ethics Committee's most recent review of Directive BCD-11 (2023) declined to revoke the directive, citing insufficient evidence that BCD-11's use constitutes a harm distinct from the outcome the subject would experience regardless of SCP-4400's use. Three dissenting committee members noted, in a minority opinion attached to the review, that the directive's continued use had not been evaluated for its effect on the personnel administering it. The dissent was not adopted.

ADDENDUM 4400-2: The original publisher of You Are Exactly Where You Need to Be dissolved in 2009. Its listed author, credited only as "someone who's been there," has not been identified.

SCP-4401.name: The Speaker's Podium
SCP-4401.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4401 remains installed in O5 Council Chamber Archive-Zero-1, accessible only to personnel summoned to address the Council in person. Use requires written authorization from no fewer than three sitting Council members, logged under a designation separate from standard containment logs and held only in the Chamber's own record, which SCP-4401 itself maintains (see Description). Foundation personnel who are informed of a colleague's use of SCP-4401 are to make no attempt to independently verify that colleague's employment history, tenure, or prior existence within the Foundation; such verification attempts are administratively discouraged rather than anomalous in nature, per Council directive 4401-A.

A standing order requires that no individual address the Council from SCP-4401 more than once in a five-year period, and that a designated Archive Zero recordkeeper (currently Archivist Voss) be present at every use to note, off the record the object itself keeps, who stood at the podium and what was said. This secondary record is stored outside Archive Zero and is the only reliable account of SCP-4401's operational history.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4401 is a wooden lectern, approximately 1.2 meters in height, of a design consistent with Foundation furnishing standard from an indeterminate period between 1948 and the present; carbon dating of its structural components has returned results ranging across this entire span depending on which section is sampled. It bears no maker's mark.

When an individual delivers a formal address to the O5 Council while standing at SCP-4401, the content of that address becomes, from that point forward, attributed within all Foundation records, personnel files, and the memories of everyone who heard it, to the most recent prior individual to have addressed the Council from the same location on the same general subject. The current speaker's own participation is not merely uncredited; it is retroactively absent. Personnel files are found, upon audit, to show the current speaker never having given the address at all, and in cases where the speaker held no other independent record of employment prior to that address, personnel files show no history of the individual's employment with the Foundation whatsoever.

The individual so affected does not disappear and reports no subjective loss of memory or identity. They continue to hold whatever position they held before addressing the Council, and are inconvenienced primarily by an inability to produce documentation of their own career predating the incident, and by colleagues' inability to recall having worked with them for longer than roughly five years, regardless of true tenure.

ADDENDUM 4401-1: SCP-4401 was not discovered by the Foundation. Site records indicate it was commissioned and installed by the O5 Council in 1966, following the third documented instance of a Council member being coerced, under threat to Foundation security, into publicly disclosing classified testimony to a hostile party. Its intended and continued use is to permit a Council member to make a given disclosure, secure the tactical benefit of having done so, and then transfer authorship of the disclosure to a predecessor who, by the time the transfer completes, has already been removed from active service and is not positioned to object. Fourteen individuals are known to have been used as the terminal recipient of a transferred address since 1966. None have been interviewed. Their current locations, if they are still living, are not recorded anywhere the Council will disclose, including, notably, in the private record kept by the Archive Zero recordkeeper, whose most recent entry states only that the practice "should have stopped by now."

SCP-4402.name: The Duplicate Vault Door
SCP-4402.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4402 refers collectively to seven identical steel vault doors, each installed as the primary containment barrier for a high-security storage vault at a separate Foundation site (current locations: Site-19, Site-45, Site-77, Site-88, Site-103, Site-120, and Archive Zero). All seven are to remain permanently closed except during scheduled inventory, which must be coordinated across all seven sites simultaneously via Archive Zero Central Scheduling, with a minimum 72-hour advance notice to each site director. Under no circumstances is any single SCP-4402 door to be opened without this coordination.

Each vault behind an SCP-4402 door currently stores material whose loss, exposure, or duplication would constitute a critical Foundation security failure; the specific contents of each vault are compartmentalized and no Level 6 personnel are assumed to have full knowledge of all seven inventories. A standing SCP-4402 Coordination Committee, reporting directly to the Council, reviews any request to open a door.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4402 doors are, by all available physical and forensic evidence, a single door existing in seven locations simultaneously, rather than seven separate objects of identical manufacture. This determination follows from the object's central anomalous property: any action performed on one SCP-4402 door — opening, closing, damage, cleaning, the application of a lock — occurs identically and without delay on all seven doors, regardless of distance between sites. A scratch inflicted on the Site-19 instance in 2003 appeared simultaneously on all six other instances and has persisted, identically positioned, since. Personnel who have opened one instance report a mundane act of pulling or rotating a handle; there is no reported sensation of the door's non-locality.

The vaults themselves are not linked; they are separate rooms with separate contents at separate sites, sealed by what is, evidently, the same door. Opening any SCP-4402 door opens all seven vaults at once, exposing seven distinct sets of critical material simultaneously regardless of the intentions or clearance of the individual who opened the triggering door. No test has been conducted to determine what would happen were the doors somehow desynchronized, largely because no proposed method of desynchronization has been approved for testing, and largely because at least one Council member has, on the record, described the prospect as "worse, in every scenario I can construct, than the current arrangement."

ADDENDUM 4402-1: In 2019, a partial breach at Site-88 resulted in an unauthorized individual gaining brief physical access to the SCP-4402 vault interior at that site before Foundation response neutralized the intrusion. Standard protocol would treat this as a Site-88 vault content exposure. Post-incident inventory found that seven vaults, not one, had recorded a two-minute unlock event. Site-19, Site-45, Site-77, Site-103, Site-120, and Archive Zero each opened and closed within the same window, unattended, with no other anomalous activity or intrusion detected at any of those sites. It has not been established whether this means all seven vaults were briefly exposed to the Site-88 intruder, or whether the intruder was, for two minutes, present at all seven locations. Both explanations have been formally proposed to the Council. Neither has been formally accepted.

SCP-4403.name: The Confession Stenograph
SCP-4403.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4403 is stored in a standard equipment locker in Archive Zero's Interview Wing when not in use. Deployment requires sign-out approval from a Level 6 interviewer and is restricted to interviews of individuals suspected of withholding information of Council-level significance. A transcript produced by SCP-4403 is to be sealed and read only by the requesting interviewer and one countersigning officer; it is not to be entered into the subject's permanent file under any circumstance, and is not to be read aloud in the presence of the interview subject after the session concludes.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4403 is a manual stenotype machine of a make no longer in production, functionally unremarkable in appearance. When operated by a trained stenographer during a spoken interview, SCP-4403 does not transcribe the words spoken by the interview subject. It transcribes what the interview subject currently believes to be true, expressed as though the subject had stated it plainly, regardless of what was actually said, including cases where the subject is lying, evasive, silent, or physically incapable of speech.

The transcript is not a record of fact. It is a record of belief, and the two are frequently identical only by coincidence. Subjects who falsely confess under duress produce a transcript denying guilt, if they privately believe themselves innocent; subjects who genuinely believe an incorrect account of events produce a transcript of that incorrect account, indistinguishable in the document from a truthful one. SCP-4403 offers no indication, textual or otherwise, of which category a given line of transcript falls into. Cross-referencing a transcript against independently verified fact is the only method by which its reliability, for a given passage, can be assessed, and this can only be performed after the fact.

The Foundation's continued use of SCP-4403, despite this limitation, rests on the observation that a subject's sincere belief, correctly transcribed, is frequently of greater operational value than their spoken testimony, particularly in cases involving deep-cover assets, compromised personnel, or individuals affected by memetic or mnestic tampering who no longer have reliable access to the true facts of their own history. In such cases, SCP-4403 produces the only account available of what the subject's mind currently holds to be true, which is sometimes the closest available approximation to the truth the Foundation can obtain.

ADDENDUM 4403-1: During a 2021 interview of a Council liaison suspected of leaking Archive Zero location data, SCP-4403 transcribed a full confession, detailed, specific, and consistent with independently known facts, while the subject verbally and consistently denied all wrongdoing. The confession was used to secure the subject's removal from active duty. A minority report filed by the countersigning officer notes that a sincere, false belief of guilt, arising from any cause including psychological stress or deliberate induction, would produce an identical transcript, and that SCP-4403 provides no mechanism to distinguish the two. The subject's current status, and the eventual truth of the matter, remain unconfirmed.

SCP-4404.name: The Intake Wristband
SCP-4404.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The forty-one remaining unused units of SCP-4404 are stored in a sealed container in Archive Zero, physically separated from standard personnel-processing wristband stock by a minimum of one secure corridor. No SCP-4404 unit is to be applied to any individual under any circumstance without direct, written, individually-countersigned authorization from a majority of the O5 Council. As of this writing, no such authorization has been requested since 2011.

Nine individuals currently employed by the Foundation are known to be wearing an active SCP-4404 unit, applied prior to the current containment protocol. These individuals are not to have their units removed; removal is addressed in Addendum 4404-2. Their case files are held separately from standard personnel records, under joint O5 and Ethics Committee review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4404 units are plastic hospital-style intake wristbands, visually identical to those used in standard Foundation personnel processing, distinguishable only by a serial prefix. When an SCP-4404 unit is affixed to an individual during processing, a full exchange occurs between that individual and one other living human being, selected by a mechanism the Foundation has not determined, though it is not random: statistical review of past applications shows the selected counterpart is, in every confirmed case, a person who at the time of exchange held no formal employment, standing family, or fixed residence, and who was, again in every confirmed case, unaware of the Foundation's existence.

The exchange transfers the individual's entire pre-Foundation biographical history — birth record, education, relationships, memory of a lived civilian life — onto the unaware counterpart, who receives it as their own remembered past with no awareness of the substitution. The Foundation employee retains their current identity, skills, and Foundation-specific memory, but their biographical record prior to Foundation employment is, from the moment of exchange, held by someone else, living an ordinary life under what they believe to be their own name and history. The employee's own memory of their pre-Foundation life does not vanish, but becomes, on questioning, difficult for them to access and prone to described "borrowed" uncertainty, as though recalling someone else's account of it.

SCP-4404 was developed, not discovered; early Foundation records credit its design to an Ethics Committee initiative intended to grant deep-cover and high-mortality-risk operatives a genuine civilian identity to fall back into should Foundation employment end catastrophically, without requiring falsified paperwork vulnerable to discovery. Its use was suspended in 2011 following the determination that the unaware counterpart receiving the operative's original life is a real, uninvolved person whose own prior existence is, in the same instant, permanently and irretrievably displaced, with no established means of return, notification, or compensation.

ADDENDUM 4404-2: Ethics Committee finding 4404-2-E states that removal of an active unit does not reverse the exchange, and instead appears to sever the wearer's Foundation identity from any biographical record whatsoever, including their Foundation-issued one. One such removal was attempted in 2014. The subject is currently held in long-term Foundation care. Their case file lists no name.

SCP-4405.name: The Sub-Basement Elevator
SCP-4405.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4405 occupies the northeast freight elevator shaft of Archive Zero and remains in general operational use for authorized transport between Sub-Basements 1 through 4, its designated legitimate range. The control panel's additional, unlabeled buttons, currently numbering between six and eleven depending on inspection, are covered by a locked panel plate. Any employee who reports the plate open, missing, or bypassed is to be interviewed and their most recent 96 hours cross-referenced against facility access logs.

Maintenance staff are not to be assigned to SCP-4405 individually; a minimum of two technicians must be present for any servicing, and both must remain in constant visual contact with each other for the duration.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4405 is, in outward appearance and mundane function, a standard freight elevator car. Its anomalous property concerns the unlabeled panel buttons described above, each of which corresponds to a sub-basement level not reflected in any Archive Zero blueprint, construction record, or structural survey, and which cannot be reached by any known stairwell, service shaft, or excavation.

Pressing an unlabeled button transports the car and any occupants to the corresponding level, where the doors open onto a hallway or room consistent in construction material and general condition with the rest of Archive Zero's substructure, but containing no signage, no personnel, and no entries in any facility floor plan. Occupants who travel to these levels and return report no memory of the intervening time between the doors closing and reopening at their origin floor, regardless of how long the doors remain open at the anomalous level; a 2018 incident in which two technicians were unaccounted for at SCP-4405's destination floor for approximately eleven minutes by elevator mechanical logs was recalled by both technicians as an uninterrupted, single-second door cycle.

The elevator car's mechanical wear, measured by cable tension, motor runtime, and floor-counter increment, is inconsistent with its logged legitimate usage by a factor the maintenance department estimates at roughly 340%, suggesting SCP-4405 travels to unlabeled floors considerably more often than any authorized or witnessed instance accounts for, with neither passengers nor operators aware of having initiated or experienced the trip.

No O5 Council member has confirmed ordering the elevator's construction, its unlabeled floors, or any use of them, and no maintenance order for the missing 340% of runtime has been located in Archive Zero's own procurement records, which are otherwise considered complete for the relevant period.

ADDENDUM 4405-1: Floor-counter logs recovered during a 2022 refit show the floor-counter incrementing at regular, roughly weekly intervals during a six-month period in 2005 when Archive Zero's personnel roster shows no active maintenance or operational staff assigned to the site at all, the facility having been placed in caretaker status pending a since-cancelled decommissioning review. No party has offered an explanation for who, or what, was operating SCP-4405 during that period, and the review that would have determined whether the site should remain open was, records confirm, resumed and approved less than one week after the elevator's logged activity ceased.

SCP-4406.name: The Correction Box
SCP-4406.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4406 is maintained in Archive Zero's Records Integrity Office under the direct authority of the Archive Zero Chief Archivist, who reports its use, on a quarterly basis, only to the Council. Items are submitted to SCP-4406 exclusively via a standing request process requiring the sign-off of the Chief Archivist and one Council member. No item is to be submitted to SCP-4406 for personal, non-institutional reasons under any circumstance; two personnel have been dismissed for violations of this rule since its formalization in 2015.

A duplicate of every document or item submitted to SCP-4406 is to be photographed and separately filed prior to submission, under Protocol 4406-Shadow, so that the Foundation retains a record of what a given item was before correction. This duplicate record is itself held at Archive Zero and, per Addendum 4406-3, is not to be treated as necessarily reliable.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4406 is a steel document box, dimensions 40cm x 30cm x 20cm, of unremarkable institutional manufacture, kept locked when not in active use. An item placed inside SCP-4406 and left for a period of exactly one Foundation business day (24 hours, excluding recognized holidays, for reasons not understood) is removed to find itself altered: not damaged, not replaced, but corrected, in the sense of now representing an edited, more internally consistent version of whatever it originally was.

A contradictory internal report becomes a report whose contradictions have resolved themselves into a single coherent account. A photograph of a redacted document is returned showing the same document with additional information redacted, never less. A damaged specimen container is returned intact, its damage absent from both the object and, per multiple confirmed instances, the incident report describing how it was damaged, which itself corrects to no longer mention the incident. SCP-4406 does not create information; it appears to select, from among versions of a document, record, or object that could exist, the one that is most complete and most consistent with whatever context that item now sits within, and substitutes it for the original.

The Foundation's institutional use of SCP-4406, formalized under Council authorization in 2015, is as the terminal step in Archive Zero's document sanitization process: incident reports, personnel files, and historical records too inconsistent, incomplete, or compromised to be safely retained are submitted to SCP-4406 and returned in a form suitable for the permanent archive. This process is understood by the Chief Archivist's office to be, functionally, indistinguishable from falsification, with the caveat that SCP-4406 does not require anyone to decide what the falsified version should say.

ADDENDUM 4406-3: A 2023 internal review comparing three decades of Protocol 4406-Shadow duplicate records against the current permanent archive found matches for 94% of entries. The remaining 6%, comprising 211 individual items, show no shadow duplicate for a corresponding archive entry that Foundation systems otherwise confirm was, at some point, submitted to SCP-4406. Whether Protocol 4406-Shadow has itself, at points, been circumvented, or whether SCP-4406's correction extends to records of its own use, has not been determined and is not, per a note appended to the review by the Chief Archivist, expected to be.

SCP-4407.name: The Diagnostic Stethoscope
SCP-4407.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4407 is stored in a standard medical equipment cabinet in the Archive Zero infirmary, unlocked, and is not distinguished from mundane equipment by any external marking beyond a small inventory tag. Containment relies entirely on restricting its use to authorized medical staff for its designated anomalous function, described below; SCP-4407 poses no risk if used as an ordinary stethoscope, which is its most common actual use, and staff are not required to treat it with special caution during routine physical examinations.

Use of SCP-4407 for its anomalous diagnostic function requires the presence of a staff Ethics Committee liaison and is restricted to cases specifically referred by the Council or the Medical Director. Findings are to be recorded in a sealed supplemental file, separate from the patient's standard medical record, accessible only to Level 6 personnel with explicit need.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4407 is a stethoscope of conventional design and materials, functioning identically to a mundane equivalent in all standard uses. Its anomalous property manifests only when the chestpiece is placed against a subject specifically while the examiner mentally poses the question of whether the subject is, in a clinically meaningful sense, alive.

In such cases, SCP-4407 transmits a heartbeat sound regardless of whether the subject has a detectable pulse by any other instrument. For the overwhelming majority of examined subjects, this sound is consistent with, and simultaneous to, their actual cardiac activity. In a small number of documented cases, comprising 34 individuals examined to date, SCP-4407 has transmitted a steady, clinically normal heartbeat sound for a subject independently confirmed, by every other available medical instrument and by direct physical examination, to have no cardiac activity whatsoever, including several subjects examined at intervals of years, with a consistent sound recorded at each examination, and including four subjects who were, by all conventional medical standards, deceased at the time of examination and remained so for the subsequent observation period.

SCP-4407 offers no explanation for this discrepancy, and its output cannot be used to revive, resuscitate, or otherwise medically treat a subject; the sound appears to be diagnostic information only, of an axis of "aliveness" not currently captured by any other Foundation medical instrument. The Foundation's working position, adopted by the Medical Director's office in 2017, is that SCP-4407 measures something other than cardiac function, tentatively glossed in internal documents as "standing," and that a subject's standing and their conventional vital status are usually, but not necessarily always, identical conditions.

ADDENDUM 4407-1: Of the 34 discrepant cases, three involved sitting or former O5 Council members, examined during routine Archive Zero medical intake between 2018 and 2024. All three results have been independently reconfirmed on at least one subsequent occasion. No further examinations of current Council members using SCP-4407 have been scheduled, and no directive addressing the finding has been issued by the Council.

SCP-4408.name: The Occupancy Placard
SCP-4408.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4408 is kept in a fireproof document sleeve in the Council Chamber anteroom at Archive Zero, accessible to any sitting Council member without further authorization, reflecting its status as a standing Council resource rather than a conventionally contained anomaly. Its use by any other Foundation personnel requires unanimous Council authorization and has occurred on four recorded occasions outside Council use, each documented in Addendum 4408-1.

Any room in which SCP-4408 is in active use is to be treated, for external logging purposes, as occupied for a duration equal to the actual elapsed exterior time, regardless of the subjective duration reported by occupants upon exit, to avoid creating discoverable discrepancies in facility scheduling records.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4408 is a laminated card, approximately 10cm by 15cm, printed with the text "IN SESSION — DO NOT DISTURB" in a typeface consistent with mid-20th-century Foundation signage standards. When hung on the exterior handle of a closed door, the room behind that door becomes temporally decoupled from the surrounding facility for as long as the card remains in place. Time within the room continues to pass for its occupants at a rate the Council has, in internal usage notes, estimated at between 40 and 60 times the exterior rate, though the ratio has never been precisely measured and may not be constant.

Removing the card ends the effect immediately; occupants exit into a facility where an amount of exterior time has passed consistent with only a fraction of their subjective experience inside, typically registering as a single unremarkable meeting of ordinary length to anyone outside the room, including, per multiple confirmed incidents, individuals who checked the door and found it, by external appearances, in routine use throughout. No occupant has reported hunger, fatigue, or aging effects disproportionate to their subjective time inside, suggesting the room's occupants, and not merely their perception of time, are genuinely operating on the accelerated internal clock.

The Council's use of SCP-4408, formalized as a standing procedure since at least the 1970s per available records, allows extended private deliberation, drafting, or crisis planning to occur within a single externally brief window, without the fact of an extended session being reflected in any external schedule, log, or witness account. Its primary documented use is for Council sessions addressing matters the Council has determined should not appear, even in redacted form, to have consumed unusual time or attention.

ADDENDUM 4408-1: The four recorded non-Council uses of SCP-4408 include one 1991 instance in which it was authorized for use by a two-person medical team attending to a Council member during a medical emergency, permitting several subjective days of continuous treatment within an exterior window of approximately three hours. The patient's identity and ultimate outcome are redacted above Level 6 clearance, a redaction level unusual for a matter otherwise fully described within this file.

SCP-4409.name: The Site Map
SCP-4409.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4409 remains mounted, under permanent guard, in a restricted chamber adjacent to the Council Chamber at Archive Zero. No pin, marker, or annotation currently placed on SCP-4409 is to be moved, added, or removed without unanimous Council authorization, logged individually by pin. A photographic record of SCP-4409's current configuration is updated weekly and stored off-site, at a location not itself marked on SCP-4409.

Personnel assigned to guard or maintain SCP-4409 are rotated every 30 days and are not to be informed of its anomalous property prior to their first shift; briefing occurs only after initial exposure, per Protocol 4409-Orient, which has reduced incidents of unauthorized pin movement by guard personnel by an estimated 80% since adoption.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4409 is a wall-mounted world map, approximately 3 meters by 2 meters, marked with pins indicating the current locations of active Foundation sites. It is not, by any evidence available to current researchers, an accurate representation of Foundation holdings; it is understood by the Council, per surviving internal correspondence, to be the actual mechanism by which those holdings are located.

Site locations correspond to pin placements on SCP-4409, not the reverse. Moving a pin from one point on the map to another results, within a period ranging from immediate to approximately six hours in documented cases, in the corresponding Foundation site physically relocating to correspond with the new pin position: buildings, personnel present at the time of relocation, and contained anomalies transfer as a unit, with local geography and surrounding population adjusting around the site's new location as though it had always been there, and adjusting away from its prior location as though the site had never existed at the old coordinates, including revision of any local infrastructure, records, or population memory dependent on the site's former presence.

Personnel who are off-site, on leave, or in transit at the moment of relocation are not transported with the site and instead find, on attempting to return, that their site's prior location now shows no trace of Foundation presence, while the site itself continues operating at its new coordinates with no gap in service. Reintegration of such personnel is handled case-by-case; 22 individuals are currently listed as separated from a relocated site by this mechanism, of whom 9 have been successfully relocated to their site's new position and 13 remain unaccounted for.

The Council's principal documented use of SCP-4409 is emergency relocation of a compromised site faster than any conventional evacuation could achieve, at the accepted cost of any personnel not physically present within the site's boundary at the moment of the move.

ADDENDUM 4409-1: SCP-4409 currently displays 6 pins for which no corresponding site appears in any active Foundation directory. Council correspondence references these as "reserved" without further explanation. No living Council member has, on record, claimed authorship of these six placements.

SCP-4410.name: The Indeterminate Scalpel
SCP-4410.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4410 is stored in the Archive Zero pathology suite in a sealed sterile case, distinguishable from the 11 other scalpels of identical make stored alongside it only by a serial number etched into the handle. Use requires two attending pathologists, one of whom must not have prior knowledge of the deceased subject's cause of death, containment history, or identity, to preserve the validity of findings described below.

Any autopsy conducted with SCP-4410 is to be treated, until confirmed otherwise, as producing findings that may not correspond to the subject's actual internal condition at time of death, and no operational, medical, or legal determination is to rest solely on an SCP-4410 finding without independent confirmation by conventional autopsy instruments.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4410 is a stainless-steel autopsy scalpel of standard Foundation medical-examiner issue.
