When used to perform an internal examination of a deceased subject, SCP-4410 does not necessarily reveal the subject's internal anatomy as it existed at the moment of death. In a minority of examinations, estimated at 6% based on cases where comparison was possible, SCP-4410 instead reveals an internal condition inconsistent with the subject's recorded cause of death, prior medical history, or, in several instances, basic human anatomy, before conventional re-examination of the same body reverts to showing findings consistent with expectation.

Documented discrepant findings include organs present in a subject whose medical history recorded their prior surgical removal; a cause of death, confirmed by every other means, that SCP-4410 findings do not support, the subject's internal condition being inconsistent with the recorded fatal event ever having occurred; and, in four cases, internal structures not matching any known human physiology, subsequently absent on re-examination with conventional instruments performed within the hour.

The Foundation's working hypothesis, unconfirmed, holds that a body's internal condition is not, prior to direct examination, a single fixed fact, but exists as one of several physically possible states consistent with the subject's external condition and available records, and that SCP-4410 does not reveal a hidden truth so much as make an examination-dependent selection among these states, a selection conventional instruments do not appear to replicate. This hypothesis is disputed by at least two Level 6 medical staff, who maintain that SCP-4410 findings represent a genuine anomalous history for the subject that conventional re-examination is itself failing, rather than succeeding, to detect.

Subjects have not been observed to react differently to death depending on subsequent SCP-4410 findings, and no correlation between SCP-4410 discrepancies and any property of the subject knowable prior to examination has been established.

ADDENDUM 4410-1: SCP-4410 was used, under standard post-mortem protocol, during the 2020 autopsy of a Council-adjacent researcher whose recorded cause of death was cardiac arrest. SCP-4410 findings showed no heart present in the body at all, an absence not replicated on conventional re-examination performed ninety minutes later, which found a heart consistent with the recorded cause of death. The attending pathologists' report notes, without further comment, that the researcher's personnel file had, three years prior, been the subject of an SCP-4407 examination returning an anomalous result (see SCP-4407, Addendum 4407-1).

SCP-4411.name: The Emergency Landline
SCP-4411.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4411 is installed in a dedicated alcove adjacent to the Council Chamber at Archive Zero, connected to no exterior line, junction, or exchange that Foundation telecommunications engineers have been able to identify. It is not to be unplugged, relocated, or physically altered; two prior attempts to trace or disconnect its wiring resulted in no anomalous consequence but also no success in locating any endpoint, and further attempts have been suspended pending Council review.

A staff member is assigned at all times to remain within audible range of SCP-4411. Upon it ringing, the on-duty staff member is to answer, record the call to the fullest extent possible, and immediately notify the Council, regardless of hour. No individual is to attempt to keep the line open past its natural termination, described below.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4411 is a rotary-dial telephone handset of a design consistent with Foundation equipment from the 1970s. It rings on an irregular basis, averaging roughly four times per year, and when answered carries a voice, always different, identifying itself as Foundation personnel at a named site, reporting an emergency or critical incident in progress at that site.

In one hundred percent of confirmed cases to date, the reported incident has not, at the time of the call, occurred, or begun to occur, at the named site. In the majority of cases, no such incident occurs at all. In eleven confirmed cases, an incident consistent with the call's description occurred at the named site at a later date, ranging from six hours to eleven months after the call, with the caller's voice, when subsequently cross-referenced against site personnel, matching no individual who is confirmed to have been present at, or connected to, that site at the time of the actual incident.

Calls always terminate after between ninety seconds and four minutes, regardless of the recipient's actions, with a disconnection the Foundation's telecommunications staff describe as consistent with a normal call ending rather than any interruption. No caller has, in any recorded instance, provided information sufficient to prevent the eventual incident; details are consistently too vague, too late, or accompanied by a description of the responding personnel's own actions in a manner that renders the warning self-defeating; and among the eleven confirmed predictive calls, three documented attempts by the Foundation to alter the outcome based on the call's information resulted in a different, and in each case more severe, incident occurring at the named site instead of the one originally described.

The Council's current standing position, reached after the third such attempt in 2016, is that SCP-4411 should continue to be answered and recorded for archival and pattern-analysis purposes, but that its information should not be acted upon to alter Foundation operations at the named site, a position several former Council members are known to have disputed at the time it was adopted.

ADDENDUM 4411-1: The most recent SCP-4411 call, received eleven days prior to this document's most recent revision, named Archive Zero as the site of a reported incident. No further detail was given before the call terminated at the ninety-second mark. No incident has yet occurred.

SCP-4412.name: The Contingency Board
SCP-4412.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4412 is installed in a restricted planning room at Archive Zero, accessible only during Council-authorized contingency planning sessions, attended by no fewer than two Council members and one Ethics Committee observer at all times. All writing on SCP-4412 is to be photographed before erasure and archived under seal. Erasure of any written content is mandatory at the conclusion of every session, without exception, regardless of whether the scenario discussed has been resolved, abandoned, or left incomplete.

Any personnel who observe, report, or suspect a real-world event corresponding to content previously written on SCP-4412 are to notify the Ethics Committee immediately via Protocol 4412-Echo. No session is to describe, even hypothetically, harm to a named, identifiable individual; sessions are restricted to institutional, systemic, and scenario-level planning.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4412 is a wall-mounted dry-erase board, approximately 2.5 meters wide, of standard institutional manufacture. Text or diagrams written on SCP-4412 describing a specific hypothetical scenario begin, within a period ranging from days to several months, to manifest as small, isolated, individually deniable real-world occurrences consistent with the written scenario, in a location and at a scale proportionate to the specificity and detail of what was written.

A vaguely sketched contingency, noted in a few words, tends to produce no detectable manifestation. A scenario described in structured, multi-step detail, including named institutions, systems, or general categories of location, has in documented cases produced a corresponding sequence of minor real events: a described supply-chain disruption scenario for a named class of Foundation material preceded, by approximately five weeks, an unrelated-appearing but functionally identical disruption in the actual supply chain for that material; a described containment-breach contingency for a specified anomaly class produced, six weeks after the session, a minor and independently unexplained procedural failure at a site holding an anomaly of that class, though not the specific anomaly discussed.

No individual, harm, or death has been written on SCP-4412 with confirmed subsequent correlation to a real event, per the standing prohibition described above, and no test of this specific boundary has been formally authorized. The Foundation's continued use of SCP-4412, adopted as a Thaumiel-classified planning tool in 1988, treats this manifestation property as a genuine, if partial and imprecise, capability to pre-test institutional contingency plans against reality before a real crisis occurs, at an acknowledged and unresolved cost: every contingency scenario discussed on SCP-4412, once written, appears to become somewhat more likely to occur in the world regardless of whether the Council intends to enact it, meaning every planning session simultaneously prepares the Foundation for a crisis and marginally increases the odds of that crisis occurring.

ADDENDUM 4412-1: A 2021 internal audit found that of forty-one major contingency-level incidents affecting the Foundation between 1988 and 2020, records show SCP-4412 sessions addressing a matching or closely related scenario prior to twenty-six of them, a proportion the auditing statistician's report describes as "not adequately explained by the Foundation planning for events it correctly anticipated." No changes to SCP-4412's operational status have followed from this audit's findings.

SCP-4413.name: The Witnessing Octopus
SCP-4413.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Specimens (currently 3, designated 4413-1 through 4413-3) are held in individual saltwater tanks at Site-88's marine xenobiology wing, tanks lined with matte non-reflective material to reduce triggering. Personnel handling specimens must complete Psychological Clearance Form 4413 before contact, as ink discharge exposure has produced lasting distress in D-Class and researchers. Any newly discovered wild specimen is to be captured only by teams equipped with polarized full-face visors; direct eye contact with a distressed specimen during ink release is to be avoided. Ink samples recovered from field sites are catalogued and stored in light-sealed containers at Site-88; only personnel with Level 3 clearance or higher may request playback or visual analysis of recovered ink patterns, and only in the presence of a staff psychologist.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4413 designates a small population (est. 40-70 individuals) of an octopus species, otherwise resembling Octopus vulgaris but for an enlarged and structurally unique ink sac. When an SCP-4413 individual perceives that a nearby human is drowning, or discovers a drowned corpse, it releases ink in a pattern that, when the cloud is filmed and the footage played back at reduced speed, resolves into a first-person visual reconstruction of the final approximately ninety seconds of that person's life, as seen through their own eyes. The mechanism producing this effect is not understood; SCP-4413 has no observed sensory organ capable of receiving optical information from another organism, living or dead, and the ink's pigment chemistry does not differ measurably from that of baseline octopuses.

The reconstruction is consistently accurate to known facts when the drowning was witnessed or recorded by other means, including details SCP-4413 could not plausibly have observed (objects submerged from view, events occurring behind the victim, or, in one case, the victim's own thoughts rendered as overlaid text legible only in specific languages the victim spoke). SCP-4413 does not require faces, bodies, or any physical contact with the deceased to produce a reconstruction; proximity to the location of death, within roughly 200 meters and within 6 hours, is sufficient.

SCP-4413 was brought to Foundation attention after amateur footage of a wild specimen's ink discharge, filmed near ██████████ Harbor, was slowed down by a hobbyist and found to depict the final moments of a local fisherman who had gone missing nine days prior, at a time when the specimen filmed had not yet been born according to growth-ring analysis of its beak conducted post-recovery. This finding is currently unresolved and has prompted a reclassification proposal currently pending before the O5 Council (see Addendum 4413-A).

ADDENDUM 4413-A:
On ██/██/2023, ink recovered from 4413-2 was found, upon playback, to depict the final ninety seconds of Dr. ██████ ██████████, a senior researcher assigned to Site-88's marine division, three days prior to Dr. ██████████'s actual death by drowning during a supply dive at the same site. The recording was discovered and reviewed by two junior staff before its contents were understood; both have been placed on administrative leave pending psychological evaluation. Dr. ██████████ had not yet been assigned to the dive at the time the ink sample was collected. The Ethics Committee has recommended immediate cessation of all ink-analysis research pending further review. The O5 Council has, as of this writing, declined to approve that recommendation.

SCP-4414.name: The Continuing Mind
SCP-4414.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Suspected SCP-4414 growth sites are to be identified via the quarterly cross-reference of Foundation burial records against regional mycological survey data. Any grave belonging to a former Foundation staff member who held Level 3 clearance or higher, or any grave within 500 meters of such a grave, is considered high-risk and is to be inspected biannually by a two-person mycology team under Site Director authorization. Confirmed SCP-4414 mycelial networks are not to be disturbed, excavated, or destroyed under any circumstances without direct authorization from the Ethics Committee and one O5 Council member, as destruction has in three documented cases produced an immediate and total discharge event (see Addendum 4414-B). Electroencephalographic monitoring equipment is not to be brought within 10 meters of a confirmed site without prior approval, as such equipment has, in two cases, appeared to draw a response.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4414 is a designation for a slow-growing subterranean fungal network, taxonomically similar to Armillaria but genetically anomalous, which develops exclusively around the decomposing brain tissue of certain human corpses. In approximately 1 in 4,000 burials meeting unknown selection criteria, mycelial threads consistent with SCP-4414 will, within 8 to 14 months of interment, form a three-dimensional structure that maps with better than 99.7% fidelity onto the deceased's cerebral connectome at time of death, as reconstructed from available medical imaging.

The resulting structure exhibits measurable, patterned electrochemical activity consistent in frequency and distribution with slow-wave, low-amplitude human neural activity, though at approximately 1/40,000th the speed of a living brain. Foundation researchers who have compared successive readings taken years apart describe the pattern as "thinking, very slowly, about very little." No confirmed instance of SCP-4414 has produced coherent output resembling language, and the phenomenon does not appear to constitute continued consciousness in any legally or ethically actionable sense — this remains a position under active internal dispute.

SCP-4414 poses no known direct physical hazard. Its risk to the Foundation is informational: individuals who die with detailed unrecorded knowledge of Foundation operations, and whose remains are not cremated, have a nonzero chance of "hosting" a structure that continues, in some unquantified sense, to hold that knowledge in a retrievable physical substrate for years or decades after death, accessible to anyone with sufficiently patient equipment and no obligation to Foundation secrecy.

ADDENDUM 4414-A:
Foundation burial policy for personnel above Level 3 clearance was revised in 1998 to mandate cremation. Prior to this policy, an estimated 340 qualifying burials occurred under Foundation jurisdiction; of these, the current locations of 58 are unknown, having occurred under civilian arrangements prior to full policy enforcement.

ADDENDUM 4414-B:
In each of the three documented destruction incidents, physical excavation of a mature SCP-4414 structure was immediately followed by a single, sharp electrochemical discharge measured at levels comparable to a grand mal seizure, propagating outward through the surrounding soil and, in one case, through the metal casing of adjacent grave markers up to 40 meters away. No injuries have resulted. The subjective experience of nearby personnel, when reported, has in all three cases been described using some variation of the phrase "like being remembered by someone you never met." This description was independently offered by seven witnesses across the three incidents who had no contact with one another prior to debriefing.

SCP-4415.name: The Boundary Kestrel
SCP-4415.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A rotating team of three ornithologists under Foundation cover (Department of Migratory Wildlife Tracking, cover identity "Continental Flyway Survey") maintains satellite tag contact with no fewer than 12 tagged SCP-4415 individuals at all times. Migration path data is transmitted directly to Site-19 Records and Information Security and is not to be published, referenced in academic literature, or cross-compared against current geopolitical projections by any staff without Level 4 clearance. Historical SCP-4415 tracking data predating Foundation involvement (1962-present, compiled from ornithological society archives) is stored in a segregated archive accessible only with dual O5 authorization, as this data has been used on at least one occasion by an external actor to correctly anticipate a Foundation-relevant border change (see Incident 4415-Kiev).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4415 is a subspecies of migratory falcon, physically indistinguishable from Falco columbarius (Merlin) except under genetic analysis, which breeds in the Arctic Circle and winters across a range spanning several continents. SCP-4415's anomalous property is confined entirely to the aggregate geometry of its migration: when the flight paths of a full breeding population are plotted together over a single migratory season, the resulting boundary lines correspond, with increasing precision the further into the future the comparison is drawn, to international political borders that do not yet exist at the time of migration.

The correspondence is not exact for borders less than approximately 15 years in the future and improves asymptotically for borders further out, reaching apparent precision for events 40-70 years distant that current cartographic and statistical methods cannot distinguish from intentional design. SCP-4415 has been tracked continuously since 1962 (opportunistically) and via tagging since 1994. Retrospective analysis of pre-1994 population data, reconstructed from museum specimens and historical birdwatcher logs, shows the same correspondence extending backward to at least 1911, correctly anticipating, among other events, the 1947 partition boundary and the 1991 dissolution boundaries of several Eastern European states, decades in advance of the political events producing them.

SCP-4415 does not appear to be influenced by, nor does it influence, the events it anticipates; no successful intervention altering a border in a manner inconsistent with contemporaneous SCP-4415 flight data has yet been documented, though the Department of Analytics maintains this is very likely a matter of insufficient attempts rather than impossibility. The mechanism by which a bird population's flight paths could encode information about future human political decisions is entirely unknown, and SCP-4415 exhibits no other anomalous property; it is not more intelligent, long-lived, or physiologically unusual than a baseline Merlin.

ADDENDUM: Incident 4415-Kiev.
In 2019, an unaffiliated academic paper analyzing publicly available SCP-4415 (referred to in the paper by its zoological designation only) migration data was found to have, several months prior to a significant regional border adjustment, correctly forecast the adjustment's approximate location to within 40 kilometers. The paper's author has since been placed under Foundation observation; there is no indication the author is aware of the anomaly's significance, believing the correlation to be either coincidental or evidence of an undiscovered ecological sensitivity to infrastructure development. This belief is not being corrected.

SCP-4416.name: The Committee Warren
SCP-4416.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The SCP-4416 colony is maintained in a climate-controlled subterranean enclosure at Site-██, replicated as closely as possible to its original burrow system (located beneath ████████████, ██████, and excavated in full in 1989). No individual member of SCP-4416 is to be removed, injured, or allowed to die of unnatural causes; the colony's population and internal hierarchy are to be observed exclusively through remote camera and passive acoustic monitoring. Feeding, cleaning, and enclosure maintenance are performed by a rotating team of three handlers who have no knowledge of the current composition or recent activity of the O5 Council and are debriefed and reassigned to unrelated duties every 90 days to prevent pattern recognition. Any handler who independently notices and reports a correlation between colony events and Council activity is to be commended, reassigned, and monitored for a period of no less than one year.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4416 is a colony of eusocial mole-rats (Heterocephalus glaber, naked mole-rat) numbering, as of the most recent count, 91 individuals, distinguished from baseline populations of the species by an internal social hierarchy consisting of exactly thirteen non-breeding "senior" workers who occupy fixed positions within the colony's tunnel architecture and exhibit behavioral patterns — including dominance displays, coalition formation, and turn-taking in defensive and foraging leadership roles — that do not correspond to any documented naked mole-rat social structure.

Cross-referencing of colony records against the (redacted at time of writing) membership and internal activity of the O5 Council, conducted retroactively in 1994 following an unrelated behavioral study, revealed a correspondence exceeding 97% between changes in the colony's thirteen-member senior hierarchy — including replacement following the death or incapacitation of a senior individual, contested succession events, and reordering of apparent seniority — and equivalent changes within the Council, with a mean lag of 6.4 days between the colony event and the corresponding, subsequently confirmed, Council event. In eleven documented cases, the colony event preceded the Council event by a margin large enough to constitute foreknowledge.

The mechanism is entirely unknown. SCP-4416 has no possible sensory or informational access to Council composition, which is itself among the Foundation's most closely guarded categories of information; no communication channel, conventional or anomalous, has been identified. The colony was discovered accidentally, and its correspondence with the Council was itself discovered accidentally, by researchers who did not hold sufficient clearance to know what they were looking at until after the correlation had already been formally reported up the chain.

The primary containment concern is not the colony's behavior, which is otherwise unremarkable, but the informational hazard the correspondence represents: any party capable of covertly observing SCP-4416's senior hierarchy gains predictive access to Council composition roughly a week in advance, including, per the eleven anticipatory cases, apparent foreknowledge of Council member deaths. The Council has, to date, declined three separate proposals to euthanize the colony, cull its senior tier, or otherwise disrupt the correspondence experimentally.

ADDENDUM:
On the two occasions when the senior hierarchy showed sudden, unexplained turnover outside of any observed death or incapacitation within the colony (2009, 2021), no corresponding Council change occurred. Both instances remain unresolved. The Council has requested no further inquiry into these two discrepancies.

SCP-4417.name: The Inherited Tongue
SCP-4417.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known carriers of SCP-4417 (currently 6 individuals, designated 4417-1 through 4417-6, all Foundation personnel infected prior to identification of the anomaly) are housed at Site-77 under standard biological monitoring conditions and are permitted to continue limited administrative duties under supervision. SCP-4417 is not transmissible through air, food, or water; transmission requires direct exchange of bodily fluid, typically via medical procedure, open wound contact, or bite. All carriers are informed of their status and have signed Foundation Biological Containment Agreements restricting physical contact with uninfected personnel. Blood and tissue samples from carriers are stored at Bio-Site-12 under standard Class II pathogen protocols. Speech produced by a carrier during an episode (see Description) is to be transcribed by attending staff but is not to be treated as a statement of Foundation record, per Ethics Committee ruling EC-4417-1.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4417 is a gram-negative bacterium, provisionally classified within genus Bartonella but genetically divergent from all catalogued species, which establishes a chronic, asymptomatic, non-fatal infection in human hosts. Infection confers a minor but consistent benefit: measurable resistance to several common bacterial and fungal toxins, including a documented case of survived exposure to a dose of amatoxin that should have been fatal. This benefit was the means by which SCP-4417 was first isolated, during investigation of an anomalous mushroom poisoning survival.

The anomalous property of SCP-4417 is behavioral. Approximately once every 10-40 days, a carrier will experience an "episode" lasting between four and twenty minutes, during which their speech patterns, vocabulary, characteristic phrases, and — per voice stress analysis — vocal cadence shift to closely match those of a previous human host of the same bacterial lineage. Carriers report no memory of episode content and typically describe the experience as "blacking out" or "losing the thread," though they remain conscious, responsive, and capable of complex action throughout.

Genetic sequencing of the bacterial population within a given carrier can be used to construct an approximate lineage of previous hosts, extending in the longest traced case (4417-3) across an estimated eleven previous carriers spanning approximately 140 years, the earliest identifiable by episode content referencing verifiably historical events and using vocabulary and idiom consistent with early 20th-century regional dialect, despite 4417-3 having no known exposure to such speech patterns.

It is not established whether episodes represent genuine transfer of memory, learned behavioral mimicry encoded somehow at the bacterial level, or an unrelated phenomenon coincidentally correlated with infection. Carriers have, across documented episodes, provided verifiably accurate personal information belonging to deceased previous hosts unknown to the current carrier by any conventional means, including one instance in which 4417-2, during an episode, correctly stated the bank account number and safety deposit box location of a previous host who had died 34 years prior, information subsequently verified by surviving family members contacted independently.

ADDENDUM:
4417-6, infected via workplace injury in 2019, has begun, during recent episodes, using vocabulary and phrasing consistent with no previous identified host, but instead anticipating, in one reviewed case, information about a Foundation incident that had not yet occurred at the time of the episode. This finding has not been replicated and is not currently considered established.

SCP-4418.name: The Deep Listening Sponge
SCP-4418.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Living SCP-4418 colonies identified at confirmed wreck sites are not to be disturbed, harvested, or relocated without a standing request approved by the Maritime Recovery Division and countersigned by a Level 4 archivist. Harvested tissue samples are stored in refrigerated saline at Site-64's marine archive in sealed, individually logged containers; each sample's chemical "readout" (see Description) is to be transcribed by a two-person team, one of whom must not personally know the identity of the individual whose final thoughts are believed to be recorded, in order to reduce interviewer bias in transcription. Recordings and transcriptions of SCP-4418 readouts are classified at the same level as the incident that produced the source material and are subject to the Foundation's standard grief-disclosure restrictions; next-of-kin notification is prohibited except where separately authorized under Foundation Humanitarian Protocol 12.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4418 refers to colonies of a deep-water sponge species, morphologically similar to genus Hyalonema (glass sponge) but chemically anomalous, found exclusively within 300 meters of confirmed shipwreck or drowning sites less than approximately 80 years old. SCP-4418 tissue, when processed using a proprietary Foundation extraction method developed from declassified 1970s chemical-signal research, yields a legible "readout": a linear sequence of extracted biochemical markers that, when algorithmically translated (current translation fidelity approximately 71%, per Site-64 Analytics), corresponds to coherent verbal content consistent with the final conscious thoughts of a human being who died by drowning within the sponge colony's effective radius and within roughly six months of the colony's growth at that location.

The mechanism by which a filter-feeding sponge could encode discrete verbal cognitive content, particularly given the absence of any known neural tissue in the phylum, is entirely unresolved. SCP-4418 does not appear to actively seek out drowning events, grow preferentially near them, or exhibit any other behavior distinguishing it from baseline deep-water sponges apart from the readout property; colonies have been found at wreck sites with no possibility of surviving drowning victims (total submersion, extreme depth) and have still produced content consistent with the final thoughts of crew members who died elsewhere aboard the same vessel before it sank, suggesting the mechanism is not purely proximity-based.

Recovered content is overwhelmingly mundane: readouts most frequently consist of fragments of ordinary, unremarkable thought (recollections of unrelated errands, repeated fragments of songs, worry about unrelated minor obligations) rather than anything resembling final words, insight, or resolution, a finding that has proven distressing to Foundation personnel involved in transcription work, three of whom have requested reassignment following extended exposure.

Foundation interest in SCP-4418 is primarily historical-intelligence: readouts recovered near several vessels of interest have provided corroborating detail for otherwise unverifiable historical incidents, including confirmation of the presence of an unlisted passenger aboard the ███████████, sunk in 1954, whose readout content included personal information later cross-verified against unrelated Foundation records, prompting a minor but still-unresolved revision to that incident's official file.

ADDENDUM:
Harvesting of SCP-4418 for non-essential research purposes was suspended in 2020 following an internal review characterizing the practice, in the words of the reviewing ethicist, as "listening in on people's dying thoughts for information we mostly do not need." The suspension remains in effect for all requests below Priority 2.

SCP-4419.name: The Detached Instant
SCP-4419.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4419 individuals (currently 2 living specimens, designated 4419-1 and 4419-2) are housed in a standard reptile enclosure at Site-64. Shed skins produced by either specimen (see Description) are to be collected within one hour of shedding using non-conductive tools, placed in individually labeled transparent containers, and stored in the SCP-4419 skin archive, currently holding 118 catalogued specimens. Archive containers must permit unobstructed observation, as several catalogued skins remain in continuous motion and unrestrained containment could result in loss. Skins that have ceased motion for a period exceeding 6 months may be reclassified as inert and transferred to standard biological storage following review.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4419 designates a small population of gecko, physically unremarkable and taxonomically unclassifiable beyond family Gekkonidae, whose shed skins retain coordinated, apparently voluntary movement for a period ranging from several days to (in one case, ongoing) over eleven years following separation from the living animal. A freshly shed SCP-4419 skin will, without exception observed to date, continue performing whatever specific action the animal was engaged in at the moment of shedding — walking a fixed route, consuming a specific prey item, climbing a particular surface — in a repeating loop, with no apparent awareness that the skin is no longer attached to a body, functioning organs, or a nervous system in any conventional sense.

The skins exhibit no measurable neural or muscular tissue beyond ordinary keratinized epidermis; standard veterinary and biophysical instrumentation detects no mechanism capable of producing directed movement. Motion gradually degrades in complexity and fidelity over time — early-stage skins perform the original action with near-perfect accuracy, while advanced-stage skins (over 5 years post-shedding) exhibit only a simplified, repetitive approximation, described by handling staff as resembling "the shape of the memory of walking" rather than walking itself — before eventually, in all but two catalogued cases, ceasing motion entirely.

The two exceptions (Skin-004, shed by a wild-caught specimen prior to Foundation acquisition, and Skin-058) have shown no measurable decline in motion fidelity across 9 and 6 years of continuous observation respectively. Both continue to perform their original action — Skin-004 a specific eleven-step foraging sequence, Skin-058 a defensive threat display — with reportedly undiminished precision, a finding staff have been unable to explain given the total absence of any biological substrate that would typically be required to sustain motor precision over such a period.

No SCP-4419 skin has ever performed an action other than the one the animal was engaged in at the moment of shedding, and no skin has shown any response to external stimuli, including direct physical contact, predator scent, or attempts at feeding.

ADDENDUM:
Skin-004 was, for a period of approximately 3 years prior to reclassification of its containment tier, mistaken by two separate incoming research staff for a living specimen, owing to the precision and apparent purposefulness of its movement. Both staff members reported the subsequent correction as "more unsettling than the original mistake."

SCP-4420.name: The Inherited Shadow
SCP-4420.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
A live SCP-4420 breeding population is maintained under Biosafety Level 2 conditions at Site-77 for study purposes only; no specimen is to be permitted contact with unauthorized personnel. Any Foundation staff member confirmed bitten by an SCP-4420 specimen is to be placed under Shadow Monitoring Protocol 4420, consisting of weekly photographic documentation of the affected individual's shadow under standardized lighting conditions, for no less than five years following the bite. Affected personnel are not to be informed of the specific nature of the anomaly prior to onset of Stage 2 symptoms (see Description) unless clinically necessary, per Ethics Committee guidance intended to prevent anticipatory psychological distress.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4420 is a tick species, morphologically consistent with genus Ixodes but of undetermined specific classification, whose bite produces a slow-onset anomalous effect in human hosts affecting the visual properties of the host's own cast shadow. The effect progresses in three documented stages. In Stage 1 (average onset 3-8 months post-bite), the host's shadow begins to deviate marginally from expected geometry under controlled lighting — proportions shift by small but measurable degrees, inconsistent with the host's actual body shape. In Stage 2 (average onset 14-20 months post-bite), the shadow's deviations stabilize into a consistent alternate silhouette, differing from the host's own in ways such as height, posture, apparent limb length, or in one case, apparent presence of long hair on a bald host. In Stage 3, reached in 4 of 9 confirmed cases to date, the shadow demonstrates movement independent of the host's own motion, with lags or divergences of up to several seconds, on one occasion moving in direct contradiction to the host's simultaneous physical action.

Genetic and historical analysis of confirmed cases indicates that the Stage 2 silhouette consistently and specifically matches the physical characteristics of the tick specimen's previous host, as determined by engorgement analysis and, where available, prior host records. SCP-4420 specimens appear capable of surviving for extended dormant periods (the longest confirmed interval between feedings is 11 years), and the "inherited" silhouette effect has, in every traceable case, corresponded to a previous host now deceased.

The mechanism producing this effect remains unknown; no anomalous property has been detected in host blood, skin, or ocular tissue sufficient to account for an alteration in the optical behavior of cast shadows, which is not, under standard physics, a property that can be locally modified by biological means. The Department of Analytics has noted, without further explanation offered, that shadows affected by SCP-4420 continue to obey standard laws of light and occlusion in every other respect; only the shape cast is affected.

ADDENDUM:
Case 4420-7 reached Stage 3 in month 19. The affected researcher, per standard protocol, was not informed of Stage 2 onset in advance and reported first noticing the change personally, describing the sensation as "watching someone else stretch in a mirror that's a second behind me, except it isn't a mirror." The researcher has requested, and been granted, continued assignment to the case.

SCP-4421.name: The Kin Graft
SCP-4421.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
The SCP-4421 breeding population (14 individuals) is maintained in a standard amphibian containment facility at Site-64. Any research requiring induced limb loss for study of the regeneration anomaly must be approved in advance by the Ethics Committee, which as of 2021 requires that the nearest living human blood relative of any staff member who owns or handles a specimen be informed, in general terms, of the theoretical possibility that their own tissue could be anomalously implicated, and given the option to have that specimen reassigned to a handler with no living relatives, per Policy 4421-Rev.2. No specimen is to be assigned to a handler whose closest living relative has not consented to this disclosure.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4421 designates a population of salamander, physically resembling Ambystoma mexicanum (axolotl) but genetically distinct, exhibiting standard axolotl-like limb regeneration following amputation or loss, with one anomalous deviation: regenerated tissue is, upon genetic analysis, found to match not the specimen's own genome, nor that of any other SCP-4421 individual, but rather the genome of the nearest living human blood relative of whichever person most recently handled the specimen prior to the limb loss, regardless of that relative's physical distance from the specimen or awareness of its existence.

"Nearest" is determined by standard genetic relatedness coefficients and is not affected by legal relationship, degree of personal closeness, or geographic separation; in one documented case, regenerated tissue matched the genome of a biological half-sibling given up for adoption in infancy and unknown to the handler at the time of the incident, a relationship only confirmed after the fact through separate genetic testing requested by Foundation researchers attempting to identify the tissue source. The relative in question need not be informed of, aware of, or in any way connected to the regeneration event for the match to occur, and no case has yet involved a relative who was aware of the connection prior to Foundation contact.

Regenerated limbs are otherwise functionally unremarkable and fully integrated into the specimen's body without rejection or other complication. In three documented cases, the human relative whose genetic profile was matched has independently reported an unexplained, temporary sensation — described variously as tingling, phantom pressure, or "someone else's hand" — localized to the corresponding limb, occurring within a window of several hours surrounding the regeneration event, despite having no knowledge of the specimen, the handler, or the Foundation. These reports were obtained via discreet follow-up contact conducted under cover identity and have not been formally corroborated through controlled testing, as doing so would require disclosure inconsistent with current containment policy.

The biological mechanism enabling identification of, and tissue synthesis matching, a specific living human at potentially unlimited distance is entirely unknown and represents, per internal Foundation assessment, one of the more troubling open questions in current SCP-4421 research, given its implications for the theoretical limits of anomalous biological information transfer.

ADDENDUM:
Following the 2021 policy revision, four handlers requested reassignment upon learning of the disclosure requirement. One handler, upon learning their nearest living relative was an estranged parent, requested to continue handling regardless, stating this was "the only contact we're going to have."

SCP-4422.name: The Testifying Whale
SCP-4422.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Foundation vessels operating in confirmed SCP-4422 range are required to maintain continuous passive acoustic monitoring and to report all recorded vocalizations to Site-████'s Cetacean Acoustics division within 24 hours. All recordings are classified upon receipt, pending reverse-playback analysis (see Description). Any recording found upon analysis to contain content implicating an identifiable living person or currently operating organization is escalated immediately to the Foundation Legal-Anomalous Liaison Office and is not to be referenced, discussed, or duplicated outside that office without O5 authorization. Fishing, whale-watching, and research vessels operating in affected waters are, where possible, discouraged from underwater audio recording through non-anomalous means (permit restriction, area closure under environmental pretext).

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4422 designates a small, distinct population of baleen whale, taxonomically closest to Balaenoptera physalus (fin whale) but bioacoustically anomalous, whose long-form vocalizations ("songs"), when digitally recorded and played in reverse at approximately 0.6x normal speed, resolve into intelligible spoken testimony in a human language appropriate to the whale's current geographic location, describing, in first person, specific acts of harm committed against SCP-4422 individuals or other marine life by named human individuals, vessels, or organizations.

Testimony content has, in 34 of 41 analyzed recordings to date, been independently corroborated by Foundation investigation as factually accurate, including precise vessel names, registration numbers, dates, and locations later confirmed through unrelated maritime records — information a whale has no plausible means of obtaining through any known sensory or communicative channel. Content frequently implicates ongoing commercial fishing operations, illegal dumping, and, in six cases, activity by entities with documented prior Foundation-adjacent interest, a finding that has significantly elevated the classification's priority.

The mechanism by which SCP-4422 could acquire, encode, and vocalize detailed testimonial information regarding specific human wrongdoing — including information about events the whale population could not have directly witnessed, such as boardroom decisions preceding a documented illegal dumping incident — is entirely unknown. SCP-4422 exhibits no other anomalous property and cannot be reliably distinguished from baseline fin whales without genetic or acoustic analysis.

The Foundation's central concern is not the anomaly itself but its potential exposure: recordings of SCP-4422 vocalizations exist in unknown quantity outside Foundation control, having been captured incidentally by commercial shipping, oceanographic research, and recreational recording equipment for decades prior to Foundation identification of the phenomenon in 2016. No public reverse-playback discovery has yet occurred, a state of affairs the Department of Analytics attributes to reasonable luck rather than any structural safeguard, given that the reversal technique required to reveal testimonial content is neither complex nor proprietary.

ADDENDUM:
On three occasions, testimony content has referenced specific future actions the implicated party had not yet taken but subsequently did, phrased in the same past-tense testimonial structure as historical content. The Legal-Anomalous Liaison Office has requested clarification from the Ethics Committee regarding the Foundation's obligations, if any, in cases where SCP-4422 testimony describes harm that has not yet occurred. No formal guidance has been issued.

SCP-4423.name: The Succession Brood
SCP-4423.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
All known SCP-4423 breeding sites (currently 4, located within a 200-kilometer radius of ██████████) are under continuous soil-vibration monitoring to detect nymph activity, which precedes emergence by approximately 60-90 days. Detected activity is to be reported directly and exclusively to the O5 Council liaison office; no intermediate staff, including Site Directors, are to be briefed on monitoring results without explicit Council authorization. Personnel assigned to SCP-4423 monitoring duties are selected from staff with no access to O5 Council biographical or medical information and are rotated off the assignment immediately upon any change in emergence-cycle status, to prevent cumulative pattern awareness. This document's Description section is itself restricted to Level 5 clearance; the standard Level 4 file for SCP-4423 describes only an anomalous, non-periodical cicada species of unresolved emergence pattern.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4423 is a cicada species, morphologically consistent with genus Magicicada but diverging from the genus's characteristic prime-numbered (13- or 17-year) emergence cycles. Instead, each of the four known SCP-4423 broods emerges, without exception across 118 years of retrospectively reconstructed records (via layered soil core sampling and regional historical documentation), within a window of 0 to 11 days surrounding the death, by any cause, of a sitting member of the O5 Council, with each of the four broods appearing to correspond consistently to one specific Council seat rather than to the Council as a body — that is, Brood-A has, in every traceable instance, emerged around the death of whichever individual most recently held one particular seat, and not around the deaths of individuals holding other seats.

This correspondence was first identified in 1971 following a retrospective audit prompted by an unrelated entomological survey, and has since been confirmed for 7 of 8 known Council deaths occurring within the retrospective and prospective monitoring period (1958-present); the eighth death, that of a Council member who died by means the Foundation has not disclosed even within this document, occurred without a corresponding emergence, a discrepancy that remains formally unresolved and is treated internally as more concerning than the correspondence itself, as it implies the mechanism is neither purely coincidental nor perfectly reliable.

No mechanism has been identified by which a cicada population's multi-year subterranean development could be synchronized to the death of a specific individual holding a specific, itself heavily compartmentalized institutional role. Cicada nymphs of SCP-4423 broods show no known method of receiving external information during their subterranean development period, and the seats in question have, across the retrospective sample, been held by biologically unrelated individuals of varying ages, health status, and cause of death, eliminating straightforward biological or genealogical explanations.

Foundation policy since 1994 has explicitly prohibited use of SCP-4423 emergence monitoring for any predictive or operational purpose relating to Council succession planning, a prohibition the Ethics Committee has twice reaffirmed following unconfirmed reports that the prohibition was not being fully observed at the Council level.

ADDENDUM:
Brood-D entered active nymph vibration activity on ██/██/2026, consistent with emergence in approximately 60-90 days. This document has been updated accordingly.

SCP-4424.name: The Last Reading
SCP-4424.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
Cultivation of SCP-4424 is authorized exclusively within the Archive Preservation Wing of Site-01, under direct joint authority of the Records and Information Security Administration and the O5 Council liaison office. Specimens are trained via standard espalier technique onto physical document storage racks designated for condemned material (items scheduled for destruction, redaction beyond recovery, or transfer outside Foundation control). No SCP-4424 fruit is to be consumed without a standing Level 5 authorization specific to the individual document targeted, logged in the Archive Zero ledger, and witnessed by no fewer than two Council-cleared staff. Unauthorized cultivation, transport, or possession of SCP-4424 cuttings outside the Preservation Wing is treated as a Class-3 security breach.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4424 is a climbing vine species, morphologically similar to genus Hedera (ivy) but anomalous in growth behavior and fruiting cycle, first identified growing unassisted through the shelving of a condemned records annex scheduled for demolition in 1988. SCP-4424 does not fruit on a seasonal or age-based cycle; instead, it produces a single fruit, resembling a small dark fig, only when a specific physical document it has grown in direct contact with is within approximately 72 hours of scheduled permanent destruction, redaction beyond later recovery, or unrecoverable loss, and will not fruit under any other circumstance observed to date, including deliberate attempts to simulate destruction conditions without genuine intent to destroy the document.

Consumption of an SCP-4424 fruit produces, in the consumer, a complete and highly detailed sensory impression of having personally read the source document in full, including exact wording, marginalia, physical condition, and, in several cases, contextual details not present in the document's text but apparently inferred or absorbed alongside it (the physical sensation of the room in which the document was originally filed; in one case, a fragment of a conversation that occurred near the document decades prior to any known recording of it). This impression persists as an ordinary long-term memory indistinguishable, per extensive testing, from a genuinely read document, and does not fade, degrade, or misremember at a rate different from baseline human memory.

SCP-4424 was reclassified Thaumiel in 1997 following Foundation recognition of its use in preserving otherwise-unrecoverable information: material condemned to destruction under standing Foundation retention limits, court order, containment breach, or political necessity can, if grown in contact with SCP-4424 for a minimum of 90 days prior to destruction, be "read" by a designated Archive Zero custodian and its content thereby preserved, off any physical or digital record, within a single human memory, indefinitely.

The primary cost of this preservation method is total: the custodian cannot selectively forget, cannot transfer the memory to any other person or medium by any means yet identified, and cannot be relieved of the memory except by their own death. As of the most recent audit, 61 living Archive Zero custodians collectively hold the complete content of 61 documents the Foundation has, by design, no other copy of anywhere in the world.

ADDENDUM:
Custodian designation is voluntary. The current waiting list for custodianship, maintained separately from this file, holds 340 names.

SCP-4425.name: The Man Who Signs Everything
SCP-4425.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4425 is housed in a standard personnel quarters at Site-19 under the cover assignment of "contract archivist, Records Reconciliation Division." He retains standard site privileges but is prohibited from signing any document, form, receipt, or log without a Level 3 witness present, and is never to be left alone with a writing instrument and blank paper for longer than sixty seconds. Any document bearing SCP-4425's signature discovered during routine archival digitization is to be flagged, photographed, dated by all available means (paper analysis, ink chromatography, provenance chain), and forwarded to the Archive Zero Liaison Office regardless of the document's ostensible age or subject matter.
SCP-4425 signs a witnessed control sheet each morning. Any deviation between the control signature and a newly discovered historical signature is to be logged but is not, at present, actionable; no method of preventing new appearances has been identified. SCP-4425 is barred from all sub-levels housing Archive Zero material.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4425 is a 44-year-old man, formerly employed as a municipal records clerk prior to Foundation recruitment. His signature — a specific cursive rendering of his legal name, distinguished by a consistent leftward hook on the terminal letter and a measurable, idiosyncratic pressure pattern — has been located on 61 Foundation-related documents dated between 1891 and the present, including requisition forms, decommission orders, budget ratifications, and, in three instances, internal correspondence referencing material held in Archive Zero.
SCP-4425 has no memory of signing any document he did not personally witness being signed. Graphological and forensic ink analysis confirms in all 61 cases that the signature is not a forgery, trace, or copy: it exhibits the same micro-tremor and pen-lift pattern present in his current handwriting, a pattern graphologists state is effectively unfalsifiable and typically stable only across a single living hand.
The appearances are not static. Re-photography of previously catalogued documents has on four occasions shown the signing party changed between examinations — an illegible or different name in an earlier photograph replaced by SCP-4425's signature in a later one, with no record of the physical document having been altered, reprinted, or removed from its sealed folder. In each case, the signature appears at the precise point in the document where an authorizing or witnessing signature was procedurally required, regardless of who held that authority at the time the document was originally executed.
SCP-4425 has passed all administered polygraph and cognitive-verification testing consistent with genuine ignorance of the phenomenon.

ADDENDUM 4425-1: Interview excerpt, conducted by Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes.
Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes: Do you remember signing anything for us before you were hired?
SCP-4425: No. I didn't work here. I was in Records and Assessment for the city, water permits mostly.
Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes: Does the number 1891 mean anything to you?
SCP-4425: No. Why would it.
Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes: We found your signature on a requisition form dated to that year.
SCP-4425: That's not possible. I'm not that old.
Dr. Okonkwo-Reyes: We're aware.
SCP-4425: [long pause] I don't like signing things anymore. I haven't signed a birthday card in three years. I make my wife do it.

ADDENDUM 4425-2: One document bearing SCP-4425's signature, discovered during Archive Zero cataloguing under Director-level clearance, authorizes an unspecified "founding transfer" and predates any confirmed record of the Foundation's existence under any known name. O5 Council has classified further discussion of this document's contents pending review. It remains unclear whether SCP-4425 is a downstream symptom of Archive Zero's contents or one of its conditions of origin.

SCP-4426.name: The Deathbed Clerk
SCP-4426.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4426 resides in a private suite at Site-19 furnished to resemble a modest hospice office. He is permitted supervised movement within the Pastoral and End-of-Life Services wing, which the Foundation maintains for terminal D-class personnel and, in select cases, retired or injured staff who elect Foundation hospice care over external facilities. SCP-4426 is not to be introduced to any dying individual without a standing request approved at Level 4, given the operational value and ethical hazard of his effect.
SCP-4426 must be supplied only with paper from a controlled stock (Ledger Stock 4426-A); documents completed on any other paper do not produce the anomalous effect. All completed forms are to be sealed and stored in the Vital Status Archive under continuous monitoring, as the forms themselves appear to retain some property associated with the delay described below.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4426 is a 61-year-old man, formerly an ordained hospice chaplain, recruited following an incident in which a terminal patient under his care remained in a stable, undying physiological state for eleven days past the point at which death was, by every clinical measure, already underway.
When SCP-4426 is present at the death of an individual, that individual's transition from "dying" to "dead" does not complete in the usual sense. The body ceases purposeful movement and awareness consistent with clinical death, but does not begin rigor mortis, livor mortis, or measurable decomposition; in approximately 40% of cases, minimal, non-recovering EEG activity persists at levels otherwise associated with deep anesthesia. This state — internally termed "unsettled" by hospice staff prior to Foundation involvement — continues indefinitely until SCP-4426 completes a specific form of his own design, handwritten on Ledger Stock 4426-A, and reads a closing line aloud to the body. Upon doing so, death completes within seconds, sometimes accompanied by a delayed onset of the physiological changes that should have already occurred.
SCP-4426 states he does not know why this happens and did not knowingly design the form to have this effect; he has used a version of it since early in his career "because it felt right," predating any known anomalous incident. He reports finding the effect, once he became aware of it, "obscene," and has on two occasions refused to complete the form for days at a time, both times under duress from Foundation staff citing operational necessity.

ADDENDUM: The Foundation has, with O5 authorization, used SCP-4426's effect on six occasions to delay the legal death of interrogation subjects or dying personnel possessing time-sensitive information, extending the unsettled state to permit continued, if severely limited, communication. Ethics Committee objections are on permanent record and have been overruled in each instance. SCP-4426 was not informed of the intended use in advance in four of the six cases.

Interview excerpt, Dr. Palmer, following Incident 4426-3:
Dr. Palmer: You understand why we needed the delay.
SCP-4426: I understand why you wanted it. He was still in there. I could tell. You don't get to decide that's convenient.
Dr. Palmer: We're not asking your permission retroactively.
SCP-4426: No. You never do. That's the part I can't make peace with — that it isn't a request, it's just something I happen to be able to do, and you use it because I can.

SCP-4426 has since requested reassignment away from active-duty personnel. The request remains under review.

SCP-4427.name: The Measure
SCP-4427.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4427 is housed in a self-contained habitat within Site-██, constructed at a fixed distance of 340 meters from the Archive Zero vault door, a distance determined through the calibration procedure described below. The habitat is fitted with full medical monitoring, and SCP-4427's apparent physiological age is to be recorded every six hours. Any deviation of more than 18 months of apparent age within a 24-hour period is to be reported immediately to the Archive Zero Liaison Office, as this has historically preceded changes in Archive Zero's internal state.
Access to SCP-4427 is restricted to Level 4 medical staff and designated Archive Zero personnel. Under no circumstances is SCP-4427 to be moved without a written order co-signed by two O5 Council members, given that any change in her distance from the vault produces an immediate and currently unpredictable shift in her physiological age. SCP-4427 has not been informed, and is not to be informed, of the reason for her placement.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4427 is a woman whose apparent physiological age varies as an inverse function of her distance from the Archive Zero vault door. At the vault threshold, SCP-4427 regresses toward late infancy over a period of hours; at approximately 1.2 kilometers, she ages toward apparent senescence and physiological death within a comparable window. Between these extremes, her apparent age moves along a continuous curve that is not fixed — recalibration has been required eleven times since her acquisition, as the distance corresponding to any given apparent age shifts gradually over months, in a pattern the Archive Zero Liaison Office has, since 1988, cross-referenced against undisclosed internal readings from the vault itself.
SCP-4427 was acquired as an infant in 1961 under circumstances the Foundation's own records describe only as "family relocated; compensation issued." No further detail on her biological origin, or on why her physiology is linked to Archive Zero specifically, has been recovered, including from personnel present at her acquisition, several of whom no longer hold clearance to discuss it and one of whom is deceased.
SCP-4427 is, at her current stabilized distance, chronologically 65 years old and physiologically consistent with a woman in her late thirties. She has lived her entire remembered life inside varying radii of a door she has never been permitted to see.

ADDENDUM: In 2019, a containment breach elsewhere at Site-██ resulted in SCP-4427's habitat losing power for six hours, during which her position relative to the vault could not be confirmed by automated systems. Physical inspection found her apparent age had not changed, but medical staff reported she had, for the first time on record, asked a direct question: "Is it close." No further elaboration was obtained. The Archive Zero Liaison Office has since flagged this incident for review at O5 discretion, noting that SCP-4427 should have no means of perceiving the vault's proximity independent of her own body. Liaison staff have separately noted that the interval between required recalibrations has been shortening: roughly fourteen months elapsed between the first and second recalibrations, while under five months separated the tenth from the eleventh, a trend the Office has not yet explained and has declined to speculate on in writing.

SCP-4428.name: The Council's Memory
SCP-4428.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4428 is housed in a private apartment within the O5 Command Annex, a location whose existence is itself classified above Level 4. She holds standing authorization to be present, unescorted, at any O5 Council session she is summoned to. No session at which SCP-4428 is present may be recorded by any other means; her attendance is understood by all thirteen Council members to substitute for formal minutes in matters too sensitive to commit to any retrievable record.
SCP-4428 is prohibited from initiating contact with any Council member outside of a summoned session, and from disclosing the content of any session to any party, including other Council members, except when a majority of the currently sitting Council jointly requests a specific recollection. She is permitted no recording devices, correspondence, or unsupervised communication with Foundation personnel outside her designated household staff, themselves under standing nondisclosure sanction.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4428 is a woman of documented age 52, employed by the Foundation for 24 years in her current capacity. Any O5 Council member who converses with her in person retains no memory of the conversation, nor of her presence, beyond approximately 24 hours; this amnesia is total, extending to physical evidence such as notes the Council member may have taken, which the member subsequently does not recognize as their own handwriting despite forensic confirmation that it is.
SCP-4428 herself is unaffected. She retains complete, apparently perfect recall of every conversation she has attended since her assignment began, including the content of decisions later reversed, denied, or omitted from the Council's official record. She has, on 340 recorded occasions, been consulted by the Council collectively to resolve disputes about what was previously agreed upon, functioning as the only continuous, accurate record of the Council's actual deliberations — as distinct from its official minutes, which are compiled independently and do not consistently match her account.
The mechanism producing selective amnesia in Council members specifically, and not in other Foundation personnel who interact with SCP-4428 in an unrelated capacity, has not been identified despite extensive testing. SCP-4428 has stated she does not know why she remembers or why they do not, and has described the arrangement, when asked directly, as "the job."

ADDENDUM: SCP-4428 has never requested reassignment, retirement, or disclosure of her situation to any outside party, and Foundation psychological staff assigned to her welfare have noted, across successive annual reviews, a marked and consistent decline in her willingness to discuss her life prior to Foundation employment. Her personnel file prior to year 12 of her assignment has been sealed at O5 discretion. It is not known whether she has ever been asked whether she wishes to continue in this role.
In 2022, following the death of a sitting Council member, SCP-4428 was, for the first time in her assignment, asked directly by the incoming replacement to describe her predecessor's final weeks in office — a conversation the replacement subsequently had no memory of initiating, and later reintroduced himself to SCP-4428 as though the two had never met.

SCP-4429.name: The Unrepeatable Likeness
SCP-4429.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4429 is housed in standard personnel quarters at Site-19. All photography, filming, sketching, painting, or other visual depiction of SCP-4429 is strictly prohibited except under controlled testing conditions authorized by the Photographic Anomalies Unit. SCP-4429 is issued a written advisory to be carried at all times, informing any personnel who encounter her that depicting her likeness by any means is forbidden, as incidental phone photography by visiting or transferred staff unfamiliar with her file has been the leading cause of containment testing to date.
Any image inadvertently created of SCP-4429 is to be reported immediately; the Foundation has developed no reliable method to prevent the resulting transference (described below) once an image exists, though rapid destruction of the image within approximately ninety seconds of creation has, in four of seven recorded cases, prevented the effect from completing.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4429 is a 33-year-old woman who cannot be accurately visually depicted by any means. Photographs, video, and hand-rendered images of her subject invariably depict, instead, an accurate likeness of a real, specific, and previously uninvolved individual located elsewhere, whose location cannot be predicted in advance and whose identity is unknown until independently traced.
Approximately 45 to 90 seconds after such an image is completed, the depicted stranger — regardless of distance, and with no known upper limit demonstrated to date — involuntarily assumes, for a period of several seconds to roughly one minute, the exact posture, facial expression, and apparent emotional affect shown in the image, with no memory of the episode afterward. Subjects located and interviewed post-incident uniformly describe the experience as a brief, disorienting "blankness," and none have reported distress beyond mild confusion, though the Foundation has classified the long-term cumulative risk to repeatedly-targeted individuals as unknown.
SCP-4429 has never met, and has no traceable connection to, any of the eleven strangers identified to date as recipients of her transferred likeness. No pattern linking the recipients (geography, appearance, occupation, or otherwise) has been established.

ADDENDUM: SCP-4429 has requested, on separate occasions, that the Foundation "just let someone take one," stating that she wants to know "what happens to them, really, not just what we can prove." This request has been denied on ethical and containment grounds. She keeps no mirrors in her quarters by personal choice, unrelated to any anomalous effect; standard mirrors reflect her normally. She has stated this is not for any reason the Foundation would write down.
Foundation researchers have noted that the eleven identified recipients, considered together, form no coherent demographic pattern by geography, age, appearance, or occupation. Three have since been placed under passive, non-intrusive monitoring at the Ethics Committee's recommendation, a precaution intended to track any cumulative effect of repeated involuntary transference; SCP-4429 has not been informed that this monitoring exists, or that any of the eleven have been identified at all.

SCP-4430.name: The Borrowed Biography
SCP-4430.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4430's physical form is housed in a standard containment cell at Site-19; her personnel/subject file (designated SCP-4430-File) is stored separately in a single hardcopy original within a sealed reading room, Site-19 Sub-level 3. The file may not be digitized, photocopied, or transcribed by hand in full; partial summaries prepared by cleared personnel for administrative purposes are permitted provided the preparer has read no more than one page at a time with a mandatory ten-minute cooldown between pages.
Any individual who reads SCP-4430-File is to be quarantined for observation for no less than six hours following completion of reading, and is to be interviewed by a psychologist unfamiliar with SCP-4430 prior to release, to confirm resolution of the effect described below. SCP-4430 herself is permitted no reading material referencing her own designation or history.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4430 is a woman of approximate age 30, physically unremarkable, who reports no continuous memory of her own life exceeding approximately six weeks in duration at any time; earlier memories, when tested, are consistently found to be fragments belonging to other individuals, discussed further below.
SCP-4430-File, her Foundation personnel record, functions anomalously when read in its entirety by any person: for the duration of reading and for a variable period afterward (recorded range: eleven minutes to four days), the reader experiences SCP-4430's stored biography as a set of first-person autobiographical memories, indistinguishable subjectively from their own remembered life. Readers reliably report, when interviewed during the effect, that they are SCP-4430, and provide biographical detail consistent with the file's contents, including details not present in the file's written text.
SCP-4430 herself appears to possess no stable memory independent of whoever is currently reading her file; during periods when the file is not being actively read by anyone, interview subjects report she describes herself only in the present tense, stating she does not know what she did "before now" and does not appear distressed by this, a response Foundation psychological staff have been unable to characterize as either genuine equanimity or an absence of the capacity for distress.
It has not been established whether SCP-4430's original, "true" biography exists anywhere, including within the file itself, or whether the file's contents were generated by the act of prior reading, in a process with no identifiable origin point.

ADDENDUM: Following a Level 5 review of SCP-4430's potential utility for information-extraction operations against captured hostile personnel — theorized to function by having a target read a modified version of SCP-4430-File containing false biographical content, potentially overwriting the target's own memory — O5 Council has authorized a limited feasibility study. SCP-4430 was not consulted. Ethics Committee objection is on record.
Preliminary trials under this study have, for the present, been restricted to non-human test material pending further Ethics Committee review; however, the O5 Council retains sole authority to expand the study's scope to human subjects, including captured hostile personnel, without further consultation with any subordinate body, a point the Ethics Committee's objection specifically and unsuccessfully sought to contest.

SCP-4431.name: The Foundation's Word
SCP-4431.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4431 continues to serve in an active field capacity as a Foundation negotiator, deployed exclusively to sapient or negotiation-capable anomalous entities under O5-approved rules of engagement. All statements made by SCP-4431 during a sanctioned negotiation are to be scripted and pre-approved by a Level 4 legal-anomalous liaison prior to deployment wherever operationally feasible, given the binding effect described below; unscripted statements, including apparent pleasantries, are to be minimized but cannot at present be eliminated.
Outside of sanctioned negotiations, SCP-4431 is to be accompanied at all times by a monitor trained to interrupt any statement that could be construed as a promise, commitment, or stated intention, as such statements — whether or not SCP-4431 intends them as binding — reliably produce the effect on him described below regardless of context.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4431 is a 47-year-old man, a Foundation field agent since 2003, redesignated as an SCP entity in 2017 following confirmation of the anomaly described here. Any promise, agreement, or stated commitment made by SCP-4431 on the Foundation's behalf during a formal negotiation with a sapient anomalous entity becomes, upon completion of the negotiation, enforced by means external to any known Foundation capability: violation of such an agreement by the counterparty has, in all nine documented cases, resulted in a specific, proportionate consequence to the violating party, ranging from localized power loss to, in one case, the sudden and total cessation of an entity's anomalous properties.
The Foundation has used SCP-4431 successfully to secure lasting compliance from entities previously considered unreliable negotiating partners. The reciprocal cost, confirmed across seven years of observation, is total: SCP-4431 is now constitutionally incapable of breaking any promise he makes, including trivial or unintentional ones made outside operational contexts. A 2021 incident in which SCP-4431 told a colleague "I'll bring your coffee back" before being called away for eleven hours resulted in SCP-4431 experiencing a documented physiological distress response — elevated heart rate, sweating, disorientation — that resolved only once he personally delivered the coffee, cold, eleven hours later.
SCP-4431's capacity for ordinary, non-binding speech has narrowed accordingly. He now visibly deliberates before making statements colleagues consider unremarkable, and has, per his own request, been issued a standing script of pre-approved conversational phrases verified not to trigger the effect.

ADDENDUM: When asked by Foundation psychological staff whether he would consent to reassignment away from field negotiation, SCP-4431 stated: "I don't think I can promise you an answer to that." He has not been asked again.
Colleagues who have known SCP-4431 since before 2017 describe him as noticeably quieter than he once was, and note that he now says a full goodbye at the end of every conversation, however brief or incidental, as though unwilling to leave anything between himself and another person unfinished, even by implication.

SCP-4432.name: Unwanted Recognition
SCP-4432.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:
SCP-4432 is housed at a remote Foundation facility no closer than 4,000 kilometers to any confirmed or rumored O5 Council meeting location, under a standing cover identity as a long-term psychiatric care resident. Relocation of SCP-4432 requires sign-off from three O5 Council members, reflecting both the severity of the 2014 incident described below and the logistical difficulty of verifying, in advance, that a proposed new location meets distance requirements against Council movements that are not shared with facilities housing SCP-4432.
SCP-4432 is not to be informed of the specific reason for her isolation. Standard cover explanation (a fabricated diagnosis and care history) has been maintained successfully for eleven years.

DESCRIPTION:
SCP-4432 is a 39-year-old woman who, upon coming within an estimated 500 meters of any sitting O5 Council member, involuntarily and permanently perceives that individual's unconcealed physical appearance, identity, and — in four of five tested cases — a small number of unprompted biographical facts about them, regardless of any measure (masking, voice alteration, remote presence, identity compartmentalization) taken to prevent this. The perception is not visual in a conventional sense; SCP-4432 describes it as "just suddenly knowing, like remembering someone you've always known," and the effect persists indefinitely once triggered — she retains the recognition permanently, with no observed method of reversal.
SCP-4432 has, to date, been exposed to three sitting Council members, one deceased former member, and one individual since confirmed by the Foundation to have never held a Council seat despite being present, unremarked, at a session SCP-4432 was inadvertently routed near in 2014 — an incident that resulted in her current isolation protocol and that remains under O5-restricted review. SCP-4432 has not been informed that the fifth individual's status is considered anomalous by the Foundation itself.
