When read by a properly cleared individual, the compound instead produces a measurable, temporary uptake through the lacrimal apparatus, correlating with significantly accelerated reading speed and near-total short-term recall of the passage, effects that fade within 24 hours under first exposure.

Effects do not fade under repeated long-term exposure. Salted Readers with exposure counts above approximately 2,000 documents report permanent, non-fading total recall of every SCP-4476-treated passage they have ever read, arriving unbidden and simultaneously during low-stimulation periods, described uniformly by affected personnel as "all of it, at once, all the time, quietly."

ADDENDUM 4476-1: Seven Salted Readers have requested voluntary reassignment to duties involving no further SCP-4476 exposure, citing the cumulative recall as the reason. All seven remain, per program terms, permanently ineligible for discharge from the Continuous Recall Monitoring Program, as the condition it monitors does not resolve upon reassignment.

SCP-4477.name: The Muffling Drape
SCP-4477.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The single confirmed bolt of SCP-4477, sufficient for eight standard drape units, is stored in Archive Zero's secure textile locker and issued only for sessions or interviews conducted in rooms designated "affect-sensitive" by the Ethics Committee. Each drape unit is logged before and after use, with the identity of all present recorded regardless of whether the drape covered a recording device or was present in the room for any other reason. No replacement material has successfully replicated SCP-4477's properties; three attempted reweaves using recovered thread produced ordinary, non-anomalous fabric.

Any debriefing, interrogation, or testimony session conducted under an SCP-4477 drape must be flagged in its transcript header, and any affect-based deception analysis performed on recollections of that session by personnel present is prohibited from being entered as primary evidence.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4477 is a heavy, dark wool-silk blend fabric of unknown weave origin, recovered from a decommissioned Cold War-era Foundation listening post during its 1987 decommissioning survey; the post's own records do not indicate when or how the fabric entered its inventory. When draped over an active recording or transmission device, SCP-4477 dampens sound transmission through the device consistent with its physical density, an entirely mundane property in isolation.

The anomalous property concerns memory rather than transmission. Individuals present in a room where SCP-4477 is draped over any device, whether or not that device is recording, later recall the emotional content of conversations held in that room as uniformly flat and affectless, regardless of the conversation's actual tenor at the time. This applies even to participants who were, by all external evidence including their own contemporaneous behavior, visibly distressed, angry, or otherwise emotionally engaged. The distortion affects recall only, not real-time perception; individuals in the room experience and respond to genuine emotional content normally while present, and only the retrospective memory of that content is altered.

This has created recurring difficulty for post-session affect analysis used in detecting deception or duress in testimony given near Council business. Three documented interrogations conducted under an SCP-4477 drape produced written transcripts substantially at odds, in emotional register, with the interviewing officers' own later recollections of the same exchange — recollections which, per the anomaly, cannot be trusted regardless of the officers' confidence in them.

ADDENDUM 4477-1: A 2019 review of Council-adjacent testimony flagged a recorded argument between two senior researchers, transcribed as heated based on word choice and cadence, which both participants later described, independently and years apart, as "a calm disagreement, nothing more." Neither participant has been informed that an SCP-4477 drape was present in the room at the time.

SCP-4478.name: The Standing Air
SCP-4478.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4478 refers to the distinct atmospheric composition of Sub-Level Archive Zero-9, the lowest accessible level of Archive Zero. Standard ventilation and atmospheric exchange systems operate continuously at this level but have not, across eleven years of monitoring, succeeded in bringing the level's air into full compositional parity with connecting levels; independent gas chromatography confirms a persistent trace deviation that regenerates within approximately six hours of any forced exchange.

Personnel assigned to Zero-9 duties are limited to continuous shifts of 60 hours or less, followed by a mandatory 48-hour rotation off-level. All Zero-9 work requiring chronological accuracy (date-stamping, sequencing of archival material, incident timelines) must be independently verified against timestamp systems physically isolated from Zero-9's local clocks and logged by personnel who have not exceeded 24 hours of continuous on-level presence.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4478 is not associated with any adverse physiological symptom under current monitoring; personnel exposed to it report no respiratory, neurological, or other bodily effect distinguishable from ordinary indoor air exposure. Its anomalous effect is exclusively on a specific cognitive faculty: the ability to correctly order remembered events, decisions, or document handlings relative to one another in time.

Personnel with continuous exposure exceeding approximately 72 hours report increasing difficulty determining whether a specific memory — of having read a document, made a decision, or been told a fact — occurred before or after another specific memory from the same exposure period. This is distinct from forgetting; affected individuals retain full content of both memories, often in vivid detail, but cannot reliably state which came first, and confidence in incorrect orderings is reported as equal to confidence in correct ones. External verification (physical timestamps, third-party corroboration) resolves the confusion for that specific instance but does not prevent recurrence for the next.

The effect reverses fully within 48 hours of leaving Zero-9's atmosphere and has not been observed to produce any lasting sequencing impairment. It has, however, made unsupervised long-term archival work at Zero-9 impractical without external chronological scaffolding, and at least one documented instance exists of an archivist reordering physical files into an incorrect sequence with full sincerity and no detectable distress at having done so, discovered only through independent audit.

ADDENDUM 4478-1: The origin of Sub-Level Zero-9's atmospheric deviation predates its incorporation into Archive Zero's current structure; construction records from the level's original excavation do not specify any process that would account for it, and no comparable deviation has been detected at any other Archive Zero sub-level despite structural and ventilation similarity. Whether Zero-9 was built around a pre-existing condition, or came to acquire one afterward, remains an open question the Facilities Division has deprioritized in favor of continued operational accommodation.

SCP-4479.name: The Incinerated Testimony
SCP-4479.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All disposal of Level 6/O5-Eyes-Only documentation by incineration is to occur exclusively at Disposal Unit Archive Zero-Cinder, operating under negative pressure with full-face supplied-air respirators mandatory for all personnel present regardless of the specific document being destroyed, as the conditions correlating with SCP-4479 formation have not been reliably isolated in advance. Post-incineration, the unit undergoes forced positive-pressure flush for no less than six hours before re-entry without respiratory protection is permitted.

Any documented instance of a Foundation employee exhibiting apparent firsthand knowledge of an incident predating their employment, or occurring in a division to which they have never held access, is to be referred immediately to the Cinder Exposure Review Board before any administrative or security action is taken on the assumption of an unauthorized information leak.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4479 is a residual property observed in the ash produced by incineration of certain classified documents, specifically those whose content describes incidents involving direct O5 Council decision-making with documented human cost. Not all such incinerations produce the effect; the Foundation has not identified the distinguishing variable, and standard incineration of otherwise comparable classified material at other facilities has never produced it.

When ash exhibiting SCP-4479 is inhaled, even in trace quantities such as those present in disposal unit ambient air despite respiratory protocols, the exposed individual develops a false autobiographical memory of having personally witnessed the events described in the destroyed document. This memory is subjectively indistinguishable from genuine recollection, including sensory detail — sound, smell, tactile sensation — never present in the source document's text, and resists correction through evidence of the individual's actual whereabouts or employment status at the time of the described incident.

Affected individuals have, in several documented cases, acted on these false memories as though they were genuine obligations: attempting to contact affected parties, filing incident reports for events that occurred before their employment, or expressing guilt and requesting counseling for actions they did not take. Standard memory-correction protocols developed for other Foundation anomalies have shown limited effect; the false memory can be suppressed but reliably resurfaces under stress, and subjects uniformly describe the suppressed version as "still true, just quiet."

ADDENDUM 4479-1: Disposal Unit technician D. Ossa, employed four years after the incident described in the destroyed document in question, attempted to file a whistleblower report naming himself as a withheld witness to a containment breach with three recorded fatalities. Personnel records confirm Ossa was eleven years old and residing outside Foundation-controlled territory at the time of the incident. Ossa's report was not accepted, but Ossa has, per his most recent psychological evaluation, not been persuaded that his memory is false.

SCP-4480.name: The Executive Seal
SCP-4480.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The remaining stock of SCP-4480, approximately four kilograms of dark red sealing wax, is held in Archive Zero under direct O5 Council custody, released only for the sealing of a Council-authored Executive Order and only after the order's text has passed review by no fewer than two members of the Drafting Compliance Office. Unlike standard containment review, Drafting Compliance's function with SCP-4480 is not to catch harmful phrasing but to confirm the issuing Council member has been shown, and has acknowledged in writing, the projected cost table described below before the order is sealed. No Executive Order may be sealed with SCP-4480 without this acknowledgment on file, regardless of stated urgency.

Council members are not permitted to seal an Executive Order anonymously or through a proxy signatory; SCP-4480 requires the sealing hand to belong to a credentialed member of the issuing seat, verified biometrically at the moment of sealing.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4480 is a dark red sealing wax used exclusively for Executive Orders — direct, binding written instructions issued by the O5 Council to individual Foundation personnel, bypassing standard chain-of-command transmission. Breaking a seal made with SCP-4480 produces no detectable effect on the recipient; instructions sealed with it are followed or not followed entirely according to the recipient's own judgment, exactly as an unsealed order would be, and Foundation testing has found no compulsion, compliance pressure, or literalism effect of any kind on the person who opens it.

The anomalous effect instead applies, invisibly and at the moment of sealing, to the Council member who signed the order. Once an order sealed with SCP-4480 is opened and acted upon — successfully, partially, or in a manner producing unintended harm — the issuing Council member experiences an irreversible reduction in remaining lifespan, assessed by longitudinal biometric monitoring at a rate correlating with the human cost of the order's actual outcome rather than its intended outcome: a routine logistics order sealed with SCP-4480 has produced reductions as small as several hours; EX-1188 (see Addendum) produced a reduction independently estimated at just under four years.

No Council member has reported subjective awareness of the toll at the moment it is paid, and the mechanism by which SCP-4480 assesses "human cost" — evidently accounting for suffering and consequence rather than simple casualty count — has resisted every attempt at formal modeling. The effect cannot be declined, redirected to another party, or insured against by any tested method; three Council members have independently and separately proposed distributing the cost across all thirteen seats regardless of authorship, and all three proposals have failed to pass a Council vote.

The Foundation maintains SCP-4480 deliberately. Internal position, attributed to no single author, holds that an order whose signer pays a real and irreversible price for its consequences is issued with a different quality of consideration than one that costs its author nothing — a position the Ethics Committee has neither endorsed nor been able to disprove through comparison against Council orders issued by unsealed, ordinary means.

ADDENDUM 4480-1: Executive Order EX-1188, sealed with SCP-4480 and issued during Containment Breach 4480-B, instructed its recipient to "prevent the subject from leaving containment by any means available." The recipient, a facility engineer acting on ordinary judgment under no compulsion, remotely triggered the chamber's structural collapse mechanism with the subject inside. The order's author has since undergone measurable and, per attending Foundation physicians, permanent biological aging consistent with the assessed toll, and has neither requested reassignment from further use of SCP-4480 nor commented on the outcome for the record.

SCP-4481.name: The Continuance Fluid
SCP-4481.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4481 is administered only to the remains of deceased O5 Council members, per standing Council protocol, and only by the two embalming specialists currently cleared for the procedure. Treated remains are stored in a dedicated climate-controlled chamber within Archive Zero, wired with implanted electrode leads accessible from an external interview station without requiring physical disturbance of the remains themselves. No treated remains may be relocated, cremated, or otherwise disposed of without unanimous sitting-Council authorization, which has not, to date, been granted for any treated remains regardless of elapsed time since death.

Continuance Interviews require the presence of at least two Level 6 personnel and a certified neural-response interpreter. All interview transcripts, including sessions producing no coherent response, are sealed at Level 6 and cross-referenced against currently active operations for any apparent correspondence.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4481 is a viscous embalming compound of proprietary Foundation formulation, administered exclusively to O5 Council members' remains as a standing procedural privilege of the seat. Beyond its stated preservative function, SCP-4481 maintains limited electrochemical responsiveness in specific regions of treated cranial tissue for a period extending years beyond clinical death, gradually degrading rather than ceasing abruptly.

This residual responsiveness permits "Continuance Interviews": queries posed to treated remains via implanted electrodes, interpreted by trained specialists as fragmentary word- or phrase-level responses rather than coherent conversation. Interviews are conducted to attempt retrieval of information a Council member held at time of death regarding unresolved classified matters. Reliability decreases measurably with time since death and interview responses are not treated as conclusive without independent corroboration.

A minority of interview responses, across the program's history, have appeared to reflect awareness of events occurring after the interviewed member's death — information the member could not, under any known retrieval mechanism, have possessed at time of death. These instances are flagged, retained, and have not been explained; current working theory holds them as interpretive artifacts of an inherently unreliable signal, though this theory has not been formally tested against the flagged cases with any confidence.

ADDENDUM 4481-1: A Continuance Interview conducted with a Council member deceased eleven years produced a fragmentary response accurately naming an active operation whose classification was assigned nine years after the member's death, by personnel with no documented connection to the member during their tenure. No living authorized party has confirmed briefing the remains, formally or otherwise, on this operation at any point. The interview transcript remains open, without further annotation, pending a resolution the program has not scheduled.

SCP-4482.name: The Faithful Pigment
SCP-4482.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: All master cartography of Archive Zero's substructure is maintained using SCP-4482-based ink on a single set of reference maps stored in the Facilities Cartography Office. Supply of SCP-4482 is limited to approximately 200 milliliters, mined from a single depleted source whose location is no longer accessible; current use is restricted to essential corrections only, prioritizing levels with active anomaly containment over administrative or disused areas.

Any decommissioned, sealed, or destroyed area of Archive Zero whose corresponding ink has faded from the master maps is to have its prior existence cross-filed in the non-anomalous Facilities Records Office before the fade completes, wherever possible; Facilities Records Office holdings are the sole recognized backup, and no procedure currently compensates for their loss.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4482 is a mineral-based pigment of unknown geological origin, used as ink for hand-drawn cartography of Archive Zero's substructure — a layout subject to genuine physical change over time through both authorized renovation and undocumented structural drift not fully understood by Facilities Division. Maps drawn with SCP-4482 exhibit slow, continuous self-correction: over a period of hours to days, lines on the page migrate, fade, or newly appear to track the actual current layout of the mapped area, without any redrawing by cartography staff.

This property has made SCP-4482 maps the Foundation's most reliable record of Archive Zero's lower structure, obviating the need for constant manual resurvey of areas that are, by design, difficult and hazardous to access repeatedly. The corresponding limitation is total: when a mapped area is sealed, destroyed, or otherwise ceases to exist as an accessible space, its corresponding ink fades completely from the master maps within approximately 24 hours, removing not only the layout but any associated labels, room designations, or annotations, with no partial or degraded state observed in between.

The map does not retain history. It reflects only what currently exists. Any knowledge of a decommissioned area's prior existence depends entirely on records maintained outside the SCP-4482 system; where such records are incomplete or lost, the Foundation's own institutional knowledge that the space ever existed is not preserved by any means the pigment provides.

ADDENDUM 4482-1: A 1974 facilities memo references "Room Z-114, adjacent to the eastern archive spine" in the context of a since-resolved structural issue. No room by that designation appears on any current SCP-4482 master map, no Facilities Records Office holding corroborates its prior location, and no currently employed staff member, when asked, has recognized the designation. Whether Z-114 was sealed, renamed, or never existed as described in the 1974 memo has not been determined.

SCP-4483.name: The Closed-Door Loaf
SCP-4483.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: No source of SCP-4483 has been identified. A single loaf, sufficient for the attendees present, is found in the antechamber of the O5 Council's designated closed-door session room approximately thirty minutes before any session confirmed to exceed six hours in duration; the antechamber is monitored continuously, and no delivery, preparation, or placement of the loaf has ever been recorded on camera, by attendant staff, or by any tracked individual. Kitchen and catering staff assigned to Archive Zero have, without exception, denied preparing it when asked, and none has been found to have falsified this denial.

Attendees are not required to consume SCP-4483 and may decline. Medical staff maintain a cross-reference log correlating post-session health reports of all attendees at sessions where SCP-4483 was consumed, reviewed whenever any attendee reports a health complaint within 24 hours of such a session.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4483 is a plain unleavened flatbread of consistent recipe and preparation across all recovered instances, appearing only in connection with extended closed-door O5 Council sessions as described above. Chemical and nutritional analysis finds nothing anomalous in its composition; it functions as ordinary food, providing standard caloric and nutritional value.

Individuals who consume SCP-4483 retain no memory whatsoever of the act of eating, its taste, or its texture, though they retain full memory of the surrounding session content and of having felt hungry beforehand and sated afterward. This amnesia is narrowly specific to the loaf itself and does not extend to other food or drink consumed in the same sitting.

The primary anomalous property concerns the attendees collectively rather than individually: attendees who consumed SCP-4483 during the same sitting exhibit correlated physiological outcomes over the following 24 hours, independent of individual diet, health history, or subsequent activity. Where one attendee reports gastrointestinal discomfort, mild fatigue, or a specific minor symptom within that window, other attendees from the same sitting independently report matching or closely analogous symptoms at comparable severity, verified across medical logs with no evidence of communication between the affected individuals prior to reporting. No shared external cause (contaminated water, unrelated illness, environmental factor) has been identified across the eleven years this correlation has been tracked.

ADDENDUM 4483-1: Following a nine-hour session in which four attendees shared a single SCP-4483 loaf, all four independently reported, over the following day and without contact with one another, an identical and clinically unremarkable symptom: a persistent, mild ringing in the left ear only. No audiological cause was found in any of the four. The symptom resolved in all four within the same six-hour window.

SCP-4484.name: The Deletion Residue
SCP-4484.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4484 accumulation is currently confirmed only within Archive Zero's Deletion Processing Vault, the facility's terminal point for authorized destruction of physical records, digital data, and administratively-approved memory suppression procedures. The vault undergoes mechanical cleaning on a daily cycle; cleaning is retained and measured rather than discarded, as the accumulation rate itself is the primary object of ongoing study. No method of decontamination has reduced net accumulation below its natural regeneration rate.

Personnel assigned to the vault are limited to four-hour shifts in positive-pressure suits and are rotated permanently off Deletion Processing duty after a cumulative lifetime exposure threshold determined by current dosimetry, with no return to the assignment permitted regardless of subsequent psychological clearance. Any personnel reporting a persistent, specific sense of having forgotten something important that they cannot identify, beyond ordinary occupational stress, are to be pulled from vault duty immediately pending evaluation, and are not to be reassigned to the vault at any future date.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4484 is a fine grey dust of consistent composition, elementally unremarkable under standard analysis, whose sole distinguishing property is its exclusive appearance in locations where information has been permanently and completely removed from all known record: physically destroyed documents, securely wiped digital archives, and the endpoint of Foundation-approved procedures for administratively suppressing specific memories in personnel, where those procedures are executed to completion without any retained backup. Personnel researching the phenomenon refer to it informally, and against standing style guidance, as "unmaking dust." Small, isolated quantities are inert and have produced no measurable effect under controlled exposure. The accumulated quantity present in Archive Zero's Deletion Processing Vault, built up over decades of the site's continuous operation, is not inert.

Exposure to accumulated SCP-4484 produces a specific and consistent psychological effect: a mounting, intrusive certainty that the exposed individual is forgetting something of vital importance, without any content, cue, or category attached to the sense of loss — a structural absence rather than a recognizable gap, consistent with the theorized nature of the dust's source. Mild exposure produces distress and compulsive searching behavior (repeatedly checking notes, records, or one's own memory for an absence that cannot be located because, by the phenomenon's nature, its content is unknowable). Prolonged or heavy exposure has produced, in three documented cases among vault personnel prior to current rotation limits, complete catatonic withdrawal, with the affected individual unresponsive except for continued, escalating search behavior directed at nothing external observers can identify.

No decontamination or suppression method has reduced net accumulation. The Foundation's working theory holds SCP-4484 as a physical byproduct of information's deletion from the totality of its own existing record — not damaged, not hidden, but removed such that no trace, including the deleted content's own potential to be remembered, persists anywhere. This theory remains formally unconfirmed.

ADDENDUM 4484-1: Volume measurements of the Deletion Processing Vault across the last six years show SCP-4484 accumulating at a rate exceeding what the Foundation's own documented destruction volume — physical, digital, and administrative combined — can account for, by a margin research staff describe as "not close." Two explanations remain under consideration: that undocumented deletion, of a scale and origin not currently identified, is occurring somewhere within Foundation operations; or that the accumulation is not a byproduct of Foundation action at all, and something else, elsewhere, is also being made to not have happened. Neither explanation has been ruled out. This addendum will be updated pending further measurement.

SCP-4485.name: The Induction Reel
SCP-4485.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: One physical film print (16mm, designated Reel-4485-A) is stored in a climate-controlled vault at Site-19, Archive Wing, accessible only to personnel holding Level 6 clearance or higher, or to O5 Council members. The projector used to screen the reel (Unit 4485-P) is stored separately and must be requisitioned in writing; the two components are never to be stored in the same building. Viewing of SCP-4485 requires the presence of at least two Level 6 personnel, one of whom must not have previously viewed the reel, and both must submit to a post-viewing debrief and memetic screening within four hours. Under no circumstances is SCP-4485 to be duplicated, digitized, or transferred to any format other than its original medium; three prior attempts at digitization resulted in complete loss of the transferred data and, in one case (Incident 4485-Gamma), the technician's inability to recall having attempted the transfer at all. Requests to screen SCP-4485 for training purposes must be submitted to and approved by a sitting O5 Council member.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4485 is a 44-minute black-and-white 16mm film reel presenting itself as a Foundation orientation video for incoming Level 6 personnel. Its title card reads "WELCOME TO YOUR WORK," followed by an unnamed narrator addressing the viewer directly using the viewer's own first name, employee number, and — in 61% of recorded screenings — a personal detail not present in the viewer's personnel file at the time of screening.

The film's content changes between screenings and cannot be predicted or recorded by any external device; audio recorders and cameras aimed at the screen produce only static, though human observers report no interruption. Despite this, every viewer who has watched SCP-4485 in the presence of at least one other viewer describes the same narrative in their independent post-viewing reports: a calm recounting of the founding of the Foundation that omits any named individual, any specific decade, and any acknowledgment that the organization was ever smaller than it currently is. The film asserts, in each account, that the Foundation "has always been this size" and "has never had a first day."

Viewers consistently report a lasting conviction, unsupported by any memory of persuasion, that questioning the Foundation's origin is a symptom of incomplete training rather than a legitimate inquiry. This conviction does not fade with time and has proven resistant to standard memory and belief-correction protocols (Class-B amnesticization reduces but does not eliminate it; see Addendum 4485-1). The effect appears to require no repetition; a single viewing produces the same durable result as multiple viewings, and no additional effect has been observed from repeat screenings by the same individual.

Of the 340 personnel who have viewed SCP-4485 as part of Level 6 induction since its discovery in 1987, none have subsequently sought reassignment, resignation, or transfer out of Level 6 duties. This is noted without further comment in the original discovery report and has not been investigated further, per standing instruction from the O5 Council.

ADDENDUM 4485-1: Following the induction screening of Dr. ██████ in 2023, exit interview notes recorded the following exchange, transcribed by the attending psychologist:

"Do you remember when the Foundation was smaller than it is now?"
"It wasn't."
"It employed twelve people in 1908."
"That's not something that's true. That's something that's written down."

Dr. ██████ remains active in Level 6 duties. No further addenda have been approved for this file.

SCP-4486.name: Minutes of a Meeting Not Yet Held
SCP-4486.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The physical stenographic transcript designated SCP-4486 (currently 212 pages, bound) is held in a sealed records box at Site-19, Records and Information Security Administration, under permanent Level 6 restriction. The box may not be opened except by direct written order of the O5 Council, and any such order must specify the maximum number of pages to be read; partial reading has proven containable, full reading has not been attempted since Incident 4486-1 and is expressly prohibited. SCP-4486 grows by an average of 1.4 pages per month regardless of storage conditions, access frequency, or whether the box is opened. Foundation stenographers are not required for this growth, and no mechanism for it has been identified. Any newly appended pages are to be read only by the currently serving Council Liaison, who will file a redacted summary and then return the box to seal.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4486 presents as an ordinary shorthand-transcribed record of an Ethics Committee proceeding, formatted identically to genuine Foundation committee minutes, including standard header fields for date, attendees, and agenda item. The date field has never been filled in. The attendee list uses only Council seat numbers, never names, consistent with standard redaction practice; however, cross-referencing the recorded statements against actual committee attendance for any date in Foundation history has never produced a match.

The anomalous property of SCP-4486 is that its recorded proceedings consistently describe committee decisions, personnel actions, and containment reclassifications that have not yet occurred at the time of reading, but which subsequently occur, in the same substantive form, within 6 to 34 months of the page being read (not written — read). This has been confirmed independently across 19 instances by comparing sealed, dated copies of read pages against later, unrelated committee records. In no instance has a decision described in SCP-4486 been prevented by foreknowledge; in three instances, Foundation staff who attempted to alter a described outcome after reading the relevant page report that they cannot recall the specific content of their intended alteration once the described decision is underway.

It is not established whether SCP-4486 records a proceeding that will genuinely occur, records a proceeding that occurs because it has been read, or represents some other relationship between reading and outcome. The Ethics Committee has never convened a session matching any content of SCP-4486 and denies, when asked directly, that any such session is planned. This denial has itself twice appeared, near-verbatim, on pages of SCP-4486 read prior to the denial being given.

ADDENDUM 4486-1: Incident 4486-1 (event details restricted to O5 Council and assigned Liaison only) resulted in the reading of 40 consecutive pages by a since-reassigned researcher. Following the incident, the researcher requested and was granted transfer to a non-Foundation-affiliated cover identity. Standard practice would require full amnesticization prior to such a transfer; the Council Liaison of record has confirmed, in writing, that amnesticization was administered, but has declined to confirm what, if anything, it removed. The researcher's prior personnel file remains sealed under the same authority as SCP-4486 itself.

SCP-4487.name: The Coloring Book
SCP-4487.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The 26 known copies of SCP-4487 are stored in a single locked cabinet in the Site-19 Family Services wing. Copies are not to be distributed to any child under Foundation care without prior written authorization from a Level 6 child welfare liaison, and only under direct supervision. Any additional copies discovered in the field are to be recovered, photographed for records, and added to the cabinet; burning, shredding, or other destruction of a copy has never successfully reduced the total count, which self-corrects to 26 within one week regardless of method. Personnel supervising a sanctioned use of SCP-4487 must not, themselves, color in the book at any point.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4487 is a 40-page children's coloring book, professionally bound, titled "MY FRIENDS AT WORK" on its cover in a typeface consistent with mid-1990s commercial printing. Each interior page depicts a simple black-and-white line drawing of an adult engaged in an ordinary workplace activity — filing papers, drinking coffee, answering a telephone — captioned with a short rhyming couplet. No two known copies have identical illustrations, though all follow the same format and page count.

When a child between the approximate ages of 4 and 9 colors a page of SCP-4487 to completion, the specific adult depicted on that page will, within 3 to 11 days, take an action in their own life directly corresponding to the color choices made by the child, regardless of whether the child has ever met, seen, or heard of that adult. This has been confirmed in 71 documented cases, primarily involving Foundation dependents coloring pages depicting unfamiliar staff members at other sites. Coloring a shirt red has preceded the depicted individual's involvement in a workplace altercation; coloring a coffee cup black has preceded that individual skipping a scheduled meal; coloring the sky in the background a color other than blue has, in four cases, preceded the depicted individual filing an unscheduled leave request citing personal reasons.

The correspondence is loose and interpretive rather than literal, and does not appear predictive of anything the depicted adult would not plausibly have done regardless. No case has resulted in harm exceeding minor inconvenience to the depicted individual. Children who use SCP-4487 report no unusual sensation and do not appear to select colors with any discernible pattern or intent; interviews conducted afterward indicate the children were not aware their choices corresponded to anything, and several were unable to recall which colors they had used.

The identity of the individual corresponding to any given page cannot be determined prior to a child completing that page. Family Services has authorized limited, supervised recreational use of SCP-4487 on the grounds that its observed effects are consistently mild and that withholding a functioning coloring book from Foundation dependents raises its own welfare concerns; this authorization is reviewed annually by the Level 6 liaison.

ADDENDUM 4487-1: A proposal to identify which staff member corresponds to a blank, uncolored page in advance, so as to notify them, was rejected by the reviewing liaison on the grounds that "there is no way to ask that question that does not eventually involve giving a child a crayon."

SCP-4488.name: Cross-Stitch Pattern 88
SCP-4488.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4488 is stored as a sealed pattern chart (graph paper, hand-annotated) inside a fire-rated document safe at Site-19. No physical thread, fabric, or embroidery hoop is to be stored in the same room as the chart. Any personnel who complete a stitched reproduction of SCP-4488, in whole or in part, are to report to Medical within six hours for evaluation regardless of apparent condition. Partial reproductions (under 200 stitches) have not produced containment-relevant effects and may be destroyed without special protocol. The original chart itself is not anomalous when merely read or photocopied.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4488 is a hand-drawn cross-stitch pattern chart depicting, when fully stitched, an aerial view of a rural property with a farmhouse, silo, and surrounding field boundaries, rendered on a 14-count grid across approximately 6,400 stitches. The chart itself carries no anomalous properties under standard testing. The anomaly manifests only in physical, completed embroidery produced from the chart using any thread and any fabric.

Upon completion of a full stitched reproduction, the stitcher gains specific, verifiable knowledge of a real property matching the depicted layout, including its current address, ownership history, and at least one non-public fact about a past occurrence on the property (e.g., an unrecorded death, an unfiled property dispute, a buried structure). This knowledge arrives without any accompanying memory of research, and stitchers uniformly report being unable to explain how they know it. In 34 of 34 tested completions, the identified property has been confirmed to exist and the associated fact has been independently verified as accurate, though the specific property identified differs between stitchers using identical charts and identical materials.

The Foundation maintains SCP-4488 under continued study because several identified properties have, upon investigation, been found to contain additional undiscovered anomalies (7 of 34 to date), suggesting the pattern functions as an inconsistent but non-random locator for anomalous sites. Recruitment of contracted embroiderers for this purpose is authorized under Protocol 4488-LOCATE, though the Ethics Committee has restricted this practice to volunteers briefed on the general nature of the task, as three uncontracted completions by Foundation dependents (prior to containment) resulted in the disclosure of gravesite locations that families involved had not wished to have found.

Test subjects who stitch the pattern a second time, using new materials, locate the same property as their first completion rather than a new one. It is not known why the depicted property is fixed per individual rather than per chart.

ADDENDUM 4488-1: Site-19 currently retains four contracted embroiderers under Protocol 4488-LOCATE. A fifth resigned after her third completion identified a property she recognized as her grandmother's childhood home, associated with a fact her family had never disclosed to her.

SCP-4489.name: Terms of Continued Service
SCP-4489.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4489 exists as a clickwrap end-user license agreement embedded in the internal Foundation software suite "Compass" (personnel scheduling and task management, used at 41 sites). The agreement text is not to be altered, translated, or summarized by any means other than direct reproduction; automated summarization tools applied to SCP-4489 have consistently returned summaries describing an unrelated, mundane software license with no anomalous content, and personnel are cautioned not to rely on such summaries. All Compass users are required to "accept" SCP-4489 upon first login and are presented with it again, unprompted, on an interval that has not been successfully predicted (observed range: 40 to 900 days). Personnel may not decline; declining prevents further use of Compass, which is mandatory for shift assignment at affected sites.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4489 is the End User License Agreement presented within Compass, approximately 11,000 words in its full form, formatted identically to a standard corporate software agreement. No employee has been recorded reading the agreement in full prior to acceptance; the software does not require scrolling to the bottom before the "I Agree" button becomes active, consistent with typical corporate software design and not itself anomalous.

The anomalous property of SCP-4489 is that its full text, when read start to finish by a single individual in one sitting, is never the same document twice, and no two full readings by different individuals have ever been confirmed to match, despite the software presenting what its metadata describes as "Version 1.0" at all times. Sections not read are retrospectively unavailable for comparison; screenshots or copies of unread sections, when later examined, show only placeholder text ("Lorem ipsum" boilerplate) regardless of what the software displayed on screen at the time of the screenshot.

Nine personnel are known to have read SCP-4489 in full. Each reports the document containing, somewhere within its boilerplate legal language, one clause specifically and individually relevant to their own life — most commonly a described contingency ("in the event that the User's spouse should predecease the User") matching an event that had already occurred, was later confirmed to occur, or, in two cases, directly contradicted an event the reader had believed to be true about their own life. All nine readers accepted the agreement regardless.

The Foundation has not pursued removal of SCP-4489 from Compass, as doing so would require replacing the scheduling software at 41 sites, and the observed effect has not been shown to cause measurable harm distinct from ordinary occupational stress. Personnel who report distress after reading SCP-4489 are offered standard counseling; none to date have requested amnesticization specifically regarding its content. Compass currently serves approximately 2,900 active accounts across the affected sites, meaning the agreement's periodic re-presentation is, at any given moment, occurring somewhere in the network on a near-daily basis, though no two accounts have yet been confirmed to receive the prompt on the same calendar day.

ADDENDUM 4489-1: A researcher who read the full agreement in 2024 requested, afterward, only that the clause she had read not be repeated to her verbally under any circumstance. This request has been honored and is noted in her personnel file without further explanation.

SCP-4490.name: The Fortune Slip
SCP-4490.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The single known instance of SCP-4490 is stored inside a humidity-controlled glass slide mount in Site-19's small-object archive. It is not to be unfolded further than its current creased position, photographed under magnification only, and handled solely with non-latex gloves. SCP-4490 is not to be eaten, despite originating from and retaining the general appearance of a fortune cookie; the cookie itself was consumed prior to containment and its disposal is not considered anomalous.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4490 is a standard paper fortune slip, approximately 5 cm by 15 cm, printed in black ink on white stock consistent with mass-produced fortune cookie inserts. It was recovered in 2019 from a takeout order placed by a since-retired Foundation researcher at a restaurant with no other recorded anomalous activity. The printed text reads: "You will not finish reading this." The restaurant itself has since closed for unrelated reasons, and no other fortune slip recovered from its remaining paper stock, retained separately in evidence storage, has displayed any comparable property.

The anomaly consists of the fact that no individual who has begun reading the full text of SCP-4490 aloud has been recorded successfully finishing the sentence; in all 22 documented attempts, the reader is interrupted before completing the final word by an external, mundane event unrelated to SCP-4490 itself — a phone ringing, a door opening, a sudden sneeze, a colleague entering to ask a question. The interrupting event differs each time and has never been foreknown, staged, or prevented by advance planning; attempts to read the slip in a sealed, monitored, single-occupant room have still resulted in interruption, in one case by a sudden and otherwise unexplained power flicker lasting 0.4 seconds.

Silent reading of SCP-4490 does not appear to be affected; personnel report no difficulty reading the text privately, and several have confirmed understanding its content without incident. The anomaly applies specifically to the act of vocalizing the printed sentence to completion, by any speaker, in any language (translated readings have also been interrupted, tested in 4 languages to date).

The printed sentence has not changed, faded, or shown any deterioration since recovery, and its assertion has, definitionally, never been falsified: no reading of SCP-4490 has yet been finished. The Foundation has classified this as Safe on the basis that no attempt to complete the reading has resulted in harm to the reader; the interrupting events themselves have ranged from trivial to mildly inconvenient and show no pattern of severity increasing with repeated attempts.

Testing of SCP-4490 has been deprioritized following a 2022 recommendation that further attempts serve no research purpose beyond confirming an outcome that has, to date, never once failed to occur.

ADDENDUM 4490-1: A junior researcher's written proposal to attempt the reading during a scheduled site-wide silence drill, in which no interrupting event could plausibly occur, was approved. The drill was cancelled that day for unrelated maintenance reasons before the test could be conducted.

SCP-4491.name: Typeface Zero
SCP-4491.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The digital font file constituting SCP-4491 ("TYPEFACE-0.ttf") is stored on a single air-gapped drive within a Faraday-shielded cabinet at Site-19. The file is not to be installed on any system connected, currently or in the future, to a Foundation network, and printed samples of text rendered in SCP-4491 are to be treated as anomalous documents in their own right, stored separately from the source file, and reviewed only by personnel cleared for both Level 6 access and Class-IV visual memetic exposure. Any Foundation document discovered to be rendered, in whole or part, using SCP-4491 outside of authorized testing is to be reported as a Level 6 security incident.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4491 is a digital typeface file of unknown origin, discovered embedded in the font cache of a decommissioned Records and Information Security Administration workstation in 2021, with no record of its installation. The workstation itself carries no logged assignment history predating 2014, despite an inventory record listing it as continuously in service since 1998. Rendered as plain text in isolation, SCP-4491 produces a conventional sans-serif typeface with no anomalous properties.

The anomaly manifests only when SCP-4491 is used to render existing Foundation documents that have undergone prior redaction. Text rendered in SCP-4491 displays the original, unredacted content beneath and through any standard redaction formatting (black bars, "[DATA EXPUNGED]" placeholders, [REDACTED] tags) applied to the source document, regardless of the redaction method, the software used to apply it, or whether the underlying unredacted text still exists anywhere in Foundation records. In 6 confirmed cases, SCP-4491 has revealed content for which no unredacted original has been located in any Foundation archive, raising the unresolved question of whether SCP-4491 restores erased information or generates new information indistinguishable from what was erased.

Content revealed by SCP-4491 has, in 4 of 6 testable cases, been independently corroborated as accurate by unrelated sources with no access to the original document. The remaining 2 cases involve information that cannot currently be verified or falsified by any available means, including information concerning individuals whose identities are not otherwise recorded in Foundation systems.

O5 Council directive 4491-C restricts all further testing of SCP-4491 against documents originating from Council-level proceedings. This restriction followed a single unauthorized test (Incident 4491-1) in which a researcher rendered a redacted Council memorandum using SCP-4491; the researcher's subsequent report was itself redacted by an unidentified party before reaching the reviewing committee, and the researcher has since been placed on administrative leave pending an inquiry that has not concluded.

ADDENDUM 4491-1: SCP-4491 has never been observed to reveal content within its own containment file. Attempts to render this document (SCP-4491's own file) using SCP-4491 produce only the word "NO," repeated to fill the page, in place of any redacted or unredacted content.

SCP-4492.name: The Non-Disclosure
SCP-4492.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The master copy of SCP-4492 is held by the Office of the O5 Council and is not catalogued in the general Site-19 archive. A single notarized reproduction is kept by the assigned Legal Liaison for use under Protocol 4492-SEAL. SCP-4492 is deployed exclusively by O5 Council authorization, on a per-signature basis, to individuals the Council has determined require permanent, self-enforcing silence regarding a specific matter where standard amnesticization is inappropriate (e.g., where the individual's continued unaltered memory and cooperation are operationally necessary) or has previously failed. Each deployment must be logged with the specific matter covered, in a registry accessible only to sitting Council members.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4492 is a legal non-disclosure agreement, four pages, using standard contract language and formatting indistinguishable from conventional Foundation NDAs at a glance. Its signature block requires the signer's full legal name written in their own hand; no other method of execution (typed name, digital signature, proxy) has been observed to produce the anomalous effect, and the Foundation has, on three occasions, used this fact deliberately to allow a signature to be legally binding without anomalous consequence, by having the individual type rather than write their name.

Upon a handwritten signature, the signer retains full, accurate, ordinary memory of the matter covered by the agreement. However, the signer becomes permanently, structurally unable to communicate that matter to any other person through any medium — speech, writing, gesture, code, or any other channel yet tested — not because they forget it, but because the specific words, symbols, or expressions required to convey it consistently fail to form, are substituted with unrelated content mid-utterance, or are physically prevented (in two cases, involuntary muscle failure interrupting handwriting mid-word). The signer is aware, in the moment, that they are being prevented, and reports no distress beyond ordinary frustration; the effect does not appear to constitute compulsion in the traditional sense, functioning instead as a structural limit on the physical act of disclosure itself.

The effect does not impair the signer's ability to think about, plan around, or use the withheld knowledge in non-disclosing ways, nor does it affect the signer's ability to discuss the matter's existence in general terms, only its specific content. 214 individuals currently carry an active SCP-4492 obligation. No signer has successfully disclosed covered information since deployment began; no signer has requested release from the agreement, though the mechanism for such release, if one exists, has never been documented or tested.

ADDENDUM 4492-1: The origin of SCP-4492 — who drafted it, when, and by what means it acquired its property — is not recorded in any file accessible below O5 clearance. The current Legal Liaison, when asked in 2024 whether any Council member present at its first use is still serving, responded only that the question was "outside the scope of the Liaison's need to know," and has since declined to discuss the matter further, though not, notably, under any apparent compulsion.

SCP-4493.name: The Wrong File
SCP-4493.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The physical manila folder constituting SCP-4493 is stored in a sealed records box in the Site-19 archive, separate from all active personnel files. Access requires Level 6 clearance and a co-signing witness. SCP-4493 is not to be photocopied; all 14 attempted photocopies to date have produced either blank pages or pages containing content unrelated to any known personnel record. Personnel who open SCP-4493 are to be informed, prior to opening, of the folder's effect, and may decline to proceed without penalty.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4493 is a standard Foundation personnel dossier folder, tabbed and labeled identically to genuine active files, bearing a placeholder designation ("EMPLOYEE FILE — PENDING ASSIGNMENT") rather than any specific name. The folder's physical paper stock, when tested, matches material manufactured no earlier than 2009, though the earliest confirmed sighting of SCP-4493 in archive inventory logs predates that year by six years, a discrepancy that remains unresolved. The folder's contents — photograph, biographical summary, service record, incident history, commendations, and disciplinary notes — are, upon opening by any individual, generated to depict that individual's own life, written in the third person in standard Foundation dossier format, rather than the life of any assigned employee.

The generated dossier is accurate with respect to publicly known or Foundation-recorded facts about the reader's life, but consistently includes additional entries for which the reader has no memory and which cannot be corroborated by any other Foundation record: named incidents, dated commendations, disciplinary actions, and in nine documented cases, a "Reassignment" entry listing a Foundation site or role the reader has never worked at or held, dated in the reader's future. Of these nine future-dated reassignment entries, four have subsequently occurred, as written, within 18 months; three remain pending; two involve sites that, at time of reading, did not yet exist under the name given and were established under that name at a later date.

No reader has been able to alter, correct, or dispute an entry within SCP-4493 by any means, including administrative correction requests processed through standard personnel channels for their genuine, non-anomalous file — corrections applied to a reader's real dossier do not propagate to SCP-4493's version, and re-opening SCP-4493 reproduces the same generated content on each occasion for the same reader, unchanged except for the addition of newly-elapsed future entries becoming past entries.

Foundation policy currently prohibits informing personnel of their own future-dated entries prior to those entries' occurrence, following an incident (4493-2) in which a researcher's attempt to avoid a listed disciplinary action is believed to have directly caused the circumstances leading to that action.

ADDENDUM 4493-1: The folder has never, in any recorded opening by any individual, generated a dossier belonging to someone other than the person opening it, and has never been opened successfully by two individuals simultaneously; the second individual present during any opening reports seeing a blank folder.

SCP-4494.name: Reply All
SCP-4494.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4494 refers to a specific, recurring email thread within the Site-19 internal mail server, subject line "RE: RE: RE: Supply Closet Access." The thread is not to be deleted, forwarded outside the Foundation network, or replied to by unauthorized personnel; the Information Security team maintains a standing filter that flags any new message in the thread for immediate review before delivery is permitted to proceed. The original 2016 message and all subsequent replies are retained on an isolated mail archive not connected to the live server.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4494 is an email thread originating from a genuine, mundane 2016 message concerning supply closet key access at Site-19, sent by a since-departed logistics clerk to a departmental distribution list of 34 recipients. The thread has continued to receive new replies at irregular intervals (average: one every 40 days) despite the original sender no longer being employed by the Foundation and despite no living recipient admitting to having sent any of the subsequent messages. The distribution list itself, though nominally frozen since 2016, has since been found to include three names belonging to individuals hired by the Foundation after that date, none of whom have any record of being deliberately added to it.

Each new reply in the thread is visible only to the specific recipient viewing it at the time; when two personnel with mail access to the thread compare their inboxes, each sees a different message as the "latest" reply, with different senders (always listed as a current member of the original distribution list, regardless of that person's actual current access or, in six cases, regardless of that person's death), different content, and different apparent send times, though all copies share the same subject line and thread ID. No recipient has been able to produce a copy of a message another recipient reports seeing.

The content of each individually-viewed message is consistently mundane in form (a short reply about supply closet logistics) but contains one sentence, embedded naturally in the mundane text, that recipients uniformly interpret as directed personally at them regarding a private matter unrelated to supply closets. Recipients report the sentence as unsettling specifically because of its offhand, administrative tone rather than its content, which ranges from mildly cryptic ("might want to double check with the second key, just in case, you know how the last one went") to specific enough to alarm ("no rush on the closet — figured you'd want to deal with the Site-17 business first anyway").

Recipients removed from the distribution list continue to receive replies. Recipients who have left Foundation employment and had their accounts deactivated report, in exit interviews, no longer receiving them, though this has not been independently verified.

ADDENDUM 4494-1: A 2023 attempt to trace the thread's mail headers to a single originating server was inconclusive; headers were internally consistent and correctly formatted but referenced a server hostname not present in any Foundation infrastructure inventory, past or current.

SCP-4495.name: The Familiar Narrator
SCP-4495.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The master audio file of SCP-4495 (approximately 9 hours, 14 minutes, digital format) is stored on an isolated server at Site-19 with no external network connection. Playback for research or containment purposes requires Level 6 authorization and must occur through hardwired headphones only, never through open speakers, to prevent unintended exposure of bystanders. Personnel who have completed a full listen are placed on a 90-day monitoring schedule and are not to be assigned to complete a second full listen at any point in their Foundation career.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4495 is a digital audiobook recording of an unremarkable, non-anomalous public-domain novel (a 1911 adventure narrative, author and title withheld pending unrelated copyright review), narrated by a single voice. The novel's source text has been cross-checked against three independently published public-domain editions and matches all of them exactly, ruling out alteration of the underlying narrative itself as a contributing factor. The recording's anomalous property is that the narrating voice is, for each individual listener, an exact vocal reproduction of a person the listener personally trusts — most commonly a parent, close friend, mentor, or long-term partner, living or deceased — despite no listener having provided any sample of that person's voice to Foundation researchers prior to listening, and despite the voice being reported as unmistakably, specifically that person's by 100% of tested listeners (n=61) to date.

Two listeners in the same room, listening to separate copies of the identical audio file through separate headphones, consistently report hearing different voices matching their own respective trusted individuals; the underlying waveform, when analyzed, does not correspond to any known individual's recorded voice and does not change based on the listener, remaining bit-for-bit identical across all tested playback instances.

The narrated content itself is unremarkable and matches the source novel's text precisely. However, listeners uniformly report a persistent, several-week increase in their trust toward whatever the recognized voice tells them going forward, in contexts entirely unrelated to SCP-4495 — a form of durable, source-independent credibility transfer. Three listeners have reported acting on instructions they believed, in the moment, to have come from their trusted individual through ordinary conversation, before realizing the instruction had no basis outside their memory of the recording.

The Foundation has not identified a mechanism by which SCP-4495 selects or synthesizes the voice, and has declined, per O5 directive, to test the file against Council members directly, citing unacceptable operational risk should any Council member's voice prove reproducible by the file for other listeners, which would constitute an unquantified security exposure regarding the Council's own trusted-voice authority within the organization.

ADDENDUM 4495-1: A researcher assigned to catalog SCP-4495's audio metadata, without listening to the recording, reported that the file's internal title tag reads, in every checked copy, simply: "for you."

SCP-4496.name: Reminder: Renewal Due
SCP-4496.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4496 manifests as a push notification on Foundation-issued mobile devices and cannot be contained at the software level; disabling notifications, uninstalling applications, or replacing the device has not prevented recurrence, including on devices freshly imaged and issued for the first time. All Foundation-issued devices are treated as potential vectors. Personnel who receive SCP-4496 are instructed not to tap or open the notification and to report its exact wording, timestamp, and any listed deadline to Information Security within one hour.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4496 is a mobile push notification, formatted identically to a standard system or application reminder, that appears without warning on the lock screen of a Foundation-issued device. It always reads "Reminder: Renewal Due," followed by a specific date, and, on approximately 40% of occurrences, a named item or service ("Reminder: Renewal Due — Passport, June 14" or similar). No application on the device has been found responsible for generating the notification; forensic analysis of device logs shows the notification appearing with no corresponding process, push service call, or scheduled trigger.

The anomalous property of SCP-4496 is that the named item or listed date, when present, consistently corresponds to something in the recipient's life that genuinely requires renewal, review, or attention by that date — not always the literal item named (a "Passport" reminder has, in 9 cases, preceded discovery of an unrelated but comparably time-sensitive lapse, such as an expired containment authorization or an overdue psychological evaluation) but always something the recipient would, upon reflection, recognize as a genuine and previously overlooked obligation.

Recipients who act on the notification's implied deadline uniformly avoid a negative consequence that later investigation confirms would otherwise have occurred. Recipients who ignore the notification experience the consequence as though the warning had never been given. The notification does not repeat once its associated date has passed, regardless of whether the recipient acted on it, and a given recipient does not appear to receive the notification more than once per calendar year.

The Foundation has not determined the source of SCP-4496 or how it identifies a genuinely overlooked obligation specific to each recipient. A 2023 Ethics Committee review concluded that instructing personnel to ignore the notification, in order to study consequences without intervention, would constitute an unacceptable and avoidable harm given the reliability of the notification's accuracy, and Level 6 authorization is required to approve any non-response study protocol.

ADDENDUM 4496-1: On one occasion, SCP-4496 appeared on a device belonging to a staff member who had been deceased for eleven days, prior to the device's return to inventory. The notification read: "Reminder: Renewal Due — Next of Kin Contact Information, [date]." The listed contact information on file was subsequently found to be eight years out of date.

SCP-4497.name: Rehearsal Copy
SCP-4497.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The single bound script constituting SCP-4497 is stored in the Site-19 Recreational Therapy office and may be checked out only for supervised use within the drama therapy program, which uses table-read exercises as part of standard personnel stress processing. Sessions using SCP-4497 must be recorded on audio only (no video) and reviewed by the attending therapist before the recording is filed. The script is not to leave the therapy office under any circumstance.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4497 is a 32-page stage play script titled "Intermission," formatted conventionally with a small cast of unnamed characters designated only by letter (A, B, C, D). The printed dialogue is ordinary and unremarkable when read silently, depicting a loose, naturalistic conversation between four people waiting in an unspecified place for an unspecified event. The script's paper and binding have been dated to a print run consistent with the mid-1990s, though the Foundation holds no acquisition record indicating when or from where the copy entered inventory, and the therapy program's own equipment log lists it only as "donated, source unrecorded."

When SCP-4497 is read aloud by a group of players in a table-read format, each player assigned to a role finds that their character's lines, as spoken, diverge from the printed text on the page in front of them, replacing scripted dialogue with lines addressing a genuine, currently unresolved personal concern of the specific player reading that role, phrased as though spoken by their assigned character within the play's fictional scene. Other players in the group hear only the substituted lines and have no perception that a substitution has occurred; the reading player, by contrast, sees the printed line and hears themselves speak the substituted one simultaneously, describing the sensation as mildly disorienting but not distressing.

Recordings of sessions confirm that the substituted dialogue is audible on tape and matches what players reported hearing, while the printed script recovered after each session shows no alteration to its text. The therapy program has found supervised use of SCP-4497 clinically useful as an indirect disclosure tool, allowing participants to voice concerns they had not consciously planned to raise, and 22 of 30 participating personnel have reported the exercise as helpful in post-session evaluations. No participant has reported the substituted content revealing anything they did not, on reflection, already know about their own situation.

The mechanism by which SCP-4497 selects relevant content for each reader is unknown, and testing with non-Foundation script formats or blank scripts read under identical conditions has not reproduced the effect; the anomaly is specific to this physical script.

ADDENDUM 4497-1: A supervising therapist noted that Character D's lines have, across 30 recorded sessions, never once been substituted, regardless of which player is assigned that role, and that the printed dialogue for Character D consists entirely of the single stage direction "(D says nothing.)"

SCP-4498.name: Word of the Day
SCP-4498.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: The complete deck of SCP-4498 (118 cards) is stored at Site-19's dependent education annex and is deployed exclusively through Protocol 4498-LESSON, administered by cleared Family Services educators to Foundation dependents aged 6–12 whose parent or guardian holds Level 3 clearance or higher, as part of an authorized supplementary curriculum. Use outside this protocol is prohibited. Cards are inventoried before and after each session; any card reported missing is to be treated as a Level 6 security concern regardless of apparent triviality.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4498 is a deck of illustrated vocabulary flashcards, professionally produced, each card presenting a single invented word (e.g., "flenwick," "sordane," "cabrilon") in a child-friendly font alongside a simple illustration and a one-sentence definition, formatted identically to a conventional early-literacy vocabulary aid. None of the printed words exist in any human language; linguistic analysis has found no consistent etymological pattern across the deck. Deck inventory audits conducted quarterly since 2019 have never recorded a discrepancy in card count prior to the 2024 insertion described below, and the deck's plastic coating and print quality remain consistent with its original manufacture despite an estimated 400 individual teaching sessions to date.

Each card's invented word and definition correspond, under systematic comparison, to a specific, genuine Foundation anomaly currently held at Keter or Euclid classification, restructured into a form comprehensible to and memorable by a young child without disclosing the anomaly's classified designation, containment specifics, or hazard level. A child who learns and retains a card's word demonstrates, without further instruction, an accurate, age-appropriate working understanding of the corresponding anomaly's basic nature and associated safety behavior (e.g., the card for "sordane" corresponds to a light-sensitive entity; children who learn the word consistently and independently begin closing curtains at dusk in unrelated contexts, without prompting).

The Foundation deliberately maintains and uses SCP-4498, on Ethics Committee authorization, as a low-disclosure method of preparing Foundation dependents — who statistically face elevated likelihood of anomalous exposure due to parental occupation — for future encounters, without requiring formal briefing or exposing them to classified material. Children who complete the full deck demonstrate, in blinded follow-up testing, measurably improved outcomes in unrelated simulated anomalous-encounter safety drills compared to non-exposed control groups of similar age and background.

The mechanism by which SCP-4498's cards acquire accurate correspondence to classified anomalies — information to which the deck's original, unknown compiler should not have had access — remains uninvestigated by Council directive, on the stated grounds that the deck's continued beneficial function is of greater operational value than resolving its origin, and that active investigation risks altering or losing the correspondence.

ADDENDUM 4498-1: A 119th card was found inserted into the deck in 2024, blank on both sides. No word has yet appeared on it. It has not been removed.

SCP-4499.name: In Memory Of
SCP-4499.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4499 is a brass memorial plaque mounted in the Site-19 Wall of Remembrance, a corridor commemorating Foundation personnel deceased in the line of duty. The plaque is not to be removed, relocated, or polished by anyone other than personnel assigned to Protocol 4499-READ, who inspect it on a weekly basis. Any newly appeared name is to be cross-referenced against active personnel records within the hour of discovery. The corridor remains accessible to general Site-19 staff as part of standard memorial function; restricting access has been assessed as more disruptive to morale than the plaque's contained risk warrants.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4499 is a standard bronze dedication plaque, indistinguishable on manufacture from the 40 other genuine memorial plaques mounted in the same corridor, bearing the header "IN MEMORY OF THOSE WHO SERVED" followed by engraved names, in the same typeface and layout as its neighbors. It was first noted as anomalous in 2020 when a name appeared on it belonging to a staff member who was, at the time, still alive and on active duty.

New names appear on SCP-4499 engraved into the metal itself, with no visible tool marks, seam, or discoloration distinguishing them from names present since the plaque's installation (date of installation not established; no procurement record for the plaque has been located). Each new name belongs, without exception, to a currently living, active Foundation staff member, and precedes that individual's death, in the line of duty, by an interval ranging from 11 days to just over 6 years. No name has ever appeared for an individual who did not subsequently die in a manner qualifying for memorial inclusion under standard Foundation criteria, and no engraved name has been observed to be removed or altered after the corresponding death.

The plaque does not appear to cause or influence the deaths it precedes; investigated cases show causes consistent with the specific hazards of each individual's actual duties, with no discernible connection to the plaque, its viewing, or awareness of one's own name appearing on it. Personnel whose names have appeared and who were subsequently informed (a practice discontinued after 2021, see Addendum) uniformly reported the knowledge as psychologically burdensome without altering the eventual outcome.

Current policy, per Ethics Committee ruling, is that new names are logged but not disclosed to the named individual or their immediate colleagues, on the grounds that foreknowledge has shown no protective value and measurable psychological cost. The Protocol 4499-READ team consists of rotating volunteers who have waived standard disclosure rights regarding their own potential appearance on the plaque.

ADDENDUM 4499-1: Disclosure to named individuals was discontinued following a 2021 case in which a staff member, informed of his name's appearance, requested and was granted immediate reassignment to the lowest-risk available posting. He died eight months later of unrelated natural causes, of a kind the plaque had never previously listed, prompting the current non-disclosure policy under the unresolved concern that disclosure itself may not be neutral.

SCP-4500.name: The Archive Entry
SCP-4500.text:
SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-4500 is not a physical object but a designation slot within the Foundation's own archival indexing system — the same system, at the schema level, used to generate, number, and cross-reference every document in this database, including this one. No conventional containment procedure applies; SCP-4500 cannot be moved, sealed, or physically secured, as it has no location outside the index itself. Access to SCP-4500's entry is restricted to the O5 Council and to any individual the entry itself has independently granted access to, a category the Council does not fully control and cannot reliably predict membership of. Personnel who discover they have been granted unsanctioned access are to report the fact immediately and are not, notably, penalized for the access itself, per standing Council guidance.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-4500 is an anomaly in the structure of the Foundation's document archive rather than in any single document. Standard archival entries are created by staff, reviewed by editorial oversight, and assigned a number in sequence; SCP-4500's entry has no recorded author, no creation date consistent with the numbering sequence surrounding it, and no editorial history, despite occupying a numbered slot that every audit confirms should exist and be filled.

The content of SCP-4500's entry — this document — is not fixed. Each authorized reader receives a version of this file describing a different anomaly, formatted identically to every other entry in the archive, internally consistent, cross-referenced correctly against surrounding case numbers, and indistinguishable during reading from a genuine record. No two readers, to date, have compared notes and found matching content, and attempts to preserve or externally verify a specific version of SCP-4500's content between readings have failed in a manner consistent with several previously logged information-hazard anomalies elsewhere in the archive, without SCP-4500 itself ever being formally connected to those cases.

The Foundation's working hypothesis — never confirmed, and explicitly noted in this entry as unconfirmed regardless of which version a given reader receives — is that SCP-4500 functions as a kind of structural seam in the archive itself: a slot that exists to be filled, that fills itself with whatever content its current reader is prepared to receive, and that may have done this consistently, undetected, for longer than any single custodian of the archive has served. Whether this constitutes a passive property of the indexing system, a deliberate design choice by an unidentified original architect of the archive, or something the archive does to itself without design at all, remains — as it has for every prior custodian who has reached this entry — unresolved.

The O5 Council has declined, on four separate occasions across its recorded history, to close, delete, or renumber SCP-4500's slot. No stated reason for this restraint appears in any accessible record. The entry persists. It is being read now.

ADDENDUM 4500-1: This document does not have a fixed final line. It has whatever one the archive has decided you are ready to read next.

END OF FILE.
